entries.note: MEASURED EVERYTHING, AND OVERTURNED TWO PROPOSALS. Built the offline driver and proved timer.c CAN be driven in the diff_*.c idiom (one stub: gettimeofday). CENSUS: emulated_hz is an int, so INT_MAX bounds every legitimate request - the ceiling is DERIVED, not picked. POLICY TABLE: 'drop missed ticks' is NOT A POLICY BUT A DEFECT (it caps every timer at 65 Hz - a 100 Hz timer runs at rate 0.65 with no burst at all); the flagship's cap of 65536 BREAKS a legitimate 4e7 Hz timer (1.0000 -> 0.1065); 2^20 is the smallest power of two that leaves every legitimate case BIT-IDENTICAL to shipped. And clamping at :137 alone is not just insufficient but A REGRESSION - it loses idempotence on five of six classes because the early-out then compares a clamped record against a raw request. Caught its own first probe (it held time fixed and would have cleared the defect).

**THE FIX:** clamp `lentoread` to the current block's remainder; advance `buf` by what was consumed. Same shape as `diskimage_access__cue()` in the same file.

**A seat supplied the algebra I had not derived:** `curofs + remain` **is** `(curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1`, identically -- so the clamp is *provably consistent* with the loop's existing advance rather than merely compatible with it.

*** THREE THINGS CAUGHT ME, ALL BY GUARDS: ***
  1. **`buf += OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` appears TWICE.** The other is in `fwrite_helper`, where the fixed stride is CORRECT because that path refuses unaligned access. **Patching the first occurrence would have broken the write path**; the anchor-count guard stopped it.
  2. **I reformatted 6 lines I never touched** -- a whitespace pass removed 7 trailing-tab lines when I had introduced 1. Reverted and re-applied; the diff is now 17+/3- with `-w` giving an identical stat.
  3. **The mutant script's anchor went to 0 after the fix landed** and said so, rather than silently patching nothing.

**Post-fix:** `52 rows, 0 failures, DISKIMAGE_IO_PASS`. All 11 offline differentials green. Twin trees and ALL THREE build trees byte-identical (an earlier draft said 'both' and was MEASURED FALSE -- it forgot the WSL arc tree, which was stale).

**FILED, NOT FIXED:** the short-read path is unchanged -- on a short read in a non-final iteration `len` decrements by the requested amount while `totallenread` grows by the actual, so the caller's zero-fill can cover the wrong region. Pre-existing; the patch neither helps nor worsens it.

*** CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 by an adversarial opus pass that tried to break all four steps and could not. Three refinements, and the first is a REAL NARROWING I had missed. ***

**PRECONDITION: the defect requires `d->nr_of_overlays > 0`.** With no overlay the function takes a fast path (`:1347`) that is a single `fseek`+`fread` and is correct. My record did not state this. **It is not a get-out:** overlays come from the `V` prefix (`:1810`) and from `R:` (`:2095`), and `R:` is routine in this project's own rigs (`gate_ab.sh:82` uses `LUNA_IMG="R:..."`, and `drive_guest.py` and several probes do the same).

**UNALIGNED OFFSETS ARE GUEST-REACHABLE, with a census rather than an example:**
  * `promemul/dec_prom.c:167-170` -> `:148` -- `lseek` stores an arbitrary 64-bit guest value as `current_file_offset`; `read()` passes it straight through with a guest length up to 64 MB. **Gives both faults.**
  * `promemul/arcbios.c:1923` -> `:1761` -- ARC `Seek` stores an arbitrary 64-bit offset from guest memory; `Read` uses it with a length up to 64 MB. **Gives both faults.**
  * `diskimage_scsicmd.c:725`/`:830` -- variable-length tape READ via `tape_offset`.
  * `bootblock_iso9660.c:271-282` -- unaligned, but a fixed 256-byte length means one iteration, so **wrong-layer only**, no misalignment.

*** THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IS AN ASYMMETRY I HAD NOT LOOKED FOR: THE WRITE SIDE HAS THE GUARD THE READ SIDE LACKS. *** `fwrite_helper` explicitly refuses a non-multiple length (`:1273-1280`) and an unaligned offset (`:1281-1286`), both returning 0, both under `#164`. `fread_helper` has **no such guard anywhere**. The read path was simply never given the check the write path was.

**THE MECHANISM IS SHARPER THAN I STATED, in a way that matters for the detector:** iteration 1 is **positionally CORRECT** (`buf[k] = file[offset+k]`); its only fault is the LAYER. The positional corruption begins at iteration 2 and is caused by the fixed `buf += OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` stride paired with a variable-start read. **So the two halves have different trigger conditions:** wrong-layer needs only an unaligned offset; duplication additionally needs `len > 512 - (offset & 511)`. A detector must cover both.

**AND IT IS NOT A MEMORY-SAFETY ISSUE, which was checked explicitly:** `buf` advances 512 only when `lentoread == 512`, and any short `lentoread` zeroes `len` and ends the loop; `len` cannot underflow. **Silent wrong data, no overrun.**

**The cue idiom is confirmed as the fix template** (`:1091-1144`): `chunk = CDROM_SECTOR_SIZE - intra; if (chunk > len) chunk = len;` with `buf + total_copied`. It clamps to bytes-remaining-in-sector AND indexes the buffer by bytes actually delivered -- **both halves of what the overlay loop lacks.**

**ADJACENT, not claimed by this row:** on a short read the loop does `len -= lentoread` while `totallenread += lenread`, so a short read in a NON-FINAL iteration makes the caller's `memset(buf + lendone, ...)` zero the wrong region. Worth a row of its own if this is worked.

*Honest limit the seat stated and I keep: no rig was measured actually issuing an unaligned >512-byte read against an overlaid disk. Reachability is READ, not MEASURED.*

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, GUEST-REACHABLE, AND IT CORRUPTS READ DATA. The most severe bare-title row worked so far. Verified by reading the loop; the mechanism is worse than the title says. ***

`src/disk/diskimage.c:1358-1402`, the overlay read loop:

```c
for (curofs=offset; len != 0;
    curofs = (curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1) {
        for (overlay_nr = d->nr_of_overlays-1; overlay_nr >= 0; overlay_nr --)
                if (overlay_has_block(d, overlay_nr, curofs))   /* layer chosen for THIS block */
                        break;

        lentoread = len > OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE? OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE : len;   /* NOT clamped to the
                                                       block's REMAINDER */
        ... fread(buf, 1, lentoread, <chosen layer>) ...

        len -= lentoread;
        buf += OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE;          /* fixed stride */
}
```

**`lentoread` is clamped to the BLOCK SIZE, never to the bytes left in the CURRENT block.** So when `offset` is not block-aligned, the loop picks a layer for the block containing `curofs` and then reads up to a full block from it -- **running past that block's end into the next one or two blocks, which may live in a different layer.**

**Worked example, offset 511, len 1024** (`OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` = 512):
  * iteration 1: `curofs = 511` -> layer chosen for **block 0**; `lentoread = 512`; reads file offsets **511-1022** into `buf[0..511]`.
  * `curofs = (511 | 511) + 1 = 512`; `buf += 512`.
  * iteration 2: layer chosen for **block 1**; reads file offsets **512-1023** into `buf[512..1023]`.

**The guest asked for offsets 511-1534 and receives: wrong-layer bytes in the first half, and file offsets 512-1022 DUPLICATED at two different buffer positions.** The tail it asked for (1023-1534) is never read at all. This is silent read corruption, not a refusal.

*** THE LOOP'S OWN ADVANCE EXPRESSION PROVES UNALIGNED OFFSETS WERE ANTICIPATED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS AN OVERSIGHT AND NOT AN UNDOCUMENTED PRECONDITION. *** `curofs = (curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1` rounds UP to the next block boundary. If `offset` were always block-aligned that expression would simply be `curofs + OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE`. **The author wrote alignment-handling into the advance and omitted it from the length.**

**GUEST-REACHABLE** (seat's sequence, structurally consistent with the code, which carries no alignment guard anywhere): an overlaid ARC disk, guest writes blocks 0 and 2 so they land in different layers, then a byte-granular `Seek(511)` + `Read(1024)`. ARC exposes byte-granular seek/read, so the unaligned offset reaches this loop. **Not verified by execution -- needs a build.**

**Observable for a detector:** the guest-visible read payload. Write distinct sentinel bytes into blocks that land in different layers, then read across the boundary from an unaligned offset; broken returns the wrong layer's sentinel and a duplicated range, fixed returns the requested bytes in order.

*** THE FIX IDIOM IS ALREADY IN THIS FILE. *** `diskimage_access__cue()` (`:1083`) does exactly the right thing for the same shape of problem -- it clamps each step to the remainder of the current sector and writes at `buf + total_copied` rather than on a fixed stride (see its `memset(buf + total_copied, 0, chunk)` at the same offset discipline). **Transferred warrant: clamp `lentoread` to the current block's remainder, and advance `buf` by the amount actually consumed rather than by a constant.**

**A SECOND, SEPARABLE HALF reported by the seat and NOT verified here:** a short `fread` on the flat (non-overlay) path is said to return zero even after reading bytes, causing the caller to zero the whole requested buffer. Recorded as the seat's claim; check it before it rides along with the fix, because a row covering two defects buries one when the other closes.

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, and THE ROW COVERS TWO DEFECTS OF DIFFERENT SEVERITY -- which is the shape that buries one when the other closes. Split before working it. ***

entries.ev: Agent seat (fable5) adjudication 2026-08-29; census, osiop:500-505, asc:1395-1400 and the raw-vs-call grep contamination all re-verified by the main loop against source
entries.outcome_note: return 0 refuted on consumer evidence rather than structure; my helper counts were contaminated by the comment header and definition; the ATAPI route is the WRONG witness channel, which inverts what I assumed.
entries.note:
VERDICT: **`return 0` IS REFUTED -- not merely a sketch, but a MEASURED-BY-READING
BEHAVIOURAL REGRESSION on two controllers with ZERO benefit on the third.  The right shape
is `diskimage__return_check_condition(xferp, d, 0x05, 0x20, 0x00)` PLUS the fall-through
`return 1` -- the file's own refusal idiom at four shipped sites.**  Every claim below was
re-verified by me against the source before recording.

*** MY CENSUS WAS CONTAMINATED AND SO IS THE ROW'S.  Both counted the COMMENT HEADER and the
DEFINITION as calls. ***

    grep -c 'diskimage__return_default_status_and_message'          -> 25   raw
    grep -c 'diskimage__return_default_status_and_message(xferp'    -> 23   CALLS
    grep -c 'diskimage__return_check_condition'                     ->  5   raw
    grep -c 'diskimage__return_check_condition(xferp'               ->  3   CALLS
    grep -c $'^\tcase '                                             -> 22   top-level labels

So **the row's "the only one of 25" is wrong under ANY unit** -- 25 is the contaminated raw
count.  The correct statement is **"the only one of 20 TOP-LEVEL ARMS"** (22 labels forming
19 bodies, since MODE_SENSE/10, READ/READ_10 and WRITE/WRITE_10 share bodies, plus the
default).  My own `~30` counted NESTED labels.  *A re-deriver caution worth keeping: 
`grep -E '^\tcase'` silently matches NOTHING, because `\t` is a literal `t` in ERE -- use
`$'\t'`.  I hit that exact trap on this file earlier today.*

**THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM SURVIVES, verified arm by arm**: all 19 bodies call the status helper
on every completing path.  ONE QUALIFIER: at PATH level the two `return 2` first passes also
set no status -- correctly, because the command is incomplete and the DATA_OUT re-entry sets
it, and all three SCSI controllers re-call.  My return enumeration was exact.

*** WHY `return 0` IS WORSE THAN A SKETCH -- three consumers, each read: ***
  * **`dev_osiop.c:500-505`** -- `res == 0` sets **`d->scripts_running = 0`**.  A guest
    probing one unsupported opcode **kills its own SCRIPTS engine**; no status phase ever.
  * **`dev_asc.c:1395-1400`** -- `ok == 0` gives `STATE_DISCONNECTED` + `NCRINTR_DIS`.  The
    guest sees a target DISCONNECT instead of CHECK CONDITION: retry/reset instead of
    REQUEST SENSE.  **This also refutes the row's own state_note, which says asc does not
    test for 0 at all** -- its select path does.
  * **`dev_wdc.c:1528-1541`** -- the `res == 0` arm sets **no error bit**, and `status_byte()`
    raises `WDCS_ERR` only from `d->error`.  So on wdc, `return 0` is guest-INDISTINGUISHABLE
    from success-with-no-data.

> **`return 0` helps no consumer and harms two.**  That is a stronger refutation than my
> structural one, and it is the form a future round should cite.

**THE FIX, WITH ITS WARRANT:** CHECK-CONDITION-then-`return 1` is ALREADY this file's refusal
idiom at four shipped sites, and all four controllers demonstrably handle it today.  `d` is
non-NULL in the default arm (the NULL path returned earlier).  #417's latch semantics come
free: REQUEST SENSE reads `d->sense_key/asc/ascq` and the next success retires them.
*The state_note's cited precedent is the WRONG one -- that shape exists only because `d` is
NULL there and `check_condition` would dereference it; its own comments say `// ?` and `TODO`.*

**MUST NOT BREAK:** (a) do NOT allocate `data_in` -- all three SCSI controllers pick the
DATA_IN phase off `data_in != NULL`, and status-only completion is already TEST_UNIT_READY's
shape; (b) leave the pre-switch not-connected `return 0` alone; (c) `est/` byte-identical
propagation, shared file; (d) **the fix ALSO cures `mb89352halt`'s mechanism** -- `status_len`
becomes 1, so the PH_STAT read no longer trips 'read longer than buffer?' into
`cpu->running = 0`, consistent with the standing ONE-ROUND-for-both ruling.

*** THE ATAPI ROUTE IS REAL AND IS THE **WRONG WITNESS CHANNEL**, which inverts what I
assumed when I raised it. ***  `dev_wdc.c:1515` does feed packet commands in, and `res == 1`
with no data gives PHASE_COMPLETED and no error bit.  **But `atapi_st->status` is read
NOWHERE in dev_wdc.c** -- so an ATAPI witness stays RED after a dispatcher-only fix, because
it witnesses the COMBINED dispatcher+wdc defect.  The discriminating channels for THIS fix
are **asc** (ICCS fifo byte 0x00 -> 0x02, pmax rig) or **mb89352** (loudest pre-fix symptom
on record: the emulated CPU stops).  The wdc consumer repair is its own hunk in a different
file and should be filed separately -- the one-omission-in-one-shared-function warrant does
not stretch to it.

RANKING: raises reachability BREADTH within the band, not harm class.  Keep rank 3.  Plausible
but UNMEASURED: MMC opcodes 0x46 (GET CONFIGURATION) and 0x4A (GET EVENT STATUS NOTIFICATION)
are not among the 19 arms and period ATAPI attach code issues them routinely -- one flagged
boot would settle it.

**FILED, NOT FIXED (a sibling this round does not touch):** `SPACE`'s NESTED `default:`
`fatal()`s and then FALLS THROUGH to the status helper, **telling the guest GOOD for an
unimplemented SPACE type**.  Same false-success class, inside a KNOWN arm rather than the
default one, so b120u's fix does not reach it.  b120r-shaped.

rows.state_note:
[2026-10-22] CARRIES the external-fixes research's T9 (regress/artifacts/research_20261022/TRIAGE.md T9; regress/artifacts/research_20261022/adj_20261022/ADJ_RULINGS.md B: not re-filed): WRITE AND VERIFY(10) falls into this row's default arm, so where a controller reports GOOD its data is never written; VERIFY(10) and RESERVE/RELEASE(6/10) are GOOD by accident (report rows A5-20, A5-21, A5-42; rs6000 75010de, https://github.com/prozacchiwawa/gxemul-rs6000-860/commit/75010dedf93747f1c6391430688971a922400418; NetBSD PR pkg/54114, https://gnats.netbsd.org/54114, quotes the SPC answer: CHECK CONDITION, ILLEGAL REQUEST, ASC 0x20).  The per-controller outcomes are this row's own record.  ||  *** L4 WRONG RECORD, CORRECTED IN PLACE 2026-08-27. An adversarial opus pass REFUTED THE MECHANISM THIS ROW STATED BELOW. The defect is real; my explanation of it was false, and the true picture is four different wrong outcomes rather than one. ***

**WHAT I GOT WRONG.** I wrote that `scsi_transfer_alloc()`'s `memset(p, 0, ...)` leaves a status BYTE of 0x00, which the guest reads as GOOD. **`status` is `unsigned char *` (`diskimage.h:196-197`)** -- so the memset leaves `status == NULL` and `status_len == 0`. **There is no zeroed status byte anywhere.** Nothing reads a 0x00 out of that struct. The conclusion happened to hold for one controller, for an entirely different reason.

**WHAT SURVIVES, and it is the structural half:** the `default:` arm is the **only one of 25** that never calls `diskimage__return_default_status_and_message()` or `diskimage__return_check_condition()` -- verified by grepping every case/helper pair -- and it falls through to `return 1`, which the function's own header (`:263-266`) documents as the success token (`2` = expects DATA_OUT, `1` = otherwise ok, `0` = error).

*** THE HONEST STATEMENT: ONE OMISSION, FOUR DIFFERENT WRONG OUTCOMES. ***
  * **`dev_asc.c` -- guest IS told GOOD**, but via an explicit `else fifo_write(0x00)` fallback at `:1284-1292`, which `git log -S` places in the unmodified upstream 0.7.0 import, NOT a fork change. Right conclusion, wrong reason.
  * **`dev_mb89352.c` -- REFUTES the 'told success' claim outright.** `data_in == NULL` sets `phase = PH_STAT` (`:284`); the guest's PH_STAT read takes `p = status (NULL), len = 0`, trips the `read longer than buffer?` arm (`:173`) and **sets `cpu->running = 0`**. The guest is not told anything -- the emulated CPU is STOPPED. **Filed separately as [[mb89352halt]].**
  * **`dev_osiop.c:573-582`** -- `while (... && i < status_len)` with `status_len == 0` writes **no status byte at all**; the guest's destination memory keeps its prior contents.
  * **`dev_wdc.c` (ATAPI)** -- `atapi_st->status` is read nowhere in the file; `res == 1` with `data_in == NULL` gives `PHASE_COMPLETED` with `WDCS_ERR` unset: a successful packet command.

> **That is a BETTER case than the row originally made, not a weaker one** -- a single omitted completion step producing four distinct wrong behaviours across four controllers. But it is not the claim as written, and the claim as written was the one being ranked.

**A SECOND CONSEQUENCE THE ORIGINAL RECORD MISSED:** the helper also RETIRES LATCHED SENSE (the `#417` fix, `:187-188`). The `default:` arm skips that too -- so an unimplemented command following a failed one leaves `sense_key/asc/ascq` latched, and a follow-up REQUEST SENSE attributes the OLD failure to the command that just ran. That is exactly the regression `#417` was written to remove, reachable by a different door.

**FIX SHAPE, now pinned by the in-tree idiom at `:319-327`:** call the helper, set `status[0] = 0x02` (CHECK CONDITION), then `return 0`. Note `return 0` is **distinguishable on only two of four controllers** -- osiop stops the SCRIPTS engine, wdc completes with a latched warning, while asc and mb89352 do not test for 0 at all -- so the status buffer, not the return value, is what carries the refusal.

--- the original record follows, kept so the correction is checkable ---

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, GUEST-REACHABLE, and the highest-severity bare-title row worked so far. Established by reading; the fix idiom ALREADY EXISTS in this file. ***

`src/disk/diskimage_scsicmd.c:1380-1388`, the dispatcher's `default:` arm:

```c
default:
        debug("[ UNIMPLEMENTED SCSI command 0x%02x, disk id=%i", xferp->cmd[0], id);
        // exit(1);
}
debug(" ]");
return 1;
```

**Three things go wrong together:**
1. it logs through `debug()`, which is verbosity-gated and normally invisible;
2. **it never calls `diskimage__return_default_status_and_message()`** -- every implemented arm does (`:1212`, `:1257`, `:1298`, `:1340`, `:1347`, `:1376`);
3. it falls through to **`return 1`, the same value a SUCCESSFUL command returns.**

**And the status the guest reads is GOOD, which was checked rather than assumed:** `scsi_transfer_alloc()` ends with `memset(p, 0, sizeof(struct scsi_transfer))` (`diskimage_scsicmd.c:89`), and `dev_asc.c:326-330` frees and reallocates per command. Status 0x00 IS GOOD. **So an unsupported opcode is reported to the guest as a completed, successful command.**

*** THE COMMENTED-OUT `exit(1)` IS THE TELL. *** This site was de-fatalised by commenting out the kill, which removed the death without adding an error path -- the incomplete form of the de-fatalisation this fork otherwise does carefully.

*** THE FIX HAS A TRANSFERRED WARRANT ALREADY IN THIS FILE, found by grepping the tree for the existing idiom rather than reasoning from scratch. *** `diskimage__return_check_condition()` is defined at `:208` and already used for exactly this class at `:823-824` -- `0x05, 0x21`, ILLEGAL REQUEST -- and again at `:909`. **The correct refusal for an unknown opcode is CHECK CONDITION with ILLEGAL REQUEST / INVALID COMMAND OPERATION CODE, and the helper to do it sits three hundred lines above the defect.**

**NOT FIXED: needs a build.** The detector must show the pre-fix build reporting GOOD for an unsupported opcode and CHECK CONDITION after -- and floor clause (b) needs the `return 1` reinstated verbatim. Both are measurements. Queued behind the embargo.

rows.title: n3  footbridge timer: a guest load value of 0 makes the host loop not stop (panel discovery)
rows.hold: R9 - timer round B with n5, after round A

closure.note: Statement of record: a guest write of 0 to a timer load register yields an infinite rate, a zero interval and a signal-handler loop that never advances - and the same state reaches random() %% 0 (measured SIGFPE, the host dies); the two race. The prescaler shift of the RESET-DEFAULT load is signed-overflow UB, reachable by writing CONTROL before LOAD. CONFIRMED, all three states measured. *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: THE TITLE'S PREMISE IS MIS-STATED AND THE UNDERLYING DEFECT IS REAL AND WORSE THAN EITHER THE TITLE OR THE SEAT DESCRIBED. It is a MISSING `else`. ***

The title blames *wrap-around*. A farmed seat checked that premise -- as the brief asked -- and refuted it: ordinary periodic wrap is handled. **But it confirmed the mechanism, and reading the code shows a sharper defect than the one it named.**

`src/cpus/cpu_mips_coproc.c:796-819`:

```c
int32_t compare_diff = tmp - cp->reg[COP0_COMPARE];
double hz;

if (compare_diff < 0)
        hz = tmp - cp->reg[COP0_COUNT];        /* (A) */

if (compare_diff == 0)                         /* SEPARATE statement */
        hz = 0;                                /* (B) */
else
        hz = (double)emulated_hz / (double)compare_diff;   /* (C) */
```

**(A) IS AN UNCONDITIONALLY DEAD STORE.** The `if/else` at (B)/(C) is a separate statement, and both its arms assign `hz` -- so whatever (A) wrote is always overwritten. When `compare_diff < 0`, (C) runs and yields a **NEGATIVE** `hz`; `if (hz > 0)` at `:812` is then false and **the timer is neither created nor updated**.

**The three cases, exhaustively:**
  * `compare_diff > 0` -- (C) gives a positive rate; timer set. **The only working path.**
  * `compare_diff == 0` -- (B) gives 0; `hz > 0` false; nothing set.
  * `compare_diff < 0` -- (A) computed the intended value and (C) throws it away for a negative one; `hz > 0` false; nothing set.

**Consequence, which is what the title was reaching for:** if the timer was never created it stays NULL, so **no timer interrupt is ever delivered again**; if it already existed it keeps its stale rate. Either way a guest write that ought to reprogram the timer silently does nothing.

*** THE DEAD STORE IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, because it shows INTENT. *** The author wrote handling for `compare_diff < 0` and it has never executed. This is not a design choice being second-guessed -- it is a chain of `if`s that lost its `else`, and (A) is the evidence.

**REACHABILITY -- PARTLY SETTLED, and the unsettled half is recorded as unsettled rather than asserted.** The gate is `emulated_hz > 0` at `:797`; **21 assignments to `emulated_hz` exist across the tree.**
  * **arc: DORMANT, verified here** -- `machine_arc.c` contains ZERO `emulated_hz` assignments, so the gate cannot pass.
  * **pmax: OPEN.** It DOES set `emulated_hz` (`machine_pmax.c:96`, `:160`), so the `:797` gate passes. The seat argued pmax is nonetheless dormant because its default R3000 is `EXC3K`, citing `cpu_dyntrans.c` -- **a file not read here, so this is recorded as the seat's claim, not as verified.** Settle it before ranking this row.
  * the seat named `algor` (RM5200/EXC4K, `machine_algor.c:49`) as directly reachable. Also unverified here.

**Observable for a detector:** guest-visible timer interrupt delivery -- `Cause.IP7`. Broken: no assertion at all after a write with `compare_diff <= 0`, or delivery stuck at the stale cadence. Fixed: the newly programmed cadence.

**Related:** see `dfreq`, whose closure text also concerns the MIPS compare write converting a distance-to-deadline into a frequency. **Check for overlap before opening a round on either** -- a queue id covering two defects is how one gets buried when the other closes.

**THE CLAIM IS TRUE, and the asymmetry is unmistakable rather than arguable.** `diskimage_add()` (`src/disk/diskimage.c:1631-2104`) links the new disk into the chain at `:1822-1830`. **Six `return -1` exits sit AFTER that link** -- `:1964`, `:1980`, `:1991`, `:2074`, `:2088`, `:2099` -- and not one of them unlinks `d`. The most reachable is the plain `fopen` failure at `:1984-1991`: a disk whose file cannot be opened is left on `machine->first_diskimage` with `d->f == NULL`.

**What makes it clearly unintended rather than a design choice: the PRE-link failures clean up correctly.** `:1803` does `free(d)` before the link exists. So the function frees on early failure and leaks-onto-the-list on late failure -- the split falling exactly at the link point, which is the signature of checks added after the link rather than of a decision.

*** BUT IT IS NOT OBSERVABLE, AND THE CENSUS IS COMPLETE RATHER THAN SAMPLED. *** `grep -rnw diskimage_add` over `src/` returns **8 references, of which exactly TWO are calls**:
  * `main.c:707` -- on `< 0` prints `Aborting.` and `return 1` (`:708-709`), with NO disk cleanup between;
  * `emul_parse.c:558` -- on `< 0` calls **`exit(1)`** (`:561`).
**Both terminate the process immediately.** There is no debugger or runtime path that adds a disk to a live machine (0 hits in `src/core/debugger*.c`), so the stale entry cannot outlive the call.

**The one second-order route was checked and is also closed:** a shutdown walker would dereference the half-built entry (`d->f == NULL`). `atexit` appears **once** in the whole tree -- `emul.c:913`, `atexit(fix_console)` -- which restores terminal state and never touches the disk chain. *That check is the reason this is recorded as latent rather than as a possible NULL dereference at exit.*

**DISPOSITION: TRUE, LATENT, NOT FIXED.** Unlinking on the late failures is a few lines and would be tidier, but the addition licence wants a measured delta or a transferred warrant and there is neither: the entry is unreachable by construction, so no row could redden on it and no detector could be built that is not vacuous. **It becomes live the moment any caller survives a failed add** -- that is the trigger to re-open this, and it is the thing to check in any round that adds a runtime disk-attach path.

entries.note: *** REFUTED THE AUTHOR'S OWN DUPLICATE SUSPICION, with the code. *** The shipped work (#281/#283/#286, #263) is DATA_OUT transfer counts in HBA registers; this is a DIFFERENT LAYER AND THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION -- length fields embedded in the DATA_IN payload, which no HBA clamps. MODE SENSE: `retlen += 100` (:589) sizes the buffer (:596), then :599 restores data_in_len but NOT retlen, so :607 `data_in[0] = retlen` reports asked+100. A prior capture (_scratchpad/s1_asc.txt) shows a guest asking 32 and receiving 32 while the reported MODE DATA LENGTH is 132; allocation length 156 wraps the field to 0. * TRAFFIC: pmax/OpenBSD 2.2 (old-style rz driver) issues ZERO MODE SENSE across a full multiuser boot plus disklabel, mount and raw dd -- a clean negative. arc/OpenBSD 2.2 issues 5x MODE SENSE(6) page 4: asked 32, got 32, TOLD 132, true 36. That reproduces the brief's capture exactly. luna88k/OpenBSD 7.7 issues 11x across pages 0/4/8: asked 254, got 254, TOLD 98.
* *** THE WRAP IS ALREADY EXERCISED IN NORMAL OPERATION: luna88k asks 254, so 254+100=354 WRAPS to 98. *** It merely lands on a value the guest tolerates. Measured sweep: reported==0 at exactly alloc==156, and reported < true-1 for alloc in [156,190]. No rig asks 156, so the defect is ONE allocation-length change away from the arm-C behaviour below, not a hypothetical.
* THE CHANNEL IS LIVE, proved by a POSITIVE CONTROL rather than assumed: sending cyl=1234/heads=9 changes arc's attach line from '2081 cyl, 16 head, 63 sec' to '1234 cyl, 9 head, 188 sec'. The response body IS consumed.
* AND IT REFUTED ITS OWN DRAFT: it had written that a page-4 rpm change proves consumption; arm D showed disklabel still printed 3600 because that value comes from the ON-DISK LABEL, not from MODE SENSE. The control killed its own claim before it shipped.
* HARM, MEASURED: luna88k told-98 vs told-35/11 produce ORDERED TRANSCRIPTS IDENTICAL, 0 diff lines across 97 lines each. But told-0 FLIPS CONTROL FLOW -- 32 MODE SENSE instead of 11, including MODE SENSE(10) fallbacks and page 5. OpenBSD 7.7 branches on this byte. So 98 and 132 sit in a tolerated 'nonzero and >= true' region; 0 does not.
* *** THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG: `retlen -= 100` writes the ALLOCATION LENGTH. *** The spec wants true_len-1, measured as 11/23/35/35/43 for pages 0/1/3/4/5 -- the allocation length is correct only by coincidence at alloc==191. The true value is not known at :607 because the page is written later at :630+, so the write must MOVE AFTER the pagecode switch.
* BLAST RADIUS: nothing reads retlen after :607 (next use :746 is an assignment in the READ case), and data_in[0] is read NOWHERE outside diskimage_scsicmd.c across all of src/ -- every HBA sizes from data_in_len, so the guest is the only consumer. No overflow: max write is q+29 = 45 against a >=100-byte buffer.
* DETECTOR built and feasible offline. TWO DESIGN POINTS THAT MATTER: the rows MUST SPAN PAGES {0,1,3,4,5}, because every page-4 case has true_len 36 and a mutant hardcoding 35 would pass a page-4-only test; and an INVARIANCE row -- the reported length must not vary with the allocation length -- NAMES THE DEFECT RATHER THAN A VALUE, so a '+100 -> +0' half-fix cannot pass it. -ffunction-sections/-Wl,--gc-sections is required or mymkstemp/debug_indentation fail to link.
* ADJACENT, measured en route: MODE SENSE(10) writes the 6-BYTE header layout, so a conformant guest parses block_desc_len=0 while 8 real descriptor bytes sit at offset 8 -- STRICTLY WORSE than b120r, and unreached today only because no rig issues MS10. And data_in_len is set to the FULL allocation length even when far less data exists (alloc 255 -> 255 bytes, 219 of them zeros) where a real drive transfers 36, which affects residual logic.
* HONEST UNKNOWN, stated by the seat: three guests measured, ALL OpenBSD. Whether a NetBSD/Ultrix/Linux driver asks an allocation length in [156,190] was not measured.
* It also caught a citation error of mine: REQUEST SENSE forcing is :964-967, not the :957-960 my brief claimed. Verified and corrected above.  [agent b120r 2026-08-19]

PASS 1 MEASURE SEAT -- built a private tree, BOOTED THE RIG, and refuted three of my own measurements.
* REACHABILITY, MEASURED POSITIVE, so this is a FIX not a document: instrumented the SCSI dispatch and booted luna88k UNMODIFIED to login:. The guest issues SYNCHRONIZE CACHE (0x35) ONCE, immediately after the log line '/dev/sd0a: MARKING FILE SYSTEM CLEAN' -- the exact moment the command exists for, and the worst moment to lose a write tail. pmax runs OpenBSD 2.2 whose scsi/ contains no 0x35 at all; landisk is ATA, not SCSI.
* THE DETECTOR IT BUILT AND THEN ATTACKED: 34 rows, 17 fail on shipping code, 0 with the fix, identical at -O0 and -O2, 0 faults. THREE OF ITS FOUR ATTACKS DEFEATED IT: nblk 4->16 (ONE DIGIT -- one whole buffer flushes completely), exit() instead of _exit(), and the one my brief did not list -- ONE MORE SCSI READ AFTER THE SYNC, whose my_fseek flushes the pending write. Any realistic-looking test that does anything at all after the sync is silently green.
* THE VACUITY CLASS THAT WOULD HAVE SUNK THE ROUND: run the same binary with its workdir on /mnt/c (drvfs, st_blksize=512 -- where _scratchpad, _images and BOTH RIGS live) and EVERY byte row passes with the defect fully present, because each 512-byte fwrite reaches the kernel immediately. Its [VACUITY CONTROL] row fires and declares the section meaningless. The --wrap=fsync/fflush call-recording rows stay red on drvfs -- filesystem-independent, and the ONLY rows that can see defect (b) at all.
* Q1 NO do_fsync GATE, with costs: dirty fflush+fsync 5.85 ms ext4, clean 0.56 ms. The flood surface ALREADY SHIPS (the handler fsyncs unconditionally today); the fix makes it at most ~3x, synchronous and single-threaded, so a guest cannot get asynchronous amplification. Not the cflood shape -- there the cost is a diagnostic, here the cost IS the semantics.
* Q2 YES, same class as #286, and #416/#417 already settled the harder half: :907-910 already returns MEDIUM ERROR for HOST-side failures, and #417 tested it against a real errno (RLIMIT_FSIZE -> EFBIG). Honest UNKNOWN: Linux >=4.13 reports an fsync failure ONCE and drops the dirty pages, so a LATER sync returns success after data was already lost.
* Q3 DO NOT sync d->f under overlays, and it is worse than pointless: diskimage.c:1984 opens d->f in mode r whenever prefix_R is set while :1971 sets writable=1, so R: -- WHAT BOTH RIGS USE -- gives a writable disk whose base handle is READ-ONLY, and the temp overlay is already unlinked. fflush on a read-mode stream is UB in C99 7.21.5.2p2; fsync on O_RDONLY is rc=0 on glibc but UNKNOWN on NetBSD/OpenBSD/Solaris, where it would turn every R:/CD-ROM sync into a spurious MEDIUM ERROR. Plus 14.34 ms to fsync a 512 MB untouched file on drvfs.
* Q5 ONE COMMAND: luna88k issued START STOP UNIT 5x, ALL with cmd[4]=0x01 (START, no LOEJ, no STOP). The durability-adjacent case was never observed.
* ADVERSARIAL -- THREE DEFECTS IN MY PROPOSED FUNCTION, one measured into silent corruption: (i) int ok = 1 returns SUCCESS for a disk with nothing open, losing the #134 diagnostic; (ii) THE ORDERING HOLE -- it sets ok=0 on a failed overlay-data fsync AND THEN FSYNCS THE BITMAP ANYWAY, publishing 'the overlay owns block N' while N's bytes are not durable. It BUILT that state and drove the shipping read path: the guest reads 0x00 from the overlay's HOLE and the base's good 0xBB bytes are GONE -- silent corruption of data the guest never touched, reported as a successful read. It does NOT fall through to the base. Honest counterweight: NOT reproducible in the current write path (BIT_SET_BUT_DATA_MISSING=0 across n=1..129; the per-block fseeks keep them in lockstep), so it is a hole the FIX would INTRODUCE, not a live defect; (iii) directory-entry durability CHECKED AND NOT A HOLE -- user overlays open r+ and must pre-exist, and the only created file is the unlinked temp overlay. An honest negative.
* Also found: there is NO fclose of d->f or the overlays at shutdown anywhere. A clean exit() flushes stdio so a normal quit is safe, but a SIGKILLed emulator loses the tail regardless.
* ITS OWN ERROR, reported rather than dropped: its first detector left c.nblk UNINITIALIZED, so every overlay row went red -- AGREEING WITH ITS HYPOTHESIS -- and at -O2 malloc(512*garbage) SIGSEGVd into 4 FAULTS it nearly reported as an overlay-path defect. Its own words: a red row that confirms your hypothesis is the dangerous kind.  [panel_20260817_215052]

*** NAMED A MEASUREMENT NOBODY HAD RUN AND TOLD ME TO RUN IT BEFORE WRITING THE CHANGELOG SENTENCE: an fflush-ONLY (no fsync) arm. Its words: 'If that arm persists after _exit, the kill-and-check row is not an fsync test.' I RAN IT AND IT WAS RIGHT. *** MEASURED, one 512-byte write: fflush only -> 512 bytes DURABLE to a separate reader; fsync only (what ships today) -> 0. So _exit() simulates PROCESS death, not host death -- the page cache belongs to the KERNEL and outlives the process -- and a kill-and-check test therefore measures the missing FFLUSH, never the missing FSYNC. This SPLITS THE DEFECT: (a) missing fflush is byte-testable and bounded; (b) overlays never fsynced at all is NOT byte-testable by ANY process-kill test, needs the --wrap rows, and is unbounded on real power loss. It also placed the detector correctly (beside diff_diskimage_io.c, NOT on the #411 write-fail fixtures) and filed six things explicitly NOT to do this round.  [panel_20260817_215052]
GO-WITH-CHANGES. diskimage_sync() with fflush+fsync covering overlays and base, propagate CHECK CONDITION on sync failure, and keep scope bounded to SYNCHRONIZE CACHE.  [panel_20260817_215052]

GO-WITH-CHANGES with two REQUIRED changes: (1) the handler must report sync failure as CHECK CONDITION -- Q2 = yes, same class as #286; (2) the detector needs both a no-fix and a with-fix arm, or it cannot show it can fail.  [panel_20260817_215052]

PASS 2 ON THE DIFF, AND IT KILLED MY DETECTOR. Verdict SHIP-WITH-CHANGES.
* *** THE DETECTOR WAS STILL VACUOUS: --wrap counted HOW MANY calls and never WHICH FILE, so FOUR mutants that restore real data loss all passed green *** -- v1 rename f_bitmap to f_data (bitmap NEVER synced), v2 invert the data/bitmap order (the rule the code itself calls load-bearing), v3 delete the ordering continue, v4 sync d->f instead of the bitmap. Every one keeps the totals at 2 and 2. Smallest defeating edit: v1, ONE identifier. And the row NAMES overclaimed -- 'fflushes data and bitmap' passed with the bitmap untouched, and the gate grepped those exact names as its evidence.
* *** AND THE FIXTURE HAD NEVER WRITTEN A BYTE. *** SCSICMD_WRITE is 0x0a = WRITE(6) driven with a 10-byte CDB, so the length parsed as 256 blocks; and the handler requires data_out_offset == size, which the fixture never set. Both overlay files were 0 bytes after every run -- corroborated by identical 0-byte leftovers already in the repo from an earlier run. THAT is why the file-blind mutants lived: with nothing written there is no durability property to check, only call counts.
* Q1 THE `continue` IS RIGHT -- it tried and could not build a state where skipping is worse; a stale bitmap makes a read fall through to the base (stale but real) rather than to the overlay's hole (zeros). TWO CORRECTIONS AROUND IT: the comment overclaims, because after 4 writes with NO sync an independent reader already sees bitmap[0]=0x07 -- the per-block fseeks already pushed both to the page cache, so the continue declines to FORCE publication rather than preventing it; and a multi-overlay disk reports CHECK CONDITION when a non-last overlay's fsync fails even though every guest byte is durable.
* ADVERSARIAL: THE DURABILITY CLAIM IS FALSE UNDER R:. diskimage_add_overlay(d, tmpname, true) unlinks BOTH overlay files right after opening (:177-184; measured fstat().st_nlink == 0), so they are anonymous temporaries no post-crash reader can open. Not introduced by the diff -- R: is meant to be ephemeral -- but the new comment presents R: as the motivating case, which it should not.
* Q2 safe for luna88k (d == NULL returns before the switch, so CHECK CONDITION needs #134's NULL d->f or a real error). But it MEASURED an exposure the diff introduced: for r:/CD-ROM the new FLAT branch fflushes and fsyncs a handle opened "r" -- precisely what the function's own comment says it avoids. *** ADJUDICATED 2026-08-27 (fable): the collapse onto [[b120]] is CONFIRMED **MEASURED**, but it is a collapse of the SAFETY HALF ONLY -- do NOT read it as 'drop ovsync'. ***

b120's fix makes opcode 0x91 an honest CHECK CONDITION. **It does not implement SYNCHRONIZE CACHE(16), so it does not make the flush happen.** That residual -- implement 0x91, or formally decline it -- is NOT covered by b120 and is what this row should carry from now on.

So: keep this row OPEN and NARROWED to the implement-or-decline question. The false-success danger is b120's; the missing flush is this row's.

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, BUT NARROWER THAN THE TITLE -- and the live half turns out to be AN INSTANCE OF [[b120]], which neither row could show on its own. ***

**HALF THAT IS ALREADY FIXED:** SYNCHRONIZE CACHE(10) is `SCSICMD_SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE = 0x35` (`diskimage.h:254`), handled at `diskimage_scsicmd.c:915`, and it **does** flush -- `:932` calls `diskimage_sync(d)`, with `:925` recording that this was the TODO carried out. *So the title, read as covering all synchronize-cache commands, is FALSE for the one the tree implements.*

*** THE LIVE HALF, AND ITS DIAGNOSIS: SYNCHRONIZE CACHE(16) IS OPCODE `0x91`, AND `0x91` APPEARS **ZERO** TIMES IN THE DISPATCHER. *** It therefore falls into the `default:` arm at `:1380` -- which logs through a verbosity-gated call, never sets a status, and returns the same value a successful command returns. **The guest asks for a cache flush, is told GOOD, and nothing is flushed.**

> **SO THIS IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT DEFECT: IT IS [[b120]] WEARING A SPECIFIC OPCODE.** `b120`'s fix -- refuse an unknown opcode with CHECK CONDITION / ILLEGAL REQUEST via the existing `diskimage__return_check_condition()` helper -- would convert this from a SILENT FALSE SUCCESS into an honest refusal, letting a guest fall back to CACHE(10). **A full `ovsync` fix additionally implements `0x91`**; the two are separable and should be ranked separately.

**Rank `b120` first.** It is the general case, it is cheaper, and it makes this row's damage visible instead of silent. Implementing `0x91` without fixing `b120` would close one opcode and leave every other unimplemented one lying about success.

*Method note: the seat reported the CACHE(10)/CACHE(16) split and the existing `diskimage_sync()` idiom; the `0x91`-falls-to-default connection was found here by grepping the dispatcher for the opcode and getting zero hits. **A count of zero was the whole finding** -- and it is only evidence because the denominator was checked: the file really does dispatch by opcode, and `0x35` is present in the same census.*



**RESIDUAL-REMAINS.**  `4d0981d` fixed CACHE(10) -- data and bitmap now get ordered flush/sync with
failure reporting.  **CACHE(16) is still unimplemented** and falls through the generic default,
which neither flushes nor explicitly refuses it.

*And a founding overstatement corrected: the row asserted the base was ALREADY flushed pre-fix.  It
used `fsync()` without the stdio `fflush()`, which is not the same claim.*

Its cited `dev_footbridge.c:548` is stale: :548 is `console_putchar` and the timer mask is at :640. **So a witness WAS built, and it witnesses a different path from the one this row's closure defines.** THE MIPS MECHANISM IS SOURCE-DEMONSTRABLE AND WORSE THAN 'a different internal representation': a Compare write installs a PERIODIC host timer (`cpu_mips_coproc.c:796`), every expiry increments `compare_interrupts_pending` (:418), and a guest Compare write acknowledges only ONE pending event while clearing Cause.IP7 (:822). If two or more callbacks have accumulated, the next dyntrans update re-asserts IP7 before any new Count==Compare event -- **a wrong guest-readable Cause value and an extra interrupt exception**, not an observationally equivalent model. IT ALSO KEPT THE EVIDENCE LADDER HONEST: the ~615,384-callbacks-per-signal figure came from a timer-core SCRATCH probe, not an end-to-end MIPS guest observation; and the 40.2-second guest clock freeze that was measured belongs to the separate `fbpending` overflow defect, whose #442 bound is in today's source. Neither witnesses MIPS `dfreq`. *** CONSEQUENCE ACTED ON: CLAUDE.md's line 'dfreq's [no-witness claim] was measured false by building the witness in one session' is a WRONG RECORD and was corrected in both carrier copies. The RULE -- that 'no witness of either kind' is checkable and must be checked -- is untouched and remains one of the most useful lines in the file. ***

VERDICT DOCUMENT-ONLY.  The cited witness (footbridge_sites_probe.py, -E cats, SA110) observes readback, not MIPS Compare timing -- it does not reproduce dfreq.  But the source supports a guest-visible fidelity defect: the periodic callback increments compare_interrupts_pending, and a Compare write only decrements it, so the non-EXC3K dyntrans path can re-assert IP7 without a Count/Compare crossing (conditional source reasoning, unmeasured).  Proposed record: 'MIPS timer fidelity defect supported by source; matching guest witness outstanding'.

rows.title: hlen  Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit)
rows.hold: census done; promote to a FIX round?

closure.note: Opened from the b75 refutation, then characterized by census. A device handler that switches on the address and cannot service a width will read or write only the first register of an 8-byte access. MEASURED SCOPE: 62 spanning-capable handlers of 167 registered; 20 on machines this project boots. TWO BOOTED MACHINES ARE PROVABLY IMMUNE - SH-4 has no 8-byte access at all (fmov.d is two 4-byte accesses) and MIPS32/R3000A treats LD/SD as reserved, so landisk and pmax cannot produce the access. NO CONVENTION EXISTS in the tree: no helper, no macro, no rule - only three hand-rolled decompositions that are all big-endian-specific and that disagree with each other about the else branch, so there is no single idiom to copy. FIRST WITNESS NAMED: dev_irqc on testarm, the only spanning-capable device on that machine, where the two halves of one aligned 8-byte access have OPPOSITE legal directions (status is read-only, mask is write-only), which makes the miss unambiguous. DETECTOR SHAPE: an offline differential in the diff_*.c family - no boot, no rig, no serialization.

entries.note: CENSUS: 118 files, 62 spanning-capable handlers, 20 on booted machines. Coverage PROVED by set-difference against the 167 registered handlers, not asserted. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT WHETHER len IS MENTIONED: 115 of 167 pass len only to memory_readmax64, which marshals bytes and does nothing about a span across two registers - so 'uses len' does not mean safe, and the naive definition undercounts the class about 15 times. Also measured: fatal() DOES NOT HALT (debugmsg.c:384 is a plain wrapper), so the 8 warn-then-service handlers are the defect with a log line.

* IT SIDESTEPPED THE `put w` WARMS / `put b` DOES NOT TRAP RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT: the slow path's own memory_rw inserts the page on its way out (memory_rw.c:732, no NO_EXCEPTIONS), so the first bdt access to a cold page is slow and every later one is fast. Running the IDENTICAL instruction twice makes the divergence a difference between two executions rather than a value that depends on trusting a seeding rule.

Thumb PUSH/POP (cpu_arm.c:1670,1677) call the same two functions; arm_pop/arm_push have exactly four callers, all enumerated.
* *** THE EXISTING GATE IS BLIND TO IT, MEASURED: arm_writeback_probe.py scores 22/22 on ALL THREE binaries including the ENTRY mutant that corrupts the writeback, and gate 14's 261 checks touch neither arm_pop nor arm_push. *** The single check separating the correct fix from the #357 trap is the W=1 writeback row.       0x00021000  00000000 44332211
    dump from an UNALIGNED start -- what `read_mem32` actually issued:
      0x00021000           44332211 00000000
                  ^^^^^^^^ the leading group is BLANK-PADDED

`read_mem32()` searched for the line labelled `(addr & ~0xF)` -- **which matches in BOTH cases** -- then indexed `line[12:48].split()` by `(addr & 0xF) // 4`.  **When the dump starts unaligned the leading groups are ABSENT and `.split()` collapses the padding, so every index shifts and `parts[idx]` silently returns a NEIGHBOURING WORD.**

    read_mem32(0x21004) -> parts == ['44332211', '00000000'], idx 1 -> 0

*This is the padded-column trap this project already records, in a new place: the label matched, so every check that looked for the right line passed, and the CONTENT came from the wrong column.*

**REPAIR: dump from `(addr & ~0xF)` for 16 bytes, so all four groups are always present -- which is what the index arithmetic already assumed.  One line.**

*** SCOPE, AND IT IS WIDER THAN THE ONE RED ROW: 8 OF 10 LEGS CHANGED VALUE WHEN THE INSTRUMENT WAS REPAIRED. ***

| leg | table 4 | table 5 |
|---|---|---|
| `BASE` | 31/32 | **32/32** |
| `HEAD` | 19/32 | **17/32** -- the pre-fix build was failing MORE rows than reported |
| `RESTORED` | 19/32 | 17/32 (= HEAD) |
| `M_ENTRY` | 26/32 | 27/32 |
| `M_MASK1` | 28/32 | 29/32 |
| `M_PBITCOND` | 30/32 | 31/32 |
| `M_POP_ONLY` | 25/32 | 23/32 |
| `M_PUSH_ONLY` | 25/32 | 26/32 |
| `M_MASK7`, `M_NULL_MEDIUM` | unchanged | unchanged |

**The defect was in the probe AS ORIGINALLY BUILT**, so it affected every `read_mem32` call at a nonzero 16-byte offset -- the STM and Thumb PUSH clobber rows -- across tables 1 through 4.  **Every number those rows produced before this table is superseded.**  *Grepped: no other probe in the tree shares the shape, so the blast radius is this round's instrument alone.*

=== THE FLOOR, NOW CLEAN ===

| clause | leg | score | killed on |
|---|---|---|---|
| -- | `BASE` | **32/32** | **nothing -- clean** |
| (a) pre-fix red | `HEAD` | 17/32 | the defect rows |
| (b) reinstatement | `RESTORED` | 17/32 | = HEAD exactly |
| (c) null medium | `M_NULL_MEDIUM` | 8/32 | 24 rows |
| **(d)** | `M_MASK1` | 29/32 | the three `P2` rows |
| **(d)** | `M_MASK7` | 30/32 | the two `BIT2` rows |
| **(d)** | `M_PBITCOND` | 31/32 | **`THUMB_PUSH_COLD_DATA_P2` alone -- the minimum** |
| de-escalation | `M_ENTRY` | 27/32 | **all five writeback rows, nothing else** |

**Every mutant dies on exactly the cells written for it, and `M_PBITCOND` on precisely one.**  *The class closure holds under a correct instrument, which is the thing table 4 could not establish.*

*A small one of mine, recorded because I spent today cataloguing this class: my own shell check for a clean BASE tested `[ -z "$B" ]`, but the probe prints `FAILING: none` when clean -- a NON-EMPTY string -- so the check took its else branch and printed 'BASE still red on: none'.  The score `32/32` is what settled it.  A check that reports the opposite of the truth on a green run is the same family as the ones I filed against other people's scripts today.*

*** 2026-09-11 PROMOTED TO regress/ AND WIRED INTO gate_arm.sh -- 32/32 AGAINST THE GATE'S OWN BINARY. ***

**This discharges the obligation the round could not previously claim.**  Fable's adjudication found that *neither of today's probes is under `regress/` proper, so 'shipped a detector with the fix' is not yet true of either round.*  For `#524` it is true now.

=== THE PROMOTION IS A COPY, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE ===
`regress/artifacts/armbdt/agy_armbdt_witness_20260911.py` **stays in place as the AS-RUN record of tables 1-5**; `regress/arm_bdt_probe.py` is the copy that evolves and that the gate executes.  *Editing the artifact copy would falsify what those tables actually measured* -- the same reason the repaired kill-table driver was written as a new file rather than over the old one.

**The promoted copy differs only by two PRINT-ONLY lines (`ARMBDT_CONTROL=`, `ARMBDT_RESULT=`, matching the gate idiom the other ARM probes use) and a header note.  Verified: the `record()` count is unchanged, so no row was added or lost in the copy.**  Its header also carries the `read_mem32` alignment warning, so the next probe copied from it does not inherit [[probereadalign]].

=== MEASURED AGAINST THE GATE'S OWN BINARY, NOT THE SCRATCH CLONE ===
`$PMAX` is `build/gxemul`.  After the propagate+rebuild, the promoted probe run directly against it returns **`SCORE 32/32`, `ARMBDT_CONTROL=OK`, `ARMBDT_RESULT=32/32`, `FAILING: none`**.  *A pre-check worth the thirty seconds: wiring the probe in BEFORE the rebuild would have run it against a pre-fix binary and produced a red gate that meant nothing about the fix.*

=== THE GATE SECTION, AND WHY THE DENOMINATOR IS A LITERAL ===
Follows `arm_writeback_probe.py`'s shape exactly: run -> `gate_skip` if no result line -> print the ok/FAIL rows -> check the control -> **`check "bdt rows run" "$bwant" 32`** -> check correct == run.

> **The denominator is pinned to a LITERAL deliberately.  The probe grew 25 -> 29 -> 32 rows across three kill tables as clause-(d) mutants were closed, and a gate that trusts the probe's own denominator cannot tell a probe that LOST rows from one that never had them.**

The section also records all five measured-dead mutants with their scores and the row family that kills each (`M_ENTRY` 27/32 writeback rows, `M_MASK1` 29/32 the `+2` rows, `M_MASK7` 30/32 the bit-2 rows, `M_PBITCOND` 31/32 Thumb PUSH `+2`, `M_NULL_MEDIUM` 8/32), **so a future reader meets the evidence at the gate rather than having to find the artifacts.**

*Targeted gate run in flight.  Nothing committed; the owner's hold stands until it is green.*

*** RANKING AND ONE REFUTED DOUBT, 2026-08-27. ***

**Ranked 6th of 8** in today's adjudication -- loud, guest-drivable host termination, placed BELOW the silent interrupt-fidelity rows, following this project's own revealed ordering (a loud-termination row already sits below a lost-interrupt row in the queue). **The adjudicator flagged this as its softest call**: a pure denial-of-service view would lift it above an INFERRED hang, since a guest reading a documented register ends the emulator process. Recorded as a flagged call, not a settled one.

*** THE ADJUDICATOR DOUBTED THE ACCEPT PREMISE ON THE GROUND THAT NO DC21285 MANUAL IS IN `_scratchpad/` -- AND THAT IS REFUTED. *** The manual is present: `dc21285.pdf` (1,059,970 bytes) and `dc21285.txt` (445,677 bytes). The statement was verified twice, from two channels:
  * Table 7-10, `dc21285.txt:6826` -- `188h    IRQEnable    IRQEnableSet`;
  * prose at `:6913-6915` -- *"**This read-only register** is used to mask the interrupt input sources... The value of this register can only be changed by writing to the EnableSet and EnableClear registers."*

> **The doubt's ROOT CAUSE is the defect this round already fixed:** the carrier's primary-sources list named about seven manuals when fifteen are present, and this datasheet was one of the six it omitted. **A seat checking that list would conclude the manual is absent.** That is the stale-inventory failure reaching one step further than expected -- it did not just stop a round finding the manual, it caused a later seat to doubt a correct finding drawn from it.

Table 7-1's access legend (`dc21285.txt:4512`) defines **R as 'Read only.  Writes have no effect.'** while WO is defined only as 'Write only.'  S7.3.29 (`:6886`) and S7.3.30 (`:6901`) confirm Status/RawStatus read-only.  **S7.3.33 (`:6937`) specifies what WRITES to EnableClear do and supplies NO READ RESULT** -- and the reserved-bit rule at `:6835` does not specify zero for a whole read of a write-only register.

| access | documented behaviour |
|---|---|
| WRITE to the four read-only registers | **no effect** |
| READ from EnableClear | **no specified result**, and no explicit 'undefined' declaration either |

**DISPOSITIONS, and they differ by ANNOUNCEMENT POLICY:** the four writes -> **DECLINE (silent)**, because the documented operation is a no-op; `+0x18c` -> **DECLINE + BOUNDED LATCHED ANNOUNCE**, disclosing the emulator's choice where the hardware result is undocumented.  *The announcement is a design recommendation, NOT a datasheet requirement, and the seat said so explicitly.*

*** THE LEAK OBLIGATION IS ENFORCED BY THE RETURNED DATA, NOT BY THE ANNOUNCEMENT: a bounded message alongside `odata = d->irq_enable` STILL FAILS. ***  At `:593` the invalid-read arm assigns `odata = d->irq_enable` BEFORE terminating, so the common read-result copy does not currently execute -- **a repair that keeps that assignment while allowing completion INTRODUCES the mask exposure.**  The proposed policy is **zero, explicitly documented as a fallback under an unknown hardware result**, using the existing `odata = 0` init at `:501` and preserving the common copy at `:754`.  *Zero is an implementation decision, not an answer obtained from the datasheet* -- and leaving the caller's buffer untouched would be an INCOMPLETE decline, which the source itself warns about for TimerClear.

=== THE ORACLE IS VACUOUS AS THE BRIEF IMAGINED IT, AND THE REASON IS MEASURABLE ===
The probe parses `r7` (`:188`) but **no row asserts its value**, and device init zeroes the state (`dev_footbridge.c:768`) while the probe BODY (`:92`) **never programs IRQEnable**.

> *** SO 'REPOINT THE READ AND ASSERT `r7 == 0`' WOULD BE VACUOUS AGAINST THE MASK-RETURNING VARIANT: ITS MASK WOULD ALSO BE ZERO.  A check that cannot fail, caught at DESIGN time. ***

**The leak row needs TWO DISTINCT, INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED NONZERO MASKS.**  The property is **INDEPENDENCE FROM THE ENABLE MASK**, not numerical inequality for every mask -- a legitimate zero fallback necessarily equals a zero mask.  And **the mask setup may NOT be checked by a guest read of `+0x188`, because that still terminates today.**  Survival, unchanged device state and announcement count **cannot detect the mask copy by themselves** -- the defect preserves all three channels, so giving one of those rows the leak's detection duty would be vacuous by construction.

**IF K1 IS REPURPOSED it must cease being a death control**: new expectation SURVIVED / exit 0 / no terminating signal, with the `ENABLE SET` matcher, the instruction description, the arm label and the gate's 'still dies' text **all changed together**.  A stale K1 fails **TWO** gate checks -- the named K1 check and the aggregate PASS check.  *Also noted: D1's stepping loop breaks on failure BEFORE checking that step's disassembly, so its zero-mismatch result does not independently validate the terminal K instruction.*

*** SCOPE: TWO ROUNDS, NOT ONE. ***  The four writes share one repair design and one detector contract (access completes, host continues, no architectural or interrupt-output change).  `+0x18c` adds the returned-data obligation -- **a repair can satisfy every completion/no-effect check and still expose the mask** -- which is what establishes the separate oracle.  A shared helper or one probe script may serve all five; it does not merge the contracts.

entries.note: *** VERDICT: THE FILE IS THE WRONG UNIT -- MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. Close as documented-only with the census as the standing answer. *** **91% IS THE KILLER:** of 118 `.c` files in src/devices/, **107 carry at least one terminating site** -- so a per-file 'stops the host' flag marks 91% of the population, because CHECK_ALLOCATION at init is near-universal (144 of 183 macro sites are INIT, and INIT is 47% of the whole tally). **A metric that flags 91% of its population ranks nothing and schedules nothing.** Only **29** files carry an ACCESS site at all, so 78 of those listed are permanently zero in the only bucket that matters. Even within ACCESS the distribution defeats per-file completeness: top 5 files are 54%, median 2, and 13 of 29 have exactly one. **THE QUEUE HAS CONFUSED THESE DENOMINATORS MORE THAN THE BRIEF ADMITTED:** it traced 114 -> 170 -> 220 -> 253/271 -> 360 across the record, with devexit's own closure note carrying two different universes in one sentence AND the warning 'RECORD THE UNIVERSE OR THE NUMBER LOOKS WRONG LATER'. The brief said 'confused once'; it is at least three times. THE THREE UNITS, and only two are needed: **FILE is a SCHEDULING unit and never a coverage denominator**; **guest-reachable ACCESS SITE (90) is the ELIGIBILITY denominator** -- with the caveat that even ACCESS contains known non-defects (dev_cons.c:80's intended exit(0), dev_ram.c:132's guest-unreachable mode), so 90 is eligibility and not a defect count; and **DE-FATALISED PREDICATE is the OBLIGATION denominator**, the only one that maps onto existing machinery (accept rows and clause (d) are both per-predicate). *** THE RECORD THE ROW ASKS FOR ALREADY EXISTS, PER-SITE, IN THE SOURCE: 51 sites across 12 files already carry a `/* #NNN: was exit(1) */` tag *** -- dev_pvr.c 25, gdrom 5, osiop 5, 8253 4, pcc2 4, and seven more. That is more precise than the per-file tally requested, written at the site, keyed by round, in the fork's own tagging ethos. Combined with `census_exits.py --by-file`, which ships and the seat ran, both halves are satisfied. BOUNDED RESIDUAL: nothing answers 'of the 90 ACCESS sites, which already carry a tag?' -- a one-flag addition (`--tagged`), discharged once, not a standing policy. CONSTRAINT ON THE PREDICATE UNIT, measured and limiting: **the latch idiom is not uniform** -- at least four spellings coexist (struct `warned_*`, function-local `static int warned`, `static int w_warned/r_warned`, and others) -- so a predicate census needs the idiom normalised first, which is separate work and must not be smuggled in.

entries.note: *** VERDICT: KEEP OPEN, ADOPT THE ANCHOR-ROW CHECK -- AND **REJECT THE CHECK THE BRIEF PROPOSED**, because it is MEASURED GREEN ON BOTH LIVE BLIND INSTANCES. *** THE COUNT, and the row's own thesis confirmed a THIRD time: **14 differentials today, 13 at the hold's own commit** (diff_fbpending_bound.c landed after). 7 -> 13 -> 14. **13 of 14 read a project `#define` in code** (comments and string literals stripped -- diff_wdc_ identify.c's apparent hits were row-name artefacts). **Only 2 of 13 carry an absolute anchor**, and both are the files a previous round already fixed. *** WHY THE PROPOSED WANT-SIDE GREP FAILS, and this is the finding: *** it built the classifier and found macros on the expectation side in only three files -- all TAG IDENTITY (DISKIMAGE_*, MACHINE_*, CMMU_FLUSH_SUPER_ALL), harmless, no external numeric truth exists. **Meanwhile the two genuinely blind files score ZERO on it:** diff_fbpending_bound.c computes its expectation into a LOCAL (`ceiling = TIMER_MAX_CATCHUP * TIMER_BASE_FREQUENCY`) and uses a `row(name, bool, ...)` idiom with **no `want` argument to grep at all** -- its header even states the absolute truth 68,157,440 and PRINTS it, while no row asserts it, a claim->row gap; and diff_sh4_tmu.c has the macro CANCEL between stimulus and oracle, so every row is invariant under any nonzero value and it appears only on the stimulus side. **5 of 14 differentials use a boolean-predicate idiom with no `want` argument -- a third of the population is structurally invisible to a want-side check, and that third contains both live instances.** THE CORRECT SHAPE IS ALREADY IN THE TREE: diff_footbridge.c drives stimulus from macros and holds expectations as literals; diff_ieee_store.c asserts bare hex. rows.title: mrwstore2  A straddling store whose tail faults makes an MMIO head see the write twice
rows.hold: *** THE OLD BLOCKING REASON IS REFUTED AND WAS AN L4 -- corrected 2026-08-26. *** It read 'the fix may itself DIVERGE from real hardware'. **A fix cannot diverge, because the behaviour is PERMITTED and never REQUIRED.** Four PowerPC manuals are now local in `_scratchpad/` (OEA Book III v2.01, VEA Book II v2.01, MPCFPE32B Rev 2 -- the 32-bit PEM covering the PPC750 this row's witness uses -- and the 2005 32/64-bit PEM), fetched and extracted with the same pdftotext used for ddi0100i.txt. PEM 3.2.2 / Book II 2.1: a misaligned store is not atomic, so it falls in the 'any other load or store instruction MAY be partially executed and then aborted... and then re-executed' bucket; 6.1.4 says 'some bytes just before the boundary may have been updated'. **So an emulator that never partially executes is conformant under every one of them -- the INTERSECTION of both readings, not a divergence from either.** *** AND THE MANUALS DISAGREE ON THE CASE THIS ROW IS ACTUALLY ABOUT, recorded as an honest UNKNOWN rather than settled by the stronger document: *** Book III v2.01 4.2.4.1 says that for an access whose first byte is Caching-Inhibited AND Guarded -- exactly the MMIO-head shape here -- a DSI means 'the portion of the storage operand that is in Caching Inhibited and Guarded storage is NOT accessed', i.e. the device write must not happen. The PEM contains no such rule and its 6.1.4 explicitly permits the head bytes to have been updated. Whether a real PPC750 suppresses the device write is NOT established. THE REASONS THAT SURVIVE and on which this row stays filed: REACHABILITY (zero straddling stores measured across three real boots) and SEVERITY (a duplicated device write -- guest-visible, no host kill, no memory-safety consequence; both PowerPC and ARM put the burden on software). *** SCOPE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE BLOCKER: 'memory_rw is the choke point' is FALSE FOR THE CLASS. *** stmw/stswi/lmw/lswi and ARM's bdt_store each loop and return on the first failing element, so they have the identical partial-completion-across-a-fault property at the INSTRUCTION level, entirely outside memory_rw -- and PEM 6.1.4's first bullet is about exactly those. **A memory_rw fix would be a partial fix that reads as a complete one**, which is the argument for filing this properly rather than shipping a round a future reader mistakes for closure. TWO SIDE-EFFECT CAUTIONS FROM A PRIOR SEAT MEASURED ABSENT IN THIS TREE: FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS returns before every SPR write and before ppc_exception(), and there is NO R/C writeback on PPC at all -- so the recorded warning about PPC603 software reload describes hazards that do not exist here. FILED SEPARATELY, all from the same reading: `X(stvx)` does a raw 16-byte memory_rw with no `EA & ~0xF` mask (a second straddling producer, and a divergence in its own right); diff_memory_rw.c has a coverage hole exactly at this row's shape (device head + FAULTING tail); and memory_ppc.c:302-305 is an unlatched guest-drivable fatal(), one per translation fault -- the floodclass shape #464 just closed six of.

entries.note: From R5 pass 2. The first chunk is written, the second faults, the instruction restarts -- so a device at the head of the access sees the store twice. The differential's E4 comment records the READ side of partial completion honestly; this is the store side, and it is the one with a visible consequence. The memblock split has had this property all along, but the page split fires 256x more often.

*** REPRODUCED AT RUNG 3 -- AND THREE OF THIS ROW'S CLAIMS ARE MEASURED FALSE. ***  The defect is real; the severity argument that put it top of a cluster is not.

THE WITNESS: unmodified in-tree `testppc` (-E testppc -C PPC750 -M 32), cold debugger, real guest instructions, real decode, real memory_rw. A PPC guest sets DBAT0 over a 128 KB window, sets MSR[DR]=1, and executes `stw r6,0(r5)` with r5 = 0x1201fffe -- unaligned, crossing the 1 KB split granule. Head (2 bytes) reaches the in-tree `fb` device; tail (2 bytes) has no BAT and no PTE, so a real DSI fires; a planted `rfi` at the DSI vector is the GUEST'S OWN restart. The same instruction re-executes, unbounded. Counters: one architectural store, FOUR device writes. **The trace is from a fully stock HEAD binary with zero instrumentation** -- the counters only counted. Controls all green: liveness (RAM through the same decode), DEVICE SIGNATURE (same program, only DBAT0L changed: PA->device reads back 0x3344, PA->no device reads back 0x0000), and a negative control two bytes lower that does not split.

CLAIM 1 -- 'not introduced by #430' -- MEASURED FALSE. Built from `git show 2458cfb^:src/cpus/memory_rw.c`, stock otherwise: the same guest program produces NO exception, NO restart, ONE device write. Pre-#430 the tail was silently mis-applied to the physically-following location -- the defect #430 fixed -- so there was nothing to restart. **#430 CREATED the fault, and the double-application is a direct consequence of it.**

CLAIM 2 -- 'the memblock split has had this property all along' -- MEASURED FALSE, twice. Post-#430 the memblock split can only fire on PHYSICAL accesses (a translated 4 KB write across 1 MB costs 4 translations / 4 host lookups; PHYSICAL costs 0 / 2), and its head can NEVER be a device in either version because device dispatch `goto do_return_ok`s first -- measured with a device straddling the memblock boundary.

CLAIM 3 -- '256x' -- MEASURED WRONG: it is **1024x**. The granule was measured by walking offsets, not read: MRW_SPLIT_MASK is 0x3ff, so 1 MB / 1024 = 1024. The 256 came from comparing 1 MB to a 4 KB page -- the granule this split does not use. *** THE SAME WRONG NUMBER WAS ALSO IN THE SOURCE, at memory_rw.c's own 'one boundary in 256' comment: ONE mis-derived constant became TWO records defects, and the row repeated it as a severity argument. Both corrected. ***

REACHABILITY IS FAR NARROWER THAN THE ROW IMPLIES, and this is why it re-ranks DOWN:
  * ONLY PowerPC can emit a straddling store at all. MIPS (AdES; swl/swr do an ALIGNED RMW), ARM, SH, M88K and Alpha all force alignment -- each checked in source. PPC's `if (addr & (LS_SIZE-1))` at cpu_ppc_instr_loadstore.c:229 is a FAST-PATH BAIL-OUT, not an exception, so the generic path passes the unaligned address through.
  * PPC is also the ONLY family whose device-failure path can restart: memory_rw's device-failure arm raises an exception only under #ifdef MEM_MIPS / #ifdef MEM_M88K.
  * THREE REAL GUEST BOOTS, instrumented: OpenBSD/pmax to root login, OpenBSD/luna88k to `login:`, NetBSD/macppc to the root-device prompt -- **ZERO straddling stores from guest code**. The seat first read macppc's 95 split-loop writes as guest activity and REFUTED ITSELF by logging the addresses: all are len=65536 at pc=0x0, i.e. file_elf.c:448's loader chunks running before any guest instruction.
  * Of the 1024 offsets in a granule only ELEVEN (0x3f9..0x3ff) can start a straddling 2/4/8-byte access, and the head's device offset is always within 7 bytes BELOW a 1 KB boundary -- so a register at offset 0x00/0x10/0x20 can never be a straddle head.

*** AND THE FIX MAY ITSELF BE WRONG. ***  Partial completion on a page-crossing misaligned store, with restart re-applying the first part, is what real PowerPC hardware does -- so gxemul may be CORRECT here and a fix may introduce a divergence. There is no PowerPC manual in _scratchpad/ (ARM, MIPS and m88k only), so the seat stated that as REASONING, NOT A CITATION -- the same trap CLAUDE.md records for SH. **Obtain a PPC manual before any edit.**

The minimal fix, if one is wanted: a dry-run pre-pass on WRITES only, walking the chunks with FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS and committing only if all translate. Zero cost on the hot path -- it sits inside the `while (len > granule - offset)` body, which no aligned access enters. Watch TLB-miss handlers with side effects (PPC603 software reload) and do not let the dry run update referenced/changed bits.

rows.hold_question: A straddling store whose tail faults makes an MMIO head see the write twice. The row was REPRODUCED at rung 3 and then RE-RANKED DOWN -- three of its factual claims were measured false, it is PPC-only, no in-tree guest reaches it, and the fix may itself DIVERGE from real hardware. *** L4 CORRECTION 2026-08-27: MY OBSERVABLE IS WRONG AND MY RANKING WAS TOO HIGH. The mature ledger entry already measured three of this row's claims FALSE, and I did not read it before writing a fresh note on top. ***

**THE OBSERVABLE IS NOT 'TWO WHEN BROKEN, ONE WHEN FIXED'.** It is **1 -> 4+ writes**. My two-versus-one framing was a guess at the shape of a count, not the measured count.

**THREE CLAIMS ALREADY MEASURED FALSE in this row's own history**, which I wrote over rather than read:
  * *introduced by `#430`* -- FALSE;
  * *the memblock split always had it* -- FALSE;
  * *256x* -- the real figure is **1024x**.

*** AND THE REACHABILITY IS NEAR-NIL, MEASURED: three instrumented guest boots -- pmax, luna88k, macppc -- produced **ZERO** straddling stores. Only **11 of 1024** offsets can even start one, and it is PowerPC-only. *** It may also be architecturally CORRECT partial-completion-with-restart, which no one has refuted.

**DISPOSITION: DOCUMENTED-ONLY, ranked LAST of the guest-reachable set (8th of 8).** Not a live-corruption peer of [[b115]] or [[wdcringambig]], which is where I had implicitly put it.

*The lesson is mine and specific: I recorded a fresh seat answer as a NEW note on a row that already had a mature, more-measured entry underneath. **A row with existing evidence must be READ before it is written to** -- otherwise a fresh reading silently outranks an older measurement, which is the opposite of how evidence should compose.*

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, guest-reachable on PowerPC, and the observable is unusually clean -- a COUNT, not a value. ***

**The mechanism, and it needs the guest's own fault handler to complete it:** a store that STRADDLES a page boundary performs its head chunk BEFORE translating the tail. When the head lands in MMIO and the tail is unmapped, the MMIO side effect COMMITS, then the tail raises DSI. PowerPC saves the faulting PC, and the guest's `rfi` restarts **the whole store** -- so **the MMIO head runs a second time.**

**MEASURED (existing evidence cited by the seat, not re-run here):** `stw` at `0x1201fffe` -- two bytes of MMIO head, then an unmapped tail.

*** THE OBSERVABLE IS A COUNT AND THAT IS WHY THIS ROW IS WORTH RANKING: **MMIO-head side-effect count after one fault-and-retry -- TWO when broken, ONE when fixed.** *** A count-based oracle is immune to the value-only blindness that has made several detectors in this tree vacuous: it cannot be satisfied by reading back the same value twice.

**FIX PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS (transferred warrant):** `ppc_translate_v2p(... FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS | FLAG_WRITEFLAG)` fails BEFORE any SPR write, so the tail can be translated before the head is committed. The shape is 'probe both halves, then commit', and the primitive to probe with is already in the tree.

**NARROW: PowerPC only, and it needs a guest that restarts the faulting store** -- which is what a normal PPC fault handler does, so this is not an exotic path. Ranks below the silent read-corruption rows because it requires the fault, but it is a genuine double-side-effect, not a fidelity nit.

entries.note:
THE ADVERSARIAL FINDING, and it BOUNDS THE ROUND: the settled two-arm doctrine has a MISSING THIRD ARM, and a mechanical sweep would ship a worse defect than it removes.
* sh4_dmac_transfer (dev_sh4.c:340-428, DEVICE_ACCESS-reachable, exits at :372/:381/:390/:422/:427): the ONLY implemented CHCR_RS mode is 0x200, which by its own comment transfers nothing; there is no memory-to-memory path at all. Apply complain-and-continue and a guest programming ordinary dual-address DMA gets NO BYTES MOVED, CHCR_TE never set, no interrupt -- it polls TE forever or reads a destination that was never written. Silent corruption or a silent hang surfacing in a driver far from the DMAC, strictly HARDER to diagnose than today's exit(1), which names the mode in one line.
* AND THE LATCH MAKES IT WORSE, NOT BETTER: for a hot STATUS register latching is right, but for a STATEFUL OPERATION the first dropped transfer reports and every later one is invisible -- the latch actively SUPPRESSES the evidence of accumulating divergence. That inverts the #433 refinement instead of extending it.
* Same class at sh4_pcic's window-base registers (PCIMBR :917, PCIIOBR :926, PCILAR0/1 :891/:909, PCILSR0/1 :882/:900): dropping a write leaves the emulator decoding at the OLD base while the guest believes it moved, so every later PCI access lands at the wrong address -- possibly on a different device that answers.
* NOT A NEW CLASS -- #433's own adjudication hit it once (FLUSH_SUPER_LINE: a silently ignored TLB flush leaves the guest translating through a torn-down mapping) and solved it LOCALLY, without writing the rule down. So a mechanical pass over 170 sites would ship it at least three more times.
* THE ARM, stated so it applies per site: complain-and-continue is safe ONLY when the dropped write's only observable consequence is the register's own value. If the write's PURPOSE is to change how the emulator decodes, translates, transfers or invalidates -- address windows, TLB/cache flushes, DMA descriptors, coherency ops -- dropping it makes the model LIE rather than LAG, and the guest cannot tell. For that class: implement it, or stop honestly with cpu->running = 0 (which unlike exit(1) preserves the debugger and the emulator's own diagnostics) -- NEVER a latched drop. Three meanings, not two.
* AND THE ARM VINDICATES THE ROUND'S OWN SITE RATHER THAN BLOCKING IT: INT_ST_MASK IS state-changing (it is an SPL write), BUT the guarded portion -- bits 25..0 -- is MEASURED DEAD, so store-as-is drops nothing and the latched shape is correct at :816. That is exactly why this one site is safe and a blanket sweep is not.  [panel_20260817_112300]

rows.hold: Scope widened 2026-08-16 by the R6 pass-2 codex seat (read late): beyond the four listed defects it should cover external-event handling, reserved CONTROL-bit masking, and the retained/down-counter model. entries.note: UNBLOCKED: the 21285 datasheet was obtained (_scratchpad/dc21285.pdf, Intel 278115-001). Four defects are now specifiable. (1) SS7.3.41 bit 6: FREERUN wraps to FFFFFFh and keeps counting; PERIODIC reloads TimerNLoad; the clock source is bits 3:2 alone, identical in both. reload_timer_value() computes one rate and hands it to a repeating timer -- the PERIODIC cadence unconditionally -- so a FREERUN timer is too fast by up to 2^24/load. (2) TimerNValue is READ-ONLY (SS7.3.38/7.3.40) but the model accepts a guest write, and TIMER_1_CLEAR has NO writeflag test, so a guest READ of a write-only register reloads the counter and deasserts the IRQ. (3) Reset values diverge: hardware gives CONTROL 0x00 and LOAD 0, the model gives TIMER_MODE_PERIODIC and TIMER_MAX_VAL -- and this is the model bug #432's first draft mistakenly cited as evidence for its own zero mapping. (4) The random() counter model is now fully specified by SS7.3.40 + SS7.3.41 bit 7: a 24-bit down-counter, readable any time, RETAINED across disable and resuming on re-enable. The author's TODO is discharged; only a rig is missing.

Expand the item: external-event handling, reserved CONTROL-bit masking, and the retained/down-counter model belong in it alongside the four already listed. Ordering it after i8253zero would also be defensible, since i8253zero has a direct datasheet answer.

entries.note: SETTLED FROM A REAL DOCUMENT, which is the whole point of the item. i8253reg.h says nothing about a zero count (read in full, 102 lines), so the belief rested on memory -- exactly the trap this project names. The Intel 8254 datasheet (_scratchpad/i8254.pdf, 231164-005) states it twice on p.17: 'The largest possible initial count is 0; this is equivalent to 2^16 for binary counting and 10^4 for BCD counting.' So dev_8253.c:125's `else hz = 0` -- which the timer core then floor-clamps to 1e-8 Hz, i.e. never fires -- is wrong against the hardware convention. Cite it as the 8254, NOT the 8253: the count-0 convention was verified in the 8254 document only.
