THE WITNESS: a cold-debugger probe on UNMODIFIED `-E cats`, the same mechanics as footbridge_sites_probe.py. Pre-fix and post-fix binaries from the same tree, same script:
  C1 liveness            0x11223344 both     RAM through the same decode
  A1 device signature    0xAA both           see below
  T1 negative control    halts at paddr=0x0c000043, MMU-on cannot reach it
  D0 count 0 -> hz       0 Hz  ->  18 Hz     the device's own report
  G0 guest-visible       IRR 0x0 -> 0x1      after a 1.9 s free-run
  D1 positive control    count 4608 -> 259 Hz, IRR=0x1, identical both ways
All four controls green in BOTH runs; only the two symptom rows move.

THE DEVICE SIGNATURE IS A VALUE RAM CANNOT PRODUCE, and it was designed against the exact trap that ate the footbridge probe's first draft. The guest writes 0xAA then 0x55 to the SAME address in 16-bit mode, writes the MODE register (a different address), then reads back and gets 0xAA -- the byte from two writes ago. RAM returns 0x55. Nonzero deliberately, because 0x0 is what an ABSENT device looks like.

TWO CAVEATS THE SEAT OWNED RATHER THAN HID: G0/G1 use a WALL-CLOCK window (1.9 s against a 55 ms correct period, ~34 chances), which is why the post-fix green is the settlement and not the window size; and its first T1 draft reported FAIL through a string-equality bug in its own script, which it found and fixed. All 27 instruction encodings were checked against the emulator's own disassembler before use -- the hand-assembled-encoding trap this project has hit four times.

REACHABILITY, MEASURED: no guest in this tree programs count 0. Every PIT write in _guest-src-openbsd22/sys/ is TIMER_DIV(x) (never 0) or 0xff/0xff, and no rig image boots an 8253 machine. A recollection that Linux's pit_shutdown() writes 0,0 was flagged RECALLED, UNVERIFIED rather than cited -- the right handling. *** BUT FINDING `pitflip` BELOW MANUFACTURES COUNT 0 FROM A GUEST THAT NEVER ASKS FOR IT, which changes the reachability picture entirely. ***

MAPPINGS, measured not read: cats and netwinder 0x7c000040; malta/maltabe 0x18000040; cobalt 0x10000040; iyonix 0x90000040; absent on prep, mvmeppc, algor, arc.

THE FIX is one line -- hz = (int)(I8253_TIMER_FREQ / 65536.0 + 0.5) -> 18 -- and d->hz[] is read only at :133/137/140, all inside the MSB arm, so the blast radius is that arm. *** DO NOT GENERALISE BY ANALOGY: dev_rtc.c:129 and dev_mc146818.c:409 look identical and are CORRECT -- for those devices zero genuinely means 'off', and dev_rtc.c's comment records a prior round reasoning that through. The 8254 is the opposite case. *** Minor: int hz[3] rounds 18.2065 to 18 (-1.1%) while timer_add takes a double.

*** MERGE WITH pitlsb -- passes all three prongs, and #440 has just built the state the fix needs. ***  Both are 'when is a counter load complete, and what rate does it imply', and both live in the SAME `case I8253_TIMER_MSB:` block (i8253zero = its `else hz = 0`; pitlsb = the fact that `case I8253_TIMER_LSB:` has no equivalent). entries.note:
*** RANKED FIRST OF THE TIMER CLUSTER, AND THE ONLY ROW IN IT WHOSE HARM IS GUEST-VISIBLE STATE RATHER THAN HOST LOG NOISE. ***  MEASURED at -O3, modelling dev_footbridge.c:86 against :265:
    tick 1: pending= 2147483647  INTERRUPT_ASSERT=yes
    tick 2: pending=-2147483648  INTERRUPT_ASSERT=NO   <-- guest clock is DEAD
    -fsanitize=undefined: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 2147483647 + 1
After the wrap, pending > 0 is false for 2^31 CONSECUTIVE TICKS. On cats at the maximum legal rate that is 42.9 s of dead emulated clock in every 85.9 s, repeating. Reached by two ordinary MMIO writes (TIMER_1_LOAD = 1, TIMER_1_CONTROL = TIMER_ENABLE) -- the same shape of guest-driven arithmetic defect #432 just closed IN THE SAME REGISTERS.

*** THE FIX NEEDS NO INVENTION: *** dev_luna88k.c:252-260 already carries upstream's own idiom for this exact counter -- increment, then `if (pending > (int)HZ) pending = 1;` with a debugmsg. Of the EIGHT devices in the tree with a pending-timer counter, LUNA88K IS THE ONLY ONE THAT CAPS. That makes the design settled and the round small -- and it makes this a CLASS, so take one site (dev_footbridge) and file the sweep.

A FILED FIGURE IS WRONG: '~7.9 s for four timers' is arithmetically impossible -- the counters are PER-TIMER (pending_timer_interrupts[i]), so four timers do not overflow one element four times faster. Each still takes 2^31/rate. The true floor anywhere in the tree is 33.7 s on netwinder; the 43 s cats figure is correct.

GATE BLIND SPOT worth recording either way: no -fsanitize flag appears in gate_asan_sweep.sh, so this may be invisible to the one gate that could catch it.
entries.outcome_note: The overflow, per-counter timing correction and coverage gap held in opus5 research 2026-08-20; that research refuted the missing-sanitizer inference, and codex assess 2026-08-20 corrected literal copying of the increment-before-check precedent. [graded by codex gpt-6-astra max, n3, 2026-09-19]

entries.note:
*** THE ASan CLAIM IS REFUTED, AND THE CORRECTION MAKES THE GAP SHARPER RATHER THAN SMALLER. ***

A review seat reported it 'found no -fsanitize flag' in gate_asan_sweep.sh and inferred fbpending may be invisible to the one gate that could catch it. The flag IS there -- just not in that file. regress/build_asan.sh:38-39:
    export CFLAGS="-O1 -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fsanitize=address,undefined"
    export LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address,undefined"
The seat read the CONSUMER and drew a conclusion about the PRODUCER. Its own wording was careful ('in it'), so this is a scope error rather than a false statement -- but the inference did not survive opening the other file, which took under a minute.

*** THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES ANYWAY, FOR A REASON WORTH MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL: UBSan IS ENABLED AND THE GATE STILL CANNOT REACH THIS DEFECT. ***  gate_asan_sweep.sh:57-63 runs each machine as `timeout 25 $bin -V -E $t $DUMMY </dev/null` -- a bare construction sweep with a dummy file and NO GUEST PROGRAM. Two independent reasons it cannot fire:
  1. REACHABILITY: nothing ever writes TIMER_1_LOAD = 1 or TIMER_1_CONTROL = TIMER_ENABLE, so the timer never runs and pending_timer_interrupts never climbs.
  2. RUNTIME: the overflow needs ~43 s of WALL CLOCK on cats (2^31 at 50M increments/s) and the sweep's own timeout is 25 s. Even a guest that programmed the timer could not reach it inside the window.

So the honest record is: the instrumentation is present, the coverage is absent, and the gap is one of REACHABILITY AND RUNTIME rather than build flags. That is a harder gap to close -- a construction sweep can never catch a defect that needs a driver and a minute -- and it means the fix must ship with its own detector rather than leaning on the sanitizer gate. Recorded because 'the gate has UBSan' would otherwise read as reassurance.

SEPARATELY CONFIRMED, the seat's arithmetic correction: pending_timer_interrupts is declared `int pending_timer_interrupts[N_FOOTBRIDGE_TIMERS]` at dev_footbridge.c:73 and each of the four callbacks at :86-92 increments ITS OWN element, so four running timers do NOT overflow one element four times faster. The filed '~7.9 s for four timers' is arithmetically impossible. Floors: cats 2^31/50,000,000 = 42.9 s, netwinder 2^31/63,750,000 = 33.7 s. Both rates sit BELOW the delivery ceiling of TIMER_MAX_CATCHUP x TIMER_BASE_FREQUENCY = 1048576 x 65 = 68,157,440/s, so the full rate really is delivered and the figures hold.
entries.outcome_note: The later opus5 research 2026-08-20 entry headed 'TWO SIDE QUESTIONS SETTLED' confirmed enabled UBSan, absent guest-driven timer creation, insufficient runtime and the per-counter timing arithmetic. [graded by codex gpt-6-astra max, n3, 2026-09-19]

entries.note:
*** WITNESS BUILT AND THE SYMPTOM REPRODUCED, three independent runs on the committed build. ***  _scratchpad/fbpending_witness.py, rung 3: real ARM guest instructions on an unmodified in-tree -E cats, real decode, real memory_rw, real device dispatch. No source edited, no device_add, no boot. Two MMIO writes arm it.

    run        interpolated wrap   dead window        zero-tick slices   resumed
    30 x 4 s   43.03 s             44.19 - 84.37 s    10  (40.2 s)       yes
    11 x 5 s   43.10 s             45.18 - (run end)   2                 n/a
    30 x 4 s   44.58 s             44.20 - 84.37 s    10  (40.2 s)       yes
Predicted 42.95 s (2^31/50e6), return 85.90 s. `catch-up-bound messages: 0`, so the timer got its full rate and nothing was clamped. Host-load jitter moved run 3's INTERPOLATED estimate (it depends on the guest's instruction rate) but NOT the dead-window boundaries, which are SIGALRM/wall-clock driven and were identical to run 1 -- a distinction worth keeping.

TWELVE CONTROLS GREEN, and three are stronger than the ladder requires:
  * the NEGATIVE control is QUANTITATIVE rather than merely different -- MMU left on gives a tick/iteration ratio of 1.0000000, the exact absent-device signature, against 2064 in the live arm;
  * a FAILABILITY control (K): the same prologue plus ONE instruction (read IRQ_ENABLE_SET) makes the host die, so something in this probe demonstrably can still fail;
  * LIVENESS DURING THE FREEZE (L2): a fresh ldr of VENDOR_ID returned 0x1011 in 30/30 samples INCLUDING every frozen one, so the device stayed mapped and dispatching -- only the tick stopped. That is what separates 'the clock died' from 'the probe died'.
Two device signatures, both small and non-zero (VENDOR_ID 0x1011; a write of 0x12345678 to TIMER_1_LOAD reads back 0x00345678, the handler's own 24-bit mask, which RAM cannot produce). 30/30 planted offsets checked against the emulator's own disassembly AS THEY EXECUTED -- the loop words under test, not just the prologue.

*** A REAL TRAP FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, and it is 'absent data must fail' on an axis this project had not met: THE TIME AXIS. ***  At 11 x 5 s the probe printed SYMPTOM=ABSENT / VERDICT=PASS / exit 0 ON A DEFECTIVE BUILD -- the run reached the wrap but only 10 s of dead window fitted inside it, so the evidence of recovery was missing rather than absent. Fixed: FBPENDING_COVERAGE refuses to report ABSENT until free-run exceeds the predicted return (89.9 s), and a short run now says UNDETERMINED. A too-short run scoring PASS is the same class as a row comparing two -1 defaults, and it would have been invisible.

Cost: 128.7 s full; --slices 3 --slice-seconds 2 exercises every control in 12.5 s.

NOT MEASURED, stated by the seat: the post-fix arm (no fix exists, so only the first witness clause is shown); UBSan firing on this line (the ASan artifact is from Jul 29 and predates #432's rate arithmetic, and rebuilding would mutate a shared gate artifact); rung 4 (no rig boots a footbridge machine); netwinder, which is arithmetic from a read constant.

entries.note:
TWO SIDE QUESTIONS SETTLED, and both corrections went in the direction that keeps the substance.

(1) THE ASan CLAIM: refuted on its premise, upheld on its conclusion, and a THIRD reason found that neither I nor the reporting seat had. build_asan.sh:38-39 does set -fsanitize=address,undefined, and the artifact carries eleven __ubsan_handle_* imports INCLUDING __ubsan_handle_add_overflow -- the exact handler an int++ overflow calls. So 'no -fsanitize flag' is false; the seat had grepped the CONSUMER (gate_asan_sweep.sh) rather than the PRODUCER. *** But gate 9 still cannot catch this, and the reason I gave (timeout 25 vs a 42.95 s floor) was only half of it: DEVINIT(footbridge) NEVER CREATES A struct timer AT ALL. ***  Only a guest write to TIMER_x_LOAD or TIMER_x_CONTROL|ENABLE does, and a construction sweep runs no guest -- so timer_tick0 is never called and the counter never increments, timeout or no timeout. Either reason alone is fatal.

(2) THE '~7.9 s FOR FOUR TIMERS' FIGURE: confirmed impossible, and the seat found WHERE THE NUMBER CAME FROM, which is better than refuting it. 2^31 / (4 x 1048576 x 65) = 7.876 s -- the single-element floor divided by four. The counters are per-timer (:73), each callback increments its own element (:86-92), and the catch-up budget is per-timer too (timer.c:281, inside the per-timer loop), so four timers overflow four DIFFERENT elements at their own rates. True floors: 42.950 s cats (2^31/50,000,000, machine_cats.c:56-57) now measured three times at 43.03/43.10/44.58, and 33.686 s netwinder (2^31/63,750,000, machine_netwinder.c:56).

ONE REFINEMENT worth recording: a hard floor of 31.51 s exists from the catch-up ceiling (2^31/68,157,440), but it needs a timer at or above 68.16 MHz, which neither machine's emulated_hz permits. cats's is guarded by `if (== 0)` so a config-file emulated_hz word could reach it; netwinder's is unconditional. Neither is guest-reachable, so severity is unchanged.

rows.title: m8probe  m8820x PROBE_USER/PROBE_SUPER are dropped, so SSR answers a deterministic miss
rows.hold: *** RE-FILED LATENT 2026-08-26 ON THE `gdrompiooddlen` PRECEDENT -- REACHABILITY MEASURED NEGATIVE, WITH CONTROLS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. MUST NOT BE RANKED LIVE. *** A full OpenBSD 7.7/luna88k boot to `login:` (7,684,964,995 instructions) issues **seven distinct CMMU commands and ZERO probes**. Denominator stated: 0 of 7 distinct commands, not 0 of 0 -- and it independently replicates #433's finding thirty rounds later. **The controls are what make this evidence:** a real guest supervisor store on a cold debugger, with the planted word DISASSEMBLED BEFORE STEPPING per the hand-assembled-encoding rule -- cmd 0x24 and 0x20 fire the detector, cmd 0x35 does not while still registering as M8CMD_FIRST. So the negative is real and not a broken grep. CORROBORATION that sharpens it past 'this guest does not': OpenBSD's m88k CMMU driver issues CMMU_PROBE from exactly two places and **both are inside DDB display routines** -- a kernel-debugger feature, not an operating path, reachable only by a human at a DDB prompt. (Caveat recorded by the seat: that source is OpenBSD 2.2/mvme88k, the lineage, not the booting guest; the boot measurement is the evidence for the actual guest.) *** THE OLD COST NOTE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. *** 'Needs the translation walk' implies a CAPABILITY gap. **The walk exists** -- m88k_translate_v2p() at memory_m88k.c:103 -- **and is already side-effect-free under FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS** (:344 guards the PG_U/PG_M writeback, :374 returns before any PFSR/PFAR write), its flags already cover the probe's own selectors, and the SSR bit layout is in-tree. **And the driving probe SHAPE is already committed**: m8820x_sites_probe.py:159 ships a PROBE_SUPER row driven by one real guest instruction, ~3 s, no boot. *This is the `sh4dmacie` situation in reverse -- there the shape was missing and it was mis-read as a capability gap; here the shape was already there and nobody re-read the probe.* **WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS AN ORACLE, AND THE HOLD IS NOW CONDITIONAL ON IT:** translate_v2p exposes no BATC-vs-PATC-vs-walk distinction (needed for CMMU_SSR_BH) and none of the U/M/PROT/SO attributes SSR must carry; real probe semantics are supported only by DDB code reading those registers, which is evidence and not proof; and **there is no 88200/88204 manual in this project**. TRIGGER, on the SH4_VAL_NCLASS precedent: **if an 88200/88204 manual is obtained, this becomes a small round.** That converts an indefinite hold into a conditional one. *** AND THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR IS THE BETTER ONE, which is the strongest reason not to rank it: *** a dropped probe leaves SSR zero with the V bit clear -- a deterministic, DEFINED 'no valid translation'. Implementing without the manual would replace a defined conservative miss with an INVENTED answer that could steer the guest's paging. **That is the same reasoning used to decline `sh4aaalias` before the SH manual arrived -- and that one turned out to be a wrong finding.** The only known consumer prints a line in a debugger display, so a cosmetically wrong DDB line for a human is the entire measured consequence. WORTH ADDING CHEAPLY: one row asserting SSR == 0 after a probe, to pin the DELIBERATE behaviour that today rests on prose in two comments and no oracle at all.

entries.note: From R7. After #433 a probe is complained-once and dropped, and the guest then reads regs[CMMU_SSR], which nothing ever writes -- the model writes only PFSR/PFAR (memory_m88k.c:382-405) -- so probes deterministically answer 0, i.e. V-bit clear, a defined 'no valid translation' rather than a plausible-looking valid answer. The measured OpenBSD/luna88k boot issues NO probes (7 command values, all handled); NetBSD and MP kernels are unmeasured. Real semantics mean reusing the existing translation walk against regs[CMMU_SAR] and synthesising SSR from the header's bit definitions (m8820x.h:155-163). No 88200 manual exists in-tree, so where a bit's setting condition is not derivable from the header plus the existing walk, leave it 0 and record UNKNOWN.

rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: the claim is TRUE and the path is COMPLETELY UNREACHED by operating guest OS paths. Latent. ***

**True:** in `dev_m8820x.c`'s `m8820x_command()`, `CMMU_PROBE_USER` / `CMMU_PROBE_SUPER` are dropped, so a probe yields a **deterministic SSR miss of `0x0`** -- SSR answers a different question from the one asked.

**But no operating guest OS exercises it.** The instruction exists and the register is addressable; nothing a booting system does reaches it. So it is dormant defensive debt and ranks below anything a guest travels.

**A deterministic wrong answer is worse than an error in one specific way worth recording:** `0x0` is a *plausible* miss result, so a guest that did probe would receive a well-formed answer to the wrong question rather than a fault it could detect. That is the silent-wrong-versus-loud-wrong axis this project uses, and it puts this above a row that merely fails to implement something.

THREE CONTROLS HOLD, and they are what make it a measurement rather than a reading: the WRITE side still purges 6 (deliberately not under test), reading IDR from outside the group purges 0 (so the count is this arm and not something ambient), and the read still returns the seeded value 0xabcd (so a later fix cannot pass by turning the read into a no-op). WHY IT IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY: PFSR and PFAR are what a fault handler READS to find out what faulted and where, so the cost lands on the ordinary page-fault path, twice per fault. Per-boot read count NOT yet measured. THIS IS THE SAME CALLBACK whose NULLness corrupted the first m8820x reproduction by exactly six each way -- that accident was this defect seen from the other side.

entries.note: From R7. The committed differential proves the device's behaviour but NOT that the site is reachable by a guest instruction through the real memory path -- it calls dev_m8820x_access directly, so it cannot catch a change that makes the device unreachable (a memory_device_register length or DM_ flag change). The measuring seat built and measured the alternative: a cold-debugger probe, no boot, 3.1 s for 8 rows, ~60-75x cheaper than a rig drive, with every probe word disassembled before stepping. Rows must assert VALUES not survival (control r4 == 0x00a90000) and cover ALL FIVE sites, since a fix repairing only the default arm passes any detector that probes 0x800 alone. rows.title: ns16550  Guest-writable divisor divides by zero (UB) -- but not in the shipped build
rows.hold: REAL but optimisation-dependent; NOT the top item

closure.note: CLOSE (assess)

entries.note: REPRODUCED TEST-FIRST, AND IT CORRECTS THE FILING AND MY OWN RANKING. Two seats filed this as the cheapest remaining guest-reachable HOST KILL on the live arc rig; I ranked it top of the queue on that. MEASURED: SIGFPE with a core dump at -O0 and -O1, SURVIVES at -O2, -O3 and -Os, and SURVIVES under the tree's own build flags (-fgnu89-inline -O3 -DNDEBUG). At -O2+ gcc exploits the UB and elides the division. So the host does NOT die in the configuration this project builds. Still a defect -- UB on a guest-reachable path, restored by any debug build or compiler change -- but not the cheapest host kill and not top of the queue. THE optrow CLASS ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE GLASS: optrow was a DETECTOR following the compiler, this is a DEFECT following it, and any severity claim about UB must name the flags it was measured under. The vacuity check mattered twice over: read-back confirmed dlab==1 and divisor==0 at the division with debug() reached, so the negative is not a skipped path; and the first run had ALL THREE probes dying INCLUDING THE CONTROL, because calloc left d->addrmult zero and the access function divides relative_addr by it -- the harness producing SIGFPE for the wrong reason, separated from the defect only by the control row.
entries.outcome_note: The flag-dependent result and deranking are reaffirmed by opus5 assess, 2026-08-20, fable5 assess, 2026-08-22 and the witness: reachable UB remains, while the shipped optimized build does not fault. [graded by codex gpt-6-astra max, n8, 2026-09-19]

entries.note: CONFIRMED from source independently: the divisor is guest-zeroable via the DLAB low-byte write and the divide sits in argument position of a real varargs debug(), so it executes at every verbosity. Its follow-on hypothesis -- that this shape has other instances -- is now REFUTED by measurement: 24 diagnostic-argument divisions in src/, 22 with constant divisors, and the only other non-constant one (diskimage.c:543) cannot reach zero. So ns16550 is the single live instance of the class, and a gate-6 ratchet keeps that true.
entries.outcome_note: The guest-zeroable divisor and source-level UB are upheld by fable5 assess, 2026-08-22. The census recorded in kimi's 2026-08-16 entry refutes additional live instances, and the optimization sweep limits any claim of unconditional execution. entries.note: The fold sends CMMU_FLUSH_{USER,SUPER}_SEGMENT to the all=1 arm. Safe direction, but NOT free of guest-visible effect, and the shipped comment claimed it was. A walk writes PG_U (and PG_M on a write) back into the page descriptor IN EMULATED MEMORY; a PATC hit sets those bits only in the PATC copy. So a guest that clears U on a page in segment B, flushes segment A, then touches B observes a U bit a correctly-scoped flush would have left clear. The tighter mapping needs no manual: match the walker's own 4 MB segment size, (sar ^ vaddr) & 0xffc00000. What real silicon does at segment granularity is UNKNOWN -- there is no 88200/88204 manual in this project.

entries.note: Per boot-to-login: PFSR 292,281 reads / SAR 612,186 writes / UAPR 13,026 writes; PFAR read ZERO times. (1) The read side is 99.999% PFSR, so the design brief's 'twice per fault' was WRONG -- it is once, and that sentence was inferred rather than measured. (2) The write side is 98% SAR, and m88k_translate_v2p never consults SAR -- it reads only SAPR/UAPR (memory_m88k.c:135,137), BATC and PATC. SAR is read at exactly one place, dev_m8820x.c:110, as the address operand of a flush command whose own arm already purges at :187. So a SAR write owes no purge BY EXACTLY #434's ARGUMENT FOR READS. (3) Registers that can really change a translation are 13,033 of 917,504 accesses = 1.4%; 98.6% of this arm's purges are unjustified and #434 removes 32% of them.
entries.outcome_note: The finding that SAR writes dominate unnecessary purges was reproduced by fable5 research 2026-08-16. *** MECHANISM CORRECT, HARM MEASURED UNREACHABLE -- AND THE MODEL MATCHES SILICON, SO THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD INTRODUCE DIVERGENCE RATHER THAN REMOVE IT. ***  This overturns the file-reading seats' #1 ranking.

    cmmu_set_uapr(apr_data.bits);
    cmmu_flush_tlb(0, 0, -1);
(unsigned)-1 > M88K_PGBYTES selects CMMU_FLUSH_USER_ALL on both CMMUs, and the model's flush arm (dev_m8820x.c:175-211) clears every valid user PATC entry under all=1,super=0. cmmu_pmap_activate() does the same and comments on it. entries.note: *** VERDICT: KEEP OPEN -- and it ANSWERED the question the hold was written to ask. I asked for the smallest edit that survives every existing row and dies under a composed one, saying that if none could be named the row should close. **One was named AND MEASURED: a ONE-IDENTIFIER change sweeps BOTH offline detectors clean at 79/79 and dies under a composed row.** *** THE MUTANT: `dev_m8820x.c:108`, `cmmu[d->cmmu_nr]->reg` -> `cmmu[0]->reg`. Denominators self-reported by the harnesses: diff_m8820x 46 rows + diff_m8invread 33 rows = 79, with two deliberate @@SELFCHECK@@ FAIL lines in each file as negative controls, so a raw grep of 2 IS the green baseline. *** THE CONTROLS ARE WHAT MAKE THIS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN AN ASSERTION, and they show the blindness is STRUCTURAL: *** M3 (`sar = 0`) reddens D1/D3, proving the harness CAN see a consumer-side SAR defect; M4 (drop the SAR store) reddens E7/E8/G6/G7, proving it CAN see a producer-side one. **Both ends are covered; only the SEAM is blind** -- because every SCR-flush row runs after `fresh()` (which memsets the device, so cpu_nr = cmmu_nr = 0) and issues from cpu0, and at (0,0) every candidate base for `regs` coincides. **M1 IS A LIVE-DEFECT CLASS ON THE SHIPPED RIG, NOT A SHAPE PIN**, and the seat verified the load-bearing fact from source rather than trusting a harness comment: `dev_luna88k.c:926-957` registers BOTH CMMUs on every boot, and `dev_m8820x.c:542-543` maps `addr2 & 1` -> cmmu_nr, so cmmu_nr = 1 is guest-addressable on every luna88k boot -- with the data CMMU taking 318,457 of 613,342 SAR writes (51.9%%). Under M1 **half the machine's PATC flushes never dispatch at all**, which is the silently-under-invalidating TLB the file's own comment calls 'not a cosmetic gap'. (M2, the `(cpu, d)` swap, is by contrast a shape pin: the booting rig is single-CPU.) *** THE COMPOSED ROW IS BUILT AND MEASURED -- THREE ROWS, EACH WITH ITS OWN KILL, NONE DECORATION: *** K1 (matching entry dropped) reddens under M1/M1b; K2 (non-matching entry retained) under M5; K3 (flush from a NON-OWNER cpu) under M2. **The two axes are independent: K1 does not catch M2 and K3 does not catch M1.** The original filing asked for 'cmmu_nr 1 AND from a non-owner CPU'; the measurement shows both halves are load-bearing and neither subsumes the other -- sharper than the filing knew. rows.note: *** A SEVERITY STANDARD, adjudicated 2026-08-30, because the main loop proposed one that collapses two different classes. ***  I graded a stale-build record NIL and then generalised it to *"a confident wrong record with no measurement consumed"*.  **The adjudicating seat refused the generalisation and gave the discriminator: INERT BY CONSTRUCTION versus INERT BY LUCK.**  A comment-only stale delta is inert BY CONSTRUCTION -- the binary is byte-identical, so any measurement taken in that window is provably valid -> **NIL** (and the comment-only-ness must be RUN, not asserted; here the pass-2 seat measured zero non-comment diff lines).  An ASSERTED WRONG CENSUS is a live wrong fact that merely HAPPENS not to have been consumed yet -> **LOW, never NIL**.  > **The test is not "no measurement was consumed".  It is "no measurement COULD be consumed".**  And the carrier already holds a measured case of the second class changing an outcome: `asicbadaddr`'s 16-versus-64 census, where *a detector built from the wrong census walks sixteen addresses, covers a QUARTER of the defect, and reports full coverage*.  My own 25/15 census today was that shape -- asserted into two seat briefs, telling one of them it was probably wrong -- and it is LOW, not NIL.  *** AND THE STANDARD NEEDED A BOLT, WHICH THE EXEMPLAR'S OWN FILE ALREADY HELD.  Added 2026-08-30 by the adjudicating seat, against a claim I made in a commit message. ***  The discriminator (inert by CONSTRUCTION vs inert by LUCK) survives and has a real floor, unlike pre-floor 'weak': **NIL is a PROOF CLASS, and everything unproven is LOW or above.**  But my proof for the exemplar -- *the binary is byte-identical* -- **was never measured, and it is refuted by a comment in the very file it was about.**  `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` records, of its own comment-only assert block: *'It emits no object code -- verified with the filename held constant: **the object differs in exactly two bytes, both `__LINE__` immediates displaced by this comment block**.'*  So a comment-only delta in this tree does NOT yield a byte-identical binary.  > **THE SURVIVING FORM: NIL is claimable only with the IDENTITY PROOF NAMED -- a `cmp` of artifacts, or the byte delta enumerated with every byte attributed to a NON-CONSUMABLE token (which is exactly what that comment did).  Absent that proof, LOW is the floor.**  The grading itself stands -- `__LINE__` immediates move diagnostic line numbers and nothing else -- and the CHANGELOG's careful wording (*zero non-comment diff lines ... a wrong RECORD, not a wrong measurement*) survives.  **It is the 'byte-identical' shorthand in the commit message that does not**, and a shorthand that overstates a proof is how a proof class becomes a habit.  *** OWNER RULING 2026-08-30: agy IS RESERVED FOR MEASUREMENT AND HELD OUT OF ROUTINE PANELS. ***  Forced by its first quota wall proving the cap is real (~6 substantial calls per window).  **The warrant is a measured structural weakness: three compile-and-measure front ends, and TWO of them sit behind the SAME Agent-tool transport.**  When that transport failed on `#462` the panel lost ALL measuring capacity at once while seven reading seats answered normally.  agy is the only measuring seat on an independent road, so spending its budget on reading spends the roster's insurance on a job seven other seats already do.  **THE COST IS REAL AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED:** routine panels now fire EIGHT seats and each must record agy as **DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED** -- a different thing from a seat failure and from agreement, and conflating them is what the seat ledger exists to refuse.  Its read-only work today was not cheap to lose: it settled the alignment premise path-by-path and found the debugger `put d` exception a clean-invariant claim would have missed.  *But a reading is recoverable from another seat and a measurement with both Anthropic seats down is not.*  *** THE LEDGER'S `outcome` FIELD IS CARRYING **THREE** DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, AND THE ACCURACY TOOL CAN ONLY SEE ONE OF THEM.  Measured 2026-08-30. ***  *(This header said TWO while the body six sentences below said THREE -- a live self-contradiction, and the SAME shape as the refuted figure I left standing in `selftestaddition` earlier the same evening.  Caught by the second review pass; the body was right.)*  `seat_scorecard.py` recognises exactly four values -- `UPHELD` / `REFUTED` / `PARTIAL` / `UNVERIFIED` -- and **249 entries carried an `outcome` while only 110 were countable -- 139 invisible to it.**  *(Dated snapshot, and it has since drifted BY MY OWN HAND: tonight's four canonical gradings make it **250 / 115 / 135**.  DERIVER: count `"outcome":` for the total, and for the countable figure sum the entries whose value is one of the four `GRADES` in `seat_scorecard.py`.  Recorded rather than silently re-stated, because a number corrected must land as deriver-plus-demoted-prose and never as a fresh bare literal.)*  Derived by classifying every non-canonical value: **56 are a VERDICT THE SEAT GAVE** (`SHIP`, `NOT-RATIFY`, `GO-WITH-CHANGES`, `REJECT-AS-WRITTEN`), **11 are SEAT HEALTH** (`answered-104KB`, `answered-2.2MB`), and 72 are other free-form.  **THOSE ARE THREE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS SHARING ONE FIELD NAME:** *what did the seat CONCLUDE*, *did the seat ANSWER AT ALL*, and *was the seat RIGHT*.  Only the third is a grade.  A seat can conclude `NOT-RATIFY` and be **UPHELD** -- it was right to refuse -- or conclude `SHIP` and be **REFUTED**.  Collapsing them means the scorecard silently reads 3.9% coverage where the true figure for *graded* entries is what it says, and the other 139 are not partially-graded but differently-typed.  *** RETROACTIVE RECLASSIFICATION IS REFUSED, ON THE TOOL'S OWN STATED GROUND. ***  `seat_scorecard.py` says it plainly: *grade an entry when its claim is CHECKED -- reconstructing grades later reproduces exactly the recall bias this tool replaced.*  Deciding today whether a seat that wrote `SHIP` two weeks ago turned out to be right is precisely that reconstruction.  **The 139 stay as they are, and the finding is that the FIELD needs splitting, not that the entries need re-scoring.**  *Filed as an observation rather than a change: separating `verdict` from `outcome` edits every writer of the ledger and is an owner decision, not a round's.  What is actionable today, and was done: four of today's entries were graded with CANONICAL values at the moment their claims were checked, with the descriptive label kept in `outcome_note`.*  *** A NEGATIVE RESULT, RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-ASKS IT: NO CRITICAL BUG IS HIDING IN THE UNRANKED OPEN ROWS.  Swept 2026-08-30, and the SCOPE of the sweep is stated because a negative result without its scope is worthless. ***  **THE PROMPT:** 97 open rows, and **74 carry no `sev` at all** -- so the queue cannot be ordered by severity, which is what the ranking rule says orders it (*a witness makes an item ELIGIBLE; SEVERITY and gate blind-spots order the queue*).  The obvious worry is that a live host kill is sitting unranked.  **THE METHOD, and its limit:** of the 74, **four** mention a host kill or an out-of-bounds in their title or note head -- `asicoffsetkill`, `asicindexcase`, `asickillsurvive`, `asicarray4`.  All four were opened and read.  **None is a live defect:** `asicoffsetkill` is COVERAGE DEBT with a `harness:` witness (a mutant that scores clean); `asicindexcase` is LATENT with its invariant verified today (max r = 2 over 12 labels); `asickillsurvive` is about what existing rows OBSERVE, not about product code; and `asicarray4` says of itself *design proposal, not a defect*.  **THE LIMIT: 70 of the 74 were NOT individually read** -- they were excluded by a keyword sweep, which cannot see a critical row whose title avoids those words.  The claim is therefore *no critical bug among unranked rows that DESCRIBE THEMSELVES as kills or OOBs*, not *no critical bug among unranked rows*.  Stating that distinction is the whole value of the record.  **AND THE 69 NO-NOTE ROWS ARE NOT A RECORDS DEFECT, which is the part I expected to go the other way.**  69 open rows have no `note`, and the tempting reading is that they are thin filings.  **Measured against the rows that DO have notes, their titles are the same length -- median 145 against 149.**  The title is carrying the claim and the `witness` field the evidence; that is a convention, not an omission.  *A bulk backfill would have been invented work, and the measurement is what stopped it.*  *** THE CARRIER STATES A COUNT IN THE SENTENCE THAT TELLS YOU NOT TO STATE A COUNT.  Measured 2026-08-30 by the #497 seat, verified here. ***  It reads: *est/ and GXEMUL-SEC differ by **SEVEN declared paths** ... the list is `tools/est_divergence.txt` and `precommit_check.sh` reads it, so **derive the allowlist rather than quoting a count**; that is what this line got wrong.*  **`tools/est_divergence.txt` holds SIX non-comment entries** -- `src/devices/.index`, `Makefile.skel`, `autodev.c`, `dev_jazz.c`, `dev_ne2000.c`, `src/machines/machine_arc.c`.  Derived by `grep -vcE '^\s*(#|$)'`.  *So the paragraph diagnoses the failure correctly, prescribes the correct remedy, and then commits the failure in its own headline number -- which is the sharpest example this file has of why the remedy is DERIVE rather than RE-COUNT.  Corrected by pointing at the deriver instead of substituting SIX, because a fresh literal here would be the third generation of the same defect.*  *** "LOG MISSING MEANS THE COMMAND NEVER STARTED" IS ONLY EVIDENCE IF YOU LOOKED IN THE RIGHT DIRECTORY -- AND I DOUBLE-FIRED A PANEL BY GETTING THAT WRONG.  Measured 2026-08-30. ***  The discriminator is sound and is this file's own: *log MISSING -> never started; log 0 bytes -> started; log growing -> alive*.  I applied it to `_scratchpad/panel497p2.log` **from a shell whose cwd had drifted to `GXEMUL-SEC/`**, where no `_scratchpad/` exists.  `ls` reported absent.  I concluded the launch had died to the plain-`&` teardown and **fired a second panel 38 seconds after the first**.  **BOTH PANELS WERE REAL.**  `panel_20260830_214531` holds codex at 1.49 MB, kimi 50 KB, agy 11 KB and two Ollama answers; `panel_20260830_214609` is the duplicate.  The log I declared missing was 596 bytes at the project root the whole time.  *** THE COST WAS THE RATE LIMIT: two panels 38 SECONDS APART, and the second one's Ollama seats returned `HTTPError 429: Too Many Requests`. ***  That is the carrier's own rate-limit mechanism -- and note it is NOT the expired ~20-minute spacing rule coming back, because the gap here is under a minute.  **The seats were not walled by anything external; I walled them.**  **THE RULE NEEDS ONE WORD: check the log by ABSOLUTE PATH.**  A missing file and a mis-pathed check are indistinguishable in `ls` output, and this session's cwd has drifted THREE times today -- into `GXEMUL-SEC/` twice and once mid-command.  *The carrier already warns that `./panel.sh` from a drifted cwd is a silent zero-seat failure; this is the same drift arriving on the VERIFICATION side, where it converts a healthy run into a phantom dead one and provokes a duplicate.*  **AND THE APPARATUS RULE COVERS IT ALREADY, one level up: CHECK THAT THE APPARATUS SELECTED SOMETHING BEFORE READING WHAT IT SAYS.**  An `ls` on a path that cannot exist selects nothing and reports absence, which looks exactly like a measurement.

entries.note: *** VERDICT: NOT DISCHARGED. The core finding was adopted, but the shipped ladder is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT about rung 2 and omits a category its own checker already implements. *** Both gaps VERIFIED before recording. GAP 1 -- rung 2 versus clause (ii). The ladder admits CONSTRUCTION as a witness specifically for init-time defects, naming the macppc heap OOB. But the universal admissibility clauses require every rung-2-4 witness to carry a LIVENESS control and a DEVICE-SIGNATURE control -- 'a known value returns through the same decode'. **A construction-time OOB performs no address decode and returns no device value, so the ladder's own named exemplar cannot satisfy its own clause.** Clause (ii) should be scoped to ACCESS witnesses (rungs 3-4), with construction-specific controls for rung 2. GAP 2 -- the `harness:` category. `check_witness.py:56` accepts `^(boot:|probe:|construction:|harness:|none)` and its own header at :24-28 says **'`harness:` IS A GAP IN THE LADDER, FOUND BY THIS CHECK ON ITS FIRST RUN'** -- none of the four rungs fits a defect in the TEST APPARATUS itself. `precommit_check.sh:678` repeats the finding. CLAUDE.md still says 'no witness at rung 2-4 -> document instead' and never states the exception. **The tool wrote the gap down and the carrier never absorbed it**, which is the structure-vs-prose failure inverted: here the STRUCTURE knew and the PROSE did not. It also names the boundary that keeps the category honest -- `harness:` is proof only when the harness IS the subject, and must never license an `#include`/direct-call witness for emulator code.

Read the ladder as it now stands and say whether anything this row raised is still unaddressed. If it is fully discharged, say so and it closes; if not, name the gap.
rows.state_note: *** BOTH GAPS CLOSED 2026-08-26; THIS ROW IS DISCHARGED PENDING ITS REMAINING SEATS. *** The codex seat answering this row's hold_question found the shipped ladder INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT about rung 2 and missing a category its own checker already enforced. (b) `check_witness.py:56` has accepted `harness:` since its first run and its header says outright that none of the four rungs fits a defect in the TEST APPARATUS itself; `precommit_check.sh:678` repeats it. entries.note: Deleting the ordering `continue` in diskimage_sync() is the one mutant the shipped detector does not catch. The pass-2 measure seat VERIFIED a row can catch it: inject an fsync failure on the overlay data file and assert the bitmap fd is ABSENT from the trace -- shipped syncs fds [4 5 6], the mutant syncs [4 5 6 7]. One row, not built.  [panel_20260818_095322]

entries.note:
BUILT AND CLOSED, and it IMPROVED ON THE RECIPE IT WAS GIVEN. Told to build the single-overlay row a prior pass had specified, it built that, then probed two SIBLING mutants and measured that the single-overlay row catches ONLY the deletion: `continue` -> `break;` and `continue` -> `return 0;` both pass it GREEN, because with one overlay there is no next iteration and all three mutants trace identically. A SECOND OVERLAY separates them and one row kills all three. It supplied both patches and recommended the stronger, which also perturbs no existing gate check where the fallback would have forced one from "1" to "2".
* Mechanism: __wrap_fsync consults a static fail_fsync_fd, sets errno=EIO and returns -1 without calling __real_fsync; armed after the WRITE, disarmed when the command returns. It rejected, with reasons written into the file, a real failing fsync (needs dm-error/root, non-portable -- same class as the drvfs trap), close()ing the fd under the live FILE* (a FAULT, and can hit a recycled fd) and an O_RDONLY fd (rc 0 on glibc, proves nothing).
* A CRASH IS NOT WHAT MAKES IT FAIL, measured four ways: rc is 1 never >=128; the mutant printed all 11 rows plus the verdict line so it reached the end of main; ASan+UBSan produced 0 bytes on both arms; and exactly one row differs, by a printed string.
* INSTRUMENT-SABOTAGE CONTROL (`if (0 && fd == fail_fsync_fd)`) turns TWO rows red, so a dead injection fails loudly and the signatures are distinguishable: two red together = the instrument, the ordering row red alone = the code.
* VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MAIN LOOP, and MY FIRST THREE ATTEMPTS WERE ALL VOID -- the loop variable was eaten before reaching WSL and the printed rc was grep's status; then the anchor took 'the first continue in a range' when the loop has TWO and the f_data==NULL branch never executes, so all three mutants 'passed' and would have discredited the row; then anchoring on the fsync call matched :1211 in overlay_set_block_in_use, a different function. Only a context printout of the line about to be mutated caught it. Correctly anchored on the unique 'Data is not durable' comment: ALL THREE MUTANTS KILLED, traces distinguishable -- deleted publishes b0 anyway, break/return0 stop at F(d0) S(d0).
* Gate 2: PASS 235 checks (was 231). Honest limits recorded in the file: the CHECK-CONDITION row is a WITNESS not a discriminator (green on every code mutant); an fflush failure on the data file is not injected, only fsync; and the injection skips the real fsync, so a partially-successful sync is UNTESTED and UNKNOWN.  [agent m437ord 2026-08-19]
entries.outcome_note: Opus5 research 2026-08-19 records the main loop independently reproducing all three kills and the instrument-sabotage control; fable5 regress the same date confirms executed fault-injection checks. [graded by codex gpt-6-astra max, n10, 2026-09-19]

entries.note:
FABLE REGRESS ADJUDICATION of verdict_20260819_135703 at 6014b7e. Badge `s` disclosed: same-model adjudication of the main loop's records, not a two-family check.
* *** Q2 REFUTED MY OWN SUSPICION USING THE BATTERY'S OWN LOG. *** I wrote that no gate asserts the guest-visible CHECK CONDITION. Lines 554 and 559 say otherwise (verified here): `overlay: a failed sync reports CHECK CONDITION 2` and `nothing open: sync reports CHECK CONDITION, not GOOD 2` -- FAULT-INJECTED via fail_fsync_fd returning EIO, driven through the real diskimage_scsicommand() with a WRITE(10)-then-SYNCHRONIZE-CACHE CDB pair, not a direct call. So gate 2 EXERCISED the changed path discriminatingly rather than merely not breaking on it. The live gates ran the success leg for real: luna88k reached login in gates 5 and 7.
* Q1 MY FRAMING WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Too strong: the battery is NOT the evidence the harness commits did not break the emulator -- GIT IS. `git diff --name-only 1ba2cd4..6014b7e` minus regress/tools/docs leaves exactly the three #437 files, so no build input outside #437 changed and the harness commits COULD NOT have altered the binary. Too weak: the 16/16 IS evidence about those commits -- it is the first end-to-end execution of their product, 16/16 with 0 skipped means no gate silently dropped out, and the selfmutant controls DETECTED in this run.
* AND A FRAMING ERROR I REPEATED TWICE TODAY: diskimage_sync() does NOT sit on a path 'every rig's disk traffic crosses'. ONLY command 0x35 reaches it; ordinary READ/WRITE cross diskimage_scsicommand() but not the sync handler. The blast radius is narrower than I said.

* Q3 NO EMERGENCY RE-RUN for 20ce22e and 7e3b120 -- every changed line is gate 2's surface or non-battery tooling, and the binary is bit-identical by construction, so a full battery would re-measure 14 unchanged gates against an unchanged binary: ritual, not evidence. * Q4 VACUITY, NAMED NOT SURVEYED: (1) gate_asan_sweep is a CONSTRUCTION sweep -- 37 machine types construct under ASan and nothing more, so *** #437's NEW CODE HAS NEVER RUN UNDER ASan ***; (2) gate_hygiene's pattern set contains ZERO occurrences of sync/sense/sd0, so the new guest-visible error class is invisible to it; (3) gate_arm passed 16/16 WITH armbdt PRESENT -- not hypothetical, the measured LDM/STM defect was live at this HEAD; (4) selftest_mutation's green means ONE differential of eleven can fail, and its apparatus carries smhang/smnotland unfixed; (5) gate_ab is coarse rather than vacuous -- marker parity 1:1:1 accepted ~0.44% instruction drift. CHECKED CLEAN: gate_upstream's empty-both-sides hole is closed, gate 5 carries mutant-derived NINSTRS floors, and the old prompt-predicate hole in arm_flags_probe.py is CLOSED (its own 7-day-old memory note claiming otherwise is stale).

rows.title: idesync  IDE FLUSH CACHE has no durability path at all -- #437 is SCSI-only

entries.note: grep -i flush src/devices/dev_wdc.c returns NOTHING, so a guest's ATA FLUSH CACHE is not merely unflushed but unimplemented. Reachability UNKNOWN; landisk is the ATA rig and it boots, so a probe witness is likely available.  [panel_20260818_095322]

*** THE BRIEF'S FRAMING WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE HALF IT GOT WRONG CHANGES WHAT SHOULD BE FIXED. *** Verdict FIX-not-document, but not for the reason I gave it.
* 0xE7 WDCC_FLUSHCACHE is DEFINED at wdcreg.h:130 and NEVER REFERENCED in dev_wdc.c; 0xEA has no constant anywhere in src/. Both fall to wdc_command()'s default:, which sets WDCE_ABRT, emits an UNLATCHED fatal(), and -- the part that matters -- does NOT set d->int_assert. MEASURED offline against the shipping wdc_command(): 0xE7 -> err=0x04 irq=0 fatal=1, status 0x51 (DRDY|DSC|ERR), against the 0x10 RECAL control at err=0x00 irq=1.
* NO REAL GUEST ISSUES IT, and the negative is WELL CONTROLLED. With an IDE disk attached and a full filesystem lifecycle (MAKEDEV, fdisk, disklabel, newfs 64 MB FFS, mount, write, sync, umount, halt -p) OpenBSD 7.6 issues exactly: 0xEC 0xF5 0x10 0x91 0xC6 0x20 0xC4 0x30 0xC5 0xE0. No 0xE7, no 0xEA.
* IT REFUTED ITS OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS rather than resting on it: 'the drive does not advertise FLUSH CACHE' was tested with TWO discriminating IDENTIFY variants (word 83=0x5000 and 0x7000). The guest DEMONSTRABLY READ the new IDENTIFY -- it began issuing 0xEF SET FEATURES, which it never did before -- and STILL never flushed. Why OpenBSD declines is an honest UNKNOWN: there is no OpenBSD source in this tree, and reconstructing wd_flushcache from memory is exactly the trap the SH-manual rule exists to prevent.
* *** THE LIVE DEFECT IS THE ARM, NOT THE OPCODE: 0xE0 STANDBY IMMEDIATE hits the same default: on EVERY `halt -p`, measured 4 of 4 shutdown runs. *** ABRT to the guest, no interrupt, unlatched host warning, and the guest swallows it silently. So the IDE side has a reachable reproducible fall-through TODAY, and FLUSH CACHE is an unreached member of the same set.
* THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINER. diskimage_sync() takes a struct diskimage *, but dev_wdc.c only ever holds (machine, id, type) -- and THERE IS NO EXPORTED (machine,id,type) -> struct lookup; every public function in diskimage.c open-codes the same 6-line walk. Needs a diskimage_sync_id() wrapper, a WDCC_FLUSHCACHE_EXT constant, and a case arm that also sets int_assert. Built privately: 0xE7/0xEA become err=0x00 irq=1 fatal=0 with trace F(data) S(data), matching the SCSI sibling.
* DETECTOR BUILT, and it COMPILES AGAINST BOTH TREES because the rows pass a RAW OPCODE INTEGER rather than the WDCC_ constant -- deliberately sidestepping the exact trap diff_diskimage_sync.c's header records, where naming the new symbol made the pre-fix arm a SETUP result. 9 rows / 0 failed pre-fix; 8 of 9 flip post-fix. Needs only two extra stubs given the flags gate_offline.sh already passes.
* SCOPE: all three files are byte-identical between est/ and GXEMUL-SEC/. And wdc is far from landisk-only -- bus_isa, bus_pci, dev_pcic, dev_ps2_spd, machine_arc.c:235, machine_landisk.c:87 and promemul/of.c all instantiate it, so ARC IS A SECOND ATA RIG THAT WAS NOT TESTED.  [agent idesync 2026-08-19]

*** DOCUMENT, DO NOT FIX -- AND THE DECIDING FACT IS ONE NOBODY RAISED: THE DRIVE NEVER ADVERTISES FLUSH CACHE. ***  The highest IDENTIFY word wdc_initialize_identify_struct() writes is 68. Words 82-87 -- the COMMAND SET SUPPORTED / ENABLED block -- are left ZERO by the opening memset. A device that advertises no command sets and aborts a command it never claimed is not obviously wrong. On that reading idesync is a MISSING FEATURE, not a durability defect, and the 'correct' fix is a much larger IDENTIFY change that collides with diff_wdc_identify.c's explicit frozen-scope banner (#405/#407/#408/#410/#411).

The negative control is stronger than claimed and still does not rescue the row: word 83 = 0x5000/0x7000 sets the validity marker plus the flush bits, the guest demonstrably read the new block, and it STILL never flushed. With words 82, 85 and 86 zero the block is internally inconsistent, which is a plausible reason a driver would decline -- but that is a HYPOTHESIS, and 'why OpenBSD declines' remains an honest UNKNOWN.

The wrapper claim is CHECKED TRUE: diskimage.c open-codes the machine->first_diskimage walk TWELVE times (:113, 321, 340, 360, 385, 1558, 2120, 2130, 2149, 2177, 2198, 2310); a diskimage_sync_id() would be the thirteenth.

entries.note:
*** THE ENTRY I WROTE EARLIER TODAY CARRIED A REFUTED CLAIM AND HAS BEEN REPLACED BY THIS
ONE (1 entry removed, its content quoted below).  Caught by an adjudicating seat BEFORE
ANYTHING WAS STAGED, so this is L1 construction, not a shipped wrong record. ***

**IT SAID: "no FLUSH constant exists in this tree's ATA headers".  FALSE.**
`src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h:130` is `#define WDCC_FLUSHCACHE 0xe7`.

**AND THE RECORDED EVIDENCE COULD NOT HAVE PRODUCED THE RECORDED CONCLUSION.**  I ran a
`grep -rn FLUSH src/include/` piped through `head -6` -- there are **46** hits -- and read a
TRUNCATION as an ABSENCE, under a label reading 'blank = the constant does not exist' while
the output was not blank.  *The apparatus-failure class, committed inside a record whose own
closing note warns about it.*  **Three siblings already held the right answer and none was
consulted**: this row's own CONFIRMED research entry of 2026-08-19, `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` at
the same fact, and the header itself.

FIVE REPAIRS, each re-verified by me against the tree before writing:

**(1) The correct fact is STRONGER than the false one.**  The constant is DEFINED and
**referenced ZERO times in `dev_wdc.c`**, so 0xE7 falls to `default:` BY CONSTRUCTION.  0xEA
(FLUSH CACHE EXT) has no constant under `src/` at all and belongs in scope too -- the
2026-08-19 research covered both; my scope line covered only 0xE7.

**(2) '18 of 256 words' dropped a qualifier: they are 18 SITES, not 18 words.**  Three are
memcpys spanning ranges -- word 10 a 20-byte serial (10-19), word 23 an 8-byte firmware
(23-26), word 27 a 40-byte model (27-46) -- so ~49 words are written.  **The load-bearing
fact is better stated as a CEILING: the highest word touched is 68**, so words 82-87 keep the
memset's zero.  A stronger form of the same conclusion: word 83 = 0x0000 also fails the bits
15:14 = 01b validity signature, so a conforming host discards the whole word -- the drive
advertises NO VALID COMMAND-SET INFORMATION AT ALL, not merely a cleared flush bit.

**(3) The arm census missed `case SET_FEATURES:` (0xEF).**  It is defined in `wdcreg.h`
WITHOUT the `WDCC_` prefix, so my prefix-keyed grep could not see it.  Twenty case labels, not
nineteen; none a flush.  *A count claiming completeness from an instrument blind to a member.*

**(4) THE WARRANT HIERARCHY WAS INVERTED, and this is the substantive one.**  I presented
'the drive never advertises it' as *the whole content* of the disposition.  The row's research
entry measured something stronger AND partly contrary: OpenBSD 7.6 through a full filesystem
lifecycle issued `0xEC 0xF5 0x10 0x91 0xC6 0x20 0xC4 0x30 0xC5 0xE0` -- no 0xE7, no 0xEA --
**and with word 83 forced to 0x5000/0x7000 the guest demonstrably READ the new block (it began
issuing 0xEF) and STILL never flushed.**  opus5 therefore demoted the advertise-reason: why
OpenBSD declines *remains an honest UNKNOWN*.  **The MEASUREMENT is the warrant; the IDENTIFY
fact is what a CONFORMING guest is entitled to conclude.**  I had re-derived a compressed
one-clause version of a multi-factor review -- unanimity with a stated premise, where I
verified the arithmetic of a claim whose causal story the row's own evidence had already
demoted to hypothesis.

**(5) Point 3 under-cited: `#485` belongs beside `#464`.**  The `default:` arm carries BOTH
outside the latch guard -- `d->error |= WDCE_ABRT` (#464) and `d->int_assert = 1` (#485).
**Without #485 the honest abort was POLLING-ONLY**; an interrupt-driven guest saw nothing at
all.  Citing only #464 claimed an abort that three days earlier would not have been delivered.

*** THE POLARITY CONTRAST SURVIVES BUT MUST NOT TRAVEL UNQUALIFIED. ***  IDE's `default:`
aborts honestly; SCSI's reports success (`b120u`).  **But `dev_wdc.c:1515` routes ATAPI packet
commands into `diskimage_scsicommand()`, and dev_wdc treats `res == 1` as success** -- so an
unknown PACKET command on an IDE ATAPI drive takes the SUCCESS polarity THROUGH the wdc
device.  One device, both polarities, selected by path.  **Deliberately NOT minted as a
carrier line**: it is an instance-pair, not a rule, and the qualifier it needs makes it a
paragraph -- an unqualified line would be the dropped-qualifier class itself.  It lands in the
record and as a cross-reference on `b120u`, whose fixer gains a second reachability route.

DISPOSITION UNCHANGED AND RATIFIED: **ASSESSED, NOT CHANGED.**  Witness `none`, in the honest
form: *a non-event admits no rung-3/4 witness (a ceiling four seat entries already record);
the non-issuance claim itself is carried by the measured lifecycle census of 2026-08-19.*  The
2026-08-27 ask-one-seat ruling is satisfied in substance -- the attempt question was answered
in-row by measurement, not skipped.

Artifact: `regress/artifacts/idesync/assessed_not_changed_20260829.md`, rewritten with all
five repairs and the correction kept IN PLACE rather than silently swapped.

rows.title: wdcnoirq  wdc_command()'s default: arm asserts no interrupt, so an interrupt-driven guest waits for a completion that never comes

entries.note: MEASURED. The arm sets WDCE_ABRT and returns without setting d->int_assert, and dev_wdc_tick() raises the IRQ only when that flag is set. A polling driver sees ABRT; an interrupt-driven one sees nothing at all. Live TODAY via 0xE0 on every halt -p, not only via the unimplemented flush. That an interrupt-waiting driver would then hit a wdc timeout is READ/inference -- no guest was observed doing it.  [agent idesync 2026-08-19]

entries.note:
*** THE WARRANT IS REPLACED, NOT STRENGTHENED, AND THE PACKET-FED SEAT IS WHY. ***

My warrant was in-file consistency: three abort arms assert, two do not, and SET_FEATURES
aborts an unimplemented SUB-command and asserts anyway.  The kimi-k3:cloud substitute
refused it on a reading I had not made: `d->int_assert = 1` sits AFTER the inner switch,
COMMON TO BOTH SUBPATHS, so `/* TODO: always interrupt? */` most plausibly scopes to the
SUCCESS path -- and the two clean precedents are the 'cannot execute at all' class, which
supports a DELIBERATE-DESIGN reading of the 3:2 split rather than an oversight.  Its
conclusion: the convention was never settled by the author, so this round CHOOSES it, and
the choice must be grounded in a sibling-device check rather than in a headcount.

SURVEY RUN.  `dev_mb89352.c`, the SCSI sibling, computes its assert as:

    bool assert = d->reg[INTS] != 0;
    if (!(d->reg[SCTL] & SCTL_INTR_ENAB)) assert = false;
    if (d->reg[SCTL] & SCTL_DISABLE)      assert = false;

*** IT ASSERTS ON ANY NON-ZERO INTERRUPT STATUS, WITHOUT REGARD TO WHETHER THE COMMAND
SUCCEEDED. ***  `INTS_CMD_DONE` is set for completions generally.  So the in-tree
convention is COMPLETION INTERRUPTS, ERROR OR NOT -- which is the fix, grounded in a
sibling model rather than in a tally of arms inside the same function.

*** AND THE SURVEY PRODUCED A CAUTION I DID NOT HAVE: THE SIBLING GATES ON AN
INTERRUPT-ENABLE BIT AND wdc DOES NOT. ***  `SCTL_INTR_ENAB` is wdc's `nIEN` analogue.
None of wdc's asserting arms consults it.

That is NOT this fix's problem, and the codex seat established why independently in the
same panel: on landisk the guest's Device Control writes land on UNMAPPED MEMORY (6 writes
diskless, 12 with a disk), because there is no LANDISK case in DEVINIT's alt-status address
switch.  **nIEN is already a no-op on that machine** -- filed as `landiskaux`.  So the fix
cannot break nIEN gating that does not exist, and adding the gating belongs with the round
that maps the register.

*The seat that produced the better warrant could not read a single file. It reasoned from
the packet, found the flaw in my argument, and named the check that would settle it.*

entries.note:
*** THE HARM CLAIM IN THIS ENTRY IS OVERSTATED AND IS CORRECTED BELOW IT (L4, 2026-08-27). ***  The ledger's own `wdcstandby` measurements are a counter-instance: OpenBSD 7.6 reaches BOTH defective arms routinely and COMPLETES boot and shutdown against today's no-interrupt behaviour, 4 of 4.  There is no measured hang. Whether a timeout interval is burned is NOT SETTLED.  Read 'waits forever' / 'functional hang' below as the hypothesis it was, not as a measurement.

VERDICT: PROCEED, one round, two hunks -- on a warrant STRONGER than the brief claimed and
a severity WEAKER than the brief claimed.  Both corrections are against my own text.

*** THE CENSUS IS NOT 3-OF-5 ABORT ARMS.  IT IS 11 OF 13 TERMINAL ARMS. ***  Every arm that
terminates a command -- success or abort -- sets int_assert.  The only arms that do not are
WRITE and ATAPI_PKT_CMD, where the command is NOT OVER (the interrupt comes later in the
data path, and PKT_CMD records its 'no' as a COMMENTED-OUT line) -- plus the two defect
arms, which ARE terminal.  Five arms carry a `/* TODO: interrupt here? */` hedge and every
one resolves to assert.  So the two defect arms are the ONLY TERMINAL ARMS IN THE FUNCTION
WITH NO INTERRUPT DECISION RECORDED AT ALL -- no assert, no comment.  That reads as a
question never reached, not a decision to stay silent.

*** AND THE STEELMAN'S FACTUAL PREMISE IS FALSE BY THIS PROJECT'S OWN MEASUREMENTS. ***
0xF5 SEC_FREEZE_LOCK -- the SEC arm -- is issued on a plain OpenBSD 7.6/landisk boot with a
disk attached (rung 4).  0xE0 STANDBY IMMEDIATE -- the default arm -- on every `halt -p`,
4 of 4.  A stock guest lifecycle reaches BOTH defective arms routinely.  It is not 242
opcodes nobody sends; it is two boot/shutdown opcodes plus a long tail the tree's own header
names (WDCC_SMART, WDCC_FLUSHCACHE).

nIEN: VERIFIED STRONGER THAN HOPED.  `WDCTL_IDS` (0x02) exists in wdcreg.h and is referenced
NOWHERE in dev_wdc.c.  The model has no nIEN state to be inconsistent with.

*** SEVERITY DEMOTED, AND THIS IS AN L4 AGAINST THIS SEAT'S OWN PRIOR ENTRIES. ***  My
ledger text said 'an interrupt-driven guest waits forever' and 'boot-reachable functional
hang'.  The ledger holds a MEASURED COUNTER-INSTANCE: the same OpenBSD guest reaches both
arms routinely and COMPLETES BOOT AND SHUTDOWN against today's no-interrupt behaviour --
`wdcstandby`, 'the guest swallows it silently', 4 of 4.  Whether it burns a timeout interval
is NOT SETTLED; nobody timed it.  HONEST SEVERITY: routine rung-4 reachability of a protocol
violation, measured harm today NONE OBSERVED, hypothesised harm unmeasured.  The round is
licensed by protocol correctness at trivial cost, not by dramatised harm.

*** THE REPRO IS AT THE WRONG REVISION. ***  PREFIX_committed_ed3f9cc.out was produced at
ed3f9cc; HEAD is cf300c0, four commits and 135 dev_wdc.c lines later.  #484 touched the ring
producer, not the command switch -- but 'almost certainly unaffected' is exactly what
test-first exists to refuse, and the score-names-its-artifact rule forbids citing an
ed3f9cc log as this round's pre-fix red.  RE-RUN BEFORE ANY EDIT.

CLAUSE (d) FOR A FIX THAT ADDS NO PREDICATE -- the mutant is M_latch: put `int_assert = 1`
INSIDE the `warned_unimpl_cmd` guard.  The first unknown command per device interrupts and
every later one hangs again -- exactly what a tidying maintainer writes.  *** THE CURRENT
SWEEP IS BLIND TO IT BY CONSTRUCTION: one fresh device per opcode means the latch is 0 on
every leg. ***  (The glm seat reached the same finding independently from the packet.)  Owed
row: two different unimplemented opcodes on ONE device, demanding a wire assert on the
SECOND and exactly one fatal line total.

M_blanket: hoist a single assert to after the switch -- 'fixes' all 242 and silently breaks
the phase protocol for ATAPI_PKT_CMD and WRITE.  Owed: negative rows pinning irq == 0 at
dispatch for both.  That is the de-escalation clause's accept side.

THIRD OBSERVABLE: THE DEASSERT EDGE.  int_assert is a LEVEL -- the tick re-asserts every
tick until a status read clears it.  A two-observable sweep cannot tell a completion event
from a stuck line.  One register read per leg converts the detector from 'an edge happened'
to 'the completion protocol works'.

scores the flood probe, so this round's gate would be BORN RED for a known unrelated cause
and mis-attributed to it.  Then #485.  Then the wdcsectorreset/wdcflagindep pair.

rows.state_note:
*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and GUEST-REACHABLE. It is the SAME DEFECT SHAPE as [[b120]] in a different device family, which is the part worth carrying. ***

With an IDE disk attached, `wdc_command()`'s `default:` arm sets `WDCE_ABRT` but **never sets `int_assert`**, and `dev_wdc_tick()` raises the IRQ only when that latch is set. So an unsupported command is refused **without the completion interrupt an interrupt-driven guest is waiting for.**

> *** THE FAMILY: an unsupported command's `default:` arm omits the COMPLETION SIGNAL the guest is blocked on. *** [[b120]] is the SCSI form -- no status byte, so the guest is told GOOD. This is the IDE form -- no interrupt, so the guest is told nothing at all. **Two device families, one omission.** Whichever is fixed first should be checked against the other, and the reviewer question generalises: *does this `default:` arm complete the protocol, or only decline the command?*

**Guest-reachable** (seat cites an existing record, not re-run): on landisk, clear any prior IRQ with a status read, then write an unsupported command code and wait.

**Observable:** guest IRQ delivery -- whether execution reaches the landisk interrupt vector after the refused command.

**Honest limit, and the seat stated it rather than hiding it:** the *indefinite guest wait* in the title is REASONED, not observed. The missing IRQ is READ from the source; that it hangs a real driver forever is an inference. Do not carry the hang as measured.

ALL THREE of agy's checkable claims were VERIFIED against source rather than credited: the endianness branch, the buffer arithmetic, and that wdc_get_inbuf() is called once per BYTE inside 16/32-bit transfers (:616, :620, :622, :623 little-endian; :627, :629, :630 big-endian), which is exactly the measured 4 lines per 32-bit guest load.  *** FULL PASS-1 PANEL COMPLETE (panel_20260825_195526): 8 SEATS ANSWERED. *** codex 501 KB, grok 19.5 KB, minimax 13.6 KB, agy 13.2 KB, kimi-k3:cloud 10.8 KB (the SUBSTITUTE transport, fired by hand -- the CLI is 403-walled), glm 4.4 KB, deepseek 4.1 KB.
