CHECKED: of the eight, `gdromcondlies` covers exactly TWO (:639 GDROM_UNKNOWN_0x88 and :699 GDROM_COND, the BADVAL pair). *** THE OTHER SIX HAD NO OPEN CARRIER AT ALL, *** so a census that read as 'filed' was really six live guest-reachable host-kill sites sitting in nobody's queue -- the 'half a census reads as a whole one' hazard one level up, where the census is complete and the QUEUE is not. THE SIX, with line numbers re-derived 2026-08-23 after the last edit to the file: :294 'GDROM Read TOC not 408 bytes?'; :346 'unimplemented data format 0x%02x'; :424 handle_command default, 'unimplemented command 0x%02x'; :600 'Too much GDROM_DATA?'; :804 'DMA transfer but d->data is NULL'; :820 the DMA arming-mismatch report. The first four are command-layer, reachable through GDROM_DATA packets; the last two are the DMA+0x18 pair. RANKING NOTE: the DMA pair is the interesting half, because #461 made the surrounding window survivable, so a guest can now reach +0x18 without dying on the way -- and one nonzero store there still ends the host. It is also the blocker gdromdmawidth is gated behind: the row that would pin that item's real contract cannot be built until these two exits go.

TODO') observed first -- site :820, the arming-mismatch report, reached because count (+0x0c) and enable (+0x14) are both 0 on a fresh device so the `dma_reg[3] == 1 && dma_reg[5] == 1` test fails. entries.note: *** SETTLED THE codex/grok SPLIT EMPIRICALLY, AND BOTH SIDES WERE PARTLY WRONG. *** It re-fetched mainline drivers/cdrom/gdrom.c: the post-trigger wait is wait_event_interruptible_timeout(..., GDROM_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) = HZ*7, and the pre-trigger poll is guarded by time_before(jiffies, timeout) with HZ/2. EVERY WAIT IN THE DMA PATH IS TIME-BOUNDED, so a decline lands on a 7-second timeout -> BLK_STS_IOERR -> EIO. Degraded and bounded, NOT a hang: codex's and glm's central fear does not materialise. *** BUT IT FOUND THE MECHANISM NEITHER SIDE NAMED, AND THE FOUR-ROUND IDIOM WALKS STRAIGHT INTO IT. *** The DMA window's tail store runs after every aligned break. The SUCCESS arm sets `idata = 0` before breaking -- which is why a completed transfer polls idle -- and both exits die BEFORE the tail. So 'keep the diagnostic, drop exit(1)', the shape #447/#459/#460/#461 all used, lets the guest's trigger value 1 flow into dma_reg[6] and *** +0x18 READS BUSY FOREVER. *** For Linux that is a bounded HZ/2 tax per transfer; for a guest that waits the NetBSD way -- its own control-window waits are unbounded spins, fetched verbatim -- it is a real hang. Fix is one line per declined arm: `idata = 0` before break, mirroring the success arm. *** AND FIRING THE COMPLETION EVENT IS THE ACTIVELY HARMFUL OPTION, the opposite of what the brief asked about. *** gdrom_dma_interrupt clears gd.transfer UNCONDITIONALLY and checks no error bit anywhere, so firing SYSASIC_EVENT_GDROM_DMA on an empty transfer exits the wait with BLK_STS_OK -- the block layer is told the read succeeded when zero bytes moved, and the guest consumes whatever was in the destination page AS DISK DATA. That is #460's invented-behaviour class reproduced at the block layer. The driver has exactly one error channel, the timeout, so 7-second EIO is not a compromise but the only honest signal available. IT ALSO STRENGTHENED THE ROUND'S WARRANT: :804 is a COMPLIANT-GUEST path today. gdrom_readdisk_dma writes the four DMA registers before sending packet 0x30; if diskimage_access fails on a short image, or OB-20's sector clamp rejects the request, handle_command leaves d->data == NULL and Linux -- told nothing it checks -- byte-writes 1 to +0x18. On committed HEAD that is host death from a protocol-correct guest with an imperfect disk image, i.e. two shipped defensive declines currently feed a host kill. CORRECTED THE WITNESS CLAIM, precisely: only :820 had been measured; :804 needs three stores and 'test-first is not satisfied by a sibling's witness'. Measured in response -- arming with no staged data kills the host, own diagnostic seen, control with trigger=0 survives. CORRECTED THE SCOPE AND THE TITLE: :600 is NOT guest-reachable (busy&0x08 is set only by COND=0xa0 which zeroes cmd_count; increments are +2; at exactly 12 the flag clears), so 'six guest-reachable' was false for it -- AND it should stay fatal because it has MEASURED value as an invariant tripwire: #460's rejected Option C was caught precisely because it made :600 reachable. De-fatalising it would delete the one accidental detector of the cmd_count invariant. The census is also EIGHT sites, not six; :639/:699 are carried by gdromcondlies, so the arithmetic was defensible but the brief never stated the exclusion and the seat had to consult the ledger to avoid re-filing them. L4 NIT FOR THE ROUND: the transfer diagnostic prints `length` (the guest's +0x08 value) while the code transfers d->data_len -- so it lies in exactly the sessions where the discrepancy matters. One word, inside the hunk being edited.

entries.note: [panel_20260823_230930] *** DO NOT SHIP -- the lone dissent, and it found the one hole that mattered. Its verdict is explicitly about the DETECTOR: 'The C hunk does not need a redesign.' *** The finding: firing SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT on a declined path PASSES EVERY ROW, because nothing reads the pending register. That is exactly the mutant the flagship seat identified as ACTIVELY HARMFUL -- worse than the defect this round fixes, since gdrom_dma_interrupt() clears gd.transfer unconditionally with no error check, so a completion signalled on an empty transfer returns BLK_STS_OK and the guest consumes the destination page as disk data. A host death is loud; that is silent. The flagship seat had SPECIFIED that row in its design and the round did not build it -- grok caught the omission by measuring rather than by re-reading the design. It also named the observable precisely (SYSASIC_BASE 0x5f6900, pending_irq[0] at offset 0, bit 14 = 0x4000, guest-readable), which is why the row could be written immediately. TWO records defects in its list were live: check_probe_wiring still said '32 rows', and a constant insertion had stranded DMA's comment on GDROM_DATAP so a CONTROL-window address was labelled 'the DMA window, SEPARATELY registered'. Both fixed.

entries.note: *** SEAT DIED ON AN API 529 (server-side overload) MID-RUN -- recorded as a SEAT FAILURE, never as agreement, and re-fired once because a 529 is TRANSPORT and not a wall. *** But it got its decisive measurement out first, and it is the one that settles the round's detector question. IT CONFIRMED THE COMPLETION EVENT IS OBSERVABLE BY AN ORDINARY GUEST LOAD at 0xa05f6900 (ASIC pending_irq[0], bit 14 = 0x4000), and measured both harmful mutants individually:                     fix      m_event_null   m_event_else fresh               0x0      0x0            0x0 nodata decline      0x0      0x4000         0x0 arm decline         0x0      0x0            0x4000 accept              0x4000   0x4000         0x4000 *** THE LAST ROW IS THE FINDING: `accept` reads 0x4000 under ALL THREE BUILDS, so an accept-only row could NEVER have caught either mutant. *** It takes the DECLINE rows reading 0x0 -- which is exactly the pair added on grok's finding (`nodata quiet` and `accept event`). So the measurement says both are load-bearing and neither is redundant: grok predicted the gap by reading, this seat measured both halves of it, and the two mutants are separable rather than one defect seen twice.

entries.note: L1 RESTRUCTURE APPLIED ON OWNER DECISION: the four accept rows now share ONE staging session instead of four. *** THE SHARING IS THE POINT, NOT THE SAVING. *** Four independent TOC stagings meant the rows observed four SIMILAR transfers; driven from one session they observe THE SAME transfer, so 'it ran', '+0x18 polls idle', 'the event fired' and 'no decline fired' are four facts about ONE event. A row set describing one transfer can contradict itself and be caught; four separate transfers can each be individually consistent and jointly wrong. It also fixes the 1800s budget overrun that gate 10 would have inherited (filed as probeslow). Verified: one staging occurrence where there were two, one session driving all four rows, row count unchanged at 44, no name near the 12-char column limit. THE SUPERSEDED RUN IS NOT WASTED -- it measured the pre-restructure form at 44/44 with the decisive pair reading in OPPOSITE directions (`nodata quiet` clear, `accept event` set), which is the cross-check that makes the restructured version comparable rather than a fresh guess.

entries.note: *** THE ROUND'S DECISIVE MEASUREMENT, PRODUCED BY A SEAT THAT HAD NEVER BEEN ASKED TO BUILD C IN THIS PROJECT, DURING AN OUTAGE OF BOTH SEATS THAT NORMALLY DO. *** Mutant: delete ONLY the `idata = 0;` in the `d->data == NULL` arm -- leaving the latch, the diagnostic and the `break`. That is precisely what the #447/#459/#460/#461 idiom would have produced, so the mutant IS the obvious fix. MEASURED 43/44, reddening `nodata idle` ALONE, at value 0x1 against an expected 0x0. *** THE VALUE IS THE POINT: 0x1 is the guest's own trigger value, stuck in dma_reg[6] by the tail store -- exactly the mechanism the flagship seat predicted by reading the TAIL of the function rather than the arm being edited. *** So the prediction chain closes end to end: predicted by reading, row written from the prediction, kill measured independently, and the observed value matches the predicted one rather than merely being non-zero. AND THE ISOLATION IS AS IMPORTANT AS THE KILL: `arm idle` stays GREEN (it pins the other site, correctly unaffected) and `nodata quiet` stays GREEN (the completion event is not involved). One mutant, one row -- so `nodata idle` is neither vacuous nor redundant, and the two idle rows are separable rather than one property observed twice. SEAT NOTE: agy built its own binary in /tmp/gxagy, applied the mutant correctly (2 `idata = 0;` against the repo's 3), ran the 44-row probe against it, and left the repo untouched -- verified rather than trusted, since it runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions and the brief is the only thing keeping it out.

entries.note: ROUND SUMMARY, recorded under the adjudicator seat because this ledger has one entry per seat and no panel-wide value -- the per-finding attributions inside the note are the accurate ones. PASS 2: nine seats fired, nine answered, none down. Verdicts grok DO-NOT-SHIP, codex CHANGES-REQUIRED, fable5 code-sound-but-not-on-this-record, opus5 ship-code-fix-detector, agy GO, glm PASS, deepseek ACCEPT, minimax APPROVE, kimi PASS. *** THE FIVE APPROVING SEATS WERE RIGHT ABOUT THE CODE AND WRONG ABOUT WHAT THE DETECTOR PROVED. *** The code needed ONE fix; the detector needed SEVEN rows, all from the four seats that pushed back -- a vote would have shipped a detector blind to every escape. Rows added and what each closes: arm halfarm (repair conditioned on count/enable, which a FRESH device satisfies and every existing row used a fresh device); nodata len (conditioned on programmed LENGTH -- no row wrote +0x08); arm bytetrig (conditioned on access WIDTH -- no row byte-stored +0x18, and this tree already documented Linux byte-writes it; also triggers with 0x5a since every other row triggers with 1 and `idata &= ~1u` would have passed); arm quiet (L3 undischarged obligation -- the arming arm had NO completion-event row); arm twice (repair moved INSIDE the latch block -- every idle row triggers once in a freshly forked emulator); accept data (NOTHING anywhere observed the DMA's data movement, and it implements the device-signature control the comment already claimed); both decl (the two arms collapsed onto ONE warn bit, unobservable because no session reached both arms -- predicted BEFORE the table ran). entries.note:
*** THE SIX SITES ARE NOT ONE EDIT.  THEY ARE THREE CLASSES, AND TWO OF THEM CORRUPT IF
THE exit(1) IS SIMPLY DELETED. ***  This is the round's design finding and it is the
carrier's own 'dropping exit(1) alone would have...' trap, live at two sites.

CLASS B -- BARE REMOVAL CORRUPTS.  An explicit decline is MANDATORY, not stylistic:

  :662  guard `if (d->cmd_count >= 12)`, and the struct declares `uint8_t cmd[12]`.
        Deleting the exit runs `d->cmd[d->cmd_count++] = idata;` TWICE with
        cmd_count >= 12 -- an out-of-bounds WRITE past a 12-byte array inside the
        device struct.  The kill is currently the only thing preventing it.
  :357  guard `if (d->cnt != 408)`, and the next statement is `alloc_data(d)`, which
        does `d->data_len = d->cnt; malloc(d->data_len); memset(...)`.  Deleting the
        exit allocates `cnt` bytes where the TOC writer below expects 408 -- a heap
        UNDER-allocation for any cnt < 408, and malloc(0) at cnt == 0.

CLASS A -- BARE REMOVAL IS SAFE, because the enclosing control flow already does the
right thing:

  :486  `default:` in handle_command().  Falling through reaches the common tail, and
        the tail is CORRECT for an unhandled command: d->data is NULL, so it takes the
        else branch, sets d->cnt = 0, clears COND_DATA_AVAIL, and fires
        SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT.  That is precisely 'the command did nothing' reported
        properly.
        *** AND AN EARLY `return` HERE WOULD SKIP SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT AND LEAVE THE
        GUEST WAITING FOREVER.  The sketch rule's exact failure mode, live at this
        site. ***  Any proposed edit must be run against the real tail.
  :761  falls to a `break`.  Clean decline, no state mutation.
  :701  falls to a `break`.  Clean.

CLASS C -- THE FILE ALREADY DECIDED, ONE LINE UP:

  :409  the arm immediately above is `if (d->cmd[1] == 0x24) fatal("... Continuing
        anyway")` -- no exit.  So an unimplemented data format ALREADY continues for
        one value and dies for every other.  The precedent for surviving is in the
        same `if`/`else if`.
  :701  the same shape INSIDE ONE CASE: the READ arm's exit is already commented out
        (`// exit(1);`), only the WRITE arm still dies.

  *That asymmetry is a sibling-parity finding the round must put to the panel rather
  than resolve by tidying: somebody already judged that continuing is acceptable here,
  and the question is whether that judgement generalises or was specific to 0x24.*

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUND: the de-fatalisation option set must be chosen PER SITE, and
the two Class-B sites need the accept-side reasoning that clause (d) demands -- their
guards are load-bearing bounds checks wearing diagnostic clothing, so a mutant that
weakens `>= 12` or `!= 408` is squarely inside the DEPENDS-ON bound.

entries.ev: direct reading of the TOC arm, alloc_data(), free_data() and handle_command()'s head
entries.note:
*** TWO PREMISES I HAD ASSERTED WITHOUT CHECKING, BOTH CHALLENGED BY PACKET-FED SEATS THAT
COULD NOT SETTLE THEM FROM THE PACKET, NOW SETTLED BY READING.  ONE IS CONFIRMED AND IS
WORSE THAN I WROTE IT; THE OTHER'S DOUBT IS ANSWERED. ***

`:357` IS A GUEST-CONTROLLED HEAP OVERFLOW, not an under-allocation question.

  `alloc_data()` mallocs `d->cnt` bytes.  glm and deepseek both asked, independently and
  correctly, whether the TOC writer then writes `d->data_len` bytes (safe under any cnt) or
  a fixed 408 (unsafe below it).  Neither, and the answer is the bad one:

    memset(d->data, 0xff, d->cnt);        <- uses cnt, safe
    d->data[0*4] = ...  d->data[1*4] = ...  d->data[99*4] = ...
    d->data[100*4] = ...  d->data[101*4+3] = ...   <- HARDCODED indices

  Derived mechanically rather than by eye:
    grep -oE 'd->data\[[0-9]+\*4(\+[0-9])?\]' src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c
      -> highest byte index 407, so the writer needs 408 bytes REGARDLESS of cnt.

  `cnt` is guest-supplied.  So deleting the exit(1) yields `malloc(cnt)` followed by writes
  up to index 407 -- **an overflow of up to 408 bytes whose size the guest chooses**, and
  the exit(1) is currently the only thing preventing it.  `cnt == 0` gives malloc(0) plus
  the full 408.

  CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUND: `:357` and `:662` are not merely 'bare removal corrupts'.  Both
  guards are load-bearing BOUNDS CHECKS on guest-controlled quantities, and both fixes must
  decline BEFORE the guarded statement rather than after it.  That is a different fix design
  from the four unimplemented-command arms, which strengthens the case for Class B being its
  own round.

`:486`'s Class-A claim HOLDS, and deepseek's doubt is answered.  It asked whether `d->data`
is reliably NULL on entry to `default:`, since a stale non-NULL would make the common tail
set COND_DATA_AVAIL wrongly.  It is: `handle_command()` calls `free_data(d)` at `:343`
(tagged #465) before the switch, and free_data() sets `d->data = NULL` and `data_len = 0`.

AND A CLASSIFICATION ERROR OF MINE, found by glm: **`:701` appears in BOTH Class A and Class
C.**  It genuinely has both properties -- its WRITE arm falls to a `break`, and its READ
arm's exit(1) is already commented out -- but listing it twice without saying so may mean
the class boundary is drawn on the wrong axis.  Put to the adjudicator explicitly.

*Both settled premises came from seats that CANNOT READ FILES refusing to certify what a
brief asserted.  That is the packet-fed seats doing exactly what they are for, and it is the
second round running in which their refusal-to-ratify found a real hole.*

Its :662 refutation is CONFIRMED by reading, and it reverses a claim I made three times in committed records.  Its :357 refinement is sharper than my own and its round-scope proposal is better than mine.
entries.note:
VERDICT: DO NOT SHIP THIS AS SIX SITES / THREE CLASSES.  It refuted my taxonomy, my
reachability census, and my scope proposal -- and the refutations are in the tree.

*** :662 IS NOT GUEST-REACHABLE, AND MY RE-CENSUS SAID IT WAS.  I CONFIRMED THE REFUTATION
BY READING BEFORE RECORDING IT. ***

  `busy |= 0x08` has EXACTLY ONE WRITER (`:753`) and the very next line is
  `d->cmd_count = 0`.  Stores increment by TWO (`:665`, `:666`), and at `cmd_count == 12`
  the gate CLEARS (`:668`).  So the arm cannot be ENTERED with cmd_count >= 12: what
  prevents the overflow is the busy&0x08 gate plus the +2 stride landing exactly on 12 --
  **not the exit(1)**.

  *** AND THE RECORD WAS IN THE PRODUCT FILE ALL ALONG, TWENTY LINES ABOVE A SITE I WAS
  CENSUSING. ***  #460's own comment reads: 'the next write reaches the "Too much
  GDROM_DATA" exit -- OTHERWISE UNREACHABLE', and records that a proposed fix was REJECTED
  because it would have re-opened it ('A fix that re-opens a dead site is worse than the
  defect').  The 2026-08-26 witness design on this same row had already concluded 'NO
  TRIGGER ROUTE -> :662 -> document the invariant instead.'

  **MY 2026-08-27 RE-CENSUS CONFLATED 'the exit(1) is still in the file' WITH
  'guest-reachable'.**  Those are different questions and I asked only the first.  I then
  wrote 'the kill is currently the only thing preventing it' into three committed records.
  That is the unread-review class turned on a product comment: the answer was in the file
  I was censusing.

  DISPOSITION: **KEEP :662 FATAL.**  It is the measured tripwire for the cmd_count
  invariant, de-fatalising it buys no guest-facing safety, and it is the detector that
  caught #460's Option C.

:357 -- CLASS B HOLDS AND IS SHARPER THAN I PUT IT.  The memory-safety bound is
`cnt < 408`, NOT `cnt != 408`: cnt > 408 is a host-SAFE over-allocation, 1..407 is the
heap OOB, and cnt == 0 is malloc(0) then OOB **or** CHECK_ALLOCATION -> FAILURE() ->
another exit(1).  So the live guard is the stricter PROTOCOL check and the fix must decline
BEFORE alloc_data(), then `break` into the common tail -- never `return`.

:409 -- NOT A SAFETY CLASS AT ALL.  Deleting the exit does NOT OOB; it falls into the
2048-byte sector path and returns disk data AS IF the format were 0x20.  **Invented
success, not host corruption.**  And the 0x24 arm is a SPECIFIC exception -- if it
generalised, the `else if` would not exist.  Keep 0x24 continuing; latched `break` for every
other format.  It could not settle 0x24's hardware meaning from this tree and said so
rather than inventing one.

:486 -- fall-through is safe (free_data() at entry), the early-`return` warning is right,
but BARE DELETION leaves an UNLATCHED fatal() with no -q early-out: floodclass, in a
function a guest can call in a loop.  *** AND ITS SHARPEST POINT: Linux's GET SENSE is
packet 0x13, so `default:` is hit by a COMPLIANT DRIVER, not by junk opcodes. ***

:701 / :761 -- **already designed in `gdromcondlies`**, a different row, and Class A is
FALSE for :761.  Pulling them here duplicates that row's work.

SCOPE, and it is better than mine: **take the three handle_command exits as ONE round** --
one semantic class, one fix design (decline + latched announce, break to the common tail),
one detector.  Leave :662 fatal.  Leave :701/:761 to gdromcondlies.

It also names a FIFTH option member my set lacked: **keep the kill** -- which is exactly
the right disposition for :662 and which a four-member set cannot express.

VERDICT: THREE implementation rounds among the FIVE reachable sites -- and it reached
`:662`'s exclusion INDEPENDENTLY of grok.

  1. `:357` ALONE -- malformed fixed-size TOC transfer, bounds-dominating decline.
  2. `:409` + `:486` TOGETHER -- unsupported packet selector/opcode, same common-tail
     decline and the same detector oracle.
  3. `:701` + `:761` TOGETHER -- already the `gdromcondlies` round.
  `:662` gets DOCUMENTATION or a separate internal-invariant hardening filing, **not
  de-fatalisation.**

'If gdromexitsix excludes the two sites already owned by gdromcondlies, then that carrier
becomes exactly two rounds: site 1, then sites 2+3.'

*** SO CODEX AND GROK AGREE ON EXCLUSIONS AND SPLIT ON GROUPING: grok says the three
handle_command exits are ONE round, codex says TWO (`:357` alone, then `:409`+`:486`). ***
That is a real disagreement about round scope and it goes to the adjudicator.  The
substance behind codex's split is that `:357`'s decline is BOUNDS-dominating while
`:409`/`:486` are protocol declines sharing one oracle -- which is the same distinction I
drew as Class B vs Class A, arriving at a different grouping.

AND IT KILLED ONE OF MY PROPOSED CHEAPER DISCRIMINATORS for the closure gate: **'A
distinguishable nonzero emulator exit code is not acceptable -- it merely reintroduces a
host kill under a different number.'**  Its alternative is oracle STRENGTHENING rather than
expectation correction: assert the failure, show the correct probe green, flip `cmd[0]` and
`cmd[1]` independently in probe mutants and show those red, then de-fatalise and show the
same mutants still red.  It notes this is why requiring the unmodified product to go RED
would be inappropriate here -- the oracle-correction order does not apply to strengthening.

the equality clears the flag -- so at the guard `cmd_count` is in {0,2,4,6,8,10} and the
predicate is UNSATISFIABLE.  Then it found `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md:8274`, which already says

wrong by one** -- plus the in-file `#460` comment.  My brief re-litigated a settled
adjudication without citing it.

  load-bearing bounds checks on GUEST-CONTROLLED quantities'.  `d->cnt` is guest-controlled;
  **`cmd_count` is device-internal and cannot reach the guard.**

(b) `:701`/`:761` ARE CARRIED BY THE OPEN `gdromcondlies` ROW, whose pass-1 design already
exists and is BETTER than my Class-A treatment: decline must leave `d->cond` UNCHANGED,
decline rows must use NEIGHBOURS so mask-widening mutants cannot escape, the 0x88 diagnostic
needs a %x before content-keyed accept rows are possible.  The record even says a seat 'had
to consult the ledger to stop itself re-filing them' -- **and my brief is the next seat,
repeating it.**

(c) MY CLASS-A CLAIM FOR `:761` IS A WRONG RECORD.  `d->cond = idata` sits ABOVE both arms,
and `COND_DATA_AVAIL` is 0x08 -- so a declined store of 0x08 FORGES the flag the data port
consults.  Today the process dies before a guest can observe it; after a bare deletion it
can.  (`:701`'s write arm genuinely mutates nothing -- that half was right.)

SCOPE RULING: **Round 1 = `:357`/`:409`/`:486`** -- one function, one guest entry, one
decline semantics, one probe, and the closure-gate obligation lives entirely inside it.
**Round 2 = `gdromcondlies`.**  **`:662` = no round.**  My A/B/C axis is right for EDIT
CONTENT and wrong for ROUND BOUNDARIES -- and the `:701`-in-two-classes symptom is the proof.

and `:357`/`:409` in the other, **smearing the gdrompionull re-pin across two rounds**.

THE FIFTH OPTION MEMBER IS REAL AND MECHANICALLY UNAVAILABLE HERE, which is better than
either answer I had: a guest-visible ERROR decline exists in `dev_wdc.c`, but this model has
no error register, `update_stat()` regenerates `stat` on EVERY read so a latched bit is
overwritten before any guest sees it, and `cond`'s error semantics have no local oracle.
Add it as CONSIDERED AND DECLINED with that warrant, re-openable if `gdromdriverclaims` is
discharged.  **ACCEPT checked at all six: none qualifies** -- belief now checked.

THE OBLIGATION MY BRIEF MISSED ENTIRELY: **the latch-bit budget.**  Six of `warned`'s eight
bits are used; Round 1 adds up to three, and the seventh fires the PRE-SET `gdromwarnbits`
trigger -- widen `warned` and convert `GDROM_W_*` to an enum ending `_NBITS`.  Skipping it
is how `1u << 8` truncates to zero and the ninth latch floods silently.  agy raised the same
thing independently as an implementation blocker.

the probe's attribution rule is FILE-WIDE, so Round 2 erodes the same discriminator and owes

CLOSED when a tenth bit arrives.  The three grounds on which a disjointness assert was
rejected for `dev_sh4.c` were each checked and each fails here.  FILED for the owner.

is `{M_growA}`; `accept sil`'s is `{M_growA, Md_hoistannounce}` -- **a strict SUBSET.**  So
`accept sil` is proven non-redundant and **`acceptA` is not**.  KEEP BOTH is right, but on

It also found the 0x24 filing its own adjudicator had ruled forced existed nowhere (now created as `gdromfmt24`), that `stale how`'s kill attribution was FALSE as written (corrected in-round), and that `gdromdefaultstatusless` was materially advanced without knowing it.

The only early-answering seat with repo access, and the only one able to check the gate question at all -- which is itself the evidence for this panel's central finding.  Verified the gate section against the probe with line citations: denominator pinned at 20, name list enumerated and matched.

*** THE DEEPEST WORK OF THE PANEL, and it found the enum door INDEPENDENTLY of codex. ***  Two single-token enum aliases compile clean under `|` because an explicit duplicate enumerator drags GDROM_W_NBITS down with it and the OR equality re-balances.  **It then went further than any other seat: it worked out the RUNTIME half too** -- `crossbit` catches the (7,6) shape and `both sites` the (8,7) -- and independently MEASURED that `|` -> `+` refuses every shape it tested.  **And it named a THIRD shape it explicitly DECLINED to claim**: a TRIPLE alias (TOCLEN_B = OVERREAD_B) whose runtime half it had not measured, stating that plainly rather than guessing.  *Measured afterwards by the main loop: `+` REFUSES it, so the runtime question never arises.*  It also verified the decline probe emits exactly its 20 names IN ORDER, that the default probe's 60 are 52 literal + 8 loop-generated with every name within the width limit, and that the gate's 60-name list does NOT follow emission order -- mechanically immaterial, since each check greps the whole log, but reported because the brief asked.

entries.note: 18 builds, 20 probe runs, against source byte-identical to ba30e64. FIVE new 32/32 escapes. FILED not fixed: the stopping rule reserves in-round fixes for a MEASURED FALSE PASS or a WRONG RECORD, and #461's detector is above the vacuity floor on all four clauses -- so these are coverage debt, the #447 disposition. *** E1 IS THE FINDING, AND IT DEFEATS THE ROUND'S STRUCTURAL DEFENCE BY GOING ROUND IT. *** Exchange the word- and bit-index expressions in gdrom_unimpl_first (`bits[k >> 5]` / `1u << (k & 31)` transposed). rows.title: gdromwarnbits  six of eight warn bits are used and they are hand-assigned hex masks; the ninth overflows a uint8_t SILENTLY and floods

entries.note: Raised by the main loop while writing #462's pass-2 brief, then checked against the tree. `d->warned` is a uint8_t and GDROM_W_LEN/NODATA/NOTWAIT/OVERREAD/DMANODATA/DMAARM are hand-assigned 0x01..0x20 -- SIX of eight, and #462 is what took it from four to six. *** THE FAILURE MODE AT NINE IS SILENT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH FILING RATHER THAN NOTING. *** `warned |= (1u << 8)` truncates to 0 in a uint8_t, so the latch never sets, `!(warned & BIT)` stays true forever, and the diagnostic FLOODS -- the exact behaviour every one of these latches exists to prevent, arriving with no compile error and no runtime complaint. A duplicate hand-assigned mask fails the same way for a different reason: two sites share one bit and the second is silenced by the first. *** THE ZERO-COST STRUCTURAL FIX HAS IN-TREE PRECEDENT AND THE CARRIER RECORDS IT. *** dev_sh4.c:124-263 converted its SH4_VAL_* defines to a C99 enum ending in SH4_VAL_NCLASS, 'correct by construction instead of by maintenance'. The shapes differ -- those are ARRAY INDICES, these are BIT MASKS -- so the analogue is an enum of bit POSITIONS ending in GDROM_W_NBITS, with each mask defined as `1u << GDROM_W_x_B`. Duplicates become impossible, and NBITS gives a checkable bound against the width of `warned`. *** NOT FIXED NOW, AND FILED WITH A PRE-SET TRIGGER, WHICH IS HOW THE SH4 ONE GOT DONE ON TIME. *** That conversion carried the trigger 'when a tenth class arrives'; SH4_VAL_SCICMD was the tenth and the work happened. #462's semantic class is de-fatalising the DMA pair -- converting the latch representation is a different change, and the stopping rule reserves in-round work for a measured false pass or a wrong record. THE TRIGGER HERE: **the seventh warn bit**. At seven, widen `warned` and convert to the enum form in the same edit; there is no reason to wait for the overflow.

*** THE PRE-SET TRIGGER FIRED EXACTLY AS WRITTEN, AND THAT IS THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING
AS MUCH AS THE CONVERSION. ***  It was set as 'at the SEVENTH bit'.  `gdromexitsix` Round
1 adds THREE latches to the six in use, so the NINTH would be `1u << 8` -- truncating to
zero in a uint8_t, never setting, and letting the diagnostic it guards FLOOD, with no
compile error and no runtime complaint.

TWO SEATS REACHED IT INDEPENDENTLY on that round's pass 1: the adjudicator named it as an
obligation the brief had missed entirely, and agy called it a critical implementation
blocker.  Neither was told about the trigger; both derived the budget from the code.

CONVERSION: six `#define`d masks -> an enum of bit POSITIONS ending in GDROM_W_NBITS, with
each mask `(1u << ..._B)`, and `warned` widened uint8_t -> uint32_t.  GDROM_W_NBITS is now
correct BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by maintenance, and a duplicate mask is impossible to
write -- which was the file's other stated hazard ('the second site is silenced by the
first').

BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVATION MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: a compiled check confirms all six masks are
BIT-IDENTICAL to the hand-assigned originals (0x01/0x02/0x04/0x08/0x10/0x20) and reports
GDROM_W_NBITS == 6 with 26 bits free.  The device object compiles.  Propagated identical
to est/, build/ and build-asan/.

*Precedent transferred rather than invented: dev_sh4.c did the equivalent conversion for
its value-class keys on its own pre-set trigger ('when a tenth class arrives'), and the
carrier records that one as discharged.  A trigger set in advance, fired by an unrelated
round, and discharged without a fresh design argument is the cheapest thing in this
project -- and it only worked because the condition was written down as a CONDITION rather
than as a note saying 'watch out for this'.*

THE RULE, in applicable form:
  A pre-set trigger buys exactly ONE thing: the DESIGN debate.  When it fires, the round
  executes the settled form without re-opening pass-1 design, and the brief cites the
  trigger VERBATIM as a settled premise.  **It buys nothing at REVIEW**: the executed diff
  is panelled like any diff -- riding in the firing round's pass 2, or on its own full
  stage whose brief inlines the whole diff -- and the row closes only on full stages.
  The discharge brief NAMES the trigger verbatim and LISTS every delta between the
  trigger's text and the executed diff, so seats review the choices actually made instead
  of re-litigating the settled form.

THE BOUND, so the panel requirement cannot un-make triggers: a discharge-panel dissent
against the settled FORM itself (enum-ness, count suffix, mask shape) is a LATE DESIGN
DISSENT -- it files under the late-dissent rule's disposition 3 and does NOT block the
discharge.  The panel's jurisdiction is the execution and its unfixed choices.

entries.note: MEASURED while running #462's detector. The probe was comfortable at 32 rows and at 41; at 44 it overruns 1800s, because the four ACCEPT rows each drive a full TOC staging sequence (several emulator sessions apiece) rather than the one or two a value row needs. *** THE COST IS NOT THE RUNTIME, IT IS THAT AN OVERRUN LOOKS LIKE NOTHING. *** The wrapper captured output with `out=$(timeout 1800 ...)` and grepped for specific patterns, so a kill mid-run yielded an EMPTY log and exit 0 -- indistinguishable from a run still in progress. Compounded by stdout buffering, which the carrier already records: under a timeout nothing flushes, so even a traceback vanished. Two diagnostic attempts returned no output at all before the cause was found. MITIGATION APPLIED, and it is the general fix rather than a bigger number: run the probe with `python3 -u` and STREAM to a file instead of capturing at the end, so a partial run is visible and row-by-row progress can be watched. The budget was raised to 5400s too, but the streaming is what turns a silent failure into a legible one. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OWED: gate 10 runs this probe, so the gate's own budget inherits the overrun. Either the accept rows share ONE staging session -- they currently stage independently, which was never necessary -- or the gate's timeout rises with the probe's. The first is better: four stagings for three observations is the real waste, and sharing them would also make the rows measure the SAME transfer rather than three similar ones.

PARTLY ADDRESSED BY #462, and the honest state is worth separating from the fix. *** WHAT IS DONE: *** the four accept rows now share ONE staging session instead of four, which was this row's recommended repair and was applied in-round on the owner's decision (L1, pre-ship construction). Three of the four TOC stagings are gone. Verified: one staging occurrence where there were two in the source, one session driving all four rows, row count unchanged at 44, and the detector measures 44/44 with the four accept rows reading coherently -- yes / 0x0 / set / 0. *** WHAT IS NOT MEASURED: whether the probe now fits the original 1800s budget. *** The run that produced 44/44 was given 5400s and completed, which proves it fits 5400 and says nothing about 1800. So the row stays OPEN on exactly that question, because gate 10 runs this probe and the gate's own budget is what actually matters -- and 'it feels faster' is not a measurement. The next run should be timed. *** AND THE ROW'S OTHER HALF -- THE ONE THAT MATTERED MORE -- IS FULLY ADDRESSED. *** The original finding was not that the probe was slow but that AN OVERRUN LOOKED LIKE NOTHING: output captured with `out=$(timeout ...)` and grepped for patterns, so a mid-run kill yielded an empty log at exit 0, indistinguishable from a run still in progress. Every measurement since streams `python3 -u` to a file, and that change earned itself twice within the hour -- once on a plain-`&` launch that killed its own child, and once on a NameError at row 41 whose failing line was visible instead of silent.

*** THE HEADLINE ABOVE WAS OVERTAKEN BY THE ROUND THAT FILED IT, and is corrected in place rather than superseded. *** This row said the probe 'exceeds its 1800s budget at 44 rows'. MEASURED 2026-08-24 at 51 rows: 809s (probe_pre51.raw), less than HALF the cited budget. The cause the row named -- the accept rows each driving a full TOC staging sequence -- was FIXED in the same round by collapsing them onto ONE shared session, so the overrun was true when filed and false by the time the row was read. *** AND THERE IS NO BUDGET TO EXCEED. *** gate_sh_rounding.sh runs the probe with `|| true` and no `timeout`, and run.sh sets none for the gate, so the failure mode was never a truncated log -- it is a slower weekly battery. Stating that plainly matters because 'exceeds its budget' implies a red gate. THE RESIDUAL IS REAL AND IS probetimebased: 52 rows are driven by 35 session() calls, each forking an emulator and then sleeping a FIXED settle=8.0 regardless of when the guest is ready -- ~280s of pure settle. Every other pty probe in regress/ detects the prompt with endswith('>'). TWO LEDGER ROWS, ONE CAUSE, and neither entry said so until now. The right unit is SESSIONS: a row sharing an existing session is nearly free (the accept group is 5 rows on 1), a row opening one costs ~8s minimum.

*** THE SEAT WITHDREW ITS OWN PROPOSAL, AND FOUND THAT THIS ROW'S 'MITIGATION APPLIED' WAS FALSE. *** (1) `--only` row subsetting is WITHDRAWN on two grounds I could not have found: gate_sh_rounding.sh PINS the denominator at 57, so a subset run reports a smaller one and the gate FAILS -- it cannot make the battery faster by one second; and worse, GDROM_DEF_CONTROL prints OK when all(rows) is true, and all([]) is TRUE, so any --only excluding the control rows makes the probe claim liveness HAVING MEASURED NOTHING, under a gate check named 'control proves it measures'. The first use of the feature would manufacture a vacuous claim automatically. (2) THE STREAMING MITIGATION THIS ROW RECORDED AS APPLIED, AND CALLED 'THE GENERAL FIX', WAS APPLIED TO NONE OF THE SIX GATE INVOCATIONS -- the -u lived only in ad-hoc measurement scripts. NOW ACTUALLY APPLIED to all six. (3) The session count in this row is wrong: 35 is CALL SITES; three are loop-nested (x4, x8, x5), so executions are 52. Settle alone is 52 x 8.0 = 416s, about HALF of the measured 809s, not the ~31% recorded. (4) VERDICT ON THE ACTUAL QUESTION: 2181s for gate 10 is ACCEPTABLE -- do nothing about the clock. 36 minutes once a week on a machine that must be idle anyway. (5) Worth doing instead and unrelated to this probe: run.sh has NO timing instrumentation at all, so 2181s is the first timed figure this gate has ever had and it was measured by hand. Three lines in the gate loop makes every future performance claim checkable by existence.

rows.state_note: *** AND THE FEATURE'S VALUE WAS DEMONSTRATED THE SAME HOUR, BY A SEAT THAT BUILT ONE. *** While measuring Round 2's mutants the opus seat wrote its own probe WITH session selection (`tprobe2.py 'S1 badfmt,S4 acceptA'`) and used it immediately: for the Site A fallthrough mutant it ran TWO sessions instead of eight, because only those two can distinguish a decline from an accept. **That is the argument for the feature and, read carefully, also the argument for why it is a separate round.** Selection is CHEAP in a purpose-built probe where it is designed in; the cost measured here is RETROFITTING it to a 1200-line probe whose 36 sessions run at module level. The two facts are not in tension -- they are the same fact seen from each end, and a future round should read them together rather than citing one. *** A FOURTH COST FACT, MEASURED 2026-08-28, AND IT IS ABOUT THE FIX RATHER THAN THE COST: A ROW FILTER IS NOT A SMALL CHANGE TO THIS PROBE. *** Round 2 was going to fold one in -- the owner approved it on a cost I stated -- and the estimate was wrong by roughly 10x. Measured before building: session() calls at MODULE level (column 0) 36 session() calls inside a block 3 -- 39 **Skipping a row therefore means skipping TOP-LEVEL STATEMENTS.** A filter in `row()` alone changes what is SCORED and saves NOTHING, because the expensive part -- the session -- has already run by the time row() is called. Real per-row selection needs either a label threaded through all 36 call sites with an early-return in session(), or the probe restructured into per-row functions. **WITHDRAWN FROM ROUND 2 BY OWNER DECISION** so the strengthening diff stays about the replacement channel, which is what its pass 2 reviews. It ships as its own round with its own panel and its own negative controls -- a filter that silently selects nothing is this project's most-recorded failure class, and it must not ride in on a diff reviewed for something else. WHEN IT IS BUILT, the guards are already specified: print a DENOMINATOR (`selected N of 58`) beside every result; HARD-FAIL on zero matches; HARD-FAIL on a selector naming a row that does not exist (so a renamed row cannot silently stop being tested); and unset MUST be byte-identical to today, which is the negative control the gate itself provides. Name derived from the tree rather than invented: `GDROM_DEF_ROWS` -- the house idiom is `os.environ.get("_")` (SELFMUTANT_RUN_TIMEOUT and friends) and this probe already owns the GDROM_DEF_ namespace via GDROM_DEF_RESULT= / GDROM_DEF_VECTOR=. *** AND THE GATE PINS THE DENOMINATOR AT 58: *** gate_sh_rounding.sh names rows in a `for v in ...` list and checks the ratio, so any filter must leave the unset-path denominator untouched. *** A THIRD COST VARIABLE, MEASURED 2026-08-27: COMMANDS PER SESSION. *** This row's headline is *"cost is SESSIONS, not rows"*, and that was derived from probes whose rows each run one short session. **A row added to `asic_badaddr_probe.py` today is ONE session -- cheap by this row's own measure -- and took roughly SIX MINUTES.** ``` the other 13 rows ~15 s each one session, a handful of debugger commands `sweep 256` ~6 min one session, 768 debugger commands ``` It walks all 256 offsets of the SYSASIC window with `r1=; pc=; step 1` per offset. Each of those is a pty round-trip, and the round-trips dominate: the emulator work itself is 256 byte loads. **SO THE RULE NEEDS A SECOND TERM.** A probe's wall clock is roughly `sessions x boot_cost + total_debugger_commands x round_trip`, and the two terms are traded against each other by DESIGN CHOICES that look unrelated: folding N rows into one session removes N boots and keeps every command. **THE CHEAPER SHAPE, not built:** drive the walk from GUEST CODE -- a loop, or an unrolled block written once with `put h` -- so one `step N` replaces hundreds of round-trips. Not done today because hand-assembling SH is this project's documented encoding trap, and a wrong encoding yields a probe that measures the wrong thing while looking green. *Recorded rather than acted on: the six minutes buys a row that defends 256 offsets where nine were defended before, and the alternative risks a silently-wrong instrument.*

entries.note: *** CENSUS CORRECTED 16 -> 64, AND THE BRIEF WAS THE SOURCE OF THE ERROR. *** relative_addr is not necessarily word-aligned: a BYTE access at +0x0d gives 0x0d/4 == 3, &3 == 3, and dies like +0x0c. entries.note: ATTACKED THE PASS-1 BRIEF BEFORE THE PANEL SAW IT, and found TWO premises stated flatly that are wrong against source -- which is the failure that costs a whole panel cycle, because a wrong fact in a brief comes back CONFIRMED. The round therefore does not DROP the protection, it PRESERVES it as the structural-invariant comment plus the accept rows. It is UB and a STATE-CONFUSION hazard, not an out-of-bounds, and `build-asan/` CANNOT SEE IT (ASan does not detect intra-object overflow without field-padding, which GCC lacks). So pointing at ASan as residual coverage would be a wrong record. *** AND IT FOUND A REGRESSION IN MY BRIEF AGAINST THIS ROUND'S OWN RECORD: *** the brief says the detector owes the twelve offsets `written-then-read`, i.e. INTERLEAVED; the authoritative record says ALL WRITES FIRST, THEN ALL READS. Under the interleaved form the round's sharpest named mutant (`& 3` -> `& 1`) PASSES EVERY ROW, because each sentinel round-trips through its own aliased cell; batched, the +0x18 write clobbers index 0 and the +0x10 readback returns C instead of A. Same at +0x18/+0x28/+0x38: THE THIRD REGISTER OF EVERY IMPLEMENTED GROUP, both directions. **The severity story stops needing `a guest probes reserved space` and becomes `a guest uses a documented register at the wrong SZ`.** It also made `safe 8`'s comment a WRONG RECORD (fixed). *** SECOND MISS: THE INVARIANT'S MOST LIKELY VIOLATOR IS IN ANOTHER FILE. *** SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e) = BASE + 4*((e)>>5) (dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:74), so ANY event >= 96 gives e>>5 == 3 -> relative 0x0c. The edit that reaches it is adding a #define to a HEADER with no change to dev_dreamcast_asic.c at all -- **a structural-invariant comment in the device file cannot govern it.** *** THIRD: PREMISE 2 HAS A THIRD, MORE ACCURATE ANSWER. *** Deleting the block does NOT remove the diagnostic: 0x0c is not a case label, falls to `default:` (:177-183) which already prints the ADDRESS, and that debug() PRINTS UNDER STEPPING (verified against debugmsg.c:365-376: v == 0, so the early-out does not fire). The record should say **demoted a redundant fatal()+exit(1) to the pre-existing default: debug()** -- neither `removed a diagnostic` nor `replaced a latent bounds check`. FURTHER: mask_9[3] is NOT another mask, it is `asserted_13`, the int edge-latch the tick compares against old_asserted_13 -- writing a mask value there desynchronises ASSERT/DEASSERT. The batched sweep is BLIND to `% 3` (every write-then-read round-trips through its own permuted cell) and `% 3` is the most plausible naive repair anyone will write here; only the assertion channel can see a permutation. And three of the twelve batched offsets carry NO SIGNAL (pending_irq guest-writes only clear, start at 0) -- **it is NINE live offsets, not twelve.** It also caught a FALSE WARRANT in the witness: `safe 4`'s comment claimed `& 1` kills +0x04, but under `& 1` r is in {0,1} so r==3 is never true and nothing dies -- the killing mutant is `if (r == 3 || r == 1)`. Both wrong records fixed pre-ship (L1).

entries.note: RESEARCH STAGE, filled last (the row's codex research entry had been a HELD MARKER, not an answer -- counted as one by a name-count, which is the gap-closes-itself shape). VERDICT: the DECLINE is the better trade; **the LATCH is not**. FOUR facts no other seat had. (1) *** `mask_13[4] IS mask_11[1]` IS AN OBSERVED ABI/LAYOUT CONSEQUENCE, NOT VALID C -- the subscript is UB regardless of member adjacency.*** Every other seat, the adjudicator and I treated it as a well-defined layout fact. **That makes an EXECUTABLE bound more valuable, not less.** (2) *** FIRST HARDWARE ORACLE IN THE ENTIRE ROUND. *** The project holds no Holly ASIC documentation and the ledger records that absence; codex cited external sources -- Linux's mach-dreamcast IRQ code documents three status words and three per mask group, and KallistiOS exposes exactly +0/+4/+8. **The three-word bound is a HARDWARE fact, not an implementation choice**, which independently condemns `[4]`. (3) *** THE ARGUMENT AGAINST THE LATCH, AND IT IS GROUNDED IN THIS ROUND'S OWN ASSESS FINDING: a latched warning would fire on legitimate traffic -- *** WITHDRAWN 2026-08-25: this was measured too broad. The handler receives `len`, so a byte at +0x0d or an unaligned call IS distinguishable from any lane of a legal 8-byte access; the predicate is empty only for an ALIGNED 32-BIT access at +0x0c. Silence remains defensible as POLICY, not as forced ***. *** The old alarm fired on reserved lanes INCLUDING the second half of a legitimate split access -- and kimi's transaction-closure finding proves those are normal: every 8-byte access based at one of the FOUR word-2 registers (+0x08/+0x18/+0x28/+0x38 -- an earlier version of this sentence omitted +0x38 and said 'an implemented register', which reads as all twelve; word-0 bases do not die and word-1 offsets are not 8-byte aligned at all) touches a reserved lane by construction. Verified here. **So a bounded announce would announce normal operation. *** WITHDRAWN 2026-08-25 -- true only of the aligned 32-bit case; a predicate excluding aligned 4-byte subaccesses is non-empty. ***** The suppressible address-bearing `debug()` is the right diagnostic. (4) `return 1` is not merely tail-skipping: it relies on the DISPATCHER pre-zeroing read buffers (`memory_rw.c:485`), a non-local guarantee -- so the decline should fall through to the epilogue rather than return early. Also notes `return;` bare is invalid, DEVICE_ACCESS expanding to an int function. It agrees the shipped fix introduced no PRESENT silent OOB (all twelve cases yield r <= 2; the default path is old, only the pairing is new) and that the weakness is PROSPECTIVE.
entries.outcome_note: The undefined-subscript and prospective-bound findings stood. The same codex research entry explicitly withdraws the argument that every bounded warning must flag legitimate traffic: distinguishable access classes exist, so silence is a policy choice. rows.state_note: *** SEVERITY CORRECTED 2026-08-24, AT ROW LEVEL, BEFORE THE ROUND RUNS: THIS IS NOT A MEMORY-SAFETY DEFECT AND THE ROUND MAY NOT CLAIM ONE. *** The pass-1 brief said a future `case 0x0c:` indexing with `r` would make `r == 3` `a real out-of-bounds`. **It would not.** Verified by reading `dev_dreamcast_asic.c:53-66`: the four `uint32_t[3]` arrays are declared CONSECUTIVELY with no intervening members, so every r==3 index lands INSIDE THE SAME ALLOCATION -- `pending_irq[3]` IS `mask_13[0]`, `mask_13[3]` IS `mask_11[0]`, `mask_11[3]` IS `mask_9[0]`, and `mask_9[3]` is `asserted_13`, an int of the same width. It is UB and a STATE-CONFUSION hazard; it is not an overrun of the allocation. *** AND THE PROJECT'S EXISTING SAFETY NET CANNOT SEE IT: *** ASan does not detect INTRA-OBJECT overflow without `-fsanitize-address-field-padding`, which GCC does not have and this tree does not use -- so citing `build-asan/` as residual coverage here would be a WRONG RECORD. Corrected at ROW LEVEL rather than only inside the seat entry that found it, because a fact fixed in an entry and left standing in the field a ranker reads is the laundering shape this project corrected twice today on other rows. *The defect is still worth the round -- a single guest LOAD ends the host at 64 byte addresses -- but the harm class is DoS, not memory corruption, and the de-escalation argument must rest on that.*  *** SEVERITY REFRAMED -- ADJUDICATED A FLOOR ITEM FOR THE RECORD, 2026-08-24. The FIX is unchanged and the fmov.d ROW is FILED, but the round may NOT ship the old framing. *** The honest statement is **`a documented register accessed at the wrong SZ ends the host`**, not `a guest probes reserved space`. Confirmed from source in both directions: an SZ=1 `fmov.d` at 0xa05f6908 passes SH_ALIGN_CHECK_LD(addr,7), splits, and its `+4` sub-access reaches relative 0x0c -- r==3, exit(1) -- BEFORE +0x08 is touched (cpu_sh_instr.c:798 load, :1478 store). Same at 0x18/0x28/0x38, the THIRD REGISTER OF EVERY IMPLEMENTED GROUP. *** WHY THE RECORD-HALF IS THE FLOOR ITEM AND THE ROW IS NOT: *** floor clause (a) is already discharged -- the byte/word/store rows die pre-fix at r==3 -- so the fmov.d row adds a WIDTH AXIS, which is coverage debt ABOVE the floor, and its real cost (clear SR.FD, set FPSCR.SZ) is why it is filed rather than built here. But shipping `reachable only by probing reserved space` would be a MEASURED-FALSE UNDERSTATEMENT, which is the census-4x class -- this project's most expensive failure. The deletion covers every access width anyway (byte, word, store and the fmov.d split alike), so fmov.d expands the RECORD, not the fix. *** AND IT IS THE SAME LESSON AS THE `% 3` BLINDNESS AT A DIFFERENT DEPTH: *** a sub-access SPLIT and an index PERMUTATION both reach r==3 by a route the batched readback sweep cannot see. The split is witnessable and severity-bearing; the permutation is structurally invisible to readback and is clause-(e) non-coverage. **Keep them distinct in the record so neither is read as covering the other.**  *** AND THE INVARIANT CLAIM IS SCOPED, NOT GLOBAL: *** the structural-invariant comment this round leaves in `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` governs THAT FILE ONLY. A second route to `r == 3` exists via `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR` whenever `(e>>5) & 3 == 3` -- `[96,127]`, `[224,255]`, `[352,383]` -- **not for 'any event >= 96', which is false because `[128,159]` maps to `+0x10` (r = 0); see the correction on `asiceventaddr`** -- and the edit that reaches it adds a `#define` to a header with no change to the device file -- filed as `asiceventaddr`. **The round may not claim the invariant is fully protected.**  *** THE WITNESS IS NO LONGER A DESIGN -- IT RAN ON THE COMMITTED BUILD AND REPRODUCED THE DEFECT: 5/9, with EXACTLY the four intended reds and nothing else (`regress/artifacts/asic463/witness_prefix_HEAD.raw`). *** All three controls green: `live` returns 0x5eed through RAM, `devsig` returns the SH4 IPRD reset value 0xda74 proving dispatch, and `asic ok` stores-and-reads-back 0x5a on mask_13[0] -- which RAM cannot fake and a deleted case cannot satisfy. Both accept rows green. And the four kill rows all read `died` against a wanted `survived`. *** THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THAT `safe 8` AND `safe 4` SURVIVED WHILE +0x0c, +0x0d AND +0xfc DIED: the death is r-SELECTIVE, not `any touch of this window`. *** Three of the reds carry findings that took two panels to establish: `kill byte` at +0x0d proves the census is 64 byte addresses and not the 16 word-aligned ones that six of nine seats once ratified; `kill far` at +0xfc is GROUP 15, closing the group-narrowing escape the first draft would have missed because all three of its killing rows sat in group 0; and `kill store` confirms the guard fires for writes as well as reads. **The round is now licensed by a measurement rather than by nine seats' agreement.**  *** THE FIX IS APPLIED AND MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: 5/9 RED on committed HEAD `6cae5e4`, 9/9 GREEN with the fix -- SAME SCRIPT, SAME ROWS, OPPOSITE COLOUR (`regress/artifacts/asic463/witness_prefix_HEAD.raw`, `witness_postfix.raw`). *** The whole `if (r == 3)` block is deleted, not just its `exit(1)`, on three grounds that hold together: keeping `fatal()` converts a host kill into a GUEST-DRIVABLE FLOOD (no early-out and `-q` cannot silence it); keeping `r = 0` leaves a LATENT aliasing hazard, dead today and silent tomorrow; and deleting the block removes NO DIAGNOSTIC, because 0x0c is not a case label and falls to `default:`, which already prints the ADDRESS that `Bad address` never did. *** THE TWO ACCEPT ROWS ARE WHAT MAKE THIS MORE THAN A DEMONSTRATION: `safe 8` and `safe 4` were GREEN BEFORE the fix and GREEN AFTER -- so the deletion removed the kill WITHOUT WIDENING ANYTHING. A fix that had accidentally broken the accept side would show there, and does not. *** Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings, `.o` rebuilt and binary relinked, verified by `binary -nt source` rather than by make's exit status; est/ byte-identical; all three NO-VPATH trees propagated. **WHAT REMAINS IS THE LESSON #462 PAID FOR: THE WITNESS IS A REPRODUCTION, NOT A DETECTOR.** Removing a host-fatal guard DELETES THE ACCIDENTAL TRIPWIRE that made guard growth self-announcing -- so `safe 8` and `safe 4` are now ACCEPT ROWS each owing a MEASURED KILL, and the adjudicated mutant form is **`if (r == 2)` ALONE, not `r >= 2`**: `r >= 2` reddens the kill rows too, so it cannot demonstrate that `safe 8` carries anything.  *** PASS-2 PANEL: `_scratchpad/panel_20260825_020219`. SEVEN REVIEW SEATS FIRED AND ALL SEVEN ANSWERED, plus Fable in the adjudicator role; **Opus 5 was NOT FIRED on this pass** (reserved for the ask-again). One transport substitution recorded. *An earlier version of this note said 'nine seats fired, nine answered' -- contradicted by the seat list further down this same note, which records Opus as not fired. Corrected in the round block first and left standing HERE for another hour: mechanical rule 2 (grep a claim's SIBLINGS before calling it fixed) failing inside the very row that memorialises it. Caught by a records-vs-diff panel.* *** codex 5.6-SOL (894 KB) -- found the `/ 4` -> `/ 2` escape, and REFUTED TWO OF THIS ROUND'S OWN FRAMINGS on precision: `r == 3` is not itself an out-of-bounds access (only `array[r]` would be, and nothing on that path indexes), and the 'two halves' invariant was incomplete because `/ 2` satisfies BOTH halves textually while breaking the mapping. rows.title: gdromdriverclaims  #462's design rests on three guest-driver claims with no local artifact, and ONE of them was measured false the same day

entries.note: There is NO copy of Linux's drivers/cdrom/gdrom.c or NetBSD's sys/arch/dreamcast/dev/gdrom.c anywhere in this tree, yet #462's design rested on three claims about them. *** ONE WAS REFUTED FROM ITS OWN QUOTED LINE. *** Four records cited `while ((GDROM_BUSY & 0x88) != 0x08) ;` as an unbounded NetBSD poll of +0x18. That loop exits only when bit 3 is SET and bit 7 CLEAR; +0x18's domain is {0 idle, 1 busy} and neither ANDs to 0x08 -- IT WOULD HANG ON CORRECT HARDWARE. Independently, dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:722-737 -- code this round never touched -- documents that same wait as NetBSD's COMMAND-START handshake on the CONTROL window's BUSY register and sets d->busy |= 0x08 in reply. The exhibit was lifted from that comment and re-pointed at a register it says nothing about. The conclusion survives on Linux; the reason does not, and a wrong reason gets reused -- this project already has the fatal()-is-byte-for-byte-debug() case on record. All four corrected IN PLACE. This is the #357/#362/#365 shape: citations from panel output rather than a local source. Obtaining the SH manual refuted a wrong finding the same session it was raised; obtaining these two drivers is the same cheap move.

rows.title: gdrompionull  the PIO data read dereferences d->data with no NULL test, reachable with LEGAL values only and with no diagnostic at all

entries.note: Found while answering a pass-1 question about gdromcondlies, a DIFFERENT defect. Three facts, each verified by opening the file: COND_DATA_AVAIL is 0x08 and 0xef & 0x08 == 0x08, so the LEGAL value 0xef sets the emulator's data-available flag; handle_command frees d->data and NULLs it but NEVER resets d->data_len (the only writer is alloc_data); and the PIO read guards ONLY `cur_data_offset < data_len` before dereferencing d->data[...] -- there is no NULL test. The DMA arm received one in #462; ITS PIO TWIN DID NOT, because it relies on cond & COND_DATA_AVAIL, a flag the guest can set back. Sequence, legal values throughout: stage TOC (data_len=408) -> stage Mount 0x70 (frees data, data_len STAYS 408, bit 3 cleared) -> write COND=0xef (bit 3 back on) -> read +0x80 -> d->data[0] on NULL. OB-20's two breaks reach the same data==NULL/data_len>0 state without needing 0x70. *** AND IT CONSTRAINS gdromcondlies: the naive Site B fix (decline but keep d->cond = idata) turns this from ONE legal value into EVERY unmodelled value with bit 3 set -- that round would be the one that WIDENED a NULL-deref primitive. Leave d->cond UNCHANGED on decline; cond bit 3 is INTERPRETED as a readiness flag gating a pointer path, so storing an arbitrary guest byte hands the guest a direct write to internal readiness state.

entries.note: VERDICT GO -- the one-line tail fix is the right member and needs no change. A READING seat by its own declaration: it opened GXEMUL-SEC/src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c with line numbers matching the brief exactly, ran no builds, and labelled every mutant trace REASONED rather than measured. *** IT CORRECTED THE BRIEF'S OWN PREMISE AUDIT, AND THE REASON MATTERS MORE THAN THE CORRECTION. *** The audit claimed 'one break at :415'; there are FIVE (:379, :406, :415, :456, :466). Verified independently, and the cause is an apparatus defect: the scan pattern was return/exit/goto and NEVER LOOKED FOR break AT ALL -- :415 surfaced only because its comment reads '/* OB-20: was exit(1) */', so A PATTERN MATCHED A COMMENT AND WAS READ AS CODE. Re-scanned with comments stripped: exit() 3, break 5, return 0, goto 0. The CONCLUSION is unchanged and in fact stronger (zero return AND zero goto over 177 lines), but the stated fact was wrong and the brief had already been sent to eight other seats. *** IT CLOSED THE ENUMERATION THE BRIEF LEFT OPEN. *** Q1, the question the brief called most likely to sink the fix, is answered exhaustively: every data_len READ site classified -- :309-310 (inside alloc, post-write), :442 (post-alloc), :611 (the target guard), :616/:619 (dominated by :611 true), :950/:954 (DMA, dominated by the :846 'data == NULL' decline). ZERO readers legitimately consult data_len while data == NULL. It also found a THIRD d->data writer the brief missed -- DEVINIT at :1136-1141 memsets the whole struct, so the invariant holds at birth -- and noted CHECK_ALLOCATION (misc.h:190-193) exits on failure, so a failed malloc cannot leave data == NULL with data_len already set. *** ON CLAUSE (d), THE QUESTION POSED AS GENUINELY OPEN: IT DOES NOT ENUMERATE THE EMPTY SET. *** Under the corrected DEPENDS-ON reading it enumerates exactly the :475 tail guard, with operand swaps drawn from the else-body fields {cnt, data_len, cond}. m1 ('data != NULL' -> 'data_len != 0') and m2 (-> 'cnt != 0') are killed by the death-mode oracle. **m3 -- reordering the assignment above 'd->cnt = 0;' -- is killed ONLY by a row that includes the guest GDROM_COND write. That is a DETECTOR OBLIGATION this round now owes.** m4/m5 are predicted EQUIVALENT and should be built and recorded as results per the non-dying-mutant rule, not treated as gaps. *** ITS BEST ADVERSARIAL FINDING SITS OUTSIDE THE BOUNDED (d) ENUMERATION -- AND IT SAYS SO RATHER THAN SMUGGLING IT IN. *** Swapping :611's operand to d->cnt is equivalent on the defect route, but lets a guest inflate cnt mid-read via CNTLO/CNTHI (:704/:712) and read past data_len into the heap. A value oracle cannot kill it reliably (heap garbage may equal 0xffff); the DIAGNOSTIC channel can, deterministically -- shipped fires #460's once-latched W_OVERREAD and returns 0xffff, while the mutant serves data silently. ON THE OPTION SET: the three-membered de-fatalisation rule does not literally bind (this fix removes no fatal()/exit(); the defect is a SIGSEGV). It grepped the tree for precedents and CHECKED them rather than citing -- dev_fb.c:207-212 (#182) is the settling-point invariant member already shipped, :846 (#462) the consumer-guard member. The proposal composes both and inherits the bounded-announce member for free, because the repaired state routes into #460's once-latched decline. It REJECTED an extra NULL test at :611 under the ADDITION LICENCE: no measured delta, no transferred warrant. ON SCOPE: AGREES the surviving exit(1)s are a separate item, and notes they are ALREADY FILED -- the device-exit tail class names 'dreamcast gdrom' explicitly and sh4gdromexit counts 14 sites in this file. The round creates nothing; it only must not absorb them. It flagged one adjacent pre-existing defect: :444's fatal('GDROM: diskimage_access failed? TODO') is UNLATCHED and fires per failed command -- a guest-drivable flood belonging to floodclass, worth one line because this fix routes more traffic past it. *** AND A CROSS-ROUND CONSEQUENCE WORTH RECORDING BEFORE IT LOOKS LIKE A REGRESSION: *** once this invariant holds, #462's guard-field/body-field swap at :846 ('data == NULL' -> 'data_len == 0') becomes EQUIVALENT in all settled states. That is a DESIGNED consequence of this fix, not a detector regression, and a future re-measurement reading it as one would be a wrong record.

AND A RESULT WORTH KEEPING: `m_free` and `m_top` both score 13/16 but NOT THE SAME 13 -- each witnessed route is the sole killer of one relocation mutant, so the two are NOT redundant and a future round tempted to drop one as duplicative is measured wrong.

*** ORDERING DEPENDENCY EXPORTED to `gdromexitsix` 2026-08-26 -- recorded here so a reader of this row never sees false completeness. *** This round's detector oracle is the DEATH MODE, and it depends on three command-layer `exit(1)` calls that `gdromexitsix` is scheduled to de-fatalise. That obligation now lives on THAT row as a CLOSURE-GATING re-pin, with the oracle-correction order baked in -- because the LATER round breaks the EARLIER round's detector, so it must sit where the round that will trip it will see it.

  *** WITNESS BUILT AND MEASURED 2026-08-25. THE DEFECT IS REAL, AND IT IS CHEAPER AND QUIETER THAN THIS ROW SAID. *** The committed build dies with **SIGSEGV on NINE guest accesses**, every value legal. A second, independent 18-access staged route fires too. *** THE ORACLE IS THE DEATH MODE, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES `died` EVIDENCE HERE. *** Every OTHER death in this device is `fatal()` + `exit(1)`; this one is a NULL deref, so the probe reports HOW the process ended and `sig11` != `exit1` != `exit0`. **That validates the hand-assembled packet for free**: a wrong `cmd[0]` lands in `handle_command`'s `default:` arm and a wrong `cmd[1]` in the 0x30 format check -- both `exit(1)` -- so a coding error in the probe CANNOT be mistaken for the defect. This project has a recorded hand-assembled-encoding trap; this probe is immune to it by construction. `grep -c 'SIGSEGV|SIGBUS'` over `src/` is 0 of 0, so nothing catches it. THE NINE ACCESSES: store 0x00a0 to COND (0xa05f709c) sets `busy |= 0x08`; six stores to DATA (0xa05f7080) spelling `30 20 ...` = read-sectors, format 0x20, sector 0, count 1; `cnt == 0` so :409 sets cnt = 2048 and `alloc_data` sets **data_len = 2048**; `diskimage_access` returns 0 non-fatally; :445-446 does `free(d->data); d->data = NULL`; **the tail zeroes `d->cnt` and clears COND_DATA_AVAIL but NOT `data_len`**; store 0x00ef to COND restores bit 3; then ONE LOAD of DATA -- `0 < 2048` is true, `d->data[0]` on NULL, SIGSEGV. *** ATTRIBUTION, BY A ONE-LINE CONTROL RATHER THAN BY ARGUMENT: *** a second scratch copy with `DIFF_LINES=1` -- one added `if (d->data == NULL) { odata = 0xffff; break; }` at :611 -- scores **11/13, red at EXACTLY `cheap trig` and `staged trig`** (sig11 -> exit0), every other row byte-identical. The kill is attributed to that deref and nothing else. *The seat was explicit that this mutant is an ATTRIBUTION CONTROL, not a fix recommendation -- the option set has three members and it did not adjudicate them.* *** THIS ROW'S OWN ESTIMATE IS CORRECTED, AND UPWARD IN PRECISION: 9 IS THE MINIMUM, DERIVED RATHER THAN GUESSED. *** `data_len` becomes nonzero only via `alloc_data`, which needs a dispatched command; dispatch needs `busy & 0x08`, set only by COND = 0xa0; the packet needs six stores (the width guard consumes 2 bytes at ANY width, so no wider store shortens it); bit 3 must be restored by the guest because the tail clears it unconditionally on the NULL branch, and **0xef is one of only TWO values GDROM_COND accepts at all** -- every other value hits `exit(1)` at :745. 1 + 6 + 1 + 1 = 9. *** AND A WRONG RECORD IN A SIBLING ENTRY IS CORRECTED: THE DEFECT IS NOT DISKLESS-ONLY. *** The opus5 entry attributes the cheap route to 'no IDE disk attached'. No gdb backtrace was taken; attribution rests on the one-line control plus the sig11/exit1/exit0 discriminator, which the seat judged stronger than a stripped -O3 trace. THE MECHANISM PREMISE IS CONFIRMED AT EVERY STEP, THE FIX IS MEMBER 2, AND #462 IS **NOT** A WRONG RECORD. *** **THE WRONG-RECORD QUESTION, ANSWERED NO — I asked it and the answer is that #462 scoped itself honestly.** Its CHANGELOG carries a dedicated section *"### Scope: the DMA pair only"* stating that the four command-layer exits do not join on different reach and a different fix idiom, and the `gdromexitsix` row's own TITLE says *"the DMA+0x18 pair ... and the four command-layer exits split out"*. It was never a claim to have fixed the invariant. **No correction owed.** *** THE DECISIVE FACT MY OPTION SET MISSED, FOUND BY GREPPING THE FORK AS THE THREE-MEMBERED RULE DIRECTS: THE PIO READ ALREADY HAS A SHIPPED, REVIEWED DECLINE PATH. *** At :625-641, the `else` of the :611 guard is **#460's over-read handler — warn-once, `odata = 0xffff`, break** — annotated as this device's own idiom for *"read when there is nothing to give"*. **MEMBER 2 IS THE FIX, and its best form is not the one I proposed.** One line in the TAIL ELSE-BRANCH beside the existing `d->cnt = 0` at :481 — **NOT at the free sites**. The derived argument, which is a correctness argument and not a preference: `d->data` is NULLed only inside `handle_command` (:326 top, :446 on read failure), and **every such path falls through to the unconditional tail whose else-branch runs iff `data == NULL`** — so ONE assignment maintains the invariant on ALL NULL-leaving paths, where a free-site reset needs two and the :326 one is dead in the common realloc case. It co-locates invariant maintenance with the sibling `cnt` zeroing already there. **And it carries a TRANSFERRED WARRANT: with `data_len = 0` the PIO read's `0 < 0` is false and the access routes into #460's existing decline — no new behaviour, no new decline site, and LOUDER than a NULL test's silent 0xffff, because it fires the #460 diagnostic once.** Every consumer of the pair benefits, including the DMA arm: its `data == NULL` guard and a hypothetical `data_len == 0` guard become equivalent once the invariant holds. **MEMBER 1 (NULL test at :611) REJECTED as the fix** — symptom-only, leaves `data_len` lying for every future consumer, and **invents a second bespoke decline site THREE LINES ABOVE the existing #460 one**. It remains a valid ATTRIBUTION CONTROL, which is what it was built as. **MEMBER 3 (both) REJECTED** — the extra NULL test is licensed by neither a measured delta nor a transferred warrant. Its only residual concern, a future edit bypassing the tail, is a DETECTOR obligation under clause (b)/(d), not product code. Per the ADDITION LICENCE, *"cannot hurt" is how dead guards accrete*. No fourth member is needed. *** RANKING: TOP OF THE UN-STARTED QUEUE, BUT DO NOT PREEMPT `wdcflood`. *** A host SIGSEGV on nine legal accesses is MEMORY-UNSAFE and uncontrolled, which outranks even the controlled `exit(1)` items **because it is invisible to the exit-code oracle the battery leans on** — and far above a stderr flood. But `wdcflood` is mid-round with its table running, and the carrier is explicit that more witnesses create more candidate ROUNDS, never bigger ones. This row is witnessed and filed; it loses nothing by waiting one round, whereas preemption discards settled work. **Sequence: finish `wdcflood`, then this.** One check when it starts: confirm `sh4chcr`'s held state before ranking against it — a SIGSEGV still outranks a controlled `exit(1)`, but verify the hold rather than assume it. *** WHAT THE SHIPPED DETECTOR OWES BEYOND THE 13-ROW WITNESS: *** (a) trigger rows red pre-fix / green post-fix — **already have it**. (b) **THE REINSTATEMENT ROW THE WITNESS DOES NOT CARRY**: because the fix is a single assignment, REMOVING `d->data_len = 0` verbatim reinstates the defect, and a row must redden under that. Buildable directly from the attribution artifacts. (d) the fix adds NO PREDICATE, so this is the DEPENDS-ON case: the mutant reroutes the EXISTING guard's repair, drawn from the enclosing function only. Two forms — **(i) relocate or scope `data_len = 0` so the :445-446 read-failure path is not covered, which reddens `cheap trig` and is the load-bearing one**; and (ii) operand-swap the surviving :611 guard to a body-read sibling such as `d->cnt`. **Because member 2 drives ALL length fields to 0 in the NULL state, some operand swaps will measure EQUIVALENT — record that as a RESULT under the won't-die rule, not as a gap.** (accept) a successful PIO read must still return real device bytes: **the existing `devsig gd0`/`gd1` rows (0x0010 / 0xffff9600) ARE that row** — just confirm they run against the FIXED build's success path, proving member 2 did not over-zero `data_len` on the good path; an unconditional `data_len = 0` reddens them. (e) the header names what it catches: removal or relocation of `data_len = 0`, guard-operand swap at :611, reintroduction of free-without-reset. **(f) ANCHOR RULE: N/A — this is a NULL-deref detector, not a decode-position one, and makes no claim about WHERE an access lands. State that in the contract so a later reader does not read the absence as a gap.** *** PROVISIONALITY, STATED BY THE ADJUDICATOR ITSELF: the DEFECT is fully panel-vetted (all nine seats reviewed it 2026-08-24 plus the opus5 rung-3 measurement), but THE OPTION-SET RULING IS A RECOMMENDATION TO CARRY INTO PASS 1, NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR IT. *** Pass 1 must still test the tail-else form against the seats with one specific question: **does routing into the #460 decline path change any guest-visible behaviour on the SUCCESS path?** That is the single thing the adjudication reasoned rather than measured.
