rows.title: asicannounce  #463 deleted the ASIC's only diagnostic on a warrant that was measured too broad -- a bounded latched announce IS constructible, on a predicate that is not empty
rows.witness: none needed to file -- the measurable consequence is READ from source and stated below. A rung-3 witness is cheap and is the same access `asic_badaddr_probe.py`'s `kill byte` row already drives (a byte probe at +0x0d).
rows.state_note: *** FILED 2026-08-25 UNDER THE LATE-DISSENT RULE, DISPOSITION 3, AND IT IS FILED SEPARATELY BECAUSE AN EARLIER DRAFT FOLDED IT INTO `asicindexcase` -- WHICH IS THE ONE-ID-TWO-DEFECTS FAILURE THIS PROJECT RECORDED ON 2026-08-24. *** `asicindexcase` is about an INDEXING `case` added at an r == 3 offset. Someone could close that with a bounds guard and **the announce question would vanish with it**, unexamined. Different question, different id. *** THE DISSENT, CARRIED VERBATIM AS PROVENANCE (three seats, independently -- codex and grok file-reading, deepseek packet-fed): *** codex -- *"byte/word probes are distinguishable using `len`, and unaligned calls using `relative_addr`; a predicate such as 'not an aligned 4-byte subaccess' is demonstrably nonempty. Therefore a bounded diagnostic remains viable. Silent fall-through may still be chosen as policy, but this commit has not proved that a latch would announce legal traffic or that every useful handler-local predicate is empty."* deepseek -- *"A byte access to +0x0d is not a lane of a legal multi-word access... the predicate would not be empty; it would select byte accesses to reserved word 3."* grok -- *"The latch FILTER is empty for len=4 in the modelled groups; that does NOT refute the in-tree bounded-announce option."* *** WHAT #463 ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, restated correctly: *** the predicate is empty ONLY for an ALIGNED 32-BIT access at +0x0c, where a legal `fmov.d` half and a direct probe are byte-identical calls at the handler. Every other shape -- byte, word, unaligned -- is distinguishable. The round's record claimed the option was REFUTED; it was not, and that claim is corrected in place in the CHANGELOG and the ledger. *** IT CLEARS THE 'EARNS A ROUND' DISCRIMINATOR, WHICH A DESIGN DISSENT USUALLY DOES NOT: IT STATES A MEASURABLE CONSEQUENCE. *** MEASURED BY READING: `core/debugmsg.c:375` is `if ((quiet_mode && !ss) || v < 0) return;`, and free-running at `verbose == 0` gives v = -1. So a byte probe at +0x0d produces **ZERO host output today**; under a bounded latch it produces N. **That delta IS the self-announcing property the round's own de-escalation clause says the fix destroyed** -- so this is not documented-only, it is a measurable behaviour difference. SUPPORTING MEASUREMENT from the same seat, worth keeping because it is what makes the predicate safe: every multi-word path in this tree decomposes into ALIGNED 4-BYTE lanes only -- `fmov.d` via `cpu->memory_rw(..., sizeof(data), ...)` in all six encodings, and the store queue at `cpu_sh_instr.c:3767-3775` as eight ascending 4-byte calls. So `not an aligned 4-byte subaccess` excludes EVERY lane of EVERY legal multi-word access. *** AND THE THIRD OPTION IS ALREADY IN THE TREE, which is what the THREE-MEMBERED OPTION SET rule was minted from on this very round: *** the fork's house idiom is an N=1 per-instance latch plus `fatal()`, ~34 sites across 11 device files, with the `dev_asc.c:248-257` warrant for keeping `fatal()` over `debugmsg()`. The round debated delete-versus-keep and never costed the third member. DO NOT reopen `#463` for this. The code shipped, is gated and is witnessed; this is a NEW round if it runs at all, ranked by severity against live defects like any other filed item -- and on severity it is insurance, not a live defect.

rows.title: gdrompiooddlen  the GDROM PIO read guards ONE byte and then reads TWO -- LATENT, because no path can produce an odd length today
rows.witness: none, and none is possible today -- the OWED reachability measurement was done BY READING and came back NEGATIVE. The code asymmetry is real; the route to it is not. See the correction below.
rows.state_note: *** FOUND 2026-08-25 WHILE VERIFYING A PREMISE IN THE `gdrompionull` PASS-1 BRIEF, NOT WHILE LOOKING FOR IT. *** The brief's Q4 asked, almost as an afterthought, whether `d->cur_data_offset` is reset anywhere -- because the round had reasoned about `data_len` throughout and barely looked at the guard's OTHER operand. It is reset (`:327`, beside the NULL). But reading the guard to check that showed something else. *** THE GUARD CHECKS ONE BYTE AND THE BODY READS TWO. *** Verified by reading, three lines:   (1) `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:611` -- `if (d->cur_data_offset < d->data_len) {`   (2) `:612-613` -- `odata = d->data[d->cur_data_offset ++];` then `odata |= (d->data[d->cur_data_offset ++] << 8);` -- **two increments, one bounds test**   (3) `alloc_data` `:309` -- `malloc(d->data_len)`, **exactly `data_len` bytes, no padding, no rounding**. So at `cur_data_offset == data_len - 1` the guard PASSES, the first read is the last valid byte, and **the second read is `d->data[data_len]` -- one byte past the allocation**. *** REACHABILITY, STATED AS WHAT IS READ AND WHAT IS OWED. *** READ: `data_len = d->cnt` (`:307`), and `d->cnt` is GUEST-WRITABLE A BYTE AT A TIME -- `:704` sets the low byte from a CNTLO store and `:712` the high byte from CNTHI, so an ODD count is expressible. The two subsequent adjustments do not remove oddness: `:409-410` only replaces `cnt` when it is ZERO, and `:486-487` only rewrites the single value 65536. **OWED: a measurement that an odd `cnt` actually survives to `alloc_data` on a path a guest can drive.** The existing `gdrom_pio_null_probe.py` already stages commands through these registers and could answer it with two extra stores; I have NOT run it, and this row does not claim the defect is reachable until that runs. *** WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT FROM `gdrompionull` AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. *** That row is `data` NULL while `data_len` lies -- a state-invariant violation whose fix is one assignment in the tail. This is an OFF-BY-ONE in a bounds test, on a path where `data` is a perfectly valid pointer and `data_len` is honest. Different fix design (`< data_len` becomes `+ 1 < data_len`, or the read becomes width-aware), different oracle (a heap over-read, not a SIGSEGV), so under the reopening rule they are separate rounds. **Note the two interact in the safe direction: `gdrompionull`'s fix sets `data_len = 0`, under which this guard is false and the over-read cannot occur on THAT path.** It does nothing for the odd-count path. *** AND UNLIKE THIS DEVICE'S OTHER OUT-OF-BOUNDS ISSUES, ASan SHOULD SEE THIS ONE. *** The file's own comment at `:272` records that ASan cannot detect its member-to-member overrun because that is intra-object inside one malloc. **This is a read PAST a malloc'd buffer's end**, which is the case ASan is built for -- so `build-asan/` is a real second oracle here, where for the aliasing family it was not. That is worth testing early because it is cheap and because a positive ASan result would settle reachability and severity in one run. SEVERITY, stated honestly and NOT inflated: a ONE-BYTE heap over-READ. It does not write, and the byte it returns goes to the guest as the high half of a 16-bit read. That is an information leak of one adjacent heap byte per odd-length transfer and a potential crash only if the allocation ends exactly on a page boundary. It is materially less severe than the SIGSEGV in `gdrompionull` and should rank below it.  *** REACHABILITY SETTLED 2026-08-25, THE SAME DAY THIS ROW WAS FILED, AND IT SETTLED AGAINST THE ROW. *** The filing said the odd-count route was OWED and explicitly did NOT claim the defect was reachable. That was the right caution, and the answer is NO. *** `data_len` HAS EXACTLY ONE WRITER, AND BOTH ROUTES TO IT FORCE AN EVEN VALUE. *** Verified by grepping every assignment: `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:307` in `alloc_data` (`d->data_len = d->cnt;`) is the only one -- the apparent second hit at `:413` is a printf FORMAT STRING, not an assignment, which is the kind of match that would have made this look open if counted rather than read. `alloc_data` has exactly two call sites and each is guarded:   * `:342`, the Read-TOC path, is preceded by `:338-341` -- `if (d->cnt != 408) { fatal(...); exit(1); }`. **408 is even**, and nothing else reaches this call.   * `:418`, the read-sectors path, is preceded by `:412-415` -- `if (sector_count * 2048 != d->cnt) { fatal(...); break; }`. **Any multiple of 2048 is even.** Note `:409-410` only substitutes a count when `cnt == 0`, so a guest-set odd count survives THAT line -- and is then rejected by the equality check two lines later. **So the guest CAN express an odd `cnt` at the CNTLO/CNTHI registers (:704, :712), and that half of the filing was right; what it cannot do is get that value past either guard into `alloc_data`.** *** DISPOSITION: LATENT, NOT LIVE. SEVERITY DROPS FROM A ONE-BYTE HEAP OVER-READ TO A STRUCTURAL HAZARD WITH NO ROUTE. *** The asymmetry itself is untouched and still worth recording: `:611` guards `cur_data_offset < data_len` and `:612-613` reads TWO bytes, while `alloc_data` mallocs exactly `data_len` with no padding. **Any future edit that admits an odd length -- a new command arm, a relaxed guard, a different transfer size -- makes this live immediately, and the code carries nothing that would stop it.** That is a real thing to know and a cheap thing to fix (`+ 1 < data_len`, or make the read width-aware), but it is NOT a defect a guest can reach today and this row may not be ranked as one. *** AND THE ASan NOTE IN THE FILING IS NOW MOOT AND IS WITHDRAWN. *** It said `build-asan/` would be a real second oracle here, unlike the intra-object aliasing family. True in principle and irrelevant in fact: ASan cannot observe an access no execution reaches. *Process note worth keeping: this row was filed with reachability marked OWED rather than asserted, and the owed check refuted it within the hour -- at the cost of two greps. Had it been filed as a live heap over-read it would have been a WRONG RECORD ranked above real work, and the correction would have arrived later and cost more.*

rows.title: wdcperopcode  wdc_command()'s unimplemented-command latch is per-DEVICE, so a guest cycling opcodes gets ONE line and 255 silent aborts -- a SPEC choice, filed not fixed
rows.witness: n/a -- this is a SPEC improvement, not a defect. The shipped behaviour is deliberate and is pinned by the `unimpl 2op` row, which fires TWO different opcodes and demands ONE line.
rows.state_note: *** FILED 2026-08-26 BECAUSE THE SHIPPED DETECTOR'S CONTRACT CLAIMED A FILING THAT DID NOT EXIST. *** `wdc_flood_probe.py`'s header says *"deepseek argued for a per-opcode set; FILED, not shipped"* -- and no row carried it; the only trace was prose inside `wdcflood`'s state_note, which is not something a reader can find. **A contract line asserting a disposition is a WRONG RECORD until the disposition exists as a row.** Caught by the readiness adjudication before the round shipped. THE PROPOSAL, from the deepseek seat on the `wdcflood` pass-1 panel: `:583`'s diagnostic VALUE [dev_wdc.c; at 987cb596 the latch and its message are :1156-1161] is the opcode, so a single per-device flag suppresses every later unimplemented command and hides distinct guest actions. A 256-bit set (`uint32_t warned_unimpl_cmd[8]`) is cheap and preserves them. WHY IT WAS NOT SHIPPED, and the reason is not that it is wrong: the scalar is exactly what stops a guest cycling 0x00..0xff for 256 lines, which is the flood the round exists to bound. Per-opcode-versus-per-device is a SPEC choice between two acceptable behaviours, and the adjudication ruled that clause (d) tests the CHOSEN spec's repair rather than adjudicating between specs -- deepseek's framing ("the scalar IS the (d) mutant") is circular, since it assumes per-opcode is the baseline and then calls the alternative a weakening. *** THE SHIPPED SPEC IS PINNED, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE TO DEFER: *** the `unimpl 2op` row fires TWO DIFFERENT opcodes and demands ONE line, so a later change to per-opcode is a VISIBLE spec change that reddens a row, not a silent drift. The same row kills a "last-warned-opcode" latch (measured: `M3`, 21/22, that row alone), under which an alternating guest floods forever. IF IT IS EVER WORKED, the option set is THREE-membered and the third member is the one the dispute never named: scalar (shipped), per-opcode set (deepseek), and the in-tree COUNT-BOUND idiom (`n_trunc_msgs`, `src/cpus/memory_rw.c:495-523`). Note also that #337's other latched messages at `:816`/`:855` [dev_wdc.c; at 987cb596 the `warned_badlen` latches :1604-1609 and :1638-1643] carry NO value payload, so "three latches in this file" is weaker precedent for discarding value-resolution than it looks -- `:583` [dev_wdc.c; at 987cb596: :1156-1161] is the only site whose message names an opcode.

rows.title: wdcexpecteddata  an EXPECTED DATA write has no quiet pin, so dropping !write_in_progress would warn-and-latch on legal I/O with every detector row green
rows.witness: none -- building it needs a WRITE-command staging sequence `wdc_flood_probe.py` does not have, which is why it is filed rather than fixed.
rows.state_note: *** RAISED BY THE grok SEAT ON THE `wdcflood` PASS-2 PANEL AND RECORDED NOWHERE UNTIL THE READINESS ADJUDICATION FOUND IT DROPPED. *** The unexpected-DATA-write site is guarded by `!d->write_in_progress && !d->atapi_cmd_in_progress`. **Drop the first conjunct and the site warns-and-latches on a perfectly legal write during an active transfer** -- and every row in the 22-row detector stays GREEN, because none of them stages a WRITE command. *** THIS IS THE ACCEPT-SIDE HOLE THE OTHER THREE QUIET PINS CANNOT COVER. *** `accept ec`, `accept w8` and `accept r8` pin legal COMMAND, legal narrow WRITE and legal narrow READ. None of them puts the device into `write_in_progress`, so the one predicate whose accept side is guest-reachable during real I/O has no pin at all. COST OF CLOSING IT: a WRITE-command staging sequence (set up a 0x30 WRITE, reach DRQ, then store to DATA), which is materially more than the one-or-two-instruction stimuli every other row uses. That is the honest reason it is filed -- not that it does not matter. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY IT REVEALS, which generalises past this row: a latch's accept side is only as good as the STATES the detector can reach, and a detector built from cheap stimuli systematically under-covers predicates that depend on expensive state.

rows.title: wdcflagindep  three of six wdc latch classes are pinned at one site each, and per-INSTANCE storage is unpinned entirely -- the fork has a two-controller rig
rows.witness: n/a -- coverage debt against a shipped detector, not a defect.
rows.state_note: *** FILED 2026-08-26 FROM THE opus5 FINAL-DIFF READ, AS THE RESIDUE OF A CONTRACT BULLET THAT WAS UNSCOPED. *** `wdc_flood_probe.py` listed reset-on-normal-operation and guest-resettable-operand under DESIGNED TO CATCH with no scope, while each was measured at exactly ONE site of six. Now scoped in the contract; the missing rows are here. **UNPINNED, each a known-reachable escape:** reset-on-normal at :160, :704 and :145; operand-swap at :583 -- and that one is CONCRETE: the guard reads `warned_unimpl_cmd` while the body reads `d->seccnt` at :660, a field the guest writes at :1003, so `if (!d->seccnt)` scores a clean sweep and no row builds the disagreeing state. **AND THE RING-PAIR HALF OF FLAG INDEPENDENCE:** `wr indep` now pins :607/:1025 by firing both in ONE session; the same shape pins :145/:160 at the cost of one more runloop. *** PER-INSTANCE STORAGE IS THE ONE THAT NEEDS A DIFFERENT RIG, AND THE FORK HAS ONE. *** A process-global `static` latch passes every row because every row starts a fresh emulator. `dev_pcic.c:234-242` adds TWO wdc instances unconditionally at 0x14000180 and 0x140001f0 (its comment: 'Yuck. Now there are two.'), reached from every hpcmips subtype via `dev_vr41xx.c`. Use a WIDTH site, not :583 -- the width check precedes command dispatch, so no disk image is needed at all. New MIPS encodings, bounded work, and honestly lower value than the three-line rows above.  *** THE ASK-AGAIN ADDED THREE MORE MEMBERS TO THIS ROW, AND ONE OF THEM REFUTES A CONTRACT LINE. *** (1) **LAST-VALUE LATCH AT :704 IS UNPINNED.** Keying `warned_data_unexpected` on `len` -- or on `idata` -- sweeps clean, because `datawr x2` writes an IDENTICAL len and an IDENTICAL 0x1234 twice. The two width sites are now pinned by `w mixed`/`r mixed`; this one is not. (2) **RESET-ON-NORMAL AT :583 IS PINNED FOR ONE VALID OPCODE OF NINETEEN.** `interleave`'s only valid command is 0xEC, so a reset hidden in `WDCC_RECAL`, `WDCC_IDLE_IMMED`, `SET_FEATURES`, `ATAPI_SOFT_RESET` or `WDCC_DIAGNOSE` sweeps clean. The recorded kill is opcode-specific and the record did not say so. (3) *** AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: A RESET ARRIVING THROUGH THE SIBLING HANDLER IS PINNED NOWHERE. *** `dev_wdc_altstatus_access` shares the same `d` as `dev_wdc_access`, and **zero rows in the probe touch its address** -- verified by grep. Clearing the six flags alongside `d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET` on a `WDCTL_4BIT` write sweeps clean. **That is where a real driver's reset goes**, which makes it the most plausible member of the family and the least covered. It refutes the contract's earlier 'reset-on-normal -- pinned at :607/:1025' as a general claim: those rows pin resets arriving through `dev_wdc_access` only. Contract corrected in place. *The pattern across all three: a row set built from ONE handler cannot see state changes arriving through a SIBLING handler that shares the device struct. That is a probe-shape gap, not a missing mutant, and it generalises past this device.*

closure.note: ASSESSED, NOT CHANGED.  The MACHINE_HPCMIPS arm in DEVINIT(wdc) is arithmetically a no-op -- 0x14000180 + 0x206 == 0x14000386, exactly the default -- and the only address it can see comes from a hardcoded literal in dev_pcic.c.  The row's claim is therefore TRUE.  No code changed: the arm is UPSTREAM (39748e3) and its `/* TODO: Fix */` is not discharged by the arithmetic, because whether +0x206 is architecturally right for hpcmips is a hardware question and no manual in _scratchpad covers VR41xx.  Deleting a marker that may point at a live defect needs a warrant this round does not have.

entries.ev: direct reading of DEVINIT(wdc), arithmetic shown
entries.note: VERIFIED INERT BY ARITHMETIC, so the row is settled rather than open-pending-work. The default two lines above the switch is `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206`. The MACHINE_HPCMIPS arm fires only `if (devinit->addr == 0x14000180)` and then assigns 0x14000386. 0x180 + 0x206 = 0x386, so the guarded assignment reproduces the value the default already produced, for the ONE address at which the guard is true. It is dead code in the strict sense: no input distinguishes it. DISPOSITION: do NOT delete it, and this is a change from the filed suggestion. The addition licence has a mirror -- removing code needs a warrant too -- and the branch carries a `/* TODO: Fix */` that is INFORMATION even though the code under it is not: it records that someone believed hpcmips's alt-status address was wrong. Deleting the branch deletes the signal and leaves nothing saying the question was ever raised. Severity is NIL by construction (identical value), so there is nothing to fix and no detector could distinguish the deletion -- DEVINIT is invisible to the offline differential. The right output was the measurement, which is now recorded.
entries.outcome_note: The first arithmetic assessment is confirmed by the second opus5 assess entry of 2026-08-27 and the closure: 0x14000180 + 0x206 equals 0x14000386. Keeping the upstream TODO also matches the closure, which leaves hardware correctness unsettled. [graded by codex gpt-6-astra max, n4, 2026-09-19]

entries.ev: direct reading of dev_wdc.c, dev_pcic.c and git log -L
entries.note:
THE ROW'S CLAIM IS TRUE AND IS SETTLED BY ARITHMETIC.  `DEVINIT(wdc)` defaults
`alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206`, then a switch applies per-machine hacks.  The
MACHINE_HPCMIPS arm fires only when `devinit->addr == 0x14000180` and sets
`alt_status_addr = 0x14000386`.

    0x14000180 + 0x206 == 0x14000386

Identical.  For the ONLY address it can see it recomputes the default, and for any other
address the `if` does not fire.  The arm is dead.

AND THE ADDRESS IT CAN SEE IS FIXED, so 'the only address' is a closed claim rather than a
guess: the sole producer is `dev_pcic.c`, which builds the devinit string with a HARDCODED
literal -- `snprintf(..., "wdc addr=0x14000180 irq=%s.giu.9", ...)`.  `machine_hpcmips.c`
registers no wdc of its own.  Repo-wide, `0x14000180` and `0x14000386` occur only in those
two files (plus an unrelated SGI IP32 alias comment).

*** BUT THE DISPOSITION THE ROW IMPLIES -- DELETE THE DEAD ARM -- IS PREMATURE, AND THE
REASON IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT ALREADY WRITES DOWN ABOUT REMOVING TRIPWIRES. ***  The arm
carries `/*  TODO: Fix  */`, and that TODO is NOT discharged by proving the arithmetic is a
no-op.  It asserts something the arithmetic cannot: that somebody once thought hpcmips
needed a DIFFERENT alt-status address.  Whether `+0x206` is architecturally right for
hpcmips at all is a hardware question, and it is UNSETTLED here --
`ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` lists fifteen manuals and NONE covers VR41xx or hpcmips.

  If `+0x206` is right, the arm is redundant and deleting it is tidy-up with zero delta.
  If `+0x206` is WRONG for hpcmips, the arm is a MARKER pointing at a live defect, and
  deleting it removes the only thing in the tree that says so.  I cannot tell which, and a
  removal needs a measured delta or a transferred warrant -- 'it cannot hurt' is not a
  licence in either direction.

PROVENANCE, checked rather than assumed: `git log -L` on those lines returns ONE commit,
`39748e3` (the unmodified upstream import).  **This is upstream's arm and upstream's TODO,
not the fork's.**  That matters for the disposition: the fork tracks its divergence from
upstream deliberately, and deleting harmless upstream code for zero behavioural gain buys
tidiness at the cost of a divergence entry.

DISPOSITION: ASSESSED, NOT CHANGED.  No product edit.  What the row asked -- is the arm a
no-op? -- is answered YES with its arithmetic shown.  What it did not ask, and what would
have to be answered before touching the code, is now stated as the successor question.

*Filed under the ethos line this project already keeps: an honest 'assessed, not changed'
record.  The alternative was a three-line deletion I could not warrant, on upstream code,
for no measurable effect.*
entries.outcome_note: The producer/provenance assessment is adopted in the closure: the sole hardcoded address makes the arm redundant, while the upstream TODO lacks a removal warrant. Opus5 assess 2026-08-27 records the arithmetic and producer check; no hardware-correctness claim was established. [graded by codex gpt-6-astra max, n4, 2026-09-19]

rows.state_note: *** FILED 2026-08-26 FROM THE #464 PASS-2 PANEL (_scratchpad/panel_20260826_090604), codex seat, [P2]. *** THE MUTANT, verbatim as given: add `d->warned_nonbyte_write = 0;` to the `wd_sector` write arm, after the existing `d->sector = ...` assignment. One line, no guard touched, no diagnostic removed. **A guest that alternates a wide write to wd_seccnt with an ordinary 8-bit write to wd_sector then floods at one host line per pair, forever.** *** WHY ALL 26 ROWS STAY GREEN, AND IT IS THE SAME BLIND SPOT `interleave` WAS BUILT FOR, ONE REGISTER OVER: *** `interleave` pins reset-on-normal-operation at :583 only, using a valid COMMAND opcode. No row in the file writes wd_sector between two wide accesses, so no row can observe a reset keyed there. The detector's own contract already discloses this class as scoped to one site of six -- it is recorded as `wdcflagindep` coverage debt -- but that row names the SITES, not this CONSTRUCTION, and closing `wdcflagindep` on a different site would bury this one. *** IT IS SMALLER THAN THE ESCAPE THE CAPPED ASK-AGAIN FOUND. *** #464's ask-again found width-keying (two lines, at the guard). This is ONE line at a different register and produces an unbounded flood rather than one-line-per-store. **So the ask-again's cap was not the binding constraint here -- the ask-again asked about the GUARD, and this edit never touches a guard.** Worth recording as a limit of that technique rather than a failure of it. DISPOSITION, and it follows the rules rather than a preference: not a wrong record; not a MEASURED false pass, because the seat labelled it source-proven and explicitly un-measured. #464's detector satisfies vacuity-floor clauses (a) through (f), so an escape above the floor is COVERAGE DEBT -- the #447 precedent exactly. FILED. FIRST JOB: build the mutant and score it. If it sweeps 26/26 as predicted, this becomes a measured escape and the row carries the escape list; the closing row is a reset-on-normal-operation probe at wd_sector, which the #464 harness can express directly. **Do NOT fold this into `wdcflagindep`** -- that row is about which SITES share a flag; this is about WHICH REGISTER can clear one.

rows.title: panelrefire  panel.sh printed 're-firing once' and re-fired nothing -- message corrected; the automatic retry itself is not implemented
rows.witness: harness:read -- panel.sh:395-396 printed the claim then `return 2`, and every caller is a bare `check "name" "$file"` whose exit status is discarded, with no seat command re-invoked anywhere after the seat check. Verified by reading the script; no build or run needed.
rows.state_note:
*** FILED 2026-08-26 BY THE CARRIER EXEMPLAR AUDIT. The FALSE MESSAGE is already fixed; what is filed is the missing BEHAVIOUR. *** `panel.sh` printed **'re-firing once (a wall can be minutes long) ...'** and then `return 2`. Nothing consumed that status and nothing was ever relaunched. *** WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STALE CITATION, and it is the reason it was fixed the same hour it was found: *** a stale citation misleads a reader who chooses to follow it. This printed a claim of ACTION, to the operator, at the exact moment a seat was lost -- so the one person who could have re-fired it by hand was told it had already happened. **It is the failure panel.sh itself warns about sixty lines earlier: 'a documented check that cannot fail, which is worse than no check because it reassures.'** DONE: the message is now an INSTRUCTION ('RE-FIRE THIS SEAT ONCE BY HAND ... NOT done automatically') rather than a false report, and the carrier's 'both applied' claim is corrected in place. OWED, and deliberately not done in the same edit: **the automatic retry.** It is a behaviour change to the script EVERY panel runs, so it owes two negative controls before it ships -- (i) prove the retry actually fires on a walled seat, and (ii) prove a seat that ANSWERED is not retried. Without (ii) the retry could double every panel's cost silently, which is the mirror failure. Ranking: harness coverage, below live defects. But the value is concrete -- the carrier records a real instance where a walled seat was recovered only because the owner happened to notice it available in their own UI, which is precisely the human-noticing this harness exists to stop depending on.

**SEVERITY SET LOW, 2026-09-07, by the MAIN LOOP** (not a flagship adjudication -- opus5/fable5 are reserved for the 09-09 adjudication, and a rating is exactly the kind of judgment call that seat exists for; overturn it freely).  REASON: the false message is already corrected; what remains is the unbuilt automatic re-fire, which owes two negative controls.
rows.note: *** panel.sh printed `re-firing once (a wall can be minutes long) ...` AND RE-FIRED NOTHING. ***  Every caller is a bare `check "name" "$file"` whose exit status is discarded, so the `return 2` never had a consumer.  **Worse than a stale citation**: it printed a CLAIM OF ACTION at the exact moment a seat was lost, so the one person who could re-fire it by hand was told it had already been done -- the check-that-cannot-fail shape, reassuring rather than merely wrong.  **DONE (2026-08-30):** the message is an INSTRUCTION and now also says WHERE the command lives.  It stopped at *re-fire this seat by hand* and did not say how, leaving the operator to find one of SEVEN differently-shaped launches 200 lines up -- at the worst possible moment to go looking.  It **points rather than duplicates**: copying the invocation into the message would create a second copy that drifts from the launch, and this project has already carried a FALSE SEAT ROSTER for days for exactly that reason.  Section J holds the carrier's seat table byte-identical to its tracked copy, so a pointer there cannot go stale in silence.  CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, 9 checks, `WALLMSG_PASS`: a walled seat gets the instruction, the pointer, and `$BRIEF`/`$f` EXPANDED TO REAL VALUES; a healthy seat gets none of it and scores `answered`.  *The control's first version used a 59-byte fixture, hit the SIZE branch before the wall branch, and tested nothing -- it would have reported a pass.  The fixtures are now padded past that threshold and the first check asserts the wall branch was reached at all.*  *** STILL OPEN, AND THIS IS THE REMAINING WORK: AUTOMATIC RE-FIRING IS NOT DONE. ***  It cannot be bolted on -- the seven seat launches are inline, in seven different shapes, 200 lines above the checks, so re-firing needs each refactored into a re-runnable unit.  That is a behaviour change to the script EVERY PANEL RUNS and owes two negative controls of its own: prove the retry fires on a walled seat, and prove a seat that ANSWERED is not retried.  **Its own harness round.**  Recorded here rather than half-built, because a partial auto-refire is precisely the class this row is about.

rows.title: depsrm  the standing `rm src/cpus/*.o` rests on a FALSE reason -- the deps ARE tracked. Is the rm needed at all, and what does it cost every mutant table?
rows.witness: harness:read -- src/cpus/Makefile:214 (the GENERATED makefile make reads) lists `cpu_sh.o: cpu_sh.c cpu_sh_instr.c cpu_dyntrans.c memory_rw.c tmp_sh_head.c tmp_sh_tail.c`, from Makefile.skel:194. No build needed to establish that the stated reason is false; a build IS needed to establish whether the rm is still necessary for some other reason.
rows.state_note:
*** OWNER DECISION 2026-09-16: NOT NOW. *** Asked directly, bundled with the other two harness speed-ups (targeted gate-section mode; concurrency for non-timing probes): the answer was NONE OF THEM, keep the queue on #529 and #530.  The measurement is still the right one -- the carrier's stated reason for the `rm' is already known FALSE and a mutant table rebuilds once per mutant -- it is simply NOT SCHEDULED.  A later round may re-raise it with a NEW reason; it may not re-raise it by forgetting this one.  *** THE CARRIER SAID THE `#include`d `.c` FILES ARE 'INVISIBLE TO THE DEP RULES'. THEY ARE NOT. Measured 2026-08-26 by the carrier exemplar audit and verified here. *** `src/cpus/Makefile:214` -- the GENERATED makefile, the one make actually reads -- names them as explicit prerequisites of `cpu_sh.o`, and `Makefile.skel:194` is where that comes from. **Make tracks them.** *** WHY THIS IS A THROUGHPUT QUESTION AND NOT A TIDY-UP: *** the `rm` is executed before EVERY mutant build, and a mutant table is the dominant cost of a round -- one round built NINE binaries. If incremental builds are sound here, that cost drops substantially, and mutant-table time is the single largest lever on how fast this queue moves. **KEEP THE `rm` UNTIL THIS IS MEASURED.** The asymmetry decides it: an unnecessary rebuild costs minutes, a stale object costs a WRONG MEASUREMENT, and this project has already paid that price once. The rm survives as a conservative clean-build precaution -- it has simply never been justified by the reason given for it. THE MEASUREMENT OWED, and it is small: on a scratch copy, (1) build clean; (2) edit one `#include`d `.c` (e.g. cpu_sh_instr.c) and rebuild WITHOUT the rm; (3) assert the resulting binary differs and `[ binary -nt source ]`; (4) repeat for a tmp_*.c generated file, which is the case most likely to still need it. If any step shows a stale object, the rm is necessary and the reason should be recorded CORRECTLY this time. *Found while answering an owner question about what would speed up bug resolution -- and I had just cited the false reason to the owner as a recommendation, which is why it is filed rather than left as a corrected sentence.*

**SEVERITY SET LOW, 2026-09-07, by the MAIN LOOP** (not a flagship adjudication -- opus5/fable5 are reserved for the 09-09 adjudication, and a rating is exactly the kind of judgment call that seat exists for; overturn it freely).  REASON: the standing `rm` rests on a false reason but is retained as a conservative clean-build precaution; the cost is build time, not correctness.

rows.title: countderiver  the transcribed-count class -- ADJUDICATED 2026-08-26: one prose rule, zero new tools, and a pre-specified escalation trigger
rows.witness: none -- documented-only. The class was established by the carrier exemplar audit (five codex jobs over all 2097 lines) and the disposition by adjudication; no code changed and none is owed unless the trigger fires.

closure.note: ADJUDICATED: adopt the deriver rule; reject both mechanical options.

rows.state_note: *** RULING: option (d) 'do nothing' is CORRECT ON ITS EVIDENCE AND WRONG AS A DISPOSITION. *** No stale transcribed count has ever changed a decision -- the adjudicator hunted and found none -- but 'do nothing' misdescribes the record, because the audit's own last three commits already did something, three times, converging on one resolution: **A LITERAL REPLACED BY A SOURCE.** THE RULE ADOPTED: a count written into a durable record NAMES ITS DERIVER (command, script, manifest or log) or carries method+date inline; and **a count being CORRECTED may never land as a fresh bare literal** but as deriver-plus-demoted-prose. STOP CONDITION in the same sentence: fires only on NEW and CORRECTED counts at writing time, audits nothing retroactively, builds NO checker, and the ~70 legacy counts stay under the existing read-side rule with anything decayed FILED rather than swept. *** THE FIFTH OPTION WAS ALREADY SHIPPING IN FOUR PLACES, UNCODIFIED -- which is why the adjudicator was asked to go looking in the tree rather than reason from my list of four. *** `census_exits.py`'s row says 'Re-run it; its output is authoritative and this text is not'; `gate_asan_sweep.sh:27-28` says 'The counts drift with the machine list; that is why nothing below asserts one'; commit `2acd102` re-keyed six drifted citations to grep tokens; commit `26cb38f` 'states the numerator, refuses the denominator, and gives the COMMAND'. Verified all four. The tree had solved this and never written it down. *** BOTH MECHANICAL OPTIONS REJECTED ON MEASUREMENTS, and re-measuring here made the case STRONGER than the adjudicator had it: *** the carrier holds **33 digit+noun counts against 67 WORD-number forms** -- the blind spot is TWICE the visible population, not merely larger -- and the word forms are dominated by rhetorical structure ('ONE LESSON', 'TWO INSTANCES'), not facts. A checker policing the minority while alarming on prose is the switched-off-check shape. The CADENCE option was rejected too: the one-time audit was the right control after three exemplars failed in one day, but as a recurring cost it spends five codex jobs per period against a harm with ZERO measured decision cost. **PRE-SPECIFIED ESCALATION so nobody re-argues it: the FIRST measured decision that consumes a stale count converts the writing rule into the `check_cited_artifacts.py` idiom -- existence-only, forward-only from a cutoff, carrier files only. Until then, no machinery.** PREMISE CHECKS: my 'eleven of ~53' HOLDS (it independently re-bucketed from the audit commits and got 10-12); '29 remain' confirmed as an order of magnitude; derivability HOLDS, spot-checked twice -- `git rev-list` gives 28 for 2026-08-13 in one command, and the carrier WAS 39,942 bytes when '38 KB' was written, so that one genuinely decayed rather than being wrong. It also refined the class: at least two of the eleven fail by **UNIT AMBIGUITY, not decay**, which strengthens the citation rule because the named command is what pins the unit. *** ONE CORRECTION TO THE ADJUDICATION, verified before recording: it could not locate my 'census 13 of 18 mutants' row and asked me to name its source. IT EXISTS -- `regress/drive_guest.py:209` ('13 of 18 driver mutants were measured') and `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md:4212` ('If 13/18 is typical, every "verified" claim in this harness...'). The row was sourced; the search missed it. Recorded because an unanswered caveat in a closed adjudication reads as an unsourced claim forever.***

rows.title: gdromallocpair  alloc_data() does not release before it allocates -- #465's free_data() pairing is CONVENTIONAL, not STRUCTURAL
rows.witness: none -- documented-only. READ and verified 2026-08-26: no third call site exists today, so there is nothing to reproduce. The hazard is what a future caller would do, which is why it is FILED rather than fixed.
rows.state_note: *** FOUND BY THE GROK SEAT ON #465's PASS 2, VERIFIED HERE BY READING. *** `free_data(d)` runs ONCE at the function entry (`:343`); both `alloc_data(d)` sites (`:359`, `:435`) are downstream, so today the buffer is always released before it is replaced. **But `alloc_data()` overwrites `d->data` unconditionally with no release of its own** -- a future THIRD call site not preceded by that entry release leaks the previous buffer, silently. *** THE SHAPE IS THE POINT, and it is #465's own lesson one level up: *** that round added `free_data()` as `alloc_data()`'s counterpart precisely because two fields set together were being released apart. The pairing it established is CONVENTIONAL -- every current path happens to do it -- rather than STRUCTURAL, where the unpaired form is impossible. That is exactly the distinction the round's own corrected comment now draws, after a pass-2 seat refused the word 'unrepresentable'. NOT FIXED, deliberately: a release inside `alloc_data()` is an ADDITION to product code, and the addition licence requires a measured delta or a transferred warrant. **Neither exists yet -- with no third caller, no mutant can measure the difference.** The honest disposition is to record the hazard with its warrant so a round that ADDS a third call site inherits the obligation. Related, same seat: `d->cnt` is guest-writable at `GDROM_CNTLO`/`CNTHI` and reaches `data_len` only through `alloc_data()`. Assessed as a related pair, not this defect.

rows.title: preserveinstrument  the durable-path rule preserves MEASUREMENTS but not the INSTRUMENT -- and the instrument is what makes a result portable
rows.witness: harness:derived 2026-08-30 by censusing the 14 most recent artifact directories that hold a measurement -- 12 preserve their instrument by COPY, 2 by COMMITTED REFERENCE, 14 of 14 identifiable.  Deriver in the note; do not quote the count after more dirs land.
rows.state_note:
*** A SECOND MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, FROM THE SAME PASS: MY CRLF CENSUS WAS OFF BY ONE IN BOTH HALVES, AND THE REASON IS INSTRUCTIVE. *** I reported '55 LF / 2 CRLF of 57'. At `HEAD~1` it was **54 LF / 3 CRLF** -- the third CRLF file was THE PROBE ITSELF, so I had evidently taken the census AFTER my own conversion and then cited it as the BEFORE state. **A census that includes the thing it is measuring the effect of is not a baseline.** The substance survives unchanged and the decision to keep the conversion is right (26 insertions / 3 deletions under `--ignore-all-space`; 667 = 345+322 by numstat); only the number was wrong.

*** THE CLASS WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS ARGUED, AND IT IS SMALL. 2026-08-26. *** Audited every WITNESS field in the ledger for code artifacts (.py/.sh/.c) and asked whether the named file still exists anywhere under the repo or the scratchpad: **48 of 50 resolve. TWO are dead, both on ONE row (`gdromexitsix`: `exitsix_witness.py`, `exit804_witness.py`).** **THAT BOUNDS THE PRACTICE GAP AND IT ARGUES AGAINST MACHINERY**, on the precedent the `countderiver` adjudication set the same day: measure the class before building a checker, and reject the checker when the evidence does not support it. Two dead artifacts on one open row is a note, not a gate. **Recorded so nobody re-argues this as though it were widespread -- my own instinct on finding the first instance was that it would be.** The rule that survives is the cheap one and it is forward-only: **when preserving a seat's measurement, copy the INSTRUMENT alongside the OUTPUT.** One more `cp`, at the moment the outputs are already being saved. *The audit script is not committed: it is a one-shot census, and the honest reading of its own result is that a standing checker is not warranted. Re-derive it by walking each row's `witness` field for filenames and testing existence -- about twenty lines.*

*** THE EXISTING RULE IS RIGHT AND INCOMPLETE. *** It says a measurement cited in a durable record must live at a durable path, because a driver that reuses log names makes a citation point at something ELSE on the next run. That is about the claim being CHECKABLE. **This is about the claim being REPRODUCIBLE and PORTABLE, which is a different property and the one a later round actually needs.** #465's pass-2 seat found that six rows the round called 'owed' had already been built and measured by an earlier seat, and recommended porting them in-round on the explicit grounds that 'the construction and measurement cost is already paid'. It was not: the outputs were preserved and the PROBE was not, so the cost had to be paid again. PROPOSED, not adopted -- it is a practice change and owes the usual scrutiny: **when preserving a seat's measurement, preserve the INSTRUMENT alongside the OUTPUT.** It is one more `cp`, and the asymmetry is stark -- a probe is a few KB while the outputs already cost 22 files, and without it a future round re-derives from prose. *Note the shape: this is the same lesson as `#465`'s own defect, one level up. The round fixed two fields that were SET together and RELEASED apart. Here an output and its instrument are PRODUCED together and PRESERVED apart.*
rows.note: *** THE DURABLE-PATH RULE PRESERVED MEASUREMENTS AND SAID NOTHING ABOUT THE INSTRUMENTS THAT PRODUCED THEM.  A score whose probe is gone is a number you cannot re-derive -- checkable by existence, but not re-runnable. ***  **MEASURED 2026-08-30 rather than asserted.**  Deriver, so this is re-runnable when more dirs land:  `for d in $(ls -dt regress/artifacts/*/*/); do` count `.py`/`.sh` against `.out`/`.txt`/`.log` `; done`.  Result over the 14 most recent dirs holding a measurement: **12 preserve their instrument by copy; 2 do not, and BOTH ARE LEGITIMATE** -- their instrument is a COMMITTED file that is itself the thing under test.  `divsweep_controls_20260830` holds a before/after pair whose instrument is `regress/diag_div_sweep.py`; `batteryreds/tgate_20260829` holds a gate log whose own header names the gate that wrote it.  *** SO THE RULE NEEDED REFINING, NOT ENFORCING, AND THE CENSUS IS WHAT SHOWED THAT. ***  A copy-in-the-dir rule would have scored those two as defects and demanded a duplicate of a committed file -- which is the drift hazard this project already pays for elsewhere (a second copy that diverges from the first).  **THE RULE AS IT SHOULD READ: the instrument must be IDENTIFIABLE from the artifact -- preserved beside the measurement when it is a scratch script, or named when it is a committed file.  Never duplicated.**  NO CHECKER, and the reason is the pattern this project already settled for the counts and citation classes: **no measured decision has been consumed by a missing instrument.**  Every case where a number could not be re-derived was a missing MEASUREMENT (the volatile-path class), not a missing instrument.  Pre-specified escalation, so nobody re-argues it: the first measured decision consumed by an unidentifiable instrument converts this into an existence check on artifact dirs, forward-only from a cutoff.  Until then, prose.  *Closed on a census rather than on a habit.  The practice was already universal when it was measured -- which is the honest reason to close, and is also why the measurement was worth taking before closing rather than after.*

rows.title: probewiringscope  check_probe_wiring.py cannot see any detector below regress/'s top level, while its own docstring claims it covers them
rows.witness: harness:READ and verified 2026-08-26 -- `check_probe_wiring.py:2` says "Every committed DETECTOR under regress/"; `:475` filters `f.endswith('.py') and "/" not in f` and `:481` uses `os.listdir(regress)`, so the walk never descends. Found by the opus5 seat on #465's pass 2.
rows.state_note:
*** FIXED AS #471, COMPLETE RATHER THAN PARTIAL -- which is what the farmed design demanded: 'land a complete path-aware fix WITH an explicit non-shipping classification and the controls above. Do not land only re-key + walk.' ***

**RESULT: 43/47 detectors gated (was 42/46), 60 artefacts seen (was 57), selftest 21/21 mutants red (was 18/18).** The blind spot that let `#465` ship a detector no gate ran is closed, with controls that catch its return.

**FOUR COORDINATED CHANGES, and each was found by the previous one failing:**
  1. dropped the `"/" not in f` filter -- `git ls-files` already yields paths RELATIVE to `regress/`, so top-level files stay bare basenames and **all 57 existing MANIFEST keys keep matching unchanged**. Only nested files gain a path key. That made the re-key far smaller than 'convert 57 entries'.
  2. the on-disk fallback `listdir` -> `walk`, because a check whose coverage depends on which branch it took is the shape this file refuses.
  3. **`exec_sites()` path-keyed** -- a nested invocation was being classed as EXTERNAL and IGNORED, so the detector `#465` wired by hand still reported UNWIRED once the scan could see it. The design predicted this exactly: *'provided exec_sites() is path-keyed too'*.
  4. **the selftest's OWN COPY was flat**, so every nested MANIFEST entry became a GHOST inside it and reddened the unmutated control. **The same blind spot one level up, inside the harness that tests for it** -- a flat copy cannot exercise a recursive scan.

**`CLASS_RESEARCH` earned itself immediately.** Without it the two preserved instruments (`mism_probe.py`, `mutate.py`) face a false choice: MISFILED as tools because of the `_probe.py` suffix, or UNWIRED as detectors owing a gate they should never have. They are EVIDENCE, not tests. *And I created that conflict this morning by preserving them under the `preserveinstrument` rule -- my fix for one row blocking the fix for another.*

*** THE SHARPEST FINDING IS ABOUT THE HARNESS, NOT THE CHECKER: M14's FIRST VERSION MEASURED GREEN. *** I aimed it at the `git ls-files` branch -- but **the selftest copy is not a git repo**, so the header reads `[on-disk (git could not answer)]` and the WALK FALLBACK is what actually runs. **A mutant aimed at a code path the test never takes proves nothing.** Re-aimed at the fallback, it reddens correctly. **Consequence worth carrying: the git branch is UNTESTED by this selftest, and it is the branch that runs in production.**

THREE MORE SELF-INFLICTED TRAPS, all of which the file had already solved:
  * `\\n` became a REAL NEWLINE inside a string literal -- the backslash trap, **fourth instance today**. Fixed with `chr(10)`.
  * my COMMENT quoted the mutant's own find-text, so `_st_apply` saw it twice and REFUSED -- the harness correctly rejecting an ambiguous mutant, and the **third time today** that documentation broke a tool which greps for what it documents.
  * the file already had **`_lit()`** for exactly that: *'Join fragments, so the assembled search string appears nowhere in this source.'*

*The pattern across all four: the file had already solved each problem, and I re-derived each solution the hard way. `_lit()`, the `chr()` constants, the mutant-applies guard -- every one was built by someone hitting exactly what I hit.*

*** FIX DESIGNED 2026-08-26 BY A FARMED codex JOB -- AND IT FOUND THAT THE NAIVE FIX WOULD BREAK SOMETHING I CREATED EARLIER THE SAME DAY. ***

**THE NAIVE FIX -- re-key `MANIFEST`/`EXEMPT` from basename to relative path, swap `listdir` for `walk` -- MUST NOT LAND ALONE.** Recursion immediately pulls in `regress/artifacts/gdrompionull/opus_p2_20260826/mism_probe.py`, which is an ARCHIVED RESEARCH instrument, not a shipping detector. Its `_probe.py` suffix means classifying it as `tool` trips the checker's MISFILED rule, while classifying it as a detector demands a gate or an exemption it should never have. **It is a file with no honest class.**

*** AND I PUT IT THERE. *** It was preserved this morning under the `preserveinstrument` rule -- filed one hour earlier, applied on its first opportunity. **My fix for one row created the conflict that blocks the fix for another**, and neither row could see it: the population is exactly TWO nested probes, the gated detector and the instrument I archived.

**SO THE PROJECT'S OWN 'do not alarm on the rest of the class' OBJECTION APPLIES HERE, and the seat said so explicitly** -- the naive fix would force an archival file into a false choice between MISFILED and UNWIRED. **The recommendation is all-or-nothing: land a complete path-aware fix WITH an explicit `research`/`nonshipping` classification, or do not land it. Do not land only re-key + `walk`.**

THREE SELF-TEST CONTROLS SPECIFIED, for the file's existing 18-mutant `--selftest` harness:
  * **NESTED GREEN** -- the unmodified copied tree must show the nested detector as RUN by its gate, not IGNORED or UNWIRED.
  * **NESTED RED** -- delete its real invocation from the copied gate; require exit 1 naming the FULL RELATIVE PATH as UNWIRED.
  * **COLLISION** -- add a second classified detector with the SAME BASENAME in a different subdirectory, gate only the original, require the second to remain UNWIRED. **A regression back to basename keying would incorrectly turn BOTH green** -- which is the silent failure the re-key exists to prevent.

*Checked: NO same-basename collision exists in `regress/` today, so that hazard is PROSPECTIVE. The existing duplicate-literal guard still works with path keys, provided `exec_sites()` is path-keyed too.*

**DISPOSITION: still worth fixing** -- the seat was asked whether it might not be, and answered that `#465`'s escape is direct evidence the blind spot matters even though today's detector is now wired by hand. But it is a LARGER change than the row implied, and shipping half of it is worse than shipping none.

*** THIS IS THE STRUCTURAL LANDING SPOT FOR #465's HEADLINE LESSON, AND THE ROUND MISSED IT. *** #465 found that its detector was wired into NO GATE, recorded 'a detector no gate runs is not a detector', and discharged it by a HUMAN GREP. **The mechanical check for exactly that class already exists and was BLIND BY SCOPE** -- `gdrompionull` lived at `regress/artifacts/gdrompionull/`, one level down, where the checker cannot look. **So the round wrote its lesson as prose while the structure that should have carried it sat one directory away, silently not covering the case.** That is the carrier's structure-first rule failing in its own terms, and it is a CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL for a whole subtree -- the class this project named twice today (`panel.sh`'s phantom re-fire, `grok models` as a tier check). **EXPOSURE IS ZERO TODAY, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED IN-ROUND:** 1 of 57 tracked `regress/**.py` sat below top level, and it is now gated by hand. The defect is latent, not live. THE FIX, as the seat scoped it: re-key `MANIFEST`/`EXEMPT` from BASENAME to RELATIVE PATH and replace `os.listdir` with `os.walk`. **It owes negative controls in both directions** -- prove a subdirectory detector with no gate is now RED, and prove a gated one stays GREEN -- and the file already carries an 18-mutant `--selftest` harness to hang them on. A basename->path re-key can silently collide (two files with the same basename in different directories), so that needs its own row. *A checker whose docstring overclaims its scope is worse than one that admits a limit: the docstring is what a future round reads when deciding whether the class is already covered.*

rows.title: loadfragile  every pty probe waited on an ABSOLUTE deadline, so a merely SLOW run failed identically to a STUCK one -- the battery could only be trusted on an idle machine
rows.witness: harness:selftest_inactivity.py -- proves the property behaviourally against a stub, no rig and no build. Negative-controlled both directions: removing the reset from one probe turns it RED and names the file; restoring goes GREEN.
rows.state_note:
*** PASS 2 ON 29b450c REFUTED THIS ROUND'S SAFETY LEMMA, TWO SEATS INDEPENDENTLY. ***

I wrote that the inactivity deadline *'cannot turn a passing run into a failing one'* and presented it as the whole safety argument. **It is correct and INCOMPLETE, which is worse than wrong because it reads as a proof.** codex: *'monotonic for successful runs, but not failure-safe; noisy failure defeats the bound.'* kimi, independently: *'both failure directions exist.'*

**THE HONEST PROPERTY: monotonic for SUCCESSFUL runs, UNBOUNDED for NOISY FAILURES.** A run that fails while still producing output never trips the deadline at all. A run that hangs SILENTLY is still caught -- which is the case the deadline was written for, so the change is still right; the CLAIM was over-general.

**TWO MORE OVERCLAIMS -- AND CHECKING THEM CORRECTED MY OWN CORRECTION.** An earlier draft of this note said both were *'corrected in the round block'*. **Neither was IN the round block.** Verified: the CHANGELOG already says *'Scope is two probes ... the remaining ~245 sites are FILED as `loadfragile`'*, and it never claims `free_run` is the ONLY absolute window -- it only explains why that one is not converted.
  * *'changes every pty probe deadline'* -- **that was in MY BRIEF, not the record.** It changes TWO. codex caught it as a contradiction between my prose and my own CHANGELOG, which means the CHANGELOG was the half that was right.
  * *'`free_run` is the only intentional absolute window'* -- **also the brief.** There is another: `max_drain_s` in `run_arm`, which bounds and measures the whole drain phase. I claimed completeness on an enumeration I had not finished.
  *So the shipped RECORD was accurate on scope and my BRIEF was not -- which is the opposite of what I first wrote here. A correction block earns the same scrutiny as the thing it corrects; this one did not get it until the anchor failed and forced a check.*

*** AND A BRIEF DEFECT THAT IS WORSE THAN ANY OF THEM, because it degrades the panel itself: MY BRIEF LABELLED A TRUNCATED EXTRACT 'THE PRODUCT DIFF, verbatim'. *** It carried 78 lines -- the header hunks only -- of a **12-file, 427-insertion** commit, and `#467`'s probe change was ABSENT ENTIRELY while two of my five questions asked about it.

**The Ollama seats CANNOT READ FILES. They see only what is inlined.** So calling a truncated extract 'verbatim' does not merely omit -- it tells a packet-fed seat that the omission is the whole thing. kimi caught it by checking the hunk-header arithmetic against what followed, and said so in its verdict line.

*Both dissents were worth more than a ratification: they found the guard's negative-domain hole, the incomplete lemma, and three wrong records -- while confirming the code itself is sound.*

*** RAISED BY THE OWNER ASKING WHETHER WINDOWS COULD EVER BE IDLE ENOUGH. The honest answer was no -- and that reframes the problem: do not chase idleness, remove the load-sensitivity. ***

**MY FIRST FRAMING WAS WRONG AND I CORRECTED IT BEFORE ACTING.** I proposed converting the worst offenders to WORK-ACCOUNTING, on `#419`'s precedent (`LUNA_BUDGET` counts guest instructions, so a loaded host executes the same work and the oracle holds). Classifying the 249 wall-clock references showed that is not the defect:

    guest-side budgets, already work-accounted      3
    pty TRANSPORT timeouts                        245
    true measurement oracles (the #419 case)        1

**Work-accounting cannot fix a transport timeout**: while you wait for bytes there are no guest instructions to count -- the whole point is you do not know whether the guest is running. Converting literally as proposed would have changed ONE thing.

**THE REAL DEFECT, and it is bigger: ZERO files used an inactivity deadline.** Every one read `t = time.time()` once and looped `while time.time() - t < timeout` -- a TOTAL-TIME budget spent by the clock rather than by the guest. A boot that normally takes 40 s and takes 90 s under load FAILS while bytes arrive steadily throughout.

**THE FIX: reset the clock when the buffer grows**, so `timeout` means SILENCE. `rd()` cannot report progress -- it returns True both on data and on a quiet select() tick -- so progress is `len(self.buf)` changing. **SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: strictly more permissive for a run that produces output, identical for one that does not. It cannot turn a passing run into a failing one.**

*** `free_run(seconds)` IS DELIBERATELY NOT CONVERTED. *** It is not a timeout at all -- it is an EXPOSURE WINDOW that runs the guest for a set period and then SIGINTs. Converting it would change the experiment rather than protect it, **and a naive sweep over `time.time()` sites would have eaten it.** That is why this converts one NAMED method rather than a pattern.

DETECTOR SHIPPED WITH THE FIX: `selftest_inactivity.py`, two legs OPPOSITE IN SIGN -- slow-but-progressing (old shape FAILS, new PASSES) and genuinely-stuck (BOTH must still FAIL). **The second leg is the one that matters: a conversion that made the timeout unreachable would sail through the first and defend nothing.** Plus a source leg catching a silent revert.

SCOPE: two probes converted -- the measured worst offenders, 7 tight budgets each. The remaining ~245 sites are the same class and are FILED here rather than swept, because each needs the `free_run` distinction checked by hand.

*One conversion needed care: `fbpending_drain_probe.py` is one of only two CRLF files in the tree. It was converted PRESERVING its line endings (+16/-0), because normalising would have produced the ~500-line churn diff this session already had to justify once.*

rows.title: mb89352halt  An unimplemented SCSI command stops the emulated CPU rather than refusing the command
rows.witness: none -- folded into [[b120]], which is the same omission at the same site. Not an independent finding.
rows.state_note:
*** DROPPED 2026-08-27 AS A DUPLICATE I FILED MYSELF. It is [[b120]]'s mb89352 face, not a separate defect -- and my own b120 record already lists it as one of that row's four outcomes. ***

**The halt fires BECAUSE of b120**: the shared dispatcher's `default:` arm (`diskimage_scsicmd.c:1380-1388`) leaves `status` / `status_len` unset and returns 1; mb89352 then enters `PH_STAT` and hits `if (d->transfer_bufpos(0) >= len(0))` at `dev_mb89352.c:173`, which sets `cpu->running = 0`.

**So fixing b120 to return CHECK CONDITION with sense (`status_len >= 1`) makes that read succeed and REMOVES THE HALT.** One fix site, one semantic class -- there is nothing left for a separate row to carry.

*My error, and worth naming: I filed it while recording b120's own correction, in the same sitting where I wrote 'CPU halt on mb89352' as b120 outcome number four. **A finding that arrives as a by-product of another row's analysis is the easiest kind to double-file** -- it feels new because it was found separately.*

**FILED SEPARATELY AND DELIBERATELY NOT HERE:** a weaker defence-in-depth item -- mb89352 should refuse gracefully rather than `cpu->running = 0` on ANY zero-length status, hardening it against any future path that leaves status empty. That is a different (and smaller) claim than this row made, and it is not b120's round.

*** FILED 2026-08-27, found by an adversarial opus pass while REFUTING the mechanism of [[b120]]. It is a separate and more severe defect than the row it was found under. ***

On `dev_mb89352.c`, an unimplemented SCSI command reaches the dispatcher's `default:` arm, which leaves `data_in == NULL`. The controller then sets `d->phase = PH_STAT` (`:284`). The guest's PH_STAT `DREG` read takes `p = xferp->status` (**NULL**) and `len = xferp->status_len` (**0**) (`:158-161`), with `transfer_bufpos` reset to 0 (`:429`) -- so `0 >= 0` trips the `DREG: read longer than buffer?` arm at `:173`, which emits at `VERBOSITY_ERROR` **and sets `cpu->running = 0`.**

> **A guest that issues an unimplemented command to an mb89352 target STOPS THE EMULATED CPU.** That is not a refusal and not a false success -- it is a guest-drivable halt, and it ranks above [[b120]]'s false-success behaviour on harm.

**Relationship to [[b120]]:** same omission, different controller. b120's fix -- populate a status buffer and return CHECK CONDITION -- **would also fix this**, because the halt is caused precisely by the absent status buffer. So this does not need an independent fix, but it DOES need its own detector row, since b120's observable (a status byte) is not this one's (the CPU still running).

**Observable:** whether the emulated CPU is still running after an unimplemented opcode is issued to an mb89352 target. Binary, and it needs no status decoding.

*Filed rather than fixed: the stopping rule files anything that is not a measured false pass or a wrong record against shipped material, and this is a newly found defect, not a defect in what shipped today.*

rows.title: m8sarrows  The m88k CMMU seam is structurally blind: a ONE-IDENTIFIER edit sweeps both offline detectors 79/79 while half the machine's PATC flushes stop dispatching
rows.witness: harness:the mutant M1 and its controls were MEASURED against the two shipped offline detectors (diff_m8820x, diff_m8invread). `harness:` is the right kind -- the subject is the test apparatus, and the proof is a mutation the tools fail to catch.
rows.state_note:
*** FILED 2026-08-27 as the successor to [[m8sarseq]], carrying its dissent VERBATIM as provenance. The spec below was MEASURED by an opus5 assess on 2026-08-26 and existed in exactly ONE place -- that row's entry text -- until this row was created. ***

**THE MUTANT (M1):** `dev_m8820x.c:108`, `cmmu[d->cmmu_nr]->reg` -> `cmmu[0]->reg`. **One identifier.** Verified at that line today: it reads `uint32_t *regs = cpu->cd.m88k.cmmu[d->cmmu_nr]->reg;`.

**IT SWEEPS BOTH SHIPPED DETECTORS CLEAN: 79/79** -- `diff_m8820x` 46 rows plus `diff_m8invread` 33 rows, denominators self-reported by the harnesses. Each file carries deliberate `@@SELFCHECK@@` FAIL lines as negative controls, so a small non-zero raw grep IS the green baseline. *(I flagged a discrepancy here and there is none: a grep counts THREE markers per file, but one is the explanatory comment -- *"THE PROBE ROWS ARE NAMED @@SELFCHECK@@ SO THEY CANNOT BE MISTAKEN FOR A ROW"* -- and the other two are the deliberately-mismatched rows `check("@@SELFCHECK@@/str", "a", "b")` and `check("@@SELFCHECK@@/num", "1", "2")`. **The entry's two is correct; my three counted the comment.** Same substring trap as counting `exit(1)` matches that are prose.)*

*** THE CONTROLS ARE WHAT MAKE THIS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN AN ASSERTION, AND THEY SHOW THE BLINDNESS IS STRUCTURAL: ***
  * **M3** (`sar = 0`) reddens D1/D3 -- the harness CAN see a CONSUMER-side SAR defect;
  * **M4** (drop the SAR store) reddens E7/E8/G6/G7 -- it CAN see a PRODUCER-side one.
**Both ends are covered; only the SEAM is blind.** The reason is mechanical: every SCR-flush row runs after `fresh()`, which memsets the device so `cpu_nr = cmmu_nr = 0`, and issues from cpu0 -- and at (0,0) every candidate base for `regs` coincides.

*** M1 IS A LIVE-DEFECT CLASS ON THE SHIPPED RIG, NOT A SHAPE PIN -- and the load-bearing facts were re-verified from source today rather than trusted from a harness comment: ***
  * `dev_luna88k.c:1041-1042` [at 987cb596: :1078-1081, one call per CPU 0-3; each call adds that CPU's instruction and data CMMU (:946-961), so CPU 0's call alone registers both] calls `add_cmmu_for_cpu(devinit, 0, ...)` AND `(devinit, 1, ...)`, so **both CMMUs are registered on every boot**;
  * `dev_m8820x.c:541-543` -- *`// cmmu nr 0 = instruction, 1 = data.`* then `d->cmmu_nr = devinit->addr2 & 1;` -- so **`cmmu_nr = 1` is guest-addressable on every luna88k boot**;
  * the data CMMU takes **318,457 of 613,342 SAR writes (51.9%)**.
**So under M1 roughly HALF the machine's PATC flushes never dispatch at all** -- the silently-under-invalidating TLB that the file's own comment calls *'not a cosmetic gap'*.

*(M2, the `(cpu, d)` swap, is by contrast a SHAPE PIN: the booting rig is single-CPU.)*

*** THE FIX IS THREE ROWS, EACH WITH ITS OWN MEASURED KILL, NONE DECORATION: ***
```
  K1   matching entry dropped            reddens under M1 / M1b
  K2   non-matching entry retained       reddens under M5
  K3   flush from a NON-OWNER cpu        reddens under M2
```

rows.title: exitdenom  The terminating-site census counts SITES, not defects -- and the number has had three generations (114 -> 170 -> 360), each recorded as if authoritative
rows.witness: harness:tools/pipeline/exit_census.py, controlled BOTH ways -- a real scope reports 118 files / 292 raw / 174 live and ends EXITCENSUS_DONE; an empty scope REFUSES rather than reporting zero
rows.state_note:
*** FILED 2026-08-27, RESCUED FROM A ROW THAT HAD JUST BEEN CLOSED. It was the 'REMAINING QUESTION for the next seat' inside [[exitsweep]]'s hold -- and closing that row put a question addressed to a future seat somewhere no seat will ever be fired at it. ***

**THE QUESTION, verbatim from that hold:** *what is the honest DEFECT denominator, as opposed to the site count?*

**WHY IT IS NOT PEDANTRY.** The census reports **360 sites, 90 inside DEVICE_ACCESS** (deriver: `python tools/pipeline/census_exits.py`, default invocation, confirmed by two independent seats at HEAD). But its own output says **'This counts SITES, not defects'**, and it counts:
  * `exit(` with ANY status -- not only `exit(1)`;
  * `abort()`, `CHECK_ALLOCATION(` and `FAILURE(`;
  * **known NON-defects** -- the INTENDED `dev_cons.c:80` `exit(0)`, the UNREACHABLE `dev_ram.c:132`, and init-time failures where terminating IS the correct behaviour.

It also does **not resolve HELPER reachability** (101 of the 360 are in helpers), so a helper site that no guest path reaches counts the same as one a single load reaches.

*** THE COUNT HAS HAD THREE GENERATIONS AND EACH WAS RECORDED AS AUTHORITATIVE: *** **114**, then **170** (*'corrected up from a recorded 114 by a denominator measurement'*), then **360**. And two further superseded figures sit on [[devexit]] -- *'271 exit(1) calls in 50 of the 118 files'* and *'398 exit sites with 120 inside device handlers'*. **Five numbers, one quantity, and they do not all count the same thing** -- which is the substantive point rather than the tally: the drift is mostly a changing DEFINITION, not a changing tree.

> **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: classify the 360 into DEFECT / NON-DEFECT / UNREACHABLE, with the rule for each class written down**, and make the classifier part of the tool so the answer re-derives instead of being transcribed. A site count is a workload estimate; a defect count is a queue. **The scheduling questions the parent row asked -- batching, per-device versus per-class, what each batch owes -- cannot be answered against a number that includes `exit(0)` on purpose.**

**Cheap and read-only**: no build, no rig, no wall-clock oracle. It is a classification pass over a list the tool already produces.

*Provenance: [[exitsweep]] closed 2026-08-27 in the adjudicated closure sweep. The close was correct -- the inventory was done and its witness admissible -- but the row carried a live question for a future seat, and closing a row silently retires every question inside it. **That is the general hazard this row exists to illustrate as well as to answer.**


*** MAIN-LOOP RECORD 2026-09-07 (triage stage) -- written into state_note, NOT into `entries'. ***
`entries' is the SEAT ANSWER list: check_stage_panels.py counts entries to decide whether a stage's
nine seats were fired, and gen_dashboard.py REFUSES TO RENDER on a seat id no column declares.  A
main-loop note parked there is not merely mis-filed -- it MANUFACTURES A SEAT ANSWER THAT NEVER
HAPPENED, which is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape inverted.  Seven such entries were
written during this session and all seven were migrated here when the generator refused.

**A MECHANISM FOR THE FIVE-NUMBERS PROBLEM, found by running the tools rather than by reading the records:
THERE ARE TWO CENSUS TOOLS WITH NEAR-IDENTICAL NAMES AND DIFFERENT DEFINITIONS.**

    tools/pipeline/census_exits.py    <- this row's deriver: 360 sites, 90 in DEVICE_ACCESS
    tools/pipeline/exit_census.py     <- 152 LIVE calls, 118 files, comment-aware

`census_exits' and `exit_census' are the same two words in the opposite order, they live in the same
directory, and they answer the same-sounding question with figures differing by more than 2x -- because they
count different things (this row already records that its deriver counts `abort()', `CHECK_ALLOCATION(' and
`FAILURE(' and any exit status, while the other reports comment-stripped `exit(1)' calls).

**Neither is wrong.  What is wrong is that a record citing `the census' does not say which**, and a reader
re-deriving with the other tool gets a different answer and reasonably concludes the record decayed.  That is
a mechanism for at least part of the 114 -> 170 -> 360 drift this row was opened about, and it is not
something re-deriving can fix: **both derivers are live, correct, and disagree.**

Noted rather than acted on -- renaming a tool breaks every record that cites it, which is a decision for the
round that takes this row, not a rider on a triage pass.  What IS cheap and is done here: the `sgirekills'
title now names its deriver inline, so that one row cannot be re-derived with the wrong tool.
rows.note: *** A DERIVER SHIPPED INSTEAD OF A FOURTH NUMBER.  `tools/pipeline/exit_census.py`, 2026-08-30. ***  This row's whole complaint is that the census has had three generations -- 114 -> 170 -> 360 -- *each recorded as if authoritative*, and none comparable because none said what it counted.  **Writing down a fourth would have been the defect, not the fix.**  WHAT THE TOOL PINS, and these are exactly what the old numbers left unsaid:  **SCOPE** `src/devices/*.c`, overridable by `$GXEXITDIR`, path derived from `__file__` rather than hardcoded;  **PATTERN** `exit(` / `abort(` / `_exit(`;  **UNIT** SITES, not defects -- a site may be unreachable, construction-time or already triaged, and the tool says so rather than implying a defect count.  *** AND IT MEASURES THE THING THAT MADE THE OLD NUMBERS DRIFT: 118 OF 292 RAW GREP HITS -- 40% -- ARE INSIDE COMMENTS. ***  A naive `grep -c` overcounts by 68%, and **that error GROWS with every fix**, because this fork's de-fatalisation comments QUOTE the `exit(1)` they removed.  The census therefore gets steadily more wrong as the tree gets more honest -- the same shape as the stale-text grep that cannot tell an assertion from a quotation of one.  The tool strips comments with a state machine that respects string literals, and prints the raw count BESIDE the live one so the two can never be confused again.  *I hit this myself an hour earlier: a one-file grep scored `break;  /* OB-20: was exit(1) */` as a live exit.*  CONTROLLED BOTH WAYS on the day it landed: a real scope reports its figures and ends `EXITCENSUS_DONE`; an EMPTY scope **refuses outright** -- *'ZERO live calls across 0 files is a contradiction, not a result'* -- which is this project's pattern-selects-nothing guard built into the tool that would most suffer from it.  **THE ROW STAYS OPEN.**  A deriver fixes the DENOMINATOR's instability; the row's other half -- that SITES ARE NOT DEFECTS -- is a per-site reachability question no census can answer, and 174 live sites is emphatically not 174 defects.  *** AND THE TOOL NOW ANSWERS PART OF THE ROW'S SECOND HALF -- the part that IS mechanical. ***  `SITES are not DEFECTS` stays true and unanswerable in general, but the enclosing construct is decidable by reading:  **DEVICE_ACCESS 99 (56.9%) -- on a guest access path BY CONSTRUCTION**; static helpers 51; **DEVINIT 17 (9.8%) -- construction-time, no guest reaches them**; file scope 6; DEVICE_TICK 1.  The 99 live in 30 of 118 files.  So the queue's search space is **99 sites in 30 files**, not 174 in 118 -- and 17 are provably out of scope for a guest-reachability question.  *** THE TOOL PROVES ITS OWN LIMIT ON ITSELF, WHICH IS WHY THE NARROWING IS HONEST: the first DEVICE_ACCESS site it reports for `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` is `:1055`, and that site is UNREACHABLE. ***  `cmd_count` steps by 2, the `== 12` equality clears the busy bit at the boundary, and `0xa0` resets it -- a warrant that had to be derived by hand.  **DEVICE_ACCESS means WHERE TO LOOK, never WHAT IS BROKEN**, and the tool says so in its own output.  CROSS-CHECKED against a hand census: run on `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` alone it reports **3 live calls, all DEVICE_ACCESS** -- exactly the three I derived by hand (`:1055`, `:1094`, `:1154`), with the `:792` comment false-positive correctly excluded.  A tool that reproduces an independently-derived count, including the trap that fooled the hand version, is worth more than one that merely runs.  Both controls re-run after the extension, because a control that is not re-run after the thing it controls changes is not a control.  *** TWO CONCRETE INSTANCES OF THE CLASS, BOTH FOUND 2026-08-30, AND THEY DIFFER IN A WAY THAT MATTERS FOR HOW THIS ROW SHOULD BE FIXED. ***  The census counts SYNTACTICALLY live `exit(1)` calls; neither of these can execute.  **(1) `dev_sgi_re.c` `sgi_mte`, the shape `if (len == 4) ... else if (len != 4) ... else { fatal(); exit(1); }`** -- reaching the else needs `len != 4` and `len == 4` at once.  **UNDOCUMENTED**: nothing in the file says the guard is dead, and `sgirekills` counts it among its 15 live DEVICE_ACCESS kills.  **(2) `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c`, the `cmd_count >= 12` / "Too much GDROM_DATA" arm** -- `cmd_count` steps by two from a zero that is set in the same breath as `busy |= 0x08`, so it meets `== 12` exactly and clears busy before the `>= 12` test can ever see it.  **FULLY DOCUMENTED, and better than documented -- MEASURED**: the file records that a proposed narrow-access fix *"makes eleven byte writes plus one word write go 11 -> 13, SKIPPING the `== 12` equality, so busy&0x08 never clears and the next write reaches the 'Too much GDROM_DATA' exit -- otherwise unreachable"*, and would additionally write `cmd[12]`, one past the array.  *"A fix that re-opens a dead site is worse than the defect, and only a build saw it."*  > **SO THE CENSUS'S DENOMINATOR IS INFLATED BY AT LEAST TWO, AND THE REMEDY IS NOT A > REACHABILITY ANALYSER.**  Case (2) shows why: its deadness is CONDITIONAL on an > arithmetic invariant (step-by-two from a paired reset) that no static pass would derive, > and a round that 'fixed' the arm would resurrect it.  What separates the two cases is > whether the file SAYS SO -- and case (2) says so with a measurement attached.  **The cheap, honest fix for this row is therefore an ANNOTATION, not an analysis: a dead site carries a comment saying it is dead and why, and the census subtracts annotated sites and reports them separately.**  That keeps the number checkable, keeps the warrant next to the code where a future round will read it before editing, and cannot silently mis-classify a live site as dead -- because writing the annotation is a deliberate act with a stated reason, which is exactly what case (2) already demonstrates and case (1) lacks.

entries.note:
*** THIS ENTRY IS THE MAIN LOOP'S OWN WORK, NOT A SEAT ANSWER. ***  It is filed
under the opus5 column because the ledger declares no main-loop column, and the
seat ledger's own rule is that seat and main-loop hat are DISTINCT -- so saying so
here is the only thing that keeps the column from lying.  The opus5 SEAT's entry
is separate and was PENDING when this was written.
REPRODUCED ON THE COMMITTED BUILD BEFORE ANY EDIT, which is what licenses the round.

`fread_helper()` splits an overlayed read into 512-byte pieces and its three accounting
lines disagree about which length they use -- `buf` and `len` move by the REQUESTED
amount, `totallenread` counts the ACTUAL one.  A short read in a NON-FINAL iteration
therefore leaves a stale HOLE at its own position while later iterations still land
correctly, and the caller's tail `memset(buf + lendone, 0, len - lendone)` then destroys
an equal number of VALID bytes at the far end.  The access returns 1.

MEASURED, 1536 bytes at offset 0 over a 200-byte overlay claiming block 0:
