entries.note:
VERDICT: FIX B -- zero-fill the hole in place, count the requested length, continue.
It filled the ninth seat it had been deferred from, and it corrected me twice on facts I
had already checked once.

*** (1) 'A IS NOT FAIL-STOP -- IT IS FAIL-MORE.'  THE SINGLE SENTENCE THAT SETTLES THE
ROUND. ***  The read path's system-level postcondition is FIXED by the caller whichever
fix ships: the tail memset runs, the function returns 1, and the only read-side `return 0`
(the bounds arm) is unreachable from a short read.  So the ONLY degree of freedom either
fix controls is WHICH BYTES ARE FABRICATED ZEROS.  B fabricates exactly the lost bytes --
the minimum possible.  A fabricates the lost bytes PLUS every healthy byte after them, up
to 63.5 sectors of a 64-sector wdc__read chunk.  'Stop and report the prefix' is a
principled shape only where the report can change the outcome; here the caller converts
the report into more zeros and success either way.

  And a non-reason, stated so nobody credits it later: A's larger zeroed region is NOT
  'louder' to the guest.  Zeros carry no signal -- the fork's own #416 comment in
  diskimage_scsicmd.c records exactly this, that a zero-filled short read 'reports a
  successful read of zeros, which is why a short or refused transfer was invisible'.

*** (2) I HAD READ HALF THE PRECEDENT.  diskimage_access__cue CONTAINS BOTH SHAPES, KEYED
BY CAUSE -- AND ITS FIRST ARM IS FIX B. ***  The `t == NULL` arm zero-fills in place,
COUNTS THE CHUNK, and CONTINUES.  My sibling-parity write-up cited only the short-fread
arm and concluded 'precedent points at A'.  In-place-zero-and-continue is already the
fork's house shape for 'this piece has no data but the access must proceed'.

  AND THE DISANALOGY I OFFERED IS THE CORRECT READING, with a sharper warrant than mine:
  arm 3's break is harmless AT ITS HOME SITE because a CUE track file spans tens of
  megabytes while a guest access spans kilobytes -- the rest of the access almost always
  resolves in the same broken file, so stopping discards nothing recoverable.  In
  fread_helper the layers interleave at 512-byte granularity BY DESIGN, so the same shape
  discards up to an access-full of healthy data.  *The warrant element that makes arm 3
  safe -- 'what follows is probably in the same bad file' -- measurably fails to transfer.*
  That is the carrier's transfer-a-precedent rule working: check each ELEMENT, not the
  shape.

*** (3) THE FIFTH DEAD PREMISE, WHICH I ASKED FOR AND GOT: 'THE READ PATH HAS NO FAILURE
CHANNEL' IS FALSE AS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE SYSTEM. ***  diskimage__internal_access returns
0 for reads on the bounds arm, and diskimage_scsicmd.c has a LIVE, FORK-BUILT (#416)
consumer that turns that 0 into CHECK CONDITION with sense data.  What is true is
narrower: the HELPER's shortfall is severed by the tail memset, and the wdc caller
discards the result.  The round's conclusion survives -- neither fix can signal through
the severed link -- but the OPTION-SET consequence is real and is filed (below).

*** (4) A SEVERITY ELEVATION I MISSED, AND I RE-VERIFIED IT BY READING BEFORE RECORDING
IT.  '312 STALE CALLER BYTES' UNDERSELLS THE COMMITTED BEHAVIOUR. ***  In wdc__read the
hole is not abstract caller memory:

  COMMON ARM   reads directly into `d->inbuf + d->inbuf_head`, the PERSISTENT RING, so
               the hole retains PREVIOUS RING CONTENTS -- stale prior-sector data replayed
               to the guest.
  WRAP ARM     reads into `unsigned char buf[512 * MAX_SECTORS_PER_CHUNK]`, a plain
               UNINITIALISED automatic array, and then copies EVERY byte into the ring
               with `for (i=0; i<512*to_read; i++) wdc_addtoinbuf(d, buf[i]);` --
               unconditionally, regardless of what the read actually filled.  So the hole
               is UNINITIALISED HOST STACK MEMORY handed to the guest.

  Both verified in the tree by me before this was written down.  The class is therefore
  corruption PLUS host-memory disclosure on the wrap arm, and BOTH FIXES CLOSE BOTH.  SCSI
  holes read as zeros (its transfer buffer is allocated zeroed), so this is wdc-specific.

(5) IT ATTACKED GROK'S ENOSPC REFUTATION AND REPORTED THAT IT SURVIVES, which is the right
way to treat a refutation that favours one's own convenience.  `do_fsync` defaults off, but
POSIX fseek flushes unwritten output and the per-block fseek pattern flushes data before
the bitmap within every iteration -- so a crash loses the BIT while keeping the DATA, the
benign direction.  One residual narrow window (a deferred-ENOSPC whose data flush fails and
is discarded at the next iteration's fseek while the already-durable bit stands) is
footnote-grade, and the clean-close path already orders data-before-bitmap deliberately.

(6) A RECORD NOTE THE ROUND MUST CARRY IN PROSE, or a future reader files a defect against
it: under B, fread_helper's return degenerates to FULL LENGTH OR 0, so BOTH the write-only
short-transfer check AND the read-side tail memset become no-ops for overlaid reads.  That
is by design.  The caller's memset stays load-bearing for the no-overlay fast path (which
still returns a raw fread count) and for CUE, so it must NOT be deleted -- and saying so is
what stops a later round 'simplifying' it away.

FILED, NOT FIXED (riders on B, explicitly not competitors to it):
  * propagate a loss-vs-conventional-gap distinction so SCSI guests get a real error.  Two
    traps for whoever takes it: #416's hardcoded sense is ILLEGAL REQUEST / LBA OUT OF
    RANGE, and a medium loss needs MEDIUM ERROR / UNRECOVERED READ ERROR -- reusing #416's
    code would ship a wrong record IN SENSE DATA; and wdc discards the result anyway.
  * the INCOMPLETE READ fatal() names disk id and offset but NOT THE LAYER, so a routine
    base-EOF gap read and an actionable overlay truncation print identically.  The overlay
    arm should name the overlay file, with the house per-instance latch and `(once)`.
  * the open-time companion (per-bit: highest set bitmap bit vs data-file length) --
    endorsed, and it cannot replace B because truncation can postdate open.

The length row alone passed two clause-(d) mutants that keep the 32768 guard and null its

EMPTY) and `Md_wrongoff` (refill from `data_in[j]` -- every chunk returns chunk 0, silent data
corruption).  Two corruption oracles added; both now die.

**The arm row already carried a corruption oracle and this one did not.**  The sibling-parity
check exists for exactly that asymmetry and would have found it before the table ran.  Closed
under L1 (pre-ship construction); the same finding on shipped material is an L2 floor breach.

*** STILL OWES A RUNG-3/4 WITNESS.  Not discharged by this round. ***

*** FIXED AND COVERED 2026-08-27, third reproduction attempt. ***

```
  BEFORE  FAIL re-arm: >32768 remaining is not zeroed   atapi_len = 0, want 32768
  AFTER   ok   re-arm: >32768 remaining is not zeroed   32768
          ok   re-arm: the branch was actually taken    1
```
**The value moved from the defect's own 0 to the correct 32768**, and the counting oracle proves the branch was taken rather than the call merely surviving.

**THE FIX:** clamp to 32768 instead of assigning 0, and REFILL the next chunk from `data_in[atapi_received ...]`. Safe because at the re-arm `atapi_len == 0`, so the guest has drained the previous chunk and the ring is empty, and `data_in` is still live.

*** SECOND ATTEMPT, BETTER-INFORMED, STILL NOT ACHIEVED -- but the failure is now LOCALISED, which the first attempt's was not. ***

**Built the device the way DEVINIT does** rather than extending a zeroed struct: `mkdev()` mirrors `DEVINIT(wdc)`'s complete field list -- `addr_mult`, `data_debug`, `io_enabled`, `error`, `inbuf`, `base_drive`. Sized `data_in` to match the `data_in_len` it claims. Confirmed `fake_cpu()` populates `cpu->machine`.

*** THE CRASH IS INSIDE `dev_wdc_access`, NOT IN THE FIXTURE. *** A progress marker prints immediately before the call and nothing after it. **That narrowing is the entire result of this attempt**, and it only became visible after fixing a harness defect -- see below.

**RULED OUT, so the next attempt need not re-test them:** the six DEVINIT fields; the `data_in` buffer being shorter than its declared length; `cpu->machine` being NULL (fake_cpu sets it); and the wd_data read path touching `cpu->machine` at all (it does not).

**WHAT IS LEFT: a debugger.** Every cheap hypothesis is spent, and further guessing is the thing that produced five false reds on the first attempt.

*** A REAL HARNESS DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED ALONG THE WAY, and it is why the crash could be localised at all: `diff_wdc_identify.c` had NO `setvbuf`. *** With stdout block-buffered, a segfault loses every row and the run looks like a build failure -- the carrier documents this exact trap. `diff_diskimage_io.c` sets it and says why. **That fix is KEPT** and is worth more than the row that motivated it: it applies to every future crash in this differential.

**The ring-overrun row is unaffected and remains a genuine reproduction.** Only the re-arm row was removed -- twice now, deliberately, rather than leaving a crashing row that looks like evidence.

*** THE PRE-EDIT RED WAS ATTEMPTED AND NOT ACHIEVED. The row is REMOVED, not left red -- a red-for-the-wrong-reason in the tree looks like evidence and is worse than none. ***

**WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN RETRYING BLIND: every attempt produced a RED, and every one of them was red for the WRONG REASON.** Only rule 4 -- *did it fail for the reason under test?* -- separated five false reproductions from a real one. The tell each time was the VALUE: `atapi_len` kept reading back as the number the fixture had SET, which no code path could produce.

*** THE FIXTURE GAP MAP, in the order the handler hits them -- this is the deliverable: ***
```
  1  d.inbuf              a POINTER, zeroed_alloc()'d in DEVINIT.  NULL -> segfault.
  2  cpu                  the read path derefs cpu->byte_order at once; NULL is not ok.
                          (the differential already has fake_cpu())
  3  d.atapi_cmd_in_progress   guards the ENTIRE consume/re-arm block
  4  d.addr_mult          the handler's FIRST line is relative_addr /= addr_mult
  5  d.io_enabled         the SECOND line is `if (!io_enabled) goto ret;` -- this was the
                          one actually blocking, and it returns BEFORE the switch
  6  ...and then it segfaults deeper in, still unmapped
```

> **A zeroed `struct wdc_data` is NOT a usable device.** Unlike `struct wdc_data`'s ring functions -- which take only the struct and work zeroed, which is why the OVERRUN row was easy -- the ACCESS HANDLER needs a configured device. **The two defects in this round are not equally reachable offline, and that asymmetry was not visible until it was tried.**

**WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD DO INSTEAD:** stop extending a zeroed struct field by field and **build the device the way DEVINIT does**, then drive it. `dev_wdc.c`'s DEVINIT is the authority on what a usable `wdc_data` contains; the five gaps above are simply the fields it sets that a memset does not.

*The ring-overrun row is unaffected and remains a genuine reproduction: `first pop = 11`, the predicted `513 % 251`. Only the re-arm row was removed.*

*** FILED 2026-08-27 by adjudication, split from [[wdcringambig]] BEFORE that row closes -- the carrier's rule that a queue id covering two defects buries one when the other closes. Both are closed by ONE diff; they are two ROWS, not two rounds. ***

**THE DEFECT.** `dev_wdc.c:758-759`, in the DATAIN re-arm:
```c
  if (d->atapi_len > 32768)
          d->atapi_len = 0;
```
The INITIAL arm clamps to 32768 in the identical condition. So when the remainder exceeds 32768 the re-arm reports **zero bytes remaining while `atapi_received < data_in_len`** -- the byte count goes to 0, and **no path ever completes the command.**

*** THIS IS LIVE TODAY, not a consequence of any fix. Every transfer above ~64 KB already stalls, and the (64K, 256.5K] band never overruns the ring at all -- it is broken purely by this. *** That fact demolished the scope argument the parent row was holding on.

**IT IS A DEFECT, NOT A DELIBERATE GIVE-UP, and the evidence is historical:** the zeroing is **upstream-inherited verbatim** -- the pristine 2021 copy carries it identically -- and `#341` rewrote the ENCLOSING countdown (`-= len` to `-= consumed`) while neither touching nor assessing it. No fork record defends it. The read-time clamps are **dead code** under both write-side caps: the signature of an unfinished chunking implementation.

**And even read as a give-up it is the wrong one by the fork's own standing class:** reporting 0 remaining while data remains is exactly `#341`'s *the count reported has to be the count that happened* -- the truthfulness family with `#283` (ASC) and `#338` (mb89352).

*One caveat on that classing: the file comment placing this family here describes `#341`'s countdown sibling. **The zeroing itself is uncommented** -- so the family membership is an argument, not a citation.*
  OWNER DECIDED 2026-09-13.  *** FOUR MORE UNREAD ANSWERS READ 2026-09-18 (panel_20260827_050852).  THIS ONE IS A RATIFICATION, AND THAT IS RECORDED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN LEFT BLANK -- the gate's own rule: if a seat truly had nothing new to say, record THAT, because a blank cell and a seat failure must not look alike. ***  agy: VERDICT GO, 'all premises, calculations, diff hunks and test oracles are verified against the repository'.  glm, minimax and deepseek concur.  NO live defect found, and none of the four raised a floor or coverage breach.  *** THE ONE SUBSTANTIVE CONVERGENCE, reached INDEPENDENTLY by agy and deepseek, and it is a warrant the round should keep: THE TWO DEFECTS WERE NOT SEPARABLE AND SHIPPING THEM TOGETHER WAS MANDATORY. ***  Bounding the initial push WITHOUT the re-arm refill would have made every transfer in (32768, 65536] worse than pre-fix: the initial push queues only 32768, the guest drains it, atapi_len goes 0, the re-arm then sets atapi_len = remaining while THE RING IS EMPTY -- so the guest is told bytes remain and none do.  That band WORKED pre-fix by accident (the whole transfer was pushed on the initial arm), so a half-fix would have INJECTED corruption into a working band.  glm's one nit, a RECORDS point: the commit message states the re-arm fix is for the >32768 remaining case and separately that bounding is for the >262656 wrap, which reads as two independent fixes when the coupling is tighter than that.  Commit messages are immutable history, so this is noted rather than edited.  ALL FOUR independently confirmed the round's SCOPE BLOCK is honest: a rung-1 direct-call harness is a DETECTOR and never a witness; only the FIRST re-arm is pinned; wdc_addtoinbuf() remains unbounded (filed); and *** wdcrearmzero STILL OWES A RUNG-3/4 WITNESS *** -- which is the one actionable item this panel leaves, and it is why the row is HELD rather than closed.  *** PROGRESS: 15 of 23 READ.  EIGHT REMAIN (panel_20260827_134019 x5 -> wdcaltctrlbit [closed]; panel_20260907_221353 x3 -> lcashiftub [closed/low]). ***

*** A SEAT SAYS THE LADDER GAP MAY BE NARROWER THAN THIS ROW ASSUMES. 2026-08-27. ***

Reviewing `wdcoddstep`, the Fable seat noted that a **rung-3 cold-debugger probe looks
BUILDABLE** for that defect -- real guest stores of 0xA0 plus a CDB, then real 4-byte
data-port loads through decode, on an in-tree wdc machine.  If so, that defect need not
shelter under this row at all.

**Which sharpens the owner question rather than answering it:** is the gap a genuine
ladder hole, or a habit of reaching for the offline differential because it is one second
instead of one boot?  *Three rounds shipped rung-1; nobody asked whether a rung-3 witness
was AVAILABLE for any of them.*  Worth one attempt before proposing a new term.

*** A POLICY GAP THAT THREE ROUNDS HAVE NOW HIT INDEPENDENTLY.  Filed 2026-08-27. ***

`b115` (#472), `wdcringambig`/`wdcrearmzero` (#473) and `fbclearread` (#474) all shipped a
REAL FIX whose only evidence is a rung-1 offline differential plus a measured kill table.  The
witness ladder classes a rung-1 direct-call harness as a DETECTOR and never as a reproduction,
so none of the five witness terms fits:

* `boot:` / `probe:` / `construction:` -- false, and `probe:` is actively dangerous because
  `check_witness.py`'s SHAPE regex would score it rung-3.  Its own header calls naming an
  #include/direct-call harness there "the laundering this field exists to make visible".
* `harness:` -- admitted ONLY when the round's SUBJECT is the test apparatus.  None of the
  three qualifies; all three fix emulator code.
* `none` -- defined by `state_semantics` as DOCUMENTED-ONLY, so on a round that shipped a fix
  it asserts that no code changed.  **A wrong record, not a conservative one.**

So every such round parks at `held` carrying a prose note, and the note is doing the work a
schema value should do.  That is survivable once; at three it is a pattern, and a fourth will
copy whichever note it happens to find.

**THE QUESTION FOR THE OWNER:** does a fix shipped on rung-1 evidence alone need an explicit
OWNER EXEMPTION per round, or should the ladder gain a term for it?  A candidate term is
`detector:<path>` -- honest about what exists, structurally distinct from `probe:`, and it
would let `check_witness.py` tell "fixed with a detector" from "documented only", which it
cannot do today.

**NOT proposing the term unilaterally.**  Adding a ladder rung changes what every future round
may claim, and the ladder's existing terms were adjudicated rather than invented.  Work
continues meanwhile: the three rows are `held` with honest notes, which is correct under the
current schema and costs nothing to revisit.

*** FABLE ADJUDICATION 2026-08-27: OPTION A, ONE ROUND -- and it found a FIFTH option,
refuted my framing of Q3, and named the escape that would sweep my planned detector. ***

**THE REAL WARRANT FOR A, replacing the underflow argument that died:** `atapi_received` has
TWO LIVE MID-TRANSFER CONSUMERS -- the re-arm length and the refill's source offset
`data_in[atapi_received + j]`.  A guest makes `atapi_len` odd mid-chunk with a single 1-byte
read, then overshoots with a 4-byte read while `received < data_in_len` is STILL TRUE.
Under B/C the re-arm then resumes at a skewed offset, **permanently skipping up to 3 real
transfer bytes that the guest was served as ring-empty 0xff**, while the counters claim full
delivery.  *That is `#283`'s exact defect shape re-created.*

**A FIFTH OPTION EXISTS -- E: count SUCCESSFUL POPS**, transplanting `#338`'s
`transfer_bufpos` idiom (`dev_mb89352.c:260-266`, verified).  Rejected on three read
grounds: on a polluted ring it advances a TRANSFER-indexed counter on FOREIGN bytes,
corrupting the same two consumers that make B wrong; on a clean ring it is byte-identical to
A; and it is not one line, because `wdc_get_inbuf`'s failure signal is IN-BAND
(`(uint64_t)-1`, indistinguishable from data after masking).

*** AND THE DECISIVE FIND: OPTION A IS THE TREE'S OWN IDIOM, NOT AN INVENTION. ***
VERIFIED by opening the file -- `dev_asc.c:610-614` is `#283`'s clamp half:

```c
    if (d->xferp->data_out_offset + len2 > d->xferp->data_out_len) {
            len2 = d->xferp->data_out_len - d->xferp->data_out_offset;
    }
```

That is 'clamp the step to what remains, before the move' -- option A in different variable
names.  A TRANSFERRED WARRANT, and the addition-licence rule is satisfied by it.

**Q3 REFUSED AS FRAMED, correctly.**  `atapi_received` is not 'bytes the guest received' --
its three consumers all use it as *how far the walk of `data_in[]` has got*.  The refill
pushes exactly `atapi_len` bytes of `data_in`; every other byte in the ring during DATAIN is
foreign by construction.  **So A is correct under BOTH ring states, and never needed the
ring-empty premise I built the question around.**

*** THE ESCAPE THAT WOULD SWEEP MY PLANNED DETECTOR: `consumed = d->atapi_len;` *** -- the
min degraded to a plain assignment, a plausible future 'simplification'.  Both my end-state
rows pass (0 and 37) while the FIRST 4-byte read consumes the whole transfer and completes
after 4 bytes delivered.  **The detector owes an INTERMEDIATE-STATE row** -- after nine
4-byte reads: not completed, byte-count registers read 1.  Second escape: `consumed >
atapi_len + 1`, killed by a 2-byte read of a 1-byte remainder.  `>` -> `>=` is an
EQUIVALENCE (self-clamp is identity) and is recorded as one per the non-dying-mutant rule.

*** THE PANEL REPLACED MY DEAD ARGUMENT WITH A BETTER ONE. Cloud seats complete
2026-08-27, 4 of 4 answered -- the kimi substitute came back after two 503s. ***

**Tally on my wrong premise ('B/C open the underflow'): glm and kimi REFUTED it, deepseek
and minimax RATIFIED it. 2-2, and the code sides with the refuters** -- the subtraction is
inside `received < data_in_len`, which an over-count makes false. Settled by reading, which
is the standing rule, not by the tally.

**THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT SURVIVES, from kimi: the MID-CHUNK overshoot.**  On a non-final
chunk `atapi_len` is 32768, so uniform-width reads never overshoot -- but WIDTH-MIXING
does: consume 32767 in byte reads, then issue a 4-byte read.  Under B/C the counters
overshoot and the re-arm STILL FIRES, because mid-transfer `received < data_in_len` is
true.  The refill then indexes `data_in[received + j]` with a skewed `received` -- **a
guest-visible hole in the delivered stream, one per overshoot point.**  Option A cannot
produce it because the counters never leave the transfer.

*Note what makes this reachable: `#473`'s multi-chunk road.  Before that round no transfer
walked past the first re-arm, so a mid-chunk overshoot had nowhere to go.*

**OPTION D IS REJECTED, and on a point neither I nor glm raised.**  A 4-byte port read must
return four bytes, so D either SYNTHESISES padding -- byte-identical to the empty ring's
0xff, but it **suppresses the latched over-read warning, which is the only witness-signal
that a guest did this** -- or it 'refuses', which the architecture cannot express on a port
read.  *D-done-right converges to A-minus-the-warning, with a second site touched.*

**AN ASSUMPTION TO PIN BEFORE COMMITTING, also from kimi:** option A is sound only while
`consumed` equals the ACTUAL pops.  Today `len == 3` gives `consumed == 2`.  If the memory
subsystem ever delivers a genuine 3-byte read that pops three, the same class reopens in
the OTHER direction as an UNDER-count.  Either pin that in-tree or confirm `len == 3` never
reaches this handler.

unreachable. minimax's own table calls it *'REASONED - verified by sign-and-width walk'* --
a true statement about the expression, offered as a verification of the claim.

*The carrier already records that a brief that presents a DERIVATION directs seats to check

*** TWO SEATS DISAGREED ON THE SAME QUESTION AND IT WAS SETTLED BY READING, NOT BY VOTE.
2026-08-27. ***

| seat | claim |
|---|---|
| glm | B/C **bypass** the underflow -- the guard fails, so the re-arm is skipped |
| deepseek | B/C **open** it -- 'the gate fires while the overcount remains' |

**glm is right.** The nesting settles it:

```c
    if (d->atapi_len == 0) {                        /*  B/C make THIS fire  */
            if (d->atapi_received < data_in_len) {  /*  ...but THIS still guards  */
                    atapi_len = data_in_len - atapi_received;   /* the subtraction */
```

The unsigned subtraction is INSIDE `received < data_in_len`, and an over-count is exactly
the condition that makes that test FALSE. So the branch is skipped and the underflow never
executes. deepseek is right that B/C make the OUTER gate fire and wrong that this reaches
the subtraction.

**AND MY OWN BRIEF WAS WRONG IN EXACTLY DEEPSEEK'S WAY.** I derived the underflow from the
types (`int` = `size_t` - `size_t`) and presented it as the strongest argument for option
A. It is not an argument for anything: **the underflow is unreachable under every option**,
so it is not a discriminator and must not be used as one.

*A hazard found by reading TYPES is a hypothesis about control flow, and the control flow
has to be checked separately. The guard that makes it unreachable is the line immediately
above it, and I had read that line -- in a different context, for a different question.*

**WHAT SURVIVES AS A REAL DISCRIMINATOR** is glm's tail/counter argument: on a dirty ring a
four-byte read pops FOUR real bytes and advances `inbuf_tail` by four, while option A
credits three -- desynchronising the ring from the bookkeeping. Option D (clamp the read
LENGTH before the pop) is the only option that keeps them in lockstep.

*** A CLAIM I PUT IN THE PASS-1 BRIEF IS REFUTED, BY THE glm SEAT, AND I RE-DERIVED THE
REFUTATION BEFORE ACCEPTING IT. Corrected 2026-08-27. ***

I wrote that options B and C -- which let the command complete while leaving
`atapi_received` over-counted -- would OPEN the re-arm's unsigned-underflow path
(`atapi_len = data_in_len - atapi_received` assigned to an int). **That is false.**

On the LAST chunk the arm sets `atapi_len = data_in_len - atapi_received`, so
`atapi_len + atapi_received == data_in_len` and the two move in lockstep thereafter
(`-= consumed` / `+= consumed`). Therefore **`atapi_len < 0` if and only if
`atapi_received > data_in_len`** -- and in exactly that case the re-arm's own guard
`if (atapi_received < data_in_len)` is FALSE, so the block is skipped and the underflow
subtraction never executes. On a NON-last chunk `atapi_len` is clamped to 32768 and cannot
reach zero from below at all.

**B and C BYPASS the hazard rather than open it.** The underflow remains unreachable under
every option, so it is not a discriminator between them and must not be used as one.

*** AND THE SEAT SUPPLIED A BETTER ARGUMENT THAN THE ONE IT REMOVED, which is the part
worth keeping. ***  Against option A (clamp `consumed` to the remainder) it observes: if
the ring is DIRTY -- and this week proved it can be, via the unguarded data-port write arm
-- then a four-byte read of a three-byte remainder pops FOUR REAL bytes and `inbuf_tail`
advances by four, while option A credits only three. **That desynchronises the ring from
the bookkeeping**, losing a byte the guest actually received. Option D (clamp the read
LENGTH before the pop) keeps tail and counters in lockstep and is the only option that
does, if the dirty-ring premise holds.

*My brief asked whether a dirty ring breaks option A. It does, but not by the mechanism I
proposed -- not an under-count of undelivered bytes, but a tail/counter divergence.*

*** SEVERITY RAISED 2026-08-27 BY READING THE SCSI LAYER: THE ODD LENGTH IS GUEST-CHOSEN,
NOT AN EDGE CASE. ***

`diskimage_scsicmd.c` sets the transfer length from a SINGLE GUEST BYTE:

```
  :370   INQUIRY        retlen = xferp->cmd[4];        <- allocation length, 0..255
  :371   ...clamped to a MINIMUM of 36, never to an even value
  :572   MODE SENSE     retlen = cmd[4], or cmd[7]*256 + cmd[8]
  :589                  retlen += 100;                 <- still freely odd
  :746   REQUEST SENSE  retlen = cmd[4];
```

and `scsi_transfer_allocbuf(&xferp->data_in_len, &xferp->data_in, retlen, 1)` makes that
value `data_in_len` directly.

**WORKED PATH, no re-arm and no oversized transfer involved:** a guest issues INQUIRY with
allocation length **37**.  `atapi_len` starts at 37; nine four-byte reads consume 36 and
leave 1; the tenth four-byte read makes `consumed` 4 and drives `atapi_len` to **-3**.
`== 0` never fires again, the command never completes, and `atapi_received` reaches 40
against a `data_in_len` of 37.

*This was filed as a residual of `#473` and is considerably more than that.  `#473` added a
second road via an odd FINAL chunk; the FIRST road is a one-byte field in one of the most
ordinary SCSI commands there is.*

*** MEASURED 2026-08-27, on the committed tree, in a scratch fixture. ***

```
  atapi_len = 3 (ODD), guest does a FOUR-byte read of wd_data
  -> atapi_len      = -1        (wanted 0)
  -> atapi_received =  4        (data_in_len is 3)
```

**TWO defects in one subtraction.**  The counter steps PAST zero, so `if (atapi_len == 0)`
never fires again and the command never completes -- and `atapi_received` ends up LARGER
than `data_in_len`, so the device claims it delivered more bytes than the transfer holds.

**THIS IS THE `#341` CLASS SURVIVING AT THE SAME SITE.**  `#341` fixed `consumed` so it
counts what the reads actually POP (`len == 4 ? 4 : (len >= 2 ? 2 : 1)`) rather than what
the guest asked for.  It did NOT make the subtraction saturate, and its own comment
describes exactly this symptom -- *"let atapi_len step PAST zero, which its `== 0` test
then never catches"* -- as the thing being fixed.  The mismatch it removed was
len-vs-consumed; the mismatch that remains is consumed-vs-REMAINING.

**PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED BY `#473`.**  A small odd transfer (MODE SENSE, REQUEST
SENSE) reaches it with no re-arm at all.  But `#473` gives it a SECOND road: before that
round every transfer over 32768 bytes died at the first re-arm, so a multi-chunk transfer
with an ODD FINAL CHUNK could never be walked to its end.  Now it can.  *Strictly fewer
transfers break than before -- this is a residual of a real improvement, not a regression,
and it is filed rather than reverted.*

**FOUND BY ATTACKING A PREMISE, WHICH IS WHY THE BRIEF ASKED FOR IT.**  `#473`'s pass-2
brief named the refill's "the ring is empty at the re-arm" claim as its load-bearing
premise and asked seats to break it.  A grok working note -- *"the re-arm's emptiness claim
is only a drain-path invariant"* -- prompted the trace.  **The emptiness claim itself HELD**:
`head`/`tail` are never reset anywhere, but the packet path requires `inbuf_len == 12`
EXACTLY, so a dirty ring can never issue a packet command and the arm is only reachable
from an empty ring.  The counter defect was found on the way past.

**THE FIX IS ONE LINE AND IS NOT YET MADE:** saturate the subtraction, or test `<= 0`.
Which one is a real question -- saturating hides the over-count in `atapi_received`, while
`<= 0` completes the command but still reports having delivered 4 of 3 bytes.  **The
truthfulness half needs its own answer**, and this fork's own precedents (`#283` ASC,
`#338` mb89352, `#341` here) all say the count reported has to be the count that happened.

Found by the codex seat, adopted by the Fable adjudication 2026-09-17. ***  The title says the length *"is a GUEST-CHOSEN allocation byte, so a plain INQUIRY reaches it"*.  **The INQUIRY producer raises allocation lengths below 36 to 36** (`diskimage_scsicmd.c`), so an allocation byte of 3 does NOT produce the 3-byte fixture the row's measurement used. **THE DEFECT AND THE CLOSURE BOTH STAND; ONLY THE REACHABILITY STORY NARROWS.**  Odd lengths remain reachable by another route (codex: 110 of 256), and the arithmetic class is **any nonzero residue mod 4** (glm and kimi-sub, independently) -- which the shipped clamp covers and which the two odd-only rows do NOT pin.  *So the coverage is narrower than the class, which is coverage debt on a closed row rather than a live defect.*

entries.note: *** #484's COMMIT MESSAGE AND ROUND BLOCK BOTH CLAIM THIS ROW CLOSED.  THE DETECTOR #484 SHIPPED SAYS THE OPPOSITE, IN ITS OWN CONTRACT SECTION. ***  Verbatim from `regress/diff_wdc_identify.c`: *`wdc_addtoinbuf()` itself is still UNBOUNDED.  The fix bounds its CALLER, and no row here constrains the primitive.  A future caller that pushes without a clamp reproduces the same overrun and these rows will not see it.*  Two bullets down the same block names this row as tracked open work -- **in the very commit whose message reports it closed.**  A third comment gives the structural reason: *a detector aimed at a primitive cannot verify a fix made in its caller: right defect, wrong instrument.*  *** THE HARM IS THE QUEUE-ID-COVERING-TWO-DEFECTS SHAPE REACHED THROUGH PROSE RATHER THAN THROUGH THE ROW. ***  The ids were never merged -- two correct rows existed.  One sentence in a commit message merged them, and prose is what a reader trusts when deciding whether to re-open something.  **The ledger was RIGHT and the prose was WRONG, which is why this survived: every check that compares the two reads the LEDGER as the thing needing correction.**  Found only because closing the sibling row required reading the detector instead of trusting the commit message that named it.  L4 correction inserted in the #484 round block, quoting the false sentence and leaving it standing.  **The quotation is DEFANGED** -- the id is spelled out away from the verb -- because the deriver that found this greps for exactly that adjacency and would otherwise re-match its own quotation, which is the quoted-marker-re-arms-the-tool class this project has already paid for once.

entries.note: *** THE REOPENING WAS RIGHT AND ITS WARRANT WAS ALREADY OBSOLETE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN.  This entry corrects a claim I made yesterday and repeated four times in one day. ***  The sentence quoted as proof -- *wdc_addtoinbuf() itself is still UNBOUNDED ... no row here constrains the primitive* -- is **`#473`'s**, written at 04:59:34 and scoped in its own heading to *the six #473 rows*.  **`#484` bounded the primitive at 17:59:02 the same day** (`git log -L` on those lines returns exactly two commits: the upstream import and `cf300c0`), adding a refuse-before-the-store guard with a sacrificed slot and a latched diagnostic, plus four detector rows that call the primitive DIRECTLY and assert the refusal.  So at HEAD: the primitive is BOUNDED, rows DO constrain it, and a future caller that over-pushes gets a silent byte-drop plus one latched `fatal()` rather than a silent overwrite of unread data.  **All three clauses of the quoted warrant are false.**  The `#473` contract block was simply never revisited when `#484` landed -- a frozen record inside the artifact that exists to prevent frozen records.  *** WHAT SURVIVES IS ENOUGH, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT. ***  The contract's SECOND bullet is intact and is the one that names this row: the data-port write arm pushes with **no phase guard**, confirmed by reading the path -- between handler entry and the `wdc_addtoinbuf()` calls there is a debug print, a latch and a width switch, and `d->atapi_phase` is read nowhere.  **And the one diagnostic that could announce a stray write is suppressed precisely in the dangerous state**: its condition requires `!d->atapi_cmd_in_progress`, which is 1 for the whole of DATAIN.  So a guest writing mid-transfer pushes bytes SILENTLY, they sit ahead of the next chunk without touching `atapi_len`, and the re-arm refills on top of them.  **THE ROW IS THEREFORE A DESYNCHRONISATION DEFECT, NOT A CAPACITY ONE**, and the two want different fixes, different oracles and different severity language.  The title has been corrected accordingly; it previously read *"wdcaddtoinbufbound  wdc_addtoinbuf() is still UNBOUNDED, and the live route is the data-port WRITE arm, not the DATAIN arms #473 fixed"*.  *** SEVERITY IS ALSO OVERTAKEN, DOWNWARD. ***  The rider that raised this above *the guest corrupts its own transfer* -- a spurious CDB dispatch freeing `atapi_st`, a LIFETIME hazard -- is **no longer reachable**: `#477` added a `PHASE_CMDOUT` conjunct to that dispatch, so it cannot fire during DATAIN.  *** AND A RUNG-3 WITNESS IS AVAILABLE, WITH A THIRD WORKED EXAMPLE ON THIS VERY DEVICE. ***  `regress/artifacts/wdcringambig/rung3_20260827/` already drives 262654 pushes through the data-port WRITE arm on unmodified `evbmips -e malta` and reads back through the same port, 20/20, in 1.53 s.  The sketch: arm READ(10) for 32 blocks on a `ciR:` CD-ROM, drain all but one byte of chunk 1, issue ONE 2-byte store, drain the last byte to fire the re-arm, then read.  **The committed build hands the guest its own injected byte back as disk data; a fix returns the first byte of chunk 2** -- an ABSOLUTE oracle tied to disk content through a channel outside the ring, so it satisfies the anchor rule.  Risks named honestly: the 2-byte store width is unproven at rung 3 (fallback: two byte stores), and the CD image must satisfy `res == 1` with `data_in != NULL`.  **ROUND-DESIGN CONSTRAINT, and it is the one most likely to be missed:** any fix that keeps foreign bytes out of the DATA-IN stream turns the SHIPPED row `re-arm: refills a NON-EMPTY ring too` RED.  That puts this round under the ORACLE-CORRECTION rule -- re-pin the oracle first, measure the committed build red under the new expectation, THEN change the code, with verbatim provenance and the old pin corrected in place.  **The measured symptom has NO re-runnable artifact.**  The 32768-byte figure appears in three prose sites and every panel occurrence is a seat quoting the source comment back; no `artifacts/wdcaddtoinbufbound/` exists.  The MECHANISM has a shipped rung-1 row; the guest-visible SYMPTOM has prose only.  So the round starts owing a witness rather than inheriting one.  IN-TREE CENSUS of ring producers, five files: `dev_pckbc.c` and `dev_asc.c` refuse BEFORE the store (pckbc additionally exposes a `room_left()` helper so callers can ask first -- a fourth option nobody had named), `dev_wdc.c` now matches pckbc, and **`dev_luna88k.c` and `dev_dreamcast_maple.c` still check AFTER the store with UNLATCHED `fatal()`s** -- the same shape `#288` and `#484` fixed, and flood candidates besides.  Filed as a separate observation, not this round.  TWO RECORDS DEFECTS FOUND IN PASSING: this row's `hold_question` was BYTE-IDENTICAL to `wdcringambig`'s and asked about that row's bulk-arm mutants -- a seat fired against it would have answered the wrong row's question, which is the id-merge this correction is unpicking, one level up.  Corrected.  And `tools/pipeline/fable_queue.md` says *119-row detector* where the CHANGELOG says 127.

*** REFUTED THE BRIEF'S LOAD-BEARING PREMISE BY OPENING THE FIXTURE, AND THE REFUTATION CHANGES WHAT THE ROUND OWES. ***  The brief said any fix keeping foreign bytes out of the DATA-IN stream turns the shipped `re-arm: refills a NON-EMPTY ring too` row RED, so the oracle-correction rule applies unconditionally.  **It does not.**  That row plants its foreign bytes by DIRECT PRIMITIVE CALLS -- five `wdc_addtoinbuf(&e, 0x77)` -- and fires the re-arm with a `MEM_READ`.  **A write-arm fix never touches it.**  Only the re-arm option reds it.  So the protocol is OPTION-CONDITIONAL, and it warned against running it anyway: re-pinning an oracle no code change will redden is expectation churn with no red to show, **which the oracle-correction rule itself calls the laundering signature.**  It then swept every OTHER shipped row for collateral under a write-arm fix and found none: the three `midxfer` rows and both mid-DATAIN write rows assert `stub_frees == 0` with NO occupancy oracle, and their fixtures were already re-pinned so a phase-keying fix does not false-fail.  **A3 confirmed AND UNDERSOLD.**  The severity downgrade is larger than claimed: the source's `shared ring feeds the CDB-dispatch and drain paths` hedge is ALSO dead, because `wdc_new_command_reset()` flushes at the top of every `wdc_command()`.  Blast radius at HEAD is the guest's own current transfer plus self-inflicted DRQ ghosting -- **no host-safety, no cross-command reach** -- which ranks it below every row with a host-safety or flood channel, including the two check-after-the-store siblings the brief keeps out of scope.  It required the downgrade be WRITTEN with its carrying rows named, since the row's `sev` is empty and a reader would otherwise re-derive the old rank from the prose trail.  **A4: ONE STRUCTURALLY DISTINCT OPTION MISSING** -- allowlist-by-DIRECTION (decline unless the device expects host->device bytes) rather than blocklisting DATAIN.  That is what real hardware does, and it covers the idle-state and COMPLETED-phase pushes a DATAIN blocklist leaves alive -- today even the `not expecting any` arm announces and then PUSHES ANYWAY.  It also measured that the re-arm option is **a partial fix by construction**: an injection during the LAST chunk has no following re-arm.  **Q2 CONFIRMED, and pinned by a SHIPPED ROW rather than by argument** (`no-push write does not dispatch`: occupancy 12, push-free write, DATAIN, frees 0) -- which it noted is unlike the transferred warrant that bit this round earlier.  **A5: `wdcrearmwalk` does NOT join** -- it is coverage debt, not a fix site, so *one fix design covers both* fails definitionally.  But it ruled the follow-on precisely: if this round's clause-(d) enumeration forces a multi-re-arm row, that row is THIS round's under L1 and `wdcrearmwalk` then closes as OVERTAKEN under the three conditions, rather than joining.  Named FOUR stale records with their line anchors; three were corrected this session after verifying each against source.

*** FOUR DEFECTS FROM THE PACKET'S OWN INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, AND ONE WOULD HAVE LET A WRONG FIX SHIP. ***  Its Q2 finding is the sharpest in the panel: **the defusal holds IFF the fix keys on `atapi_phase`.**  `#477`'s hazard lives at occupancy-12, which is CMDOUT -- where the `PHASE_CMDOUT` conjunct is SATISFIED and therefore blocks nothing.  A phase-keyed guard never suppresses in CMDOUT, so it is doubly safe.  **But a FLAG-keyed guard -- `atapi_cmd_in_progress && !write_in_progress`, the diagnostic's own predicate -- matches CDB collection too, re-enters that state, and re-arms #477's objection with the conjunct no help at all.**  So the fix must ADD a phase read: the very variable the brief says is read nowhere on that path.  It said plainly the panel must not let an implementer pick the flag-keyed form.  Three witness holes, each with its control: a ONCE-LATCHED decline passes a witness that injects once (inject twice); a decline keyed on ring-occupancy or `atapi_len > 0` passes a witness that only ever injects into a non-empty ring (inject into an empty one); and whichever store WIDTH the run settles on, the other is a hole (cover 2-byte and two 1-byte).  Also: Q1's option set omits accept-and-re-pin, and Q5's join justification is contradicted by the brief's own arithmetic.

Refused ratification on scope rather than on mechanism: the core defect is READ and the option set largely complete, but **Q2's transferred warrant is not settled from the packet** -- converging with glm from a different direction -- Q3's mutant is trivial, and **Q4's weakest control is the unproven 2-byte store width**, which is the same hole glm named third.  Short and correctly scoped; it named what it could not settle instead of guessing.

Verified the chain SSC premises -> SSD mechanism -> SSC2 oracle-correction rule does not contradict itself, then named two gaps the brief itself flags, one option-set refinement, and a Q2 caveat that survives its reading -- the third seat to land on Q2 independently.

Confirmed BOTH halves of the reframing against the tree: the primitive is bounded, and the earlier claim that it was unbounded was retired by `#484`.  That is the correction the brief leads with, checked by a file-reading seat rather than accepted.

Opened by verifying the brief's premises against `dev_wdc.c` and the ledger before answering, and worked the whole write-arm path in the tree.  Its reasoning is visible in the transcript as it happens.

entries.note: *** THE WITNESS IS BUILT AND IT WORKS -- 20 of 20, both legs, every control green -- AND IT REFUTED TWO OF THE BRIEF'S PREMISES, ONE OF WHICH CHANGES THE ROUND'S DISPOSITION. ***  Badge A disclosed unprompted: it was the opus5 seat on `#494`, so its baseline contains its own fix, same device and file.  **(1) THE SKETCH AS BRIEFED COULD NOT HAVE EXHIBITED THE DEFECT AT ALL.**  I wrote *32 blocks on a CD-ROM* assuming 2048-byte blocks.  In this tree CD-ROM `logical_block_size` is **512** -- the 2048 branch is inside `#if 0` -- so 32 blocks is 16384 bytes, under the 32768 chunk clamp: no second chunk, no re-arm, nothing to measure.  **It needs 128 blocks.**  A seat that had merely followed the brief would have produced a clean run and called the defect absent.  **(2) `ANY FIX THAT KEEPS FOREIGN BYTES OUT TURNS THE SHIPPED ROW RED` IS MEASURED FALSE**, independently confirming what the fable5 adjudication derived by reading the fixture: fixA (write-arm guard) leaves the detector at **128 rows, 0 failures**; only fixB (flush at the re-arm) reds it, at 1.  **So the round is NOT under the oracle-correction rule unless it picks the re-arm option**, and the row is a rare DISCRIMINATOR between the two -- the opposite of the carrier's *green under every candidate fix, settles nothing* corollary.  *** (3) THE FLOOR FINDING, AND IT GOVERNS THE ROUND: THE SHIPPED 128-ROW DETECTOR DOES NOT OBSERVE THIS DEFECT AT ALL. ***  `base` scores 0 failures WITH THE DEFECT LIVE, so vacuity-floor clause (a) -- fails on the pre-fix build -- is **not satisfiable from existing rows**.  If the round ships the write-arm guard, **the witness must ship AS the detector or it ships below the floor.**  And two one-expression clause-(d) mutants escape the detector entirely (`!= PHASE_CMDOUT` -> `== PHASE_COMPLETED`; `&& len == 1`), caught only by the witness at 17/20.  **fixA's zero is a MEANINGFUL zero**, and it proved that rather than asserting it: `mutA1` moves 14 rows on the same arm, so the rows ARE sensitive to a guard there.  That is the negative control for *fixA disturbs nothing*.  **THE WITNESS AND THE DETECTOR ARE COMPLEMENTARY AND NEITHER SUBSUMES THE OTHER** -- mutA1 is caught by the detector and by the witness's signature control; mutA2/mutA3 only by the witness.  Ship both.  **Two option members missing, and the first is orthogonal to my whole axis:** (e) DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE -- my (a)-(d) are LOCATIONS, refuse-vs-announce is a DISPOSITION and they compose; the silence is a separate defect from the push, and a guest can inject into a live transfer with nothing anywhere saying so.  (f) COUNT the foreign bytes into `atapi_len` -- **named so nobody takes it**, since it turns guest bytes into transfer data, but an unnamed option is one a later round re-invents.  It also noted (c) SUBSUMES (a) and removes a coupling: **fixA's correctness is not self-contained** -- it is safe only because `#477`'s read-arm phase test stops a stray read moving the phase off CMDOUT mid-CDB.  **A LIVE L4 IN PRODUCT CODE:** `#477`'s objection cites the `default:` len-3/8 arm as its example, and `#479` retired that example with `!badlen_this` **in a comment block fifteen lines below it in the same file**.  The warrant was already dead of a second cause and its text was never updated -- the second time this campaign has been bitten by a warrant a later round retired.  **AND IT CAUGHT A LIVE HAZARD ON THIS MACHINE**: `/tmp/gxsec-build`, the WSL arc tree, held a PRE-`#494` `dev_wdc.c` while `build/`, `build-asan/` and `est/` all carried the fix.  A scratch clone taken from it would have measured `#494`-less code in the file under review and `cmp`-ed clean against its own donor.  Propagated and rebuilt with the two-part clearance run; filed as `novpadfourth`.  It also proved SEC moving under its run was behaviourally null rather than asserting it -- compiled both sources with identical flags and found the objects differ in exactly three `push $<line>` constants, each +9, with `.rodata` identical and a negative control showing the comparison CAN fail.

entries.note: *** FOUND FOUR MORE ESCAPES AND A DEFECT IN THE SCORING ITSELF.  Badge A: it authored the pass-1 mutants AND the witness this round ships, and its headline finding is a defect in ITS OWN M3. ***  **E1 `&& len == 2` -- the MIRROR of its own M3.**  `len == 1` reds 3 rows; `len == 2`, one character away, sweeps clean, because the probe injects with a 2-byte store.  **The round measured the inert member of the family and concluded the family was covered.**  Reproduced independently here at 22/22; repaired by making the second injection a SINGLE byte, which closes the family with one instruction.  **E2 `atapi_cmd_in_progress` -> `atapi_st != NULL` -- and it MEASURED the damage.**  Post-packet push/pop reads `5a,a5` shipped versus `ff,ff` swapped.  `atapi_st` is allocated at first dispatch and never nulled, so after one command the swap refuses every ordinary data-port write for the life of the device. rows.state_note:
*** RIDER FROM THE FABLE SEAT 2026-08-27: THE WRITE-ARM BOUND COVERS MORE THAN DATA
CORRUPTION. ***

The CDB dispatch keys on ring OCCUPANCY `== 12` while the write arm is unguarded during
DATAIN.  So a mid-DATAIN write sequence can drive occupancy to exactly 12 and trigger a
**SPURIOUS COMMAND DISPATCH, which frees and replaces `atapi_st`** -- while a transfer is
live and holding pointers into it.

*That is a lifetime hazard, not a data hazard, and it raises this row above 'the guest
corrupts its own transfer'.  Filed from READING; not measured.*

*** FILED BY `#473`, AND ITS RATIONALE WAS CORRECTED THE SAME DAY BY TWO SEATS. ***

`#473` bounded the two DATAIN arms.  It did NOT bound the primitive: `wdc_addtoinbuf()` has
no capacity check and `head == tail` still means BOTH empty and full.

**THE FILING SAID "correct and complete for every caller in the tree today".  THAT IS
IMPRECISE, and both the Fable and grok seats named the same live counter-example
independently:** the data-port WRITE arm pushes guest bytes with no phase guard and no
capacity check, and its unexpected-write latch is SUPPRESSED precisely because
`atapi_cmd_in_progress` is set.  A guest writing while `write_in_progress == 0 &&
atapi_cmd_in_progress == 1` accumulates unboundedly.  **That is the live unbounded route
and it is independently reachable.**

**AND THE REFILL `#473` ADDED IS ITSELF A CAPACITY-UNAWARE CALLER**, as the codex seat put
it: *"at most 32768 calls is not a capacity bound unless at least 32768 free slots are
established."*  On every in-tree driver the ring is empty there; on an adversarial
interleaved write it is not.

*** PRIORITY ARGUMENT, and it runs the OPPOSITE way to the usual one: `#473` made the
BENIGN route bounded and silent, so the hole now self-announces LESS. ***  Before that
round a legitimate oversized READ(10) would trip the `warned_inbuf_overrun` announce.  The
Fable seat's reading is that this argues for RAISING the item's priority rather than

rows.note: *** AN OPEN ROW THAT CARRIED NO NOTE AT ALL until 2026-08-30.  Filled from the rounds that deferred it, because a row whose whole content is its title cannot be ranked, adjudicated, or refused. ***  THE GAP: `regress/wdc_addtoinbuf_probe.py` walks exactly ONE chunk boundary.  The ATAPI DATA-IN path refills the ring in 32768-byte chunks and re-arms at each boundary; the probe drains chunk 1, injects, crosses ONE re-arm, and reads the first bytes of chunk 2.  **Every row in it lives within that single crossing.**  The probe's own BLIND-TO block names this: *'it walks ONE chunk boundary, not several'*.  WHY IT MATTERS: `#473` measured that the refill loop was unbounded and the clamp sat on the wrong side of it, so a transfer larger than the ring was pushed whole -- WDC_INBUF_SIZE is exactly 513 blocks and block 514 wrapped onto unread data.  That is a MULTI-crossing defect class, and the instrument that would exhibit it walks one crossing.  A state that only goes wrong on the second or third re-arm is invisible here by construction.  *** RULED NOT TO JOIN `#495`, AND THE REASON IS THE ROUND-SCOPE RULE RATHER THAN DIFFICULTY. ***  A second site joins a round only if it is witnessed, in the same device and semantic class, and covered by the SAME detector with no new oracle.  A multi-crossing walk needs new oracles -- per-chunk content expectations across several refills -- so it is a candidate ROUND, not a bigger one.  **THE MACHINERY NOW EXISTS, which is what changed on 2026-08-30.**  `wdcatapistswap` gave the probe a drain loop parameterised by chunk size (DRAIN_CHUNK2), a second injection at a different phase AND width, a 4-byte store emitter (`sw`, which nothing had), and a two-vehicle command arm.  A multi-crossing variant is now mostly a loop around existing pieces rather than new apparatus.  RANKED LOW: no witness exists, the single crossing is the one a real driver takes most often, and `#473`'s clamp is in place and pinned by the offline detector from the other side.  This is COVERAGE DEPTH, not a live defect -- but it is depth along the one axis the shipped instrument holds fixed, which is the class this project keeps finding late.

rows.title: fbclearidempotent  the DC21285 says a timer clear has no effect if the interrupt was already clear, but the write arm reloads a periodic timer unconditionally

entries.note:
THE ROW'S CLAIM IS TRUE, AND THE RESEARCH LOCATES IT TO ONE OF THREE EFFECTS RATHER THAN
TO THE ARM AS A WHOLE.  Brief-ready; no product code touched.

PRIMARY SOURCE, quoted verbatim.  *** CITED BY GREP ANCHOR, NOT BY LINE NUMBER, because
the extracted text is regenerable and a line number in it is a wrong record waiting for
someone to re-run pdftotext. ***  Both anchors below are VERIFIED UNIQUE (grep -cF == 1):

  grep -nF 'effect if the associated interrupt was already clear' _scratchpad/dc21285.txt

    'Any write to the TimerNClear register (any data) clears the associated interrupt.
     THE WRITE HAS NO EFFECT IF THE ASSOCIATED INTERRUPT WAS ALREADY CLEAR.  TimerNClear
     is a write-only register.'

*** THE OFFSETS WERE STRADDLE-CALIBRATED, NOT GUESSED, AND THE TABLE NEEDED IT: TWO
EXTRACTED LINES DISAGREE. ***  Table 7-12 renders with the NAME column shifted two rows
against the ADDRESS column, so a naive read gives `Timer1Clear 324h` while the section
head gives `30Ch`.  Pairing strictly in order down each column yields Timer1Load=300h,
Timer1Value=304h, Timer1Control=308h, Timer1Clear=30Ch, Timer2Load=320h -- and
`dc21285reg.h` pins exactly TIMER_1_LOAD 0x300 / TIMER_1_CONTROL 0x308 / TIMER_1_CLEAR
0x30C / TIMER_2_LOAD 0x320.  Calibration points STRADDLE the value of interest, per the
refined rule, and the UNSTAGGERED PROSE ('Offsets 30Ch, 32Ch, 34Ch, and 36Ch') confirms
independently.  The tree's constants are right; 324h is the artefact.

THE CODE.  The `TIMER_1_CLEAR` arm fires three effects on a write, and only ONE of them
is unfaithful:

  pending_timer_interrupts[n] --     guarded by `> 0`      ALREADY IDEMPOTENT
  INTERRUPT_DEASSERT(...)            unguarded, but a LEVEL HARMLESS
  reload_timer_value(cpu, d, n)      guarded ONLY by TIMER_MODE_PERIODIC -- NOT by
                                     whether anything was pending      *** THE DEFECT ***

So a guest writing TimerNClear with NOTHING PENDING restarts a periodic timer's
countdown, where the datasheet says the write has no effect.  The guest-visible symptom
is a timer that SLIPS: the next tick arrives a full period late, and a guest that clears
more often than the period could starve its own timekeeping indefinitely.

NOT DETECTOR-BACKED, and this is the row's second half confirmed: every #474 row in
`diff_footbridge.c` and `fbpending_drain_probe.py` SETS UP A PENDING INTERRUPT and then
clears it.  **Nothing exercises a clear with nothing pending** -- which is precisely the
state the defect lives in.  The existing rows cannot see it by construction.

*** WHAT THE ROUND MUST NOT ASSUME, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED:
whether reload-at-CLEAR belongs in the model at all. ***  On real hardware a periodic
timer reloads ITSELF at zero and needs no Clear write to do it.  The model's
reload-at-clear may therefore be a modelling shortcut standing in for the automatic
reload, in which case hoisting it under a pending guard is right for a different reason
than the datasheet sentence gives -- and if it is NOT a shortcut, the guard changes when
periodic timers reload.  A panel question, not a reading question.

THE OPTION SET AS I SEE IT, offered for completeness-audit rather than as a decision:
  (1) hoist all three effects under `pending > 0`, the literal datasheet reading;
  (2) hoist ONLY the reload, leaving deassert unconditional (it is idempotent anyway);
  (3) leave the code and correct the record, if reload-at-clear is load-bearing;
  (4) something the fork already does elsewhere for a write-only acknowledge register --
      NOT YET GREPPED FOR, and the option-completeness rule says it should be before any
      round opens.

SIBLING: `fbclearaliases` (the four-address fold 0x30C/0x32C/0x34C/0x36C is READ from the
code and not detector-backed -- every #474 row exercises timer 1).  These two share a
fixture and probably one round, but that is a round-scope judgement the panel should make,
not an assumption: same device and same arm, but different semantic classes.

entries.ev: grep census of INTERRUPT_DEASSERT across src/devices/*.c
entries.note:
THE OPTION-COMPLETENESS GREP IS DONE, AND ITS ANSWER IS A NEGATIVE ONE -- WHICH IS THE
USEFUL KIND, because it stops the round from transferring a warrant that does not reach.

The rule says the fork's own precedents are part of the design space, so I asked: what
does this tree already do with a write-only ACKNOWLEDGE register?  110 INTERRUPT_DEASSERT
sites across src/devices/*.c.  TWO devices carry a real idiom for 'do nothing if the state
did not change', and both are EDGE DETECTION on a saved snapshot:

  dev_dreamcast_asic.c   if (d->asserted_N != old_asserted_N) { assert or deassert }
  dev_sh4.c              if (a && !old_a) ASSERT;  else if (!a && old_a) DEASSERT;

*** SO THE IDIOM EXISTS AND IT DOES NOT COVER THIS ROW. ***  Both guard the INTERRUPT
LINE, and the interrupt line is the one effect in the TIMER_x_CLEAR arm that is already
harmless -- deasserting an already-clear level is a no-op.  Neither guards a SIDE EFFECT
like `reload_timer_value()`, which is the effect that actually violates the datasheet.

  So there is NO fourth option member to be had from the tree, and the round should say
  so rather than leaving the member open as though a grep might still supply one.  The
  choice really is between the three already named.

*A precedent that addresses the harmless two-thirds of an arm is not a precedent for the
harmful third, and the way to find that out is to name which EFFECT each idiom guards
rather than counting devices that 'do the idempotent thing'.  A coarser census -- how many
deasserts look guarded -- returns a number and answers nothing.*

VERDICT: **(1) OPTION C WAS NOT WRONGLY DISMISSED, AND MY QUESTION WAS MIS-POSED.
(2) OPTION F STAYS FILED, with two named promotion triggers.  (3) NO rung-3 ask was
made or recorded -- a one-line records debt.**  Evidence basis: 7 of 9 mandated seats;
opus5 still owed, so this ruling is PROVISIONAL on its face.

*** FOUR ERRORS FOUND IN MY OWN FRAMING, and the third is a live records defect. ***

**(i) THE (1) PREMISE IS FALSE.**  I wrote that #477's read-arm repair 'did a phase-scoped
version of exactly' option C.  It did the OPPOSITE.  C truncates the flag's LIFETIME; the
repair phase-scopes ONE READER and deliberately leaves the stale state in place.  Different
state object (the len/received pair, not the flag), opposite mechanism.  The shipped code's
own comment says so: *"that leaves this window untouched (the flag is legitimately 1 here)"*.
C is orthogonal to the window this row reproduces -- the defect fires MID-DATAIN, before any
completion event, so no clear-at-completion rule can reach it.  C also breaks the ATAPI
handshake at four verified register-read sites.  **The tree converged on the ANTI-C, twice.**

**(ii) 'THREE GUARDS' IS AN UNDERCOUNT -- IT IS FIVE, AND THE TWO I MISSED ARE THE STRONGEST
EVIDENCE FOR MY OWN ARGUMENT.**  Four dispatch conjuncts plus the read-arm scope.  Four of the
five exist to compensate for shared-ring aliasing, and two have measured catastrophic
weakenings (M_phaseonly swept 52 rows and destroyed a sector; M7_ge12 is a heap overflow
invisible to 44 rows).  So the structural argument has measured teeth -- but a GUARD CENSUS IS
NOT A MEASURED DELTA, which is why F is round-eligible and still correctly ranked below live
defects.

**(iii) 'A SEAT MEASURED F's MIGRATION COST' IS AN UNARTIFACTED OVERCLAIM, AND IT WAS
ECHOING.**  No build, no table, no log anywhere.  It was a READ.  Worse, it originated in
OUTSTANDING_BUGS, I inlined it into two briefs, and codex quoted the diff back -- so five
artifacts now carry the word 'measured' and a future grep reads independent confirmation.
**CORRECTED IN PLACE the same hour** (OUTSTANDING_BUGS, the `wdccdbaccum` residual), including
the content: the accept side ports nearly as-is, and the reject rows go TARGET-DEAD owing
case-2 absence records rather than 'stopping working'.  Migration and target-death are
different dispositions.  The real cost is a re-cut plus a full re-table -- a STRONGER argument
for filing than the wrong one was.

**(iv) THIS ROW HAS A SECOND HOLD AND I DID NOT SEE IT.**  Beyond the research stage, a
regress-phase hold carries its own unanswered rule question -- *which panel discharges a row:
its own stage, or the fixing round's?* -- and that was NOT among today's three adjudications.
**Even at 9/9 research this row stays held until that is ruled.**

THE TWO PROMOTION TRIGGERS FOR F, both mechanical so no future round re-argues this:
  * **(a) THE SIXTH-GUARD TRIGGER** -- the first time a MEASURED LIVE defect's fix would add
    another dispatch predicate or another phase-scoped consumer guard, ship F instead.  At that
    point the accumulated deltas ARE the measured warrant.
  * **(b) THE DATAOUT TRIGGER** -- when DATAOUT payload support lands, F ships as its enabling
    structure.  Implementing DATAOUT into the shared ring would create the aliasing a THIRD time.

F's contract, if it ever ships: three classes become unrepresentable -- the `==12` occupancy
collision, the `>= 12` heap overflow, and wdcringnoflush's CDB-drop consequence.  An F round

and tools classify an entry by its NOTE CONTENT.  Once defanged, the note no longer

*** FOUND BY THE codex SEAT ON `#473`'s PASS 2, and confirmed by grepping both files. ***

Section P (`check_bugfile_sync.py`) fails when an OPEN LEDGER ROW has no entry in
`OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md`. **Nothing checks the other direction.**  On 2026-08-27 four rows --
`wdcaddtoinbufbound`, `wdcrearmwalk`, `fbclearidempotent`, `fbclearaliases` -- existed as
prose entries with no ledger row at all.

**Why that direction matters more than it looks.** The ledger is the single source of truth
and `matrix.html` renders it, so a row filed only in prose is **invisible to every tool in
the pipeline**: it gets no seat coverage tracking, no stage panel, no dashboard line, and
section H never asks whether it ran a panel.  *A row that exists only in prose is filed in
the sense that a reader could find it and unfiled in every sense a tool cares about.*

This is the unread-review class one level up: the work is recorded, and the machinery that
exists to act on records cannot see it.

row-id tokens (the backticked ``id`` convention already used), and fail when one names
no ledger row.  **Dated-cutoff and forward-only**, like `check_bugfile_sync.py` itself: a
rule that retro-fails the whole file blocks the next commit on reconstruction nobody
scheduled, and a rule that does that gets switched off.

**NOT BUILT YET, deliberately.**  It is a behaviour change to the script every commit runs,
and it owes two negative controls: prove it reds on a bugfile-only row, and prove it stays
green when the ledger row is added.  The four instances are already fixed by hand.

rows.state_note:
*** DID `#476` CLOSE THE CLASS OR ONE INSTANCE?  ENUMERATED 2026-08-27, and the answer is
THE CLASS -- but the enumeration is the point, not the answer. ***

`#475` taught that repairing a counter can WAKE DEAD CODE, so fixing one dereference proves
nothing about the others.  All nine derefs of `atapi_st` in the file, with their protection:

```
  :812  atapi_received < atapi_st->data_in_len   <- the #476 site, NOW GUARDED
  :877  atapi_len = atapi_st->data_in_len - ..   <- nested inside :812's true arm
  :884  wdc_addtoinbuf(.. atapi_st->data_in[..]) <- same block
  :1033 atapi_st->cmd = scsi_cmd                 <- immediately after the alloc
  :1034 atapi_st->cmd_len = 12                       at :1023
  :1039 atapi_st->cmd_len = 10
  :1072 if (atapi_st->data_in != NULL)
  :1082 atapi_len = atapi_st->data_in_len
  :1087 wdc_addtoinbuf(.. atapi_st->data_in[j])
```

**The first three are the reachable family and all three are inside the arm `#476` guards**
-- `:812` runs only when `atapi_len == 0 && atapi_st != NULL`, and `:877`/`:884` are nested
within its true branch.

**The remaining six sit after `scsi_transfer_alloc()`, WHICH CANNOT RETURN NULL** -- verified
by opening it: on malloc failure it prints and `exit(1)`s.  (That exit is a separate,
pre-existing, OOM-only concern and is not guest-reachable.)

*Worth noting for anyone reasoning about the free: `scsi_transfer_alloc` runs a FREELIST, so
a fresh alloc typically REUSES the just-freed chunk.  That is why a pointer-identity oracle
reads a false negative on a plain build and only separates under a sanitiser's quarantine --
a seat measured exactly that.*

**So no second host kill of this family is in the tree.**  Recorded as an enumeration a
reader can re-derive rather than as an assurance.

*** A REGRESSION I SHIPPED, FOUND BY THE MEASURING SEAT ONE COMMIT LATER, FIXED THE SAME
HOUR.  2026-08-27. ***

```
  d894e35 (before #475)   a DATA read with no transfer survives   exit 0
  d64a1fc (with #475)     a DATA read with no transfer survives   host killed, signal 11
```

**THE MECHANISM IS ENTIRELY #475's.**  Before it, a data-port read with `atapi_len` already
0 drove the counter NEGATIVE, so `if (atapi_len == 0)` never fired again and the
`d->atapi_st->data_in_len` deref on the next line was **dead code**.  The clamp makes
`atapi_len` STAY 0.  The test fires.  `atapi_st` is NULL.

> **A FIX THAT STOPS A COUNTER GOING NEGATIVE CAN MAKE A PREVIOUSLY-UNREACHABLE BRANCH
> REACHABLE.**  The clamp was right; the branch it woke was never NULL-safe.  *Repairing a
> counter can enable code that was only ever protected by the broken value* -- and nothing
> in `#475`'s own kill table could see it, because every mutant there attacked the clamp
> rather than what the clamp let through.

MEASURED `SIGSEGV at address 0x48` = `offsetof(struct scsi_transfer, data_in_len)`.  Two
guest register accesses from a fresh device: write ATAPI_PKT_CMD to COMMAND, then read
DATA.  The seat's control -- the same command with NO data read -- survives on both blobs,
so it is the READ.

**THE BISECT IS UNAMBIGUOUS AND PLEASINGLY SYMMETRIC:** on the same pair of builds, the row
for the defect `#475` FIXED goes one way and the row for the defect it CREATED goes the
other.

**FIXED** by declining with the file's own latch idiom -- a device that cannot service an
access must not take the emulator with it, which is the `#337`/`#184`/`#186`/`#315`/`#316`/
`#326` class this fork has spent many rounds closing and which I had just reopened.

*The row FORKS: the defect is a SIGNAL, and an in-process oracle would take the differential
down with it and report nothing at all.*

rows.title: wdccdbaccum  give the ATAPI CDB its own accumulator, as dev_mb89352.c does, instead of trigger-matching on a SHARED ring occupancy
rows.witness: none -- structural, filed from two seats' reading of the in-tree precedent.
rows.state_note:
Filed by `#477`, which shipped the point-fix (phase-guard the dispatch) rather than this.

**THE ALIASING IS THE ROOT.**  `inbuf_len == 12` is a SHARED-RING trigger: it cannot tell CDB
bytes from DATA-IN payload from disk-write payload.  Every candidate fix considered in that
round -- guard the push, guard the dispatch, clear the flag, guard the free -- is a patch over
that ambiguity.

**THE IN-TREE ANSWER, verified by opening it:** `dev_mb89352.c` switches on `d->phase` to
SELECT A DESTINATION BUFFER (`PH_DATAOUT` -> `data_out`, `PH_CMD` -> `cmd`) with a declining
`default:`, and its dispatch trigger is **`transfer_bufpos >= len`** -- *this phase's own
buffer is full* -- never a shared count.

So: `unsigned char cdb[12]; int cdb_pos;` filled only in `PHASE_CMDOUT`, dispatching on
`cdb_pos == 12`.

**COST, MEASURED BY A SEAT RATHER THAN GUESSED:** with the fix in place it still reds two
existing rows, because they hand-fill the ring with `wdc_addtoinbuf()` to fake a CDB.  **It
relocates where a CDB lives, so every probe that fakes one stops working.**  That is the
migration cost, and it is why the round shipped B.

*One caution against copying `dev_mb89352` wholesale: its `default:` arms set
`cpu->running = 0`.  Transfer the SHAPE, never the halt -- removing exactly that from this
file is what `#337` was for.*

entries.note: CLOSED 2026-08-29 AS A RECORDS ACTION.  **The fix shipped 2026-08-27 and this row never learned.**  `#479` (`2343036`) added `wdc_new_command_reset()`, clearing exactly the three tenants at the top of `wdc_command()` -- the F-narrow variant the 2026-08-27 five-variant matrix recommended.  `#480` is its pass-2 receipt, `#481` extended it to the ALT-CTRL caller, `#482` hardened the rows per tenant.  *** THE GHOST-ROUND MECHANISM, recorded because it cost a whole panel: *** the row carried a full 9/9 RESEARCH stage; the work then shipped under FOUR commit numbers; **zero entries landed back on the row**; the ledger froze at 'in work'; and two days later the main loop -- correctly treating the ledger as the queue -- drafted a fresh PASS-1 brief to do it all again and fired nine seats at it.  **The CHANGELOG knew (its Round 479 block names all three row ids); the ledger did not.**  This is the unread-review class one step worse: an unrecorded ROUND.  The existing gates are structurally blind to it -- section H skips stages that never STARTED, and the implement/review stages never started on these rows.  **DETECTION WOULD HAVE COST TWO COMMANDS**: `git log -- src/devices/dev_wdc.c` and `grep <rowid> CHANGELOG.md`.  Neither was run, because the ledger said 'in work' and was believed.  *** WITNESS TERM CORRECTED, and the old one was LAUNDERING. ***  It read `probe:offline differential, 73 rows` -- but `probe:` on an offline differential is exactly the mis-scoring `check_witness.py`'s own header calls laundering, and the `detector:` term was adopted on 2026-08-27 for precisely this shape.  The count was also stale and is now UNCITED: the string said 73, `TABLE.txt` says 80, and a fresh derivation gives 95 -- three numbers for one quantity, so the artifact PATH is cited instead of any of them, per the names-its-log rule.  BADGE `A`: the recommender (fable5's matrix), the implementer's reviewer and the closer overlap.  Disclosed rather than implied.  FILED, not closed here: `Mq_pktretry` escaped `#480`'s table honestly and is recorded as such.  *** AND ONE ELEMENT OF THE ORIGINAL RECOMMENDATION IS SUPERSEDED, NOT PRESERVED. ***  It said to record the ALT-CTRL gap as a deliberately RED row. `#481` CLOSED the gap instead, which is better, and the adjudicator ruled against its own disposition on the reasoning that a permanently red row is the dual of a check-that-cannot-fail -- **a check that cannot PASS** -- and violates the blanks rule, since a deliberate red and a regression red render identically. entries.note: REGRESS REVIEW of a closure that is RECORDS-ONLY: no code changed here, so what is reviewed is whether the SHIPPED detector still holds at HEAD.  It does, and it was measured today rather than assumed.  **Both kill tables are preserved and were re-verified**: `regress/artifacts/wdccmdreset/killtable_20260827/TABLE.txt` (13 of 13, including `MdEndRing` KILLED 5 red, and `MdNoPhase`/`MdNoWip` as SOLE carriers) and `regress/artifacts/wdcaltctrl/killtable_20260827/TABLE.txt` (10 of 10).  **The detector was RUN at HEAD in a scratch tree: 128 rows, 0 failures, sentinel `WDC_IDENTIFY_PASS`.**  Nine fresh mutants aimed at the partial-reset shape were then built against it: SEVEN KILLED -- including the per-SITE subsets (`MdAltRingOnly`, `MdAltWipOnly`, `MdAltNoRing`) and `MdNoFlag`, which drops a FOURTH tenant neither shipped table enumerates and still dies 6 red -- and TWO ESCAPED and were PROVED EQUIVALENT by a positional differential rather than assumed: the inbuf is a correct circular buffer, so head/tail position is unobservable through occupancy, capacity or readback.  *ATTRIBUTION, because the regress hat is fable-only and the measurement was not fable's:* the chronology reconstruction and both table verifications are fable5's; the 128-row run and the nine-mutant table are the opus5 seat's, run read-only in `/tmp/gxopus_wdc`. rows.title: wdcaltfixture  every alt-ctrl row runs in a state NO REAL DRIVER IS EVER IN, so eleven single-field qualifications escape the whole file
rows.witness: none -- filed from a MEASURED escape set, no fix work done yet.
rows.state_note:
*** FILED BY `#483` FROM ELEVEN MEASURED ESCAPES, AND AS **ONE** ITEM WITH A ONE-ROW
REMEDY -- NOT AS ELEVEN ROWS. ***

`altctl_fresh()` memsets the device struct, so EVERY predicate that is true at zero
escapes every altctl row in `diff_wdc_identify.c`.  `&& !d->lba` is the exemplar the
seats measured; it is NOT the item.  Eleven single-field qualifications were built and
all eleven swept the file clean.

**THE HONEST BOUND, and it is what stops this becoming `#392`:** a guard can be added on
any of ~40 struct fields, so the enumeration is unbounded and chasing members is the
wrong shape.  The principled scope is THE FIELDS A REAL DRIVER SETS IN ORDINARY
OPERATION -- and the finding is that today every altctl row runs in a state no real
driver is ever in, which is a property of the FIXTURE, not of any one guard.

Remedy shape: one row that drives the device through a realistic prologue (a command
issued, LBA/head/sector registers written as a driver writes them) before the control
write, so a qualification on any driver-set field reddens.  Cost is one row and no new
oracle; it needs no `scsi_transfer_alloc()`, which is the boundary that would have made
it expensive.

rows.title: wdcaltwidth  the alt-ctrl register's ACCESS WIDTH is unpinned: every row uses len == 1 while the region is registered TWO bytes wide
rows.witness: none -- filed from a reading of the registration, no measurement yet.
rows.state_note:
*** FILED BY `#483`. ***  `wdc_altstatus` is registered with LENGTH 2 (pristine
upstream), and its handler consults NEITHER `relative_addr` NOR `len`.  Every one of the
103 rows in `diff_wdc_identify.c` calls it with `len == 1` at offset 0.

So two decode questions are unpinned by construction: what a 2-byte store does, and what
a store at `+1` does.  Both are inside the region the model claims.

Sibling of `wdcwidthmatrix`, which records the same gap for the DATA port -- the two

*** THE 'SPEED NOT CORRECTNESS' CLAIM BELOW NEEDS A QUALIFIER AND IS CORRECTED HERE (L4, same day, by the adjudicating seat). ***  It is TRUE for seeing the synchronous assert, and FALSE AT THE MUTANT LEVEL: under stepping `debug()` PRINTS, so a `fatal(` -> `debug(` downgrade at the producer stays INVISIBLE to a stepped row -- the contract's own documented escape, guarded today only by a gate floor on the fatal( count, which a compensating addition elsewhere would net out.  A free-running row at verbose 0 REDS on that downgrade, because debug()'s early-out goes quiet while fatal() does not.  **So free-running buys a per-site DETECTION CAPABILITY, not only wall-clock**, and the choice is not purely economic.  Shipped in 6f39c95 without the qualifier.

THREE OF THE PANEL'S FOUR NOT-SETTLED ITEMS SETTLED BY READING, while the timing seat runs.

P4 -- CAN THE TWO REGEXES BOTH MATCH ONE LINE?  NO.  `P_OVERRUN` matches
`wdc_addtoinbuf(): WARNING! wdc inbuf overrun`; `P_DATA` matches `wdc: write to DATA, but
not`.  Two distinct fatal() calls in the device, two distinct texts, no shared substring
either pattern would match.  The #464 unexpected-write latch cannot pollute the overrun
count.

P5 -- DOES ADDING A runloop VARIANT BREAK ANOTHER ROW?  NO.  `runloop` has EXACTLY ONE call
site in the whole probe, and it is the `overrun x2` row itself.  Converting it in place is
therefore as safe as adding a variant, and cheaper.

*** Q3 -- AND THIS ONE DE-RISKS THE ROUND. ***  The overrun `fatal()` lives INSIDE
`wdc_addtoinbuf`, reached SYNCHRONOUSLY from the data-port write handler inside the guest's
own store instruction.  Nothing this row depends on comes from a host timer.  By the
carrier's own refined rule -- a step-based probe sees an assert that is SYNCHRONOUS, and
misses only what a host-timer callback produces -- A STEPPED PROBE CAN SEE THIS.

  **So free-running is a SPEED choice, not a CORRECTNESS one.**  That matters for the
  disposition: if the timing run says `step 394202` is tolerable, the re-aim needs no
  free-running conversion at all and the round shrinks to a count change plus the header
  correction.  The substitute seat raised exactly this possibility -- 'possibly a full

battery is a standing mis-attribution engine, which is what this round exists to prevent.

TWO MUTATIONS OWED, and the second is the anti-fake control:
  M_relatch  remove the latch guard and flag-set, keep the fatal() and the refusal return.
             Every refused byte then announces -- expect the count >> 1 against want 1, RED.
  M_silent   DELETE the producer's fatal(), keep the guard and the refusal.  The row must
             read 0, RED.  *** THIS IS WHAT PROVES THE COUNTED 1 COMES FROM THE PRODUCER'S
             ANNOUNCE and not from a widened regex: the smallest fake is a one-token widening
             of P_OVERRUN so the datawr line feeds it, and M_silent is the only row-level
             check that catches it -- a polluted row reads 1 and stays green. ***

FOUR FACTS BEYOND THE BRIEF:
  1. P4 is disjoint BY DESIGN, not by luck.  #484's bulk-arm message deliberately names
     wdc__read() instead of the producer, with an in-source comment saying the shared latch

     producer's own announce.  The regex-to-site mapping is pinned in product prose.
  2. *** A len=4 ROUTE HALVES THE COST AND ALREADY EXISTS IN THE ROW SET. ***  The write
     arm's `case 4` pushes four bytes per store, WD_DATA is 4-byte aligned, and `datawr x2`

  3. THE STEPPED FORM IS A LOAD-SENSITIVE ORACLE IN ITS WORST SHAPE.  The announce fires at
     ~99.9% through the run and session() reads for a FIXED spin with no completion
     detection -- so a load-starved spin truncates the transcript BEFORE the announce and the

  4. *** MY OWN FRAMING NEEDS A QUALIFIER -- see the L4 correction on the entry below. ***

    half store   131328 to fill   131368 with margin   ~394106 single-steps

seat quoted 65,700 / 197,102; the small difference is the margin choice, not a disagreement.

the run halves the exposure; it does not remove it.
