rows.state_note:
*** OVERTAKEN BY `#481`, AND THAT DISCHARGES THE PAIRING HAZARD. ***

The row: the ALT-CTRL write arm triggered on `WDCTL_4BIT` (0x08) -- the head-count bit a
driver holds as steady state -- instead of `WDCTL_RST` (0x04), the soft-reset bit.

`#481` changed the predicate to `if (idata & WDCTL_RST)`.  VERIFIED by reading the arm at
HEAD, and the arithmetic settles the consequence: `0x08 & 0x04 == 0`, so a routine
`WDCTL_4BIT` control write no longer latches COMMAND_RESET.

*** WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN CLOSURE: IT WAS A PREREQUISITE FOR `landiskaux`. ***
The queue recorded, correctly at the time, that shipping `landiskaux`'s one-line mapping fix
ALONE would make the ALT-CTRL arm live on landisk WITH ITS PREDICATE STILL WRONG -- six of
the twelve measured Device Control writes are `0x08`, so mapping the register would have
started latching COMMAND_RESET on six routine writes per probe.

That reasoning was sound and its premise is now false.  With `#481` shipped, the six `0x08`
writes are INERT, and `landiskaux` is safe to ship on its own.

*The queue entry says these two 'MUST SHIP TOGETHER'.  They no longer must.  It is the third
stale-severity finding of the day, and the same shape each time: a severity that was an
answer to a question rather than a property of a row, left standing after the question
changed.*  *** L4 -- OVERTAKEN CONDITION (2) IS UNMET IN THE FIELD THE RULE NAMES.  Corrected 2026-09-17, found by the Opus 5 seat. ***  The carrier requires *"THE CARRYING ROWS NAMED by label and probe path, in the witness or closure field."*  This row's witness read only *"#481's rows pin the RST predicate"* -- **no labels** -- where the sibling precedent (`wdcoddstep`) names *"the two `odd chunk:` rows"*.  The labels exist and the seat verified all five in `diff_wdc_identify.c`. **AND CONDITION (1) IS MET MORE STRONGLY THAN THE CLOSURE NOTE CLAIMED**, which is the unusual direction for a records defect: the note said *"verified by reading the arm at HEAD"*, while the preserved evidence is `bin_Md_bitswap.out` (8 rows red) plus `PREFIX_committed_device.out` (the five reproduction rows red on the committed PRE-FIX device).  **The row UNDERSTATED its own evidence.** *** AND THE BRIEF'S ARITHMETIC WAS WRONG AS LITERAL C, WHICH IS WORTH KEEPING: `0x08 & 0x04 == 0` PARSES AS `0x08 & (0x04 == 0)` = `0x08 & 0` = **0**, not 1 -- `==` binds tighter than `&`. ***  Harmless in prose; this project has shipped a wrong constant from a hand-written expression before, and the same text pasted into a probe row is a VACUOUS ROW. **THE SEAT ALSO REFUTED THE BRIEF'S FRAMING OF THE CONSEQUENCE, and its version is better.**  Disjointness (`0x08 & 0x04 == 0`) establishes only that the predicates are INDEPENDENT.  What settles the consequence is DRIVER TRAFFIC: libata holds `4BIT` as steady state and asserts SRST as `ctl|ATA_SRST` -> 0x0c/0x0e, releasing with 0x08/0x0a, so under the old predicate the RELEASE latched a reset; older OpenBSD asserts 0x06 with 4BIT clear, so the old predicate MISSED a real reset.  **On 0x0c/0x0e old and new predicates AGREE -- libata's assert was never the broken half, which is exactly why the wrong bit survived so long.**  A reader taking the brief's framing would believe the two predicates always differ, which is false for the dominant driver's assert. *The detector already covers the both-bits case: `diff_wdc_identify.c` writes `buf[0] = WDCTL_RST | WDCTL_4BIT; /* 0x0c -- assert */`, and its signature row records exercising both 0x06 and 0x0c.  The carried coverage is better than the brief described.*  *** NINE-ROW CLOSURE PANEL, 2026-09-17 -- AND IT CONVERGED ONCE SEAT CLASS WAS RESPECTED, WHICH IS THE DOCTRINE WORKING RATHER THAN A DISAGREEMENT. ***  Seven seats answered; the kimi CLI hit its weekly wall and its `kimi-k3:cloud` substitute COVERED the seat (not lost). **THE SPLIT IS BY SEAT CLASS, NOT BY OPINION.**  The four FILE-READING seats (opus5, grok, agy, codex) each verified against HEAD and the preserved artifacts, and reached **CLOSE on rows 1-8, KEEP-OPEN on row 9**.  The four PACKET-FED seats kept rows open where the packet could not show them a witness -- and glm stated that standard explicitly: *"I CLOSE where the packet is internally coherent and the witness shape matches the recorded defect; I KEEP-OPEN only where the packet"* cannot.  **deepseek kept all nine open "on packet-only review", which is an honest not-checkable and is NOT a vote on repo fact** -- exactly the distinction PIPELINE.md draws. *** ROW 9 IS UNANIMOUS KEEP-OPEN ACROSS EVERY SEAT THAT GAVE A PER-ROW VERDICT, AND THE ROW WAS RE-OPENED. ***  Two file-reading seats reached it by DIFFERENT EVIDENCE: opus5 diffed the working tree against HEAD and found the tightened oracle uncommitted; grok checked the `commits` field and the file's last-commit history.  codex reached it a third way -- *"row 9's 'not applied' and 'unproven' descriptions are stale locally"* -- and characterised the disposition precisely: *"an oracle repair of its own, rather than an OVERTAKEN disposition; its remaining issue is landing the validated work."* *** THE BRIEF'S OWN PREMISE ABOUT ROW 9 WAS FALSE AND TWO SEATS INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED IT SO. ***  It asserted the repair was *"named and deliberately not applied"*; it was applied and is uncommitted.  **Third trial of the premise-audit opener, third catch.** **ROW 5's LABEL DEFECT WAS FOUND BY TWO FILE-READING SEATS INDEPENDENTLY** -- opus5 and codex both report OVERTAKEN condition (2) unmet, codex putting it flatly: *"'#481's rows' is insufficient"*.  Corrected in the witness field. *** AND deepseek's HYPOTHETICAL MUTANT FOR ROW 9 IS WHAT HEAD ACTUALLY CONTAINS. ***  It proposed, as the smallest edit that breaks the fix and still passes: *"edit the oracle back to substring `Transfering`; all 62 rows stay green."*  **That is the committed state.**  A packet-fed seat with no file access described the real defect as a thought experiment -- which is the strongest possible corroboration of the two file-reading seats, precisely because it could not have been copied from the tree. **CODEX ALSO ANSWERED THE OPTION-SET QUESTION WITH FIVE IN-TREE IDIOMS THE BRIEF DID NOT NAME**, including *"combine page base with a masked virtual offset, as the MIPS translator does"* (`memory_mips_v2p.c`) -- the option-set rule working as designed, by grepping the fork rather than reasoning. The labels are now written out. **AND THE DISCRIMINATING PAIR IS NARROWER THAN EITHER MY BRIEF OR MY FIRST CORRECTION SAID** (grok and glm reached it by enumeration, Fable adopted it): the writes that separate the old predicate from the new are **0x06** (old predicate's false NEGATIVE -- a real SRST it missed) and **0x08** (its false POSITIVE -- a routine write it latched as a reset).  *** `0x0c` SETTLES NOTHING EITHER WAY -- under both predicates it is a reset -- and the 0x0c row is GREEN under `Md_bitswap`. ***  So my brief's libata-0x0c framing was not merely incomplete, it named the one case that cannot discriminate. **codex ranked this strongly enough to withhold the closure (KEEP-OPEN 5); the Fable seat ruled ANNOTATE rather than re-open**, on the ground that the rule's trigger for re-opening is *"a candidate that cannot meet (1) or (2)"* -- and this row CAN meet (2), because the labels exist. So nine cells read `### N. <id> (SEV, closed) -- <title>`: the packet, handed back as the seat's verdict. *** IT IS WORSE THAN AN UNREAD REVIEW AND FABLE SAID WHY: "an unread review filed under a RECORDED seat -- section G cannot see it because an entry exists." ***  The blank that would have been caught was filled with something that looks like an answer. **AND MY OWN AUDIT OF IT UNDER-COUNTED 9 AS 6**, because the pattern I checked required a severity token `(LOW|MED|HIGH)` and three headings carry only `(closed)`.  *Sixth correlate-keyed check of this session, committed inside the audit of the fifth.* Codex's real verdict, recorded now: **CLOSE 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8; KEEP-OPEN 3, 5, 9.**  *** L4 -- MY 'SPLIT BY SEAT CLASS' ADJUDICATION IS A WRONG RECORD, AND THE FABLE SEAT SHOWED IT IS FALSE ON THE PACKET'S OWN DATA.  Corrected 2026-09-17. ***  I wrote that the four FILE-READING seats reached CLOSE 1-8 / KEEP-OPEN 9 while the PACKET-FED seats kept rows open. **Codex is file-reading and its verdict line reads `CLOSE 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8.  KEEP-OPEN 3, 5, 9`** -- I tabulated it as CLOSE 1-8.  Meanwhile minimax (packet-fed) CLOSED rows 1 and 5, kimi-sub CLOSED 1/3/4/6/7, glm CLOSED 1/3/4/6/7/8.  **The classes do not sort the verdicts.** *** AND THE RULING WAS CIRCULAR, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. ***  My own brief's S0 told the seats *"an unsettleable row stays open, which is the safe direction"* -- which converts every honest not-checkable into a KEEP-OPEN vote -- and I then read those votes back as evidence that the doctrine was working.  **I instructed the behaviour and then cited it as a finding.** **THE RULING FORM THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN WRITTEN** sorts the packet-fed KEEP-OPENs BY KIND, not by class: (a) NOT-CHECKABLE-FROM-PACKET, *discharged by naming the file* -- row 2's condition (c), row 8's figures, deepseek's rows 1/3/4/6/7 -- where *"the file-reading seats verified it" is the right answer ONLY when the file is named*; and (b) SUBSTANTIVE, adjudicated on merit regardless of class -- row 9 (all four right), row 5's arithmetic, row 5's unnamed labels (raised by kimi-sub and glm, the SAME finding as codex and opus5, so a class split puts those seats on the wrong side of their own finding). *** AND ONE SUBSTANTIVE PACKET-FED CLAIM WAS FALSE AND A CLASS RULING IS EXACTLY HOW IT GOES UNREFUTED: *** glm's *"nothing pins the suppression side, 0x08 must NOT fire"* is answered by the row `a routine 0x08 preserves the command` in `diff_wdc_identify.c`.  **That deserved a refutation by file, and my ruling gave it a category instead.** **THE COST OF THE MIS-STATEMENT:** it hid codex's row-3 dissent (the row now re-opened on a measurement), and it converted a three-seat finding on row 5 into "the file-reading seats said CLOSE".

rows.title: landiskaux  DEVINIT has no MACHINE_LANDISK case, so twelve measured Device Control writes land on unmapped memory -- one line, and now UNBLOCKED

entries.ev: direct reading of DEVINIT(wdc) and machine_landisk.c
entries.note:
A STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION, AND THE PART OF IT I NEARLY OVERCLAIMED.

*** THE ALT-STATUS ADDRESS IS COMPUTED FROM AN UNSCALED BYTE OFFSET, WHILE THE MAIN REGISTER
BLOCK IS SCALED BY addr_mult. ***  All four rules -- the default +0x206, MACPPC's +0x160,
HPCMIPS' hardcode and IQ80321's +0x402 -- consult `devinit->addr` and never
`devinit->addr_mult`, while the main registration uses `DEV_WDC_LENGTH * devinit->addr_mult`.

AND LANDISK IS THE ONLY IN-TREE wdc WITH addr_mult != 1 (it passes addr_mult=2; every other
instantiation omits it and gets 1).  So it is the only machine where the two conventions can
disagree -- which looked like a complete explanation for why it is the only machine whose
device-control writes land nowhere.

*** IT IS NOT THE EXPLANATION, AND I CHECKED BEFORE WRITING IT DOWN AS ONE. ***  Scaling does
not produce the measured address: 0x206 * 2 = 0x40c, and the driver writes +0x2c.  Neither
the raw ISA offset nor any scaling of it predicts 0x2c, so landisk's aux block genuinely
sits somewhere machine-specific.  A `case MACHINE_LANDISK:` is therefore the RIGHT SHAPE,
matching MACPPC and IQ80321 -- not a paper-over of a scaling bug.

WHAT SURVIVES IS A LATENT HAZARD WORTH RECORDING AND NOT FIXING: the offsets are unscaled,
so a FUTURE machine with addr_mult != 1 that falls through to the default rule would get a
wrong alt-status address for exactly the reason landisk does not.  Landisk escapes it only
by getting an explicit case.  Filed as an observation on this row rather than as its own
item, because no such machine exists today and inventing a guard for one would be the
'it cannot hurt' addition this fork refuses.

TWO OF THE PANEL'S OPEN QUESTIONS SETTLED BY READING, while the third is measured.

Q3 -- WHAT DOES A MAPPED WRITE ACTUALLY DO?  The entire write arm, comments stripped, is:

        if (idata & WDCTL_RST) {
                d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET;
                wdc_new_command_reset(d);
        }

Nothing else.  Two effects -- latch the ATAPI signature, and reset the ring/tenant state --
and BOTH are gated on 0x04.  A read returns status_byte() and has no side effect.  So the
'untraced code path' the steelman worries about is four lines long.

P5 -- COLLISION?  NO.  landisk registers exactly one wdc block, 0x14000000-0x1400000f, and
+0x2c lies outside it.  Nothing else in the machine claims that address.

*** AND THAT SHARPENS THE ONE QUESTION THAT IS STILL OPEN INTO SOMETHING WORTH MEASURING:
IF ANY OF THE TWELVE WRITES CARRIES WDCTL_RST (0x04), THEN MAPPING THE REGISTER STARTS
PERFORMING REAL RESETS ON A MACHINE THAT HAS NEVER HAD ONE. ***  The prior report said six
of twelve are 0x08 and did not record the other six.  0x08 is inert post-#481; 0x04 is not.

PANEL DISPOSITION, adopted: SHIP, BUT NOT ON THIS PACKET.  The twelve-write measurement
comes from a LOST LOG -- the third artifact lost from the same seat's scratch directory --
so every number in the round's warrant is a seat's report rather than a citation.  A re-take
is in flight, and it carries the control that discriminates the two diagnoses: if the
command-block accesses at +0x00..0x0f SUCCEED, the defect is a missing offset case; if they
do NOT, the defect is a wrong devinit->addr and the one-line fix would paper over it.

AND A DISPOSITION THE PANEL WAS RIGHT TO STATE PLAINLY: do NOT fold this into wdcnoirq as a
rider.  nIEN stays dead either way, and the two rounds answer different questions.

Disclosed rather than excluded, and this seat's 100% rate should not be read as accuracy.]  It confirmed the lost seat's figures across four runs AND captured what no previous report had -- the other six values, one of which carries WDCTL_RST.  Its discriminating control (does the command block succeed?) came back decisively and settles which of two diagnoses is right.  Its MEMORY_RW_ONE_PAGE relative-offset trap is a real instrument finding that plausibly explains the earlier report.

entries.note:
VERDICT: CONFIRMED -- the lost seat's numbers were right, AND THE RE-TAKE FOUND WHAT THE
ORIGINAL NEVER RECORDED.  The panel's gate is discharged: the warrant no longer rests on
an unpreserved artifact.

Q1 -- twelve writes to 0x1400002c, six of value 0x08?  **YES TO BOTH.**  Reproduced on
four runs (three pristine boots plus the instrumented build): 12 writes, 0 reads, all
len=1, all from pc=0x8c15f6e8 <obio_iomem_write_1+0x8>, all real guest stores
(no_exceptions=0).

*** Q2 -- THE VALUES, WHICH NO PREVIOUS REPORT CAPTURED, AND ONE OF THEM CARRIES
WDCTL_RST. ***

     1   0x0c   WDCTL_4BIT | WDCTL_RST      <-- SRST ASSERTED
     2   0x08   WDCTL_4BIT                  <-- SRST released
  3..12   0x02 / 0x08 alternating (IDS / 4BIT, five pairs)
  histogram: 0x0c x1, 0x08 x6, 0x02 x5

So the FIRST write is a real ATA soft-reset assert/release pair at the head of the channel
probe, silently discarded today.  Bit names taken from the tree's own
src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h, not from memory.  Confirmed independently ON THE
UNMODIFIED BINARY by the tree's committed write-watchpoint (#250): same paddr, 0x0c first,
same value set.  It saw 9 of 12 because the watchpoint self-suppresses while
about_to_enter_single_step is set -- **a lower bound BY CONSTRUCTION**, so it corroborates
the VALUES and not the count, and the seat said so rather than reporting 9 as a discrepancy.

  CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX, and it is the question this round has been holding for: mapping
  the register makes that first write REACH `wdc_new_command_reset()` -- clearing
  atapi_cmd_in_progress, atapi_phase and write_in_progress, and purging the inbuf ring.
  On a fresh channel probe those are already zero, so the effect is probably nil HERE; but
  it is a real state change and the round must say so rather than describe the arm as inert.
  The 0x08/0x02 writes hit no WDCTL_RST branch.  COMMAND_RESET's only two consumers (the
  cyl_lo/cyl_hi read arms) are both diskimage_is_a_cdrom()-gated and do not fire on this
  IDE-disk rig.  **The fix-side measurement was deliberately NOT taken.**

*** Q3 -- THE DISCRIMINATING CONTROL, AND IT DECIDES BETWEEN THE TWO DIAGNOSES: THE
COMMAND BLOCK SUCCEEDS. ***  12,718 accesses across all eight registers (2560 DATA reads,
10,033 status polls, 33 sdh writes, 14 commands), and wd0 ATTACHES: 131 cyl / 16 head /
63 sec / 132048 sectors -- a device signature RAM cannot produce.  Cross-checked against
the pristine build's own -v output, which counts 2560 `wdc: read from DATA`, matching the
hook exactly.

  So the defect is a MISSING OFFSET CASE, not a wrong devinit->addr, and the one-line fix
  is aimed correctly.  Had it come back the other way, the one-liner would have papered
  over a misplaced device.

Q4 -- anything else claiming 0x1400002c?  NO, and confirmed on the CONSTRUCTED machine via
`device list` rather than by grep alone.  And the registered wdc_altstatus at 0x14000206
receives ZERO accesses for the entire boot -- the handler that exists is never reached.

*** THE INSTRUMENT TRAP, WHICH IS THE PART THAT OUTLIVES THIS ROW. ***  The seat's FIRST
census hook reported 12 unmapped writes and ZERO command-block accesses -- clean,
confident, and half wrong.  The device arm of MEMORY_RW_ONE_PAGE does
`paddr -= mem->devices[i].baseaddr` BEFORE calling the handler, so device accesses reach
do_return_ok carrying the RELATIVE offset.  **A window predicate on `paddr` is therefore
blind to exactly the mapped half -- the half that answers Q3.**

  That is plausibly how the earlier lost report came back with the writes and no control:
  not a lost log so much as an instrument that could only see one side.  It is the
  phantom-absence class with a subtraction in it, and the fix was an entry-paddr latch
  plus PROVING THE INSTRUMENT SEES THE POSITIVE CASE BEFORE BELIEVING ITS NEGATIVES.

NOT SETTLED, recorded as such: whether delivering the reset changes the boot outcome
(fix-side, deliberately untaken); CD-ROM rig behaviour; anything past the installer
prompt.  All numbers scope to OpenBSD 7.6 RAMDISK #70's probe/attach phase.

Repo untouched by the census; HEAD moved 77b7c03 -> 772edb9 during the run and the drift
was CHECKED -- `git diff --stat 77b7c03..HEAD -- src/` is empty, so the measurement still
describes current HEAD's source.

entries.note: *** READ-ONLY PREP DONE 2026-09-18, so the round starts warm.  It is now the strongest CRITICAL-AND-EASILY-RESOLVABLE candidate on the queue: a ONE-LINE fix that became SAFE TO TAKE only when `wdcaltctrlbit' closed. ***  VERIFIED BY READING, not assumed: (1) the switch is at dev_wdc.c's 'Special hacks for individual machines' block -- THREE cases (MACHINE_MACPPC +0x160, MACHINE_HPCMIPS a hardcoded 0x14000386, MACHINE_IQ80321 +0x402) and NO MACHINE_LANDISK, so landisk falls through to the default `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206'.  (2) `devinit->addr_mult' EXISTS (src/include/device.h, `int addr_mult') and dev_wdc.c already uses it in four places -- so agy's prescribed form `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x16 * devinit->addr_mult' is well-formed rather than invented.  (3) machine_landisk.c creates the device by STRING at port 0x14000000-0x1400000f ('wdc0 at obio0 port 0x14000000-0x1400000f irq 10'), not by a direct dev_wdc_init call -- which is why a grep for dev_wdc_init in that file finds nothing and could be misread as 'landisk has no wdc'.  (4) the arithmetic is consistent with the measured driver behaviour: a seat measured the OpenBSD 7.6 driver writing +0x2c, and 0x16 * 2 == 0x2c.  *** THE ONE FACT STILL TO SETTLE BEFORE THE EDIT: landisk's ACTUAL addr_mult.  The 0x2c consistency HOLDS ONLY IF it is 2, and that has NOT been read -- stated as owed rather than assumed, because the whole fix is one constant and a wrong multiplier maps the register to the wrong address silently. ***  ORDER SAFETY, re-verified: the danger was mapping the register WHILE the alt-ctrl predicate still triggered on WDCTL_4BIT (0x08) -- six of the twelve measured Device Control writes are 0x08, so the device would have latched COMMAND_RESET six times per probe.  `wdcaltctrlbit' fixed the predicate FIRST and is CLOSED, so that hazard is spent and this row is UNBLOCKED.

entries.note: *** THE OWED FACT IS SETTLED 2026-09-18: landisk passes `addr_mult=2'. ***  Read from src/machines/machine_landisk.c, in the device string itself -- "wdc irq=%s.cpu[%i].irq[0x%x] addr_mult=2 addr=0x14000000".  SO THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES: 0x16 * 2 == 0x2c, which is exactly the offset a seat measured the OpenBSD 7.6 driver writing, and agy's prescribed line resolves to 0x14000000 + 0x2c == 0x1400002c.  *** THE FIX IS NOW FULLY SPECIFIED AND EVERY FACT UNDER IT HAS BEEN READ: ***  add to the 'Special hacks for individual machines' switch in dev_wdc.c --      case MACHINE_LANDISK:          alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x16 * devinit->addr_mult;          break;  This was deliberately NOT inferred from the 0x2c consistency alone.  The whole fix is one constant, and a wrong multiplier maps the register to the wrong address SILENTLY -- no crash, no diagnostic, just a control register nobody reaches.  That is the hand-assembled-constant trap, which bit this session twice in one night (an invented 0x0ff20000 that returned the SENTINEL, and a mutant anchored on the wrong guard), so the multiplier was READ rather than derived from agreement.  NOT TAKEN THIS CYCLE, and the reason is scope rather than doubt: #531's verifying table is in flight, and the loop's own rule is to ADVANCE THE IN-FLIGHT TASK rather than open a second round whose propagation and rebuild would contend.  The round is READY: order safety re-verified (wdcaltctrlbit closed the predicate first, so mapping the register can no longer latch COMMAND_RESET on the six routine 0x08 writes per probe), every fact read, and the edit is three lines.

entries.note:
[NOT A SEAT ANSWER] (#534 R2: was the stage-scoped no-panel token, which this entry never meant)  *** AND THE REASON THIS TOKEN IS HERE IS ITSELF THE FINDING: I RECORDED THIS VERIFICATION AS `seat: opus5' AND IT PROMOTED landiskaux's assess stage FROM A ONE-SEAT FILING TO 2/9, REDDENING BOTH STAGE GATES -- one hour after `#532' shipped the token for exactly that class, against its own author. ***  No panel has been convened on `landiskaux'; pass 1 is about to run.  The reading below is MAIN-LOOP work, not a seat answer, and crediting it to opus5 would have manufactured a review that never happened -- the same defect `#532' found in `gen_dashboard.py' this morning, arriving from the authoring side instead of the rendering side.  *The lesson is not `remember the token'.  It is that the entry-writing step has no check on whether a `seat' field names something that actually answered, and the gate can only see the count.*

*** EVERY FACT UNDER THIS ROUND RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BEFORE ITS PANEL, and the one that mattered most was NOT in the row: the proposed address could have COLLIDED with the main mapping, and nothing had checked. ***

  1. `dev_wdc.c:2098` switches on `devinit->machine->machine_type` with exactly THREE cases -- MACPPC (`+0x160`), HPCMIPS (a hardcoded `0x14000386`, guarded on `addr == 0x14000180`) and IQ80321 (`+0x402`).  No MACHINE_LANDISK.  CONFIRMED.
  2. `src/include/device.h:53` declares `int addr_mult`, and `dev_wdc.c` uses it at `:1174` (`relative_addr /= d->addr_mult`), `:2083`, `:2123`.  The prescribed form is well-formed, not invented.  CONFIRMED.
  3. `machine_landisk.c:87-88` builds the device string `"wdc irq=... addr_mult=2 addr=0x14000000"`.  **`addr_mult=2` read from the string itself**, not inferred from the 0x2c consistency.  CONFIRMED.
  4. `machine.h:268` defines `MACHINE_LANDISK 6004`.  CONFIRMED.

*** TWO THINGS THE ROW SAID LOOSELY, CORRECTED HERE BECAUSE A FUTURE READER WILL GREP FOR THEM AND FIND NOTHING: ***
  * The row says landisk *falls through to the default*.  **There is no `default:` arm.**  The switch ends at `:2110` with a bare `}`.  The value comes from a PRE-SWITCH initialisation at `:2095`, `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206`.  The substance is right and the mechanism is not what the word `default' implies -- and the distinction matters to the fix, because a `case` that falls out of the switch without assigning simply keeps `:2095`'s value.
  * `alt_status_addr` is NOT part of the main device mapping.  `:2120` registers a SEPARATE TWO-BYTE device, `"wdc_altstatus"`, at that address; `:2122` registers the main one at `devinit->addr` for `DEV_WDC_LENGTH * addr_mult` bytes.

*** THE COLLISION CHECK NOBODY HAD RUN, and it is the reason the second point above is worth the space: *** `DEV_WDC_LENGTH` is **8** (`dev_wdc.c:45`), so landisk's main wdc device spans `8 * 2 = 16` bytes, `0x14000000..0x1400000f` -- which is exactly the range `machine_landisk.c:86`'s own comment claims (`port 0x14000000-0x1400000f`).  The proposed altstatus lands at `0x14000000 + 0x16 * 2 = 0x1400002c`, i.e. **0x2c = 44 >= 16, comfortably beyond the main span: NO COLLISION.**  Had the multiplier been larger, or `DEV_WDC_LENGTH` bigger, the fix would have registered a two-byte device INSIDE an existing one.

AND THE DEFECT ITSELF IS CONFIRMED ARITHMETICALLY: today landisk gets `0x14000000 + 0x206 = **0x14000206**` while the OpenBSD 7.6 driver writes **0x1400002c** -- so the twelve measured Device Control writes land on memory no device claims.  The fix closes exactly that gap.

*STILL OWED BEFORE THE EDIT, and not skipped: the round's `witness` is `none`, so per the 2026-08-27 lifecycle ruling ONE seat must be asked to try a rung-3 probe before this is recorded as rung-1.  `DEVINIT` is invisible to the offline differential, but that is an argument about one instrument, not a demonstration that no guest-path witness exists -- and the last time that ask was made, a seat built one in a single invocation.*

entries.note:
[NOT A SEAT ANSWER] (#534 R2: was the stage-scoped no-panel token, which this entry never meant)  Records correction; no panel ran for this entry.

*** THE ROW SAID `witness: none -- the mapping is unverified by any row because DEVINIT is invisible to the offline differential', AND A MEASURED RUNG-4 BOOT CENSUS HAS EXISTED SINCE 2026-08-27. ***  `none` is the term this project defines as DOCUMENTED-ONLY, so the field was asserting that no guest ever reaches this path -- about a defect whose whole evidence is a guest reaching it twelve times.

**The stated reason was true and irrelevant.**  `DEVINIT` *is* invisible to the offline differential -- that is a fact about ONE instrument, and the row let it stand for the whole ladder.  This project's 2026-08-27 lifecycle ruling exists for exactly this: *an argument about one instrument is not a demonstration that no guest-path witness exists*, and the ask costs one invocation.  Here nobody even had to ask -- **the census was already on disk, in this row's own artifacts directory.**  That makes it an UNREAD REVIEW of the round's own evidence, which is the class this session has now hit four times.

MEASURED, from `census_20260827/RESULTS.txt` (read, not summarised):
  * OpenBSD 7.6 issues **exactly TWELVE byte writes to paddr 0x1400002c and ZERO reads**, reproduced on FOUR runs across TWO independent instruments (`A1/A2/A3_pristine_boot.log` on an unmodified build, `B1_hook_full_window.log` on a census-hook build).
  * All twelve are `len=1`, all from `pc=0x8c15f6e8 <obio_iomem_write_1+0x8>`, all with `no_exceptions=0` -- **real guest stores, not debugger reads.**  That is the clause-(ii) device-signature discipline satisfied from the guest side.
  * Six carry `0x08` (WDCTL_4BIT), five carry `0x02` (WDCTL_IDS), and **the FIRST carries `0x0c` = `WDCTL_RST | WDCTL_4BIT` -- a real ATA SOFT RESET, silently discarded today.**  That raises the guest-visible consequence above `a control register nobody reads': the drive is commanded to reset and never is.
  * The command block at `0x14000000..0x1400000f` SUCCEEDS -- 12,718 accesses across all eight registers, `wd0` attaches with correct geometry -- so `devinit->addr` is RIGHT and the defect is a missing offset case, not a wrong base.  **A LIVENESS CONTROL, from the same boot.**
  * `wdc_altstatus` at `0x14000206` receives **ZERO accesses for the entire boot**, and the device list confirms it registered there (`A5_device_list.log:32`).

**WHY THE FIELD IS NOT SIMPLY SET TO `boot:`**: clause (i) says a rung-2..4 witness is INVALID unless it shows the symptom pre-fix AND goes green post-fix with the SAME script.  Only the pre-fix half can exist before the fix.  The field now says which half is measured and which is owed, rather than choosing between two wrong answers.

AND THE ROUND IS NOT AS OPEN AS THE ROW IMPLIED -- prior work nobody had folded in: a pass-1 brief (`brief_p1_20260828.md`), and a codex FIX-DESIGN run (`codex_fixdesign_20260911.txt`) whose verdict is that **the replacement address is NOT established by the four permitted files** -- it calls it `Verified A' and declines to derive 0x16 from the source.  Its design constraints, each checked here before being carried forward:
  * `dev_wdc_altstatus_access` does **NOT** divide `relative_addr` by `addr_mult` -- VERIFIED by reading the function; it tests `relative_addr != 0` and nothing else.  So the primary's two-byte stride does NOT require a two-byte auxiliary registration.
  * **Twelve one-byte writes at offset 0 cannot distinguish a length-1 from a length-2 registration** -- already filed as `wdcaltwidth` (*every row uses len == 1*).
  * **Direct calls to the auxiliary handler cannot test the missing machine case at all**, since they bypass init and address dispatch -- codex deriving rung 1's own rule independently.
  * The address fix and `wdcaltdigin`'s width narrowing **compose without semantic conflict**; they edit different lines.

*** THE `0x16 * addr_mult' FORM WAS SUPERSEDED THREE WEEKS AGO AND WAS RE-PROPOSED FROM THIS ROW'S OWN PREP ENTRY. ***  `regress/artifacts/landiskaux/brief_p1_20260828.md:6` reads *VERDICT: SHIP `case MACHINE_LANDISK: alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x2c; break;`* and says the `0x16' route was *superseded by the driver source*.  The primary source is on disk: `_scratchpad/netbsd_wdc_obio.c:66` `#define WDC_OBIO_AUXREG_OFFSET 0x2c` and `:101` `oa->oa_io[0].or_addr + WDC_OBIO_AUXREG_OFFSET` -- a BYTE offset.  `0x16' is `0x2c / 2', a factorisation of the measured answer, not a landisk constant.  The 09-18 prep entry called the multiplier form `fully specified' and the 09-18 pass-1 brief (mine) inherited it; the panel caught it (grok with the citation; agy, deepseek, kimi-sub independently preferring the literal).  *Another instance of prior work on disk not folded in -- this time a prior pass's VERDICT, sitting beside the census that was read.*

Also settled by the same file: `WDC_OBIO_AUXREG_SIZE = NPORTS * 2 = 2`, so the tree's two-byte `wdc_altstatus' registration already MATCHES the driver for landisk.

COLLISION CHECK COMPLETED against the WHOLE machine, not just the main span (three seats named the gap): `census_20260827/logs/A5_device_list.log` lists every landisk device; nothing is registered between `wdc` (ends 0x1400000f) and ram at 0x1e000000 except the old altstatus at 0x14000206.  0x1400002c-2d is FREE.

Incidental, codex: HPCMIPS's guarded assignment equals its own fallback (0x14000180 + 0x206 == 0x14000386), i.e. that special case is a no-op today.  Scope note only; not this round.

rows.state_note:
*** UNBLOCKED 2026-08-27: its stated prerequisite is discharged. ***

`DEVINIT(wdc)` computes `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206` and then carries a switch
labelled *Special hacks for individual machines* with cases for MACPPC, HPCMIPS and IQ80321.
**There is no LANDISK case** -- verified at HEAD: `grep -c MACHINE_LANDISK src/devices/
dev_wdc.c` returns 0.  A seat MEASURED the OpenBSD 7.6 driver writing Device Control at
`+0x2c`: twelve writes during probe, all landing on unmapped memory.

One `case MACHINE_LANDISK:` line fixes it.

IT WAS BLOCKED, AND IS NOT ANY MORE.  The queue recorded that shipping this line alone would
make the ALT-CTRL arm live with a wrong predicate -- six of those twelve writes are `0x08`,
the bit the arm then triggered on.  `#481` changed the predicate to `WDCTL_RST`, and
`0x08 & 0x04 == 0`, so those six writes are now inert.  See `wdcaltctrlbit`.

WHAT IT STILL OWES, and none of it is blocked: a rung-3 attempt (the lifecycle ruling makes
the ASK mandatory, and landisk is the rig the measurement came from), and a detector row --
though note DEVINIT is invisible to the offline differential, which is the same problem
`wdchpcmipsaddr` has.  That is the round's real design question, not the one-line edit.

*Consequence of leaving it: on a real rig the guest's nIEN and SRST are no-ops today, and
the round that fixes wdcnoirq notes exactly that -- the fix's spurious-interrupt exposure
under nIEN is UNMEASURABLE on the only rig this project has, because the register the guest
writes is not mapped.*  *** THE LAST FIVE UNREAD ANSWERS READ 2026-09-18 (panel_20260827_134019).  23 OF 23 NOW READ -- the section-G backlog is CLEARED. ***  This was a pass-1 DESIGN panel on a now-CLOSED row, so it was read for the question `seatprescriptiondiff' exists to ask: DID THE PRESCRIPTIONS SURVIVE INTO THE SHIPPED WORK?  *** AND THE ANSWER IS YES -- A NEGATIVE RESULT THAT BOUNDS THE ROW I FILED THIS MORNING. ***  agy prescribed three items.  (1) the predicate fix -- SHIPPED, dev_wdc.c now triggers on WDCTL_RST (0x04) and not WDCTL_4BIT (0x08), with the rising-edge `prev_ctl' machinery and a recorded brace hazard beside it.  (2) the MACHINE_LANDISK alt-status mapping -- NOT in dev_wdc.c, and NOT a silent drop: it was SPLIT INTO ITS OWN ROW `landiskaux', which is open, and OUTSTANDING_BUGS carries the coupling in full.  (3) acceptance rows -- folded, per the kimi/deepseek rulings in the same panel.  *** SO `seatprescriptiondiff' HAS A POPULATION OF ONE (the #531 case), NOT A PATTERN.  A class filed from a single instance is a hypothesis, and this is the first test of it -- it did not generalise.  Recorded as such rather than left looking systemic. ***  AND THE COUPLING WAS HANDLED IN THE SAFE ORDER, which is worth keeping because the unsafe one was live: mapping the landisk register WHILE the predicate still triggered on 0x08 would have latched COMMAND_RESET on SIX routine Device Control writes per probe (a seat measured twelve writes, six of them 0x08, currently all landing on unmapped memory).  The round fixed the PREDICATE first, so `wdcaltctrlbit' is CLOSED as overtaken and `landiskaux' is now OPEN AND UNBLOCKED.  *** THAT MAKES `landiskaux' A ONE-LINE FIX THAT IS NOW SAFE TO TAKE -- a strong critical-and-easily-resolvable candidate for the next round. ***  The other seats' content was design judgement, no live defects: glm listed SEVEN uninlined premises and ranked them by load-bearingness (the premise-audit discipline working as intended); minimax named an option-set hole (C4/B5, 'the brief's C-options jump'); deepseek ruled that a channel reset must clear in-flight transfer, FIFO, phase and interrupt state but NOT per-device-life diagnostics like `warned_*' -- and dev_wdc.c carries 43 `warned_' references, so that distinction is load-bearing there.  *** READ-ONLY PREP DONE 2026-09-18, so the round starts warm.  It is now the strongest CRITICAL-AND-EASILY-RESOLVABLE candidate on the queue: a ONE-LINE fix that became SAFE TO TAKE only when `wdcaltctrlbit' closed. ***  VERIFIED BY READING, not assumed: (1) the switch is at dev_wdc.c's 'Special hacks for individual machines' block -- THREE cases (MACHINE_MACPPC +0x160, MACHINE_HPCMIPS a hardcoded 0x14000386, MACHINE_IQ80321 +0x402) and NO MACHINE_LANDISK, so landisk falls through to the default `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206'.  (2) `devinit->addr_mult' EXISTS (src/include/device.h, `int addr_mult') and dev_wdc.c already uses it in four places -- so agy's prescribed form `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x16 * devinit->addr_mult' is well-formed rather than invented.  (3) machine_landisk.c creates the device by STRING at port 0x14000000-0x1400000f ('wdc0 at obio0 port 0x14000000-0x1400000f irq 10'), not by a direct dev_wdc_init call -- which is why a grep for dev_wdc_init in that file finds nothing and could be misread as 'landisk has no wdc'.  (4) the arithmetic is consistent with the measured driver behaviour: a seat measured the OpenBSD 7.6 driver writing +0x2c, and 0x16 * 2 == 0x2c.  *** THE ONE FACT STILL TO SETTLE BEFORE THE EDIT: landisk's ACTUAL addr_mult.  The 0x2c consistency HOLDS ONLY IF it is 2, and that has NOT been read -- stated as owed rather than assumed, because the whole fix is one constant and a wrong multiplier maps the register to the wrong address silently. ***  ORDER SAFETY, re-verified: the danger was mapping the register WHILE the alt-ctrl predicate still triggered on WDCTL_4BIT (0x08) -- six of the twelve measured Device Control writes are 0x08, so the device would have latched COMMAND_RESET six times per probe.  `wdcaltctrlbit' fixed the predicate FIRST and is CLOSED, so that hazard is spent and this row is UNBLOCKED.  *** THE OWED FACT IS SETTLED 2026-09-18: landisk passes `addr_mult=2'. ***  Read from src/machines/machine_landisk.c, in the device string itself -- "wdc irq=%s.cpu[%i].irq[0x%x] addr_mult=2 addr=0x14000000".  SO THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES: 0x16 * 2 == 0x2c, which is exactly the offset a seat measured the OpenBSD 7.6 driver writing, and agy's prescribed line resolves to 0x14000000 + 0x2c == 0x1400002c.  *** THE FIX IS NOW FULLY SPECIFIED AND EVERY FACT UNDER IT HAS BEEN READ: ***  add to the 'Special hacks for individual machines' switch in dev_wdc.c --      case MACHINE_LANDISK:          alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x16 * devinit->addr_mult;          break;  This was deliberately NOT inferred from the 0x2c consistency alone.  The whole fix is one constant, and a wrong multiplier maps the register to the wrong address SILENTLY -- no crash, no diagnostic, just a control register nobody reaches.  That is the hand-assembled-constant trap, which bit this session twice in one night (an invented 0x0ff20000 that returned the SENTINEL, and a mutant anchored on the wrong guard), so the multiplier was READ rather than derived from agreement. === WHAT THE CENSUS ESTABLISHES, measured on four independent runs ===
* **Exactly TWELVE byte writes to paddr `0x1400002c`, and ZERO reads.**
* **The FIRST carries `0x0c` = `WDCTL_RST | WDCTL_4BIT`.**  Six carry `0x08` (WDCTL_4BIT), five carry `0x02` (WDCTL_IDS).  *** SO A REAL ATA SOFT RESET IS AMONG THEM AND IS SILENTLY DISCARDED TODAY. ***  The row says "writes land on unmapped memory"; **the guest-visible fact is that a soft reset never happens.**
* **The base is RIGHT and the defect is a missing OFFSET case, not a wrong base**: the command block at `0x14000000..0x1400000f` succeeds with **12,718 accesses across all eight registers** and `wd0` attaches with correct geometry.
* **`0x1400002c` falls in no device entry** -- established on the CONSTRUCTED machine via the debugger's device list (`A5_device_list.log`), not by grep.  The command block ends `0x1c` below it; `wdc_altstatus` begins `0x1da` above it.
* *** AND THE REGISTERED WINDOW IS DEAD: `0x14000206` receives ZERO accesses for the entire boot -- zero "read from ALTSTATUS" and zero "write to ALT. CTRL" under `-v`. ***  **So the handler that exists is never reached, and the twelve writes that should reach it are discarded.**

**THE FIX:** `case MACHINE_LANDISK: alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x2c; break;`  The seat independently confirmed the mechanics from the source: `alt_status_addr` is assigned BEFORE the switch, has **no later overwrite and exactly one subsequent use** (the auxiliary registration), and the secondary-controller selection uses `devinit->addr` rather than `alt_status_addr` -- so **there is no hidden default-dependent tail requiring another change.**

*** TWO CORRECTIONS THE CENSUS MAKES AGAINST ITSELF, AND THEY MUST NOT BE DROPPED: ***
  1. **`0x1400002c` IS ONE OF FIVE UNMAPPED SITES PER BOOT.**  The other four are real queue items: **`0xfe080000`** (5/boot) and **`0xfe080040`** (1/boot), SH7751R extended-INTC registers reached from `intc_init` and `intpri_intr_priority`; and **`0x10000003`** (5/boot, `rtc_ce`) and **`0x10000005`** (3/boot, `intr_init` / `extintr_establish`), landisk board registers.  *The write-up had presented only the `0x14000000..0x14000040` window while `census.py` prints an "ALL paddrs" section.*
  2. **CONSEQUENCE, stated by the census itself: fixing `0x1400002c` does NOT make `-T` usable on a landisk boot** -- four other sites still halt it.  **So any `-T`-based row is a PROBE row, not a boot row.**

**AND ONE CITATION IS EMBARGOED BY THE ARTIFACT'S OWN CAPTION:** a "2560 agreement" figure is marked OWED -- *"do not let a round block cite the 2560 agreement"* until the `-v` instrument is re-taken to completion and preserved.  *Recorded here so the next round meets the embargo rather than the number.*

**MY OWN FRAMING WAS ALSO WRONG: there is NO `default:` arm.**  `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206;` is assigned before a switch carrying exactly three cases (MACPPC `+0x160`, HPCMIPS conditional, IQ80321 `+0x402`).  LANDISK takes the FALLBACK, not a default arm -- and **a missing case does not by itself prove a defect**, since a machine matching the fallback needs no case.  What proves it here is the census, not the absence.

*A free finding from the seat: the HPCMIPS case is NUMERICALLY REDUNDANT at the tested base -- `0x14000180 + 0x206 == 0x14000386`, so that "special hack" assigns the value the fallback already gives.*

**STATUS: READY TO IMPLEMENT, with the address established and the severity raised** -- a discarded ATA soft reset rather than twelve lost writes.

rows.state_note:
*** THIS ROW'S LEDGER ENTRY WAS WRITTEN INVERTED AND IS CORRECTED HERE, 2026-08-28. ***

The entry filed in c2249eb said the gate *greps for* a token spelled `non-existant` with nothing pinning the spelling, so a typo fix would silently empty the check.  **That is the OPPOSITE of the finding.**  `gate_hygiene.sh` does NOT carry `non-existant` in its `PATTERNS` list at all.  It DOES scan the landisk log -- the loop is `for rig in luna88k landisk; do rlog=$LOGDIR/drive_$rig.log` -- it simply never looks for this string.

**So twenty-six guest stores per boot fall off the memory map and no gate says a word.**  A store that reaches no responder is precisely the class a boot-log hygiene gate exists to catch, and this is the one string that names it.

NOT A ONE-LINER, and the cost is named rather than discovered later: adding the pattern reddens every rig that currently has unmapped accesses, so it needs a census across the whole rig set and probably an address-scoped allowlist with dated entries.  Filed with that cost stated rather than shipped as a change that turns the battery red.

*METHOD NOTE PRESERVED FROM THE ORIGINAL FILING, because it is the reason the row exists: verifying the seat's claim with `grep -c 'drive_landisk'` returned 0 and was read as a refutation.  The filename is CONSTRUCTED (`drive_$rig.log`), so the literal grep matched nothing -- the pattern-that-matched-nothing class, reached WHILE applying the do-not-trust-a-seat rule.  A zero count for a gate that visibly scans several rigs is surprising, and a surprising count means open the artifact before believing it.*

*The inverted ledger entry was caught by re-reading OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md before acting on the row as an 'easy fix' -- which it is not.  Had it been trusted, a future round would have gone looking for a spelling pin that has nothing to do with the defect.*

**SEVERITY SET MED, 2026-09-07, by the MAIN LOOP** (not a flagship adjudication -- opus5/fable5 are reserved for the 09-09 adjudication, and a rating is exactly the kind of judgment call that seat exists for; overturn it freely).  REASON: a gate check that CANNOT FIRE -- the hygiene gate greps for a token it contains zero occurrences of.  The check-that-cannot-fail class, verified both directions.
rows.note: *** A BARE TITLE WITH AN EMPTY NOTE UNTIL 2026-08-30 -- one of the population `baretitle` records -- so this is the note it should have had, written from a verification rather than from memory. ***  **THE CLAIM, CHECKED BOTH WAYS:** the boot-log hygiene gate greps for a set of diagnostic spellings and `non-existant` is not among them; nor is the correctly-spelled `non-existent`, so this is not a misspelling mismatch between gate and source -- **the gate does not look for the class at all.**  The emitter is `src/core/memory.c`, which prints `%s non-existant ...` at two sites under a verbosity gate.  **WHY IT MATTERS: the hygiene gate exists to catch guest accesses falling off the memory map, and this is precisely that message.**  A landisk boot makes 26 such accesses (`landiskunmapped4`, which carries a rung-4 BOOT witness), and the gate grades that boot's log without ever looking for them.  So the strongest available evidence for an unmapped access is invisible to the gate built to notice unmapped accesses.  **THE FIX IS ONE PATTERN**, and it must carry BOTH spellings: the tree spells it `non-existant` today, and a future correction of that typo would silently switch the gate off if it pins only the current form.  *A caution before adding it: this gate is a RATCHET, so a pattern that newly matches 26 real occurrences will turn it RED on the first run.  That is the oracle-correction ordering -- add the pattern, MEASURE the committed build red under it, then decide whether the 26 are a defect to fix or a baseline to pin.  Adding the pattern and the baseline in one commit is what laundering looks like from outside.*  *** AND THE TWO ROWS EXPLAIN EACH OTHER, WHICH NEITHER SAID. ***  `landiskunmapped4` carries a rung-4 BOOT witness -- *26 unmapped accesses, deterministic across three boots, **of which only ONE was previously caught***. rows.witness: harness:build-asan/ was measured unbuildable while every commit's propagation check reported green
rows.title: asanbaselinedrift  the propagation check is INCREMENTAL, so a stale BASELINE is invisible -- build-asan/ drifted until it would not compile while passing every commit
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-08-28 BY OWNER DECISION, from the round that fixed `asanunbuildable`.

**THE GAP:** `precommit_check.sh` enforces build-asan propagation for `$CHANGED` -- the files
THIS commit touches.  That bound is deliberate and correct; its own comment says *a gate that
hard-fails on a tree someone chose not to build is a gate that gets switched off*.  **But a
file no round happens to touch is never checked**, so a tree that was already stale when the
2026-08-27 ruling landed stays stale forever.  Measured: 111 divergent .c/.h files, of which
`diskimage.h` and `makeautodev.sh` broke the build -- neither touched by a recent round.

**THE SHAPE, worth stating because it generalises past this tree: an INCREMENTAL sync check
cannot detect a stale BASELINE.**  The tree passed every commit while compiling nothing.

*** THE DECISION: a SOFT-WARNING full `diff -rq` over the .c/.h set, SKIPPED ENTIRELY when the
tree is absent. ***  Warn, do not hard-fail -- and skip on absence -- so the
absence-is-not-a-failure property that keeps this gate switched on is preserved.  Chosen over
a hard fail (which is the exact shape the gate's author warned gets disabled) and over doing
nothing (which leaves the next drift to be found the way this one was: by someone trying to
use the tree).

**TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS ARE OWED, as for any gate change:** (1) with a source file deliberately
reverted in build-asan/, the check WARNS and names it; (2) with the tree absent entirely, the
check is SILENT and the gate stays green.  Ships as its own small harness round -- a gate edit
must not ride in on a diff reviewed for something else.

SCOPE NOTE: `Makefile`s legitimately differ (they carry the ASan COPTIM) and must be excluded;
the measured expectation after a correct sync is **14 differing files, all Makefiles, zero
others**.  `est/` is NOT in scope -- it has a declared divergence allowlist
(`tools/est_divergence.txt`); build-asan has none, which is why any .c/.h divergence there is
staleness by definition.

**SEVERITY SET MED, 2026-09-07, by the MAIN LOOP** (not a flagship adjudication -- opus5/fable5 are reserved for the 09-09 adjudication, and a rating is exactly the kind of judgment call that seat exists for; overturn it freely).  REASON: same family: the propagation check is INCREMENTAL, so a stale BASELINE is invisible and the tool reports green over it.

entries.note:
FOUND BY RUNNING THE DEAD-MAN SWITCH WHEN THE OWNER ASKED ABOUT CRON STATUS -- not by any
gate, and not by anyone reading the battery.  `nightly_check.sh` has been reporting

THE 2026-08-23 WEEKLY BATTERY WENT RED: RUN_SH_EXIT=1, VERDICT_TOKEN=REGRESS_FAIL,
passed 14 / failed 1 / skipped 1, on a DIRTY tree (`*** VERDICT DOES NOT DESCRIBE A
COMMIT ***`).  The Windows task's own LastTaskResult is 1 and has been since.

*** THE FAILING CHECK IS ONE LINE OF TEXT, AND EVERYTHING ELSE IN gate_build PASSED: ***
both trees built, 223 and 224 objects, binaries produced, zero errors, zero warnings.

    FAIL no stale allowlist entries    got=1 want=0
         STALE (listed as divergent, but the files now agree): promemul/arcbios.c

AND IT CASCADED, exactly as the carrier's serialisation note predicts: gate_build withdraws
the shared arc binary at gate start and republishes ONLY on success, so its failure left the
binary unpublished and **gate_mips SKIPPED** -- a whole gate's coverage lost, scored as SKIP
rather than as a failure.  One stale line cost two gates.

ALREADY FIXED IN THE TREE, by accident rather than by anyone chasing it: `867c697` (#481)
removed the arcbios entry.  So a re-run should be green -- but nothing re-ran it, and the
dead-man switch cannot tell 'fixed' from 'never looked at'.

*** THE DEFECT THAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH A ROUND: gate_build.sh PINS ITS OWN
ALLOWLIST. ***  `tools/est_divergence.txt` was created precisely to stop that -- its own
header says 'This file exists because the allowlist used to be PINNED inside the checker and
went stale TWICE'.  `precommit_check.sh` reads the file.  **`gate_build.sh` does not --
`grep -n est_divergence regress/gate_build.sh` returns NOTHING** -- and its pinned copy is
what went stale.

The two disagree TODAY, measured:
    gate_build.sh DIVERGENT  (5)  devices/{Makefile.skel,autodev.c,dev_jazz.c,dev_ne2000.c}
                                  machines/machine_arc.c
    est_divergence.txt       (6)  the same five PLUS devices/.index

The `.index` gap looks benign today -- the 8/23 run reported 'no divergence outside the
documented set: 0', so `list_diffs` does not surface it -- but benign-by-luck is the state
the file was written to end, and the stale entry proves the pinned copy drifts.

FIX (not taken here, because changing a gate owes negative controls): make gate_build.sh
READ est_divergence.txt, as precommit_check.sh already does.  Controls owed in both
directions -- prove it fails on an injected stale entry, and prove it passes unchanged on
the real list.

*And a scheduling hazard worth its own sentence: the battery fires on a fixed schedule and
caught the tree MID-EDIT (five modified files, including the device being worked that
afternoon).  A verdict that does not describe a commit cannot be attributed to anything,
which is the one thing a weekly battery exists to do.*

entries.ev: direct reading of gate_build.sh's list_diffs() and precommit_check.sh's section A
entries.note:
*** THE FIX THIS ROW FILED WOULD HAVE REPRODUCED THE DEFECT IT FIXES.  Found by reading,
before any code was written. ***

The row said: make `gate_build.sh` READ `est_divergence.txt`, as `precommit_check.sh`
already does, and cited the two lists disagreeing by `devices/.index` as evidence of drift.
**The disagreement is CORRECT, because the two consumers cover DIFFERENT POPULATIONS.**

  gate_build.sh   compares the whole trees via `list_diffs()`, which is
                  `find . \( -name '*.c' -o -name '*.h' -o -name '*.cc' -o -name
                  '*.skel' \)`.  **`.index` matches none of those, so list_diffs can
                  NEVER produce it.**  The gate then checks for STALE entries -- listed
                  as divergent but not actually divergent.
  precommit_check iterates `$CHANGED` from git, filtered to `src/*`, and uses the list to
                  SKIP known-divergent files.  Any path can appear there, `.index`
                  included, because the population comes from git rather than from a
                  find with extension filters.

*** SO IF gate_build READ THE FILE VERBATIM, `.index` WOULD ENTER ITS EXPECTED SET, WHERE
`list_diffs` CANNOT PRODUCE IT -- AND ITS OWN STALE-ENTRY CHECK WOULD FLAG IT STALE ON
EVERY RUN.  Permanently red.  That is exactly the failure that cost five days and a
skipped gate, reintroduced by the repair for it. ***

THE ROW'S CORE FINDING SURVIVES AND IS UNCHANGED: gate_build pins its own list, that pinned
copy DID go stale, and the staleness cost a red battery plus `gate_mips`.  What is refuted
is only the proposed remedy and the `.index` evidence for it.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, neither taken here, both now stated with the constraint they must
satisfy:
  (a) gate_build reads the file but FILTERS to the extensions list_diffs covers, so the
      expected set and the actual set are drawn from the same population;
  (b) leave them separate and add a check that gate_build's list is exactly the
      extension-filtered SUBSET of the file's -- which catches drift without coupling two
      checks that legitimately differ.

*This is the addition licence doing its job before an edit rather than after: the proposed
change had no measured delta and no transferred warrant, only 'the two lists disagree, so
unify them'.  Reading what each list is FOR took minutes and refuted it.*

rows.title: gdromfmt24  the 0x24 data-format arm is left unlatched and unbounded beside a latched sibling, and its correctness is unsettleable without an SPI/GD-ROM doc
rows.witness: none -- a DOCUMENTATION question, not an execution one.  The arm's behaviour is known and byte-identical to upstream; what is unknown is whether upstream is RIGHT, and no local manual covers GD-ROM/SPI/ATAPI packet commands.
rows.hold_question: Should the 0x24 arm keep upstream's announce-then-CONTINUE, or is that a defect?  It cannot be settled from the fifteen manuals in _scratchpad/ (none covers GD-ROM/SPI/ATAPI).  TWO SUB-QUESTIONS a seat can answer without a doc: (1) is announce-then-continue on an UNIMPLEMENTED format coherent with what the arm then does -- it falls into the 2048-byte cooked read path built for 0x20 -- or does it read the wrong shape?  (2) the arm is unlatched and guest-drivable: does it belong to `floodclass` now, independently of whether its CONTINUE is correct?
rows.state_note:
*** FILED 2026-08-29 BECAUSE THE ADJUDICATION THAT RULED IT FORCED HAD PRODUCED NO ROW.
A pass-2 seat searched the ledger, OUTSTANDING_BUGS and fable_queue and found NOTHING;
I re-verified all three before creating this. ***

`#490` de-fatalised two sites in `handle_command` and deliberately left the SIBLING data
format `0x24` **byte-identical** -- an unlatched, unbounded `fatal()` immediately beside an
arm that is now latched, with upstream's typo (`anway`) intact.

**THAT WAS THE RIGHT CALL AND IT IS NOT THE SAME AS BEING SETTLED.**  `0x24` is upstream's
gamble: it announces and then CONTINUES into the read path.  Whether that is correct needs
the SPI/GD-ROM command semantics, and `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` shows fifteen manuals with
**none** covering GD-ROM, SPI or ATAPI packet commands.  So it is unsettleable locally --
which is a REASON TO FILE, not a reason to say nothing.

**THE RECORDS DEFECT THIS FIXES:** the device comment's *"unsettleable here"* was a
disposition note doing a schema value's work -- exactly the failure the `detector:` adoption
record names, where three rounds parked at `held` carrying prose because no term fitted.

WHAT THE DETECTOR DOES AND DOES NOT PIN HERE.  `fmt 0x24` asserts the pair `1,0`: the
upstream text printed ONCE (a presence pin on the byte-identical arm) and ZERO decline
matches.  It does **NOT** pin (a) that `0x24` still CONTINUES into the read path -- an edit
converting it to announce-then-`break` keeps `1,0` green, and no row sends `0x24` expecting
data; nor (b) the arm's unlatched, unbounded character, since one packet is sent and
boundedness is unobserved in either direction.  Both are outside the contract's claim 9,
which is honest as far as it goes.

**SIBLINGS IN THE SAME FILE, same class, also unlatched and guest-drivable:** the
`rejecting sector_count` diagnostic and the `Huh?` arm.  Both fall under `floodclass`.
*And note `latch cond` BORROWS its kill channel from the first of those -- so a future
round de-fatalising it can silently turn that row permanently green.*

rows.title: The wsl-dollar hook's 18 controls are run by nothing
rows.witness: harness:the suite now runs from precommit when the hook or the suite changes -- 18 of 18, 0 wrong, preserved at regress/artifacts/makercfalse/hook_controls_20260829/CONTROL_hookctl_20260830.out; a bogus GXHOOK path makes it REFUSE rather than report 18 of 18 against a missing file
rows.note: `artifacts/makercfalse/hook_controls_20260829/hookctl.py` is an 18-row control suite (9 must FIRE, 9 must stay SILENT) for the PreToolUse wsl-dollar guard.  It is classified CLASS_RESEARCH -- evidence -- because no emulator gate can run it: it tests a Claude-Code hook, not the emulator.  **So the guard that fires on every Bash call has no regression test that anything executes.**  *** THE CASE FOR GATING IT IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the hook shipped 2026-08-29 with FOUR defects and nobody noticed for hours. *** Two false negatives (a multi-line `bash -c` block whose dollar sits below the -c -- the shape that actually bites, and which cost two confident wrong readings the same day) and two false positives that line-scoping was adopted to fix AND NEVER FIXED: a control of the very shape the hook's own comment cited as its motivating case still fired.  It scored 14/18; the rescoped form scores 18/18.  AGAINST gating: an emulator gate running a harness-tool control suite is a category mixture, and the suite depends on a file OUTSIDE the git root's normal scope.  A `tools/`-level check is likelier right than a `regress/` gate.  Cost is small (the suite runs in about a second) and it owes the usual two negative controls -- prove it reds on a broken hook, prove it greens on the shipped one.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30.  The 18 controls are run by something now: a conditional section in `precommit_check.sh`. ***  CONDITIONAL on purpose -- the suite takes ~28 s, which is too slow for every commit and is exactly how a gate earns being switched off.  It fires when the hook, or the suite itself, is in the changed set, which is when it can regress.  Not a regress gate: it tests a Claude-Code hook rather than the emulator, so no battery gate can host it.  **NO SENTINEL IS NOT A PASS.**  The section fails when `HOOKCTL_DONE` is absent, because the suite REFUSES outright if the hook is missing and that refusal must read as a failure rather than a skip.  *** AND RUNNING IT SURFACED A DEFECT IN THE SUITE ITSELF: `HOOK` WAS ONE MACHINE'S HARDCODED ABSOLUTE PATH, IN A TRACKED FILE. ***  That is the defect the whole harness migration fixed on 2026-08-17 -- *scripts DERIVE the project root from their own location; they used to hardcode one machine's absolute path, which is only half-tracked* -- and this suite was written twelve days later carrying it.  Now derived from `__file__` with a `GXHOOK` override, and it REFUSES if the target is absent instead of reporting a clean sweep against nothing.  Controlled both ways.  It still points at the `.claude/` path rather than the tracked file, deliberately: that is what Claude Code actually invokes, so testing it exercises the shim AND the hook behind it.  Pointing at the tracked file would stop testing the delegation, which is the part that can silently break.

rows.title: The battery's pre-flight git status is a multi-minute BLIND WINDOW
rows.witness: none
rows.note: *** MEASURED, NOT REASONED: `ps` showed `git -C ... status --porcelain` at 2:03 elapsed with NO verdict file and NO battery log on disk -- and the FULL span was ~15 MINUTES, not two: the task fired at 16:06:12 and the verdict's own START line reads 16:21:09. ***  (I filed 'over two minutes' from the single sample I had; the run's own record settled it afterwards. A number written from one observation is a lower bound, not a measurement.)  `nightly_battery.sh` computes `HEADSHA` and `DIRTY` BEFORE it opens either output: the verdict block ends `} > "$SUM"` and the run line is `./run.sh > "$LOG" 2>&1`, and a shell creates a redirect target only when it reaches that redirect.  So for the whole of the git call there is nothing to observe.  **THIS IS EXACTLY THE AMBIGUITY THE CARRIER'S OWN REDIRECT-TARGET RULE EXISTS TO RESOLVE, arriving inside the battery's own pre-flight.**  That rule says: log MISSING -> the command NEVER STARTED; log 0 bytes -> started.  Here the log is missing and the command HAS started, so the discriminator gives the wrong answer -- and it gives it during the exact window when an operator is most likely to be checking.  It compounds a hazard the script's own header already records: a battery launched from a Claude Code shell is ORPHANED, and *'the only tell was a log mtime 4.4 h stale'*.  During the blind window there is no mtime to read, so a genuinely orphaned start and a healthy one are INDISTINGUISHABLE by every documented check.  The only thing that separated them today was `ps -eo pid,ppid,etime,args`, which named the git child.  **REMEDY IS ONE LINE AND COSTS NOTHING: write a STARTING stamp to `$SUM` (or touch `$LOG`) BEFORE the git calls**, so the redirect-target rule works on this script.  The stamp is overwritten by the real verdict block moments later, so nothing is lost.  *Not fixed in the same pass because the battery was RUNNING and editing a shell script mid-execution is a documented defect class here -- bash reads incrementally by byte offset, and the failure looks like a syntax error in a file that parses clean afterwards.*  SECOND, SMALLER FINDING: the git call itself is slow because the repo is Windows-owned and WSL reaches it over /mnt/c.  Whether it should be narrowed (`git status --porcelain -- src/ tools/ regress/`) or simply stamped is a design question, not a defect -- **the blind window is the defect, and it exists at any duration.**  *** THE WINDOW'S DURATION IS TREE-STATE-DEPENDENT, measured the same evening on a SECOND run.  The defect is real and the ~15-minute figure is NOT its general size. ***  The 16:06 run took ~15 minutes to reach `START` because the pre-flight is `git status --porcelain` over `/mnt/c` on a DIRTY tree carrying a whole round's uncommitted work.  The 22:39 run reached `run.sh` in about SEVENTEEN SECONDS -- same machine, same command, same script -- because the tree was CLEAN.  **So the blind window is near-instant when it does not matter and long exactly when a round is mid-flight**, which is when someone is most likely to be watching it and most likely to misread the absence.  That makes it worse than a fixed-cost gap, not better: the failure mode is correlated with the moment of highest attention.  The remedy is unchanged and now has a second reason: a STARTING stamp written before the git calls costs nothing and removes a window whose length nobody can predict from the outside.

rows.title: #472's clamp introduced two -Wsign-compare warnings that cost a GATE
rows.witness: detector:regress/diff_diskimage_io.c (gate_offline.sh: compile, run, PASS token, selfmutant) and regress/gate_build.sh's `$lab: warnings` = 0 -- the measurement is regress/artifacts/diskimagesign/cascade_20260829 (pre-fix 2 warnings, post-fix 0; gate_build PASS then gate_mips PASS).  [Re-keyed 2026-10-09 by the flagship regress review, F2.3: this named only the cascade directory, a measurement and not a detector.]
rows.note:
*** NOT A COSMETIC WARNING -- IT WAS COSTING AN ENTIRE GATE'S COVERAGE, and that was found only by re-running a battery that had been RED AND UNREAD FOR FIVE DAYS. ***  `#472` replaced `len > OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE? OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE : len` with `len > remain? remain : len`, where `len` is `size_t` (parameter) and `remain` is `off_t`.  gcc warns twice at diskimage.c:1382 under the tree's own CWARNINGS.  **THE CASCADE:** `gate_build` wants ZERO warnings, so it FAILED; it withdraws `$RIG/gxsec-gxemul` at start and republishes only on success; `gate_mips` then `need_exec`s that binary and reported *'SKIP -- missing or non-executable binary'*.  **A whole gate lost, scored as SKIP rather than FAIL** -- byte-identical in shape to what one stale allowlist line cost on 2026-08-23, which is the defect `gatebuildallow` records.  **IT IS NOT A LIVE BUG AND THE ROUND SAYS SO:** `inblock = curofs & (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)` gives [0,511], so `remain` is in [1,512] and positive by construction; the conversion is value-preserving at every reachable value.  Both casts are therefore provable, not plausible.  MEASURED, control first: the reconstructed pre-fix line compiles rc=0/44072 b with **2** sign-compare warnings; the shipped source compiles rc=0/44112 b with **0**.  *** MY FIRST VERIFICATION WAS VACUOUS AND ITS OWN CONTROL CAUGHT IT: *** it reported 0 warnings for the PRE-FIX form, which must be 2.  The compile was failing on a missing include and the script read its empty output as a result -- the phantom-absence class, in a script written to prove a fix.  Take 2 reports compile rc and object size BEFORE the warning count and refuses to read the count without them.  EXPOSURE, stated honestly: warnings need a BUILD, builds are too slow for precommit, so warnings are checked only by the weekly battery -- a warning-introducing commit is invisible for up to seven days, and only if someone reads the result.  *** THE ROW NAMED NO COMMIT WHILE THE FIX HAD SHIPPED.  Found 2026-08-30 by reading `src/disk/diskimage.c`: the clamp now reads `lentoread = len > (size_t) remain? remain : (off_t) len;` with a `#491` comment proving both casts safe -- `inblock` is `curofs` masked to [0, OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1], so `remain` is in [1, 512] and can never be negative. ***  `git log -S` puts it in **18893de**, now recorded.  **This is the same shape a gate caught on `holdmarkermulti` in the same session -- work shipped, row names no commit -- and it did NOT trip here only because the state is `in work` rather than `open`.**  `check_row_states` scopes its shipped-work test to open rows, so an `in work` row can carry shipped code indefinitely without any gate objecting.  *Recorded as an observation about the checker's scope, not filed as a defect: widening it to `in work` would fire on every round that is genuinely mid-flight, which is what `in work` means.  The honest fix is the habit of filling `commits` at ship time, not a wider gate.*  The row's own EXPOSURE note stands unchanged and is the important part: warnings need a BUILD, builds are too slow for precommit, so a warning-introducing commit is invisible for up to seven days -- and only then if someone reads the battery result.

*** 2026-09-11 STATE CORRECTED: `in work` -> `closed`.  **THE LEDGER WAS THE STALE SIDE HERE, which is the opposite direction from every other finding in this sweep.** ***

`18893de` -- *'#491 diskimage: two -Wsign-compare warnings were costing an entire GATE'* -- is in the tree and is this row's own named commit.  **`OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` already records the outcome correctly**: *'Fixed and measured: pre-fix 2 warnings / post-fix 0, then `gate_build` PASS -> binary republished -> `gate_mips` PASS (was SKIP)'*.  The witness field likewise names a preserved artifact, `detector:regress/artifacts/diskimagesign/cascade_20260829`. [2026-11-02, records: since re-keyed (2026-10-09, flagship regress review F2.3) -- the witness field (ledger.json:28586 at 987cb596) names detector:regress/diff_diskimage_io.c and regress/gate_build.sh's warnings check, with cascade_20260829 as the measurement.]

> **So the human-facing file was right and the machine source of truth was wrong.**  Every other row in this sweep is stale the other way -- bug file present-tense over a closed row -- and `check_bugfile_sync.py` checks only the ledger->bugfile direction, so **neither direction of this pair is covered by anything.**

*Found by an Opus audit of the gate.  Recorded with the direction named, because a reader who learns 'the bug file goes stale' from the other twelve findings would draw exactly the wrong conclusion from this one.*

rows.title: The propagate script prints 'propagated' after a FAILED cp
rows.witness: harness:regress/artifacts/makercfalse/propagate_controls_20260830/ -- SIX checks in BOTH directions, sentinel CPGUARD_PASS.  The old idiom is reproduced and shown to announce success on a missing source; the shipped idiom is shown to report the failure AND to catch a case cp's exit status cannot see.
rows.note: Measured 2026-08-29 on my own tooling.  The build-tree propagate script does `cp "$SEC/$F" "$D/$F"` and then unconditionally `echo "  propagated"`.  When the path was wrong the log read:  *cp: cannot stat '...': No such file or directory*  immediately followed by  *propagated*.  **That is a CLAIM OF ACTION printed at the exact moment of the failure**, the same shape as `panel.sh` printing *'re-firing once'* while re-firing nothing -- which this carrier already names as worse than a stale citation, because it reassures the one person who could still fix it.  **THE SENTINEL DISCIPLINE CONTAINED IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.**  The two-part clearance reported `part 1 source cmps clean: NO` and KEPT the sentinel, so the tree was marked untrustworthy rather than silently wrong.  The false line cost confusion, not a wrong measurement.  FIXED in the rewritten script (`cp ... || { echo 'cp FAILED'; continue; }`), but the ORIGINAL at the #490 script still carries it, and any future copy inherits it.  *Root cause worth naming: the bad script was GENERATED FROM ANOTHER SCRIPT BY CHAINED `sed`, which produced `src/devices/disk/diskimage.c` from `src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c`.  Generating a script by regex is the same class as substituting a grep for a parser -- it produces something that runs and is wrong.*

entries.note: The script the row named was a scratch tool and no longer exists, so closing on its absence would have been closing on a technicality.  **The CLASS is what mattered, and the current instance was checked instead** -- `propagate494.sh`, written today and run twice, which verifies the copy with `cmp` against the intended source rather than announcing unconditionally.  *** THE CONTROL FOUND SOMETHING THE OBVIOUS FIX WOULD HAVE MISSED. ***  The natural repair is `cp ... || { echo failed; exit; }`.  That guards the case where cp FAILS -- and the control's third block shows **a cp of the WRONG file exits 0**, so an exit-status guard passes while the destination holds content that was never intended.  Only a comparison against the INTENDED source catches it, which is what the shipped form does.  So the fix is not merely present, it is stronger than the one the row asked for.  **Controlled in both directions**, because a check that only ever passes is the exact shape this row is about: the OLD idiom is reproduced and measured announcing `propagated` on a missing source, and the NEW one is measured failing there and passing on a real copy with the destination verified to have actually changed.  Kept from the original finding because it is the part that generalises: the sentinel discipline CONTAINED the failure -- the two-part clearance reported part 1 red and KEPT the sentinel, so the tree was marked untrustworthy rather than silently wrong.  **The false line cost confusion, not a wrong measurement.**  Same family as `panelrefire` (still open), where a script prints `re-firing once` and re-fires nothing.
