rows.title: diag_div_sweep.py reports line numbers that are systematically too small
rows.witness: harness:regress/artifacts/makercfalse/divsweep_controls_20260830/ -- BEFORE.txt and AFTER.txt from the same tool at the same HEAD, with the row COUNT pinned at 27 in both so the fix is shown to move WHERE sites are reported without changing WHICH are found.
rows.note: *** EVERY LINE NUMBER `diag_div_sweep.py` PRINTS IS TOO SMALL, AND `gate_hygiene.sh`'s OWN COMMENT CITES TWO OF THEM. *** MEASURED 2026-08-29: the sweep reports `dev_ns16550.c:79` for `115200 / d->divisor`, whose call really begins at **:180**; and `diskimage.c:543` for `bytes_left % ct->sector_size`, whose call really begins at **:976**.  *** THIS ROW FIRST SAID 181 AND 983.  THOSE ARE THE DIVISION LINES, NOT THE CALL-START LINES, and the sweep correctly reports the latter -- a call may span lines and the start is the sensible anchor.  Corrected after the scratch proof reported 180/976 and I checked WHICH SIDE was wrong instead of assuming the tool was. ***  It also reports `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:211 fatal`, where line 211 is PROSE inside a comment block. MECHANISM, read from the source rather than guessed: `strip_lits()` does NOT preserve offsets -- a string literal of any length becomes a single space, and a `/* ... */` block becomes a single space WITH ALL ITS NEWLINES DESTROYED.  The scan then runs over the stripped text while the line number is computed as `raw[:m.start()].count(chr(10))` -- an offset into the STRIPPED string indexed against the RAW one.  Since stripping only ever shortens, every reported line is too small, and the error grows with the size of the comment blocks above the site.  `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` carries 40-line comment blocks, which is why its site lands 400+ lines early, inside prose. *** THE COUNTS ARE UNAFFECTED AND THE RATCHET IS SOUND. ***  Match counting does not depend on line numbering, so `DIAG_DIV_TOTAL=21` and `DIAG_DIV_NONCONST=2` are correct, and both non-constant sites are correctly IDENTIFIED by file and expression.  Only their CITATIONS are false.  This is a records defect, not a coverage one. **WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY:** the wrong numbers did not stay in the tool. They were transcribed into `gate_hygiene.sh`'s rationale comment, where a future round reads them as the authoritative location of the two sites the ratchet exists to protect -- and this project's citation-form rule exists precisely because a drifted number is consumed by a reader who then opens the wrong place. FOUND BY CHASING A REFUTED SEAT CLAIM: agy attributed the 24->21 drop to '#490 consolidating 4 fatal() calls into 1 at dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:211'.  Checking it showed #490 removed ZERO fatal lines containing a division and that :211 is a comment -- so the claim was false, but the line number it rested on was the tool's, not the seat's.  *A seat's wrong answer led straight to a real defect in the tool that supplied its premise.* REMEDY: make `strip_lits` length-preserving -- replace each removed character with a space and each removed newline with a newline -- so stripped offsets index the raw text correctly.  That is the standard fix and it makes the two texts positionally identical.  Then re-derive the two citations in gate_hygiene.sh's comment.  Owes a control: the known sites must report 181 and 983.  *** REMEDY PROVEN IN SCRATCH, 2026-08-29, before any tree was touched. ***  A length-preserving `strip_lits` (one space per consumed character, newlines preserved) moves the two citations from 79 -> 180 and 543 -> 976, the true call-start lines, while DIAG_DIV_TOTAL stays 21 and DIAG_DIV_NONCONST stays 2 -- so it is a pure CITATION repair with no behavioural change, which is the property that makes it safe.  The proof harness itself failed twice first and both failures were apparatus: the scratch copy resolves ROOT from its own location and scanned an empty directory (reporting 0 sites -- the phantom-absence shape), and a `re.sub` replacement ate the backslashes in the override path.  Both were caught because the control demanded specific numbers rather than merely 'different'.  *** AND THE SURROUNDING STORY WAS WRONG TOO, MEASURED BY THE fable5 SEAT. ***  I recorded the class ratchet's 24 -> 21 as 'three sites legitimately REMOVED'.  It is a CONSOLIDATION: the pre-#462 tree carried FOUR one-division `fatal("  %08x", (int) d->dma_reg[N / sizeof(uint32_t)])` calls, and HEAD carries the SAME FOUR DIVISIONS as arguments of ONE fatal().  **No instance of the class was removed at all** -- `DIAG_DIV_TOTAL` counts CALLS carrying at least one division, so merging four calls into one moves the total while the division census is unchanged.  A round acting on my version would have gone looking for three removals that never happened.  ATTRIBUTION SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY VOTE: the two Agent seats DISAGREED -- opus5 said `fb0cc78` (#490), fable5 said `7c9dd9e` (#462).  `git show <sha> -- src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c | grep -c dma_reg` gives **9 for 7c9dd9e and 0 for fb0cc78**, so fable5 is right.  One command, no tally.

entries.note: *** REFUTED THE ONE THING I TOLD THE PANEL I COULD NOT FIND. ***  My Q3b said there was no mechanical discriminator between 'drives a pty' and 'simulates a stream'.  It is `pty.fork`, TWELVE LINES ABOVE in the same gate, already the census basis at `:162`.  MEASURED: scoping `probe_code()` to files containing it takes `whole_full` 4 -> 2 with `conv_anchor`/`conv_echo`/`conv_mark` all UNCHANGED at 23 -- **row 3 goes green with no pin moved, no allowlist widened and no filename exemption**, and it subsumes the existing `readiness_predicate_test.py` exemption automatically.  It also showed my proposed exclusion is the shape the gate itself REJECTS: `:92-95` and `:347-348` require an exemption to travel WITH a content pin on the excluded file -- *'an allowlist entry that checks what it exempts'* -- and I proposed it bare.  *** AND IT MEASURED MY ROW-5 FLOOR VACUOUS. ***  A kill table: under `>= 12`, deleting ONE latch's two-line guard pair PASSES (raw 13), restoring the exact unbounded flood #464 fixed; and gutting a guard while naming the latch twice in a COMMENT also passes (raw 15).  Six per-latch `>= 2` rows are ALSO inadequate -- satisfied by two reads and no set, while the row's label claims 'one set + one read each'.  Its shape: TWO rows over comment-stripped code, `SET_OK == 6` and `READ_OK == 6`, measured 6/6 at HEAD, killing both mutants and scoring 0/6 on a null medium (floor clause (c)).  *** THREE FINDINGS LARGER THAN THE FIVE REDS. ***  (F1) the sweep's line bug -- which I had found independently the same hour, and its measured fix agrees with mine EXACTLY: 79 -> 180, 543 -> 976, counts unchanged.  (F2) **`regress/artifacts/` is in scope for TWO censuses and out for a THIRD** -- `py_code`/`probe_code` recurse (137 files) while `_ptylist` uses a FLAT glob (59), which is evasion route #3 that this gate condemns ninety lines earlier.  TEN pty-forking promptless probes live under `artifacts/` and are invisible to the entire mechanism built to find promptless pty probes -- and the hazard is SCHEDULED in the other direction: `CLAUDE.md` MANDATES frozen probe copies, so the next round that freezes a converted probe reds this gate FOR DOING THE RIGHT THING.  (F3) the wdcflood pin counts a comment.  Verdict: THREE rounds, not one.  Honest about its own apparatus: its first census returned 9/9 from a loose grep and it corrected itself to 3/8; its first comment-strip returned 0 for every latch (a phantom absence) because gcc and python3 are stubbed in git-bash, and it re-ran under WSL.

*** CAUGHT THAT I DROPPED A RED, AND THE DROPPED ONE DEFEATS THE ROUND'S OWN MOTIVATION. ***  It is SIX reds, not five: the brief omits `asic_badaddr rows run got=14 want=13`, **which my own note file had already dispositioned as its item 5**.  A round fixing 'the five' leaves gate_sh_rounding red and the battery REGRESS_FAIL, so 'get the battery green' fails entirely on the dropped row.  It named this as my own third-listed error class recurring inside the brief that warns about it -- and noted the note file itself gives three different counts ('four ratchet reds' / 'six FAIL rows' / 'five of the seven') in one document, so the round owes ONE derived count with its deriver.  *** MEASURED CLAIM 4 FALSE: the 24 -> 21 drop is a CONSOLIDATION, not removals. ***  Four one-division fatal() calls became ONE fatal() carrying the same four divisions; `DIAG_DIV_TOTAL` counts CALLS.  Attribution `7c9dd9e` (#462) -- and opus5 said `fb0cc78` (#490); settled by `git show ... | grep -c dma_reg` giving 9 vs 0, so fable5 is right.  It found the sweep's line-number defect on the way and correctly filed rather than fixed it, per the stopping rule.  A2 UPHELD THE OWNER'S PRIORITISATION with a concrete warrant: this very run proves the cost, because a REAL regression (#491's sign-compare pair) sat in the same FAIL list as six bookkeeping reds -- under red-is-normal the next real regression is invisible.  A3 REFUTED MY ESTIMATE'S PROXY AS VINTAGE-BIASED: 'witness names an artifact kind' marks 45/86, 'row has commits' marks 64/86 -- 52% vs 74% -- and the 21-row disagreement is real emulator fixes predating 2026-08-19, when the witness field became mandatory.  **The proxy bins a third of the sample by VINTAGE, not substance.**  Report a RANGE (~60-120) with a per-row deriver (did the row's commits touch `src/`?), and note documented-only rows are not free -- each owes a rung-3 attempt, a panel and records.  A4: a cheap commit-time check DOES exist for 5 of the 6, because the class splits -- five are STATIC source greps needing no boot, so a `--static` gate mode invoked from precommit would have caught them at their offending commits (#462, #467/8, #484/5, #489, #490).  The two runtime row-count pins genuinely need probe execution and stay weekly.  It insists this ships as ITS OWN controlled harness round, not a rider.

*** THE SHARPEST OF THE SCRIPTABLE SEATS. ***  'Do not raise #3 to 4, and do not convert #5 to a total floor; Q1/Q2 are legitimate census updates; Q4 is a net re-pin with a more specific history than claimed.'  Both prohibitions were independently correct and both were followed.

Found the defect the F2 repair MISSED: `_ptylist` still used a FLAT GLOB after py_code and probe_code were converted, so the round aligned TWO populations of three -- the exact defect F2 exists to end.  It agrees today only by coincidence (recursive-minus-artifacts == flat), and a .py in any NEW non-artifacts subdirectory would be seen by two censuses and missed by the third.  Also caught the census comment reading as a PARTITION when its categories overlap.

Ruled for one round, and gave the disposition that kept the row-3 population HONEST rather than merely wider: 'Do not add the subprocess constructors to this population: they cannot carry the #392 failure.  Do not treat the alternation as a guest-process census.'  That is the reasoning recorded in the shipped comment beside codex's opposing finding, rather than one seat's view being adopted silently.  Also: 'drive_guest.py as a third rationale is right -- do not fold it into budget-drain', and on C1 'equality is right here; the members set of THIS PIN does not grow -- the device's warned_ set already did.'

Reached opus5's three-part structure INDEPENDENTLY and by a different route, and its reason is the one the adjudicator finally absorbed: 'B and C change what the gate *proves*, not just its numbers; the panel should be asked to sign off on those two explicitly, separately from A.'  fable5 credited it and applied it at PASS structure rather than ROUND structure -- the sign-off unit is the brief section a seat answers, not the commit boundary.  It also found the two-route growth (site reuse #484, prose #485) on its own.

Caught the ARITHMETIC: the new three-way census was 'arithmetically impossible as printed (3+8+1=12 against every set size the packet names)'.  It was right, and the repair it forced -- a per-member reason rather than a 'dominant' one -- was then itself wrong twice more before landing.  Also flagged the asic pin as carrying no inlined justification.

'Claim 3's proposed file exclusion is a hole and its real-instances argument is false.'  Correct on both halves: the exclusion was the shape the gate itself rejects, and the tripwire I claimed for it was a COUNT-red, not a NAME-red -- and count-reds get re-pinned routinely, which this very round does six times.  fable5 cited that concession as half its reason for overturning its own row-3 form.

'Three real defects need settling before commit, plus one soft concern.'  Its asic finding is quoted in the shipped comment: 'Zero rationale in the diff.  Just a number bump.  The other three re-pins carry paragraphs of reasoning; this one is silent.'  A silent bump is indistinguishable from fitting the pin to the output, which is why the provenance now ships with it.

entries.note: *** MEASURED AN L2 FLOOR BREACH IN THE DETECTOR THIS ROUND SHIPPED, and it was reviewing its OWN pass-1 design (badge A, disclosed). ***  Every mutant in my kill table targeted a SINGLE-SITE latch, so the table was clean on a population that structurally could not exhibit the defect.  `warned_inbuf_overrun` has TWO sites; neutralising EITHER ONE leaves the other to satisfy presence -- `if (1) {` at one site scores 6/6 GREEN while the producer flood is unbounded again, which is #464's exact defect.  Floor clause (b) demands failure on reinstatement at EVERY fixed site.  Five escapes, smallest ONE TOKEN.  It also named the inversion that is the lesson: the old pin counted OCCURRENCES so a second site moved it -- loud and wrong but alive; presence-only made losing one of two INVISIBLE.  Its measured fix (per-latch set==read, plus a latch-population count) is what shipped. Further: the `//` C99 line-continuation defect in strip_comments, WITH the coupling that the obvious fix reintroduces `divsweeplines` in the branch being fixed (2 lines -> 1, invisible to a length check, visible only to a LINE count); the unanchored READ substring (E8: `!d->warned_nonbyte_read_hi` satisfied the nonbyte_read row); the dead filename exemption still inside pty_driving(); a bare xargs where both neighbours use -print0; and the absence of a clause-(e) CONTRACT, with the measured reason it matters (E4: widening a predicate while its text survives escapes every textual census).

entries.note: *** FOUND AN L1 IN MY KILL TABLE FROM THE PUBLISHED NUMBERS ALONE. ***  'M1's sed matched nothing (the real guard is split across lines); only the set-deletion fired.  The score was the tell: a true pair deletion reads 5/5, and the table shows 5/6.'  Both M1 and M2 were MISLABELLED -- my vac() guard caught only TOTAL no-ops, so a partially-applied mutant scored as the thing it was not.  Rebuilt with per-pattern presence checks; M1 now reads exactly 5/5/5/11 as predicted.  *** AND MY REPLACEMENT CHECK REPEATED THE ROUND'S OWN DEFECT: it used `grep -c`, which counts LINES, so it demanded two LINES when the mutant put both mentions on one. ***  Also: my C1 deriver produced 3 (it matched only the gate-level rollups) where the sed-range form gives 8; the '-> 9' command as written yields 11 (9 is the changed-lines form); the HARD ORDERING it mandated did not hold in LETTER (before.out already shows rows 1/2 re-pinned) though the intent survives on two measured facts; the A/B/C separation is real at the question layer and COSMETIC at the recording layer, because one verdict line per seat lets a global RATIFY score as ratifying all three; and 'FILED' was a WRONG RECORD until the row existed.

*** THE DEFECT HAD TWO HALVES AND FIXING EITHER ALONE LOOKS LIKE A PARTIAL IMPROVEMENT RATHER THAN A REMAINING BUG -- which is what makes the shape worth recording. ***  **(1)** `strip_lits()` collapsed a whole `/* ... */` block to a SINGLE SPACE, destroying every newline inside it, so each comment shifted every later line number down.  **(2)** the line number was then counted in `raw` using an offset from `src` -- `m` matches the STRIPPED text, so `m.start()` is a src offset, and indexing raw with it mixes two coordinate systems.  Fixing only (1) moved a measured case from `:79` to `:80` when the truth was `:180`.  **A one-line improvement that still reads as broken is easy to mistake for the fix not working, rather than for a second cause.**  MEASURED, same tool, same HEAD, before and after:  `dev_ns16550.c` 79 -> **180** (the call the division sits in starts at 180; the division itself is at 181, and the sweep correctly anchors on the call start).  `diskimage.c` 543 -> **976** (division at 983).  `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` 211 -> **1383**: 211 was PROSE INSIDE A COMMENT BLOCK -- the drift was large enough to land the anchor inside the very construct being stripped -- and 1383 is a real `fatal("[ dreamcast_gdrom_dma: DMA start with dst"`.  **DENOMINATOR, because a spot-check of three proves nothing about 27:** all 21 parseable rows now point at code and **ZERO land inside a comment**.  The row count is 27 before and after, so the fix changed where sites are reported without changing which are found.  *** THE SAME CAUSE, THE SAME REPAIR, AND THE SECOND INSTANCE THIS WEEK. ***  `wdc_latch_census.py` hit it earlier the same day and its `_blank()` preserves newlines.  **Two tools, one week, one cause: a stripper written for CONTENT and then used for POSITION.**  A replacement need not preserve length -- columns are not reported -- but it must preserve the NEWLINE COUNT, because that is the only thing carrying the line number.  Both fixes now say so in their own comments.  `gate_hygiene.sh`'s comment cites two of the OLD numbers and is now stale; left for a round that touches that file, since editing a gate is not a records change.

rows.title: The class ratchet is an equality; should it be a band?
rows.witness: none
rows.note: *** FILED BECAUSE `gate_hygiene.sh` SAYS IT IS FILED.  A comment reading 'FILED, not taken here' with no row behind it is the gap-closes-itself shape, and fable5 caught exactly that on pass 2. ***  `DIAG_DIV_TOTAL` is pinned by EQUALITY.  A seat argued for a FLOOR: an equality breaks on every legitimate de-fatalisation, and de-fatalisation is this fork's whole queue.  The re-pin round declined to convert it, because that changes what the check PROVES and must not ride inside a re-pin.  *** THE ADJUDICATOR THEN REFUTED BOTH SIMPLE DIRECTIONS, which is why this is a design question and not a deferred chore. ***  A CEILING lets the sweep rot silently -- a total drifting DOWN to 0 would pass, the vacuous-green shape this denominator exists to catch.  A FLOOR >= 21 reds on every legitimate de-fatalisation exactly as the equality does, so it purchases nothing.  The equality's break on each de-fatalisation is a FORCED-ACKNOWLEDGMENT FEATURE, now priced correctly by the DOWN-direction instruction this round added: the NUMERATOR is the discriminator, and the site list is diffed at FILE granularity because the printed line numbers are wrong (see `divsweeplines`).  WHAT TO WEIGH WHEN IT IS TAKEN: a two-sided BAND, or equality-with-ritual. Both are semantic changes; neither may ride a re-pin.

rows.title: A round can ship without writing back, and no gate can see it
rows.witness: none
rows.note: *** MEASURED 2026-08-29: a complete pass-1 brief was written and NINE SEATS FIRED to redo work that had shipped two days earlier as #479/#480/#481/#482. ***  Three dev_wdc.c rows carried a full 9/9 RESEARCH stage; the work shipped under four commit numbers; ZERO entries landed back on the rows; the ledger froze at 'in work'; and the main loop, correctly treating the ledger as the queue, drafted a fresh brief.  The brief's own 'mandatory' mutant was already in the preserved kill table, KILLED.  **The CHANGELOG knew -- its Round 479 block names all three row ids -- and the ledger did not.**  *** THE EXISTING GATES ARE BLIND TO THIS BY CONSTRUCTION. ***  precommit section H reads LEDGER ENTRIES and SKIPS STAGES THAT NEVER STARTED; the implement and review stages never started on those rows.  So a round that ships without writing back cannot be seen by the check built to notice missing panel coverage.  This is the unread-review class one step worse: an unrecorded ROUND.  TAKEN ALREADY (2026-08-29): a §C0 block in BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md -- two commands, `git log -1 -- <file>` and `grep <rowid> CHANGELOG.md`, pasted into the brief's settled premises.  It lives in the TEMPLATE because the carrier's own finding is that the one piece of prose which demonstrably fires is the one in the artifact present at the moment of decision.  FILED HERE, NOT BUILT: a checker warning when a row id named in a CHANGELOG round block is still 'in work' with no post-ship entry.  Existence-only, forward-only from a cutoff, owing two negative controls (a staged unrecorded round must warn; a properly-closed row must not).  **It changes what every commit must pass, so it is an owner decision rather than a round's** -- and this project has measured that a checker policing a minority of a class while alarming on prose gets switched off, so the population it would fire on should be counted before it is written.

entries.note: *** CONFIRMED THE GHOST ROUND AND THEN FOUND A LIVE HIGH-SEVERITY DEFECT THE PANEL WAS NOT CONVENED FOR. ***  Settled the premise by `git log -S'wdc_new_command_reset'`, quoted the shipped helper verbatim, and named both preserved kill tables (13/13 and 10/10).  Then MEASURED nine mutants in a scratch tree at 128 rows baseline: SEVEN KILLED including the per-SITE partial resets (`MdAltRingOnly`, `MdAltWipOnly`, `MdAltNoRing` -- the ALT-CTRL site resetting a strict subset) and `MdNoFlag`, which drops `atapi_cmd_in_progress`, **a fourth tenant NEITHER shipped table enumerates**, and still dies 6 red.  TWO ESCAPED AND IT PROVED THEM EQUIVALENT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT: a positional differential showed `MdRingDrain`/`MdRingRewind` leave head/tail at 777 vs 0 while occupancy, capacity and readback are byte-identical -- the inbuf is a correct circular buffer, so position is unobservable.  **It then drew the consequence against the anchor rule: clause (f)'s reviewer check answers NONE for the ring and that is CORRECT here, because nothing in the device can observe the shift; an anchored ring row would be the addition licence's 'it cannot hurt'.**  THE FINDING THAT BECAME A ROW: `#481` widened offset-1 aliasing from a harmless signature latch into a FULL SOFT RESET.  `DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus)` reads `relative_addr` ZERO times over a TWO-BYTE region, so a guest write to `0x3f7` -- the READ-ONLY Drive Address Register -- aborts a live ATA write and purges 40 queued bytes.  **#481's OWN committed artifact already measured it at rung 3** and no row carried it.  Filed as `wdcaltoffset`, sev=high.  Also: the kill drivers score a CRASH as a result -- `build_run` checks the COMPILE status, then runs the mutant and greps FAIL lines without reading the run's exit status or the `WDC_IDENTIFY_PASS` sentinel, so a mutant that dies partway is scored by how far it got.  Not hypothetical here: `write_in_progress` and `write_count` are set together and CLEARED AT DIFFERENT SITES, and the drain guard divides by `512 * d->write_count` -- an operand swap leaving the flag while zeroing the count is a SIGFPE.  **It disclosed its own violation**: wrote one file into the tree against instruction, removed it, and verified `git status` and the `dev_wdc.c` md5 afterwards.

*** RULED THE ROUND ALREADY RAN, AND RULED AGAINST ITS OWN RECOMMENDATION IN THE SAME ANSWER. ***  Reconstructed the chronology from the repo: the 10:36 matrix, then `#479` at 12:18 shipping F-narrow, `#480`'s L2 call-site fix, `#481` closing the ALT-CTRL gap, `#482` splitting the joint row into four one-tenant rows.  A3: **the standing RED row it had itself recommended is DEAD** -- '`a permanently red row is the dual of this project's check-that-cannot-fail -- a check that cannot PASS`', and it violates the blanks rule since a deliberate red and a regression red render identically.  `#481` closed the gap instead, which is better.  It gave the disclosure ladder in order: close the gap; else an accept/tripwire row pinning today's behaviour GREEN; else prose plus a FILED item.  A2: **corrected MY premise** -- `#492` did NOT touch `dev_wdc.c` (`git show d9efd33 -- src/devices/dev_wdc.c` is empty); it touched a checker.  It then checked the interaction precisely and found the two detectors cover DISJOINT mutant classes, so both are needed.  A5: the witness string is defective THREE ways -- a stale count, `probe:` where `detector:` was adopted for exactly this shape (the mis-scoring `check_witness.py`'s own header calls laundering), and the rung-3 accept probe owed its own clause.  It required PER-ROW CARRIER NAMING or three closures are mutually indistinguishable, which is the overtaken-row rule's condition 2 unmet.  It named the structural remedy that was adopted: a BRIEF_TEMPLATE settled-premise line, because the carrier's own finding is that the prose which fires is the prose in the artifact present at the moment of decision.

Caught it independently while grepping the ledger, and surfaced `wdcaltwidth` -- an OPEN row with ZERO entries about the alt-ctrl register's access width -- which is what made me check whether the 'ALT-CTRL gap' was already filed under another name.  That check is what kept the round from filing one defect twice.  Its wall grep flagged it as walled and it was a FALSE POSITIVE: every match was codex QUOTING ledger rows whose notes record old seat-wall history.

Caught it, and corrected a SECOND premise of mine in the same breath: **'Two rounds have shipped since' is false as a bound** -- after the matrix came #479, #480, #481, #482 and more.  It opened by pinning session start to HEAD `d9efd33` before answering anything.

Caught it, and its reasoning is visible in the transcript as it happens: 'the fix `wdc_new_command_reset()` is ALREADY IN THE TREE -- this is #479/#480/#481 ... So the tree ALREADY contains the fix?  That would mean this round's work is already done.'
Caught it, treating F-narrow as 'the historical Pass 1 context (#479)' rather than as a live proposal.

*** COULD NOT CATCH THE GHOST ROUND, AND THAT IS NOT A SEAT FAILURE. ***  A ghost round is a REPO FACT, and a packet-fed seat can only know what the brief inlines -- the brief asserted 'PASS 1, before any edit' and it could not check that.  Recording this as a failure would be exactly the conflation the pipeline doctrine forbids.
As glm: structurally unable to settle a repo fact from a packet.  Its answer is about the design as briefed, and is sound on that scope.

As glm and deepseek.  **The three packet-fed seats failing to catch this, while all four file-reading seats caught it, is the FILE-READING vs PACKET-FED distinction confirmed by measurement rather than asserted** -- and it is the clearest instance this project has recorded.

rows.title: wdc alt-ctrl: a guest write to the READ-ONLY Drive Address Register aborts a live transfer and purges the ring
rows.witness: probe:regress/artifacts/wdcaltoffset/witness_20260829/ -- RUNG 3 on unmodified `evbmips -e malta`, reached through the machine's own committed piix4_ide path with no device_add, free-running, with BOTH controls (RAM liveness through identical instruction shapes, and a device signature: two reads of one address returning push order, which a memory cell cannot do).  Sentinel ALTOFF_DONE.  The SHIPPED fix was then re-measured against it at 18 rows, both legs, 36 of 36 predictions -- killtable_20260830/RESULTS_detector18.txt, sentinel ALTOFF_DET_DONE.  (RESULTS_shipped.txt is the 15-row witness at 30/30 and must not be cited for 36/36; a seat caught that citation error from the log itself.)
rows.note:
*** LIVE IN THE SHIPPED TREE, MEASURED AT RUNG 3, AND ITS WITNESS WAS ALREADY COMMITTED -- by `#481`, the round that made it worse. ***  Found by the opus5 seat on a panel convened for an unrelated (and already shipped) round; every element re-verified before filing.  `DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus)` **never reads `relative_addr`** -- measured, ZERO uses in the handler -- while the region is registered TWO BYTES WIDE.  Offset 0 is Device Control (`0x3f6`).  **Offset 1 is the Drive Address Register (`0x3f7`), which is READ-ONLY on real ATA hardware** and on many platforms is shared with the floppy controller.  So the handler cannot distinguish a write to a writable control register from a write to a read-only one, and treats both identically.  *** `#481` WIDENED THE CONSEQUENCE FROM HARMLESS TO DESTRUCTIVE. ***  Before it, the arm tested `WDCTL_4BIT`, so a `0x06` write did nothing at either offset -- the aliasing existed but was a harmless signature latch.  `#481` corrected the bit to `WDCTL_RST` and wired in `wdc_new_command_reset()`, which was RIGHT for offset 0 and turned offset 1 into a full soft reset.  Measured, same scenario on both builds (a live `WDCC_WRITE` with 40 bytes queued, then a one-byte `0x06` write):  pre-#481 (`867c697^`) offset 1 -> `cur_command 0x30  wip 0x30  occ 40` (untouched); HEAD offset 1 -> `cur_command 0x100  wip 0x0  occ 0` -- **the live ATA write is aborted and 40 queued guest bytes are purged**.  AND THE RUNG-3 WITNESS IS ALREADY IN THE TREE, committed by #481 itself at `.../rung3_witness/rung3_offset.txt`: a guest writing 0x06 to `0x180003f7` leaves `cyl=0x6655` unchanged pre-fix and `cyl=0xeb14` after.  *** SO A MEASUREMENT EXISTS, IS PRESERVED AT A DURABLE PATH, AND NO ROW CARRIED IT -- the unread-review class one level down, on a LIVE defect. ***  `wdcaltwidth` CANNOT ABSORB THIS and must not be used to: it is about access WIDTH (`len == 1` rows against a 2-byte region) and carries witness `none -- filed from a reading of the registration, no measurement yet`.  **Width and offset DECODE are different claims**, and merging them would be the queue-id-covering-two-defects shape that closing one buries the other.  SEVERITY: `high` and set deliberately -- this is guest-reachable, needs no harness, destroys queued guest data, and the register it fires on is one a correct guest may legitimately WRITE to expecting nothing to happen.  Note the fix is NOT to revert `#481`, which corrected a real bit error; it is to make the handler decode its offset.  *** CORRECTION 2026-08-30 (L4), AGAINST THIS NOTE'S OWN WORDS, BY THE opus5 SEAT'S PREMISE AUDIT. ***  The sentence above calls the pre-`#481` aliasing `a harmless signature latch`.  **That is true of the witness's value and false as a characterisation.**  Pre-`#481` the arm was `if (idata & WDCTL_4BIT) d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET;` -- and `WDCTL_4BIT` (0x08) is libata's STEADY-STATE `ap->ctl`, as `#481`'s own comment records.  So a store to offset 1 carrying the common case already clobbered `cur_command` and latched a bogus ATAPI signature.  The witness value 0x06 is `WDCTL_RST|WDCTL_IDS` and has bit 3 CLEAR, so for 0x06 specifically the claim holds -- **which is exactly the dropped-qualifier class: a property measured on one value, restated as a property of the arm.**  What `#481` changed is WHICH bit triggers it and it ADDED the ring purge; severity rose, but `harmless` never obtained.  Note this is the same channel m3 escapes on, which is why a signature row could measure it at all.

*** 2026-09-11: `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` STILL CARRIES AN `### OPEN` BLOCK FOR THIS ROW, WHICH IS CLOSED HERE WITH TWO COMMITS AND A RUNG-3 WITNESS.  **THE BUG FILE IS THE STALE SIDE.** ***

Checked rather than assumed, because when two records disagree the question is WHICH ONE IS BROKEN: this row is `closed`, sev `high`, commits `3521a22 c125450`, witness `probe:regress/artifacts/wdcaltoffset/witness_20260829/` -- rung 3 on unmodified `evbmips -e malta`, free-running, with BOTH controls and sentinel `ALTOFF_DONE`.  **The closure is sound; the human queue is wrong.**

**WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TIDY-UP: a fresh session reading the human queue today is told a sev-HIGH, guest-reachable, witness-in-hand wdc defect is OPEN.**  The bug file's own charter says *"Only genuinely OPEN items live here.  Resolved ones are removed, not annotated."*

**SEVEN ROWS ARE IN THIS STATE**, and the other six were checked the same way: `wdcringambig` (commit `cf300c0`), `wdchpcmipsaddr` (ASSESSED-NOT-CHANGED), and `divsweeplines`, `propagatecpsilent`, `hookctlgate`, `hookdurability`.  **The last four have NO commits -- which is exactly what a wrongly-closed row looks like, so I opened them rather than assuming.  All four carry a `harness:` witness naming a PRESERVED control artifact** (`regress/artifacts/makercfalse/divsweep_controls_20260830/`, `.../propagate_controls_20260830/`, `.../hook_controls_20260829/`), each with a sentinel and each negative-controlled in both directions.  **They are harness rounds whose deliverable is a control measurement, not a commit.  Legitimately closed.**

*The checker cannot see this class: `check_bugfile_sync.py` verifies that every OPEN ledger row is findable in the bug file, and its header asserts "the reverse direction is already clean".  That is a DIFFERENT claim -- every bug-file header has a ledger row -- not this one, which is that no bug-file OPEN header names a CLOSED row.  A check that verifies one direction while its comment claims both is the check-that-cannot-fail family's cousin.*

entries.note: *** RUNG-3 WITNESS BUILT, DURABLE AND RE-RUNNABLE -- the first this defect has ever had. ***  Its two prior measurements could not be re-run: `#481` preserved 201 bytes of OUTPUT with no driver, and a later HEAD measurement lived in a /tmp tree its own script deleted.  **VERDICT: `On the COMMITTED build phase 1 and phase 2 are BYTE-IDENTICAL`** -- a guest store to `0x3f6` (Device Control) and to `0x3f7` (Drive Address Register, READ-ONLY on real ATA hardware) produce identical results.  On the fix leg they separate.  30 of 30 row predictions; encodings 122/122 and 122/122; both legs parked.  BOTH LADDER CONTROLS, several times over and green on BOTH legs: LIVENESS -- a RAM round-trip (0x55) and a cyl readback (0x6655, reusing #481's own idiom), plus a DRQ-armed check per phase; DEVICE-SIGNATURE -- the data port reading as a FIFO (0x5a then 0xa5, so not a memory cell) and a status byte the DEVICE computes (0x51).  RAM would answer differently to every one.  **EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: the READ path is untouched, so the ONLY variable between the two legs is the aliased STORE.**  *** THE FIX LEG IS LABELLED `WITNESS FIX LEG ONLY -- NOT a proposed shipped fix`, and that distinction is kept. ***  It exists to prove the witness DISCRIMINATES, not to pre-decide the design; what the shipped fix should be is the panel's question.  The leg declines the store at offset 1 with a diagnostic and leaves the read path alone.

*** FOUND THE FACT THAT REFUTED THE ADJUDICATOR, and found it from the other side of the collision. ***  Read `wdcreg.h` and saw that `wd_digin` sits inside `#if 0 /* NOT MAPPED; fd uses this register on PCs */` -- so the header defines ONE aux register, not two.  Then pinned the counterpart: `dev_fdc.c:49` is `#define DEV_FDC_LENGTH 6 /*  TODO 8, but collision with wdc  */`, with fdc registered at `isa_portbase + 0x3f0` -- **so the tree documents the same collision from BOTH devices, and the wdc's 2-byte registration is exactly what blocks fdc from its own stated TODO of 8 ports.**  Ruled KEEP the 2-byte region THIS round and decode the write: shrinking to 1 byte makes `0x3f7` unmapped and changes device OWNERSHIP rather than repairing the measured store alias, on four platform layouts the witness covers none of.  **Named the escape mutant precisely: `relative_addr != 0` -> `relative_addr > 1`, which over a 2-byte region is NEVER TRUE, so the decline never fires -- P1 green (offset 0 was never declined), P3 green (offset 1 without RST never reset), P2 REOPENS.  That is the exact mutant proving P1+P3 do not pin the decode.**  Corrected my premise about the sibling row: `wdcaltwidth` is NOT 'exactly this registration' -- its filed escape is transaction width (`data[0]` vs `data[len-1]`), and a 1-byte registration would close the width question BY TOPOLOGY rather than prove the topology correct.  Keep the rows distinct.  Refused to fix the read under this witness on stated grounds: bit 7 high-impedance, write-gate representation and active-low drive/head selection are decisions the witness does not cover.  Declared plainly: no gate, battery or harness script run.

*** INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE `#if 0`, AND OPENED BY RE-DERIVING EVERY BRIEF PREMISE INTO A TABLE OF TRUE/OVERSTATED/FALSE RATHER THAN ANSWERING THE QUESTIONS. ***  Its table is the round's best premise audit: handler never reads `relative_addr` **True** (verified `relative_addr` appears only in `DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc)`); region length 2 **True**; offset 1 = ATA Drive Address **'True as a PC port identity, OVERSTATED as a model obligation'** -- the same port is floppy DIR on read and floppy CCR on write, and the tree's own `wdcreg.h` does not map it; ACCEPT applies **'It does not -- the model does not compute a right write result and then drop it, it performs a soft reset'**; `wdcaltwidth` can absorb this **'It cannot'**.  **Caught the vacuity that mattered: P3 is GREEN ON BOTH LEGS, so it does not kill the defect** -- it is a control, and the brief's row table invited reading it as coverage.  Also flagged that the two unbuilt mutants are 'reasoned only' and are FLOOR WORK, not optional.  Verified the witness numbers against `RESULTS.txt` and the `ALTOFF_DONE` sentinel rather than trusting the brief's transcription.

*** SUPPLIED THE ONE FACT THAT MAKES THE READ SIDE FIXABLE IN PRINCIPLE, and it was verified exactly: `dev_wdc.c` `case wd_sdh` LATCHES drive and head *** (`d->sectorsize`, `d->lba`, `d->drive`, `d->head` all set from the stored byte at :1777-1780).  So the device does hold the raw material a correct offset-1 read would need.  Read as CONTRADICTING the adjudicator's 'ACCEPT is structurally unavailable' and adjudicated as NOT contradicting it: the adjudicator ruled on the STORE (where there is no discarded right answer), kimi is describing the READ.  Different questions, both right.  It wanted the read arm decided in the same edit; codex's refusal is better warranted (the read owes an ORACLE the tree cannot supply), so the read files separately.  Did NOT find the `#if 0`.

Answered the question set and endorsed the silent-decline shape, quoting the exact diagnostic text it wanted shipped (`debug("[ wdc: write to DRIVE ADDRESS (read-only): 0x%02x, ignored ]\n", ...)`).  **Did NOT find the `#if 0`** despite being a file-reading seat with the tree available -- recorded plainly, because two of four file-reading seats missing the discriminating fact is the measurement, not a footnote.

Did not ratify.  Its lead finding is METHODOLOGICAL and lands: **'premise 3's option set is invoked outside its settled domain with its own required grep unreported'** -- the four-member de-fatalisation option set carries an obligation to grep the fork for the existing idiom BEFORE choosing, and the brief invoked the rule while reporting no census.  That is a real defect in my brief and it is the same shape the carrier already records (a rule cited by the person not applying it).  Also caught that the brief's SS-E blind-spot list claims completeness while omitting non-status effects.  **Could not settle the `#if 0` -- it is a repo fact and the brief did not inline `wdcreg.h`.  That is a BRIEF defect, not a seat failure.**

'No fatal defect found in the inlined reasoning, but several premises are not checkable from the packet and Q1/Q3 remain open.'  **The honest form** -- it named what it could not settle instead of guessing, which is exactly what the packet preamble asks for.  Its clause-(b) reasoning about the single fixed site is sound on the scope it had.

Agreed the defect and witness are sound, and identified Q2 (read) and Q3 (width) as gaps that must be resolved before pass 2 -- which matches where the file-reading seats landed.  Named the bit definitions as the premise it could not settle from the packet.  Also noted the SSC0 ghost-round check is 'exactly the guard' the previous failure needed.

*** ADJUDICATION 1 of 2.  ITS DISPOSITION SURVIVED AND ITS CENTRAL WARRANT DID NOT -- recorded here WITH the refutation rather than replaced, so no future round transfers a dead warrant. ***  Ruled (a) FIX THE STORE ONLY, and rejected option (c) on this warrant: *'the tree's own bundled header defines TWO registers in the aux region, so width 2 is a correct registration'*, citing `wd_digin`.  **REFUTED.**  `src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h` puts that define inside `#if 0 /* NOT MAPPED; fd uses this register on PCs */`.  The header defines ONE aux register (an R/W pair at offset 0) and DISABLES offset 1 with an annotation stating the opposite of the reading taken.  Found by the grok seat, which checked the premise UNDER the citation.  *** THE MAIN LOOP CONFIRMED THE DEAD WARRANT BEFORE CHECKING IT. ***  I grepped `wd_digin`, saw the line, and reported the refutation 'verified exactly' -- I verified the line EXISTS and never checked it COMPILES.  That is the day's recurring defect (a TEXTUAL FORM counted where a PROPERTY was meant) committed inside the verification meant to catch it.  WHAT SURVIVED UNTOUCHED, and it is most of the ruling: `wdcaltwidth` scored 0 of 3 on the overtaken conditions and stays open; the read half files as its own row (no oracle for the bit layout exists in-tree, so pinning it would be the #357/#362/#365 failure); the decline is SILENT; ACCEPT is structurally unavailable STORE-side.  It also prescribed the pre-table block and named the value-guard mutant BEFORE any table ran.

*** RE-RULED ON THE CORRECTED FACT AND KEPT (a) -- ON A THIRD ARGUMENT NEITHER CODEX NOR THE MAIN LOOP HAD. ***  **(c) DOES NOT EVEN RESOLVE THE COLLISION IT INVOKES.**  `dev_fdc.c:49`'s stated end-state is 8 ports = `0x3f0..0x3f7`; wdc's alt region is `0x3f6..0x3f7`; **the overlap is TWO bytes, not one.**  Narrowing wdc to 1 byte frees `0x3f7` and still blocks fdc at `0x3f6`, which wdc must keep.  So the end-state is a two-device ARBITRATION design, not a width flip -- (c) as stated fixes half a collision.  Arithmetic re-derived by the main loop before recording.  Its other two legs: the `#if 0` annotation is a PC-MAPPING decision by its own wording (*fd uses this register on PCs*), unsettled on the three non-PC layouts; and (c) is not a repair but an OWNERSHIP TRANSFER to `memory_rw`'s unassigned-address path -- machine-dependent, on four layouts, measured on none.  **VERIFIED A PREMISE Q-D RESTS ON THAT NOBODY HAD CHECKED**: `relative_addr` is bounded to {0,1} by the 2-byte registration, and a len=2 access at offset 0 still yields `relative_addr == 0` -- so codex's *'`> 1` is never true'* is verified, not assumed.  Also pinned that P2's `0x06` is `WDCTL_RST|WDCTL_IDS` and that `#481`'s own comment documents it as REAL traffic (*Older OpenBSD asserts with 0x06*).  *** A-D: THE VALUE-GUARD IS A CLAUSE-(d) FLOOR BREACH AS THE ROWS STAND, AND THE ROUND OWES A NEW ROW NOW. ***  `relative_addr != 0 && idata == 0x06` keeps P1 and P3 green by construction and re-opens the defect for every other RST-carrying value.  It passes the plausible-future-edit test exactly -- `0x06` is both the packet's only defect-side value and the comment's documented real-world SRST value, so *tighten the decline to known traffic* is the edit a well-meaning hand makes.  **The owed row is an offset-1 store carrying `0x04` (bare RST)**, chosen because it kills the equality guard while P2's existing `0x06` symmetrically kills any re-aim to `== 0x04`.  Formally L1 (nothing committed), but floor, not polish: it may not be filed.  *** AND A SKETCH-RULE CATCH THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A SECOND DEFECT: THE DECLINE MUST `return 1`, NEVER 0. ***  A `0` hands the access to the caller's unassigned-address handling -- **the same unwitnessed machine-dependent behaviour (c) was rejected for shipping.**  Required record corrections: the dead warrant corrected in place (L4); an ownership row filed carrying the `#if 0` verbatim; one sentence stating (a) leaves `len` UNDECODED so nobody reads offset decode as width coverage; and the prior *'after the fix, model and hardware agree'* qualified to STORE-SIDE ONLY -- read-side, offset 1 still returns the status mirror on all four layouts, which agrees with no hardware anywhere.  Flagged its own weakest leg unprompted: the floppy-CCR-write fact is background PC knowledge corroborated by the header comment, not provable from this tree, and the silence ruling does not rest on it alone.

entries.note: *** SIX BINARIES BUILT AND SCORED.  TWO OF ITS FOUR RESULTS GO AGAINST ITS OWN ARTIFACT, AND IT BADGED THE SELF-REVIEW `A` UNPROMPTED. ***  Provenance checked before measuring: its fix leg is byte-identical to the committed `mkfixleg.py` output AND to the preserved `fixleg.diff`, and its table IMPORTS the witness probe rather than re-implementing it. rows.title: Kill drivers score a CRASHED mutant as a table result
rows.witness: harness:read from the drivers' own source
rows.note: Found by the opus5 seat while measuring an unrelated round.  `kill479.sh`'s `build_run` checks the COMPILE exit status, then runs the mutant binary and pipes straight to `grep -c '^  FAIL'` -- **it never reads the RUN's exit status, nor the `WDC_IDENTIFY_PASS` sentinel the detector already emits.**  A mutant that dies partway through is therefore scored `KILLED (n red)` or `*ESCAPED* (clean sweep)` purely by HOW FAR IT GOT.  *** NOT HYPOTHETICAL FOR THIS DEVICE, and the shape is one edit away. ***  `write_in_progress` and `write_count` are set together in `wdc__write()` but CLEARED AT DIFFERENT SITES -- the reset helper clears the flag, only a completed drain clears the count -- and the drain guard divides: `inbuf_len % (512 * d->write_count) == 0`.  A clause-(d) operand swap that leaves the flag standing while zeroing the count is a MODULO BY ZERO.  Today the `&&` short-circuit saves it; a driver blind to exit status would report the SIGFPE as a table result.  CENSUS, with its limitation stated because it is the same defect one level up: 16 kill/measure drivers examined; **7 mention no sentinel at all**, and all seven are the 2026-08-27 wdc-family drivers (`killalt.sh`, `kill482`, `kill480`, `kill480b`, `kill477b`, `kill479`, `kill478`).  Every GD-ROM driver from 08-28 onward does check one, so the practice improved and the older drivers were never retrofitted.  *** THE CENSUS COUNTS MENTIONS, NOT CHECKS, AND IS THEREFORE A CANDIDATE LIST RATHER THAN A COUNT. ***  A driver that merely ECHOES a sentinel at the end scores as having one -- my own `killrow5c.sh` does exactly that.  Emitting a sentinel is not reading one.  Confirming each of the seven needs the driver opened.  *This is the round's own recurring defect -- counting a textual form where a property was meant -- committed inside the census that reports it.*  REMEDY: two columns, EXIT and SENT, in each driver's row output.  The opus5 seat already ran its own table that way and every mutant came back clean, so nothing measured today was mis-scored -- but the drivers cannot tell.  Cheap, and the rule already exists: *a preserved log is verified by its COMPLETION SENTINEL, not by its existence.*  *** CONFIRMED BY READING ONE OF EACH, rather than by the mention-count. ***  `kill479.sh`'s run path is three lines: `if [ $? -ne 0 ]` (the COMPILE), then `"$O/$2" > "$O/$2.out" 2>&1` (runs the mutant), then `grep -c '^  FAIL'` -- **the run's status is never captured between those two lines.**  By contrast `kill489d.sh` (GD-ROM, 08-28) extracts STRUCTURED RESULT TOKENS with `grep -o 'TOCLEN_RESULT=[0-9]*/[0-9]*' | tail -1`, so a truncated run yields a MISSING token rather than a plausible score.  **That is the difference worth copying: not 'check the exit code' but 'score from a token the run only emits when it finishes'** -- the same discriminator the completion-sentinel rule already states, applied to the scorer instead of to the log reader.  *** ONE DRIVER FIXED 2026-08-30, AND IT WAS THE ONE WRITTEN AFTER THIS ROW WAS FILED. ***  `killtable_20260830/killswap.sh` -- authored during `wdcatapistswap`, hours after this row named the class -- read NEITHER the run exit status NOR the completion sentinel.  It was PARTLY protected by accident: a missing prediction count already refused.  But the probe prints that count BEFORE its differential section and its sentinel, **so a crash in the gap scored normally** -- narrower window, same class.  It now refuses any run that did not reach `ADDTOINBUF_RUNG3_DONE`.  NEGATIVE CONTROL, and it is the one that matters for a tightening: all THIRTEEN preserved kill logs from that round carry the sentinel -- **including M7, whose guest deliberately never parks** -- so the new check rejects nothing that legitimately scored.  A gate that refuses valid runs is worse than no gate.  *The row STAYS OPEN*: the census names seven drivers with no sentinel check at all and this fixes one of them, in a file that did not exist when the census ran.  **The instructive part is that the class was FILED and the very next driver written in this project reproduced it** -- the carrier's own trigger-versus-memory finding, with a four-hour gap between the writing-down and the repetition.  *** A NEW MEMBER, ADDED 2026-08-31 BY CHECKING RATHER THAN BY WAITING FOR IT TO BITE: `#499`'s `table499.sh` HAS THE DEFECT, AND ITS TABLE IS NEVERTHELESS VERIFIED CLEAN. ***  Both halves matter and they are different claims.  **The DRIVER has it.**  `table499.sh` checks three things and none of them is the run: variant-generation rc (`VARIANT GEN FAILED ... ABORT`), binary existence (`NO BINARY -- ABORT`), and build freshness (`build: STALE -- ABORT`, the two-part clearance).  It then runs the detector and scores the output **without reading the run's exit status or the `DETECTOR_DONE` sentinel the detector already emits**.  A mutant that died partway would be scored by how far it got -- `KILLED` or `ESCAPED` depending on where it stopped.  *Note the driver is careful about the BUILD and blind to the RUN; that is the class's signature, and it is why an otherwise disciplined driver has it.*  **The TABLE is unaffected, and that was MEASURED, not assumed.**  Counting sentinels against score lines in the three committed logs: `table499.out` 6 `DETECTOR_DONE` / 6 `SCORE`; `extra_rows.out` 4 `EXTRA_DONE` / 4 `XSCORE`; `m5.out` 1 / 1.  **Every variant that produced a score also produced its completion sentinel**, so no row in `#499` rests on a truncated run.  *This is the cheap form of the repair available to any round TODAY, without touching a driver: the sentinel count and the score count must be equal, and that is one `grep -c` each.  The driver-side fix -- abort on a missing sentinel -- remains this row's work.*  **Census update: the candidate list is no longer only the 2026-08-27 wdc family.**  The practice was recorded as improving from 08-28 onward, and a driver written on 08-31 by the seat that FOUND this defect still has it -- which says the lesson lives in the finder's head rather than in a template.  That is this project's structure-versus-prose finding again, and it argues for a shared driver preamble rather than another round of care.

The mutant is `odata = 0;` -> `if (odata & WDCS_DRDY) odata = 0;`, which two seats independently
predicted would sweep the 16-row instrument 16/16.  **It now dies on exactly ONE row -- the row
written for it -- and disturbs nothing else.**  A row is not discharged by existing; it is
discharged by reddening under its mutant, and this is that measurement.

HOW THE ROW WAS BUILT, and the design took THREE attempts because the first two were vacuous:
the mutant only shows where DRDY is CLEAR, and every pre-existing row drives DRDY SET
(ST_POWERON 0x51, ST_ARMED 0x58).  A no-image session gives status 0x00, where a correctly
DECLINED 0x00 cannot be told from a LEAKED 0x00.  `WDCC_DIAGNOSE` is unreachable without an image
(`wdc_command()` clears d->error, then detects the missing image and RETURNS BEFORE the switch).
**What works is the ABSENT SLAVE plus an armed write: DRQ is INDEPENDENT OF IMAGE PRESENCE**, so
`0xb0 -> wd_sdh` between t8 and t9 gives status 0x08 -- non-zero with DRDY clear.  Three rows
(CONTROL / ACCEPT / CORE), probe 16 -> 19, gate pin moved 16 -> 19 by hand with its reason.

rows.title: 0x3f6/0x3f7 are contested between wdc and the floppy controller, and the tree documents the collision from BOTH sides while resolving it from neither
rows.witness: none -- a device-topology design question, not a bounds defect.  No measurement is owed until a disposition is chosen.
rows.note:
Filed by #494, which REJECTED narrowing the alt region and owes the reader the reason rather than a silence.  **The tree says twice that these bytes are contested, and the two statements do not agree with each other.**  `src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h` compiles the aux-region offset-1 define out entirely, under `#if 0` with the annotation *NOT MAPPED; fd uses this register on PCs* -- i.e. the wdc does not own it.  `src/devices/dev_fdc.c` carries `#define DEV_FDC_LENGTH 6` with the comment *TODO 8, but collision with wdc*, registered at `isa_portbase + 0x3f0` -- i.e. the FLOPPY is the one being truncated.  *** THE ARITHMETIC IS WHY NARROWING WAS REJECTED, and it is the whole finding: fdc's stated end-state of 8 ports is 0x3f0..0x3f7 and the alt region is 0x3f6..0x3f7, so the OVERLAP IS TWO BYTES, not one. ***  Narrowing wdc to 1 byte frees 0x3f7 and still blocks fdc at 0x3f6, which wdc must keep.  So the end-state is a two-device ARBITRATION design, not a width flip -- narrowing as proposed would have fixed half a collision and called it done.  Derived by the fable5 adjudicator on re-ruling; arithmetic re-checked before filing.  A second reason narrowing is not free, MEASURED by the opus5 seat: an unmapped access faults nothing and the guest parks normally, but it emits one `non-existant paddr` warning PER ACCESS with no latch and no counter (the floodclass shape, guest-drivable at default verbosity), a read then returns 0x00 silently, and under `-T` it sets `running = 0` on EVERY cpu.  HONEST BOUND, because the disposition is not obvious: generic ATA DOES define a read-only Drive Address register at that port, so the `#if 0` annotation is a PC-MAPPING decision by its own wording and is unsettled on the three non-PC layouts this device also serves (macppc +0x160, hpcmips 0x14000386, iq80321 +0x402).  Whatever is decided must claim only what it covers.  Blocks `wdcaltdigin`: if the byte is the floppy's, the right read value is not a wdc value at all.

*** ATA-2 MAKES THE TWO ADDRESSES SEPARABLE, WHICH IS THE ANSWER THIS ROW NEEDED AND THE ONE [[wdcaltdigin]] DEPENDS ON.  2026-09-11 (ata2batch/codex_ata2batch_20260911.txt). ***

`CS1-` is *"the chip select signal from the host used to select the Control Block Registers"* (historically `CS3FX-`), and **the register address within that block comes from the three `DA` signals** (`:1226-1234`).  So selecting the block and selecting an address inside it are separate mechanisms, and a device may answer one control-block address and not another.

**THAT LICENSES THE NARROWING DISPOSITION** [[wdcaltdigin]] arrived at from Note 1 -- registering the region one byte narrower so the odd address is never claimed is conformant at the ATA level, not merely convenient.

**WHAT ATA-2 DOES *NOT* DO, stated so the row is not over-closed: it does not arbitrate PC host-port ownership.**  The contest between this controller and the floppy controller for the 0x3F6/0x3F7 pair is a platform question the standard does not settle; what it settles is that the ATA side is free to decline the odd address.

rows.title: the no-VPATH rule has FOUR build trees and precommit section B enforces only three -- the WSL arc tree is invisible to it
rows.witness: harness:three-state negative control on the SHIPPED lines -- green in sync, RED on a one-line divergence, SKIP when absent; preserved at regress/artifacts/wdcatapistswap/killtable_20260830/CONTROL_novpadfourth.out
rows.note: **Found by a measuring seat, not by a check, and that is the whole finding.**  `precommit_check.sh` section B compares `build/` and `build-asan/` against SEC because they sit under the Windows project root and it can walk them.  **`/tmp/gxsec-build` lives in the WSL filesystem and the Windows-side checker never sees it.**  So the carrier's own no-VPATH rule -- *propagate every edit into them or you measure a stale binary* -- names four trees while the gate enforces three.  **Why it is worse than an unchecked tree**: scratch clones are made FROM these trees.  A clone of a stale donor `cmp`s CLEAN against its donor and carries no sentinel, so the two-part clearance passes on it -- the stale-binary trap reached from a direction the sentinel discipline cannot cover, exactly as the carrier already records for a different route.  Here it would have measured `#494`-less code in the file `#494` edited.  REMEDY, and it is not obviously a checker: section B would have to reach across the WSL boundary, which is a different kind of check from every other one it does.  The cheaper form may be a `wslpropagate.sh` invocation in the round-boundary step beside the existing two-part clearance -- structure where the decision happens, rather than a checker that cannot see the thing it checks.  A script exists (`regress/artifacts/wdcaltoffset/killtable_20260830/wslpropagate.sh`) and ran clean; what is missing is the obligation to run it.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30.  THE OBSTACLE THIS ROW RESTED ON DOES NOT EXIST, AND ONE COMMAND SETTLED IT. ***  The row stayed open on the assumption that a WSL tree is unreachable from the Windows-side gate.  **It is reachable**: `//wsl.localhost/Gentoo/tmp/gxsec-build` reads fine from git-bash, and a `cmp` across that boundary completes in **83 ms**.  The check was never written; nothing was ever preventing it.  `precommit_check.sh` now carries a fourth section mirroring the build-asan one: `.MUTANT` sentinel row, then a `cmp` per changed `src/` file, keyed on `${GXWSLTREE}` so it is testable without touching the real tree.  **ABSENCE SKIPS FOR TWO REASONS RATHER THAN ONE**, and the second is new: the tree may never have been built, OR the distro may simply not be running, in which case the UNC path is unreadable and nothing is wrong.  A gate that hard-fails because a VM is asleep is a gate that gets switched off.  CONTROLLED IN THREE STATES, on the SHIPPED LINES rather than a retyped copy -- the control extracts the block from `precommit_check.sh` by grep anchor and drives it with a synthetic file list, because this round edits no `src/` file and the real list would leave the loop empty:  (1) real tree in sync -> GREEN;  (2) a copy whose `dev_wdc.c` differs by ONE LINE -> **RED**, which is the control that matters because without it the section is a claim rather than a check;  (3) absent tree -> SKIP, not fail.  *** AND THE CONTROL'S OWN FIRST DRAFT FAILED IN THE CLASS THIS PROJECT KEEPS RECORDING. ***  Its awk range ended on the block's last MESSAGE (`rows skipped, not failed`) and stopped ONE LINE SHORT of the closing `fi`, so `eval` died with 'unexpected end of file'.  Re-anchored on `^fi$`.  **A range that ends on prose ends wherever the prose happens to sit** -- and the extraction prints its own line count, so a range that selects almost nothing is refused rather than run.

rows.title: the #495 guard's flag operand can be swapped for `atapi_st != NULL` and the detector cannot see it -- measured to refuse every ordinary data-port write for the life of the device

Logs at regress/artifacts/wdcatapistswap/killtable_20260830/ (TABLE.txt, kill_L0_committed_probe.out, kill_E2.out).  *** REPLACED, not appended: the previous field read 'probe:measured by the pass-2 measuring seat --...' -- a `probe:` prefix that check_witness.py scores as RUNG 3, which that file's own header calls laundering for a round whose subject is the test apparatus; and its 20/20 figure disagreed with its own note ("all 22 rows") while the artifact it cited no longer existed.  Named by the fable5 seat.
rows.note: *** AN OPERAND SWAP THAT ESCAPES ALL 22 ROWS, AND THE SEAT MEASURED THE DAMAGE RATHER THAN REASONING IT. ***  Replace `d->atapi_cmd_in_progress` in `#495`'s guard with `d->atapi_st != NULL`.  Pre-packet push/pop pair reads `5a,a5` on both legs; **post-packet it reads `5a,a5` shipped versus `ff,ff` under the swap** -- refused, empty-ring over-read.  **THE MECHANISM, READ FROM SOURCE: `atapi_st` is allocated at the first dispatch and NEVER set back to NULL.**  `wdc_new_command_reset()` zeroes the flag, the phase, `write_in_progress` and the ring pointers, and does not touch it.  So after ONE ATAPI command the swapped guard refuses every ordinary data-port write for the life of the device.  **NOT a clause-(d) breach by the letter of the DEPENDS-ON bound** -- `atapi_st` is not read by the guarded body, so the operand-swap enumeration does not reach it -- which is why this files rather than being repaired in-round.  What it shows is that the detector's ACCEPT side is unpinned for ordinary non-ATAPI writes: no row asserts that a plain data-port write still lands after a packet command has completed.  **IT IS NOT A CONTRIVED MUTANT.**  `dev_wdc.c`'s own comment files exactly this refactor, recording that `atapi_cmd_in_progress` *conflates two roles* -- so a future round separating them could write this swap believing it a simplification.  REMEDY: one accept row -- an ordinary data-port write after a completed packet command, asserted to land.  *** CORRECTED IN PLACE 2026-08-30, PASS 1 OF THE ROUND THAT CLOSES THIS ROW. THE STATE THIS NOTE NAMES CANNOT EXIST. ***  The note says the differential runs *post-packet*, reading `5a,a5` shipped versus `ff,ff` swapped, with no command in between.  A packet-fed seat challenged that from the inlined facts alone and it is right: `atapi_cmd_in_progress` has exactly TWO write sites -- cleared in `wdc_new_command_reset()`, set at the packet dispatch -- and **no completion path clears it** (the completion arm sets `PHASE_COMPLETED` and leaves the flag; the only `memset(d, 0, ...)` is devinit).  So immediately after a transfer the flag is still 1, **the SHIPPED guard refuses too**, both legs read `ff`, and the differential as described would show no difference at all.  **THE MEASUREMENT IS NOT DISPUTED -- the recorded STATE is.**  The seat's run almost certainly carried an intervening command that this summary dropped; that is being put to the seat directly rather than assumed.  *** THE CORRECTION STRENGTHENS THE REMEDY RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. ***  The states where the two builds differ are exactly `flag == 0 && atapi_st != NULL`, and ONLY a command can produce them, because the reset is the sole writer of `flag = 0` while `atapi_st` has one write site and no clear site.  So the accept row's clearing command is LOAD-BEARING, not scene-setting -- the naive post-packet form of this row would have been VACUOUS, green on both legs, and would have shipped looking like coverage.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30 in `e61ccd8`.  WHAT ARRIVED AS 'one accept row' LEFT AS TWO VEHICLES, THREE ACCESS WIDTHS AND A REPAIRED FLOOR -- every step forced by a seat rather than chosen. ***  THE ARMS: M (after `WDCC_RECAL`) and N (after `ATAPI_SOFT_RESET`), two rows each.  The second vehicle exists because with one, `&& d->cur_command != WDCC_RECAL` re-opens the hole and sweeps every row -- one conjunct cannot exempt two opcodes.  MEASURED: E3 reds the N rows and leaves the M rows green.  TWELVE LEGS, 15 rows / 30 predictions, every score generated from TABLE.txt rather than transcribed.  **Both halves of the harness proof are results of THIS round**: the COMMITTED probe cannot see the swap (LEG 0, 22/22 ESCAPED) and the EXTENDED one kills it (E2, 26/30, 4 red).  The inherited escape figure was re-measured because its artifact had vanished and the row disagreed with itself.  TWELVE OF TWELVE PREDICTIONS, written before the table ran, confirmed -- one after being corrected: M7 was predicted green on the accept rows, and a seat refuted it before any build because M7's guard fires at the DATA-IN injection and the guest never parks.  **The arms are UNREACHED, not inert**; measured 15/30.  A prediction about a row's VALUE presumes the row RUNS.  *** AND THE ROUND'S LAST PREDICTION BECAME A MEASUREMENT: E6. ***  The claim that the SECOND row of each pair is not redundant rested on an unbuilt mutant that -- unlike E2 and E5 -- sits INSIDE clause (d)'s enumeration.  Built and run alone: 26/30, 4 red, and exactly the predicted asymmetry.  The FIRST row of each pair stays GREEN (the ring genuinely is empty at that push) and only the SECOND reds.  A CLAUSE-(d) FLOOR BREACH WAS FOUND AND REPAIRED HERE: `&& len != 4` swept the whole detector while restoring the defect.  One instruction, no new row -- a 4-byte `sw` -- kills E4, M3 and M6 together, and the probe turned out to have NO 4-byte emitter at all, so the device's `case 4:` WRITE arm had never executed on any leg of any run.  Filed as `wdcwidth4`, now closed. rows.title: every wdc rung-3 probe has only a LITTLE-ENDIAN leg, so the big-endian half of each guard is unpinned by construction
rows.witness: probe:measured -- a mutant applying #495's guard only on the little-endian path escapes all 22 rows
rows.note: *** STRUCTURAL, NOT AN OVERSIGHT IN ANY ONE ROW. ***  The write arm branches on `cpu->byte_order`, and every rung-3 probe in this family runs `evbmips -e malta` little-endian only.  A mutant that applies the `#495` guard on the LE path and omits it on the BE path escapes all 22 rows -- measured, 22/22 -- because no row ever executes the other branch.  **The same hole exists for every guard in that switch**, not just this round's: the BE arm is a mirror of the LE arm and nothing walks it.  COVERAGE DEBT, filed rather than fixed: closing it needs a big-endian rig for this device, which is a rig question rather than a row question, and no round has yet needed one.  Ranked LOW because the mutant is a copy-paste asymmetry rather than a shape a plausible edit produces -- but recorded because *unpinned by construction* is exactly the class this project keeps finding late.

rows.note: *** THE CARRIED NUMBER WAS RIGHT.  MY RECOUNT WAS THE ERROR, AND THE GATE PRINTED THE ANSWER MINUTES AFTER I FILED THE CONTRADICTION. ***  A checkpoint line read *'10 closed rows carry panel entries with no seat outcome'*.  I re-derived it, got **1993 entries across 83 closed rows**, filed this row saying the carried figure was wrong by two orders of magnitude -- and then `precommit_check.sh` said: **`closed rows with panel entries but NO seat outcomes: 10 total`**, followed by *`(51 more are GRANDFATHERED pre-2026-08-23 and not counted above)`*.  **THE TWO NUMBERS COUNT DIFFERENT THINGS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS THE CLAIM.**  The checker counts CLOSED ROWS, restricted to rows carrying PANEL entries, excluding a grandfather cutoff it applies deliberately.  I counted RAW EMPTY FIELDS over every entry of every closed row, grandfathered and non-panel entries included.  My denominator was never the claim's denominator.  *** THIS IS THE SESSION'S OWN RECURRING DEFECT, COMMITTED INSIDE A ROW ABOUT COUNTING: A TEXTUAL FORM COUNTED WHERE A PROPERTY WAS MEANT. ***  `outcome` being an empty string is a textual form; *'a closed row whose panel work is ungraded'* is the property, and the checker already encodes it -- cutoff and all.  **A count that names neither its unit nor its method cannot be checked, and I wrote one while correcting one.**  *** AND THE CHEAPEST CHECK WAS THE ONE I SKIPPED: ASK WHETHER A TOOL ALREADY COUNTS THIS. ***  `check_bugfile_sync.py`/`seat_scorecard.py` had the definition, the cutoff and the population the whole time.  Re-deriving a number by hand when a checker already derives it does not verify the checker -- it produces a second, unrelated number and an argument.  THE LIVE WORK, which is small and was correctly stated from the start: **ten rows** -- `exitsweep`, `xfamscope`, `m8sarseq`, `wdcnoirq`, `verdictbold`, `gdromdefault`, `asicbadaddr`, `lethalonly` and two more the gate truncates -- need an `outcome` plus `outcome_note` per `seat_scorecard.py`.  The 51 grandfathered rows are deliberately out of scope and are NOT work.  *** ONE GENUINE DEFECT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION. ***  Row `r421` carries a codex `review` entry with **NO DATE AND AN EMPTY `ev` FIELD**, whose entire note is *'A review of the final diff is possible here.'*  That is a note saying a review COULD happen, sitting in the slot where evidence goes -- so a reader, and section G, see a review phase with a seat attached and nothing behind it.  An unrun check and a completed one must not render the same.  It is the only undated entry in the ledger, and that finding is independent of the miscount.

rows.title: an INEQUALITY width qualifier swept the whole detector -- CLOSED by injecting a third access width, so the width family is closed on both sides
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED both ways -- swept 30/30 before the repair; after it, E4 scores 29/30 with the kill on row L (want 50 got 58, the 4-byte store admitted).  Log: regress/artifacts/wdcatapistswap/killtable_20260830/kill_E4.out
rows.note: *** THE PROBE'S OWN COMMENT CLAIMS THIS FAMILY IS CLOSED, AND IT IS CLOSED ONLY ON ONE SIDE. ***  The K arm says *'No single width qualifier can refuse both'*, having made one injection 2-byte and the other 1-byte so that neither `len == 1` nor `len == 2` can refuse the pair.  **That is true of EQUALITY qualifiers and false of the inequality.**  Append `&& len <= 2` -- equivalently `&& len != 4` -- to the shipped guard and it still refuses BOTH committed injections, so every defect row stays green; row M stays green because the flag is 0 after RECAL; and **4-byte stores to the data port land in the ring during DATA-IN**, which is the defect #495 removed.  The write arm implements `case 4:` explicitly, so this is a width the device supports and no row exercises.  ABOVE-FLOOR COVERAGE DEBT, filed rather than fixed: the shipped detector sits above the vacuity floor and this is a hypothetical edit in an uncovered cell, not a live defect.  REMEDY: a 4-byte injection variant, the natural sibling of `wdcrearmwalk`.  Derived by the fable5 seat on the `wdcatapistswap` pass 1, from the probe's own closure claim -- it asked what the claim was quantified over and found the quantifier was narrower than the sentence.  *** RE-DISPOSITIONED THE SAME DAY: THIS IS A CLAUSE-(d) FLOOR BREACH, L2, REPAIRED IN-ROUND -- NOT THE COVERAGE DEBT IT WAS FIRST FILED AS. ***  Filed on the fable5 seat's derivation; the opus5 seat then MEASURED it and dissented on disposition, and the dissent is correct.  `if (X)` -> `if (X && Y)` on the predicate `#495` ADDED, which DOMINATES the edited lines, is clause (d)'s canonical form -- and `#488`'s adjudication says so in terms: *'E1 was `if (X)` -> `if (X && Y)` on the DOMINATING predicate -- the canonical clause-(d) form, i.e. a floor breach.'*  `#495` is closed, so the LATE-DISSENT rule applies: disposition 2, a MEASURED FALSE PASS against a shipped detector's floor, repaired in a follow-up commit.  `wdcatapistswap` IS that commit and was already rewriting the row list, so the repair cost nothing extra.  *** THE MEASUREMENT, and it is worse than the filing said. ***  Under E4 the guest is handed its own injected bytes AS DISK DATA and the detector scores a clean sweep -- not a hypothetical edit in an uncovered cell, but the exact defect `#495` removed, restored, invisible.  THE CLOSURE CONDITION, derived by the seat: `&& P(len)` escapes iff P is TRUE on every width the probe injects and FALSE on some width the device IMPLEMENTS.  {1,2} leaves `!= 4`; {2,4} leaves `!= 1`; {1,4} leaves `!= 2`.  **Only {1,2,4} closes the family** -- the 3- and 8-byte cases push nothing and are inert as escape routes.  REPAIRED WITH ONE INSTRUCTION and NO new row: a 4-byte `sw` beside the existing 1-byte K injection.  On the fixed leg it is refused like its neighbours so row L still reads ST_IDLE; on the base leg it lands like them so row L still reads ST_DATAIN.  It kills E4, M3 and M6 together.  *** AND THE PROBE HAD NO 4-BYTE EMITTER AT ALL -- no `sw`, no `lw` -- so the device's `case 4:` arm and its whole `consumed` accounting had never been executed on any leg of any run this detector ever made. ***  That is the real finding: not an uncovered mutant, an uncovered ARM.  *** CLOSED 2026-08-30, IN THE ROUND THAT FOUND IT.  The state and the substance had disagreed: this row shipped `in work` with a present-tense title -- *sweeps all 26 ... no row injects at len == 4* -- for a defect the same diff repaired. ***  A future reader who trusts states reads that as live, which is false; the es438 shape, named by the fable5 seat on pass 2.  CLOSED BY: a 4-byte `sw` in the probe's K2 arm, one instruction, no new row.  The probe now injects widths {1,2,4}, and the closure condition -- `&& P(len)` escapes iff P is TRUE on every INJECTED width and FALSE on some IMPLEMENTED width -- has no remaining solution, because the device implements exactly {1,2,4} and the 3- and 8-byte cases push nothing.  *** AND THE EVIDENCE MUST BE CITED PRECISELY, WHICH IT WAS NOT AT FIRST. ***  The `a5/5a/00` readback this finding is usually quoted with came from a probe whose DATA-IN injection had been WIDENED to four bytes to demonstrate the hazard -- not from E4 against the shipped instrument.  Against the repaired probe E4 leaves G/H/I GREEN and dies on ROW L.  Same conclusion, different row; the grok seat caught the misattribution by opening `kill_E4.out` rather than reading the claim.
