rows.note: `wdc_new_command_reset()` does three things -- clears the ATAPI flag and phase, clears `write_in_progress`, and empties the ring (`inbuf_head = inbuf_tail = 0`).  **Delete the ring-emptying line and the probe scores a clean sweep**, because on the fixed leg the #495 guard already keeps the ring empty at every command boundary this probe crosses, so there is nothing left for the reset to discard.  The instrument is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to that half of #479.  Note this is a property of the probe, not of the fix: the ring reset is live and load-bearing on paths the probe does not walk.  LOW because the blind spot needs a deliberate deletion to expose and the offline detector covers ring occupancy from the other side -- the two instruments are complementary and this is one of the seams between them.  Recorded in the probe's BLIND-TO list in the same round, because a contract that does not name its blind spots is the overclaim clause (e) exists to prevent.  Derived by the fable5 seat on `wdcatapistswap` pass 1.  *** RE-MEASURED 2026-08-30 AT THE CURRENT INSTRUMENT: 30/30 ESCAPED.  The old figure said 'escapes all 26', which was the 13-row instrument this round then grew past -- a figure the round's OWN repair invalidated and nobody re-ran until a seat said so. ***  *** AND THE MEASUREMENT SETTLED A DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO SEATS, IN FAVOUR OF THE ONE THAT REASONED ABOUT WHICH TREE THE MUTANT LANDS ON. ***  The opus5 seat predicted **29/30** -- that on the BASE leg the K and K2 injections land, so the ring holds bytes at the RECAL boundary and row M/t7 would pop a stale `0xa5` where it wants `0x5a`.  The kimi seat predicted a **clean escape**, and gave the reason: the mutant is applied to the **FIX** tree, the base leg is UNMUTATED, and on the fix leg the intact guard refuses every injection -- so the ring is empty at every command boundary this probe crosses and **the reset is dead code there**.  Measured 30/30.  **Kimi is right.**  *Both seats reasoned carefully and one of them tracked which leg the mutation reaches.  That is the whole difference, and it is not a difference of care.*  SO THE BLIND SPOT IS REAL AND CONFIRMED AT THE SHIPPED INSTRUMENT: this probe structurally cannot see `#479`'s ring-reset half, because the `#495` guard it exists to pin makes that half unreachable on the only leg a mutant can alter.  **Two fixes of one round can be mutually masking**, and no row count closes that -- it needs a leg where the guard does NOT hold.  RANKED LOW and left open: closing it needs an instrument whose fix leg admits ring content at a command boundary, which is a probe-shape question rather than a row question.

rows.title: a SECOND flag-operand replacement -- `cur_command == ATAPI_PKT_CMD` -- sweeps the 15-row probe 30/30, and the two-vehicle accept arm does not defeat it
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED by the opus5 seat at 30/30 ESCAPED on the extended probe; its guest-visible divergence is DERIVED, not measured
rows.note: Replace `d->atapi_cmd_in_progress` in the `#495` guard with `d->cur_command == ATAPI_PKT_CMD`.  **30/30, clean sweep.**  *** THIS IS NOT THE ESCAPE THE N ARM WAS BUILT FOR, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ROW. ***  `E3` is `&& cur_command != WDCC_RECAL` -- an EXEMPTION of one opcode, which the second vehicle (ATAPI_SOFT_RESET) defeats because one conjunct cannot exempt two opcodes.  **E5 is a REPLACEMENT of the flag operand -- E2's own family -- and the two-vehicle argument does not touch it**: after BOTH RECAL (0x10) and SOFT_RESET (0x08), `cur_command != 0xa0`, so the guard is false and BOTH accept arms stay green.  DIVERGENCE, derived rather than measured: `wdc_command()`'s no-disk-image early return sits AFTER `wdc_new_command_reset()`, so selecting a nonexistent drive and then writing ATAPI_PKT_CMD leaves `cur_command == 0xa0` with the flag CLEAR -- shipped accepts there, E5 refuses.  Two stores, and probing a nonexistent slave is what a bus scan does.  RANKED BELOW `wdcwidth4` and FILED rather than fixed: its harm class is OVER-REFUSAL (M1's class) and TRANSIENT, where E2's is permanent for the life of the device, and the divergence is reasoned rather than run.  **The honest statement of what the accept arm buys, from the same seat: rows B and M differ in exactly ONE dimension a mutant can read -- whether a packet command has ever run.  E2 is the arm's only UNIQUE kill, because at row B `atapi_st` is NULL so E2's guard is false and B stays green.  'The accept side is pinned' is measurably false.**  *** RE-ANCHORED 2026-08-30: this row said *Ranked below `wdcwidth4`*, and `wdcwidth4` has since been DISCHARGED. ***  A ranking against a closed row conveys nothing.  The standing comparison is to the swap `wdcatapistswap` closed: **that one is PERMANENT** -- once a packet command runs, every ordinary data-port write is refused for the life of the device -- while this one is **TRANSIENT over-refusal**, cleared by the next command write, and its divergence is derived rather than measured.  That is why it files.  *** TWO SEATS DISAGREED ABOUT WHETHER THIS IS CATCHABLE AT ALL, AND READING THE FUNCTION SETTLED IT IN FOUR LINES.  2026-08-30, pass 2. ***  The kimi seat derived, at length and honestly, that the swap is **UN-CATCHABLE by any accept row** because `flag == 1` and `cur_command == ATAPI_PKT_CMD` are EQUIVALENT device-wide -- which would make filing the only possible disposition forever.  The opus5 seat derived the opposite: the distinguishing state exists via the no-disk-image early return.  **THE ORDER INSIDE `wdc_command()` DECIDES IT, and opus5 is right:** `cur_command = idata` runs FIRST, then `wdc_new_command_reset()` clears the flag, then the no-disk-image early RETURN fires -- and the flag is set again only inside the ATAPI_PKT_CMD case, which sits AFTER that return.  So writing 0xa0 to a driveless slot leaves **`cur_command == 0xa0` with `flag == 0`**: the equivalence fails and the swap is distinguishable.  **KIMI'S PROPOSED ALTERNATIVE VEHICLE IS SEPARATELY REFUTED.**  It reasoned that a control-port SRST might clear the flag while leaving `cur_command` stale at 0xa0, which would kill this swap AND the whole opcode-exemption family at once.  It does not: the SRST arm writes `cur_command = COMMAND_RESET` before calling the reset helper, so nothing is left stale.  A good idea, refuted by one line.  *** THE SEAT BEHAVIOUR IS WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY FROM THE ANSWER. ***  Kimi marked its own claim as unsettled -- *'MUST verify from source ... pending reading the actual code around 730-745, 822-870, 945-960'* -- and named the exact line ranges that would decide it.  Those are the lines that decided it.  **A seat that cannot check a premise and says which check would settle it is more useful than one that guesses**, even when its conclusion is wrong.  CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: it stays FILED, but the disposition is now stronger.  It is not un-catchable; it is catchable by an ARM, not a vehicle -- a data-port write after `ATAPI_PKT_CMD` is issued to a slot with no image.  That is a design a future round can start from rather than a hunt.

rows.title: a RELATIVE git ref inside a round's durable artifacts goes stale the moment the round commits -- twice in one day, in two files of one directory
rows.witness: harness:both instances were caught by the scripts' own guards refusing to measure -- one printed 'the two legs would be identical', the other 'there is no extension to measure'
rows.note: *** THIS EARNED ITS SECOND INSTANCE IN ONE DAY, IN THE SAME ARTIFACTS DIRECTORY, WHICH IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN TRIGGER FOR PREFERRING STRUCTURE OVER MEMORY. ***  **Instance 1, `runswap.sh`:** the base leg was `git show HEAD~1:`.  True when written.  An unrelated commit (a citation repair) then landed on top, pushing `#495` down to `HEAD~1` itself, so BOTH legs would have been built from code CONTAINING the fix.  Pinned to `67120fd^`.  **Instance 2, `killswap.sh`:** LEG 0's pre-extension probe was `git show HEAD:`.  True while the round was in flight -- HEAD held the 11-row probe and the working tree held 15.  **The round then SHIPPED**, HEAD became the 15-row probe, and the script refused a run in which there was no extension left to measure.  Pinned to `e61ccd8^`.  *** THE SHAPE IS SPECIFIC AND WORTH NAMING: a round's artifacts are written while the round is UNCOMMITTED, so every relative ref in them is written from a vantage point the round itself destroys by shipping. ***  The artifact is durable; the reference frame is not.  **BOTH WERE CAUGHT BY THE SCRIPTS' OWN GUARDS, NOT BY A READER**, and that is the reassuring half: each refused to measure rather than measuring the wrong thing.  A reproduction months from now would fail loudly instead of producing a confident wrong table.  PROPOSED STRUCTURAL FIX, filed rather than built: a precommit check warning when a file under `regress/artifacts/` contains `HEAD~`, `HEAD^` or `git show HEAD:`.  Bounded, existence-only, forward-only from a cutoff.  **NOT built in the round that found it** -- a tooling change owing two negative controls (it must fire on a relative ref and must NOT fire on a pinned SHA), which ships as its own harness round.  *The population is probably larger: only two files were exercised today.  Other rounds' artifacts have never been re-run, so a stale ref there would not yet have announced itself.  The count is unknown and is deliberately not guessed.*

(SUPERSEDED TITLE, kept only as the demoted record of what was claimed: "EIGHT probe-wiring exemptions expire on 2026-09-20 together and the checker hard-fails -- four are cheap, only four need a design round". rows.witness: harness:MEASURED by running check_probe_wiring.py at --today 2026-09-19 (PASS) and --today 2026-09-21 (FAIL, 8 problems)
rows.note:
*** EIGHT DATED EXEMPTIONS EXPIRE ON ONE DAY, AND THE CHECKER HARD-FAILS.  MEASURED, NOT REASONED. ***      python tools/pipeline/check_probe_wiring.py --today 2026-09-19   ->  PROBEWIRING_PASS  (46/54 gated, 8 dated-exempt)
    python tools/pipeline/check_probe_wiring.py --today 2026-09-21   ->  PROBEWIRING_FAIL  8 problem(s)
So **every commit after 2026-09-20 is blocked** until all eight are wired or the dates are moved.  The checker is right to do this -- a dated exemption that never comes due is not an exemption -- but eight coming due together is a scheduling hazard rather than a deadline.  *** AND THE POPULATION IS TWICE WHAT THE REGRESS REVIEW NAMED. ***  That review found *'FOUR wdc probes share the single-leg-mode debt and the same 2026-09-20 expiry'* and recommended ONE design round covering four instruments.  Correct about the wdc cluster; the expiry itself is shared by EIGHT probes with FOUR DISTINCT remedies:  **(1) single-leg mode, 4 probes** -- `wdc_altoffset_probe.py`, `_sig_`, `_4bit_`, `wdc_addtoinbuf_probe.py`.  Two-leg differentials; a gate has only one binary.  Two of them additionally need a CD-ROM rig (`ciR:`) and one needs a POISONED image the battery does not build.  This is the one-design-round cluster.  **(2) `hpcmips_ctor_probe.py`** -- rung 2, ~8 s, no rig image; wants a CONSTRUCTION gate.  Different mechanism entirely.  **(3) `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py` -> gate 10; `pit8253_latch_probe.py` -> gate 14.**  Each names the gate it belongs in; these are wiring, not design.  **(4) `fbpending_drain_probe.py`** -- REPORT-ONLY until `EXPECT_CAP` is set, so wiring it without setting that ships a row that cannot fail.  *** THE POINT IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE COUNT: four of the eight are CHEAP (two are plain gate wiring, one is a one-variable decision), and only the wdc four need a design round. ***  Doing the cheap four first shrinks the cliff from eight to four before it arrives, and each is independently shippable.  *Advisory, from the same run: the checker also notes two SELFLABEL discrepancies (`pit8253_latch_probe.py` and `wdc_addtoinbuf_probe.py` -- manifest says detector, the probe's own summary line says witness).  It flags these as advisory precisely because self-labels are measurably unreliable in both directions.*  *** ONE OF THE EIGHT WAS ABOUT TO BE GATE-WIRED WITH NO WAY TO DETECT A TRUNCATION.  FIXED PRE-EMPTIVELY 2026-08-30. ***  `pit8253_latch_probe.py`'s last output was a bare `PASS`/`FAIL` -- a word that occurs in dozens of contexts and is not uniquely greppable.  Its only SCREAMING_TOKEN was `print("MEASURED")`, a **mid-run section header** that a truncated log still contains.  So a gate row written against it could not have distinguished a completed run from a killed one, which is exactly the `killdrivercrash` class arriving in new work rather than old.  Now emits `PIT8253_LATCH_DONE`, on both the pass and fail paths -- a completed FAILURE is not a truncation.  *Doing this BEFORE the wiring means the gate row can be written correctly the first time.  `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py`, the other plain-wiring member, already carries a proper `SH4_BSC_WIDTH_PASS`/`_FAIL` pair and needs nothing.*  *** AND A METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX, because it nearly became a filed defect count. ***  A sweep for probes lacking a `_DONE`/`_PASS` token returned **34 of 46**.  That number is MEANINGLESS: gate 10 verifies `sh_rounding_probe.py` by grepping `SH_ROUND_RESULT=`, which is a perfectly good completion marker in a different shape.  The convention is per-probe and per-gate, so **there is no 34-probe defect and the question is not sweepable** -- it is 'does this probe's CONSUMER verify completion, and by what?', one probe at a time.  An earlier version of the same sweep put `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py` in the missing list, which is how the pattern was caught: it flagged a probe I had confirmed compliant ten minutes earlier.  **A pattern that selects the wrong set produces a clean, confident, wrong population**, and this is the third instance today.  *** THE CHEAP FOUR, INVESTIGATED READ-ONLY 2026-08-30 SO A ROUND CAN START WITHOUT RE-DERIVING ANY OF IT.  Ranked by what each actually needs. ***  **(a) `pit8253_latch_probe.py` -> gate 14.**  ALREADY UNBLOCKED: it lacked any completion marker and now emits `PIT8253_LATCH_DONE`.  Machine `-E cats`, 10 rows.  Gate 14 is `gate_arm.sh`, which already runs `-E cats`.  Remaining work is the exec line plus row checks.  **(b) `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py` -> gate 10.**  Machine `-E landisk`; already emits `SH4_BSC_WIDTH_PASS`/`_FAIL`.  **Gate 10 (`gate_sh_rounding.sh`) already execs three probes in exactly the needed idiom** -- `python3 <probe>.py "$PMAX" "$KERNEL" > "$LOG" 2>&1 || true`, then `check` rows against the log.  Copying that idiom is the whole change.  **(c) `hpcmips_ctor_probe.py` -> a construction gate.**  Rung 2, ~8 s, NO RIG IMAGE, takes no positional argv, accepts `--binary PATH` (default `$GXROOT/build/gxemul`), emits `HPCMIPS_CTOR_PASS`/`_FAIL`, and already runs its subprocess with a timeout.  `gate_asan_sweep.sh` is the construction gate and sweeps 41 machine types.  ONE MISMATCH TO RESOLVE, named rather than discovered later: that gate drives an ASAN binary while this probe defaults to `build/gxemul` -- `--binary` makes it parameterisable, so the decision is which binary the row should assert against.  **(d) `fbpending_drain_probe.py` -- ONE VARIABLE, BUT NOT A FREE ONE.**  It is REPORT-ONLY until `--expect-cap N` is set (`EXPECT_CAP = -1` means report only), and **wiring it without choosing N ships a row that cannot fail** -- the check-that-cannot-fail shape.  Choosing N needs a measurement, and the probe carries a **31.51 s wall-clock floor by construction**, so it is timing-sensitive and must be measured on a quiet machine.  Cheapest in code, most expensive in care.  *Ordering follows from that: (a) and (b) are mechanical, (c) needs one decision, (d) needs a measurement.  Three of the four can ship before the wdc design round even starts.*  *** `8404520` NAMED: that commit shipped this row's FIRST piece of code -- the `PIT8253_LATCH_DONE` sentinel -- and the attribution check refused the NEXT commit until the row said so.  Third time today this rule has fired (after `census` and `wdcatapistswap`), and every one was a real gap rather than a nuisance. ***  The row stays OPEN: one of eight probes is unblocked, seven remain, and the cliff is unmoved until they are wired.

[MAIN-LOOP NOTE, 2026-09-09, phase assess -- moved out of the seat entries because the dashboard declares no such seat]  RE-DERIVED FROM THE CHECKER, and three of this project's own records about this row were wrong.  (1) The exemption set is what `grep -n 2026-09-20 check_probe_wiring.py' returns, and the checker states the same count in its own comment -- the ledger TITLE said eight. CHECKPOINT.md said three.  *** SO WIRING THE FOUR AS THEY STAND WOULD SHIP FOUR GATE SECTIONS THAT CANNOT FAIL -- this project's own named class, four at once, installed BY the deadline. ***  AND A DERIVER OF MINE MEASURED A CORRELATE while correcting someone else's count: `grep -cE 'exit\([1-9]'' scored three of the four as failable, matching two `os._exit(127)' calls in forked pty CHILDREN (which give the PARENT no failure status) and one COMMENT quoting a removed call. [MAIN-LOOP NOTE, 2026-09-09, phase assess -- moved out of the seat entries because the dashboard declares no such seat]  *** THE DISPOSITION IS AN OWNER DECISION AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN. ***  Every one of the six reason strings names a prerequisite that does not exist TODAY and is still true: an unset EXPECT_CAP ('wiring is a design step first'), a construction-gate home, a single-leg mode for the two-leg differentials, a ciR: CD-ROM rig and a poisoned CD image 'the battery does not build'. Options: (a) re-date carrying each blocker's evidence, or (b) six design rounds.  If (a), each entry gains the owing round's id -- the checker's own standard is 'an EXEMPTION naming the round that owes it. [2026-11-02, records] The title's six-exit census is e302c98c's; after #564 (e7fc97e6) one remains at 987cb596, DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_mte)'s width else (dev_sgi_re.c:1775), which the witness calls unreachable.

*** MY OWN BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS THAT `gdromcondlies` HELD THE LAST LIVE GUEST-REACHABLE HOST KILLS.  IT IS FALSE, AND THE FIRST FILE I SAMPLED REFUTED IT. ***  I stated it AS A QUESTION in that brief (*'have I confused "the queue knows of no others" with "there are no others"?'*), which is the only reason this was cheap to find -- and I found it myself, before the panel answered.  **THE CENSUS SAID WHERE TO LOOK AND WAS RIGHT.**  `exit_census.py` reports 99 live terminating calls inside `DEVICE_ACCESS` across 30 files; `dev_sgi_re.c` carries **21**, seven times the gdrom file.  It is the top of that list, and I sampled it for exactly that reason.  *** WHAT IS THERE, AND IT IS A CLASS THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY FIXED ELSEWHERE: ***  the guard at the head of the CRIME_RE_TLB_A arm is  `if (len != 8) { fatal("TODO: unimplemented len=%i ..."); exit(1); }`  -- **a GUEST CHOOSING AN ACCESS WIDTH ends the host process.**  That is the `#337` class verbatim, whose own comment in `dev_wdc.c` reads *'a 3- or 8-byte access to the data port used to call exit(1) -- a GUEST choosing an access width killed the host process'*.  The adjacent arm kills on a plain READ (`fatal("TODO: read from CRIME_RE_TLB_A"); exit(1);`), which is the direction/offset class.  **REACHABILITY CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED**: `machine_sgi.c:500` calls `dev_sgi_re_init(machine, mem, 0x15000000)` and the device registers at `baseaddr + 0x1000` through `memory_device_register`.  It is a real device on a real machine, mapped into the guest address space.  **HONEST BOUND ON THE NUMBER, because this project keeps getting counts wrong: 21 is how many live terminating calls sit inside that file's `DEVICE_ACCESS` handlers.**  It is NOT a claim that 21 are individually reachable -- some may be guarded, and `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:1055` (lines of fb0cc783; at 987cb596 :1107-1108, the `Too much GDROM_DATA?` exit) is the standing proof that a `DEVICE_ACCESS` site can be unreachable and take a hand-derived warrant to establish it.  What IS established: at least two of them are reachable by construction, and they are of classes already recognised as defects here.  *** THE GENERAL LESSON, AND IT IS ABOUT THE QUEUE RATHER THAN THIS DEVICE: A QUEUE-COMPLETE CLAIM IS NOT A TREE-COMPLETE ONE. ***  The adjudicating seat flagged exactly this limit about its own answer hours earlier -- *'my no-other-live-host-kills claim rests on the queue and this file's grep, not a fresh tree-wide exit census'* -- and then I wrote the queue-complete version into a brief as a premise anyway.  The seat named the gap; the brief inherited it.  SCOPE: this is a CLUSTER and must not become one round.  The round-scope rule takes ONE site, with a second joining only if it is witnessed, in the same device and semantic class, and covered by the same detector with no new oracle.  The width guards may qualify as one class; the read-direction kills are a second.  **More witnesses create more candidate ROUNDS, never bigger rounds.**  NEXT STEP is a rung-3 witness on ONE site, not a fix: `-E sgi` machines exist in tree, the device is mapped at a known base, and the `#337` precedent gives the fix shape (latched decline, `(once)` marker) if a witness lands.  *** THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE IS INCOMPLETE AND THE TRUE ONE IS WORSE.  Corrected the same day by the opus5 seat, which MEASURED it. ***  This row was filed saying the brief had confused 'the queue knows of no others' with 'there are no others'.  **Neither.  The queue knew of NINE others.**  Ledger row `n6` is OPEN, titled *'The record says the footbridge host-halts were made graceful; nine of them are not'*, carrying a CONFIRMED rung-3 witness (`probe:regress/footbridge_sites_probe.py` row K1, gated in `gate_arm.sh`) and a `state_note` RANKING IT 6th OF 8 on 2026-08-27 -- three days before the brief claimed there were none.  The seat rebuilt HEAD clean and re-ran the COMMITTED probe: a guest `ldr r7,[r0,#392]` on an unmodified `-E cats` ends the host at `dev_footbridge.c:589`.  It then swapped the single planted word three more times and got **four of four** -- `:604` ENABLE_CLEAR read, `:565` IRQ_STATUS write, `:712` SDRAM_BA_MASK read -- each one guest instruction, each with the site's own diagnostic text as the attribution control.  **So this is the UNREAD-ROW class, not a census gap.**  The census work still stands and still found two REAL clusters nobody had filed; what it did not do is what a `grep n6` would have done in one second.  *The lesson is not 'census harder'.  It is that a completeness claim must be checked against THE QUEUE'S OWN OPEN ROWS before it is written down -- and that is the cheaper check of the two.*  *** THE CENSUS IS DONE, AND IT SPLITS THE 21 INTO FOUR CLASSES WITH ONE PROVABLY DEAD SITE.  agy seat, 2026-08-30, `regress/artifacts/widthkillclass/witness_20260830/`. ***  It is a READING, not a measurement, and is recorded as one -- but the single most surprising claim in it was CHECKED HERE BY OPENING THE FILE, and it held.  **20 of 21 guest-reachable; 1 PROVABLY UNREACHABLE.**  WIDTH (a guest choosing an access size ends the host) -- 7 reachable: the `len != 8` guards on CRIME_RE_TLB_A/B/C, CRIME_RE_TEX and CRIME_RE_LINEAR_A/B, plus `sgi_de: len = %i not implemented` (which wants len 4 or 8).  DIRECTION (a legal-width access in the wrong direction) -- 6 reachable: `TODO: read from CRIME_RE_TLB_A/B/C`, `..._TEX`, `..._LINEAR_A/B`, each reached by an 8-byte READ, i.e. **the guest does everything right except the direction**.  BADOFFSET -- 1: the `unimplemented read/write to address` arm, reached by any access to an unregistered sub-window.  BADVAL -- 6: `sgi_de: UNIMPLEMENTED drawing op`, and five `sgi_mte` arms (MTE_MODE_STIPPLE, unimplemented SRC, MTE_MODE_COPY, MTE_DEPTH_x, and an unimplemented bytemask).  *** THE UNREACHABLE ONE IS DEAD CODE AND MUST NOT BE 'FIXED' -- I VERIFIED THIS BY OPENING THE FILE RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT. ***  `[ sgi_mte: UNIMPLEMENTED read/write len %i ]` sits in the trailing `else` of `if (len == 4) { ... } else if (len != 4) { ... } else { fatal; exit(1); }`.  For every integer `len` one of the first two arms is taken, so the third can never execute.  A round that 'de-fatalises' it would be editing unreachable code and its detector could carry no row -- **the vacuous shape in its purest form, and the census is what stops it being attempted.**  **WHAT THIS MEANS FOR SCOPE, and it is the useful part: FOUR classes means at least four candidate rounds, not one.**  The round-scope rule takes ONE site, with a second joining only if it is the same device AND the same semantic class AND covered by the same detector with no new oracle.  A WIDTH guard and a DIRECTION guard sit in the SAME ARM at the same offset and are still different classes -- whether they nonetheless share one fix design is an open question this row does not settle, and it is exactly what the next research pass should answer rather than assume.  HONEST BOUND: reachability here is derived from address-decode reading, NOT measured, except for the WIDTH class -- which now has a rung-3 witness (see `widthkillclass`).  The DIRECTION, BADOFFSET and BADVAL classes have NO witness yet and a round on any of them owes one first.  *** THE COUNT'S SCOPE WAS WRONG AND A SEAT CHECKED IT: 21 IS THE FILE TOTAL, NOT THE HANDLER'S. ***  `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)` holds **13**.  Per handler: sgi_re 13, sgi_de 1, sgi_mte 1, sgi_de_status 0, helpers 6 -- summing to the 21 this row filed.  So the four-class census spans FOUR HANDLERS, not one, and that matters for scope rather than for tidiness: a round joining sites 'in the same handler' is a different population from one joining sites 'in the same file'.  **This is the dropped-qualifier class again** -- the number was right and the noun was wrong, which is exactly how `b120r`'s NIL and `#464`'s 'floods identically' went wrong.  AND THE WIDTH FIGURE OF 7 IS SHORT BY ONE against the message text: there are EIGHT width-shaped kills in the file, the six in sgi_re plus `sgi_de: len = %i not implemented` and `[ sgi_mte: UNIMPLEMENTED read/write len %i ]`.  Both are now filed separately -- `sgidewidth` (LIVE, high) and `sgimtewidth` (a mis-service plus a resurrection trap) -- because they sit in different handlers and so cannot join a sgi_re round.  *** READ-ONLY AUDIT, agy seat, 2026-08-30 -- AND THE HEADLINE IS THAT THIS ROUND MAY BE MUCH SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS: ALL SIX ARMS LOOK LIKE **ACCEPT**, NOT DECLINE. ***  The de-fatalisation option set has four members, and the fourth applies where the model already holds the right answer and merely discards it.  **`re_tlb_a`, `re_tlb_b`, `re_tlb_c`, `re_tex`, `re_linear_a` and `re_linear_b` are all WRITTEN by the store path**, so a read can return what was written -- no latch, no message, because there is no event to announce.  *A bounded-announce here would ship a wrong record in product code: printing 'unimplemented; ignored' about a read that is implemented and is not ignored.*  **REACHABILITY: all six are reachable by an ordinary guest load on unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32`**, and the addresses are derived rather than guessed -- `machine_sgi.c:500` passes base `0x15000000`, `dev_sgi_re_init` registers `sgi_re` at `baseaddr + 0x1000` for `DEV_SGI_RE_LENGTH` (0x1000), and the handler restores the full offset with `relative_addr += 0x1000`.  **Every window lies inside `0x15001000-0x150017ff`, none is shadowed, and the `else if` cascade is strictly disjoint.**  Verified here independently by opening `machine_sgi.c` and `crmfbreg.h`: the six constants are `0x1000 / 0x1200 / 0x1400 / 0x1600 / 0x1700 / 0x1780`.  **GUEST KSEG1 ADDRESSES, so a probe author does not re-derive them:** TLB_A `0xb5001000`, TLB_B `0xb5001200`, TLB_C `0xb5001400`, TEX `0xb5001600`, LINEAR_A `0xb5001700`, LINEAR_B `0xb5001780` -- read kills at lines 245, 262, 279, 296, 346, 362 of 8dd86b5a (removed by #513, e302c98c) respectively.  **One malloc serves all four handlers** (`dev_sgi_re_init` allocates one `struct sgi_re_data` and hands it to `sgi_de`, `sgi_mte` and `sgi_de_status`), so whatever latch infrastructure `#497` lands is already reachable here.  *The audit and the brief that produced it are preserved at `regress/artifacts/sgirekills/audit_20260830/` -- the ledger first cited the `_scratchpad/` copy, which the durable-path rule excludes precisely because it evaporates.  This row now has everything a rung-3 witness needs except the witness itself, which is the point of asking a seat for the addresses rather than the answer.*  *** THIS ROW'S TITLE SAID '21 TERMINATING CALLS INSIDE DEVICE_ACCESS' AND THAT WAS THE SAME CONFLATION I MADE AND CORRECTED ELSEWHERE TODAY.  Corrected 2026-08-30. ***  **21 is the FILE total.  15 are inside a `DEVICE_ACCESS`, and 13 of those in `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)`** -- the other 6 live in `draw_primitive` (1) and `do_mte_transfer` (5), neither of which is a `DEVICE_ACCESS` and neither of which a guest reaches by an ordinary access.  *** AND THE TITLE WAS NOT CARELESS -- IT FAITHFULLY REPORTED WHAT THE TOOL SAID, WHICH WAS WRONG. ***  See `exitcensus`: `exit_census.py`'s per-file totals were correct all along, but its BY-ENCLOSING-CONSTRUCT split attributed every call in a plain non-static function to the preceding `DEVICE_ACCESS`.  That bucket is a REACHABILITY claim used for ranking -- *on a guest access path BY CONSTRUCTION* -- so the defect over-stated how many host kills a guest can actually reach.  Fixed; tree-wide the bucket falls **97 -> 83**.  *** THE ACCEPT DESIGN, ADJUDICATED 2026-08-30 -- AND IT REFUTES THE AUDIT RECORDED DIRECTLY ABOVE IT ON ONE ARM OF SIX. ***  **agy ruled ACCEPT for all six read arms on the ground that BACKING STATE EXISTS in the struct.  That is not the ACCEPT test.**  The doctrine's fourth option-set member -- minted from the footbridge IRQEnable precedent -- is *the model already computes the CORRECT answer and merely discards it*.  Existence of state is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.  **FIVE ARMS ARE CLEAN ACCEPT; TEX IS NOT.**  **TLB A/B/C:** the store packs big-endian halfword pairs from raw bus bytes and a readback through the same index expression round-trips BYTE-EXACTLY on this machine -- with a premise that belongs in the comment rather than assumed: `machine_sgi.c` pins BIG ENDIAN, and while the STORE path is byte-order-agnostic the READ path is not.  **LINEAR A/B:** the store splits `idata` into two uint32 cells and the readback is its exact inverse through the `readmax64`/`writemax64` pair -- byte-order symmetric BY CONSTRUCTION, so it needs no endianness premise at all.  *** TEX FAILS THE TEST, AND THE EVIDENCE IS A GREP: `re_tex` HAS ZERO CONSUMERS ANYWHERE. ***  `tlb_a/b/c` feed `horrible_getputpixel`; `linear_a/b` feed it and `do_mte_transfer`; **`re_tex` feeds nothing.**  Its state is written through the `>> 3` index that `sgitexindex` records as a defect -- frames overlap by three, 81 of 112 cells unreachable -- so **the model does not hold the right answer for TEX; it holds a self-consistent WRONG one.**  ACCEPT is available only in the MIRRORED form (the read uses the same `>> 3` expression), which round-trips per frame while shipping hardware-wrong reads at overlapping offsets.  **That is a materially weaker claim than the other five arms', and the round record must not blur them.**  **WHAT ACCEPT OWES THAT DECLINE DOES NOT -- five items, and the second is an ORDERING DEPENDENCY on `#497`:**  (1) **round-trip rows with DISTINCT sentinels per window** -- distinctness catches a cross-wired read, while a same-window index error breaks round-trip because the store frame is position-dependent.  The JOINT translation (store and read shifted together) escapes round-trip BY CONSTRUCTION -- clause (f) territory -- so the contract names it outside, and names honestly that an out-of-decode anchor channel exists for four arms (the rendering and MTE paths consume them) and **does not exist for `re_tex` today**.  (2) **a DEVICE-SIGNATURE control**, because a faithful round-trip through a device is value-indistinguishable from RAM -- the witness ladder's own two-control lesson.  The clean discriminator: **post-`#497` a 4-byte read DECLINES and returns 0 while RAM would serve it.**  So `#497` is an ordering dependency for this round's WITNESS QUALITY, not merely for its latch infrastructure.  (3) **the dead tail's first execution belongs to `#497`, not here.**  A width-declined READ falls through the splice and runs `memory_writemax64` with `odata = 0`.  This round's new surface is narrower than it looks: **NONZERO `odata` through the BE packing**, not 'the tail runs'.  (4) **the claim must be SCOPED**: *returns what the store path recorded*, never *faithful hardware readback*.  TEX refutes the stronger phrase today, and the LINEAR arms store the PROM's own wrongly-sign-extended values verbatim -- returning them faithfully is right; modelling hardware readback is unproven.  **That is `b716a34`'s lesson pre-applied: do not put the strong phrase in a site comment.**  (5) **a PRE-WRITE read row** returning 0, which pins the memset-init as guest-visible ABI and is the minimal de-fatalisation survival row.  *** TEX POISONS THE WARRANT, NOT THE ROUND -- AND THE COUPLING IS ENFORCEABLE BY ONE ROW RATHER THAN BY A DEPENDENCY. ***  Ship TEX MIRRORED plus its round-trip row, and any ONE-SIDED future fix reds that row loudly: store `>> 1` against read `>> 3` writes cells 4-7 and reads 1-4, and the reverse likewise, while the JOINT fix keeps identity and the row stays green.  **So the round-trip row IS the coupling enforcement**, and `sgitexindex`'s fix becomes a declared two-site edit with a tripwire already in place.  Recorded in BOTH rows.  **WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE:** unmirrored `>> 1` reads over the `>> 3` store -- round-trip broken immediately, silent wrong data, worse than a decline -- or ACCEPT recorded with the same warrant strength as the other five arms.  **A LATENT THIS ROUND INHERITS RATHER THAN CREATES:** the TLB arms mask the INITIAL `tlbi` but increment it UNMASKED in the loop, so `relative_addr & 0x1ff >= 0x1fa` with `len 8` runs to index 0x102 -- three halfwords into the adjacent array.  Guest-unreachable for the alignment reason `sgilinearoob` settles path-by-path, and **a mirrored read arm makes it a second SITE of that class** -- record it there so an eventual bound fixes both directions.  *** THE TEST THAT KILLED `sgideoob` WAS THEN APPLIED TO THE SURVIVORS, BY ENUMERATION RATHER THAN BY REASONING -- AND BOTH HOLD.  2026-08-30. ***  Withdrawing a false member is only half the follow-through; the other half is asking whether the same miss is in the rows that remain.  The refuting method for `sgideoob` was *what is this index's ACTUAL RANGE?* -- so every reachable `relative_addr` in each window was walked and the resulting index recorded.  **TLB LOOP** (`re_tlb_a[256]`, `tlbi = ((ra & 0x1ff) >> 1) & 0xff`, four writes at `len 8`): with 8-byte ALIGNMENT -- the only thing a guest can produce -- the maximum index written is **255, IN BOUNDS**.  Unaligned, reachable only by the debugger's `put d`, it is **258, OOB by three halfwords**.  *Exactly as recorded: guest-unreachable, debugger-reachable, same disposition as `sgilinearoob`.*  **`sgitexindex`** (`re_tex[112]`, `tlbi = ((ra & 0xff) >> 3) & 0xff`, window `0x1600-0x16df`): maximum index written is **30, comfortably IN BOUNDS of [112]** -- so this row is NOT an out-of-bounds and never claimed to be.  Its three stated figures were each re-derived independently and all match: **81 cells unreachable**, **3 entries of overlap** between consecutive 8-byte writes.  *** SO THE CLASS AFTER THE WITHDRAWAL IS: TWO REAL OOBs (`sgilinearoob`, the TLB loop), BOTH GUEST-SHIELDED BY ALIGNMENT AND BOTH DEBUGGER-REACHABLE; ONE NON-OOB CORRECTNESS DEFECT (`sgitexindex`); AND ONE WITHDRAWN FALSE MEMBER. ***  Every one now tested by the same method, which is what the false member's whole lesson was.  *** THE WITNESS FIELD WAS STALE AND SAID THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT SHIPPED.  Corrected 2026-08-30 by the pass-2 seat. ***  It read *no rung-3 probe has been built and the round owes one before any edit* -- **false since `#497` shipped six `ld kill` rows**, each a real guest `ld` at one of the six windows, dying with per-site attribution text, on an unmodified machine.  The row's note mentioned them nowhere.  *** AND THE SAME ROWS CHANGE THIS ROW'S COST IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, WHICH MUST BE WRITTEN DOWN NOW RATHER THAN REDISCOVERED: FIXING THIS DEFECT WILL TURN A GREEN GATE RED BY SUCCEEDING. ***  Six rows' worth.  That is precisely the `n6` shape adjudicated hours earlier in this same session, so this round inherits its ordering obligation: **re-pin the six rows FIRST, measure the committed build RED under the new expectations, and only then edit** -- same scripts, opposite colour.  Without that order the re-pin is observationally identical to fitting the test to the binary.  *** THE HEADLINE COUNT INCLUDES ONE SITE THAT CAN NEVER EXECUTE.  Derived 2026-08-30. ***  `dev_sgi_re.c` holds 20 raw `exit(1)` lines; exactly FIVE are commented out (179, 188, 280, 630, 1122) and fifteen are live -- **including 1334, which is inside `sgi_mte`'s unreachable `else` (see `sgimtewidth`).**  **`exit_census.py` excludes COMMENTED-OUT code and cannot see REACHABILITY.**  That is correct behaviour for a text-level tool and it is a limit worth stating rather than discovering: "live terminating calls" means SYNTACTICALLY live.  The row's numbers are not wrong -- they are the census's numbers -- but a round quoting them as reachable host kills would be over-claiming by one.  *** THE `sgirekills` / `sgitexindex` COUPLING, ESTABLISHED 2026-08-31 AND RECORDED ON BOTH ROWS SO NEITHER CAN BE CLOSED IN IGNORANCE OF THE OTHER. ***  **The fact, which is settled:** `sgitexindex`'s `>> 1` is correct under BOTH candidate readings of a TEX entry -- 112 halfwords indexed `offset >> 1`, or 28 64-bit entries where entry `k` starts at halfword `4k`, since `(offset >> 3) * 4 == offset >> 1` for 8-aligned offsets.  **So the store's shift is wrong INDEPENDENTLY of the missing datasheet**, and there is no SGI document in `_scratchpad/`.  **Consequence for `sgirekills`:** its TEX read arm can only ACCEPT in the MIRRORED form -- reusing the store's `>> 3` -- because only that round-trips what the store wrote.  Mirroring therefore enshrines a KNOWN-WRONG index in a second place, and gives it a green round-trip row.  *When someone later corrects the shift, that row goes RED because of their correct fix.*  **Consequence for `sgitexindex`, in the other direction:** the TEX read arm is TODAY a live host kill, so **no guest can read back what those writes stored** and the aliasing is currently unobservable from inside the guest.  Fixing `sgirekills` is what would expose it.  That bears on severity and on ORDER, and neither row had recorded it.  *Neither consequence decides the disposition -- that is the question `sgirekills` is held for and a panel is answering it.  What is recorded here is the COUPLING, which is a fact either way.*  *** THE HELD TEX-READ QUESTION IS ANSWERED: DO NOT MIRROR.  3 of 3 packet-fed seats, and the dissenter's FALLBACK is the other two's first choice, so the convergence is total. ***  deepseek and minimax: **decline + latched announce** until the index fix lands.  glm: **BACKED ACCEPT with the CORRECT `>> 1` index**, round-trip oracle pinned to correct semantics and honestly red until `sgitexindex` lands -- *with decline + latched announce as its explicit fallback, and mirrored ACCEPT ranked worst of the three by all three seats.*  **MY PREMISE WAS CIRCULAR AND A SEAT SAID SO USING MY OWN INLINED FINDING.**  See its entry above. That is why all three seats land on decline as at least an acceptable answer.*  **AND ONE OBJECTION OF ITS OWN IS ANSWERED BY A GUARD I FAILED TO INLINE.**  glm marked the *31 of 112 / overlap by three* arithmetic NOT SETTLEABLE because it presupposes 8-byte-wide 8-byte-aligned stores, asserted nowhere in the packet. entries.note: *** REFUTED THE BRIEF'S CENTRAL PREMISE AS CIRCULAR, using the finding the brief itself inlined. ***  I wrote that mirrored is the ONLY ACCEPT form.  That holds only if ACCEPT is STIPULATED to mean *round-trip the current `>> 3` store*.  Since `>> 1` is correct under both entry-size readings, **an ACCEPT in CORRECT form is constructible today**; what is impossible is only a read that is SIMULTANEOUSLY hardware-right and round-trip-faithful to the unfixed store.  *The premise ruled out the third option by definition -- the question was begged, and the six-member set even names the member (BACKED ACCEPT).*  **And its P2 destroys mirroring's advertised benefit**: I called the mirrored readback *self-consistent but hardware-wrong at overlapping offsets*, and BOTH halves are misstated. Wrongness is not confined to overlaps -- mirrored index `m` diverges from correct `4m` at EVERY offset >= 8.  And self-consistency holds only in single-store isolation: with the overlap-by-three the brief itself states, a store at +8 lands in `re_tex[1..4]` and one at +16 in `[2..5]`, so a mirrored read at +8 returns a MIX of two stores -- not *what the store actually wrote*.  **Mirroring's benefit exists only for a guest that writes one slot and reads it back before touching another.**

A null-medium control is vacuity-floor clause (c); if those rounds ran one and did not preserve it, the receipts are owed, and if they did not run one, the clause was unmet.  Either way it is checkable and nobody has checked it.  It re-confirms the historical tables as honest (19/19 baseline, 5/19 pre-fix, 14/19 for the zero-status termination variant, 13/19 for suppressed announcement, 18/19 for each latch/bit-alias variant; the L2 table 21/21 -> 19/21 for mask widening) and re-confirms `sgimtewidth' as the smallest live implementation defect it could establish independently: a one-byte MTE store of 0x5a takes the two-word branch, writes 0x0000005a to the selected word and ZEROES the following one.  *** AND I TRIED TO CHECK THAT CLAIM TWICE AND BOTH DERIVERS WERE MIS-KEYED, which is this project's own `key on what defines the class, not a correlate' lesson landing on me an hour after I quoted it. ***  First attempt keyed on FILENAMES (`-iname '*null*'`): it returned ZERO for all four rounds INCLUDING `#497', which the seat says HAS a preserved receipt -- so the search was measuring whether anyone had put the word in a filename. TWO ADJACENT NON-WIDTH kills were found in the same pass and are NOT this class: a BADVAL (`pcc2: C040 interrupt assertions... TODO`, reachable by a BYTE write of 0x04 to GENCTL, which the alignment rule does not touch) and a BADOFFSET (`pcc2: unimplemented %s offset`). rows.title: a probe row whose oracle is 'the store had no effect' PASSES when the store never executed -- seven of #496's twenty-two rows, and the class is tree-wide
rows.witness: harness: derived row-by-row against regress/gdrom_cond_probe.py by the fable5 seat in #496's adjudication pass; NOT yet exhibited by a run, which is why it files rather than reopening #496
rows.note: *** THE SEED SENTINEL PROTECTS LOADS.  STORES HAVE NO EXECUTION WITNESS, AND SEVEN OF `gdrom_cond_probe.py`'s TWENTY-TWO ROWS PASS IF THEIR CRITICAL STORE NEVER RUNS. ***  Named by the fable5 seat in `#496`'s ADJUDICATION pass, as a REFINE on the round's own F11.  **THE SHAPE.**  `#496` added `SEED = 0xdead` so an unexecuted LOAD is distinguishable from a load that genuinely read zero -- and `bit()` returns `SEED-NEVER-RAN` so the sentinel cannot itself be misread as a set bit.  Both are right and both are about the READ side.  A row whose oracle is the CONSEQUENCE OF A STORE has no equivalent: if the store silently fails to execute, the device stays in its fresh state -- **and for these rows the fresh state IS the want.**  The seven, with why each is green on a dead store: `R5b cond 00` (cond stays 0x0 = want); `R7 no event` (event stays clear = want); `R7b cond st` (before == after trivially); `R10 a88 nop` (0x0|0x0|0 = want); `R3 a88 x3` and `R4 cond x3` (one live store plus two dead ones still yields count == 1 = want); `R5c cond a0`.  **R1, R2, R5, R6, R8, R9 FAIL SAFE** -- their wants are values only a live store produces.  *** WHY THE CONTROLS DO NOT COVER IT, which is the whole reason this is a class and not a note. ***  The four control rows catch a WHOLE-RUN-DEAD rig, and they are per-run.  The contention actually measured on `#496` was PER-SESSION INTERMITTENT -- the probe forks one gxemul per row, so a single row's session can die while every other row and all four controls run fine.  A per-run control cannot see a per-session failure.  **NOT A FLOOR BREACH, and the reasoning matters because it is what keeps this from being an in-round fix.**  Every enumerated mutant still reds WHEN THE APPARATUS RUNS, and no run has yet exhibited the false pass.  It is a latent apparatus risk, not a measured escape -- so it FILES under the stopping rule rather than reopening `#496`.  *** THE SKETCH, from the seat, and it costs nothing for five of the seven: assert the decline announce -- already in the transcript, count == 1 -- inside the SAME row's got string. ***  That announce is the store's own execution proof: it cannot appear unless the guest store reached the device handler.  `R10` needs a trailing canary decline instead (it has no announce of its own, by construction -- silence IS its oracle).  **`R3` and `R4` are the hard pair and no cheap form is known**: a MID-SEQUENCE store death leaves count == 1, which is exactly the want, so the announce trick is circular there.  Those two need a distinguishable per-store marker or a different oracle shape, and that is the part worth a round rather than a rider.  GENERALITY: this is not specific to gdrom.  **Any pty-driven probe in this tree whose oracle is 'the device state did NOT change' has the same hole**, because not-changing is what a dead session produces.  A sweep is NOT proposed here -- the population is unmeasured and a sweep would be `#392`'s shape.  What is proposed is the write-time question: *for each row, what does a dead session score?*  If the answer is the want, the row needs an execution witness.  *** THE COUNT WAS WRONG AND IS AT LEAST NINE, NOT SEVEN.  codex seat, same day, under the standing license while adjudicating something else. ***  **`R12` is an eighth**: its oracle is the presence of the no-data diagnostic after a declined COND write, and a FRESH device has `cond == 0` -- so if the declining store never executes, the subsequent DATA read produces exactly the wanted diagnostic anyway.  **`R13` is a ninth**, and it is the worst of them because it drives NINE stores: if the second `0xa0` or any of the first six DATA words is missed, the mutant never reaches the kill guard and the oracle still reads `0|exit0`.  *A row that drives a longer sequence has MORE ways to die silently, not fewer* -- which inverts the intuition that a richer row is a stronger row.  **THE SKETCHES ARE PER-ROW AND CHEAP FOR BOTH.**  `R12`: additionally require its own COND-decline announcement, which no dead store can produce.  `R13`: prove the BUSY TRANSITIONS rather than the absence of a kill -- set after the first `0xa0`, clear after six words, set again after the second `0xa0` -- so a missing store reds on a transition that did not happen instead of passing on a kill that did not happen.  Both are execution witnesses in the row's own channel, which is the shape the original sketch already proposed for the other five.
rows.state_note:
*** A codex CENSUS WAS FIRED 2026-09-08 AND CUT SHORT BEFORE DELIVERING THE COUNTS -- BY MY OWN
REPEAT OF A SCOPE ERROR I HAD RECORDED ONE BRIEF EARLIER.  Its partial findings are below and three
of them are new. ***

**THE MEMBERSHIP DEFINITION IT GAVE IS THE BEST STATEMENT OF THIS CLASS YET, and it is the property
rather than any correlate:**

> *"A row belongs in this census if its own oracle can pass when the tested action is OMITTED; it is
> already paired only if another check ON THAT SAME ACCESS requires positive evidence AFTER the
> action."*

It said so explicitly of the trap: *"a label such as `survives' or `unchanged' does not decide
membership"*, and *"some negative assertions include a required readback in the same predicate,
while others rely on a separate row or only on process status."*

*** A FOURTH GUISE I HAD NOT NAMED, and it is subtler than the three in this row: ***

> **"exactly one message across two or more accesses."  The FIRST access can supply the one message
> even if a LATER access never runs.**

The row looks positive -- it asserts a message is PRESENT, not absent -- and is still satisfied by a
skipped action, because the evidence was produced before the skip. *That defeats the obvious repair
for this whole class, which is "pair the negative oracle with a positive one": a positive oracle
sited BEFORE the action under test is no better than a negative one.*

*** TWO CONCRETE SITES NAMED, both of which a text search would miss: ***
* **the CMMU probe prints a row labelled "VALUE" whose return path grades only SURVIVAL** -- the
  label claims more than the oracle delivers;
* **some ARM flag rows reduce the untouched-output sentinel to a SINGLE BIT that matches the
  expected answer**, so the sentinel cannot distinguish untouched from correct.

Both are unverified here and are recorded as LEADS, not findings.

*** AND IT NOTICED ME EDITING A PROBE WHILE IT WAS READING IT. ***  Its words: *"I detected a change
to `lca_confbus_probe.py` while reading it.  I'm taking an in-memory snapshot of the permitted probes
so the final row names, counts, and line references all describe one consistent version.  No probes
have been run or files changed."*  **This project records the edit-a-running-script hazard for
SHELL and for a multi-run PYTHON driver; this is the same hazard from the READER's side**, and the
seat handled it correctly and said so. *A seat that had silently continued would have produced line
references spanning two versions of one file.*

*** WHY IT WAS CUT SHORT, AND IT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE `exit0oracle' FIRING ONE BRIEF EARLIER. ***
I wrote the scope as `regress/*.py -- the probe files only`, which is not a bound at all: it is the
whole directory. The stream reached **2.4 MB** and stopped at the snapshot step without ever
producing the per-file table.

**I had recorded the fix in [[exit0oracle]] within the hour** -- *"A READING-SCOPE BOUND MUST BE
EXTENSIONAL.  Name the files."* -- and then wrote the next brief with a glob. That is this project's
own finding about itself, exactly: knowing a rule and having it fire on the object in front of you
are different problems, and only the second is solved by writing the rule down.

**RE-FIRE OWED**, with the file list stated extensionally and the membership definition above given
as settled so the budget goes to the census rather than to re-deriving it.

rows.note: *** MEASURED 2026-08-30: A 38 KB BRIEF LOST TWO SEATS, AND `panel.sh` PRINTED A WARNING AND FIRED THEM ANYWAY. ***  `WARNING: brief is 38983 bytes (>30KB). Codex/Kimi take it on argv and may fail with 'Argument list too long'. Trim, or point those seats at the file path instead of piping its contents.`  Then it launched all seven, and:      codex.txt  ->  `.../codex: Argument list too long`   (123 bytes)      kimi.txt   ->  `.../kimi: Argument list too long`    (97 bytes)  **grok survived because it uses `--prompt-file`**, which the carrier already names as the one CLI seat immune to this; the three Ollama seats POST and have no argv at all.  So the loss is exactly the two seats that take the brief on the command line.  *** THE DEFECT IS THAT THE WARNING IS ADVISORY. ***  It correctly diagnoses the problem, correctly names the remedy, and then does the thing it just warned about.  That is one step milder than the check-that-cannot-fail this project names first -- it INFORMS and does not ACT -- and the operator it informs is the same party who just wrote the brief and is about to walk away while nine seats run.  **The failure surfaces minutes later as two ~100-byte seat files, which the seat check reports as a seat failure rather than as a launcher failure.**  **THE REMEDY IS ALREADY IN THE WARNING'S OWN TEXT and costs nothing at run time: when the brief exceeds the cap, pass codex and kimi a SHORT PROMPT NAMING THE FILE PATH instead of the contents.**  Both accept it -- recovered by hand in this incident, in one command each, and both then answered.  The file-reading seats can read the brief; only the packet-fed ones need it inlined, and those are the ones with no argv limit.  *** NOT FIXED IN THE MOMENT, DELIBERATELY: a panel was running, and editing a running shell script corrupts it mid-execution -- bash reads incrementally by byte offset. ***  That is a documented defect class here and the reason this is a filed row rather than an in-passing edit.  **WHAT THE FIX OWES, since it changes the script every panel runs:** two negative controls, in the shape this project already requires -- prove an oversized brief now reaches both seats and they ANSWER, and prove a normal-sized brief still goes on argv unchanged (so the switch does not silently become the default and change what every seat receives).  *Note the cap is not exactly 32 KB and the warning threshold is 30 KB; the measured failure was at 38,983 bytes and no bisection was done, so the true boundary is not established and this row does not claim one.*  *** FIXED 2026-08-30.  `panel.sh` WARNED ABOUT THE ARGV CAP AND THEN LAUNCHED ANYWAY -- the remedy its own message recommended was one the script could simply TAKE. ***  A 38 KB brief killed BOTH argv-fed seats with `Argument list too long`; codex and kimi had to be recovered BY HAND, while this block printed advice sixty lines above the launch that ignored it.  **IT IS THE CHECK-THAT-CANNOT-FAIL FAMILY'S SIBLING: a message reporting an ACTION the code does not take.**  The re-firing message (`re-firing once (a wall can be minutes long) ...` followed by a `return 2` every caller discards) is the same defect, and its recorded lesson applies unchanged -- telling the operator it was handled is WORSE than silence, because the one person who could fix it by hand is told not to.  **THE FIX IS THAT BOTH SEATS ALREADY READ FILES.**  Grok has been immune all along (`--prompt-file`), agy too (`--add-dir` plus a pointer prompt); codex and kimi were the only two still fed the brief on argv.  Above the cap they now get `PTR_PROMPT` -- read `$BRIEF_ABS` and review it as its own Questions section directs -- and below it the inline form is byte-unchanged.  **CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the control READS THE REAL FILE rather than a re-typed copy** -- `sed` extracts the decision block and the prompt-build out of `panel.sh` and `eval`s them, because a verification that shares the defect of the thing it verifies always passes, which this project has measured.  POST-FIX **6/6, rc=0**, including both boundary rows (exactly 30000 -> inline, 30001 -> pointer) and a both-seats-agree column.  PRE-FIX the same script reports **EXTRACT FAILED, rc=9** -- *the old form has no cap branch at all* -- which is the failability proof: the test can fail, and it fails on the code this fix replaces.  `PANEL_ARGV_CAP` exists ONLY so the branch is testable without keeping a 38 KB fixture, and the comment says so; it is not a tuning knob.  *** AND THE GATE CAUGHT A RECORD DEFECT I MADE WHILE CLOSING THIS ROW: I wrote the fix up as a ledger ENTRY with `seat: mainloop`. ***  There is no such seat -- the declared vocabulary is the nine, and `mainloop` appeared exactly ONCE in 2,278 entries, mine.  **A seat entry is what sections G and H COUNT for panel coverage, so inventing one inflates the roster with a seat that never answered** -- the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape reached from the other side, by manufacture rather than by omission. rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c's CRIME_RE_TEX index uses >> 3 where its three sibling arms use >> 1 -- consecutive writes overlap by three entries and 81 of 112 are unreachable
rows.witness: harness:ENUMERATED against the shipped source, 2026-08-30.  Walked every 8-byte access in [0x1600,0x16e0): shipped base indices run 0..27, reaching 31 of 112 cells, leaving 81 unreachable, with a 3-entry overlap between consecutive accesses.  Both figures in the row reproduce EXACTLY.
rows.note:
*** A GUEST WRITING THE TEXTURE ARRAY SEQUENTIALLY CORRUPTS ENTRIES IT HAS ALREADY WRITTEN, AND 81 OF 112 ENTRIES CANNOT BE REACHED AT ALL.  Found by the codex seat under the STANDING LICENSE while answering a scope question about a different defect in the same file. ***  **THE EVIDENCE IS THE SIBLING COMPARISON, and it is as strong as this kind of finding gets: three arms of the same handler do it one way and the fourth does it another.**  `CRIME_RE_TLB_A`, `_TLB_B` and `_TLB_C` each compute their index as  `int tlbi = ((relative_addr & 0x1ff) >> 1) & 0xff;`  -- a BYTE offset shifted right by 1 to give a HALFWORD index.  `CRIME_RE_TEX` computes  `int tlbi = ((relative_addr & 0xff) >> 3) & 0xff;`  on an array of the same kind, `uint16_t re_tex[112]`.  **THE ARITHMETIC, and it is decidable from the declaration alone.**  The window is `relative_addr >= CRIME_RE_TEX && < CRIME_RE_TEX + 0xe0` -- 224 bytes -- and 112 halfwords is exactly 224 bytes, so window and array correspond one-to-one.  The write loop steps `tlbi++` once per halfword, so an 8-byte `sd` writes FOUR entries.  But `>> 3` advances the STARTING index by only ONE per 8-byte step:      offset 0x00 -> tlbi 0, writes 0,1,2,3      offset 0x08 -> tlbi 1, writes 1,2,3,4   <- OVERLAPS THREE      offset 0x10 -> tlbi 2, writes 2,3,4,5   <- OVERLAPS THREE  So consecutive aligned writes overwrite three quarters of their predecessor.  And the top of the window, `0xdf >> 3` = 27, reaches index 30 at most: **entries 31..111 are unreachable by any access.**  **`>> 1` gives exactly the right answer at both ends**, which is what makes this a typo rather than a design: `0x00 >> 1` = 0, and `0xdf >> 1` = 111 -- precisely the last valid index.  The three siblings already use it.  *** THIS IS NOT THE WIDTH-KILL CLASS AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. ***  `widthkillclass` is a guest ENDING THE HOST by choosing an access size; this is SILENT DATA CORRUPTION inside a legal, correctly-sized access.  Different class, different fix, different detector -- and the round-scope rule's same-semantic-class arm fails, so it files rather than joining `#497`.  **Arguably worse in one respect and better in another:** it is silent, so nothing announces it and a guest gets wrong texture data rather than a dead emulator; but it corrupts only emulated device state, where a host kill ends the process.  Ranked med on that trade, not high.  *** WHAT A ROUND HERE OWES, and one of them is a trap: ***  a rung-3 witness (the machine and window are already established -- `-E sgi -e ip32`, `dev_sgi_re_init(machine, mem, 0x15000000)`, so TEX is at guest `0xb5001600`); and **an ADJACENT-OFFSET oracle, because a naive 'the sd changed something' accept row STAYS GREEN under this defect** -- the write does land, just in the wrong cells and on top of its neighbour.  The row has to write two adjacent 8-byte groups and read back the FIRST, which is the only shape that sees an overlap.  SOURCE-DERIVED, NOT MEASURED.  The seat said so explicitly and this row repeats it: no probe has been run against TEX.  The arithmetic is checkable from the declaration and was re-verified here against the three sibling arms, but the behaviour has not been observed on a running guest.  *** THE COUPLING TO `sgirekills` IS ENFORCEABLE BY ONE ROW, SO THIS IS NOT A HARD PREREQUISITE.  Adjudicated 2026-08-30, recorded in both rows. ***  If `sgirekills` ships TEX's read arm MIRRORED -- using the same `>> 3` expression as the store -- then a ONE-SIDED fix of this row reds its round-trip row loudly: store `>> 1` against read `>> 3` writes cells 4-7 and reads 1-4, and the reverse likewise, while the JOINT fix keeps identity and the row stays green.  **So this row's fix becomes a DECLARED TWO-SITE EDIT with a tripwire already in place**, rather than a change that could silently half-land.  **AND THE ORDER IS GENUINELY FREE, with a real trade either way**: this row first makes TEX's ACCEPT identical in kind to the TLB arms, and its own red-first witness needs no readback at all because the store loop's `debug("d->re_tex[%i] = ...")` lines already show the index.  `sgirekills` first is licensed by severity -- host kills outrank silent corruption -- and hands this row a strictly stronger witness afterwards, since a write-write-read overlap can then be observed through real readback.  *** RE-DERIVED BY ENUMERATION 2026-08-30, after a sibling row in this family was WITHDRAWN as a false out-of-bounds. ***  All three of this row's figures were walked rather than reasoned: every `relative_addr` in `0x1600-0x16df` mapped through `((ra & 0xff) >> 3) & 0xff` with four writes per access.  **Maximum index 30 -- so this row is NOT an OOB and does not claim to be**; `re_tex[112]` has ample headroom.  **81 cells unreachable** and **3 entries of overlap** between consecutive 8-byte writes, both matching the filed claim exactly.  *The withdrawn sibling was filed source-derived and never range-checked; this one now has been.*  *** CONFIRMED BY ENUMERATION AND RE-DIAGNOSED: IT IS A UNIT MISMATCH, NOT A WRONG SHIFT. ***  The codex seat derived the TEX geometry from the CRIME spec -- 28 entries of 64 bits at 0x1600 + 8n -- and my walk of the shipped code found base indices running exactly 0..27.  **Independent agreement on 28, one from the specification and one from the source.**  28 x 8 = 224 = 0xe0 (the window bound) and 28 x 4 = 112 (the array), so `re_tex` is 28 entries of FOUR HALFWORDS each.  **`>> 3` therefore selects the ENTRY correctly.  The array is indexed in HALFWORDS, and entry n begins at halfword 4n -- so the code writes [n],[n+1],[n+2],[n+3] where it must write [4n]..[4n+3].**  Verified over all 28 entry starts that `(addr & 0xff) >> 1` is identically `4 * ((addr & 0xff) >> 3)`, so the three siblings' `>> 1` IS the correct expression.  **NOT A MEMORY-SAFETY DEFECT** -- max index 30 against a [112] array.  Model correctness only: the guest's texture data lands in the wrong cells and clobbers its own previous write.  *The fix comment matters more than the edit here: `>> 1 because re_tex is halfword-indexed and each 64-bit entry spans four halfwords` survives a future reader, while `>> 1 to match the siblings` invites someone to "fix" the siblings instead.*  *** THE NATURAL OBJECTION TO THE PROPOSED `>> 3` -> `>> 1` FIX IS THAT IT COULD RUN OFF THE END OF A [112] ARRAY.  CHECKED 2026-08-31: IT CANNOT, AND THE MARGIN IS EXACTLY ZERO. ***  Recorded because an unanswered overflow objection is what stalls a one-token fix at review, and because "exactly zero margin" is a fact the fixing round must know rather than rediscover.  With `>> 1` the index is the halfword offset: window `[0x00, 0xe0)`, so `tlbi` spans 0..111 and the array is `uint16_t re_tex[112]` -- one-to-one, as the sibling comparison predicts.  The write loop steps `tlbi++` per halfword, so an 8-byte `sd` writes FOUR entries.  **The worst case is the last legal 8-byte slot.**  8-byte accesses are 8-ALIGNED (the guest path cannot deliver an unaligned `len == 8` -- ordinary `ld`/`sd` raise ADEL/ADES without calling `memory_rw`, and the `ldl/ldr/sdl/sdr` helper masks the address itself), so the reachable offsets are `0x00, 0x08, ... 0xd8`.  At `0xd8`: `tlbi = 0xd8 >> 1 = 108`, writing **108, 109, 110, 111** -- the last four entries, and `0xd8 + 8 = 0xe0` is exactly the window bound.  **Fits with nothing to spare.**  *The zero margin is why this is worth writing down rather than waving through: `0xdc` would give `tlbi = 110` and write 110..113, two entries past the array -- so the fix's safety rests ENTIRELY on the 8-byte alignment invariant, exactly as the LINEAR arms' own `#497` comment says theirs does.*  A round shipping this owes the same alignment note the LINEAR arms already carry, and its detector owes an accept row at the LAST slot (`0xd8`) -- which is the window's far bound, and per the 2026-08-31 correction to the accept-row rule, a SECOND row or an ANCHORED oracle for the near bound.  *** PASS-1 PACKET-FED PANEL, 2026-08-31 (`_scratchpad/panel_20260831_045142`): THE CORE CLAIM IS UPHELD BY THREE INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS, AND THE ZERO MARGIN IS CONFIRMED TWICE. ***  Reachability: **31 of 112 entries, 81 unreachable** -- glm and deepseek both derived 31 independently and it matches this row's original figure; minimax wrote 30/82 and is off by one (`[0,30]` is 31 entries).  **glm named a premise the brief never stated and I had assumed**: the whole `& 0xff` analysis needs `CRIME_RE_TEX` to be 256-aligned.  Checked: `0x1600`, so it holds, and every sibling window's mask matches its own base as well.  **minimax supplied a better warrant than the one I led with**: `112 x 2 = 224 = 0xe0` is an INTRINSIC identity between array size and window size, where the sibling comparison is merely comparative and can be answered with *maybe TEX is different on purpose*.  **The fixing round should lead with the size identity.**  **deepseek answered the detector-design question**: no index-only mutant survives a detector that writes and reads back EVERY halfword, so full distinctness closes the clause-(f) hole here.  **MY BRIEF CARRIED A COUNT DEFECT, caught by two seats independently**: it said *four* windows compute an index and then inlined *six*.  Immaterial to the arithmetic and it is precisely the class the brief's own opener warns about -- recorded rather than quietly fixed.  *** STILL UNSETTLED, AND THE SEATS WERE RIGHT NOT TO SETTLE IT: whether hardware might legitimately space texture registers every 8 bytes.  There is no datasheet for this device in `_scratchpad/`.  That question decides FIX vs DOCUMENT and is the one thing a file-reading seat or a manual could still change.***  *** THE PANEL'S ONE OPEN QUESTION IS NOW CLOSED WITHOUT A DATASHEET, AND THE DISPOSITION IS FIX RATHER THAN DOCUMENT.  Derived 2026-08-31. ***  All three seats correctly declined to settle *whether hardware might legitimately space texture registers every 8 bytes*, and `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` confirms there is **no SGI, CRIME, IP32 or O2 document** among the fifteen present.  **But the question turns out not to gate the fix, because BOTH candidate readings give the SAME index expression.**  *(a)* the struct's own declaration -- `uint16_t re_tex[112]`, indexed by halfword -> `offset >> 1`.  *(b)* the rival reading the missing spec would license -- **28 x 64-bit entries, one per 8-byte store**.  The write loop emits FOUR halfwords per store, so entry `k` must START at halfword `4k`, i.e. the correct index is `(offset >> 3) * 4`.  **For 8-ALIGNED offsets `(offset >> 3) * 4` IS `offset >> 1`** -- checked across the window (0x00->0, 0x08->4, 0x10->8, 0x40->32, 0xd0->104, 0xd8->108, identical both ways).  *** SO `>> 1` IS CORRECT UNDER BOTH HYPOTHESES AND `>> 3` IS WRONG UNDER BOTH -- under (b) it is short by exactly the factor of 4 that the loop consumes. ***  **This also strengthens minimax's intrinsic-identity warrant rather than replacing it.**  That argument (`112 x 2 = 224 = 0xe0`) depends on the `uint16_t` CHOICE being right, and the header does not confirm it: `crmfbreg.h` carries an explicit `/* 32bit entries ... */` comment for **LINEAR_A/B and not for TEX**, so the element size there is GXemul's own reading.  *The both-hypotheses derivation is the stronger form precisely because it does not need the element size to be settled at all.*  **And the window bound is confirmed from the header rather than from the guard**: the next register is `CRIME_RE_CLIP_IDS = 0x16e0`, so `[0x1600, 0x16e0)` really is 224 bytes and the guard's `+ 0xe0` is not an invention.  *What is still genuinely unknown, and is now a DOCUMENTATION question rather than a blocker: how many entries the real device has and how wide they are.  The fix is right either way; the array's declared type is a separate, smaller question that no evidence in this tree settles.*  *** THE `sgirekills` / `sgitexindex` COUPLING, ESTABLISHED 2026-08-31 AND RECORDED ON BOTH ROWS SO NEITHER CAN BE CLOSED IN IGNORANCE OF THE OTHER. ***  **The fact, which is settled:** `sgitexindex`'s `>> 1` is correct under BOTH candidate readings of a TEX entry -- 112 halfwords indexed `offset >> 1`, or 28 64-bit entries where entry `k` starts at halfword `4k`, since `(offset >> 3) * 4 == offset >> 1` for 8-aligned offsets.  **So the store's shift is wrong INDEPENDENTLY of the missing datasheet**, and there is no SGI document in `_scratchpad/`.  **Consequence for `sgirekills`:** its TEX read arm can only ACCEPT in the MIRRORED form -- reusing the store's `>> 3` -- because only that round-trips what the store wrote.  Mirroring therefore enshrines a KNOWN-WRONG index in a second place, and gives it a green round-trip row.  *When someone later corrects the shift, that row goes RED because of their correct fix.*  **Consequence for `sgitexindex`, in the other direction:** the TEX read arm is TODAY a live host kill, so **no guest can read back what those writes stored** and the aliasing is currently unobservable from inside the guest.  Fixing `sgirekills` is what would expose it.  That bears on severity and on ORDER, and neither row had recorded it.  *Neither consequence decides the disposition -- that is the question `sgirekills` is held for and a panel is answering it.  What is recorded here is the COUPLING, which is a fact either way.*

*** MAIN-LOOP MEASUREMENT 2026-08-31 (not a seat answer; recorded here rather than in `entries` so it cannot be counted toward the panel). ***  evidence: grep -rn re_tex src/ (3 occurrences, all dev_sgi_re.c)

MEASURED BY GREP, 2026-08-31, settling hold_question (1) and reframing (3): `re_tex' occurs EXACTLY THREE TIMES in the whole tree, all in dev_sgi_re.c -- the declaration, ONE write site, and a debug() on the very next line echoing what was just stored.  Nothing else in src/ mentions it.  *** SO THE `>> 3' ARM IS THE SOLE WRITER (question 1: YES, the fix's assumption holds and changing it repairs rather than splits the mapping) AND THE ARRAY HAS NO CONSUMER ANYWHERE IN THE MODEL. ***  That is stronger than the row's own framing, which says only that no GUEST can read it back because the READ arm is fatal+exit: even with that arm de-fatalised there is nothing else that consumes the array, so the aliasing's only channel today is the debug() text.  Consequence: it lowers this row (no consumer, no observable corruption) and couples it to `sgirekills', whose mirrored-TEX-read fix would create the array's FIRST consumer.  Severity change and ordering NOT applied unilaterally -- referred to the adjudicator, and hold_question (2) referred to a non-author seat because it asks for exactly that.  A NEW sub-question was raised by the grep and sent with it: the both-hypotheses derivation needs `relative_addr' 8-ALIGNED, and the arm's guard is `len != 8' which does NOT imply alignment -- the same premise that made an earlier census wrong by 4x.

entries.ev: dev_sgi_re.c re_tex[112] then re_linear_a[32]; debugger_cmds.c put d = printf not guard; sgi_re_width_probe.py stores at base+8 greps re_tex[1]; sgi_re_unmapped_probe.py 0x6d8 greps re_tex[27]
entries.outcome_note:
*** TWO SEATS, TWO FINDINGS, AND THEY DISAGREED ON A CHECKABLE FACT.  Settled by opening the files; the adjudicator was right and the reading seat was wrong. ***

FINDING 1 (reading seat, VERIFIED): the proposed >> 1 fix would INTRODUCE a new OOB write.
  >> 3 is bounds-safe UNCONDITIONALLY -- at every in-window offset it yields indices 27..30, always inside re_tex[112].  >> 1 is bounds-safe ONLY UNDER 8-ALIGNMENT.  Computed: at offset 0xdf (or 0xde) the loop writes halfword indices 111, 112, 113, 114 -- and the struct declares uint16_t re_tex[112] immediately followed by uint32_t re_linear_a[32], so 112..114 land IN re_linear_a.  Silent, in-struct, ASAN-invisible: the sgilinearoob class, newly created by a hardening fix.
  AND THE UNALIGNED ROUTE EXISTS.  MIPS guest paths enforce alignment before memory_rw.  The DEBUGGER does not: put d prints WARNING: address isn't aligned -- a printf, NOT a return -- and proceeds to store_64bit_word, whose memory_rw carries CACHE_DATA with no NO_EXCEPTIONS, so a DM_DEFAULT handler IS invoked.  Verified by reading the arm.
  DESIGN CHANGE ADOPTED: make the precondition LOCAL rather than inherited from another file --
      if (len != 8 || (relative_addr & 7))     /* the existing SGIRE_W_TEX_LEN latch */
  Under the addition licence, trading an unconditionally-safe index for a conditionally-safe one on the strength of an invariant argued in a DIFFERENT FILE and known to have an exception is not a licensed trade.

FINDING 2 (adjudicator, VERIFIED, and it CORRECTS finding 1's companion claim): the reading seat said the committed detector is structurally blind because every TEX row sits at in-window offset 0 where every shift maps to 0.  **THAT IS FALSE.  TWO COMMITTED ROWS ALREADY PIN THE >> 3 DECODE:**
    regress/sgi_re_width_probe.py   -- its accept row stores at base + 8 and greps re_tex[1]; a correct >> 1 decode gives re_tex[4]
    regress/sgi_re_unmapped_probe.py -- its last-slot row uses in-window 0xd8 and greps re_tex[27]; a correct >> 1 decode gives re_tex[108]
  The seat appears to have read the width probe's TABLE ENTRY (which lists the base address) without following to the store, which is at base + 8.  Settled by opening both files.
  CONSEQUENCE, and it is an obligation rather than a note: **fixing the shift REDS BOTH ROWS**, so the oracle-correction rule governs -- re-pin FIRST, measure the committed build RED under the new expectations (re_tex[1] -> [4], re_tex[27] -> [108]), THEN change the code.  Enumerate that re-pin set in PRETABLE.out BEFORE table 1, re-pinned deliberately rather than discovered red.

A STRONGER WARRANT that needs neither a datasheet nor the alignment premise, and should lead the row: the loop advances tlbi++ PER HALFWORD, so tlbi IS a halfword index, and the halfword index of a byte offset is offset >> 1.  >> 3 makes the start expression advance one per 8 bytes while the body advances one per 2 -- DIFFERENT UNITS.  Decidable from four lines, at any offset.

TWO DEFECTS IN THE EXISTING WARRANT.  (1) The row's end-point argument is demonstrated at offset 0xdf -- an UNALIGNED offset where the fix is WRONG; the correct end point is the last 8-aligned offset 0xd8 -> 108..111.  Conclusion survives, warrant does not.  (2) sgilinearoob states the premise in the FALSE form: len == 8 forces 8-byte alignment.  It forces nothing.

SEVERITY: MED -> LOW, and the downgrade is CONDITIONED, not free.  The MED warrant sentence -- the guest gets wrong texture data -- is refuted: re_tex is the only one of six register arrays in the file with no reader, and it is not a reader-not-yet-written but storage for a function the model does not implement (horrible_getputpixel has no TEX case; the MTE's MTE_TLB_TEX falls to default).  **RE-PROMOTE the day any consumer is proposed** -- a sgirekills TEX read-back, real RE texture rendering, any new dump channel -- and the fix must land BEFORE that consumer.

*** ORDERING: THE SEVERITY ORDER INVERTS.  This LOW row runs FIRST, as a prerequisite of the HIGH one. ***  LOW is the label; first is the schedule; the two are severed deliberately, because ranked LOW and left in severity order it would sit behind the round that depends on it.  Cost is about zero calendar time -- sgirekills still owes its own rung-3 witness and that work parallelises with this small shift round.
