*"An eight-byte LENGTH does not establish eight-byte ALIGNMENT or whole-transfer containment.  Under
`>> 1`, an unchecked start near the window's end can make the four-cell write exceed the array."*

Enumerated over EVERY offset in `[0, 0xe0)`, not just the aligned ones, with the loop's four writes:

    >> 3  (today)                 worst cell index  30   IN BOUNDS
    >> 1  (the proposed fix)      worst cell index 114   *** OOB on uint16_t[112] ***

Offset `0xdf` starts at 111 and writes 111..114.  **So the "obviously right" shift correction turns
a benign unreachable-cells bug into a memory-safety defect** -- and the arm has no bounds mask of
its own: `& 0xff` cannot help, because 111 is already inside the mask.

**AND THE UNALIGNED ACCESS IS REACHABLE.**  The device callback does NOT enforce alignment; the arm
relies on CPU-side mechanisms, and the DEBUGGER bypasses them -- `debugger_cmds.c:1549` prints
*"WARNING: address isn't aligned"* and **continues**.  *That is the same operator-reachable path
`pcc2widthkills` already measured for `put h`.*

> **SO THE FIX IS `>> 1` PLUS AN EXPLICIT BOUNDS POLICY, NOT `>> 1` ALONE.**  This is the addition-
> licence lesson inverted: not "one more line cannot hurt" but "one CHANGED character cannot hurt",
> and it could.

### 2.  MY "UNDER NOTHING ELSE" CLAIM WAS WRONG, AND THE REAL READING IS BETTER

I argued `>> 1` from the sibling arms and from `0xe0 == 112 * 2`.  codex found an EXTERNAL primary
source -- the SGI CRIME specification -- listing **`TLB.tex[28]` as 28 separate 64-bit registers**,
immediately followed by the clip-ID registers.  **So the `>> 3` reading is not arbitrary: it matches
the hardware's REGISTER numbering.**

**It still does not rescue the loop.**  For aligned byte offset `o`: register number is `o / 8`, and
the first cell of that register in a FLAT `uint16_t[112]` is `4 * (o / 8)` -- which is `o / 2`.

> **The defect is precisely a MISSING FACTOR OF FOUR between register number and backing-cell
> number.**  `>> 3` would be correct for `uint64_t[28]` or for the first dimension of
> `uint16_t[28][4]`; it is wrong for a flat array incremented once per halfword.

*That is a materially better statement of the defect than "the sibling uses `>> 1`", and it changes
what a comment on the fix should say.*

### 3.  THE DETECTOR OPTION I HAD NOT NAMED -- and the tree already uses it

I listed three unattractive options and asked for a fourth.  It is **execute the production handler
directly against a fixture and inspect the private state**, which `regress/diff_rtc_range.c:101`
already does by including the device source and calling its handler.

The regression it specifies: write distinct halfwords into NEIGHBOURING aligned registers and
require both groups to retain their values; exercise all 28 registers and compare all 112 cells
against an independently specified expected sequence; and **require it to FAIL with the original
shift restored AND with writes suppressed** -- floor clauses (b) and (a).

**Its honest scope, in codex's words:** it establishes *"backing-store mapping coverage"* and
*"neither guest rendering correctness nor a guest round-trip witness"*.  **So the witness field stays
`none` even with the host regression shipped, and the ladder's `detector:` term is what applies.**

### 4.  ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN FRAMING

*"Initialization still zeroes the whole array, so 'never written' would be too broad."*  The 81 cells
are unreachable through TEX WRITES; they are not uninitialised.  **My phrasing implied the latter.**

*** THE FIX DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE CRIME SPECIFICATION, WHICH IS NOT ON THIS MACHINE.  Derived
2026-09-08 from `crmfbreg.h` and the struct, both local. ***

I flagged S2 -- *"`>> 3` matches the hardware's 28 x 64-bit register numbering"* -- as the premise I
was least sure of, because it rests on a specification cited by ONE SEAT and `ls _scratchpad` shows
no CRIME document here.  **That premise is not load-bearing, and the header settles the fix without
it.**

    window        span                 / element   array declared
    TLB_A/B/C     0x1200-0x1000 = 0x200  /2 = 256   uint16_t re_tlb_a[256]
    TEX           0x16e0-0x1600 = 0xe0   /2 = 112   uint16_t re_tex[112]
    LINEAR_A/B    0x1780-0x1700 = 0x80   /4 =  32   uint32_t re_linear_a[32]

**EVERY array in this file is sized to its window under its sibling's indexing convention**, and
`re_tex[112]` is exactly `0xe0 / 2`.  Given the array is `uint16_t[112]` and the store loop
increments ONCE PER HALFWORD, `>> 1` is the only index consistent with the declaration.

> **BOTH READINGS FIT THE WINDOW SIZE -- 28 registers x 8 bytes is also 224 -- so the window alone
> cannot choose between them.  What chooses is the ARRAY TYPE.**  So the CRIME claim, if true, tells
> us what the HARDWARE calls these; it does not change what this code must do with a flat
> `uint16_t[112]`.  *It belongs in the fix's COMMENT, not in its warrant.*

*This is the difference between a fact that is load-bearing and one that is merely interesting, and
it is worth separating BEFORE the round leans on the wrong one: a second-hand citation in the
warrant would have made the fix only as good as a document nobody here has opened.*

*** THERE IS A STANDING FLAGSHIP RULING ON THIS ROW AND IT WAS NOT IN THIS ROW.  I SPENT A ROUND
PREPARING TO VIOLATE IT.  Recorded here 2026-09-08, where the next reader will actually look. ***

**2026-09-02 flagship adjudication** (`regress/artifacts/pcc2widthkills/fable_adjudication_20260902.md`,
and `CHANGELOG.md`), verbatim:

> *"`sgitexindex` -- **DO NOT CODE and DO NOT DROP**: close DOCUMENTED-ONLY (`witness: none -- no
> consumer, no channel`), reopen condition named; six-window single round REFUSED (multi-class
> bundle)."*

**THE REOPEN CONDITION, which is the operative part:** *"the first round that gives `re_tex` a
CONSUMER settles the scale against that consumer, not by sibling analogy."*  Nothing has given it
one, so the condition is unmet and the row stays closed to code.

*** AND THE RULING ALREADY CONTAINED WHAT I "FOUND" TODAY. ***  It says the proposed `>> 1` fix
*"would IMPORT the siblings' overrun."*  I re-derived that this evening by enumeration, wrote it up
as a new finding, and built a panel brief around it.  **The enumeration is worth having -- it puts
numbers on it (cell 114 of a `[112]` array, worst case over all offsets) -- but the CONCLUSION was
already adjudicated and I did not know.**

> **WHY I MISSED IT, and it is a records defect rather than carelessness: I read the LEDGER ROW,
> which is where a row's disposition belongs, and the ruling was in the CHANGELOG and an artifact.**
> The row said `state: open`, `sev: low`, with no note about the close.  *A standing DO-NOT-CODE
> that lives anywhere except the row it governs will be re-opened by the next person who reads the
> row -- which is the whole population of people who might re-open it.*

**Two seats caught it and I did not:** grok opened the prior adjudication before answering
(*"the prior adjudication closed this as documented-only ... do not code, do not drop"*), and it
FETCHED the CRIME 1.5 specification rather than trusting my S2 -- confirming Table 7-2 lists

UNIFORM across the device (64 x 64-bit fbA -> `uint16_t[256]` with `>> 1`; 16 x 64-bit linearA ->
`uint32_t[32]` with `>> 2`).  **So S2 is now CONFIRMED FROM THE SPECIFICATION rather than being the
premise I flagged as least certain -- and it makes the DO-NOT-CODE stronger, not weaker.**

**DISPOSITION: unchanged.  The round is STOPPED.**  `>> 1` is the right mapping for the current

*** THE PANEL SPLIT 4-1 AND IT IS NOT 4-1 ON ONE QUESTION.  COUNT THE ARGUMENTS, NOT THE SEATS. ***

    grok                              FIX-DOCUMENTED-ONLY
    deepseek, glm, kimi, minimax      FIX-WITH-BOUNDS-POLICY

**The four packet-fed seats did not know a standing ruling existed -- MY BRIEF DID NOT INLINE IT,

rows.title: sgi_mte serves EVERY access width and a one-byte store silently ZEROES the adjacent register -- and the obvious fix for its dead arm would CREATE a width kill
rows.witness: harness:READ and ENUMERATED against the shipped source, 2026-08-30.  The handler is `if (len == 4) ... else if (len != 4) ... else { fatal(); exit(1); }` -- the final else is UNREACHABLE.  Bounds enumerated separately: `relative_addr &= ~CRIME_DE_START` (0x800) caps regnr at 511 against `mte_reg[1024]`, so there is NO out-of-bounds access.
rows.note: *** A ONE-BYTE GUEST STORE TO AN MTE REGISTER WRITES THE REGISTER **AND SILENTLY ZEROES ITS NEIGHBOUR**.  Found by the fable5 seat under the standing license, verified here by reading the arms. ***  The handler is `if (len == 4) {...} else if (len != 4) {...} else {...}`.  The second arm does:      d->mte_reg[regnr+1] = idata >> 32;      d->mte_reg[regnr]   = idata;  and it is reached by EVERY width that is not 4 -- including 1 and 2.  For a one-byte store `idata` is a byte, so `idata >> 32` is **0**, and the store clobbers `mte_reg[regnr+1]` with zero.  No diagnostic, no decline: the device quietly loses a register the guest never addressed.  **THIS IS A MIS-SERVICE, NOT A KILL**, which is why it is med and not high: nothing ends the host, and the corruption is confined to emulated device state.  *** THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE REASON TO FILE THIS NOW RATHER THAN WHEN SOMEONE TOUCHES IT: the dead third arm is `fatal("[ sgi_mte: UNIMPLEMENTED read/write len %i ]"); exit(1);` -- unreachable for every integer len, as `sgirekills` records.  It DOCUMENTS AN INTENT to reject unusual widths.  A naive future repair of the unreachable-arm defect -- reordering to `len==4 / len==8 / else` -- would RESURRECT THAT exit(1) AS A LIVE WIDTH KILL. ***  So when the unreachable arm is worked it must land as a DECLINE, never as a revived exit, and this row exists to say so before the edit rather than after.  *Two defects in one arm structure, pointing opposite ways: today it serves widths it should refuse, and the obvious tidy-up would make it kill on widths it currently serves.*  *** THE IMPLEMENTING SEAT RE-DISCOVERED THIS ARM INDEPENDENTLY ON 2026-08-30 AND PROPOSED IT AS A NEW ROW (`sgimtedeadwidth`).  FOLDED HERE, NOT FILED -- it is this row, found from the other direction. ***  It arrived via the SIBLING-PARITY check on a different round, where this row came from a pass-1 reading; that two routes reach the same arm is corroboration, not two defects.  **WHAT THE RE-DISCOVERY ADDS, and it is worth folding in:** the precise extent (`dev_sgi_re.c:1162-1178`, the unreachable `exit(1)` at `:1177`), and a COUNT this row did not carry -- **the file has EIGHT width-guard sites by text but only SEVEN LIVE ones**, because this arm's `else` can never be entered.  Verified here by opening the file: `if (len == 4) {...} else if (len != 4) {...} else { fatal(); exit(1); }`, and the second condition is the exact negation of the first.  *A duplicate row would have split one defect's evidence across two ids and let a future round close one while the other stayed open -- which is the failure the queue-id rule already names.  Adjudicated FOLD.*  *** CONFIRMED, AND THE MECHANISM IS BETTER THAN THE ROW SAID: THE WIDTH GUARD IS DEAD CODE. ***  Reaching the final `else` requires `len != 4` and `len == 4` at once, so it can never execute.  Every non-4 width falls into the 64-bit path, which does `mte_reg[regnr+1] = idata >> 32; mte_reg[regnr] = idata;` -- and a one-byte store has `idata < 256`, so the adjacent register is silently ZEROED.  **So it is not that the handler "serves every width"; it is that the guard written to refuse them cannot run.**  *** NOT A MEMORY-SAFETY DEFECT, and this was checked SPECIFICALLY because the same question was answered WRONG on `sgideoob` two days ago: *** the `&= ~CRIME_DE_START` mask caps `regnr` at 511 and `mte_reg` is `[DEV_SGI_MTE_LENGTH / 4]` = `[1024]`, so `regnr+1` reaches 512 with 512 slots of headroom.  Enumerated, not argued.  **CONSEQUENCE FOR RANKING, so no round over-claims: fixing this removes a data-corruption defect and a piece of dead code.  It does NOT remove a host kill, because that kill was never reachable.**  A round closing it and reporting "one fewer host kill" would be writing a wrong record.  *Its sibling `sgi_de` is shaped `len == 8 / len == 4 / else`, so THAT else IS reachable and `sgidewidth` is a real kill.  The two handlers differ in exactly the way that matters.*

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c: FIVE arms write past a CAPPED index on an unaligned len==8 access -- TLB_A/B/C overrun uint16_t[256] BY THREE (a wider overrun than the LINEAR arms this row was filed for, and unrecorded until 2026-09-08), LINEAR_A/B overrun uint32_t[32] by one.  ONE fix design covers all five; the sixth arm (TEX) is in bounds only because its index shift is WRONG
rows.witness: none -- source-derived arithmetic over the shipped index expression, re-verified against the struct declaration.  UNREACHABLE at HEAD: the len==8 guard forces 8-byte alignment, capping tlbi at 30.  A witness is only possible on a build that permits len==4, i.e. it cannot be witnessed without first introducing the defect.
rows.note:
*** THE WIDTH GUARD `#497` IS ABOUT TO REMOVE IS CURRENTLY HOLDING AN OUT-OF-BOUNDS WRITE SHUT.  Found by the opus5 seat while auditing whether `len != 8` should be DECLINED or IMPLEMENTED; every element re-verified here by opening the file. ***  **THE ARITHMETIC.**  Both LINEAR arms compute  `int tlbi = ((relative_addr & 0x7f) >> 2) & 0x1f;`  -- so `tlbi` ranges 0..31 -- and then write BOTH `[tlbi]` AND `[tlbi+1]` into  `uint32_t re_linear_a[32];` / `uint32_t re_linear_b[32];`  **At tlbi == 31 the second store writes index 32, one past the end.**  **IT IS UNREACHABLE TODAY FOR EXACTLY ONE REASON: the `len == 8` requirement forces 8-byte alignment.**  `(0x78 & 0x7f) >> 2` = 30, so the largest reachable tlbi is 30 and `tlbi+1` is 31 -- the last valid index.  Permit `len == 4` and offset `0x7c` gives `(0x7c & 0x7f) >> 2` = **31**, and `[32]` is written.  **WHERE IT LANDS, from the declaration order** (`re_tlb_a`, `re_tlb_b`, `re_tlb_c`, `re_tex`, then `re_linear_a[32]`, `re_linear_b[32]`, then `de_reg[]`): `re_linear_a[32]` overlays `re_linear_b[0]`, and `re_linear_b[32]` overlays the start of `de_reg[]` -- **a DIFFERENT ENGINE'S REGISTERS.**  Stated from the struct layout, which is a layout fact and not a guarantee: a reorder changes which field is hit, not whether the write is out of bounds.  *** THIS IS WHY `#497` MUST DECLINE RATHER THAN IMPLEMENT, and it converts a stylistic preference into a measured-from-source argument. ***  The brief asked whether `len != 8` is 'secretly an IMPLEMENT case'.  It is not: implementing narrower widths at the LINEAR arms would MAKE THIS OOB LIVE.  The round's warrant is therefore not merely 'the model does not implement this' but 'the guard is load-bearing memory-safety today'.  **AND IT IS THE SECOND SUCH FACT IN THE SAME AUDIT.**  The TLB/TEX store loop reads `data[hwi]*256 + data[hwi+1]`, so a `len == 1` access reads `data[1]` -- one byte past the CALLER'S buffer.  Two different over-reads, both held shut by the same guard, neither noticed until a seat was asked whether the guard could be relaxed.  *** SO THE ROUND OWES A SENTENCE, NOT A ROW. ***  `#497` does not touch these lines and cannot make the OOB live -- a latched decline keeps `len == 8` mandatory.  What it owes is a comment saying WHY the guard is mandatory, so a future round that reads 'unimplemented width' as an invitation to implement one is warned at the site rather than in a queue file.  **The absence record's warrant is the alignment constraint, and any edit touching that constraint re-runs the death measurement.**  SOURCE-DERIVED, NOT MEASURED: no probe has driven a 4-byte LINEAR access, because the shipped code kills the host before reaching the store.  The reachability argument is arithmetic over the shipped index expression and was re-derived here independently of the seat's report.  *** THE LAYOUT FACTS IN THIS ROW ARE RIGHT AND MY CHARACTERISATION OF THEM WAS AN OVERCLAIM.  MEASURED 2026-08-30 by the implementing seat, which refused to ratify the brief's wording and ran `offsetof` instead. ***  **DERIVER: `offs.c` compiled and run, preserved beside the round's artifacts** -- `re_linear_a` at 1760, `re_linear_b` at 1888, `de_reg` at 2016; `re_linear_a[32]` IS `re_linear_b[0]` at +0 bytes, and `re_linear_b[32]` IS `de_reg[0]` at +0 bytes.  So this row's layout claims are CONFIRMED by measurement rather than derived from declaration order.  **WHAT WAS WRONG IS THE PHRASE I BUILT ON THEM: 'load-bearing HOST memory safety'.**  The over-run lands INSIDE the same allocation, on the adjacent register array.  The honest characterisation is **UB by the C standard (a write past the end of an array object) AND a SILENT CROSS-ARRAY CORRUPTION** -- a RENDERING-engine write reaching a DRAWING-engine register.  It is **NOT a wild write outside the allocation, NOT a host crash, and plain ASAN WOULD NOT FLAG IT because it is intra-object.**  *** THE CONSEQUENCE IS WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PEDANTRY: the brief instructed the seat to put that phrase in a SITE COMMENT.  Shipping it would have been an L4 wrong record IN PRODUCT CODE, which is the worst place to put one*** -- a future reader would reach for ASAN to catch a regression ASAN cannot see, and would rank the defect as a host crash when it is silent corruption.  The seat's own comment says the measured thing.  *Two premise audits in one day, both against me, both settled by running something rather than by arguing: the census (grep counted commented-out code) and this one (offsetof against a phrase).*  *** 'UNREACHABLE TODAY' IS PRECISELY 'NOT GUEST-REACHABLE', AND THE DISTINCTION IS A TRAP FOR WHOEVER TRIES TO WITNESS THIS. ***  Settled 2026-08-30 path by path: every guest route to an 8-byte access is alignment-enforced -- `ld`/`sd` raise ADES/ADEL before `memory_rw` is called at all, and `ldl`/`ldr`/`sdl`/`sdr` coerce with `aligned_addr = addr & ~(wlen-1)` before every one of their three `memory_rw` calls.  **But the host debugger's `put d` prints `WARNING: address isn't aligned` and then PROCEEDS**, passing the unaligned address to `store_64bit_word` and into `memory_rw`.  So this OOB IS reachable from the debugger and is NOT reachable from a guest.  **That does not give this row a witness -- it takes one away.**  Rung 3 requires a real guest instruction through real address decode; `put d` bypasses the guest instruction path, so a `put d` reproduction would be laundering, not witnessing.  The honest position is unchanged: **this defect cannot be witnessed without first introducing it**, and the debugger route is worth recording only so nobody mistakes it for a way out.  *** THE CLASS THIS ROW ANCHORS WAS BRIEFLY OVERSTATED TO THREE MEMBERS AND IS BACK TO TWO.  Corrected 2026-08-30 by the second review pass. ***  `sgideoob` was filed as a third member and **WITHDRAWN as a false OOB**: `de_reg`/`mte_reg` are sized to the FULL window `[1024]` while `relative_addr &= ~CRIME_DE_START` HALVES the index range to 511, so `regnr+1` has 512 slots of headroom.  **THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT SURVIVES IS BETTER THAN THE ONE IT REPLACES: is the array sized to the INDEX RANGE or to the FULL WINDOW?**  Sized to the index range and the `+1` overflows -- `re_linear_a[32]` against `tlbi & 0x1f`, this row; `re_tlb_x[256]` against a 255-capped index with a `+3` loop, recorded on `sgirekills`.  Sized to the full window and the over-sizing is what prevents it.  *The earlier phrasing -- arity fixed by access width, index bounded only by the offset mask -- was true of the real members and did not distinguish the false one.*

*** MAIN-LOOP MEASUREMENT 2026-08-31 (not a seat answer; recorded here rather than in `entries` so it cannot be counted toward the panel). ***  evidence: debugger_cmds.c put d arm; cpu_mips_instr_loadstore.c alignment return

*** THIS ROW'S PREMISE IS STATED IN A FALSE FORM AND IS LOAD-BEARING.  Corrected 2026-08-31. ***
It reads: unreachable today for exactly one reason: len == 8 forces 8-byte alignment.  **len == 8 forces nothing.**  What enforces alignment is the MIPS INSTRUCTION PATH, and there is a documented EXCEPTION: the debugger's put d prints a WARNING -- a printf, not a guard -- and proceeds to store_64bit_word, whose memory_rw carries CACHE_DATA with no NO_EXCEPTIONS and so reaches a DM_DEFAULT handler.  The site comment in dev_sgi_re.c states this correctly, naming both mechanisms and the exception; it is the OUTSTANDING_BUGS shorthand that is wrong.
CONSEQUENCE: this row and sgitexindex both rest on the premise, and sgitexindex's proposed >> 1 fix would CREATE a member of THIS row's own class at unaligned offsets -- which is why that fix now ships with a local alignment guard instead.
rows.state_note:
*** THIS ROW HAD A BARE TITLE AND AN EMPTY NOTE, AND IT COVERED THREE OF ITS FIVE ARMS.  Extended
2026-09-08 while checking siblings BEFORE fixing `sgitexindex' -- which is the check `#510' skipped
when it repaired two of three sites of one idiom. ***

**THE WHOLE CLASS, enumerated over EVERY offset in each window (not just the aligned ones), with the
store loop's own write count:**

    arm          aligned max   ANY offset   array          verdict
    TLB_A/B/C        255          258       uint16_t[256]  *** OOB BY THREE ***
    LINEAR_A/B        31           32       uint32_t[32]   OOB by one   (what this row was filed for)
    TEX               30           30       uint16_t[112]  IN BOUNDS -- see below

**The shape is identical in all five:** the index is masked to the array's last element
(`& 0xff`, `& 0x1f`), and then the loop writes `tlbi`, `tlbi+1`, ... **past** it.  An ALIGNED store
lands exactly at the top; an UNALIGNED one starts at the cap and runs off the end.

*** AND THE TLB OVERRUN IS THE BIGGER ONE, WHICH IS WHY MISSING IT MATTERS. ***  This row was filed
about the ONE-cell LINEAR overrun; the THREE-cell TLB overrun sat unrecorded in the same function,
in three arms, with the same predicate holding it shut.

**REACHABILITY is the same for all five and is OPERATOR, not guest:** the device callback does not
check alignment, the MIPS instruction paths supply it, and the DEBUGGER does not -- `put d` at a
misaligned address prints *"WARNING: address isn't aligned"* and CONTINUES
(`debugger_cmds.c:1549`).  *That is the same operator path `pcc2widthkills` measured for `put h`.*

*** THE TEX ARM IS IN BOUNDS ONLY BECAUSE ITS INDEX IS WRONG, AND THAT IS A TRAP FOR THE FIX. ***
`sgitexindex` proposes correcting `>> 3` to `>> 1`.  Enumerated: the corrected form reaches cell
**114 on a `uint16_t[112]` array** -- so **fixing the index defect CREATES the sixth instance of
this OOB class**, which is why that row's fix must ship with a bounds policy and not alone.

> **THE TWO ROWS ARE THEREFORE COUPLED AND THE ORDER MATTERS.**  A bounds policy adopted here covers
> TEX in advance; a `>> 1` shipped first without one adds a memory-safety defect the same day.

*Not filed as a new row: same device, same semantic class, one fix design -- which is exactly the
round-scope rule's join condition, and filing a second row would have split one fix across two.*

*** ONE CORRECTION TO THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE: "unrecorded until 2026-09-08" IS TOO STRONG. ***  The
2026-09-02 flagship adjudication of `sgitexindex` refers to *"the siblings' overrun"* as a known
thing when refusing the `>> 1` fix.  **So the CLASS was known to that adjudication.**  What was
missing is narrower and still worth fixing: **the row that carries this class named only the LINEAR
arms**, and had an empty note, so the TLB arms' three-cell overrun was not findable from the row.

*The distinction matters because it changes what the defect is: not "nobody knew", but "the record
that governs this class did not contain it" -- the same shape as the DO-NOT-CODE ruling that lived
outside the row it governs.*

*** THE REACHABILITY CLAIM IS NOW VERIFIED END-TO-END IN SOURCE, not asserted from the arm's own
comment.  2026-09-08. ***

The overrun needs an UNALIGNED access with `len == 8` to reach the handler.  The arm's comment says
alignment is supplied by two independent CPU-side mechanisms, and that is true of the INSTRUCTION
paths.  **The debugger is neither of them, and the path is three hops with no check in any of them:**

    debugger_cmds.c:1549   `put d' on an odd address prints "WARNING: address isn't aligned"
                           and FALLS THROUGH -- it does not return
    debugger_cmds.c:1558   calls store_64bit_word(cpu, addr, data) with the address UNCHANGED
    memory.c:763           store_64bit_word packs eight bytes and calls
                           cpu->memory_rw(..., addr, data, 8, MEM_WRITE, ...).
                           *** IT PERFORMS NO ALIGNMENT AND NO SPLIT. ***

So the handler receives an unaligned `relative_addr` with `len == 8`, the width guard passes (it
tests LENGTH, not alignment), and the index reaches its cap with three writes still to come.

> **OPERATOR-REACHABLE, NOT GUEST-REACHABLE -- and that distinction is why this stays `med`.**  A
> guest cannot do it: the MIPS instruction paths align, and the unaligned helper masks the address
> before dispatch.  It takes a debugger command.  *`pcc2widthkills` measured the same operator path
> for `put h` and reached the same conclusion.*

*Recorded because I had asserted this from the arm's own comment when I extended the row, and the
comment is about the CPU paths -- it does not mention the debugger at all.  The claim happened to be
right; the warrant I gave it was not one I had checked.*

rows.title: check_probe_wiring.py's selftest builds 7 of its 22 mutants by SUBTRACTING from the live EXEMPT table, so the table emptying -- the outcome it exists to drive toward -- turns SELFTEST_PASS 22/22 into FAIL 12/22
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED BY THE PASS-2 SEAT, both directions.  Empty EXEMPT table -> `PROBEWIRING_SELFTEST_FAIL 12/22`.  And the REMEDY is measured too: an ADDITION-built `M3x` (insert an exemption for the already-wired arm_flags_probe.py, expect STALE EXEMPTION) scores `ok` on that same empty table.  Logs: regress/artifacts/gdromcondlies/opus_p2_20260830/
rows.note: *** THE HARNESS PUNISHES PROGRESS, AND TWO REPAIRS HAVE NOW MOVED THE PUNISHMENT WITHOUT REMOVING IT. ***  The selftest first broke when `pit8253_latch_probe.py` was wired and its exemption deleted; `_pick_exempt_detector()` fixed that by DERIVING the exemplar.  It broke again when `sh4_bsc_width_probe.py` was discharged; deriving M5c-M5e and M12 fixed that.  **Both repairs kept the same shape -- pick a live exemption and take something away from it -- so the tripwire moved from the FIRST discharge to the LAST one.**  **THE ROOT CAUSE, named by the seat in one sentence: the selftest MUTATES LIVE INPUT DATA IT DOES NOT NEED.**  A mutant that must find a real exemption to delete is coupled to a table designed to empty; a mutant that INSERTS its own fixture is not.  M9's machinery already does exactly this for the gate list, so the pattern is in-tree rather than invented.  *** THE END STATE IS REACHABLE AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A ROUND: *** six exemptions remain, all dated 2026-09-20.  When the last is discharged -- which is the point of the table -- `precommit_check.sh` prints THE PROBE-WIRING CHECKER CAN NO LONGER BE SHOWN TO FAIL and blocks the commit that did the right thing.  *** SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-30 BY THE ADJUDICATING SEAT, AND THE CORRECTION IS MEASURED: AS FIRST FILED THIS ROW SHIPPED AN INCOMPLETE FIX. ***  **NINE mutants depend on the live table, not seven: M1, M2, M2b, M3, M5c, M5d, M5e, M5f, M12.**  I had excluded `M5f` on the ground that it *"uses a COMPUTED date rather than a live table entry, so it is addition-shaped already"*.  **That is false and the code says so in one line:** `_st_apply(chk, _exline(EX), '    "%s":   ("%s", "x"),' % (EX, _yest, ...))` computes the DATE and takes the ENTRY from `_exline(EX)` -- a LIVE PICK, exactly like the seven I did scope.  On an empty table `EX is None` and M5f falls into the byte-identical `results.append(False)` arm that **M12 has, which I DID scope.**  *I excluded one twin and scoped the other.*  **AND THE EXEMPLAR WAS WRONG IN THE SAME BREATH.**  The row held M5f up as *"the pattern the other seven should follow"*.  The genuinely addition-shaped exemplar is **`M3x`** -- the seat's insert-a-fixture-for-`arm_flags_probe.py` STALE EXEMPTION mutant, which scored `ok` on a FULLY EMPTY table.  A future implementer reading the old text would have converted seven, skipped M5f for the reason I wrote, copied the wrong exemplar, and **the selftest would still fail on an empty table** -- the exact failure this row exists to prevent, shipped inside the row that prevents it.  **SCOPE: convert the NINE table-dependent mutants from SUBTRACTION to ADDITION, using `M3x` as the pattern.**  Each owes two negative controls (it must still red on the rule it tests, and it must NOT red on a clean tree), which is why this is its own harness round and not a rider: it is fourteen controls, and a botched one silently weakens the check that guards every probe in the tree.  *Filed rather than fixed under the stopping rule: the shipped selftest is above the vacuity floor today (22/22, and the frozen-clock control proves it can fail), so this is COVERAGE DEBT with a known trigger date, not a false pass.*  *Found by the adjudicating seat when asked the load-bearing question -- WHICH of my accepted dispositions is wrong, with the count named.  It found four of six.  A round that accepts everything has either had a very good panel or has stopped arguing, and only a seat can tell you which; this one had stopped arguing.*  *** AND THE CORRECTION ABOVE WAS ITSELF WRONG, TWICE, IN THE TWO WAYS THIS PROJECT NAMES MOST OFTEN.  Both found by the adjudicating seat, one of them against its own earlier answer. ***  **(a) THE CORRECTION LEFT ITS REFUTED CONCLUSION STANDING IN THE SAME NOTE.**  A diff of this note between `43106c2` and `9ccb47b` shows the correction block INSERTED and the scope sentence rewritten -- and the region after it UNCHANGED, so the note read: scope is NINE including M5f ... then, in the closing position of authority, *'M5f is deliberately NOT in scope ... the pattern the other seven should follow'*.  Not a quotation; the original text, live.  **A future implementer reading to the END does exactly what the correction says reproduces the failure.**  That is the carrier's superseded-conclusion rule and mechanical rule 2 (grep for siblings) failing together, with the sibling 200 characters away in the same field.  Deleted, not demoted.  **(b) NINE WAS AN UNDERCOUNT.  THE SET IS TEN, AND THIS ROW'S OWN WITNESS FIELD HELD THE REFUTATION ALL ALONG.**  `M5b` mutates nothing but runs the checker with `--today 2026-09-21` wanting rc=1 and `EXPIRED EXEMPTION`; on an empty table there is nothing to expire, the checker prints `PROBEWIRING_PASS` rc=0, and M5b FAILS.  **The arithmetic proves it without running anything: the witness records `SELFTEST_FAIL 12/22`, which is TEN failures, and 22 - 9 = 13.**  A recorded count that contradicts the measurement recorded beside it -- the carried-number shape, in the row written to fix a counting defect.  **AND THE CORRECTION REPEATED THE ERROR'S SHAPE:** M5f was excluded on a FALSE ground (*addition-shaped already*); M5b was then excluded on a TRUE-BUT-IRRELEVANT one (it is not subtraction-shaped) -- when the failure class is *the table emptying breaks the selftest*, and M5b is squarely in it.  Its repair is the same insert-a-fixture pattern.  *** (c) AN ELEVENTH, OF A WORSE KIND: `M5a` GOES VACUOUS-GREEN. ***  It wants `PROBEWIRING_PASS` with `--today 2026-09-19`; on an empty table it gets PASS while testing nothing.  It does not fail, so no count reveals it -- **the check-that-cannot-fail shape, arriving inside the fix for a different defect.**  **SCOPE, RESTATED: TEN failing mutants (M1, M2, M2b, M3, M5b, M5c, M5d, M5e, M5f, M12) plus M5a's vacuity, all converted to fixtures, with `M3x` as the pattern.**  The control count is deliberately NOT restated as a literal here -- the previous figure, 'fourteen controls', was 7 rules x 2 and went stale the moment the rule count moved.  Derive it when the round is scoped, and name its unit.

rows.title: exit_census.py's BY-ENCLOSING-CONSTRUCT split attributed every call in a plain non-static function to the preceding DEVICE_ACCESS -- inflating the bucket used to rank reachability
rows.witness: harness:the pre-existing tools/pipeline/exit_census.py reports dev_sgi_re.c = 21 LIVE, which is the correct answer I spent an hour deriving by hand after a grep gave 25
rows.note: *** THIS ROW WAS FILED CLAIMING I BUILT A TOOL.  I DID NOT.  I OVERWROTE ONE THAT WAS ALREADY THERE, ALREADY CORRECT, AND ALREADY IN THE SAME DIRECTORY AS THE LEDGER I HAD BEEN EDITING ALL EVENING.  Caught by a `git diff --cached --stat` line reading `416 insertions(+), 126 deletions(-)` on a file I believed I had just created. ***  **THE `Write` TOOL SAID 'has been updated successfully', NOT 'created', AND I DID NOT READ IT.**  The standing rule is *before deleting or overwriting, look at the target*, and I did not look.  Restored from HEAD; `git status` on the path is clean, so nothing was lost.  *** WHAT THE EXISTING TOOL ALREADY DID, ALL OF WHICH I RE-DERIVED FROM SCRATCH: ***  it strips C comments with a state machine that respects string literals; it reports the denominator beside the numerator so a pattern selecting nothing is visible; it tags each site by enclosing construct (`DEVICE_ACCESS` / `DEVINIT` / `DEVICE_TICK` / `static`) so guest-reachable sites are separable from construction-time ones; and **its docstring already carries the exact lesson I thought I had found** -- *a naive grep gets steadily MORE wrong as this fork gets more honest, because every de-fatalisation leaves a comment QUOTING the exit(1) it removed.*  It even records the same false positive shape, from a different file.  **IT REPORTS `dev_sgi_re.c = 21`, WHICH IS THE ANSWER I SPENT AN HOUR REACHING BY HAND** -- after asserting 25 into two seat briefs and telling a seat its 21 was probably wrong.  One command would have settled it at the start.  *** THE REAL LESSON, and it is a generalisation of one this project already has: BEFORE WRITING A TOOL, CHECK WHETHER IT IS THERE. ***  The carrier already says a hand-maintained inventory of FILES is a wrong record waiting for someone to add a file, and mandates `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` over trusting the list.  **The same applies to `tools/pipeline/` -- `ls` it before building anything.**  This is the third instance today of the same shape: an absent-source note that was wrong (the footbridge datasheet, twelve days), a census asserted rather than derived, and now a tool re-implemented because nobody looked.  **PER-FUNCTION ATTRIBUTION WAS THE ONE THING MY VERSION ADDED, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT BEING ADDED.**  The existing tool counts per FILE and tags by construct, and its own design note says why: *UNIT is SITES, not defects* and *DEVICE_ACCESS means WHERE TO LOOK; reachability stays a per-site question*.  A per-function count invites exactly the false precision it warns against, and the addition licence requires a MEASURED DELTA or a TRANSFERRED WARRANT -- 'it would have caught my brief typo' is neither.  **My 13-in-sgi_re figure was a detail in a brief, not a decision input; the file-level 21 was the number that mattered and the tool had it.**  Closed as a RECORDS row: no code shipped, and the correct code was already in the tree.  *** AND THE TOOL DID HAVE THE BOUNDARY DEFECT AFTER ALL.  I SAID IT DID NOT, AN HOUR AGO, IN THIS ROW.  Measured 2026-08-30. ***  I closed this row concluding the existing tool *counts per FILE and tags by construct, so it never had defect 2* -- and its per-file totals ARE right, which is what I checked.  **Its CONSTRUCT split is not.**  `MARK` is `^(DEVICE_ACCESS|DEVINIT|DEVICE_TICK|static\s)`, and a **plain NON-STATIC function definition is not a boundary** -- `void draw_primitive(...)`, `void do_mte_transfer(...)` -- so every terminating call inside one was attributed to the preceding `DEVICE_ACCESS`.  **WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDY: that bucket is a REACHABILITY CLAIM used to rank defects** -- the tool literally tags it *on a guest access path BY CONSTRUCTION*.  Over-counting it over-states how many host kills a guest can reach, and at least one ledger row (`sgirekills`) took its title from the wrong figure.  **MEASURED DELTA, tree-wide over `src/devices` (118 files, 172 live calls): DEVICE_ACCESS 97 -> 83**, a 14-call / 14.4% over-count.  `static` also fell 51 -> 13, which is the same defect from the other side: a plain function FOLLOWING a static one was inheriting `static`.  **CONTROLLED against a hand-derived fixture** -- `dev_sgi_re.c`, whose true split was derived by hand and independently reproduced by two seats: `DEVICE_ACCESS` **15** (sgi_re 13 + sgi_de 1 + sgi_mte 1) and plain functions **6** (draw_primitive 1 + do_mte_transfer 5).  Before the fix the tool put all 21 in `DEVICE_ACCESS`; after it, 15/6 exactly.  **AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE FIX HAD A DEFECT OF ITS OWN, caught before shipping:** the new pattern also matched `DEVICE_ACCESS(foo)` lines, yielding two marks at one offset -- 4 duplicates in that file alone.  Harmless *today*, because at equal offset the `DEVICE_ACCESS` label sorts last and wins, **but that is a silent dependence on sort order inside a tool whose output ranks defects.**  Excluded the four MARK forms from the new pattern; duplicates now 0 across five spot-checked files.  *The honest shape of today: I diagnosed this defect correctly by hand, then wrongly concluded the shipped tool did not have it, because I checked the number people quote (per-file) rather than the number that ranks (per-construct).*

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c's unmatched-address else arm ends the host on ANY width in EITHER direction across 2080 bytes of its own registered window -- one guest `lb` at 0xb5001800 -- and NEITHER #497 nor sgirekills-as-scoped touches it
rows.witness: probe:regress/sgi_re_unmapped_probe.py -- 28 rows, gate-run by gate_arm.sh.  Test-first evidence in regress/artifacts/sgireunmapped/killtable_20260831/: 18/28 on the pre-fix build and 28/28 on the fix, plus the ORDER PROOF for the re-pinned sibling probe (34/35 RED on the committed build under the new oracle, 35/35 after), all sentinel-verified and re-run by the coordinator rather than inherited.
rows.note: *** THE WIDEST DOOR IN THIS DEVICE, AND NO LEDGER ROW COVERED IT.  Found by the adjudicating seat while ranking the OTHER four sgi_re rows; verified here by opening the file and deriving the gap arithmetic. ***  **THE SITE** is the final `else` of the window cascade in `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)` -- a `fatal()` for each direction and then a bare `exit(1)`, with **NO WIDTH PREDICATE AT ALL**.  Every other kill in this handler is reached only by choosing an unusual access WIDTH (the six `len != 8` arms) or a DIRECTION (the six read arms).  This one needs neither: any width, either direction, any unmatched address.  **THE DOOR, derived rather than asserted.**  `memory_device_register` covers `baseaddr + 0x1000` for `DEV_SGI_RE_LENGTH` = `0x1000`, and the handler restores the full offset with `relative_addr += 0x1000`, so the dispatched range is `0x1000-0x1fff`.  The six windows occupy `0x1000-0x17ff` with one internal gap:      TLB_A 0x1000-0x11ff   TLB_B 0x1200-0x13ff   TLB_C 0x1400-0x15ff      TEX   0x1600-0x16df   LINEAR_A 0x1700-0x177f  LINEAR_B 0x1780-0x17ff  leaving **`0x16e0-0x16ff` (32 bytes) plus `0x1800-0x1fff` (2048 bytes) = 2080 bytes** that fall through to the kill.  Guest KSEG1: a single `lb` at `0xb5001800` ends the host process.  *** IT SURVIVES BOTH ROUNDS THAT LOOK LIKE THEY WOULD FIX IT, WHICH IS WHY IT MUST BE FILED BEFORE THE NEXT COMPLETENESS SENTENCE SHIPS. ***  `#497` repairs the six WIDTH guards and never reaches this arm.  `sgirekills` as scoped repairs the six READ arms inside the windows and never reaches it either.  A reader of either round record could reasonably conclude the device no longer kills on a stray access.  It does.  **AND ITS FIX CANNOT BE ACCEPT**, which is what keeps it out of `sgirekills`' round rather than a scheduling preference: nothing backs an unmapped address, so there is no stored value to return.  It is DECLINE + a latched `(once)` announce -- a different fix design, so the round-scope rule's same-fix-design arm fails.  *The agy audit listed this arm as '1 unhandled offset fallback' and never asked whether it was reachable.  A census that enumerates a site without ranking it is how the widest door stays open.*  *** DESIGN SETTLED 2026-08-30 BY ADJUDICATION, BEFORE EITHER ROUND STARTS, SO NEITHER BURNS ITS PANEL ARGUING SCOPE. ***  **TWO ROUNDS, and both separate from `#497` -- all THREE round-scope conjuncts fail, worked through rather than asserted.**  SAME DEVICE fails: `sgi_de` and `sgi_re` are separate `memory_device_register` registrations at `baseaddr+0x2000` and `+0x1000`.  SAME SEMANTIC CLASS fails: `sgidewidth` is the WIDTH class with a real accept set `{4,8}` a decline must PRESERVE, while `sgireunmapped` is the BADOFFSET class where nothing legal reaches the arm at all.  **SAME DETECTOR / NO NEW ORACLE fails, and this is the one that decides it:** `sgi_de`'s registers are READABLE so its rows read back through `odata` -- a real device-signature channel -- while `sgi_re`'s else arm has NO BACKING STORE and its rows can only observe the diagnostic and the guest-gets-zero channel.  *Those are different oracles in kind, and the tempting collapse -- 'both are a refused access ending the host' -- is exactly what the no-new-oracle clause exists to refuse.*  *** THE CHANNEL FINDING, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS BLOCK. ***  `#497`'s `d_returnzero` escaped 35/35 and the reason generalises to BOTH these rounds: **the `(once)` announce prints IDENTICALLY for a correct decline and for a `return 0`**, because the announce happens before the return statement. Detector wired in the same commit, both hygiene pins raised in the same commit, all four build trees propagated and both clearance parts verified.  *** L4 CORRECTION, FOUND BY THE LATE PASS 2 -- AND IT IS THE EVIDENCE THAT THE LATE PASS WAS NOT THEATRE. ***  The measuring seat wrote that the shipped oracle's three failures are *three DISTINCT values*, and I repeated it into the pass-2 brief and the round's report.  **It is two, not three.**  Measured, from `repin2/table500b.out`:  `mexit0` -> `exit0/txt/died`;  `mret0` -> `exit0/txt/0xdeadbeef`;  `mrdexit0` -> `exit0/txt/died`.  **`died` appears twice**, so it is three FAILURES carrying two DISTINCT values.  **The substance survives and the overclaim does not.**  What the measurement supports is that the sentinel channel VARIES where the alternatives do not -- N2 fails all three while N1 (the device-signature read) fails only one -- which is the argument that actually mattered.  What it does not support is the stronger *three distinct values* framing used to dismiss the one-channel-wearing-three-hats objection.  *Caught by a packet-fed seat reading the parenthetical `(died / 0xdeadbeef / died)` against the claim it was offered to support -- i.e. by checking a claim against its OWN cited evidence, which is the cheapest audit there is and which neither I nor the seat that wrote it performed.*  **AND IT IS DIRECT EVIDENCE ON THE QUESTION OF WHETHER A LATE PASS 2 IS WORTH RUNNING**: this round shipped without one, the gate refused the next commit for it, and the pass run afterwards found a wrong record in the round's own justification within minutes.  *** codex's SEMANTIC CORRECTION, recorded because the records use the wrong word: THIS IS NOT A DECLINE AT THE CALLBACK BOUNDARY. ***  The handler returns **1** for an unmatched access exactly as for a serviced one, so `memory_rw` sees a handled access either way.  What the fix changes is that the host survives and a latched message is printed -- the access is still ACCEPTED at the boundary and answered with a defined 0 on the read side.  **The six-member option set distinguishes DECLINE from ACCEPT by precisely this boundary**, so calling it a decline blurs the distinction the set exists to draw.  *The behaviour is right and the word is wrong; a future round reading `sgireunmapped` as a DECLINE precedent would be citing something that returns success.*  *** L2 FLOOR BREACH, MEASURED BY THE PASS-2 SEAT: TWO MUTANTS SWEEP ALL 28 ROWS CLEAN, AND ONE RESTORES THIS ROUND'S OWN CITED WITNESS VERBATIM.  Repair is owed IN-ROUND however late. ***  **`W` -- re-add the pre-`#499` `len != 8` kill at the top of the catch-all, lifted verbatim from `9f666a8^`.  28/28, zero red -- and `sb` AND `lb` at `0xb5001800` die, printing the pre-fix kill text.**  That is floor clause (b): a verbatim reinstatement of the removed defect passes the detector.  **`T` -- `relative_addr < CRIME_RE_TEX + 0xe0` -> `+ 0x100`, ONE HEX DIGIT.  28/28, zero red -- and `ld` at `0xb50016e0` dies with `TODO: read from CRIME_RE_TEX`**, handing 32 bytes back to `exit(1)`.  Clause (d): a bound relaxed on a predicate dominating the edited lines.  *** THE TWO REASONS ARE STRUCTURAL, NOT LUCKY, AND I VERIFIED BOTH. ***  **(1) EVERY catch-all row uses len 8 and nothing else.**  `store()` defaults to `OP_SD_T0_A3` and `load()` to `OP_LD_V0_AT`; `OP_SB_T0_A3` exists but is aimed at the six mapped windows.  **So the detector pins the DIRECTION axis -- which the contract argues at length -- and never the WIDTH axis at the catch-all, while the round's HEADLINE is *no width predicate at all* and its WITNESS is a `lb`.**  **(2) All four catch-all offsets (`0x800/0x8c0/0x900/0x9c0`) land in the SECOND component.**  The round's own CHANGELOG names two: `0x16e0-0x16ff` (32 bytes) and `0x1800-0x1fff` (2048).  **The 32-byte component has ZERO rows.**  *This is `#498`'s `len == 2` hole one round later, in the same file: a detector that exercises one axis exhaustively and the other not at all.*  **AND THE PRETABLE MANDATE WAS ONLY PARTLY DISCHARGED, which is why the CHANNEL check did not catch it.**  The block's own header names baseline `e898c84`, the ARTIFACT detector, and the subject *discharge accept tlba/tlbb/tlbc*.  It does not cover the port to 28 rows, the fix, the re-pin, or the two new bits -- its GUARD-FIELD section enumerates SEVEN bits and says *all seven distinct today*, written before `1<<7` and `1<<8` existed.  **The CHANNEL check was never run over the catch-all rows, which is precisely where both mutants escape.**  The block's own opening line says `#498` skipped it and paid; the same shape recurred here one scope level up.  *** THE L2 IS REPAIRED IN-ROUND AND MEASURED.  Detector 28 -> 34 rows; both escaping mutants now die.  Artifacts: killtable_20260831/l2repair/. ***    fix **34/34**  |  `T` (`CRIME_RE_TEX + 0xe0` -> `+ 0x100`) **33/34**, `clip decl` red, was 28/28  |  `W` (the pre-`#499` `len != 8` kill re-added verbatim) **30/34**, all four narrow rows red, was 28/28.  **Six rows: four on the WIDTH axis** (a byte write and a 4-byte read at the catch-all, each with a survival row AND a positive channel -- the decline announced, the sentinel replaced by a defined 0, because a survival-only row is satisfied by a mutant surviving for the wrong reason) **and two on the FIRST COMPONENT** at `RE + 0x6e0`, which the handler's own `+0x1000` makes `0x16e0`.  *** AND THE VERIFICATION HIT TWO TRAPS THIS PROJECT HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN, BOTH MINE. ***  **(1)** The first `W` build died with `error: missing terminating " character` -- the `\n` in the inserted C string cooked into a REAL NEWLINE through the Bash -> heredoc -> Python path, splitting the literal.  **The measuring seat had warned me about this exact path in the same report** (*do not hand-type it ... it cost me one round-trip*) and the carrier prescribes `chr(92)`.  I hand-typed it.  Rebuilt with `chr(92)` plus a check that the literal landed on ONE line.  *The stale-binary guard is what caught it: the build failed, left the old binary, and the run ABORTED rather than scoring a false escape.*  **(2)** My extra confirmation -- *does `W` really restore the witness?* -- used a debugger `put b` and reported ZERO kill messages.  **`put b` never reaches the device**: the byte path passes `NO_EXCEPTIONS` and `memory_rw` skips the device call for `DM_DEFAULT` devices.  That is the trap measured on `pcc2` and recorded by me hours earlier.  **The probe's own rows use real guest `sb`/`lw` instructions, which is exactly why they caught `W` while the debugger poke saw nothing** -- so the four red rows are the evidence and the `put b` line is an apparatus artifact.  *** AND THE L2 REPAIR ITSELF HAD THE SAME DEFECT ONE LEVEL DOWN, FOUND BY THE PASS THAT THE `no recursion` RULING WOULD HAVE SKIPPED.  Detector 34 -> 36. ***  I diagnosed the breach as *one axis pinned exhaustively, the other not at all*, repaired the width axis at the addresses the mutants used, and left the identical hole at the other component: the two `clip` rows took `store()`'s default `OP_SD`, so the matrix read **three cells of a two-by-two** -- component1 x narrow had nothing.  **A guard re-added at the catch-all was caught; a guard re-added and CONDITIONED on the first component would not have been.**  Two rows added (`clip narrow surv`, `clip narrow decl`).  Measured:  fix **36/36**;  `T` **34/36** with TWO reds where the 34-row version had one;  `W` **30/36** with **SIX** reds where it had four -- narrow now catches at BOTH components.  *** THIS ALSO ANSWERS THE SEAT THAT DOUBTED THE ROWS: deepseek called the first-component rows *suspect as survival-only*, i.e. possibly unable to vary.  They vary -- both `decl` rows moved 1 -> 0 under `T` while their paired `surv` rows held.  The positive channel is doing the work, which is why each row was paired that way. ***  *Found by three packet-fed seats reviewing the repair -- while BLINDED, because my brief claimed to inline the diff and inlined zero hunks. rows.title: WITHDRAWN -- a FALSE out-of-bounds: de_reg/mte_reg are sized to the FULL window while the START strip HALVES the index range, so regnr+1 has 512 slots of headroom
rows.witness: none, and the absence of one is the point -- this row was filed 'source-derived' and the index-range measurement that would have refuted it was never run.
rows.note: *** THE THIRD MEMBER OF A FAMILY THIS FILE KEEPS PRODUCING: a fixed-arity store that writes `[i]` AND `[i+1]` while the index reaches the array's last slot. ***  Surfaced by the adjudicating seat while designing `sgidewidth`, and explicitly kept OUT of that round -- `sgidewidth`'s decline does not touch the `len==8` arm, so folding it in would be scope creep rather than adjacency.  `de_reg` is declared `uint32_t de_reg[DEV_SGI_DE_LENGTH / sizeof(uint32_t)]`, and the `len==8` arm writes both `de_reg[regnr]` and `de_reg[regnr+1]`.  At the top of the window `regnr+1` indexes one past the end.  **SAME SHIELD AND SAME TRAP AS `sgilinearoob`:** guest paths cannot reach it because an 8-byte access must be 8-aligned while the top offset is only 4-aligned -- but the debugger's `put d` prints a warning and PROCEEDS.  **That does not give this row a witness; it takes one away.**  A `put d` reproduction bypasses the guest instruction path entirely and would be laundering rather than witnessing.  **The pattern is now worth naming as a class rather than a coincidence:** `sgilinearoob` (`re_linear_[ab][tlbi+1]` into a `[32]`), the TLB arms' unmasked loop increment, and now `de_reg[regnr+1]`.  Three sites, one shape -- *a store whose arity is fixed by the ACCESS WIDTH while its index is bounded only by the OFFSET MASK*.  A future round should consider whether the bound belongs at the index computation rather than at each store.  *** WITHDRAWN 2026-08-30, HOURS AFTER IT WAS FILED.  IT IS A FALSE FINDING AND THE ARITHMETIC THAT REFUTES IT IS ONE LINE THE ANALYSIS SKIPPED. ***  Found by the mandated second review pass on the same session's records corrections; re-verified here by opening the file rather than taking the refutation on trust.  **THE MISSING LINE.**  `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)` reads  `int startFlag = relative_addr & CRIME_DE_START;` then **`relative_addr &= ~CRIME_DE_START;`** and only THEN `regnr = relative_addr / sizeof(uint32_t);`.  `CRIME_DE_START` is `0x0800`.  So `relative_addr` starts in `[0, 0xfff]`, is capped at `0x7ff` by the strip, and **`regnr` <= 511 while `de_reg` is `[DEV_SGI_DE_LENGTH / sizeof(uint32_t)]` = `[1024]`.  `regnr+1` <= 512: IN BOUNDS, with 512 slots of headroom.**  The `mte_reg` twin is identical -- same strip, same `[1024]`.  **HOW I GOT IT WRONG:** I reasoned *top of window / 4 = 1023, +1 = 1024 = one past the end* and simply did not see the strip on the line above the index.  *** AND THE PROCESS TELL IS SHARPER THAN THE ARITHMETIC. ***  `sgilinearoob`'s overclaim was caught because a seat ran `offsetof` instead of trusting source-derived arithmetic.  **This row's witness field says `source-derived`, and the equivalent measurement -- what is the actual RANGE of this index? -- was never applied to it.**  The same defect class, in the same file, on the same evening, caught the first time and not the second.  **THE REAL CLASS IS NARROWER AND BETTER STATED, which is what this withdrawal buys.**  I wrote *three sites, one shape: a store whose ARITY is fixed by the access width while its INDEX is bounded only by the offset mask*.  The true discriminator is **whether the array is sized to the INDEX RANGE or to the FULL WINDOW**:    * `re_linear_a[32]` is sized EXACTLY to `tlbi`'s `& 0x1f` range -> `tlbi+1` overflows.  **REAL** (`sgilinearoob`).    * `re_tlb_x[256]` with `tlbi` capped at 255 and a loop adding +3 -> overflows.  **REAL** (recorded on `sgirekills`).    * `de_reg[1024]` / `mte_reg[1024]` with the index range HALVED to 511 by the strip -> **the over-sizing is what prevents it.  FALSE.**  *** WITHDRAWING COSTS LESS THAN LEAVING IT: a false OOB row sends a future round chasing a hole the array sizing already closes, and it would have done so carrying my name and a confident derivation. ***  Withdrawn the way `sh4aaalias` was -- state `dropped`, the reasoning kept in place rather than deleted, so the next person who spots the same arithmetic finds the refutation instead of re-filing it.

rows.title: dev_footbridge.c answers FIQEnable reads with a silent constant 0 while its IRQ twin kills the host -- the whole FIQ column is softer than the IRQ column [corrected 2026-11-02: since #539 (78360718, 2026-09-19) the IRQ twin returns d->irq_enable with no exit (dev_footbridge.c:600-607 at 987cb596); the FIQ read still answers 0 (:649-652)]
rows.witness: harness:READ from the shipped source and the datasheet, 2026-08-30, both sides side by side.  `case FIQ_ENABLE_SET:` is `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE) d->fiq_enable |= idata; break;` -- a READ falls through with `odata` untouched, so the tail returns 0.  Its twin `case IRQ_ENABLE_SET:` does `odata = d->irq_enable;` and then `fatal(); exit(1);`.  Same architectural register (188h/288h, IRQEnable/FIQEnable), opposite failures.
rows.note: *** THE SIBLING-PARITY CHECK FIRING AT DESIGN TIME, WHICH IS WHERE IT IS SUPPOSED TO FIRE.  Found while adjudicating n6's ordering, 2026-08-30. ***  `n6` is about to ACCEPT the `+0x188` IRQEnable read on the warrant that the DC21285 prose makes it a documented read-only register.  **That same prose covers `188h` and `288h` JOINTLY** -- and `FIQ_ENABLE_SET` at `+0x288` has **no read arm at all**, so the model answers it with a silent constant 0.  A guest that sets FIQ bits and reads them back gets zero: **wrong value, no kill, no announce.**  **IT IS NOT IN THE EIGHT-KILL CENSUS AND THAT IS THE POINT** -- it is the same semantic class with the same one-line fix shape and the same row shape, differing only in that the IRQ column kills where the FIQ column lies quietly.  *Shipping the IRQ accept while leaving its FIQ twin silently wrong and unnamed is exactly the asymmetry the sibling-parity line exists to catch.*  **AND IT IS A COLUMN, NOT A SITE:** `FIQ_ENABLE_CLEAR`'s read side at `+0x28c` is also a silent constant 0 while its IRQ twin kills.  Worth ONE sentence in the decline round's `PRETABLE.out` rather than five separate discoveries later.  Under the reopening rule this becomes a candidate JOINER for a footbridge round once a row witnesses it, and a filed row otherwise.  *** THE DATASHEET SPLITS WHAT THIS ROW TREATS AS ONE CLASS.  Derived 2026-08-30 from `_scratchpad/dc21285.txt`, cross-confirmed in THREE independent places so no extraction stagger is possible: the register summary (`IRQEnable/IRQEnableSet 188h`, `IRQEnableClear 18Ch`), the offset table (`188h  IRQEnable  IRQEnableSet` / `18Ch  --  IRQEnableClear`), and the section heading `7.3.32 IRQEnableSet/FIQEnableSet Register--Offset 188h/288h`. ***  Constants confirmed in `src/include/thirdparty/dc21285reg.h`.  **(a) READ of 0x188 -> ACCEPT.**  *"IRQEnable/FIQEnable Register--Offset 188h/288h.  This read-only register is used to mask the interrupt input sources... The value of this register can only be changed by writing to the EnableSet and EnableClear registers.  Reset value: 0."*  The emulator ALREADY does `odata = d->irq_enable;` -- the documented value -- and then calls `exit(1)` on it.  Delete the kill, KEEP THE VALUE, **no latch**: there is no event to announce, because the read is implemented and is not ignored.  A bounded announce here would ship a wrong record in product code.  **(b) READ of 0x18c -> DECLINE.**  The offset table gives `--` for its read function: there is NO defined read.  The emulator returns `d->irq_enable`, which is a GUESS, then exits.  **Different disposition from its immediate neighbour, and the code treats them identically.**  **(c) WRITE to FIQ_STATUS (0x280) -> DECLINE.**  *"The Status and RawStatus are read-only."*  *** WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA: a single splice across all three would ACCEPT an undefined read at 0x18c and DECLINE a documented one at 0x188 -- getting both neighbours wrong, in OPPOSITE directions. ***  This is the option-set rule paying out again, with the ACCEPT member in play -- and that member is visible only from the datasheet, never from the source.  **AND IT SHARPENS THIS ROW SPECIFICALLY:** the IRQ/FIQ asymmetry recorded here is not merely an inconsistency to be normalised in either direction -- **the datasheet adjudicates which side is right.**  0x188/0x288 is IRQEnable/FIQEnable, a documented read-only register with reset value 0, so answering a FIQEnable read with a constant is closer to correct than killing the host on the IRQ side.  The fix direction is therefore ACCEPT on both, not decline on both.  *** THE TWO-LINE FIX, DATASHEET-BACKED, AND IT REPAIRS A HOST KILL AND A WRONG VALUE AT ONCE. ***  The datasheet says 188h/288h read back IRQEnable/FIQEnable -- the live enable mask, reset value 0.  So:  **IRQ side:** delete the kill and KEEP the value the model already computed (`odata = d->irq_enable`).  **FIQ side:** serve the read too -- `odata = d->fiq_enable` -- instead of falling through with `odata` at 0.  **The FIQ side is not merely 'silent', it is WRONG whenever `fiq_enable != 0`:** a guest that enables FIQ sources and reads the register back is told nothing is enabled.  That is the more insidious half, because unlike its twin it never announces anything.  *Both are member 4, ACCEPT -- no latch, because there is no event to announce: after the fix the reads ARE implemented and are NOT ignored.  A bounded announce would ship a wrong record in product code, which is exactly how the ACCEPT member was discovered.*  **RANKS AS AN EASY RESOLVABLE: two lines, three independent datasheet confirmations, no new latch bit, no struct change, and the accept rows read back through `odata` rather than through debug lines.**  Its only design question is whether 0x18c (IRQEnableClear, which the offset table gives NO read function) joins the same round -- it does not: different disposition, DECLINE not ACCEPT, per the split recorded above.

rows.title: 13 witnesses are ungated BY DESIGN, so a witness whose arms rot is indistinguishable from one that works -- and n6 is about to rot one
rows.witness: none -- a proposal about test apparatus.  Its motivating instance is measured: fbpending_witness.py scores a row on a death at the site n6 removes, and NO GATE RUNS IT, so nothing will report the breakage.
rows.note: *** THE THIRD TIER OF `n6`'s BLAST RADIUS, GENERALISED -- THE QUIETEST FAILURE THIS HARNESS CAN HAVE. ***  `check_probe_wiring.py` reports **13 witnesses correctly ungated**, and *correctly* is the right word: gating a witness would MANUFACTURE a regression, because a witness is built to INVERT after its fix (`#496`'s reads 15/15 pre-fix and 11/15 post-fix, and its record says so).  **But ungated means unrun, and unrun means a witness whose arms rot is indistinguishable from one that works.**  `n6` supplies the concrete instance: `fbpending_witness.py` scores a row on a death at the very site `n6`'s ACCEPT round removes, and no gate runs it -- so when that round ships, the witness breaks on disk and nothing anywhere says so.  **THE REMEDY IS NOT AN INVENTION -- THE IDIOM IS ALREADY IN THIS TREE.**  `fbpending_drain_probe.py` carries `EXPECT_CAP` defaulting to `-1 = report only`, with its scoring gated on `EXPECT_CAP >= 0`.  Run-but-do-not-score exists, is understood, and supplies the TRANSFERRED WARRANT the addition licence requires -- that plus a measured instance, never *it cannot hurt*.  *** AND IT IS HARDER THAN IT LOOKS, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN BUILT. ***  A witness is SUPPOSED to change score after its fix lands, so report-only output is **noisy by construction**: a flipped row is the expected inversion, or a real break, and the raw output cannot tell them apart.  Making it useful means each witness recording its **EXPECTED post-fix score**, so the report can say *expected 11/15, got 11/15* rather than *something changed*.  That changes what every witness in the tree must carry -- an owner decision rather than a round's, the same boundary that kept the per-row `kills:` comment filed rather than adopted.  **Ranked LOW deliberately:** apparatus about apparatus, competing with four open HIGH rows that are live host kills.  Filed so the `n6` round can NAME it rather than discover it, and so the next person who finds a rotted witness lands here instead of re-deriving it.

rows.title: the owner's agy-reserved-for-measurement ruling lives in the carrier as PROSE and panel.sh knows nothing about it -- so agy was fired in the very next panel
rows.witness: harness:panel_20260830_214609/ -- agy.txt exists in a routine panel fired AFTER the ruling; `grep -ci 'reserved' panel.sh` returns 0, and the launch at panel.sh's AGY block is unconditional.
rows.note: *** THIS IS THE CARRIER'S OWN STRUCTURE-FIRST FAILURE, MEASURED AGAINST ITSELF WITHIN TWO HOURS OF THE RULING BEING RECORDED. ***  The owner ruled 2026-08-30 that **agy is RESERVED FOR MEASUREMENT and held out of routine panels**, on the warrant that it is the only compile-and-measure seat NOT behind the Agent-tool transport -- the roster's insurance against the outage that once cost a round all its measuring capacity at once.  **The ruling was written into the carrier.  `panel.sh` was not touched.**  `grep -ci 'reserved for measurement' panel.sh` returns **0**, its AGY block is unconditional, and `panel_20260830_214609/` -- a routine panel fired after the ruling -- contains an `agy.txt`.  *The carrier's own diagnosis applies verbatim: knowing a rule and having it fire on the right object are different problems, and only the second is solved by writing more.  A rule that earns its second instance while sitting in that file has thereby proven it was mis-filed as prose.  This one earned its FIRST instance in under two hours.*  **THE FIX FOLLOWS THE `OLLAMA4` PRECEDENT EXACTLY, AND THE PRECEDENT'S WARNING IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART:** a variable, plus a conditional BANNER, LAUNCH, SEAT CHECK and VERDICT ROSTER.  The carrier records why all four: *blanking the variable alone would have left `panel_ollama.py` running with an empty model name, writing an error file, and producing a PHANTOM SEAT that answers the seat check.*  The agy shape is different but the hazard is identical -- a blank binary path would fail loudly rather than phantom, but the SEAT CHECK would then report a seat FAILURE where the truth is a deliberate omission.  *** AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE RULING'S COST CLAUSE: a seat DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED is a different thing from a seat FAILURE and a different thing again from AGREEMENT.  Conflating them is what the seat ledger exists to refuse. ***  So the seat check must print DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED by name, every panel, rather than silently omitting agy or reporting it down.  **DEFERRED, NOT FORGOTTEN, AND THE REASON IS A RULE THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY PAID FOR:** a panel was RUNNING when this was found, and **bash reads a script incrementally by byte offset**, so editing `panel.sh` mid-run corrupts that run -- the failure signature being a syntax error in a file that parses clean afterwards.  The edit waits for the panel to finish.  *The urge to edit arrives exactly when you are watching the script run, which is why the rule exists.*

rows.note: *** FILED BECAUSE A COMMENT ALREADY CLAIMED IT WAS.  The #497 gate comment ended 'the right answer is a gate_devices.sh split ... Filed, not done' -- and it was NOT filed: no ledger row, no queue entry, under any phrasing.  Caught by the pass-2 seat while the comment was STAGED. ***  *That is the gap-closes-itself shape: a claim that a process step is complete, shipping in the same commit as the thing it excuses.  A future reader greps for the row, finds nothing, and cannot tell whether the split was considered and rejected or simply forgotten.*  **AND THE PRECEDENT CLAIM WAS ONE STEP SHORT, which the same seat measured.**  I wrote that `gate_arm.sh` already runs footbridge and PIT probes, 'neither an ARM instruction test'.  True -- **but both run `-E cats`, this gate's OWN ARM machine, and the PIT wiring comment says it was placed there BECAUSE 'this is the only gate whose machine it shares'.**  So `#497`'s probe is not the third instance of an existing accretion; it is **the FIRST probe in this gate on a foreign machine AND CPU family**.  My words were true and my implication was generous to my own decision.  **THE FORCING CRITERION, so this row cannot sit forever:** *the NEXT device probe wired into `gate_arm.sh` converts this from FILED to OWED.*  The accretion story guarantees each addition makes the next cheaper, which is exactly how a least-bad accommodation becomes permanent.  **THE OPERATIONAL COST, named rather than left to be discovered:** a red row in `gate_arm` can now mean an SGI/MIPS device regression.  That is an attribution trap for whoever reads the battery output at 3am.  *** OWED AS OF 2026-08-31, BY ITS OWN FORCING CRITERION, AND RAISED low -> med. ***  The #497 gate block filed this row with the criterion written into the gate itself: *"the NEXT device probe wired into this gate converts it from filed to OWED."*  #498's `sgi_de_width_probe.py` is that probe, wired in the same commit that records this.  **A pre-specified trigger that fires and is ignored is worse than one never written, because the next reader trusts it.**  `gate_arm.sh` now runs THREE device detectors that have nothing to do with ARM -- the pit8253 block, #497's sgi_re and #498's sgi_de -- purely because it is the only gate with probe infrastructure and a machine they share.  *The split was not done in this round on purpose: it is a harness round owing its own negative controls, and holding a HIGH device fix hostage to a gate refactor would be the tail wagging the dog.  What was not acceptable was compounding it silently.*  *** 2026-10-19, #567: GATE 16 (regress/gate_mips_folds.sh) IS THE SECOND CPU GATE HOLDING DEVICE PROBES -- #549's fbctrl_port_probe.py and now #567's fbctrl_cmd_probe.py, both on -E testmips.  THE STOP, in GLM 5.3's form (#567 pass 2; upheld at F2 by GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4.7 and GLM 5.3): A THIRD DEVICE PROBE LANDS IN GATE 16 ONLY WITH THE SPLIT, OR WITH A PIN ON THE GATE'S LAUNCH COUNT. rows.title: sgi_re_width_probe.py's `other kill` row is a DEATH-ONLY oracle -- a one-character change to the text it claims to pin scores 35/35, MEASURED
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED by the #497 pass-2 seat in its own clone, with the prediction filed BEFORE building.  base 35/35 CONTROL=OK; x_othertext (catch-all message text altered, exit(1) untouched) 35/35 with ZERO red rows; x_readtext (one read arm's text altered) 34/35, reddening `tlb_a ld kill got=exit1-txt want=exit1+txt`.  The matched pair is the point: it proves the six siblings ARE failable and this one is not.
rows.note: *** THE ROUND APPLIED THE DEATH-AND-TEXT DISCIPLINE TO SIX ROWS AND MISSED THE SEVENTH. ***  `sgi_re_width_probe.py`'s catch-all row captures the transcript and **throws it away** -- `row("other kill", how, "exit1", ...)` uses only the how-it-died value -- while its six `ld kill` siblings twelve lines above compute an `ok_txt` membership test and report `exit1+txt`.  **So the row's own note claims IDENTITY -- *the catch-all is untouched* -- on an oracle that observes only DEATH.**  Any edit that keeps the arm fatal while changing what it is passes.  *** IT IS THE `d_returnzero` LESSON MIRRORED ONTO THE DEATH SIDE. ***  That one was a survival-only oracle at a site where SURVIVAL is the shared answer; this is a death-only oracle at a site where DEATH is the shared answer.  Same shape, opposite polarity, and the round fixed the first while shipping the second.  **AND FINDING IT DISCHARGED AN OBLIGATION THE TWO SHIPPED TABLES NEVER DID.**  Across all 41 preserved probe outputs, **SEVEN rows were red under NO mutant in either table** -- the six `ld kill` and `other kill`.  `PRETABLE.out` names their channel as *a round that silently removed the READ kills*, **but no such mutant was ever built**, so for those seven the CHANNEL line was satisfied ON PAPER.  The pass-2 pair now measures six of the seven failable.  **One remains measurably blind, and it is this row.**  **DISPOSITION: COVERAGE DEBT, NOT A FLOOR BREACH -- and the reasoning is the seat's, recorded so nobody re-argues it.**  Clauses (a), (b) and (c) pass, and the row DOES red against a null medium.  The catch-all is not a predicate the fix DEPENDS ON, so the bounded (d) closure does not reach it.  And clause (e)'s contract says *silent REMOVAL*, which this mutant is not -- **the contract is precise even though the row's inline note overclaims.**  **THE FIX IS ONE LINE:** make `other kill` symmetric with its six siblings by adding the text membership test.  It is deliberately NOT done in-round -- editing a shipped detector row means re-measuring, and the round's stopping rule fixes only measured FALSE PASSES and WRONG RECORDS.  *This is neither: it is a row that is weaker than its note claims, which the note has now been corrected to say.*  *** RECORDS DEBT, NAMED BY THE fable5 SEAT AND CONFIRMED BY LOOKING: THE 35/35 AND 34/35 RUNS ARE CITED IN TWO COMMIT MESSAGES, THIS ROW, THE BUG FILE AND A PROBE COMMENT -- AND THEIR LOGS ARE NOT PRESERVED ANYWHERE DURABLE. ***  `34/35` appears under `regress/artifacts/widthkillclass/opus_impl_20260830/` only in `PREDICTIONS.out` and `PRETABLE.out`, which are PREDICTIONS written BEFORE the run -- not the measurement.  The measuring seat built `x_othertext` and `x_readtext` in its own scratch directory and reported the scores; **the Agent seats leave no file in the panel dir**, so even the report is in volatile temp.  **This is the volatile-path rule breached from a direction it does not cover: the rule says copy the log before the record cites it, and here the record cites a log THAT WAS NEVER MINE TO COPY.**  A measuring seat's scratch evaporates with its session, and nothing in the harness asks it to hand the log back.  **DISPOSITION: the numbers are NOT retracted -- they are a seat's measured report with its method stated and a matched control, which is the ordinary evidentiary basis here -- but they are re-graded from CONFIRMED to MANUAL, because no artifact backs them.**  Re-deriving costs two mutant builds and one probe run each.  *The general fix is a brief line, not a rule: when a measuring seat reports a score, ask it to write the log to `regress/artifacts/<row>/` -- it has the file access, and the ask costs one sentence in the invocation.*  *** IT IS A CLASS WITH TWO MEMBERS, NOT ONE ROW -- censused 2026-08-31, and BOTH were shipped by the same session two days apart, which makes it a habit rather than two accidents. ***  `grep -rn 'row(".*", *how, *"exit1")' regress/*.py` returns exactly two rows whose ENTIRE oracle is *the host died*:  **`sgi_re_width_probe.py` `other kill`** (this row) and **`sgi_de_width_probe.py` `tail_acc_x`**.  Every other death assertion in the tree carries a text companion.  **The shared defect: at a site where death is the SHARED answer, a death-only oracle cannot see the message change** -- an edit that reworks the diagnostic while leaving `exit(1)` standing passes, measured 35/35 for `other kill` against a matched control at 34/35.  **The two are NOT equally exposed and the difference is worth stating rather than folding in.**  `tail_acc_x` has a sibling (`tail_acc`) that counts the message text, so the PAIR pins identity even though the row does not; `other kill` explicitly discards the transcript its six `ld kill` siblings test for membership, so nothing pins it.  *So this row is the live one and `tail_acc_x` is the latent one* -- and `tail_acc_x` additionally carries a documented expiry, since the round that fixes `sgideprimop` reds it by succeeding.  **One fix shape covers both: the `ok_txt` companion the siblings already carry.**  Doing them together is the class fix and costs one round instead of two.  *Filed, not fixed in-round: this is coverage debt against SHIPPED detectors sitting above the vacuity floor, which the stopping rule files rather than chases.*  *METHOD NOTE, because the check nearly lied to me: the census `grep -rhc ... | paste -sd+ | bc` printed **0** while the listing showed two -- `grep -c` emits nothing for non-matching files, so the sum was taken over an empty set.  The count cited here is from the LISTING, not from that arithmetic.  A denominator that disagrees with a listing you can see is the cheapest signal there is.*

I wrote the row that says so and then did not ask.*  **A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING FROM THE SAME COUNT:** `gen_codex_wall.py` prints `N held stages` and `held_rows()` returns ONE TUPLE PER ROW, phases joined -- so the number is ROWS, not stages. It is VACUOUS: that row has ZERO entries and its quotation sits in a row-level field `held_rows()` never reads, so the permissive class this row forbade passes every control and renders byte-identically.
