rows.note:
*** A SURVIVAL ORACLE THAT A WRONG `exit(0)` SATISFIES IS NOT A SURVIVAL ORACLE. ***  Found by the codex seat while answering `sgideprimop`'s pass-1 brief, in shipped material it was not asked about.  `regress/sgi_de_width_probe.py` pins host survival with `row(..., how, "exit0", ...)` at **NINE sites across FIVE probe files**, derived rather than transcribed with `grep -rn 'how, \"exit0\"' regress/*.py`:  `sgi_de_width_probe.py` 4 (`lo_alive`, `lo_alive2`, `hi_alive`, `hi_rd_alive`), `gdrom_decline_probe.py` 2, `gdrom_default_probe.py` 1, `gdrom_toclen_probe.py` 1, `sgi_re_width_probe.py` 1.  *codex named three, in the one file it had been given; the class is three times that and spans devices it was never shown -- which is why the row is filed as a CLASS and the deriver is written down instead of the number.*  The oracle reads the process's exit status after the harness sends `quit`.  **An emulator that calls `exit(0)` on the guest access under test ALSO exits 0**, so the row cannot distinguish *the host survived and was then asked to quit* from *the host died quietly at exactly the moment the row exists to observe*.  **THE REPAIR codex NAMES:** assert the `alive` value captured BEFORE the harness sends `quit`, ideally followed by a post-trigger command whose result proves the emulator was still answering.  The probe already captures `alive` -- the rows simply do not use it.  *** RANKED AS COVERAGE DEBT, NOT AN L2, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE DOCUMENTED ONE. ***  These rows are in a SHIPPED detector that sits above the vacuity floor: it fails on the pre-fix build, on a verbatim reinstatement (14/25, eleven reds) and on a null medium.  The stopping rule files findings against shipped material and fixes only MEASURED FALSE PASSES and WRONG RECORDS.  **No mutant has been built that exploits this**, so it is a hypothetical edit in an uncovered cell -- filed, ranked below live defects in the same file.  *What would promote it to L2: a measured mutant that calls `exit(0)` on the declined path and sweeps the detector clean.  That is one build and is the natural first job for whoever takes this row.*  **CHECK THE CLASS BEFORE FIXING THE INSTANCE** -- `grep -rn 'exit0' regress/*.py` across the tree, since the idiom will have been copied; this project has twice corrected an instance and left its siblings standing.  *** THE COUNT IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG WHEN FILED -- 9, AND THE POPULATION IS 13.  Corrected 2026-08-31 by the adjudicating seat, which could not reproduce my figure by any method. ***  **THE DERIVER, and it is the fix as well as the count:** `grep -rn '"exit0"' regress/*.py`, counting `row(...)` want-sites -- **13 across 5 files**: `gdrom_toclen_probe.py` 5, `sgi_de_width_probe.py` 4, `gdrom_decline_probe.py` 2, `gdrom_default_probe.py` 1, `sgi_re_width_probe.py` 1 (that one INSIDE A LOOP, so its runtime rows exceed its textual site).  **My grep was `'how, "exit0"'` -- anchored on the VARIABLE NAME rather than the ORACLE VALUE -- and `gdrom_toclen_probe.py` uses `how1`, `how2`, `how3`, `how4`.** Four sites invisible to a pattern that looked precise.  *A row filed to adjudicate oracle blindness shipped with a count produced by a blind pattern; that is the frozen-number rule arriving inside the filing that names it.*  *** THE RANKING SURVIVES, AND THE SEAT GAVE IT A MEASURED REASON I DID NOT HAVE: THE BLINDNESS IS PER-ROW, NOT PER-DETECTOR. ***  `lo_sent` reads `printed(t, "v0") if alive else "died"`, so it reds on ANY death whatever the exit code -- verified by the seat, which built a decline-then-`exit(0)` mutant of `#498` and found it KILLED by the read-side sentinel rows even though all four `*_alive` rows passed it.  **So no shipped detector is floor-breached as a whole (not L2), and no record is made false where a session-mate positive row exists (not L3).**  Coverage debt, filed, med -- confirmed, on evidence rather than on the stopping rule alone.  **THE FIXING ROUND'S FIRST JOB IS THEREFORE A NARROWER CENSUS: which of the 13 lack a death-proof SESSION-MATE?**  Those are the live ones; the rest are redundant belt-and-braces and can be repaired cheaply or left.  *That is a smaller and better-aimed job than "repair 13 rows".*

*** MAIN-LOOP MEASUREMENT 2026-08-31 (not a seat answer; recorded here rather than in `entries` so it cannot be counted toward the panel). ***  evidence: grep -h 'row(.*"exit0"' regress/*.py | wc -l = 24 on 2026-08-31

*** THE COUNT WENT STALE WITHIN HOURS OF BEING FILED, BY THE FILER'S OWN EDIT. ***  Filed 2026-08-31 as THIRTEEN; derived the SAME DAY as TWENTY-FOUR, of which sgi_re_unmapped_probe.py alone holds ELEVEN because #499 pass 4 added seven.  That is this project's documented pattern exactly -- the rounds that consult a number are the rounds that change it -- so the title now carries the DERIVER and no literal.  (Demoted: 13, filed 2026-08-31, never a current claim.)  Per-file on that date: sgi_re_unmapped 11, gdrom_toclen 5, sgi_de_width 4, gdrom_decline 2, gdrom_default 1, sgi_re_width 1.

AND THE CLASS BEARS ON #499's OWN PASS-4 ROWS.  Of the twelve rows pass 4 added, five are SURVIVAL-ONLY with an `exit0` want.  The READ side is covered -- `clip rd sent` reads `died` when the host is gone.  The WRITE side has NO post-death positive observable: surv wants exit0 and is satisfied, decl already counted its message before the exit.  A WRITE-SIDE-ONLY exit(0) is therefore PREDICTED to escape all 48 rows.  That is clause (d) shaped -- guard kept, its repair (falling through to the common tail) removed -- so it is NOT filed on my reading; it is QUEUED AS MUTANT E0W and will be measured.  Floor clause (b) is unaffected and measured green: a verbatim exit(1) reinstatement scores 18/48.

AND A SECOND SITE FOUND THE SAME DAY BY THE lcabadval SEAT, which makes this a CLASS rather than a probe-local habit: on `-E alpha -e alphabook1`, `lca_interrupt_assert` and `lca_interrupt_deassert` (dev_lca.c) are bare fatal()+exit(1), and bus_isa wires the whole ISA PIC chain to them.  So ANY interrupt assert or deassert kills the host with the SAME exit status as the value guards under test.  Any lcabadval row must match the fatal() TEXT INCLUDING ITS OWN DATUM, never the exit status -- an exit-status oracle there cannot tell the defect from the confound.

rows.title: SGIRE_W_* spells its bits as literal `1 << N`, so a duplicate is legal C and silent
rows.witness: harness:MEASURED -- the #498/#499 collision scored 14/14, a total escape
rows.note:
*** THIS CLASS HAS THREE INSTANCES IN THREE DAYS AND THE STRUCTURAL FIX IS ALREADY BLESSED IN THIS PROJECT FOR THE SAME SHAPE. ***  **Instance 1, MEASURED:** `#498` added `SGIRE_W_DE_LEN = 1 << 6`; `#499`'s witness generator independently inserted `SGIRE_W_UNMAP_WR = 1 << 6`.  Legal C, silent, and because `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)` casts the same `struct sgi_re_data *`, `d->warned` is shared -- **14/14 total escape**, with a transcript showing one guest `sb` to `sgi_de` permanently silencing `sgi_re`'s catch-all diagnostic.  **Instance 2:** the codex seat independently proposed `1 << 7` -> `1 << 6` as the canonical clause-(d) mutant for the `#500` fix -- i.e. an adversary reaches for this collision unprompted.  **Instance 3, PREVENTED:** `#499` and `#500` were both designed for `1 << 7` while in flight together.  Caught by listing the enum before writing either fix; `#500` moves to `1 << 9`.  *Two of three instances were found by measurement AFTER the fact; the third by one `grep` BEFORE it, which is the cheap end of this.*  **THE FIX, and it is the idiom the carrier already records for `SH4_VAL_*`:** that enum was converted to a C99 enum ending in `_NCLASS` precisely so *duplicates are impossible by construction*, and the carrier marks that work DISCHARGED.  The same shape applies here with one extra step, because these are MASKS rather than ids -- enumerate the BIT POSITIONS and derive the masks:  `enum { SGIRE_WB_TLBA, SGIRE_WB_TLBB, ..., SGIRE_WB_NBITS };` then `#define SGIRE_W_TLBA_LEN (1 << SGIRE_WB_TLBA)`.  **The enumerator auto-increments, so two bits cannot collide however many rounds add one**, and `SGIRE_WB_NBITS` gives a compile-time check that the set still fits `uint32_t warned`.  **NOT a rider on either round in flight.**  It touches every latch site in the file (seven today, nine after `#499` and `#500`), it is a pure refactor with no behavioural delta, and under the ADDITION LICENCE a no-delta change needs a warrant -- which it has, in a MEASURED instance rather than in "cannot hurt".  It ships as its own round with the obvious control: the pre- and post-refactor binaries must be byte-identical, or the refactor was not one.

*** MAIN-LOOP MEASUREMENT 2026-09-01 (not a seat answer; recorded here rather than in `entries` so it cannot be counted toward the panel). ***

*** THE HAZARD STOPPED BEING HYPOTHETICAL TODAY: TWO ROUNDS IN ONE DAY WERE BOTH DESIGNED FOR `1 << 7', AND THE COLLISION WAS CAUGHT ONLY BY A HUMAN LISTING THE ENUM. ***

`#499` took 1 << 7 and 1 << 8; `#500` took 1 << 9.  Both were originally written against 1 << 7.  `#500`'s own PRETABLE.out records it: *"Both rounds were designed for 1<<7 and the collision was caught by listing the enum before writing either fix."*

**WHAT A COLLISION WOULD HAVE COST, measured rather than argued:** `#498` measured a reused bit at 23/25, and `#500`'s own kill table measured `M_BITALIAS` (SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP aliased onto `#498`'s 1 << 6) at 18/21 -- killed by ONE row, `xlatch decl`, which exists only because a seat pointed out every other row ran in a fresh session.  **Without that row the collision would have been INVISIBLE**, and a duplicate enumerator is legal C with no diagnostic.

**And it crosses DEVICES, not just windows:** the sgi_re / sgi_de / sgi_mte / sgi_de_status handlers all cast ONE malloc'd struct, so `d->warned` is shared.  A bit reused between two of them is silenced by the other's ordinary traffic.

**THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL AND COSTS NOTHING AT RUNTIME**, and the tree already has the precedent: `dev_sh4.c` converted `SH4_VAL_*` to a C99 enum ending in `_NCLASS`, where duplicates are impossible by construction.  For BIT FLAGS the analogue is an index enum plus a shift --
    enum { SGIRE_B_TLBA_LEN = 0, SGIRE_B_TLBB_LEN, ..., SGIRE_W_NBITS };
    #define SGIRE_W_TLBA_LEN (1 << SGIRE_B_TLBA_LEN)
-- because auto-incrementing enumerators cannot collide, whereas explicit `1 << N` values can and did nearly do so twice today.

**NOT DONE THIS SESSION, and the reason is the addition licence rather than effort:** it touches product code in a file two rounds have just edited, it owes its own pass 1, and `#500`'s repair chain is still open.  Filed with the near-miss recorded so the next round does not have to rediscover that the hazard is live.

rows.title: dev_*.c: warn-once latches that are FUNCTION-STATIC, so one guest access to one device instance permanently silences the diagnostic for every other instance -- count DERIVED BY SCOPE, never by variable name (three name-based censuses came back wrong; see the row's deriver)
rows.witness: harness:DERIVED from the shipped source, 2026-08-31, across all of src/devices/
rows.note: *** THREE SEPARATE ROUNDS INDEPENDENTLY REACHED FOR THE SAME IDEA AND ALL THREE USED PROCESS-GLOBAL STATE.  Found 2026-08-31 by re-deriving a census a seat had made with a narrower pattern. ***  **THE DERIVER, because two separate counts of this class have already been short:**  `grep -rn 'static int w = 0;|static int first = 1;|static char .*_used\[' src/devices/*.c`  ->  **10 sites across 3 files** on 2026-08-31:  `dev_jazz.c` 2 (from `#179`), `dev_pcc2.c` 4 (from `#119`), `dev_sgi_re.c` 4 (upstream `rop_used`).  **THE DEFECT.**  A `static` inside a function is process-global, not per-instance.  Every one of these is a *warn-once* latch on a GUEST-DRIVABLE diagnostic, so **one guest access to one device instance permanently silences that diagnostic for every other instance of the same device in the machine** -- and for every later machine in the same process.  The house form is a per-instance bit in the device's own struct (`d->warned` plus `(once)` in the message text), which `#337`, `#460`, `#461`, `#497` and `#498` all use.  **THE INTENT IS RIGHT EVERYWHERE AND ONLY THE SCOPE IS WRONG.**  `#179`'s comment says *"guest-reachable; ignore the write instead of fatal()-flooding host stdout"*; `#119`'s says *"was exit(1) -> warn-once + continue"*.  Both are correct de-fatalisations that this project would make again.  **This row is about SCOPE, not disposition, and must not be read as reopening either round.**  *** HOW IT WAS FOUND IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: TWO CENSUSES OF THIS CLASS WERE BOTH SHORT, IN OPPOSITE WAYS. ***  A measuring seat censused it while answering an unrelated question and reported *"4 lines, ALL in this file, ALL inside draw_primitive(), the tree's only such sites"* -- true of its pattern (`static int first`/`_used[`) and false of the class, because `#119` and `#179` spell their latch `static int w = 0`.  Then a packet-fed seat on a DIFFERENT row challenged an `exit(` regex of mine as too narrow; the count it challenged did not move, **but chasing the four extra hits surfaced `#119`'s comments and hence the second file**.  *Neither seat was looking for this class.  A pattern-based census is only ever a census of its pattern, and the way out was two independent narrow greps disagreeing.*  **SCOPE NOTE for whoever takes this:** `dev_jazz.c` is one of the six paths in `tools/est_divergence.txt`, so a change there is SEC-only and does not owe an `est/` counterpart -- unlike the other two files.  **CONTROL a fix owes:** a per-instance latch must be shown to announce ONCE PER INSTANCE and not once per process -- i.e. a machine with two instances of the device, expecting two messages where the current code emits one.  That is the measurement that distinguishes the repair from a no-op rename.  *** THIS ROW'S OWN COUNT WAS WRONG WHEN FILED -- 23 SITES ACROSS 7 FILES, NOT 10 ACROSS 3.  THAT IS THE THIRD MISCOUNT OF THIS CLASS, AND THIS ONE IS MINE, USING THE DERIVER I WROTE WHILE TELLING OTHERS NOT TO TRANSCRIBE NUMBERS. ***  **The wider deriver:** `grep -rnE 'static int (w|warned|first) *= *[01];|static char [a-z_]+\[' src/devices/*.c`  ->  **23 sites / 7 files**: `dev_osiop.c` **8**, `dev_pcc2.c` 5, `dev_sgi_re.c` 4, `dev_jazz.c` 2, `dev_pvr.c` 2, `dev_disk.c` 1, `dev_ps2_gs.c` 1.  **My deriver matched `static int w = 0` and `static int first = 1` and missed `static int warned = 0`, which is the DOMINANT spelling** -- it accounts for 16 of the 23.  `dev_osiop.c` alone has more sites than my entire filed count, and I never looked at that file.  *** THE LESSON IS ABOUT DERIVERS, NOT ABOUT THIS CLASS.  I filed this row saying "record the deriver rather than the number, because this class has already been miscounted twice" -- and the deriver I recorded was itself too narrow.  A deriver is only a census of its own pattern, exactly like the number it replaces; what it buys is that the NEXT reader can widen it, which is what happened here. ***  *Found because a `pcc2` seat's answer mentioned a `static int warned` site my census did not contain, and I re-ran the grep instead of assuming the seat meant one I already had.*  **`dev_osiop.c` should be looked at first by whoever takes this row**: 8 sites, several commented `#118/#119: was exit(1)`, so it is the same de-fatalisation campaign and the largest single population.

rows.title: a 64-bit guarded value printed through (int) in a KILL diagnostic, so the message can name a value that would NOT have killed -- and at one site names the value the code calls ACCEPTABLE.  A CLASS, censused; derive the population, do not quote it
rows.witness: probe:regress/lca_confwidth_probe.py -- *** SCORES 2/6 AT HEAD, measured 2026-09-17: #518 replaced the IOC_CONF kill with a decline, so `kill width`, `kill notzero` and the `died` control all fail.  The surviving (uint64_t) print site has NO ROW.  Artifact: regress/artifacts/lcaconfwidth/head_20260917/. Re-pin or retire; wiring it as-is yields a PHANTOM RED. ***
rows.note:
*** FILED AS ONE SITE IN dev_lca.c; CENSUSED THE SAME DAY AND IT IS A CLASS.  Widened low -> med. ***

THE DERIVERS -- run them, do not trust these numbers, and note they answer DIFFERENT questions:

    # (1) the whole cast population -- mostly HARMLESS and NOT the defect
    grep -rc '(int)idata\|(int) idata' src/devices/*.c | grep -v ':0$'

    # (2) the sharp sub-class: a cast inside a diagnostic at a site that then EXITS
    #     (a python window scan; see the round record for the exact form)

On 2026-08-31 (1) gave 309 casts across 70 device files and (2) gave 45 host-kill sites, about twenty of which carry an explicit full-width guard on idata.

*** MOST OF THE 309 ARE NOT DEFECTS, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT -- an 8- or 16-bit register loses nothing through (int). ***  The defect needs BOTH halves:
  * a guard that tests the FULL 64-bit value -- `idata & ~MASK' or `idata != CONST'; and
  * a diagnostic that prints the TRUNCATED one.
Then a guest write whose only distinguishing bits are above bit 31 dies, while the message reports a value that would have been accepted.

*** THE SHARPEST INSTANCE, VERIFIED BY COMPUTATION AND BY READING THE ARM: dev_pvr.c's `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE && idata != 0x0cff0000)' paired with `(int) idata'. ***  A guest writing 0x1_0cff0000 fails the 64-bit compare and the host dies -- and the message prints 0x0cff0000, **EXACTLY THE VALUE THE CODE SAYS IS ACCEPTABLE**.  So the diagnostic tells a maintainer the guest wrote the correct value and died for it, which sends the investigation in precisely the wrong direction.  dev_lca.c's `idata & ~1' is the same shape, milder: it prints 0x0 for a value whose low half is genuinely zero.

SEVERITY REASONING, stated rather than assumed: none of this changes WHETHER the host dies -- the guards are unchanged and the kills are the kills.  It changes only what the log says about WHY, at the one moment the log is all that survives.  That is why it is med and not high, and why it is a RECORDS-CORRECTNESS defect in product code rather than a control-flow one.

NOT A ONE-LINE SWEEP.  Each site needs its own read: the fix is the format specifier plus a (long long) cast, but which sites are genuinely reachable with a >32-bit datum depends on the register width and the guest paths that reach it, and a blanket edit to 45 diagnostics is exactly the unlicensed addition this project refuses.  The honest first round is the ~20 sites whose guard is demonstrably full-width, ordered by whether a guest can deliver a >32-bit write at all.

Found while checking whether the dev_lca.c site was a one-off, as parallel work during a gate run.

**1. THE RECOMMENDED FIX WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS ITS WARRANT.**  The entry said `0x%llx` with a
`(long long)` cast, *"the file's own idiom elsewhere"*.  `dev_lca.c` uses **`PRIx64` five times and
`%llx` never**, and the siblings **KEEP** the cast as `(uint64_t)idata`.  My design brief compounded
it by saying to DROP the cast -- a third wrong form.  Corrected in place.

**2. `load_const` CANNOT BUILD EITHER OPERAND.**  LDA/LDAH make 32-bit sign-extended constants; the
K0SEG address needs bits 63..42 and the test value needs bit 32.  **A probe using `load_const` for
either is not this witness.**  The working bootstrap is the one the Alpha harness already uses:
`put d` the 64-bit words into RAM below 64 MB, then guest `ldq` them while `ptbr` is still 0.

**3. THE MISS MODE IS NOT ONLY 'UNMAPPED -> NOTHING'.**  Offset 0 is `LCA_IOC_BASE` (HAE), which
`break`s with no kill -- so a store to `k0(0x180000000)` is **silent while INSIDE the LCA window**.
Unmapped and HAE both read back 0, which is why the control has to distinguish them.

**4. TWO ROUTES THAT LOOK LIKE CONTROLS AND ARE NOT:**
  * **debugger `dump` cannot read the register.**  `dump` calls `memory_rw` with `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, and
    LCA is `DM_DEFAULT` rather than `DM_READS_HAVE_NO_SIDE_EFFECTS`, so the handler is **SKIPPED** and
    the caller gets the pre-zeroed buffer -- *the unmapped signature, produced by a hit.*
  * **`put d` of the killing value is not rung-3.**  `store_64bit_word` goes through `memory_rw` with
    `CACHE_DATA` and no `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, so it DOES enter the handler and `exit(1)` from the
    debugger -- a real kill, by no guest instruction.

> **THE CONTROL THAT WORKS: a guest `stq` of `0x1` followed by a guest `ldq`, same decode, BEFORE
> the killing store.**  It is the analogue of the Alpha harness's `swpctx mapped` row.  Neither it
> nor the kill text is sufficient alone -- the round-trip proves the window is THIS arm and not HAE
> or unmapped; the text `IOC_CONF: 0x0` proves the arm fired and that a 32-bit zero store could not
> have produced that pair.

**Q3 CONFIRMED IN DETAIL, and it hardens S2:** `stq` is opcode `0x2d` -> `loadstore_type 3` -> `LS_Q`;
`host_store` is NULL for a device page, so it falls to `LS_GENERIC_N` and calls `memory_rw(..., 8,
MEM_WRITE)`; the memblock granule is 1 MB so `0x20+8` crosses nothing; Alpha is little-endian and
`memory_readmax64` rebuilds the value.  **And the guard's own arithmetic is load-bearing:** `~1` is a
signed `int` (-2) converting to `0xfffffffffffffffe`, **so it sees bit 32 -- `~1U` would NOT, and
that is a different mutant worth building.**  The same function already compares against
`0x300800000ULL`, so 64-bit values are this handler's native width.

**One honest weakening:** `(int)0x100000000 == 0` is IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED, not guaranteed by C99.
GCC/Clang truncate, so the witness holds on this build -- but the row should not claim a language
guarantee.

Corrected 2026-09-17. ***  I wrote that the four FILE-READING seats reached CLOSE 1-8 / KEEP-OPEN 9 while the PACKET-FED seats kept rows open. **Codex is file-reading and its verdict line reads `CLOSE 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8. Meanwhile minimax (packet-fed) CLOSED rows 1 and 5, kimi-sub CLOSED 1/3/4/6/7, glm CLOSED 1/3/4/6/7/8.  **The classes do not sort the verdicts.** *** AND THE RULING WAS CIRCULAR, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. ***  My own brief's S0 told the seats *"an unsettleable row stays open, which is the safe direction"* -- which converts every honest not-checkable into a KEEP-OPEN vote -- and I then read those votes back as evidence that the doctrine was working.  **I instructed the behaviour and then cited it as a finding.** **THE RULING FORM THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN WRITTEN** sorts the packet-fed KEEP-OPENs BY KIND, not by class: (a) NOT-CHECKABLE-FROM-PACKET, *discharged by naming the file* -- row 2's condition (c), row 8's figures, deepseek's rows 1/3/4/6/7 -- where *"the file-reading seats verified it" is the right answer ONLY when the file is named*; and (b) SUBSTANTIVE, adjudicated on merit regardless of class -- row 9 (all four right), row 5's arithmetic, row 5's unnamed labels (raised by kimi-sub and glm, the SAME finding as codex and opus5, so a class split puts those seats on the wrong side of their own finding). *** AND ONE SUBSTANTIVE PACKET-FED CLAIM WAS FALSE AND A CLASS RULING IS EXACTLY HOW IT GOES UNREFUTED: *** glm's *"nothing pins the suppression side, 0x08 must NOT fire"* is answered by the row `a routine 0x08 preserves the command` in `diff_wdc_identify.c`.  **That deserved a refutation by file, and my ruling gave it a category instead.** **THE COST OF THE MIS-STATEMENT:** it hid codex's row-3 dissent (the row now re-opened on a measurement), and it converted a three-seat finding on row 5 into "the file-reading seats said CLOSE".

rows.note: The MTE's switch (dst_tlb) handles TLB A/B/C and LIN_A/LIN_B; dst_tlb is a 3-bit GUEST-CONTROLLED field ((mode & 0x1c) >> 2), and values 3 (MTE_TLB_TEX), 6 (MTE_TLB_CLIP) and 7 fall to default.  That arm is a bare fatal() with NO exit(1) -- so NOT a host kill -- and NO LATCH, so a guest looping over MTE operations floods host stdout without bound.  floodclass family. Found by the sgitexindex seat as a residual while checking a different question, and re-verified by reading. rows.state_note:
Surfaced by the pcc2widthkills pass-1 panel (fable5 and kimi independently) while auditing the width fix: 'ten kills removed' would read as the file being safe while a one-byte guest write still exits.  The width detector's GENCTL lanes were chosen (0xd9/0x40, C040 clear) precisely to stay off this kill; c040ok() asserts it at authoring time.  Next round after pcc2widthkills closes.  Filed in OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md (dated tail, `### pcc2c040kill`, line 14553 as of 2026-09-04); this row added 2026-09-04 so the dashboard shows it -- the bug file had it, the ledger did not.  NEW FACT 2026-09-05 (Opus design seat on pcc2defaultkill, verified: dev_pcc2.c SCCRXIACK arm has no writeflag test): a guest LOAD of SCCRXIACK 0x27 runs reassert_interrupts(), and OpenBSD's console driver cl.c reads that offset on SCC receive interrupts -- so the ENTRY into the C040 kill is routine guest traffic; only the ARMING (C040 set in GENCTL) is rare.  Reachability better than the filing says.  Must be fixed before any round implements a PCC2 IACK arm.

*** PASS-1 AUDIT 2026-09-07 (codex, `regress/artifacts/pcc2c040kill/codex_pass1_20260907.txt`).
THE CENTRAL PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION MAKES THE DEFECT SIMPLER AND WORSE. ***

**VERDICT:** *"DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE for unsupported C040 delivery.  Survival is a nonvacuous
oracle here, but cannot establish interrupt correctness."*

*** THE CORRECTION: *"the GENCTL write itself immediately calls the terminating helper.  Arming and
termination occur within that access; subsequent SCC traffic is unnecessary."* ***

**Line 459 IS `reassert_interrupts()` inside the GENCTL byte-write arm.**  So the whole
`SCCRXIACK`-plus-OpenBSD-`cl.c` entry story -- which this row records as a NEW FACT improving
reachability, and which the brief built its S4 around -- is UNNECESSARY.  **A single legal byte write
of 0x04 to offset 0x02 terminates the emulator on the spot.**  No second access, no driver, no
interrupt.

*That does not make the earlier finding wrong -- SCCRXIACK really does run the helper with no
direction test, and that really is routine traffic.  It makes it SUPERFLUOUS: the row had found a
long road to a place reachable in one step, and nobody noticed the short one because the long one was
interesting.*

**CONFIRMED BY READING, beyond what the brief asserted:**
  * `pcctwo_reg[]` holds **`uint8_t`**; GENCTL rejects non-byte writes, but the accepted byte write
    **stores `idata` WITHOUT MASKING** and immediately calls the helper.  **No read-only treatment
    prevents the bit being stored**, and the header explicitly permits byte accesses.
  * The ten call sites are confirmed with their contexts -- 383 `pcctwo_interrupt_common()`, 400 the
    device TICK (unconditionally), 459 GENCTL write, 551 T1ICR/T2ICR, 574 SCCICR, 588 SCCTX,
    602 SCCRX, 609 SCCRXIACK (no direction test), 622 SCSIICR, 662 MASK -- all reaching **one shared
    terminating branch**.
  * **THE CONDITION IS NOT STICKY:** a GENCTL write CLEARING C040 stores the cleared value before
    calling the helper.  So the state is recoverable in principle -- and unrecoverable in practice,
    because the arming write has already terminated the process.
  * **`400` is the device TICK, called unconditionally.**  So even a guest that arms C040 and then
    does nothing at all is terminated at the next tick.  That is worth stating separately: it removes
    the last version of the story in which the guest must go on to do something.

**Q4 ANSWERED, and it is the opposite of the neighbouring rounds' problem:** *"Survival is a
nonvacuous oracle here."*  This project has measured that survival rows at REFUSAL-EFFECT sites are
vacuous by construction -- guarded and unguarded code both survive.  Here the pre-fix build genuinely
does NOT survive, so survival discriminates.  **But it cannot establish interrupt correctness**, which
is the second half of the disposition question and needs its own row.

**THE WITNESS IS NOW TRIVIALLY CHEAP.**  This row's `witness` field says a rung-3 attempt *"looks
cheap (one more session in `regress/pcc2_width_probe.py`, which already byte-writes this register on
this machine)"* -- and with arming-equals-termination it is cheaper still: **one byte write and
observe that the process is gone.**  The field's promise that it says `not yet done` rather than
`did not think to ask` is now cashable in a single session.

*And a note on the brief: it was written with C5 applied FROM THE START -- neutral register, scoped
reading, no chain -- on a subject (process termination) that is trigger 1's own vocabulary.  **It was
not refused.**  First time today I wrote one that way instead of learning it from a refusal.*

**READY TO CLAIM AS A ROUND, 2026-09-07.**  The stated blocker was *"next round after
pcc2widthkills closes"*; that row now carries `commits=b78bb0f`, so the width fix is IN THE TREE and
only its formal closure is outstanding.  Nothing about this defect depends on that closure.

**THE WITNESS IS ONE SESSION IN AN EXISTING PROBE.**  `regress/pcc2_width_probe.py` already drives
GENCTL byte writes on this machine and carries an authoring-time assertion, `c040ok()`, whose whole
job is to keep its lanes (`0xd9`/`0x40`) OFF this path.  **So the probe already proves the access
works and already knows the bit is dangerous** -- the witness is the same access with the bit set,
and the oracle is that the process is gone.

  *That assertion is worth keeping rather than deleting when the row is added: it protects the WIDTH
  rows from wandering onto this path, which is a different job from the new row deliberately
  stepping onto it.  A row that turns the guard off for the whole file would re-open exactly what
  `c040ok()` was written to prevent.*

**FIX SHAPE, from the audit:** DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE, with its own latch bit -- the same
per-instance reasoning as `dev_sgi_re`'s bits, since a shared latch is silenced by the other site's
ordinary traffic.  **The open design question is Q2, which the audit did not settle from the source:**
after declining, does the helper fall through to the normal level recalculation, or return having
asserted nothing?  Those differ in what the guest observes, and the answer decides whether the round
owes a second row on interrupt behaviour -- which the verdict's own second clause anticipates
(*"survival ... cannot establish interrupt correctness"*).

*** WITNESS DESIGN REVIEWED AND NOT RATIFIED.  grok,
`regress/artifacts/pcc2c040kill/grok_witness_20260907.txt`. ***

**VERDICT:** *"NOT RATIFY as proposed.  A guest `st.b` of 0x04 at GENCTL is a sound CORE of a rung-3
witness of this kill.  Survival-only, in `pcc2_width_probe.py`, with no same-decode preset and no
site-attribution, is not.  **That is the same class as the design you asked me to assume: the
observation is either destroyed by the defect, or it reports success while measuring nothing.**"*

**THE CORE SURVIVES: one legal byte write is the right reproduction.**  What fails is my ORACLE, and
the required attribution is specific:

  1. **`how == "exit1"`, not merely `not alive`.**  `not alive` is satisfied by several unrelated
     deaths.
  2. **The transcript must contain `C040 interrupt assertions`.**  Missing text plus exit1 is
     *FAILED FOR SOME OTHER REASON*, not a pass -- which is the carrier's own rule 4 (*every
     reproduction must answer "did it fail for the reason under test?"*), applied to a row I had
     written without it.
  3. **Controls in sessions that MUST SURVIVE**, so a construction failure cannot masquerade as the
     defect: a RAM round-trip; CHIPID `ld.bu` -> 0x20 (RAM would not answer that); and a
     **C040-CLEAR GENCTL round-trip of a nonzero value** -- 0x82, already proven by existing rows in
     `pcc2_width_probe.py` and `pcc2defaultkill`.  *That third one is the same-decode preset: it
     proves the register is reachable and writable BEFORE the killing value is used.*
  4. *** THEY MUST ALL RUN BEFORE THE KILLING STORE.  Post-kill they cannot run. ***

**POINT 4 IS THE ONE I WOULD NOT HAVE FOUND, and it is the Alpha design's flaw wearing different
clothes.**  There the defect destroyed the TRANSLATION the observation needed; here it destroys the
PROCESS the controls need.  In both cases the observation and the thing observed cannot coexist, and
in both cases I designed the observation first and never asked what state it required afterwards.

*** THREE WITNESS DESIGNS OF MINE HAVE NOW BEEN REVIEWED AND ALL THREE HAD A FLAW OF THE SAME CLASS.
***  Alpha swpctx (defect destroys the translation), `#505`'s tiled row (two silent declines read as
plausible values), and this one (survival is not attribution).  **The common shape is that I design
what to OBSERVE and not how to ATTRIBUTE it** -- the ladder's clause (ii) asks for a liveness control
AND a signature control, and in each case I supplied the first and reasoned my way past the second.
Recorded here rather than as a carrier rule because three instances is a pattern about ME, and the
cheap remedy is already available: **route every witness design to a reviewer before building it.**
That has now cost one invocation each time and caught three real defects.

**ALSO FLAGGED, and it needs checking before the round:** the seat calls S3's tick claim *possibly
sequencing-wrong* -- i.e. whether call site 400 (the unconditional device tick) really does reach the
kill for a guest that arms C040 and then does nothing.  I asserted that from the call-site list; it
is not verified.

*** THE TICK CLAIM IS VACUOUS, AND SO IS 'TEN CALL SITES' AS A STATEMENT OF HAZARD.  My record,
corrected by checking the flag grok raised. ***

grok called S3's tick claim *"possibly sequencing-wrong"*.  Checked, and it is wrong:

  * `DEVICE_TICK(pcc2)` really does call `reassert_interrupts(d)` unconditionally -- that part of my
    claim is literally true;
  * **but GENCTL is written in exactly ONE place** -- its own case arm -- and that arm calls
    `reassert_interrupts()` in the SAME ACCESS.  Every other reference to `pcctwo_reg[PCCTWO_GENCTL]`
    in the file is a READ (`:271` the C040 test, `:341` the MIEN test).  A wide write is DECLINED
    BEFORE the store.

**So the process always terminates on the ARMING WRITE ITSELF, and the tick can never be the first
hit.**  *"Even a guest that arms C040 and then does nothing is terminated at the next tick"* describes
a state that cannot be reached: there is no interval during which C040 is set and the process is
alive.

*** AND THE SHARPER CORRECTION: 'TEN CALL SITES' IS TRUE AND MISLEADING. ***  All ten reach one
shared branch, which is what the audit established and which stands.  But **nine of them are
unreachable AS A FIRST HIT**, because the only way the guard's condition becomes true is a write that
immediately calls the helper itself.  **The defect has exactly ONE reachable entry.**

**WHAT THIS CHANGES:**
  * the WITNESS is simpler than the design assumed -- one session, one store; **no tick row is owed**,
    and a row waiting for a tick would wait forever;
  * the SEVERITY framing is unchanged (one legal byte still ends the emulator) but the *breadth*
    framing was inflated: ten sites reads as ten ways in, and there is one;
  * the FIX is unaffected -- de-fatalising the shared branch covers all ten regardless of which can
    reach it first, and that is the right place to repair it.

*This is the third over-broad claim of mine this session and the same shape as the others: a census I
ran correctly, restated as a claim about REACHABILITY that the census does not support.  The count of
call sites answers "how many places call this helper"; it does not answer "how many can arrive here
first", and I wrote the second while measuring the first.*

*** FULL PANEL 2026-09-07 (`_scratchpad/panel_20260907_124918`).  FOUR SEATS REJECTED MY S3
CORRECTION, AND THEY WERE RIGHT ABOUT THE WARRANT EVEN THOUGH THE CONCLUSION SURVIVED. ***

    codex      PENDING CODE REVIEW      grok      (mid-answer, 422 b)
    minimax    REJECT                   glm       answered 8.3 kB -- NO BURN this time
    kimi-sub   answered                 deepseek  answered
    kimi CLI   403-walled, covered      agy       deliberately not fired

**ZERO SEATS DOWN -- the first such panel of the day.**  glm did NOT burn, on a brief far more focused
than pass 3's, which matches the carrier's finding that burns track BRIEF COMPLEXITY rather than the
seat.

*** THE ATTACK, and glm put it most precisely: *** *"a count of references to the symbolic constant
CANNOT ENUMERATE STORES REACHING BYTE 2 -- and any wide/bulk store, nonzero reset default, or
unzeroed allocation falsifies S3 and revives S4's tick row."*  kimi-sub: *"asserted rather than
enumerated ... the packet never lists all stores into `pcctwo_reg[]`."*  deepseek: *"S3's one-entry
claim is unsupported."*

**THEY ARE RIGHT ABOUT THE EVIDENCE.**  My grep was for `PCCTWO_GENCTL` -- the symbolic constant --
which is a CORRELATE of "stores that set C040", not the class.  That is exactly the deriver failure
the carrier documents: *before writing a deriver, ask what makes a member a member.*

*** THE PROPER ENUMERATION, run by class rather than by name, and S3 SURVIVES: ***
  * **every write into `pcctwo_reg[]` in any index form** -- 40 sites; all use symbolic constants and
    none names GENCTL except its own case arm at `:458`;
  * **the one BULK write**, `memcpy(d->pcctwo_reg + relative_addr, data, len)` at `:482` -- the
    falsifier glm predicted.  It sits in the `T1CMP/T2CMP/T1COUNT/T2COUNT` arm, so `relative_addr` is
    one of **0x04, 0x08, 0x0c, 0x10** and the copy runs FORWARD.  **GENCTL is 0x02, BELOW all four.
    It cannot be reached.**  (`:429` is the read-side memcpy; `:438` a zero-fill of the caller's
    buffer.)
  * **nonzero reset default** -- `:748` sets `pcctwo_reg[PCCTWO_GENCTL] = 0x00`.  Excluded.
  * **unzeroed allocation** -- `:738` `memset(d, 0, sizeof(struct pcc2_data))`.  Excluded.
  * **numeric index 2 or byte-2 arithmetic** -- none.

**SO: S3 AND S4 STAND, AND THEIR WARRANT IS NOW AN ENUMERATION RATHER THAN A GREP FOR A NAME.**  The
seats did not find a defect in the code; they found one in my evidence, and refusing to ratify is
what produced the real check.  *Unanimity on a brief-supplied fact is worth nothing -- but unanimous
REFUSAL to accept one is worth a great deal.*

**DEEPSEEK'S SMALLEST EDIT, which is a genuine clause-(d) mutant against the design's own preset:**
*"changing the C040 test to `!= 0x82`, leaving the 0x82 control green."*  The witness design uses a
C040-clear round-trip of 0x82 as its same-decode preset -- so a repair conditioned on that exact
value keeps the preset green while the defect returns for every other value.  **The preset and the
mutant would share a constant**, which is the shared-constant hazard `m88ksfd1row` is queued about.
Recorded as an owed mutant before the round runs.

**minimax's REJECT additionally calls S6 internally inconsistent with the disposition it verifies** --
unread in detail; carried as an open item for the next pass rather than summarised from its verdict
line.

*** A GENUINE DISPOSITION SPLIT BETWEEN THE TWO STRONGEST SEATS.  FOR THE FLAGSHIP ADJUDICATION;
BOTH SIDES IN THEIR OWN WORDS. ***

**codex (pass-1 audit): DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE.**  *"Survival is a nonvacuous oracle here, but
cannot establish interrupt correctness."*

**grok (full panel): DO NOT SHIP THAT.  ACCEPT.**  *"DO NOT SHIP DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE.  S1-S4
hold after re-enumeration.  The right member is ACCEPT (store the byte, delete the `exit(1)`, fall
through)."*

*** grok's CASE, and it is the better-evidenced of the two: ***
  * **C040 is R/W in the board manual.**  `OPER R/W` on that bit in VMESBCP2 -- the manual this
    project already has at `_scratchpad/vmesbcp2.pdf`.  It is **not an unlisted offset, not a
    read-only bit, and not a wide write with a lane hazard**.
  * *** SO APPLYING `#500`/`#501`'s DECLINE IS WARRANT TRANSFER FROM THE WRONG SIBLING -- AND THAT
    WAS MY ERROR. ***  I took the disposition from the same FILE without checking the same
    SITUATION.  `#500` declines because a wide write's `idata` carries the neighbour's lane;
    `#501` declines an unlisted OFFSET; VECBASE masks bits the manual forbids; CHIPID is read-only.
    **None of those is a legal R/W bit at a listed offset.**
  * **In-tree ACCEPT precedents it names instead:** `dev_footbridge.c`'s `+0x188` IRQEnable
    (computed the right value then `exit(1)` -> ACCEPT, no latch, because there is no event to
    announce); `#432` TIMER_EXTERNAL (a legal named encoding that hit `exit(1)`); and
    `m8820x_unimplemented` (complain-once and continue).
  * **The decisive argument: a latched "C040 interrupt assertions... TODO" followed by actually
    asserting INT is A WRONG RECORD IN PRODUCT CODE** -- the same shape the IRQEnable round refused,
    printing "unimplemented; ignored" about a path that is implemented and is not ignored.
  * **C040 selects which PINS carry a level this emulator does not model.  It does not change the
    level itself.**  So storing the bit and using the existing 88100 INT path is a no-op relative to
    every observable the emulator has -- which is ACCEPT, not a refusal.
  * The addition licence: *"one more latch cannot hurt" is not a warrant*, and this file just spent a
    round moving IPL/MASK off process-global statics.
  * *(Context, offered as context and not measurement: OpenBSD/mvme88k never writes `pcc2_genctl`
    in the in-tree guest; the 68k sibling sets IEN and not C040.)*

*** ONE SENTENCE OF grok's IS FACTUALLY WRONG, AND ITS CONCLUSION SURVIVES WITHOUT IT. ***  It writes
that *"the helper ALREADY COMPUTED IPL vs MASK vs MIEN and is about to INTERRUPT_ASSERT/DEASSERT when
it dies."*  **It has not.**  The C040 test is `dev_pcc2.c:271`, the first statement after
`int assert = 0;`, and the recalculation begins at `:279-282`.  Nothing is computed when it dies.

  **But the substantive claim does not depend on the tense:** delete the kill and the helper WILL
  compute the level and assert on the existing path, and C040 does not change that level.  So the
  REASON is wrong and the CONCLUSION stands -- recorded that way rather than letting a wrong sentence
  ride inside a right verdict, which this project has been bitten by before.

**grok also holds S6's attribution INSUFFICIENT even as corrected:** *"it cannot tell bit from value,
cannot tell which repair you shipped, and at 0x04 it cannot tell Q2's two helper tails apart."*  That
third clause is the sharpest: **the witness cannot distinguish fall-through from return-without-
asserting**, which is exactly the Q2 the audit left open.

*** THIS VINDICATES THE HOLD, and it is worth saying plainly.  On codex's answer alone I would have
shipped DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE -- which grok argues is a WRONG RECORD IN PRODUCT CODE, of the
exact shape a previous round refused.  Two seats, opposite dispositions, and the owner's
hold-for-adjudication directive is what keeps it from being settled by whichever seat I asked
first. ***

**FOR THE ADJUDICATION:** the question is not "decline or accept" in the abstract.  It is whether a
LEGAL R/W BIT whose modelled effect is nil should be STORED (accept) or REFUSED (decline), and
whether an announce that describes an unmodelled PIN SELECTION while the INT path is used is a true
record or a false one.

*** THE RUNG-3 WITNESS IS BUILT AND MEASURED.  `regress/pcc2_c040_probe.py`, 3/4 on the committed
build, artifact `regress/artifacts/pcc2c040kill/witness_HEAD_20260907.raw`. ***

**The `witness` field used to read *"none -- READ, not run ... it has NOT been made, and this field
says `not yet done', never `did not think to ask'."*  That obligation is now discharged**, and the
lifecycle's own ruling is why it existed: *ask one seat to try a rung-3 probe before recording a
round as rung-1*.  The measurement:

    genctl ctl     alive        alive        CONTROL: same st.b, same GENCTL, benign 0x10
    genctl ctlq    no           no           CONTROL: the benign write must NOT reach the C040 arm
    c040 kill      died(exit1)  alive        THE DEFECT -- RED, as clause (i) requires
    c040 attrib    yes          yes          ATTRIBUTION: the death carries the arm's unique text
    EVIDENCE: pcc2: C040 interrupt assertions... TODO

**ONE legal guest byte store ends the host.**  No driver, no second access, no interrupt: the GENCTL
write arm stores `idata` UNMASKED and calls `reassert_interrupts()` in the same access, whose first
test is C040.  *That one-access reading is a codex CORRECTION of the row's own founding story* -- the
row was filed around a longer SCCRXIACK road reachable from OpenBSD's `cl.c`, which is real and
SUPERFLUOUS.  Nobody had noticed the short road because the long one was interesting.

**THE WITNESS'S OWN CONTRACT, written into its header:** it witnesses THIS `exit(1)` and is **NOT a
detector of the repair**.  The adjudicated disposition is DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE, and *"host
survives"* greens for a silent decline, a latched one and a real C040 implementation alike.  **A fix
round owes a row that discriminates them** -- for the latched form, the announce text and its
once-only property are the available channel.

*Two apparatus failures on the way in, both caught by the probe's own controls rather than by
inspection: a missing `DUMMY` made the forked child die on a NameError, and `c040 attrib` correctly
reported **died-elsewhere** rather than crediting the kill; then the `\0` in the repair cooked into
FOUR REAL NULL BYTES in the source, which is this project's escape-consumption class arriving through
a file write instead of a shell.  The second fix is escape-free by construction -- `bytes(4)`, which
no layer can consume.*

rows.note: *** THE ROW WAS FILED WITH AN EMPTY NOTE AND ZERO ENTRIES; the analysis below was written 2026-09-06 from the source and from the board manual that landed on disk the day before, NOT from the filing. ***  PATH, verified by reading: the write arm (anchor `case PCCTWO_GENCTL:') declines only WIDE writes -- that guard is #500's -- so a ONE-BYTE write passes it, is stored VERBATIM WITH NO MASK (`d->pcctwo_reg[relative_addr] = idata;`), and the arm then calls `reassert_interrupts(d)`, whose first statement is `if (d->pcctwo_reg[PCCTWO_GENCTL] & PCC2_C040) { fatal(...); exit(1); }`.  PCC2_C040 is 0x04 (mvme_pcctworeg.h).  GENCTL resets to 0x00, so the bit is clear until something writes it.  A single `st.b 0x04' to 0xfff42002 therefore ends the host process.  PRIMARY SOURCE, and it is new on disk (_scratchpad/vmesbcp2.txt, the MVME187 board manual, added 2026-09-05; anchor `General Control Register'): the register is at $FFF42002, 8 bits, layout DR0 / four READ-ONLY bits / C040 / MIEN / FAST -- so the model's constants agree with the manual -- and C040 is documented as *"CPU040.  This bit should be set when the MPU is from the M68000 family.  It should be cleared when the MPU is an MC88100.  When the bit is set, EIPL<2..0>* are driven as outputs which carry the priority encoded interrupt request from the PCCchip2 interrupt sources."*  The only machine that instantiates this device is MVME187, whose own comment in machine_mvme88k.c cites the installation guide for its `88100 MPU' -- so the manual says the bit SHOULD be clear here, which is what makes the TODO defensible as a TODO.  But NOTHING IN THE MANUAL GIVES THE CHIP A WAY TO REFUSE THE WRITE: setting C040 on an 88100 board is a misconfiguration that re-purposes three pins, not an access violation.  The model turns it into the death of the emulator.  REACH IS WIDER THAN THE WRITE ARM: `reassert_interrupts' has TEN call sites, and two are not guest accesses at all -- DEVICE_TICK(pcc2) calls it unconditionally every tick, and pcctwo_interrupt_common() calls it on every device interrupt assert/deassert.  There is no state in which C040 is set and the machine keeps running.  A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING IN THE SAME ARM: the manual marks bits 6..3 read-only and the model stores the whole byte unmasked, so a write of 0x78 sets four bits hardware would leave clear and a later read returns them.  The sibling arm one case below already carries the idiom (`case PCCTWO_VECBASE:` stores `idata & 0xf0` and announces the remainder).  Unmeasured either way -- no MVME187 boot runs in this harness.  OPTION SET, all six named before choosing (the carrier's rule): delete / decline silent / decline + latched announce (the file already has the machinery -- pcc2_width_decline() and the PCC2_W_* bit enum) / ACCEPT / fault / backed accept.  THE DECIDING QUESTION IS ACCEPT vs DECLINE: the model already computes the interrupt level and C040 only changes WHICH PINS carry it, and the model has no pins -- so if there is no observable difference inside this emulator between C040 set and clear, a decline would ship a wrong record in product code (announcing an ignore that did not happen) and ACCEPT is right.  Naming that observable is what the assess panel is for.  DE-ESCALATION COST, stated before the design is chosen: removing the host-fatal guard deletes the accidental tripwire, so the detector owes an ACCEPT-side row that REDDENS under the smallest realistic growth mutant -- a byte write of 0x04 serviced, the machine surviving, and a subsequent tick not killing.  Witness looks cheap at rung 3: regress/pcc2_width_probe.py already drives byte writes at this register on this machine, so it is one more session in an existing probe rather than new plumbing.  Assess brief written and panel-ready: _scratchpad/pcc2c040/brief_pcc2c040_assess.md (not yet fired -- a kill table held the machine).  A TRAP FOR A LATER ROUND, found while checking the constant against the manual and recorded so nobody re-derives it: mvme_pcctworeg.h defines the C040 bit TWICE, under two spellings with DIFFERENT values -- `PCC2_C040 0x04' (anchor `#define PCC2_C040') and `PCC2_GENCTL_C040 0x03' (anchor `#define PCC2_GENCTL_C040', in a second block at the end of the header alongside PCC2_GENCTL_FAST 0x01 and PCC2_GENCTL_IEN 0x02).  The manual's bit table settles it: C040 is 0x04 and the model uses the right one -- `PCC2_GENCTL_C040' has ZERO consumers in this tree (grep -rn PCC2_GENCTL_C040 src/ returns only its own definition).  It is a vendored third-party header, so this is upstream's inconsistency and not the fork's, and nothing is edited; but a future round reaching for the obvious-looking name would silently test FAST|MIEN instead of C040.

DEFECT, HIGH.  cpu_m88k.c, anchor `vector < M88K_EXCEPTION_USER_TRAPS_START && !implemented': only RESET/INTERRUPT/INSTRUCTION_ACCESS/DATA_ACCESS set `implemented = true'; nine other switch cases print a VERBOSITY_ERROR and break, so the fallback sets running=false on every CPU and returns (emul.c then breaks the main loop: a GRACEFUL guest-drivable machine halt, not an abort).  Pre-existing upstream (`git log -L' on the fallback returns only the 0.7.0 import); exposed by the #380 review, NOT introduced by #323/#380.  Reachable classes by raise site (deriver: grep -o 'm88k_exception(cpu, *M88K_EXCEPTION_[A-Z0-9_]+' src/cpus/cpu_m88k*.c | sort | uniq -c): PRIVILEGE_VIOLATION 10 (ldcr/stcr/xcr/rte/ld.usr/st.usr/tb0/tb1/tcnd in user mode), ILLEGAL_INTEGER_DIVIDE 4 (divu/div by zero, any mode), INTEGER_OVERFLOW 3 (add/sub, any mode), MISALIGNED_ACCESS 1, UNIMPLEMENTED_OPCODE 1 (prom_call in user mode); BOUNDS_CHECK and ERROR have no LITERAL-CONSTANT raise site -- but a supervisor tb0/tb1/tcnd names any 9-bit vector directly (`m88k_exception(cpu, ic->arg[2], 1)'), so both ARE reachable today (MEASURED on pass 1: supervisor `tb1 0,r3,7' halts HEAD; an earlier wording here said 'NO raise site today (latent)' -- corrected by #502's pass 1).  ERROR is additionally reached by the SFRZ re-route when a handler faults.  Vector offsets verified against Table 6-1 (mc88100.txt:8524-8538): PRIVILEGE 0x30, ILLEGAL_DIVIDE 0x40, OVERFLOW 0x48, MISALIGNED 0x20.  DISPOSITION: DELIVER (not a device-style decline -- the guest OS has handlers for these): `implemented = true' for the five, flowing through the existing common path (SFRZ, EPSR, SXIP/SNIP/SFIP shadow, supervisor switch, pc = VBR + 8*vector); MISALIGNED already fills DMT in the load/store template.  WITNESS OWED AT RUNG 3 BEFORE ANY EDIT: cold-debugger probe on committed testm88k or luna-88k (exemplars regress/m88k_idle_probe.py, m88k_rounding_probe.py): supervisor `divu r2,r3,r0', VBR into RAM, breakpoint at VBR+0x40, free-run -- pre-fix `unimplemented vector=0x008' and the machine stops; post-fix PC == VBR+0x40, SXIP = faulting instruction | XIP_V, PSR shadow frozen, machine running; plus a LIVENESS control (an already-delivered vector) and an ATTRIBUTION control (the same instruction on a non-faulting operand does not vector).  Split from m88kexcsfu1 (one fix design per round).  Ranked at the top of the live-defect tier, just below the exit(1)-abort class (this one stops gracefully). *** 2026-09-11: `commits` WAS EMPTY ON A **HIGH** ROW WHOSE FIX IS COMMITTED.  Set to `79cd12e`. ***

**This row's own title says one guest `divu rX,rY,r0` from USER MODE ends the emulation** -- and the record said the work had not shipped.  *A reader trusting `commits` reads a live user-reachable emulator-halt as outstanding.*

=== VERIFIED THREE INDEPENDENT WAYS BEFORE WRITING, because a correlate is not the thing ===
  1. **The tag is in committed source, and it is a FIX rather than a reference.**  `cpu_m88k.c` carries **seven** `implemented = true;  /*  m88kexcdeliver  */` lines -- at MISALIGNED_ACCESS, UNIMPLEMENTED_OPCODE, PRIVILEGE_VIOLATION, BOUNDS_CHECK_VIOLATION, ILLEGAL_INTEGER_DIVIDE, INTEGER_OVERFLOW and ERROR -- each an ASSIGNMENT that changes behaviour, not prose in a comment.
  2. **Line history settles the commit**: `git log -L 728,731:src/cpus/cpu_m88k.c` gives exactly two commits -- `79cd12e` and `39748e3` (the unmodified upstream import).  So the arm went from upstream's form straight to the fix, in `79cd12e`.
  3. **The commit message agrees and adds the scope**: *'#502 m88kexcdeliver (detector 46 -> 59 rows, **no product change after the fix**)'* -- i.e. that commit carries the product change, and passes 9-12 refined the DETECTOR only.

*** THE TITLE UNDERCOUNTS ITS OWN FIX: it names FIVE classes and SEVEN are repaired *** (BOUNDS_CHECK_VIOLATION and ERROR are also tagged).  Left as-is rather than rewritten, because the title is what the row was FILED as and the extra two are a fact about the repair; noted here so a future reader does not read the title as the repair's denominator.

*** STATE DELIBERATELY LEFT AT `in work`, AND THE RESTRAINT IS THE POINT. ***  Adding the commit is unambiguous -- the fix is in the tree and three checks agree.  **Closing it is not**: the sibling row [[m88kexcdetectorl2]] concerns an L2 in this very detector, and the most recent records commit (`8d372aa`) reports that *a HIGH row's 'measured clean sweep' was neither a sweep nor a failure -- the mutants target exception vectors the probe never drives*.  **A row covering work where part shipped and part is disputed is still live**, and this project's own rule is that a state misdescribing substance is the defect, in either direction.

**PROVENANCE: found by a sweep for live rows with an EMPTY `commits` whose id appears in COMMITTED `src/` -- 23 of 284 such rows matched.**  *That match is a CORRELATE, not a finding: a tag in source can equally be a comment NAMING the row as still-open (`#497` owed exactly such a comment for [[sgilinearoob]]).  So the other 22 were sent for classification rather than corrected in bulk* -- which is this project's own deriver-keys-on-a-correlate rule, applied before the error rather than after it.

**This is the SECOND ledger-is-stale-direction finding today**, after [[diskimagesign]].  Both run opposite to the twelve bug-file findings in the same sweep, and `check_bugfile_sync.py` checks only ledger -> bug file, so **neither direction of this pair is covered by anything** -- see [[bugfilereverse]].

rows.note: DEFECT, HIGH -- MEASURED (rung 3).  dev_luna88k.c: reassert_interrupts() (anchor `static void reassert_interrupts') walks `for (cpu = 0; cpu < MAX_CPUS; cpu++)' and calls INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->cpu_irq[cpu]) -- interrupt.h expands that to a direct call through `.interrupt_assert', no NULL check -- while DEVINIT connects cpu_irq[1..3] only under `if (devinit->machine->ncpus >= 2/3/4)' and memset()s the device to zero.  The INT_ST_MASK0-3 store arm (anchor `case INT_ST_MASK0:') does `d->interrupt_enable[cpunr] = idata; reassert_interrupts(d);' with NO ncpus check, and the SOFT_INT0-3 arm sets a per-slot pending bit and calls reassert synchronously.  On the default ONE-cpu luna-88k two ordinary guest word stores -- 0xfc000000 -> 0x65000004 (INT_ST_MASK1), then 1 -> 0x69000004 (SOFT_INT1) -- call a NULL function pointer: the emulator process dies with SIGSEGV, no diagnostic.  WITNESS: _scratchpad/lunaabs/luna_absentcpu_probe.py on the HEAD binary /tmp/gxopus501p4 (dev_luna88k.c cmp-equal to git HEAD 83df95c), committed unmodified `-e luna-88k', cold debugger: C1 RAM liveness OK, C2 device signature OK (MASK0 >>8), A1 the SAME two stores on the CONNECTED slot 0 SURVIVE (attribution), A2 the MASK1 store alone SURVIVES (readback 0x00fc0000: stored as-is), W1 SOFT_INT1 store: HOST DIED signal 11.  LUNA_ABSENTCPU_WITNESS=PRE_FIX_SYMPTOM, 1.4 s; log regress/artifacts/lunaabsentcpu/witness_head_20260905_2130.out, probe as run beside it.  Pre-existing upstream (the loop and the connect guards are 0.7.0 code); #438 removed the exit(1) on low bits in the SAME arm; its probe's D4 row stores 0x84000100 to MASK1 (bits 31, 26, 8 -- bit 26 SET, slot 1 ARMED for the rest of that session) and could not see this only because a cold debugger has nothing pending and the probe never stores SOFT_INT1 (an earlier wording here said 'bit 26 CLEAR'; corrected by the batch-7 Fable adjudication, which also notes that ANY device interrupt after the arming store kills the host on a running guest).  OPTION SET -- batch-7 Fable adjudication RULING (2026-09-05 ~22:40): (a) ALONE -- bound the reassert loop to `d->ncpus' captured at DEVINIT (house idiom dev_mp.c:134/:191 and this file's own RESET_CPU_ALL arm `i < cpu->machine->ncpus'); (b) declining stores to absent slots is REJECTED for this round (an unsourced board-model claim, changes guest-visible readback, reddens two shipped es438 rows D4/E2) and FILED as the question row lunaabsentmaskdecl; (c) a no-op connection fabricates plumbing with no in-tree idiom; (e) a NULL check guards the symptom.  Detector: W1 kill row + the connected-slot control + a `-n 2' ACCEPT row whose channel is cpu 1 ASSERTING (irq_asserted / vector entry), not survival; PRETABLE mutants `cpu <= d->ncpus', ncpus never assigned (slot 0 never asserted: the boot gate reds), `ncpus = 1' hardcoded.  Wire luna_absentcpu_probe.py into gate_m88k_rounding.sh.  Also owed in that round: es438cells (MASK2/MASK3 readback rows).  Ranked HIGH: guest-reachable process death by an ordinary instruction on the machine the project boots (precedent: pcc2defaultkill, m88kexcdeliver ranked on reachability, not on a known driver doing it).  Provenance: retrospective batch 7 -- GPT-6 Astra (codex, max effort, read-only) predicted it from the source ('interrupt delivery can still reach an unconnected CPU callback'); the main loop built and ran the witness the same evening; Fable 5.1 adjudication of batch 7 in flight.  The fix round runs the full nine-seat panel.

=== MAIN-LOOP ROUND RECORDS, 2026-09-06 -- moved out of the per-seat `entries' column ===

Because passes 3 and 4 both found breaches of the {slot} x {per-cpu array} alias class, the repair closes the CLASS in one diff rather than the cell: probe v6 (md5 3be01e9d) RESTORES v4's session E beside v5's all-four E as session E2 (slots 2 and 3 pending, 0 and 1 idle; rows cpu3 deliver23, cpu2 deliver23, others idle23 -- 37 rows), in which every per-cpu array the walk touches has a disagreeing alias target.  Mutants added: M_ENP1, M_SWP1 (the two predicted sweeps, each ALSO scored on the frozen v5 so the escape is measured), M_EN0, M_SW0, and -- instead of disclosing the other alias forms as debt -- M_ENX1 (`cpu ^ 1`, derived to be killed by sio5 deliver1) and M_ENSH1 (`cpu >> 1`, killed by E2).  A first draft of PRETABLE5 had disclosed `cpu ^ 1` as an escape; that was wrong about C4 and was corrected BEFORE the table ran.  Table 5 (24 mutants) launched 12:5x.

  [2026-09-06 / review] **PASS 5 -- TWO OF MY OWN RECORDS ARE WRONG, both found by codex AND grok independently, and I VERIFIED BOTH BY OPENING THE FILES.**  (1) **THE NARROWED M_NULLAB EXPIRY IS FALSE, and it came from the opus5 pass-4 answer, which I propagated without checking.**  That clause said an EMPTY interrupt name installs non-NULL `no_interrupt_assert' / `no_interrupt_deassert' stubs, so `has a callback' and `slot < ncpus' differ in MECHANISM.  Read `src/core/interrupt.c' (anchor `if (name[0] ==' the empty-string test): the arm assigns the stubs and **DOES NOT RETURN** -- the handler scan runs immediately after it, and an unregistered name falls through to `printf(... failed)' and `abort()`.  So the stub path is DEAD unless the empty string is itself a registered handler name, and `INTERRUPT_CONNECT("")` appears nowhere.  The two predicates coincide **because the stub path is dead**, not because slots 1..3 happen to use non-empty names.  grok adds that pass 1 already had this.  The M_NULLAB equivalence is UNAFFECTED and the fix is not reopened; only the expiry sentence is corrected.  (2) **THE PASS-5 PACKET NAMES THE WRONG RED ROWS FOR M_IRQACTIVEP1.**  Its table says `cpu2 deliver23, cpu3 deliver23' (session E2).  killtable5/driver.log at the `=== M_IRQACTIVEP1' anchor says **`cpu3 deliver' and `cpu2 deliver' -- session E**, and E2 passes.  Verified.  The mutant aliases a WRITE, so the first arrival of each pair consumes the latch whichever session pends them; E2 exists for the READ aliases and correctly does not red here.  A transcription error in a packet that had the log open beside it.  **WHAT THE TWO SEATS RULED ON THE ROUND'S ONE QUESTION: the closure bound HOLDS.**  grok: `function of cpu alone' is the right bound for THIS class, with the derivation -- the one-cpu session forces f(0)=0, session C forces f(1)=1, session E2 forces f({2,3}) inside {2,3}, so every single-token map except the identity dies; cells outside f(cpu) are body-field indices (`enable[irqActive[cpu]]' is [0] on the first walk and dies on C); a joint same-f on enable and software_interrupt_status still dies on E2 (opus5 measured M_ENP1 and M_ENP1E both 35/37); and expanding past single-token f(cpu) is the unbounded chase.  No clean-sweep sits in the remainder.  **ONE REAL PROBE DEFECT, ship-time rather than a new pass (grok): session E2 never sets cpu 0's VBR/PSR, though session E does.**  So `others idle23' can see a steal onto cpu 1 (M_AND1 reads BADREGS with pcs[1] at the vector) and CANNOT see one onto cpu 0 -- a CHANNEL filter on an existing row, not a new cell.  Fix: copy E's two sends.  Both seats also note the product-comment L4 is still present in killtable5/baseline_dev_luna88k.c -- correct, and it stays: that file is the frozen record of what the table ran.  The SHIPPING script (fix_lunaabs.py) was corrected before either answer landed.

M_SOFTAND1 `software_interrupt_status[cpu]&1`: 37/37, TOTAL ESCAPE.**  *** BOTH ARE MEMBERS OF FAMILIES THIS PROBE HAD ALREADY DISCLOSED, WHICH IS CLAUSE (e) WORKING RATHER THAN A FLOOR BREACH. ***  M_SOFTAND1 is the `== 1` cell opus5 disclosed on pass 4 (the body tests nonzero-ness and never partitions the nonzero class; every SOFT value any session writes is 1, so any predicate true of 1 preserves every observation) -- two spellings, one cell. *** CLOSED 2026-09-07 AS A RECORDS CORRECTION.  THE FIX SHIPPED IN `79cd12e` ON 2026-09-06 AND THE
ROW WAS NEVER UPDATED. ***

`dev_luna88k.c` carries the repair BY NAME: *"#503 (lunaabsentcpu): bound `reassert_interrupts()` to
the slots connected above.  It walked all MAX_CPUS and called the NULL interrupt_assert of an
unpopulated slot ... measured, `regress/luna_absentcpu_probe.py`."*  The loop bound changed from
`cpu < MAX_CPUS` to `cpu < d->ncpus`, the `ncpus` snapshot field was added with its own comment, and
the 48 kB probe was committed in the same commit.  Kill tables ran; two total escapes were measured
and both disposed under clause (e) as members of families the probe had already disclosed; the
residual is filed as `lunancpus3`.

**So the work was complete and only the row was wrong** -- state `open`, `commits` empty, severity
HIGH.  It inflated the open-HIGH count and would have misled anyone picking the next round: I
reported ten open HIGH rows earlier today and the true figure was nine.

*** THE SWEEP, because one instance is not a population. ***  Two derivers were run and the first was
wrong in the way this project keeps re-learning:
  * **keyed on a CORRELATE** -- open rows citing a recent commit SHA anywhere in their note -- gave
    EIGHT, and seven were false: they cite a commit as CONTEXT (a blocker, the round they audit, a
    records commit), not as their own fix;
  * **keyed on what DEFINES the class** -- row ids named inside a `#NNN (rowid)` fix tag in `src/` --
    gave THREE, of which `pcc2defaultkill` is correctly closed and `wdcflood` is `in work` WITH
    commits, a legitimate intermediate state.

**Population: ONE.**  No checker catches this shape -- `check_row_states` verifies that no open row
NAMES a committed detector, and this row named nothing; `check_bugfile_sync` and `check_witness` both
pass on it.  *A row can be complete in the tree and open in the ledger with every gate green.*

rows.title: wdcbeoddtail  on a BIG-ENDIAN machine a 16-bit data-port read that pops the last valid byte plus the empty-ring sentinel folds the sentinel INTO the valid byte -- (v << 8) + 0xffff...ff = (v << 8) - 1, so the guest reads v-1 (0x00 becomes 0xff; a borrow can alter two valid bytes on a 4-byte read); the LE arm only pollutes the padding byte
rows.witness: none
rows.note: DEFECT, MEDIUM (re-rank HIGH if a real driver is measured popping the odd tail: the tell is the `[ wdc: WARNING! someone is reading too much from the wdc inbuf! ]' line in a `evbmips -e maltabe' boot log with an ATAPI image).  Site: dev_wdc.c `case wd_data:' BE assembly `odata = (odata << 8) + wdc_get_inbuf(d)' with `wdc_get_inbuf' returning (uint64_t) -1 on an empty ring; memory_writemax64 (BE) hands buf[0] bits 15:8.  Enumerated by Fable: 2-byte/1 valid -> [v-1, 0xff]; v = 0x00 -> [0xff, 0xff]; 4-byte with valid 0x12 0x00 -> [0x11, 0xff, 0xfe, 0xff].  Reachable: MALTA BE (machine_evbmips.c `MALTA (evbmips, big endian)') gets the wdc via bus_pci.c `PCIINIT(piix4_ide)'; odd lengths from `case SCSICMD_INQUIRY:' (retlen = cmd[4], min 36); the model reports the ODD byte count unpadded in wd_cyl_lo/hi, so whether a driver pops the tail is arch-specific (OpenBSD 2.2 isa/wdc.c uses bus_space_read_raw_multi_2 with the odd len).  WITNESS OWED AT RUNG 3 before any edit: `evbmips -e maltabe' + ATAPI image, INQUIRY-37 CDB via six 16-bit data-port stores then nineteen 16-bit loads -- pre-fix the 19th returns [v-1, 0xff], post-fix intact; LE control on `-e malta'; the over-read latch line is the device signature.  OPTION SET: (1) mask each pop `& 0xff' at the assembly (no other consumer changes); (2) return 0 on empty -- changes the LE pad 0xff -> 0x00 AND reds the shipped `overread -1' row (oracle-correction ORDER rule applies); (3) pad odd DATA-IN transfers to an even count and report it (BELIEVED: the ATAPI word-transfer rule; no standard on disk).  Detector: the differential's `row_odd_width' checks counters only and its memory_writemax64 stub always serialises LE -- both must change for an offline row; discharges part of wdcletwins and wdcprobeendian.  Provenance: retrospective re-check (owner directive 2026-09-04) batch 3a -- GPT-6 Astra (codex, max effort) read-only review, adjudicated by Fable 5.1; artifacts regress/artifacts/retro_20260905/batch3a_wdc/ (astra_batch3a.txt, fable_adj_batch3a.md). *** MY ONE-ROUND HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, 2026-09-11 (wdcerrfamily/codex_errfamily_20260911.txt).  TWO ROUNDS, AND THE REASON IS PRECISE: SEPARATING THE STORAGE REPAIRS ONLY ONE OF THEM. ***

I proposed that [[wdcdiagerr]] (ERR set when the command succeeded) and [[wdcpktstatus]] (ERR clear when it failed) were one defect seen from opposite sides -- both consequences of `d->error` being the only thing that can raise `WDCS_ERR`.  **The diagnostic row is a CONFLATION of two meanings in one variable; the ATAPI row is an independent OMISSION of result propagation.**

*** THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT IS A ZERO: THERE ARE **NO** READS OF THE ATAPI TRANSFER'S STATUS ANYWHERE IN `dev_wdc.c`. ***  No `d->atapi_st->status` access, no alias, no alternative status-field read.  What the controller DOES consume from the backend is a separate return value `res`, tested only for `== 0` and `== 1`; the transfer object's data pointer, length and payload are read, and **the recorded status is left unconsumed through completion and freed at the next packet dispatch**.

So for a dispatched packet on an existing image, with no intervening command, **backend failure has no implemented route to raise ERR at all**: `status_byte()` returns `DRDY | DSC = 0x50` and the Error register stays `0x00`.  `PHASE_COMPLETED` supplies no hidden indication -- it is `WDCI_IN | WDCI_CMD` = `0x03`, and `status_byte()` takes only DRQ information from `atapi_phase`, never bit zero.

*** AND A SCOPE WARNING FOR THIS ROW SPECIFICALLY: ATA-2 DOES NOT SPECIFY ATAPI PACKET COMPLETION, SO DO NOT SOURCE THIS ROW FROM IT. ***  The fetched draft contains no ATAPI, PACKET or CHECK CONDITION definition, and its informative command summary explicitly **reserves `A0h-AFh`** (`ata2_x3t10_948d.txt:5828`) -- while `wdcreg.h` defines the model's PACKET opcode as `0xa0`.  **A claim about required ATAPI completion behaviour sourced from ATA-2 would be sourced from the wrong standard.**  The packet interface was specified separately (SFF-8020 and later folded into ATA/ATAPI-4); settling this row needs THAT document, on the same fetch-and-verify-locally pattern that settled [[ppcrlwhighhalf]] and [[wdcaltdigin]] today.

*I asked the review to tell me plainly if ATAPI was out of scope rather than answer from the wrong document, and it did.  That instruction earned its place.*

*** ATA-2 SETTLES THE SHAPE OF THIS FIX AND IT IS NOT THE CLAMP THE ROW ASSUMES.  2026-09-11 (ata2batch/codex_ata2batch_20260911.txt). ***

**WHAT WORD 1 IS:** *"The number of user-addressable logical cylinders in the default translation mode"* (S7.15.2, `ata2_x3t10_948d.txt:2807-2809`).  **A COUNT of logical cylinders** -- not a physical-geometry requirement and not the highest cylinder ADDRESS.  S7.2 makes the mapping from logical addresses to physical media explicitly vendor-specific.

*So the separate statement that cylinders are numbered 0 through at most 65,535 is an ADDRESS-NUMBER limit and does not make word 1 a 65,535-capped address.  A count of 65,536 simply cannot be represented in sixteen bits.*

*** AND ANNEX D GIVES THE LIMIT THE MODEL IS ALREADY VIOLATING, BEFORE THE TRUNCATION IS EVEN REACHED: ***

    :5590-5591  "For drives less than or equal to 528 MB, Identify Data word 1 (Default
                 Cylinders) SHALL NOT specify a value greater than 1,024."

The witnessed case is a **32 MiB** image with heads = sectors = 1, giving 65,536 cylinders.  **That geometry breaches Annex D's limit by a factor of 64 before anything overflows** -- the zero in word 1 is the SYMPTOM of a bad geometry choice, not an independent arithmetic defect.

*** SO A CLAMP IS THE WRONG FIX, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. ***  Clamping 65,536 to 65,535 -- or to 1,024 -- would report a cylinder COUNT that does not describe the image, replacing a meaningless zero with a plausible wrong number.  **That is strictly worse: a zero is visibly broken and a plausible count is not.**  The repair is to CHOOSE a default translation geometry that both fits sixteen bits and covers the image.

**A WORKED EXAMPLE, offered as illustrative and NOT as mandated** -- the review is explicit that the standard specifies no universal overflow-repair algorithm: `1024 x 2 x 32 = 65,536 sectors` preserves the whole 32 MiB and meets Annex D's limits.  **The CHS mapping must then use the selected geometry too**, since the model's read and write offsets depend on its heads and sectors-per-track arrays -- so this is not a one-line change to the IDENTIFY word.

**ANNEX D IS INFORMATIVE**, and the row must not overstate it: it is introduced with *"Maximum compatibility is achieved if the following rules are obeyed"*, and its use of *shall* does not change that stated status.  The fetched document is also a **Revision 4c working draft** whose own cover says it is not an approved standard.

RAISED TO MED from LOW: the defect is no longer *an unclamped truncation in one IDENTIFY word* but *a default geometry that violates the compatibility limit for its own image size*, and the repair touches the geometry arrays the transfer path reads.

*** THE ROW'S PREMISE IS INVERTED BY ATA-2, AND THE REAL DEFECT IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I FILED.  2026-09-11 (ata2batch/codex_ata2batch_20260911.txt), then traced locally before recording. ***

**I filed this as "the model writes 1 where the correct diagnostic code belongs".  `0x01` IS THE CORRECT CODE.**  ATA-2 `:2534-2535`: *"Device 1 sets bit 7 of the Error register to zero and posts its diagnostic results to bits 6 through 0 of Error register"*, and the reset algorithm at `:5083-5084`: *"If Device 1 completed all initialization and diagnostic without error, Set the Error register to 01h and assert PDIAG-."*  So the VALUE the model writes is right.

*** THE DEFECT IS THE COUPLING, NOT THE VALUE -- AND `d->error' IS ONE VARIABLE SERVING TWO REGISTERS WITH OPPOSITE MEANINGS. ***  Traced in `dev_wdc.c`:
  * `:1843`  `odata = d->error;`                     -- it IS the **Error register** content;
  * `:594`   `if (d->error) odata |= WDCS_ERR;`      -- it ALSO drives the **Status register's ERR**
                                                        flag, inside `status_byte()`.

**ATA-2 keeps those apart and the header does too**: the generic `ERR` flag belongs to the STATUS register, while the Error register holds either a diagnostic code or ordinary error bits depending on context -- `0x01` is *diagnostic success* after a reset or diagnostic, and `AMNF`, Address Mark Not Found, under the ordinary interpretation (`:1663-1666`).  `wdcreg.h` defines **`WDCS_ERR = 0x01` and `WDCE_AMNF = 0x01`** -- the same numeric value in two different registers.

*** SO AFTER EXECUTE DEVICE DIAGNOSTIC THE MODEL SIMULTANEOUSLY REPORTS DIAGNOSTIC SUCCESS IN THE ERROR REGISTER AND COMMAND FAILURE IN THE STATUS REGISTER. ***  A driver reading STATUS sees ERR set on a command that succeeded.  **The diagnostic code `01h` is precisely the value that makes the conflation visible**, because it is the one code meaning *success* that also lights the ERR bit through this shared variable.

**WHAT THE REPAIR NEEDS, and it is bigger than a constant:** the Error-register content and the Status ERR flag need separating, which touches every `d->error |= WDCE_ABRT` site as well as the two diagnostic assignments.  *A one-line change to the diagnostic value would leave the ERR bit wrong and is exactly the half-fix this finding rules out.*

CAVEAT THE SEAT STATED ITSELF AND I AM KEEPING: the fetched document is **Revision 4c working draft**, whose own cover says it is not an approved, completed standard.
