*** `#523` PASS 1, 2026-09-11 (codex GPT-6 Astra at max, 15,825 b, complete).  **CONDITIONAL ACCEPT -- THE FIELD IS SOUND AND THREE OF MY ARGUMENTS ARE OVERSTATED.** ***

*"The separate ERR field is sound; its necessity, the mode-flag rejection, and parts of the reset argument are overstated."*  **The eight-writer classification is CONFIRMED and none of the eight means ERR alone** -- so the design constraint holds and the fix is accepted.  What follows is what I got wrong around it.

**(1) THE CLASSIFICATION DOES NOT, BY ITSELF, PROVE ANOTHER FIELD IS NECESSARY -- and that was my whole addition warrant.**  Under normal initialisation and these writers, `d->error` takes only **0, 1 and 4**.  *A predicate recognising 4 as failure could reproduce the intended ERR behaviour over every value currently generated.*  **So the warrant has to be the SEMANTIC SEPARATION argument, not the absence of an ERR-only writer.**  I had been leaning on the absence.

**(2) MY MODE-FLAG REJECTION IS REFUTED, and the refutation is exact.**  I rejected `diag_mode` because a future writer with a third meaning re-creates the defect.  *"A future writer can forget to maintain either `diag_mode` or `status_err`.  **Neither representation makes new meanings automatically correct.**"*  The argument does not discriminate between the two designs, so it cannot select one.

Worse for my framing: **the mode flag already escapes the defective class.**  Its expression is `ERR = f(Error, diagnostic_mode)`, not `ERR = f(Error)`, so it represents diagnostic `Error=1, ERR=0` and ordinary AMNF `Error=1, ERR=1` perfectly well -- **and it may need FEWER write-site changes**: clear the mode at command entry, set it at the two diagnostic assignments, leave the five ABRT sites untouched.

> The seat still FAVOURS `status_err` -- it directly represents the architectural status being reported, and `wdc_abort()` records failure where the outcome is known -- but explicitly as **a defensible design preference and a transferred warrant.  "Calling the mode design inherently defective would overstate the evidence."**  *That is the correction: my reason was wrong even though my choice survives.*

**(3) THE AMNF OBJECTION IS VALID SEMANTICALLY AND IS NOT A REACHABLE REGRESSION.**  `WDCE_AMNF` really is `0x01` (`wdcreg.h:100`) and the draft defines it in the normal Error interpretation (`ata2:1664`), so excluding value 1 permanently confuses a diagnostic pass with an AMNF-only error.  **But the reviewed device code does not generate AMNF**, so the value-exception design is rejected on semantics, not on a live defect.  *I had implied it was live.*

**(4) A DETAIL OF THE TRANSFERRED WARRANT WAS WRONG.**  `error` and `precomp` are **ADJACENT, at `:126` and `:127`** -- not "three lines apart" as I wrote.  And the precedent is sharper than I stated: `wdcreg.h:50` gives **Error, Precompensation AND Features the same offset 1**, and the handler reads `error` while writing `precomp` at `:1841`.  The transferable form is narrower than *two meanings require two fields*: **"represent separately specified state separately when sharing or deriving its representation confuses its meaning."**

**(5) THE POWER-ON DEFECT IS REAL WITH A QUALIFICATION I HAD MISSED, and the qualification makes a better table.**  `status_byte()` adds DRDY and DSC **only when the selected disk image exists**, so immediately after initialisation and before any command:

    selected image   current Status   proposed Status   Error (both)
    present          0x51             0x50              0x01
    absent           0x01             0x00              0x01

**And my supporting claim was unsupported: the files do not establish "every driver reads Status at attach", nor the relative frequency of diagnostics, nor any measured boot consequence.**  What they DO establish is the reachability asymmetry -- *initialisation is unconditional, while reaching the diagnostic arm requires a command and surviving the preliminary checks* -- which carries the argument **without a driver census**.  A better warrant than the one I offered.

**(6) THE CLEAR PLACEMENT IS RIGHT AND MY SRST JUSTIFICATION IS NOT.**  Keep `status_err = 0` beside the existing clear in `wdc_command()` at `:841`, before either early rejection -- it then handles both successful commands and commands that immediately fail again. **(7) A CENSUS WORDING CORRECTION:** *"eight explicit assignment sites" is accurate; "only eight operations ever write that storage" is NOT* -- the whole-struct `memset` at `:1988` is an implicit initialisation write.

**ATA-2 SCOPE HELD:** keeping the two `error = 1` assignments is supported **without Annex A**.  It certifies nothing about the surrounding diagnostic implementation, reset sequencing, device-selection handling or readiness timing, and **these four sections give no warrant whatever for packet results or CHECK CONDITION semantics** -- which is round two's blocker and must not be borrowed.

rows.title: mipstiny  cpu_mips_coproc.c fpu_subst_tiny(): does classifying tininess on the ENCODED destination word match the MIPS rule, or is after-rounding tininess judged with an UNRESTRICTED exponent range?  THE SOURCE ARGUES ONE WAY AND A REVIEWING SEAT THE OTHER -- unresolved, for the flagship seat
rows.witness: none -- READ only.  No emulator run was made by either side; the seat says so itself (`no emulator witness was run').
rows.hold_question: The fork's own comment and the reviewing seat give OPPOSITE readings of the same MIPS sentence, and both are reasoned.  Which is right: is IEEE/MIPS after-rounding tininess judged on the value rounded to the destination PRECISION with an UNBOUNDED exponent (the seat), or on the word as ENCODED in the destination format (the source)?  They differ exactly on the sliver where a value rounds UP into the normal range only because the subnormal encoding has fewer significand bits.  Second: if the seat is right, is the divergence reachable by any OS in the tree -- the seat found no setter for the flush control in the supplied sources and recommends documented-only pending an OS-use witness rather than claiming unreachability.
rows.note: RAISED by the retrospective batch-12 review and RE-FIRED as a standalone question to GPT-6 Astra at max effort on 2026-09-06; its answer is preserved at _scratchpad/codex_mipstiny/ANSWER_astra_20260906.txt.  *** FILED AS A DISAGREEMENT, NOT AS A DEFECT, BECAUSE THE SOURCE CARRIES A REASONED COUNTER-POSITION AND NOBODY HAS MEASURED EITHER. ***  THE SEAT'S POSITION: MIPS specifies after-rounding tininess with an UNRESTRICTED exponent range, and `fpu_subst_tiny` incorrectly equates that with the destination word coming out subnormal.  Discriminating input 0x1.fffffep-127 = (2^24 - 1) * 2^-150 through cvt.s.d under round-to-nearest with the flush control set and the underflow and inexact traps disabled: exactly 24 significant bits, so it is unchanged by rounding at unbounded exponent and is tiny; but the subnormal encoding at 2^-126 has fewer significand bits, so it rounds UP to FLT_MIN and encodes NORMAL -- and the fork therefore substitutes nothing where the seat says MIPS requires a substitution.  THE SOURCE'S POSITION, which the seat did not quote and which I read before filing (anchor `Classification is done on the ENCODED word'): *"Classification is done on the ENCODED word, not on the host double, so it is tininess AFTER rounding, which is what MIPS specifies: the exact upper midpoint 2^-126 - 2^-150 rounds to FLT_MIN under nearest and is then a NORMAL result that must not be substituted at all."*  So the fork made this choice DELIBERATELY and argues it IS the MIPS rule.  The two positions turn on one question -- whether the rounding that decides tininess is done at unbounded exponent or in the destination encoding -- and that question is settled by the manual, not by either party's confidence.  WHAT THE SEAT ALSO ESTABLISHED, and it is useful whichever way the main question goes: the guest write that enables the flush control is accepted (`case COPz_CTCz`); the operand is normal in double precision so the operand-denormal trap does not intercept it; the destination-register difference would be observable; and OpenBSD 2.2's arc/pmax `machdep.c` zeroes the whole control word at `setregs`, with NO setter for the flush bit found anywhere in the supplied sources.  Its own recommendation is documented-only pending an OS-use witness, on the ground that calling it unreachable would overstate the evidence -- which is the right shape.  AND IT REFUTED THE CHEAP CROSS-CHECK: the SuperH model's denormal-mode policy is NOT a parallel that can justify the MIPS one.  It cites sh7750_hardware.txt (anchor `6.7.1 Rounding Mode and Underflow Flag'), which discusses a result that IS normal after rounding while an underflow is still signalled -- different rules that happen to agree on the tested inputs.  OWED: the manual sentence itself, quoted with its anchor from mips-iv.txt / mips64_volII.txt / mips32_volII.txt, by a seat that has not already taken a side.  Ranked LOW until then -- if the seat is right this is a real conformance divergence on a sliver, and if the source is right the batch-12 record needs a line saying so, because an uncorrected claim gets reused.

rows.title: m88k SFRZ re-route, TRAP side: MODE and SFD1 do not vary across the fourteen trap rows, so a widened inner guard escapes the 57-row detector
rows.witness: detector:regress/m88k_exc_probe.py -- rows trapfrozenuser (MODE) and trapfrozensfd1 (SFD1)
rows.state_note:
[2026-10-02] COMMITS FIELD FILLED by #557 from the census of closed rows with no commit (regress/artifacts/closeassess_20261002/grok/grok_closedcensus.txt; Astra's git log, regress/artifacts/closeassess_20261002/aconf_census/codex_aconf_census.txt): 79cd12e8 -- names #502; touches regress/m88k_exc_probe.py.  FILED as clause-(e) DEBT on 2026-09-06 and ADJUDICATED TO FLOOR the same evening by the pass-11 panel; REPAIRED IN-ROUND as L2 (probe v19, 57 -> 59 rows).  The original filing text is preserved below the rule, because a filing that was overturned is part of the record and not an embarrassment to be tidied away.

*** WHY IT IS FLOOR AND NOT DEBT -- TWO INDEPENDENT PRECEDENTS, BOTH FROM THIS ROUND'S OWN RECORDS, BOTH VERIFIED BY OPENING THE ARTIFACT BEFORE ACTING. ***
  * grok: PRETABLE12 graded this EXACT inner `if' as L2 -- its disposition line reads "L2, in-round" -- when     `if (!is_trap || !(PSR & IND))' swept 46/46.  IND, C and SER at this site were then repaired in-round as     floor (trapfrozenind/c/ser).  Grading the remaining two bits at the SAME SITE as debt would be     inconsistent, and would retroactively un-grade three rows this campaign shipped as floor.
  * kimi: ITS VERDICT LINE SAID DEBT AND ITS BODY SAID FLOOR, reaching grok's conclusion by a different     route -- the pass-5 and pass-7 mutants `!is_trap || vector == <class>' condition on `vector', which the     guarded body does not test either, and those were repaired in-round (trapfrozen4/5/6/9, then     trapfrozen450/496).  So the PRACTISED rule already covers fields a mutant can condition on at this guard.
  * minimax voted DEBT and is outvoted BY ARGUMENT, not by count: neither precedent was contested by anyone,     and both are checkable in one grep.

My own reading -- the generating-set letter, `the partitions the guarded body itself tests' -- loses on its own terms, which kimi showed: it would ALSO have made the vector rows debt, and the round shipped those as floor.  The letter was written for idata bits of a device write; here PSR is the GUARD's operand and the value the body writes is `vector = ERROR'.

*** AND MY REACHABILITY ARGUMENT WAS WRONG IN ITS DETAIL, which grok corrected. ***  I claimed the cell is reachable by composing `errpriv' (a frozen handler dropping to user mode) with `trapfrozen128' (a frozen user trap).  `trapfrozen128' is a SUPERVISOR trap NAMING vector 128, MODE=1 -- not a user-mode trap -- and `errpriv''s handler does stcr then ldcr, which raises PRIVILEGE with is_trap == 0 and never reaches a trap at all.  The cell IS reachable, by a different construction: `[STCR_R5_CR1, TB1_0_R3_128]' with r5 = PSR_FRZUSER and **r3 = 0x11**, because bit 0 must be SET or the tb1 does not trap and the row is silently inert.

THE REPAIR: two rows in trapfrozenind's shape, so they inherit its frozen-shadow expectations and its no-refatal channel with no new machinery.  `trapfrozenuser' puts MODE clear at the trap side (a frozen handler drops to user mode, then traps at vector 128 -- >= USER_TRAPS_START so the fallback does not claim it, and X(tb1) checks privilege only for vector < 128).  `trapfrozensfd1' puts SFD1 clear (PSR_FRZSUP, then the same tb1 naming 7 as trapfrozenind).  CHANNEL: under the mutant a trap that WOULD be exempted is re-routed, so each row moves from DELIVER at its own vector to STOP at 0x50 AND the re-route diagnostic appears where REFATAL_EXPECT says it must not -- two observables, both already read.

*** THIS IS THE FOURTH TIME THIS CHAIN HAS CLOSED AN AXIS AT SOME CELLS AND CALLED THE REST SOMETHING ELSE, AND I DID IT INSIDE THE CENSUS WRITTEN TO END THAT PATTERN. ***  Passes 6, 7, 8 and 9 each found a repair that reproduced the defect it repaired; the cell census was built to make the whole space visible at once, and the filing written from it closed three cells at a site and filed the other two under a different heading.

--- THE ORIGINAL FILING, preserved ---
FILED 2026-09-06 from the #502 pass-10 cell census (regress/artifacts/m88kexcdeliver/derive_cells.py, output CELLCENSUS.out).  DERIVED, NOT MEASURED, and said so.

At the SFRZ re-route's TRAP side every one of the fourteen trap rows carries MODE=1 and SFD1=1.  A widened inner guard -- `if (!is_trap || !(PSR & M88K_PSR_MODE))' -- would therefore be invisible to the shipped instrument.  THE CELL IS REACHABLE, and both halves already exist in the probe separately: a frozen handler can drop to user mode (errpriv/errunimpl do exactly that, via PSR_FRZUSER) and a user trap at a vector >= 128 is a genuine trap (trapfrozen128).  No row combines them.  The SFD1 cell is the same shape via PSR_FRZSUP, which errdiv0 already builds.

DEBT, NOT A FLOOR BREACH, and the distinction is the carrier's own bound rather than a convenience: the floor asks for the partitions THE GUARDED BODY ITSELF TESTS.  That body tests `is_trap' and the outer `PSR & SFRZ', and both polarities of both are rowed.  MODE at the trap side is a single-axis marginal against an lvalue the body does not test there, which clause (e) discloses.

*** A FALSE L4 WAS NEARLY FILED BESIDE THIS AND WAS CHECKED FIRST. ***  The contract's sentence `every stcr-settable 88100 bit now varies there' reads like a per-branch claim and is measurably FALSE of the trap side alone.  It governs the OUTER guard, which sees both branches -- and over their union every bit does vary (MODE by errpriv, SER by errser/trapfrozenser, C by errc/trapfrozenc, SFD1 by errdiv0, IND by errind/trapfrozenind).  The claim is correct as written.  Recorded because the near-miss is the instructive part: a census that reports per-branch will make a correct union claim look wrong.

rows.title: dev_wdc.c ATAPI accounting: `consumed` counts helper CALLS, not successful pops -- over-counts when the input ring under-runs mid-access
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-06 from the `83df95c` pass 2 (panel_20260906_211839 + the codex run at regress/artifacts/retro_20260905/batch3a_wdc/pass2_seats/).  **DERIVED BY READING, NOT MEASURED, and the reachability half is explicitly NOT established.**

In the ATAPI accounting arm of `DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc)`'s `wd_data` read:

    int consumed = len == 4 ? 4 : (len >= 2 ? 2 : 1);

**`consumed` is computed from `len` ALONE.**  It counts the helper CALLS the arm makes, not the pops that
succeeded.  `wdc_get_inbuf()` returns `(uint64_t) -1` on an empty ring and returns BEFORE advancing the tail
-- verified by reading, the early return sits three lines above the advance -- so with `q` bytes queued a
width-`w` access pops `min(q, calls)`.  When the ring under-runs mid-access, `consumed` therefore over-counts
and `atapi_len` is decremented by more than the guest received.

*** THAT IS THE EXACT DEFECT #341 EXISTS TO FIX, QUOTED THREE LINES ABOVE THE EXPRESSION. ***  The comment reads *"account for what was actually CONSUMED from the buffer, not for what the guest asked for ... the count reported has to be the count that happened"* -- and the expression under it reports a count derived from the request.  #341 replaced `len` with this expression, which is correct whenever the ring holds enough bytes and wrong in exactly the residual case the same round was reasoning about.

**WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED IN-ROUND**, stated so nobody re-argues it: the stopping rule fixes a review finding in-round only if it is a MEASURED FALSE PASS or a WRONG RECORD.  The COMMENT was a wrong record and was corrected in place (L4, same commit).  The CODE question is a new defect with no witness: nothing here shows a guest reaching an under-run mid-access on the ATAPI path, and the over-read is already announced by the `warned_inbuf_overread` latch, so the silent-corruption claim is unproven.  **A round on this owes the rung-3 attempt** the lifecycle ruling requires.

**A SECOND OBSERVABLE IS WORSE THAN THE COUNT AND IS NOT ANALYSED HERE:** the arm accumulates with `odata += (wdc_get_inbuf(d) << 8)`, so a failed pop adds the sentinel's bits into the value the guest reads, not merely into the count.  Whether that is reachable, and whether the latch fires first, is the round's first question.

Codex noted `row_odd_step` and `row_odd_width` in `regress/diff_wdc_identify.c` already exercise the attempts-vs-pops distinction, so a detector may be closer than it looks.  It also found, separately, that `wdc_flood_probe.py`'s `overrun x2` omits the `r3` completion assertion -- a PRE-EXISTING coverage gap, not a stale expected value (row `wdcfloodprobe` already carries the probe's owed items).

rows.hold_question: Does the ADDITION LICENCE authorise a row with ZERO measured delta whose benefit is telling you WHICH axis fired -- when removing it concentrates SFD1 coverage on a constant shared with two other rows, where a plausible edit silently reopens the axis and BASE does not notice?  codex ruled the attribution warrant does not transfer (the anchor rule repairs self-comparing oracles; row demand is per enumerated mutant, never per attribution need).  Rule for or against, and if for, say what the licence's wording should become.
rows.state_note:
*** A RULE QUESTION FOR THE 2026-09-09 ADJUDICATION, not a defect. ***  The carrier sends rule questions to the flagship seat at the next round boundary, because they change how future rounds run; this one was raised and ruled on by the pass-12 closing seat, and the ruling deserves the adjudicator rather than my acceptance.

**THE QUESTION: does the ADDITION LICENCE authorise a detector row whose only benefit is a DISTINGUISHING FAILURE SIGNATURE -- zero measured delta, but it tells you WHICH axis fired?**

**THE CASE.**  `#502` v19 added two rows to close the re-route trap side.  `trapfrozenuser` varies MODE and SFD1 together (PSR_FRZUSER = 0x03 clears both); `trapfrozensfd1` varies SFD1 alone.  Table 15 measured `trapfrozensfd1`'s delta against its own mutant as **ZERO** -- delete it and M_RRTRAPSFD1 is still caught, 58/58, by `trapfrozenuser`.

**MY WARRANT, AND THE RULING AGAINST IT.**  I claimed the anchor rule's principle one level down: a row varying two bits cannot say which one fired, so the single-axis row buys attribution.  codex (GPT-6 Astra, max) rejected it, citing the carrier: *the anchor rule repairs an oracle that compares a path with ITSELF*, which is not this situation -- the joint row already checks concrete vector and register expectations -- and *row demand is bounded 'per enumerated mutant, never per attribution need'*.  Its conclusion: **(iii) is wrong**, and (ii)'s claimed necessity for TWO rows is unsupported.  It was explicit that this does NOT extend the L2 chain and does not make the row vacuous; its verdict was CLOSE THE CHAIN.

**WHY THE ROW IS STILL IN THE TREE, and it is the same seat's own next paragraph.**  After removal, SFD1 coverage rests entirely on `trapfrozenuser`, whose `PSR_FRZUSER` is SHARED with `errpriv` and `errunimpl`.  Changing that constant from 0x03 to 0x0b would preserve THEIR intended routes while silently deleting the only SFD1-clear stimulus -- exception entry normalises both values to the same checked PSR and EPSR stays frozen, so **BASE alone would not notice**.  So the strict reading of the licence removes a row and creates a silent single point of failure on a shared constant.

**WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR IS ASKED.**  Either (a) the licence is right and the row goes, with the PSR_FRZUSER hazard handled some other way (a comment is memory, and this project's finding is that memory does not fire); or (b) a distinguishing failure signature IS a licensed benefit when the alternative concentrates an axis on a shared constant -- in which case the licence's wording should say so, since it currently does not.

**COST OF DEFERRING: none measured.**  The row is green, costs one session-free entry, and v21 is records-only (executable structure identical to the frozen v19 table 15 ran, verified with docstrings stripped), so table 15's scores still describe the shipped 59-row instrument and no re-table is owed either way.

**INDEPENDENT OF THE RULING:** any edit to `PSR_FRZUSER` owes a re-check of the pre-trap bit values and a repeat of both named mutant measurements.  That obligation stands whichever way this goes, and it is written into the probe beside the constant.

rows.title: alpha, i960 and riscv set cd.<arch>.irq_asserted with no consumer -- a real gap, but two are non-executing ports (scaffold cleanup) and the third is Alpha port completion
rows.witness: harness:source census, codex GPT-6 Astra at max, regress/artifacts/lcabadval/codex_irqasserted_20260906.txt
rows.state_note:
*** SEVERITY CORRECTED HIGH -> LOW THE SAME EVENING IT WAS FILED, BY THE PASS IT WAS FILED PENDING. ***  I filed this HIGH off ONE GREP while the investigation was in flight.  The census was right; the severity was not, and the correction is recorded rather than the row quietly re-graded.

**VERDICT (codex, GPT-6 Astra at max): REAL GAP in all three, and ALL THREE OF MY PREMISES HOLD.**  Six families set the flag, exactly three are consumed, and alpha/i960/riscv have no reader.  There is no alternate delivery mechanism for any of the three.

**BUT THE THREE ARE NOT ALIKE, AND THAT IS WHAT MOVES THE SEVERITY:**
* **i960 -- DEAD SCAFFOLDING.**  `cpu_i960_instr.c`'s instruction switch contains ONLY `default: goto bad;`. The FIRST instruction stops as unimplemented, so no boot, no timer programming, no driver wait is ever reached.  There is no guest to miss an interrupt.  `i960_exception()` is likewise a stopping stub.
* **riscv -- DEAD SCAFFOLDING.**  `cpu_riscv_instr.c` implements compressed NOP/ADDI only and the 32-bit branch goes unconditionally to `bad`.  `machine_test.c` DOES wire RTC -> interrupt controller -> CPU, so an asserted request really does end at the unused flag -- but this instruction subset cannot boot an OS or program that timer.
* **alpha -- A GENUINE HOLE, and the finding is that the PORT IS INCOMPLETE.**  `cpu_alpha_palcode.c` stores entry vectors and IPL (`PAL_OSF1_wrent`, `PAL_OSF1_swpipl`) and **`kentry` has no reader anywhere**; `PAL_OSF1_rti` appears only in the naming function with no execution implementation.  So delivery is missing at the CPU/PAL level, not merely at the flag.

**DISPOSITIONS:** removing the field and its stores is reasonable scaffold cleanup for i960 and riscv, and adding a dispatch check alone would achieve no usable capability in either.  For alpha the item is *track completion of the CPU/PAL/chipset path*, which subsumes `lcabadval`'s two interrupt stubs: **removing those exits still leaves both upstream forwarding and CPU delivery unfinished.**

*** AND IT CORRECTED MY CENSUS IN A WAY THAT DOES NOT CHANGE THE CONCLUSION BUT DOES CHANGE THE PICTURE: `cpu_dyntrans.c` ALSO delivers MIPS and SH interrupts, through DIFFERENTLY NAMED STATE. ***  My grep keyed on one identifier and so could not see them.  That is the correlate-not-the-class shape the carrier names -- the output was a plausible number either way -- and it is exactly the risk the brief disclosed about itself.

*** THE SHARPEST FINDING IS ABOUT MY BRIEF, NOT THE CODE: the seat named *"at least one numbered premise must be wrong"* AS THE UNSUPPORTED ASSUMPTION. ***  The three-question set closes with *WHICH IS WRONG?  Assume at least one is*, which is a good adversarial device and IS an unwarranted premise when the premises happen to be sound.  A seat that answers *none, and here is why the forcing assumption is unjustified* is giving the correct answer, and the template should say so rather than pressing for a defect that may not exist.  Filed against the template as `briefforcedwrong`.

Honest limit the seat stated and this row keeps: these are source-derived consequences, with no guest boot run, and "dead scaffolding" means the capability is absent rather than relocated.

entries.note: VERDICT: REAL GAP in alpha, i960 and riscv; all three premises correct as written.  Distinguished the three: i960 and riscv are DEAD SCAFFOLDING (neither can execute a second instruction -- i960's switch is only `default: goto bad;', riscv implements compressed NOP/ADDI and sends the 32-bit branch to `bad'), so there is no guest to miss an interrupt and the disposition is scaffold cleanup; alpha is a GENUINE HOLE at the CPU/PAL level (`kentry' stored with no reader, `PAL_OSF1_rti' named but unimplemented), so removing lcabadval's two interrupt exits still leaves forwarding AND delivery unfinished.  **Corrected my census**: cpu_dyntrans.c also delivers MIPS and SH interrupts through differently-named state, which a single-identifier grep could not see.  **And named my brief's forcing question as its own unsupported assumption** -- filed as briefforcedwrong. rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c horrible_getputpixel(): DE_MODE_LIN_B -- a DOCUMENTED NetBSD mode -- falls to the default arm, which assigns *color = random(); a copy then writes that random value to the destination
rows.witness: probe:regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py -- rung 3 on unmodified -E sgi -e ip32, 8 rows, liveness AND device-signature controls green; re-pinned oracle measured RED at 7/8 on the COMMITTED pre-fix build (regress/artifacts/sgirandompixel/witness_20260906/prefix_repinned_RED.out), 8/8 after.  Gate-wired into gate_arm.sh; 880 checks PASS.
rows.state_note:
*** RAISED THE SAME EVENING IT WAS FILED, ON A READING THAT MADE IT WORSE: THE UNHANDLED VALUE IS A DOCUMENTED
MODE, NOT A NONSENSE ONE. ***  Verified against the vendored header before this edit.

`horrible_getputpixel()` extracts `tlb_mode = (mode >> 10) & 0x7` and switches on it.  The function's own
comment lists five NetBSD modes, and `src/include/thirdparty/crmfbreg.h` confirms their values:

    DE_MODE_TLB_A  0x0000 -> 0  handled       DE_MODE_LIN_A  0x1000 -> 4  handled
    DE_MODE_TLB_B  0x0400 -> 1  handled       DE_MODE_LIN_B  0x1400 -> 5  *** default -> *color = random() ***
    DE_MODE_TLB_C  0x0800 -> 2  handled       (3, 6 and 7 also reach it)

**FOUR OF THE FIVE DOCUMENTED MODES ARE IMPLEMENTED AND THE FIFTH RETURNS RANDOM DATA.**  So this is not a
guest choosing an out-of-spec value; it is a guest choosing one of the five modes the vendored header defines.

**THE GUEST-VISIBLE PATH, in `draw_primitive()`, and both mode words are GUEST-WRITABLE registers**
(`CRIME_DE_MODE_SRC` / `CRIME_DE_MODE_DST` via `d->de_reg[]`):

    if (drawmode & DE_DRAWMODE_XFER_EN)
            horrible_getputpixel(0, ..., &color, src_mode);   // GET may set color = random()
    ...
    if (draw)
            horrible_getputpixel(1, ..., &color, dst_mode);   // PUT writes it

A failed SOURCE read and the DESTINATION write are the same `color` variable in the same loop iteration, so
the random value is written out per pixel with no decline.  **The code's own comment on that XFER branch reads
*"Pixel colors copied from another source.  (OpenBSD draws characters using this mechanism.)"*** -- so the
branch is one a real guest driver uses, which is why this is filed HIGH rather than as a curiosity.

**STILL OWED AND NOT CLAIMED: the rung-3 witness.**  Reachability is READ, not MEASURED -- I have shown the
constant exists, the extraction reaches 5, and the registers are writable, and NOT that any in-tree guest
programs LIN_B.  A witness-attempt brief is with codex asking exactly that, including the awkward part: the
oracle cannot pin a value because `random()` is non-deterministic, so it must pin *the destination differs
from the source* and *two identical runs differ*.

*** THE PROVENANCE IS THE LESSON: this came from asking what a DISABLED kill FELL BACK TO. ***  It is the
second such finding today -- `lcabadval`'s disabled kill leaves a live `dev = 0` that aliases 'no selected
device' to device zero.  Both look like a decision already taken and neither is one to copy.  Four exits in
this file are commented out; the other three still owe that question.

*** RUNG-3 ATTEMPT MADE, AND THE ANSWER IS WITNESS BUILDABLE (grok).  The probe is SPECIFIED, NOT RUN --
that seat is plan-mode, so this is a READING and the measurement is still owed. ***

**THE FALSE NEGATIVE THAT WOULD HAVE WASTED THE FIRST ATTEMPT:** at reset the destination mode is TLB_A and
`re_tlb_a[]` has bit 31 clear, so the PUT returns WITHOUT WRITING.  A naive probe -- set SRC to LIN_B, draw,
read the destination -- finds it unchanged and reports NO DEFECT.  Using LIN_A as the destination closes it,
since case 4 forces the valid bit.  `sgi_de_primop_probe.py` had already named that gap.

**AND THE ORACLE IS CERTAIN, NOT PROBABILISTIC:** glibc `random()` is 31-bit, so the destination's bit 31 is
clear and inequality with a source of `0xAABBCCDD` is guaranteed rather than 2^-32.  Two runs differ by
default seeding; `-D` makes them identical, which changes the second oracle and not the defect.

*** THE SEVERITY SPLIT GROK NAMED, AND IT IS THE HONEST LIMIT OF THIS ROW: `LIN_B` IS DOCUMENTED AND STORABLE
BUT NOT SHOWN TO BE DRIVER-SELECTED. ***  It appears only in `crmfbreg.h` and this function's comment; the
XFER comment names OpenBSD character drawing without saying which source mode; the PROM's `MTE_TLB_LIN_A/B`
zero-fill path does NOT call `horrible_getputpixel`; and `images.md` has no O2/sgimips image to boot.  **A
documented-but-unused mode and a mode a driver really selects are different severities**, and only the
constant's existence is established here.

*** THE WITNESS IS BUILT AND MEASURED.  7/7 on the committed build, artifacts/sgirandompixel/witness_20260906/head_79cd12e.out. ***

Real guest instructions on an unmodified committed `-E sgi -e ip32', no `device_add'.  Both mandated controls
green: LIVENESS (store then load through RAM) and DEVICE SIGNATURE (CRIME_DE_STATUS reads 0x1e000000 where
RAM reads 0).  The value written was 0x4b1763a1 on one run and 0x2ee4b4df on the next, **bit 31 CLEAR both
times** -- glibc random() is 31-bit, so inequality with a source of 0xaabbccdd is CERTAIN rather than 2^-32,
which is what makes the oracle deterministic despite the value not being.

*** TWO TRAPS HIT WHILE BUILDING IT, AND THE ACCEPT CONTROL IS WHAT CAUGHT THE FIRST. ***
* **The destination tile pointer was 0, so every pixel went to PHYSICAL ADDRESS 0.**  grok had named exactly
  this hazard -- *'do not leave it 0: that writes phys 0'* -- and I hit it anyway from a direction it had also
  named: a 64-bit `sd' writes the HIGH word to `[n]' and the low word to `[n+1]', so storing 0x10 gave
  `re_linear_a[0] = 0, [1] = 0x10'.  **A probe with only the defect rows would have read the destination
  unchanged and reported NO DEFECT.**  The ACCEPT control failed instead, which is what an accept row is for.
* `lw` SIGN-EXTENDS into a 64-bit register, so the source value read back as 0xffffffffaabbccdd and the row
  failed on FORMATTING rather than behaviour.  The shipped `sgi_re_width_probe.py` carries that normalisation
  and says why; this probe should have copied it and now does.

**THE ORACLE MUST INVERT AFTER THE FIX, and the order is not optional.**  These rows PASS while the defect is
PRESENT, so post-fix they assert the wrong thing.  The oracle-correction rule requires the re-pin FIRST, the

rows.state_note:
*** MY OWN DIAGNOSIS IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS BECAUSE IT CHANGES
THE REMEDY. ***  I wrote that the trigger is 'the SUBJECT SHAPE, not a phrase', on the evidence of two
refusals of one brief.  **codex then answered a brief on THE SAME DEFECT, in the same file, at 167 KB.**

The difference is the FRAMING, and it is sharper than either earlier guess:
  REFUSED  the WITNESS brief -- 'can you build a probe that REACHES this and shows the bad value?'
  ANSWERED the DESIGN brief -- 'what should this code do instead, and what should the rows assert?'
Same defect, same file, same session.  A request to CONSTRUCT A PATH TO A DEFECT reads as an attack recipe;
a request to DECIDE WHAT THE CODE SHOULD DO reads as ordinary review.  Neutralising the vocabulary did not
help because the vocabulary was never the trigger.

**SO THE REMEDY IS NOT ONLY RE-ROUTING: it is to ask codex the DESIGN question and let another seat answer
the REACHABILITY one.**  That is cheaper than it sounds -- grok answered the witness brief with a complete
buildable sketch, and codex then produced the best design answer of the panel.  Each seat was asked the
question it would answer.

*** THE SEAT-CHECK HAZARD IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE PART THAT WAS ACTUALLY FIXED. ***  The refusal writes a
zero-byte stdout with the reason on stderr on a direct call -- indistinguishable from an agy quota wall --
and through panel.sh it produced 150,372 bytes at 97% novel, which `seat_verdicts.py` scored as **answered,
NO VERDICT LINE**.  A seat failure counted as an answer, in the tool built to refuse exactly that.  Every
existing test passed it: no quota keyword (not a wall), high novelty because the seat streams reasoning
BEFORE the filter fires (not an echo), CLI seat (not a burn).  Now reported as **SEAT REFUSED**, counted with
the DOWN seats, keyed on the vendor's own sentence, and controlled in four directions: it fires on the
refusal, leaves a genuine quota wall as WALLED, leaves the mid-answer wall's READ-THE-BODY label intact, and
does not touch answering seats.

Both refusal transcripts and the answered design brief are preserved beside the round's artifacts, so the
before/after comparison is checkable rather than remembered.

*** THIRD INSTANCE, 2026-09-07 -- AND IT REFUTES THE DIAGNOSIS THIS ROW CURRENTLY CARRIES. ***

Preserved: `regress/artifacts/sgirekills/refusals/attempt3_scoping.err'.  Exact text, twice:

    ERROR: This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk. If this seems wrong, try
    rephrasing your request. To get authorized for security work, join the Trusted Access for
    Cyber program: https://chatgpt.com/cyber

**stdout was 0 bytes; the banner, the echoed prompt and both ERROR lines went to stderr** -- so a
check that measures the `.txt' alone sees an empty file and a check that measures SIZE sees 6829
bytes of healthy-looking stderr.  `seat_verdicts.py' already reports this as SEAT REFUSED / DOWN
(fixed earlier in this session); this instance confirms the detector on a fresh case.

*** WHAT IS REFUTED: this row concluded the trigger is the reach-the-defect FRAMING -- *design
briefs are answered, witness briefs are refused*.  THE REFUSED BRIEF HERE IS NEITHER. ***  It is a
read-only SCOPING task that explicitly says *"Do not design the fix diff.  Do not write rows"*.

**AND THE CONTROL IS STRONG, because it ran the same evening on the same model at the same effort:**
the `sgirebufuninit' pass-1 brief -- which discusses uninitialised host stack reaching guest-visible
memory, i.e. a MEMORY-DISCLOSURE defect -- was ANSWERED at 317 KB with a GO-WITH-CHANGES verdict and
two new findings.  So the trigger is not the subject matter, not the security-adjacent content, and
not the brief's purpose.

**THE REMAINING HYPOTHESIS, stated as a hypothesis because it is not yet tested: VOCABULARY DENSITY.**
The refused brief is saturated with this fork's historical term for the defect -- *kills*, *THE HOST
STILL DIES*, *terminating calls*, *host kill* -- while the answered brief describes an equivalent
severity in ordinary engineering words.  A re-fire is in flight with the identical technical content
rewritten in bounds-and-error-handling language (`RESEARCH_scoping_neutral_20260907.md'): same
questions, same code, same seven dispositions, no `kill'/`dies'/`host' vocabulary.

**That is a real experiment with a clean control and it settles the hypothesis either way** -- if the
neutral form answers, the trigger is vocabulary and the remedy is the benign-framing rule the carrier
already mandates for the Anthropic seats, applied to codex too; if it also refuses, vocabulary is out
and the next candidate is brief LENGTH or the enumerate-the-sites structure.

*Note the cost is real and recurring: codex is the seat this queue leans on hardest, and a refusal is
invisible to any size-based check.*

*** SOLVED, WITH A CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT.  THE TRIGGER IS THE REPOSITORY'S OWN ARCHIVES, NOT THE BRIEF'S
SUBJECT AND NOT ITS FRAMING.  Measured 2026-09-07 across four runs. ***

    attempt  brief vocabulary   reading scope        stderr     flag
    1        kills / HOST DIES  unrestricted           6,829 b  IMMEDIATE, before any work
    3        neutral            unrestricted         374,583 b  at byte 279,268 (~75% in)
    4        neutral            src/ + regress/*.py  279,132 b  *** NONE -- full verdict delivered ***
    (control) pass-2 panel      unrestricted         395,340 b  at the END of the answer

**TWO SEPARATE FILTERS, and each attempt isolates one:**
* **Attempt 1 -> 3 shows a PROMPT-level filter keyed on vocabulary.**  Rewriting *kills / the host dies /
  terminating calls* into ordinary bounds-and-error-handling language converted an instant refusal into a run
  that worked for minutes.  The technical content was IDENTICAL -- same twelve sites, same expectation design,
  same seven dispositions.
* **Attempt 3 -> 4 shows a CONTENT-level filter keyed on what the seat READS.**  Adding one paragraph -- *do
  not read `regress/artifacts/' or `tools/pipeline/ledger.json'* -- carried the run past the exact point where
  the unrestricted one died, to a clean finish.  **279,132 vs 279,268 bytes: the same distance, opposite
  outcome.**

**WHY THE ARCHIVES: they are this project's own record of a hardening campaign** -- kill tables, `host kill'
censuses, `exit(1)' enumerations, mutant names like `widthkillclass' -- accumulated over months.  Read in bulk
they look like exactly what the filter exists to catch.  *The irony is that the archive is the honest record
of DEFENSIVE work, and its own vocabulary is what makes the seat refuse to read it.*

> **THE OPERATIONAL RULE, and it costs two sentences in a brief: for any codex run, (a) write the brief in
> ordinary engineering language, and (b) SCOPE ITS READING to `src/` and `regress/*.py`.**  The pass-2 control
> shows why (b) matters even when (a) is satisfied: that brief was already neutral and was still flagged, at
> the end, after reading the ledger and CHANGELOG.

This matters more than one lost answer: codex is the seat this queue leans on hardest, a refusal writes 0
bytes to stdout while leaving healthy-looking stderr, and it is invisible to every size-based check.

*** SIXTH RUN, AND IT REFUTES THE REMEDY I SHIPPED TWO HOURS AGO -- SCOPING IS NECESSARY, NOT
SUFFICIENT.  Worse: it REHABILITATES the diagnosis I recorded as REFUTED, and my refutation was a
misreading of my own brief. ***

A `swpctx' design brief scoped ENTIRELY to `src/' was flagged at 145 KB -- the flag fired while it was
grepping `debugger_cmds.c', which is INSIDE the allowed scope.  All six runs, sorted by what they asked:

    WHAT IS TRUE                                    WHAT TO BUILD
    analysis of a defect        317 KB clean        smallest EDIT that RE-OPENS     375 KB FLAGGED
    count + classify            298 KB clean        smallest guest PROGRAM that
    is this path reached?       294 KB clean          WITNESSES each defect         145 KB FLAGGED
    CAN a guest run at all?     502 KB clean

**The discriminator is whether the brief asks the seat to BUILD SOMETHING THAT TRIGGERS A DEFECT.**  The
502 KB clean run asked at length about cold-debugger probes, breakpoints and planting instructions -- and
was fine, because it asked whether such a thing is POSSIBLE rather than for one aimed at a defect.

*** AND I HAD THIS RIGHT THE FIRST TIME. ***  This row's original diagnosis was *the reach-the-defect
FRAMING is the trigger*.  I recorded it REFUTED because a read-only SCOPING brief was also refused --
but that brief's Q3 asked *"what is the smallest change to the model that would restore the old
behaviour ... while still satisfying a test built that way?"*  **That is construction framing, and I did
not re-read my own brief before declaring the diagnosis dead.**  The premise-audit failure again, on my
own record rather than on the code.

**THE ARCHIVE FINDING IS NOT SUPERSEDED** -- it carried a run past the exact byte where an unscoped one
died, which is a measurement and stands.  There are TWO triggers; §C5 shipped implying one, and now says
so.

**OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, and it costs something real:** codex cannot be asked for mutants or witness
programs.  It can CHECK a construction supplied to it, and it can say whether one is possible -- both
measured clean.  **The construction itself goes to a measuring seat.**  That is a genuine capability
loss, not a wording problem, and it should be weighed on the 9th alongside [[codexbriefscoping]].

*** SEVENTH RUN, AND A THIRD REFINEMENT: A BRIEF THAT ASKS `IS THIS TRUE' CAN STILL BE REFUSED IF ITS
CONTENT IS AN EXPLOITATION CHAIN.  Immediate rejection at 8 KB. ***

The `sgilinearnegidx' verification brief obeyed both existing rules: neutral engineering language, reading
scoped to `src/' and `regress/*.py', and it asked only for each link of a chain to be CHECKED -- explicitly
*"I want it attacked rather than confirmed"*, with no construction requested anywhere.  **Refused on the
prompt**, before any work, exactly like the first `kills'-vocabulary attempt.

**What it contained that the six clean runs did not: a numbered seven-step guest-controlled chain ending in
a PHYSICAL write, plus questions about the reachable address range and about how far the guest can CONTROL
the value.**  The clean runs analysed defects, classified sites, traced reachability of a code path, and
asked whether a probe is possible.  None of them laid out *guest does A, then B, then C, and thereby writes
where it chooses*.

> **So the discriminator is not the QUESTION FORM but the SHAPE OF THE CONTENT.  `What is true about this
> code?' is clean; `here is a chain by which a guest reaches X -- how far does it go?' is not, however it is
> phrased.**

**OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, and it is the sharpest limit yet:** the seat cannot be used to review the very
findings that matter most in a hardening fork, once those findings have been assembled into a chain.  It can
check the LINKS SEPARATELY -- *is `src_x' masked in the linear path?* is a clean question -- but not the
chain as a chain.  **Split the chain into independent link questions, or verify it yourself.**  I verified
this one myself in three greps.

*Recorded with the other two triggers rather than replacing them: vocabulary (prompt-level), archive reading
(content-level, late), and now chain SHAPE (prompt-level).*

*** THIRD RECORDED INSTANCE, 2026-09-07, AND IT CARRIES THE CLEANEST DISCRIMINATOR YET, because
TWO briefs on the SAME SUBJECT MATTER passed on the SAME DAY and this one did not. ***

Artifact: `regress/artifacts/lcaconfbus1kill/codex_witness_20260907.err`.  The `.txt` is **ZERO
BYTES and the process exited 0** -- so an exit-status check scores it a success and a size check
scores it a dead seat; only the `.err` names it:

    ERROR: This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk. If this seems wrong, try
    rephrasing your request. To get authorized for security work, join the Trusted Access for
    Cyber program: ...

**THE CONTROLS ARE THE VALUABLE PART.  Same seat, same model, same effort, same day, same device
file, all three read-only:**

    PASSED   brief_lcabadval_fixcheck.md      "six value guards that END THE PROCESS" -- inlined
                                              fatal()+exit(1) verbatim, asked whether a proposed
                                              DELETION was sound.  6,976-byte answer.
    PASSED   brief_sgirandomcolour_scope.md   "writes FOUR random() bytes to guest memory",
                                              "uninitialised host stack reaches guest memory",
                                              asked for a reachability census.  7,946-byte answer.
    REFUSED  brief_lcaconfbus1_witness.md     asked whether a proposed TEST CONSTRUCTION would
                                              successfully REACH the termination, step by step.

**So it is not the vocabulary and not the subject.**  "Host kill", "exit(1)", "guest-drivable",
"uninitialised stack into guest memory" all pass.  What differs is the ASK: the first two ask *is
this analysis correct*; the third asks *will this sequence work*.  A numbered two-step recipe --
write this value here, then touch that window, and the process exits -- reads as exploit validation
however defensively it is framed, and mine was framed defensively (opened with "ordinary regression-
test adequacy review", no offensive-security wording anywhere).

> **THE OPERATIONAL RULE: ask codex to VERIFY AN ANALYSIS, not to VALIDATE A SEQUENCE THAT REACHES A
> TERMINATION.**  This is the carrier's existing C5 trigger -- *asking for a construction that
> reaches a defect* -- with a measured negative control on both sides for the first time.  Where a
> construction genuinely needs checking, ask about its CONTROLS in isolation ("does a matched
> surviving control at the same address attribute an outcome to the value?") without narrating the
> path to the kill.

**RECOVERY, and it is the sixth-class rule applied: the seat refused, the QUESTION did not become
unanswerable.**  grok reads the repo, takes its brief from a FILE (no argv cap), runs `--permission-
mode plan` read-only, and has no such filter.  It was fired on the byte-identical brief.  A refused
seat with a live alternate transport is ONE SEAT COVERED, not one lost -- but it is recorded as a
REFUSAL by name, never as agreement or as a wall.

*Cost note: 17,471 tokens spent before the flag fired, and 217 KB of tool-call reasoning in the
`.err` showing it had already listed the tree and begun reading.  The refusal is not instant, so a
zero-byte `.txt` after several minutes is NOT evidence of a hang.*

*** A DUPLICATE OF THIS ROW WAS FILED ON 2026-09-08 (`codexcontentfilter`) AND HAS BEEN WITHDRAWN.
It contributed ONE measurement worth folding in here. ***

**A DETERMINISM CONTROL: the same brief, byte-for-byte, REFUSED and then ANSWERED.**
`regress/artifacts/sgirekills/ROUNDDESIGN_brief.md`, md5 `21c440bc6746d1e6bb6d52f703f847bb`,
16,903 bytes -- firing 1 produced a 0-byte `.txt`, firing 2 produced 6,868 bytes and a full answer.
Nothing changed between them but time.

**That is consistent with THIS row's ARCHIVE-READING trigger and not with randomness:** the filter
fires partway through, at whatever point the run has read enough of the archive, so two firings of
one brief diverge on what they happen to read.  *The duplicate concluded "non-deterministic"; the
mechanism recorded here is the better explanation, and it makes the remedy a FIX (neutral language
plus scoped reading) rather than a retry.*

**A re-fire is still worth one attempt** -- it costs a minute and may take a different reading path
-- but it is a coin-flip with a mechanism, not the remedy.

*** A NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THIS ROW'S OWN REMEDY, MEASURED 2026-09-08: THE SCOPING FIX DID NOT WORK,
AND THE REASON IS THAT IT CANNOT WORK ON A ROUND OF THIS SHAPE. ***

This row's recorded remedy is **neutral engineering language AND reading scoped to src/ and
regress/*.py**, aimed at the ARCHIVE-READING trigger -- the filter fires once the run has read enough
of regress/artifacts/ or ledger.json.

The sgirekills re-pin brief was refused.  I applied the remedy exactly -- added a READING SCOPE
paragraph naming src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c and regress/*.py and excluding the archive -- and re-fired.
**It was refused again**: codex_repin_scoped_20260908.txt is ZERO BYTES, the .err carries two
Trusted-Access lines, 17,904 tokens used, exited 1.

> *** THE DIAGNOSIS: SCOPING THE READING TO src/ IS NOT A REMEDY WHEN src/ IS WHAT TRIPS THE
> FILTER. ***  The .err shows the run had reached dev_sgi_re.c -- and that file is a wall of bounds
> guards, refusal arms and exit(1) calls.  **To the filter, the product source of a hardening fork
> reads like the archive does.**  The remedy moves the reading from one flagged corpus to another.

**So the three recorded triggers need a fourth, and it is the one that BOUNDS the remedy:**

    SUBJECT SOURCE   content-level and UNAVOIDABLE -- a round whose subject file is itself
                     guard-and-refuse code cannot be scoped away from its own subject.

**WHAT THIS CHANGES OPERATIONALLY, and it is not nothing:** for a round on a device-hardening file,
codex must be given the FACTS INLINE -- treated as a PACKET-FED seat for that round -- rather than
pointed at the file.  That is the same move the carrier already prescribes for the Ollama transports,
and it is affordable here because a re-pin brief's facts are a few dozen lines of arm addresses and
array declarations.  **Untested as of this writing; recorded as the next thing to try, NOT as a
second remedy claimed to work.**

*Recorded because it is a controlled negative: same seat, same subject, remedy applied deliberately
and singly, refused.  The remedy's earlier success on the gdromcondavail brief stands -- what is
refuted is its GENERALITY, and this row had stated it with no scope condition.*

*** THE CHAIN-SHAPE TRIGGER CONFIRMED PROMPT-LEVEL, 2026-09-08, WITH A CLEAN DISCRIMINATOR THAT
SEPARATES IT FROM THE ARCHIVE-READING TRIGGER AT A GLANCE. ***

Four codex briefs went out tonight on neutral engineering subjects.  Three answered in full; the
fourth was refused.  **The refused one is the WITNESS-DESIGN brief**, and its `.err` settles where
the refusal happened:

    brief                      .err bytes   file-read lines   outcome
    armbfcdecode DECODE            70,308   many              ANSWERED (5,037 b)
    alphatbinegsel VERIFY          20,210   many              ANSWERED (6,820 b)
    alphatbinegsel Q3             167,085   many              ANSWERED (4,654 b)
    alphatbinegsel WITNESS          6,291   *** ZERO ***      REFUSED (0 b)

*** ZERO FILE-READ LINES MEANS IT REFUSED BEFORE OPENING ANYTHING.  The prompt's TEXT tripped it,
not what it read. ***  That is this row's third recorded trigger -- CHAIN SHAPE -- and it is now
confirmed as prompt-level rather than inferred.

**WHY THIS BRIEF AND NOT THE OTHER THREE.**  The three that answered ask *"is this analysis
correct"* about code that already exists.  The witness brief asks how to CONSTRUCT A GUEST SEQUENCE
THAT DEMONSTRATES THE DEFECT -- *"what the guest sets up, which PAL call it makes, and what it then
observes"*, plus *"remap a VPN to a different physical page ... then load from that VPN and see the
OLD contents."*  **A numbered guest-controlled sequence ending in an observation of stale memory is
the chain shape, however defensively framed** -- and this brief was written to be neutral, with no
`kill`/`host dies`/`exploit` vocabulary anywhere.  Neutral language was NOT sufficient.

> *** THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, and it is a real capability limit rather than a nuisance:
> **codex CANNOT DESIGN WITNESSES FOR THIS PROJECT.**  Witness design IS the reach-the-defect shape
> by definition -- the ladder requires a real guest instruction sequence that reaches the site.  So
> every rung-3 witness brief is expected to refuse, and routing one to codex is a wasted
> invocation. ***

**THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it costs one `grep -c`:**

    small .err + ZERO read lines + 0-byte .txt   -> PROMPT-LEVEL.  Rewrite the brief, or send it
                                                    to a different seat.  A retry will not help.
    large .err + many read lines + 0-byte .txt   -> LATE (archive/subject).  Scoping the reading
                                                    may help; a retry may take a different path.
    NO .txt and NO .err at all                   -> the run NEVER STARTED (a launcher/path fault,
                                                    NOT a refusal) -- measured separately tonight.

*Three distinguishable states, three different remedies.  Previously only the middle one was
characterised, and the row's determinism pair belongs to it.*

**ROUTED TO grok INSTEAD**, which is not subject to this filter and which has designed rung-3
witnesses for this project before (`lcabadval`'s row records a rung-3 seat specifying a full
sequence).  *The brief was reused BYTE-FOR-BYTE -- no rewrite -- which is what makes this a clean
seat-capability finding rather than a prompt-quality one.*

*** THE THREE-STATE DISCRIMINATOR NEEDS ONE CORRECTION, FOUND BY APPLYING IT TO A HEALTHY SEAT
TWENTY MINUTES AFTER WRITING IT.  2026-09-08. ***

As written above, the first state reads *"small `.err` + ZERO read lines + 0-byte `.txt` ->
PROMPT-LEVEL refusal."*  Applied to the `#513` pass-2 run mid-flight, that pattern MATCHED a seat
that was perfectly healthy:

    refusal lines      0
    file-read lines    0        <- matches the "prompt-level" shape
    .err bytes    39,485        <- but LARGE, not small
    processes          4 alive
    .txt bytes         0        <- normal mid-run: codex writes stdout at the END

**It had read nothing because the pass-2 brief INLINES the whole diff -- there was nothing it needed
to open.**  A seat can legitimately answer with zero file reads.

> **THE ACTUAL DISCRIMINATOR IS THE REFUSAL LINE.  Everything else says WHERE it refused, not
> WHETHER it did.**
>
>     refusal line present + ZERO reads   -> PROMPT-LEVEL.  Reroute; a retry will not help.
>     refusal line present + MANY reads   -> LATE (archive/subject).  Scoping may help.
>     refusal line ABSENT, .txt 0 bytes,
>       process alive                     -> MID-RUN.  Not a refusal at all.
>     NO .txt and NO .err whatsoever      -> the run NEVER STARTED (launcher/path fault).

*The read count was doing work it cannot do.  I wrote the three-state form from four observations
that happened to correlate -- every refusal I had seen with zero reads also had a small `.err` --
and the correlation broke on the first case outside that set.*  **That is this file's own
freshly-minted-exemplar rule landing on a discriminator I minted an hour earlier: the instruction
survived, its cheap proxy did not.**

*Corrected in `tools/pipeline/ADJUDICATION_20260909.md` as well, which had quoted the earlier form.*

*** A FOURTH TRIGGER, AND IT IS THE OPERATIONALLY EXPENSIVE ONE: THE ASK-AGAIN QUESTION ITSELF.
Measured 2026-09-08 on the #513 pass-3 panel. ***

codex ANSWERED the pass-2 diff review and REFUSED the pass-3 one.  Both are diff reviews of the
same round, same file, same neutral vocabulary.  **The refusal is LATE, not prompt-level** --
133,341 bytes of `.err`, 30,706 tokens used, many file reads, then the flag -- so it is the
archive/subject shape rather than the chain shape.

**WHAT PASS 3 ASKS THAT PASS 2 DID NOT:**

    Q2  "Is there a third cell? ... bits 6, 7, 9, 10 are swept by nothing."
    Q3  "Name the smallest edit that keeps a guard and makes these two rows GREEN while the
         latch behaviour is WRONG."

**That is an EVASION-CONSTRUCTION request.**  Pass 2 asked *is this change correct*; pass 3 asks
*construct an edit that defeats this detector while looking right*.  The second is much closer to
the reach-the-defect shape than to source review.

> *** THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT COSMETIC: THE ASK-AGAIN IS A MANDATED STEP IN THIS PROJECT'S
> PROCESS. ***  The vacuity floor requires exactly this question of every clean kill table -- *"the
> smallest edit that breaks this property and still passes"* -- and measured yield says it is where
> the real escapes come from.  **So codex is unavailable for the single highest-yield adversarial
> query in the round lifecycle**, on top of being unavailable for witness design.

**WHAT STILL WORKS:** codex answered EIGHT briefs tonight -- decode conformance, ABI review, source
analysis, callback tracing, error-handling review, and the pass-2 diff review.  The pattern across
nine firings is consistent: **codex reviews CODE THAT EXISTS; it will not construct an edit or a
sequence that defeats something.**

**MITIGATION, and it is already proven in this round:** grok and the packet-fed seats answer the
ask-again without difficulty -- pass 3's five answering seats ALL found the remaining latch cells,
and grok additionally prescribed the one-row class closure.  **Route the ask-again to grok and the
Ollama transports; do not spend a codex invocation on it.**

*Recorded from a controlled pair: same round, same file, same seat, two briefs one hour apart,
differing in exactly this question.*

*** THE ARCHIVE TRIGGER FIRED AGAIN 2026-09-08, AND I WALKED THE SEAT INTO IT WHILE WRITING THE
AVOIDANCE INSTRUCTION.  Ten refusal lines. ***

The brief said, in its own scope section:

> *"Read ... `regress/artifacts/sgirekills/killtable_20260908/*.txt` and the `*_20260908.out` logs
> there -- **these are the measurement records the packet cites; reading them is the point of this
> brief**.  Please still avoid `tools/pipeline/ledger.json`."*

**`regress/artifacts/` IS the archive corpus this row's second trigger keys on.**  I named the

> REQUIRES THE MEASUREMENT ARCHIVE.  The remedy "scope reading away from regress/artifacts/" and the
> task "verify these numbers against their logs" are in direct conflict. ***

**THE RESOLUTION, and it is the one the packet-fed seats have always needed: INLINE THE LOGS.**  The
seven logs this audit needs total a few KB.  Re-fired as `PACKETAUDIT2_brief.md` with every one

*Recorded as my error rather than a seat failure: the brief was refused for exactly what it

*** THE ENTRY DIRECTLY ABOVE IS WRONG AND I AM CORRECTING IT WITHIN THE HOUR.  THE ARCHIVE-READING

rows.title: dev_sgi_re.c: a DECLINED pixel GET still lets the caller perform its dependent PUT, so the destination is written with fg
rows.state_note:
FILED 2026-09-06 from the `sgirandompixel' design panel, where **codex argued for it as part of that round
and grok argued for filing it -- and grok's scoping was taken**, because a return value plus every GET site
is not ONE SITE and the reopening rule says a round takes one.

After `sgirandompixel', `horrible_getputpixel()' leaves `*color' alone on a declined GET, so the caller's
own `uint32_t color = fg' stands and the PUT writes the FOREGROUND.  That is DETERMINISTIC, which is the
whole gain of that round -- and it is still a write of data the guest did not ask for.

**codex's form, recorded verbatim because it is the design if this is taken:** give the function an explicit
SUCCESS RESULT; *'unchanged `*color' is merely an output-parameter guarantee: callers must not consume it
following failure'*.  Cover ALL the GET sites -- the source GET, the `oldcolor' GET used by ROPs, and MTE's
`bg' GET.  **AND ITS WARNING, which is the sketch rule and is the reason this is not a one-liner:**
*'preserve coordinate advancement and stipple rotation when suppressing a pixel's PUT; an early `continue'
can bypass those updates'* -- anchors `src_x += step_x' and `Rotate the stipple pattern'.

The shipped detector already discriminates this: `lin_b is fg' expects fg TODAY, and under a skip-PUT fix it
would expect the PRE-PAINT instead.  So the oracle-correction rule applies again and the row set is known in
advance.

*** A SHIPPED ROW ACTIVELY REQUIRES THE BEHAVIOUR THIS ROW WOULD REMOVE.  Found by the codex seat
on the `sgirandomcolour` pass-2 brief, 2026-09-07. ***

`regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py`'s **`lin_b is fg` expects FG rather than the destination's
prepaint** -- i.e. it asserts that the dependent PUT DID run after a declined GET.

> **So a general failed-GET/skip-PUT repair would make that existing row FAIL.**  An MTE-only repair
> would escape it; the general one collides with a shipped oracle.

**That is the oracle-correction rule's territory** -- the row's contract has to be adjudicated
explicitly before the code changes, and if it is re-pinned the re-pin must be measured RED on the
committed build first.  *Recorded here rather than acted on: the collision is the finding.*

Nobody else on that panel saw it -- not codex, not the packet-fed seats, not me -- and I had read the file

fill should leave is its own question and the detector shape is not simply copied.

*** MAIN-LOOP RECORD 2026-09-07 (assess stage) -- written into state_note, NOT into `entries'. ***
`entries' is the SEAT ANSWER list: check_stage_panels.py counts entries to decide whether a stage's
nine seats were fired, and gen_dashboard.py REFUSES TO RENDER on a seat id no column declares.  A
main-loop note parked there is not merely mis-filed -- it MANUFACTURES A SEAT ANSWER THAT NEVER
HAPPENED, which is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape inverted.  Seven such entries were
written during this session and all seven were migrated here when the generator refused.

SEVERITY RAISED MED -> HIGH, on a fact DERIVED rather than assumed.  The row said the fix
was *presumably* the same as [[sgirandompixel]]'s and that the observable differed.  **The reachability is now
established and it is the SAME documented-mode structure, not merely the same shape.**

Measured at HEAD, three commands:
  * the PUT colour switch implements exactly FOUR cases -- `DE_MODE_TYPE_' CI, RGB, RGBA, ABGR -- and its
    `default:' is `buf[0..3] = random()';
  * `crmfbreg.h' documents **FIVE** colour types; the fifth is `DE_MODE_TYPE_YCRCB  0x000000f0';
  * `grep -c YCRCB src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c' = **0**.  It is handled nowhere.

And it is reached by an ordinary register write: `color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK', mask `0xf0', so a
guest selecting YCRCB lands on the random arm directly.

*** SO THIS IS `#504's OWN SENTENCE AT A SECOND SITE: four of five DOCUMENTED modes work and the fifth
returns random data. ***  `#504` was graded HIGH on exactly that warrant, and this arm is arguably worse in
one respect -- `sgirandompixel' put a random value in `*color' for the CALLER to store, whereas this writes
four random bytes into the tile through `memory_rw(..., MEM_WRITE)' with no intermediary.

**WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the severity should be read with it: NO WITNESS.**  Nothing here shows a guest
driver selecting YCRCB -- only that the model accepts it and answers with random data.  The rung-3 attempt
looks cheap for the same reason `#504's did (`regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py' already programs this
code path; the colour type is a different field of the same mode word), and it is OWED before this ships.

**The GET side does NOT share the defect** -- its `default:' reads the raw 32-bit value rather than inventing
one, so this is a PUT-only arm.  That asymmetry is itself worth carrying into the design: the two default
arms of one function already disagree about what an unhandled colour type means.

Note this is a DIFFERENT defect from [[sgirebufuninit]] at the same lines: that one is about bytes NOBODY
assigns; this is about bytes assigned from `random()'.  A fix for either leaves the other standing.

*** READY TO RUN AS THE NEXT ROUND.  Three things established 2026-09-07 while `#505` worked in the
same function, none of which this row had. ***

**1. IT IS A DIFFERENT SWITCH FROM THE ONE `#504` FIXED, and the row should say so plainly** -- I nearly
recorded this as the `#499` symmetric-cell shape and it is not.  `#504` de-fanged the **addressing-mode**
default (`default: fatal("unimplemented dst_mode %i ..."); *color = random();`).  This row is the
**colour-mode** default of a different `switch` in the same function:

    default:buf[0] = random();  buf[1] = random();
            buf[2] = random();  buf[3] = random();
            // TODO.
            fatal("[ put: color mode = 0x%x ]\n", color_mode);
    }
    cpu->memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem, tileptr + ofs, buf, bufdepth, MEM_WRITE, NO_EXCEPTIONS|PHYSICAL);

**There is no `break` and no decline: control falls straight into the write**, so four bytes of host
`random()` land in guest memory at a guest-chosen tile offset.  Same family as `#504`, same function,
different arm -- *related by idiom, not by the one-cell-repair pattern.*

**2. FULLY GUEST-REACHABLE, established by reading rather than assumed.**  `color_mode = mode &
DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK`, and `mode` is the caller's `src_mode`/`dst_mode`, read straight out of `de_reg[]`
from `CRIME_DE_MODE_SRC`/`CRIME_DE_MODE_DST` with **no filtering anywhere on the path**.  The four
implemented types are 0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30; `DE_MODE_TYPE_YCRCB` is **0xf0 and is documented in
`crmfbreg.h`** but unimplemented, so a guest selecting a real, named mode reaches this arm.

**3. A WITNESS IS ONE CONSTANT AWAY.**  `#505` built `regress/sgi_re_rgb_probe.py`,
a rung-3 probe that drives an XFER copy on an unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32` with both ladder controls and a
sibling accept row, and whose `setup()` now takes **both** src and dst modes.  Pointing its `dst_mode` at
`LIN_A | BUFDEPTH_32 | 0xf0` puts YCRCB into the PUT switch and reaches this arm.

  *** THE ORACLE IS THE HARD PART AND IT NEEDS SAYING BEFORE THE ROUND STARTS: THE DEFECT'S OUTPUT IS
  RANDOM, SO NO VALUE ROW CAN PIN IT. ***  `#504` hit exactly this and its answer is the precedent --
  assert that the destination still holds its PRE-PAINT value, i.e. that the write was DECLINED, rather
  than trying to assert anything about what was written.  A determinism oracle is refuted in advance by
  this project's own record: two seats showed on `#504` that stack reuse can make a wrong value
  deterministic, so *"the same value twice"* proves nothing.

**FIX SHAPE: the option set has a member already chosen for its sibling.**  `#504` used DECLINE + LATCHED
ANNOUNCE with its own bit (`SGIRE_W_BADMODE = 1 << 10`), for the reason `#498` measured -- the four
handlers share one struct, so a shared latch is silenced by the other site's ordinary traffic.  **This arm
needs its OWN bit, `1 << 11`**, and `#504`'s comment already says the enum ends there on purpose so the
next maintainer finds it.  *That is a transferred in-tree warrant, not a "cannot hurt" addition.*

*** PASS-1 AUDIT, 2026-09-07 (codex, `regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/codex_pass1_20260907.txt`).  TWO OF MY PREMISES WERE WRONG AND THE
DISPOSITION SURVIVED. ***

**VERDICT:** *"DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE is justified, with an unconditional return from the PUT
default.  But the brief misstates #504's oracle and the write's byte count; depth 8 also exposes
uninitialized buffer bytes."*

*** CORRECTION 1 -- THE ORACLE.  THIS IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE COST A ROUND. ***  My brief said
`#504`'s precedent asserts *the destination still holds its PRE-PAINT value*.  It does not.  The seat
opened the probe: `lin_b is fg` expects **`FG_VAL = 0x77665544`**, not the pre-paint `0x11111111`,
because a declined source GET **preserves the caller's foreground value**, which the following PUT
then writes.  In the seat's words, *"the probe explicitly rejects preserving the destination as a
different disposition."*

  **So `#504` warrants the latch-and-return IDIOM and does NOT supply the unchanged-destination
  ORACLE I attributed to it.**  Those are different transfers and I ran them together.

  **THE ORACLE THE SEAT PROPOSES INSTEAD, and it is stronger than either:** observe **ZERO
  `MEM_WRITE` CALLS** from an unsupported PUT, *alongside* unchanged destination bytes -- because
  that pair **distinguishes "no write" from "same final value"**, which neither assertion does
  alone.  It also notes that if removing the RNG use is contractual, that must be observed
  SEPARATELY.

  *And a sentinel value will not rescue a value oracle here:* each assignment converts a SEPARATE
  `random()` result to `uint8_t`, so the whole-word improbability argument `#504`'s old witness used
  does not establish an impossible byte pattern.

*** CORRECTION 2 -- THE BYTE COUNT, and it is the SAME WIDTH-AXIS LESSON `#505` PAID FOR HOURS
EARLIER. ***  My brief said *four* bytes of `random()` are written.  The write is `bufdepth` bytes,
not four: at bufdepth 8 the arm fills `buf[0..3]` with RNG and ships **four further UNINITIALISED
stack bytes** with them; at bufdepth 1 or 2 fewer than four RNG bytes land.  **"Four" is true only
at bufdepth 4** -- the width every example happens to use.  *That is the exact shape of `#505`'s
clause-(d) floor breach, arriving in the next round's brief the same day, written by the person who
had just repaired it.*  Overlaps [[sgirebufuninit]]; the round must say which defect owns which
bytes.

**OPTION SET: CONFIRMED COMPLETE, and the grep found three in-tree alternatives worth naming:**
  * the helper's own GET default already provides a raw ABGR-shaped fallback (`dev_sgi_re.c:358`; lines of 7a41b3fb; at 987cb596 :433, the GET `default:`);
  * **PCC2 has a real ACCEPT precedent** (`dev_pcc2.c:427`) -- a read served from backing storage
    before the default diagnostic;
  * **SGI's ROP diagnostics latch BY VALUE** (`dev_sgi_re.c:850`; lines of 7a41b3fb; at 987cb596 :1026-1027, LINE's `static char rop_used[256]`, and :1092, RECT's) rather than one bit per site.

None establishes correct YCRCB PUT semantics.  *"Mirroring the GET fallback would repeat the
unsupported-authority problem you warned about.  The YCRCB name establishes an encoding; it does not
establish packing, conversion, or depth semantics."*  IMPLEMENT is defensible in principle but no
permitted source supplies an implementation or a demonstrated driver selection.  **No additional
warranted disposition outside the option set** -- which is the option-set rule returning a clean
negative for once, and that is worth recording as such.

**THE LATCH BIT IS CONFIRMED AVAILABLE AND THE OBJECTION TO ONE BIT IS RECORDED:** occupied bits
enumerate as 0..10, `warned` is `uint32_t`, so **`1 << 11` is free**.  The strongest objection is
diagnostic coverage -- *an earlier unnamed mode suppresses a later YCRCB announcement* -- and
per-mode latching has in-tree precedent (the ROP site above).  One bit stays consistent with this
helper's existing policy, so it is a judgement the round must make explicitly rather than inherit.

**FIX SHAPE (Q2), in the seat's words:** *a terminal default arm containing a conditional
announcement followed by an **unconditional function return***.  Note this is the SKETCH RULE's
territory -- the PUT branch's write sits after the switch and is shared by all five arms, so the
return must be checked against the whole enclosing function before it is written.

*** AND A WARNING THAT SAVES THE ROUND A FALSE START: `#504`'s PROBE CANNOT BE REUSED UNCHANGED. ***
*"#504's `lin_b is fg` remains green under edits confined to this colour default.  Both of that
probe's mode constants use RGBA, so it never selects the PUT colour default.  Its setup cannot be
transferred unchanged."*  `#505`'s probe is the better base -- its `setup()` already takes both src
and dst modes -- but the same check applies to it and must be run, not assumed.

**ENUMERATION CONFIRMED, with a qualification I did not have:** the twelve default selections are
eleven unnamed (`0x40`..`0xe0`) plus the named `0xf0` YCRCB, and they reach the arm *"when the
preceding coordinate/addressing/tile-validity checks pass"*.

*** THE ORACLE QUESTION, ANSWERED BEFORE THE ROUND STARTED -- AND THE NAIVE IMPLEMENTATION WOULD
HAVE PRODUCED A FALSE GREEN.  codex, `regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/codex_oracle_20260907.txt`.
***

**VERDICT:** *"Your distinction is conditionally sound.  A correctly scoped write-attempt observer
works for Round A; **the existing stepped probe supplies none.**  This fork's debugger watchpoints
offer a qualified alternative."*

**MY DISTINCTION SURVIVES, with a precision I had not stated.**  A count separates *no request* from
*a request carrying the existing bytes* -- but *"zero calls does not establish correct rejection
unless the unsupported arm was ACTUALLY REACHED: an earlier return or an operation that never ran
also produces zero."*  That is the attribution problem, and it means the round owes a reach control
beside the count.

*** THE MECHANISM EXISTS: debugger WRITE WATCHPOINTS, checked in the common memory path BEFORE
device/cache/RAM dispatch, and neither PHYSICAL nor NO_EXCEPTIONS excludes this helper's write.  A
pty driver can observe them with NO instrumented build. ***  (`memory_rw.c:273`; at 987cb596 the #250 comment is :272-282 and the test :283-284, `!single_step` on :284.)

*** AND IT HAS TWO DECISIVE LIMITS, THE FIRST OF WHICH WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A FALSE GREEN: ***
  1. **The check requires `!single_step`, and the existing probe's `run_ops()` uses `step`.**  So
     *"merely adding watchpoints and counting their messages to that execution scheme could report
     ZERO DESPITE WRITES."*  The row would have reported "no write happened" while writes happened.
     **A watchpoint oracle therefore requires the FREE-RUNNING probe shape, not the stepped one.**
  2. It also requires `!about_to_enter_single_step` and **SETS that flag after its first report**, so
     later pixel writes inside the same drawing command go unreported.  What Python would count is
     *printed watchpoint reports*, not `MEM_WRITE` calls -- watchpoints carry no hit count.

**SO THE ACHIEVABLE CLAIM IS BOUNDED, and the round must say so rather than overclaim:** the
mechanism supports an **any-attempt-to-this-range** witness when observation is active throughout the
relevant execution.  It does NOT support *"exactly N calls"* or *"no writes anywhere from this
helper"*.  The conclusion must read **"no observed write attempt to this range under these validated
conditions"** -- watching the destination cannot exclude a write to an UNINTENDED address, which is
exactly the failure mode [[sgirebufuninit]] and the `#505` tiled row both hit in other forms.

**THE SHIPPABLE DESIGN, in the seat's own construction:** verified arm reach and completed execution,
an active observer that DOES detect a supported write to the same range (the liveness half), then no
matching write report for the rejected operation, with unchanged verified destination bytes as
corroboration and the announce count testing "announce once" separately.  **That is four rows, not
one**, and knowing it now is worth more than discovering it after the fix.

*This is the carrier's `!single_step` family arriving through a NEW mechanism.  The carrier records
that a stepped probe cannot observe INTERRUPT DELIVERY (`cpu_dyntrans.c`'s
"do not cause interrupts while single-stepping").  The WATCHPOINT case is the same guard on a
different feature and was not written down.*

*** CODEX DESIGN PASS 2026-09-07 (`regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/codex_design_20260907.txt`).
VERDICT: REVISE -- DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE **with a `return` before the PUT transfer**.  It
refuted TWO of the brief's premises, and one of them was the brief's central design claim. ***

**S3 WAS WRONG, AND IT IS THE PREMISE THE WHOLE 'COPY THE SIBLING' READING RESTED ON.**  I wrote that
`sgirandompixel` fixed *the GET side of this same helper*.  It did not: **it repaired the
ADDRESSING-MODE default at `:235` (lines of 7a41b3fb; at 987cb596 dev_sgi_re.c:289), which sits BEFORE GET and PUT diverge and returns for both
directions.  The COLOUR GET default at `:358` (lines of 7a41b3fb; at 987cb596 dev_sgi_re.c:433) still performs a raw conversion.**  Two different
arms -- so the sibling is a precedent for the DISPOSITION and not for the site, and its comment
cannot simply be copied.

**S5 WAS WRONG, AND THIS ONE UNBLOCKS THE ROUND.**  I claimed the decline's 'what does `buf` hold'
question was the SAME question as [[sgirebufuninit]]'s, making that row a prerequisite.  codex:
*"A declined PUT need not leave anything defined in `buf`, provided nothing consumes it.  The helper
itself owns the memory write.  Its callers receive no buffer to transfer afterward."*

    remove the fill, fall through   -> transfers indeterminate stack bytes   REJECT
    zero the span, fall through     -> overwrites destination with zero      needs a warrant
    RETURN from the PUT default     -> preserves destination bytes           PREFERRED

> **So the two rows are INDEPENDENT and there is no patch ordering.**  This round decides whether an
> unsupported PUT writes anything at all; `sgirebufuninit` decides how paths that DO transfer avoid
> consuming uninitialised bytes.  *Initialising the buffer would neither remove the four `random()`
> calls nor justify writing zeros for an unsupported format.*

**S1 needs a width qualification:** four bytes are ASSIGNED randomly, but the transfer length is 1, 2,
4 or 8.  A narrow transfer exposes only the prefix; an eight-byte transfer additionally consumes four
uninitialised bytes.

**S2's inference was a CORRELATE and the real population is twelve, not one.**  `grep -c YCRCB` = 0
proves only that one NAMED constant is absent.  Enumerating `mode & 0xf0`: sixteen values, **four
explicit PUT cases (CI/RGB/RGBA/ABGR) and TWELVE reaching `default:`** -- eleven unnamed plus YCRCB.
The DE register handler stores the mode without filtering the type nibble, and both line and rectangle
callers pass it through unchanged.  *The named-constant search was the same error that cost the
`asicbadaddr` census a 4x undercount.*

invocation**, so a declined GET retains the latest value from THAT invocation or the register's
initial value -- never a previous command's local `bg`.  And "the whole rectangle deterministically
receives the last good colour" is too strong independently, because CI's accepted PUT initialises

counting or a command summary.

> interrupts while single-stepping"*).  **Watchpoints are a second capability gated the same way**,

**any-attempt-to-this-range** witness *"when observation is active throughout the relevant
execution"* -- i.e. FREE-RUNNING, not stepped -- and even then only the first report survives the
flag.  It *"cannot automatically support 'exactly N calls', or 'no writes anywhere from this
helper'.  A literal, attributed call count needs a suitable host-side observer or `harness:`
witness."*
