rows.title: THE UNOWNED REMAINDER: 76 guest-reachable error-exit sites across 24 files own no tracker row -- a TRACKING row so the body of work has a denominator and a pointer, not a re-derivation
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10.  Evidence: regress/artifacts/queuetriage/codex_exitaudit_20260910.txt (GPT-6 Astra at max), which enumerated the population properly for the first time.  **This row exists so the next session reads the census instead of re-running it**, which has now happened twice.

*** THE EARLIER FIGURES WERE RIGHT AND THEIR DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG: 370 and 240 count `exit(1)', NOT every `exit()'. ***  Re-derived by removing comments and string literals while preserving line positions, then locating the calls, with an independent character-state lexer returning exactly the same positions:

    src/devices    263 literal `exit('   135 calls after lexical filtering
    src/cpus       112                    74
    src/machines    35                    34
    TOTAL          410                   243   (240 of them exit(1))

LOCATION SPLIT of those 243: 150 runtime handlers and helpers, 80 init/configuration, 13 CPU generators and a standalone experiment.  The debugger is outside that scope and adds three more.

AND BEING INSIDE A RUNTIME FUNCTION IS NOT REACHABILITY.  The 150 split: **98 input-reachable through enabled in-tree wiring**; 33 dead, precluded, or not established reachable; 10 optional instrumentation; 6 unattached or disabled attachments; 2 intentional halt/reboot; 1 host RAM-config check misplaced in an access handler.

OWNERSHIP is an OVERLAY, not a disjoint population -- 22 live exits and 3 others are actively owned (n6 holds eight footbridge sites; alphavmkill one; sgirekills five; lcaisalane and lcabadval eight between them; m88kexit two dead ones) [2026-11-02, records: this list sums to 24, not the 25 stated; it omits the one dead exit sgirekills (with sgimtewidth) also covers -- the evidence audit's ownership table, regress/artifacts/queuetriage/codex_exitaudit_20260910.txt:50, and its totals row :62, 22 live + 3 other = 25].  **A strict open/held filter leaves 83, of which seven belong to in-work LCA repairs, so THE UNOWNED REMAINDER IS 76.**

*** AND ONE OF MY OWN EARLIER QUALIFICATIONS WAS TOO AGGRESSIVE, corrected here: lacking a separate CHILD repair id does not mean lacking an open OWNING row.  `sgirekills' explicitly retains its five command exits.  Conversely an incidental mention in census prose is NOT a repair row. ***

SIX E1 PREDICATES were identified -- a one-to-five-line change with an existing test carrier -- and ALL SIX ARE NOW FILED as their own rows: [[mk48nvramkill]], [[mapledmaaddr]], [[xscaleinten]], [[crimewidthkill]], [[vmedefaultkill]], [[fbctrlportkill]].  **This row therefore tracks the ~70 that remain, and they are E2/E3: real rounds, not quick wins.**  The heaviest concentrations are dev_osiop.c (14), cpu_arm_coproc.c (8 of which one is filed), dev_adb.c (7), dev_dreamcast_g2.c (6), dev_pvr.c and dev_igsfb.c (5 each).

THE ONE CONSTRAINT THAT GOVERNS EVERY DISPOSITION IN THIS BODY, and it is easy to forget: **memory_rw.c turns a failed device callback into an architectural access exception for MIPS and M88K ONLY.**  Returning zero from an ARM or SH device callback gives NO bus-error delivery, so the FAULT member is unavailable there and a round reaching for it owes the exception path first.  CPU translation and instruction handlers have their own direct mechanisms, which is a separate question.

*** THE LARGEST CONCENTRATION HAS BEEN TRIAGED, 2026-09-10: dev_osiop.c (osiopexits/codex_triage_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max; 3 cyber flags, ALL MID-STREAM and non-fatal). ***

**THE FILE HAS SIXTEEN EXPLICIT exit() CALLS, NOT FOURTEEN.**  The census's fourteen are all still executable, and two more exist that it did not list -- **and those two are the ones that turn out to be DEAD**, so the census happened to enumerate exactly the live set without saying why.

    (i)   guest register access or guest-started SCRIPTS      **14**  -- one register default,
                                                                        thirteen sequencer exits
    (ii)  unconstructible state or impossible branch          **2**
    (iii) internal failures where stopping is right           **0**

*** POPULATION (iii) BEING EMPTY IS ITSELF THE FINDING, and it is the one that licenses the whole body of work.  NONE of the sixteen checks establishes corrupted host ownership or any other condition that requires terminating.  The seat says the diagnostic wording -- notably 'cannot be combined' -- does NOT turn these into internal assertions, which is the argument a round would otherwise have to make sixteen times. ***

THE TWO DEAD PATHS, RECORDED WITH THEIR WARRANTS so nobody re-finds them:
  * the reserved-phase MOVE default -- an earlier equality check forces the instruction phase to match SOCL; initialisation and every implemented transition produce only handled phases; SET/CLEAR do not touch the phase bits; and a direct SOCL write terminates at the REGISTER DEFAULT before another SCRIPTS execution can run.  *That last clause is why this one is dead only while the register default is still fatal -- fixing the register default could REVIVE it, which a round must not miss.*
  * the outer instruction-class default is **mathematically unreachable**: the switch evaluates `dcmd & 0xc0' and explicitly handles all four possible results.

**AND IT CORRECTED THE AUDIT'S EFFORT RANKING:** the blanket E3 (`preserve command termination, status and interrupt behaviour') OVERSTATES the obligation for the register default and the redundant table-MOVE equality check, because the real status and completion sequence lives in the STATUS and MSG_IN phases, and the backend-failure branches are ALREADY de-fatalised by earlier rounds and sit outside this census.  So two of the nine prescribed rows are cheaper than the audit implied.

*** THE SEVERITY CEILING, ASKED FOR AND ANSWERED PLAINLY: 'no in-tree runnable workload drives this controller's register/SCRIPTS interface.' ***  All fourteen are guest-reachable in principle and NOTHING IN THIS TREE EXERCISES THEM.  That is worth more than a ranking: it means these rounds cannot reach rung 4, and a witness must plant SCRIPTS by hand.

A TRAP NAMED FOR THE FIRST ROW, and it is the kind that makes a one-line repair wrong: the generic byte path STORES BEFORE DISPATCH, and the word path also stores to DNAD and ADDER before reaching the unhandled-register default -- so restoring only `oldreg' would NOT undo those word stores.  And a blanket backed-accept would enable SOCL writes, **which changes the reserved-phase reachability finding above**.  The two interact.

rows.title: cpu_ppc_instr.c X(rldicl) ALWAYS WRITES ZERO: the mask is accumulated into `tmp' while the destination is assigned `tmp & tmp2' and tmp2 is never anything but 0 -- one of the most common 64-bit PowerPC instructions returns 0 for every input
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10.  Found by the GPT-6 Astra seat under the found-something-else licence while answering a tree-wide SHIFT-UB census -- it says so itself: *'one definite additional finding deserves its own correctness row ... This is CRITICAL and EASY, independently of the shift-UB census.'*  **VERIFIED LOCALLY by opening the handler before filing.**

*** THE DEFECT, and it is four lines you can hold in your head. ***
    uint64_t tmp = cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[rs], tmp2;
    while (sh-- != 0) { ... rotate tmp left by one ... }
    tmp2 = 0;
    while (mb <= 63) {
            tmp |= ((uint64_t)1 << (63-mb));      <-- the MASK goes into tmp
            mb ++;
    }
    cpu->cd.ppc.gpr[ra] = tmp & tmp2;             <-- tmp2 is STILL 0
`tmp2' is assigned 0 and never assigned again, so **the destination register is set to zero on every execution, for every operand, every rotate amount and every mask begin.**  The `|=' also corrupts the rotated value it lands in, but that is moot: the result is ANDed with zero either way.

*** THE SIBLING TWO FUNCTIONS DOWN SHOWS THE INTENDED SHAPE, which is what makes the diagnosis certain rather than inferred. ***  X(rldicr) does the same rotate and then CLEARS bits in `tmp' (`tmp &= ~((uint64_t)1 << (63-me))'), assigning `tmp' directly.  X(rldicl) was written the other way round -- BUILD a mask, then AND -- and the mask was accumulated into the wrong variable.  The fix is one character: `tmp |=' becomes `tmp2 |='.

*** WHY THIS IS THE MOST SERIOUS THING IN TODAY'S BATCH. ***  `rldicl' is not an obscure corner: it is THE canonical 64-bit PowerPC masking and zero-extension instruction, emitted constantly by compilers (`rldicl rA,rS,0,32' is the standard 32-bit zero-extend).  Every other defect filed today needs a guest to touch a particular register or width; this one is wrong on the ordinary path, for ordinary code, on every execution.

REACHABILITY IS WIRED AND CHECKED: `case PPC_30_RLDICL: ic->f = instr(rldicl); break;' in the primary decoder, reached whenever `cpu->cd.ppc.bits == 64' -- the 32-bit path deliberately goes to `bad' instead.  So it is live on every 64-bit PowerPC CPU model this tree offers, and dead on the 32-bit ones.

*** AND IT IS NOT A SHIFT DEFECT, which matters for how the round is scoped: the census explicitly records the computed count here as SAFE (mask counts 0..63, rotate counts 1..31, form NONE). *** This is a plain variable mix-up that the census found while looking at something else.  It does NOT belong to [[shiftubcensus]] or [[mipsextshift]]; it is its own correctness round.

NOT MEASURED and no witness built.  The rung-3 attempt is owed FIRST and looks unusually cheap: any 64-bit PowerPC machine, one `rldicl' with a nonzero source, and a register readback -- the wanted value is anything but zero, and the pre-fix build must show zero.  A guest-visible wrong RESULT is a far easier oracle than the process-death oracles most of this queue needs.  **Check first whether the existing PPC gates already execute one and pass anyway**, because a green gate over an always-zero instruction would itself be a finding about the gates.

*** WITNESSED AT RUNG 3, 2026-09-10, AND MY FILING UNDERSTATED IT IN THREE WAYS. ***

(a) **TWO TOKENS ARE WRONG, NOT ONE, AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR WAS BUILT AND MEASURED STILL WRONG.**  The mask is ORed into `tmp', the ROTATED VALUE, so even setting the AND aside the data is destroyed by having every mask bit forced to 1.  `tmp2' never being written is a CONSEQUENCE of the same slip rather than an independent bug.  The seat built both candidates: the one-character `tmp |=' -> `tmp2 |=' measures CORRECT at 0 of 190 wrong, while DELETING the `& tmp2' -- the edit a future reader is most likely to reach for -- ships an OR where the architecture says AND and gets 126 of 190 cells wrong.  **It is worse than the present bug in one specific way: it removes the always-zero signature that makes the defect easy to spot while leaving the value wrong.**  Recorded so the next round does not take it.

(b) **A SECOND OBSERVABLE CHANNEL: IT CORRUPTS CONTROL FLOW, NOT ONLY DATA.**  update_cr0 is fed the destination, which is always zero, so the record form reports EQ on EVERY execution regardless of operands -- measured 0x20000000 committed against 0x40000000 fixed.  Any branch on a masked compare takes the wrong arm.  A detector owes a row on this channel.

(c) **IT IS REACHABLE ON A REAL MACHINE MODEL, not only a synthetic one.**  All three in-tree machines that select a 64-bit CPU return zero: bareppc, testppc, and macppc -e g5 -- the Power Mac G5, whose constructor gives it the PPC970.

THE ORACLE CAME FROM THE MANUAL, NOT FROM THIS TREE: the rldiclx RTL in ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt plus its prose, with field placement taken from the manual's own format diagram and then independently confirmed by inverting the handler's extraction expressions.  Deriving the wants from the sibling would have been weaker and from the handler itself circular.  196 of 196 encoded words round-tripped through THE TREE'S OWN DISASSEMBLER, a different code path from the execute handler -- the defence against this project's hand-assembled-encoding trap, and it matters here because a wrong register field yields zero and zero is the symptom under test.

THE CENSUS IS NON-VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION, which is what makes 190 of 190 a real number: the source is all-ones, so the rotate is the identity and the architectural answer is exactly the mask, which is non-empty for every mask-begin in 0..63.  **And the seat measured a genuinely VACUOUS cell to show the boundary**: with a source whose selected window is all zeros the correct answer is itself zero and the row is GREEN on the broken build.  The rule for a detector author is to choose a source where every mask window is non-empty.

*** THE GATE FINDING IS STRUCTURAL AND STRONGER THAN 'NO GATE COVERS IT'. ***  Both PowerPC gates drive macppc -e g4, an MPC7400, which the CPU table marks 32-BIT -- and the decoder sends every rld* to the bad path in 32-bit mode.  **So no gate has ever instantiated a 64-bit PowerPC CPU at all, and the whole 64-bit-only instruction group is invisible to the gates BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by omission.**  That is better than a green gate passing over a broken instruction, which is what I had asked to be checked.  It is one coverage hole with one cause, and a single 64-bit probe closes all of it.

SEVERITY CEILING, stated honestly rather than glossed: the only PowerPC kernel image in the tree is loaded onto a G4 and never executed, so nothing in-tree BOOTS a 64-bit PowerPC guest.  The defect is catastrophic for any such guest and there is not currently one, which is why the witness is rung 3 and why it cannot be rung 4.

*** THE GATE CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE.  I WROTE IT INTO THREE ROWS, A CHANGELOG BLOCK AND TWO COMMIT MESSAGES BEFORE A SEAT CHECKED IT (wiringcliff/codex_ppcgate_20260910.txt). ***

**I CLAIMED: 'no gate in this tree instantiates a 64-bit PowerPC CPU at all, so the whole 64-bit-only instruction group is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION.'  THE FIRST HALF IS FALSE.**  Gate 9 (gate_asan_sweep.sh) enumerates EVERY advertised machine type and subtype -- including bareppc, testppc and macppc/g5, all of which default to the PPC970 -- so 64-bit PowerPC CPUs ARE constructed by a gate today, and have been all along.

**THE CORRECT AND NARROWER FINDING: NO GATE CHECKS THEIR INSTRUCTION RESULTS.**  Gate 9 is a CONSTRUCTION check with no PowerPC result oracle; the two PowerPC gates both drive `macppc -e g4', an MPC7400, which is 32-bit, and their probes select it EXPLICITLY rather than by default.  So the defects were invisible because nothing EXECUTES these instructions and inspects the answer -- not because nothing builds the CPU.

*** THAT DISTINCTION IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN WITNESS LADDER, ONE LEVEL UP, AND I WALKED PAST IT. ***  The ladder's whole rung-2 clause says machine CONSTRUCTION proves presence and NOT reachability, and is a reproduction only for defects that construction itself executes.  I applied that rule carefully to witnesses all day and then made exactly the error it warns about when reasoning about GATES.  A gate that constructs a CPU is a rung-2 gate; these defects need a rung-3 one.

THE PRESCRIBED CLOSURE IS SMALLER THAN MY FRAMING SUGGESTED: wire the existing 19-row regress/ppc_rldicl_probe.py into gate_ppc.sh, asserting its score AND its completion sentinel.  That closes the missing instruction-result check.  **It does NOT close all 64-bit PowerPC coverage**, and the seat says so explicitly rather than letting the round claim it does.

FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrldiclzero]] witness's sibling audit.  MEASURED, not read.

The handler rotates with a `while (sh-- != 0)' loop, which ALWAYS exits with sh == -1 because the post-decrement runs once more than the body.  The mask loop then terminates on a condition involving 63 - sh, i.e. 64 -- always.  The architecture requires the mask to END AT 63-SH (the rldimix RTL and its prose, '1 bits from bit MB through bit 63 - SH').

MEASURED with the destination seeded to 0 and an all-ones source:
    SH=8    got 0xffffffffffffffff   want 0xffffffffffffff00
    SH=32   got 0xffffffffffffffff   want 0xffffffff00000000
    SH=0    got 0xffffffffffffffff   want 0xffffffffffffffff   -- the one safe case

**This is the standard bitfield INSERT.**  A compiler using it to splice a field destroys everything to the right of that field.  Live for every SH != 0.

*** THE DURABLE REPAIR IS NOT TO PATCH THE 63 - sh EXPRESSION. ***  That loop idiom is shared by rldicl, rldicr AND rldimi; rldicr survives only because it never reads sh again.  **Any future edit that reaches for sh after the rotate loop in any of the three will be wrong the same way.**  Save sh before the loop instead.

Same reachability and the same gate blind spot as [[ppcrldiclzero]]: 64-bit CPUs only, and no gate instantiates one.

*** DESIGN REVIEW 2026-09-10 (ppcrldimimask/codex_design_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, 14,947 bytes, ZERO cyber flags): THE DEFECT PREMISE IS EXACT AND **MY PROPOSED REPAIR IS INSUFFICIENT**. ***

The post-decrement reading is confirmed exactly: the loop's final test evaluates the old value zero and then decrements to -1, **and this happens even for SH=0**, so the mask always covers architectural bits MB..63.  The rldimix RTL requires MASK(MB, 63-SH).

**BUT 'SAVE sh BEFORE THE LOOP AND KEEP THE MASK LOOP' -- which I filed as the durable repair -- LEAVES TWO MORE DEFECTS.**  Both come from the manual's own mask definition, which makes BOTH endpoints inclusive and WRAPS through bit 63 to bit 0 when the beginning exceeds the end:
  (1) the existing loop compares the INCREMENTED position against the inclusive endpoint, so where it terminates normally it **stops one bit early**;
  (2) it **never wraps**, so other operand combinations run past bit 63 and evaluate invalid shift counts -- an undefined-behaviour defect hiding inside the wrong-value one.

THE PRESCRIBED REPAIR is therefore four coordinated changes rather than one: preserve the decoded `sh', rotate with a separate counter (`int n = sh; while (n-- != 0)'), advance the mask position modulo 64 (`m = (m + 1) & 63'), and terminate on the position AFTER the endpoint, modulo 64 (`m != ((64 - sh) & 63)').

*A round that had taken my one-line framing would have shipped a fix that is still wrong at the endpoint and still undefined on the wrapping cases, and its detector -- built from the same framing -- would very likely have passed it.*

**I CLAIMED: 'no gate in this tree instantiates a 64-bit PowerPC CPU at all, so the whole 64-bit-only instruction group is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION.'  THE FIRST HALF IS FALSE.**  Gate 9 (gate_asan_sweep.sh) enumerates EVERY advertised machine type and subtype -- including bareppc, testppc and macppc/g5, all of which default to the PPC970 -- so 64-bit PowerPC CPUs ARE constructed by a gate today, and have been all along.

So the defects were invisible because nothing EXECUTES these instructions and inspects the answer -- not because nothing builds the CPU.

I applied that rule carefully to witnesses all day and then made exactly the error it warns about when reasoning about GATES.  A gate that constructs a CPU is a rung-2 gate; these defects need a rung-3 one.

That closes the missing instruction-result check.  **It does NOT close all 64-bit PowerPC coverage**, and the seat says so explicitly rather than letting the round claim it does.

*** DESIGNED 2026-09-10 (ppcrldimimask/codex_repair_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, ZERO cyber flags).  MY PREMISES HELD AND MY CHARACTERISATION OF THE DEFECT WAS HALF OF IT. ***

CONFIRMED: `sh' is `-1' on exit for EVERY decoded SH including zero (the final test reads the old value, decrements, and exits), the rotate body IS a correct ROTL64, and the mask loop therefore always stops at `m == 64' and selects bits `MB..63'.  The architectural mask is `MASK(MB, 63-SH)', INCLUSIVE of both endpoints and WRAPPING -- RTL at `ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:29908' (`m <- MASK(b, ~n)'), endpoint prose at `:29909', mask definition at `:6879'.

*** THE ROW'S TITLE DESCRIBES ONLY THE NON-WRAPPING HALF.  The defect has TWO directions: ***
  * `MB <= 63-SH' (non-wrapping) -- it OVERWRITES the low SH destination bits that must survive;
  * `MB > 63-SH' (wrapping) -- it OMITS the required insertion into positions `0..63-SH', leaving
    those destination bits UNCHANGED.
A repair tested only on non-wrapping encodings fixes one and leaves the other.

**AND SAVING SH IS NOT ENOUGH -- THREE MORE EDITS ARE NEEDED, which is why my sketch was rejected.**  The comparison happens AFTER the increment, so the stopping position is the endpoint's SUCCESSOR, and the counter must be circular:

        int m, n = sh;                       /*  1: keep SH  */
        while (n-- != 0) { ... }             /*  2: consume the copy  */
        do {
                tmp |= ((uint64_t)1 << (63-m));
                m = (m + 1) & 63;            /*  3: circular increment  */
        } while (m != ((64 - sh) & 63));     /*  4: successor, modulo 64  */

**Changing only one of edits 3 and 4 does not repair the loop.**  A partial repair that saves SH and sets the bound to 24 at `MB=40, SH=40' while keeping `m ++' walks 40..63 and then enters the body with `m == 64', evaluating `(uint64_t)1 << -1'.  *** That is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR, and the seat declined to call it an infinite loop on the ground that doing so would assign DEFINED behaviour to an undefined program -- which is the correct discipline and is what my brief's question got wrong. ***

WORKED CASE, usable as a row: `rldimi r4,r3,40,40' = instruction word **0x7864422e**, with `r3 = 0xffffffffffffffff' and `r4 = 0': the repaired loop visits 40..63 then 0..23, 48 iterations, mask **0xffffff0000ffffff**, which is also the correct result.  **The original handler produces 0x0000000000ffffff.**

MUTANT, one character, defined result: `64` -> `63` in the repaired bound.  `rldimi r4,r3,0,0' = **0x7864000c**, `r3 = ~0', `r4 = 0' gives correct `0xffffffffffffffff' and mutant `0xfffffffffffffffe' -- it drops the inclusive endpoint, architectural bit 63.

The seat validated its replacement against an independent bit-membership oracle over **40,960 cases** (every SH/MB pair x ten source/destination pairs), max loop count 64.  **It could NOT compile or run the emulator** -- no native compiler, and WSL returned `E_ACCESSDENIED' -- so this is a READING plus an offline model, not a measurement of this tree. FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrldiclzero]] witness's sibling audit.  MEASURED, not read.

The handler takes its operands as MODE_uint_t and then rotates with a shift pair using 32-sh.  cpu_ppc.c defines DYNTRANS_DUALMODE_32, so the file is compiled TWICE and MODE_uint_t is **uint64_t** in the 64-bit build.  The architecture specifies a 32-bit rotate over the LOW half of the source -- **the high half plays no part whatsoever** -- but the right-shift pulls bits out of the high half straight into the low 32 bits, which is exactly where the mask lives.

MEASURED, source 0xAAAAAAAA0000000F, destination seeded 0x5A5A..., shift 4, full mask:
    got 0x5a5a5a5aaaaaaaf0    want 0x5a5a5a5a000000f0
The 0xAAAAAA is high-half data the architecture says cannot reach there.

ATTRIBUTION IS PINNED BY TWO COMPANION ROWS: rlwinm on the SAME source and shift is CORRECT, because it casts to uint32_t before rotating, and rlwimi at SH=0 is correct because the ternary short-circuits the rotate entirely.  **So the defect is the missing truncation in this one handler, not the shape of the rotate expression.**

*A row testing this is VACUOUS unless the source's two halves DIFFER: the seat's own first draft used an all-ones source, under which a 64-bit rotate and a true 32-bit one agree bit for bit, and it corrected the row rather than shipping it green.*

ADJACENT, NOT A DEFECT BUT WORTH RECORDING so a round does not rediscover it: rldic, rldcl and rldcr are NOT IMPLEMENTED AT ALL -- the decoder's default swallows them.  rldic in particular is documented and compiler-emitted.

*** DESIGN REVIEW 2026-09-10: THE WIDTH PREMISE HOLDS AND **TRUNCATION ALONE IS NOT THE FIX**. ***

Casting the source to `uint32_t' before the rotate is necessary and not sufficient.  The prescribed repair splits the combined declaration -- `uint32_t tmp = (uint32_t)reg(...)' with the destination kept at the mode-dependent width -- **and additionally handles the WRAPPING mask**, because the manual's mask wraps when the beginning exceeds the end: `if (mb > me) ra = (ra & 0xffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)tmp << 32);' AFTER the rotation and BEFORE the existing mask loop.

*** AND A NEW FINDING THAT CONTRADICTS THE EARLIER SIBLING AUDIT: `rlwinm' AND `rlwnm' ARE NOT UNIVERSALLY CORRECT. ***  The witness measured them green on the cases it drove and the audit recorded them as correct; the design review says that is true of those cases and not of the handlers.  **A measured-green sample is not a proof of correctness**, which is this project's own reading-versus- measurement distinction cutting the other way for once -- the measurement was right about what it measured and the GENERALISATION from it was mine.  Re-check both before either is called clean, and do not let this row's fix be copied to them on the strength of the audit.

*** THE GATE CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE.  I WROTE IT INTO THREE ROWS, A CHANGELOG BLOCK AND TWO COMMIT MESSAGES BEFORE A SEAT CHECKED IT (wiringcliff/codex_ppcgate_20260910.txt). ***

**I CLAIMED: 'no gate in this tree instantiates a 64-bit PowerPC CPU at all, so the whole 64-bit-only instruction group is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION.'  THE FIRST HALF IS FALSE.**  Gate 9 (gate_asan_sweep.sh) enumerates EVERY advertised machine type and subtype -- including bareppc, testppc and macppc/g5, all of which default to the PPC970 -- so 64-bit PowerPC CPUs ARE constructed by a gate today, and have been all along.

**THE CORRECT AND NARROWER FINDING: NO GATE CHECKS THEIR INSTRUCTION RESULTS.**  Gate 9 is a CONSTRUCTION check with no PowerPC result oracle; the two PowerPC gates both drive `macppc -e g4', an MPC7400, which is 32-bit, and their probes select it EXPLICITLY rather than by default.  So the defects were invisible because nothing EXECUTES these instructions and inspects the answer -- not because nothing builds the CPU.

*** THAT DISTINCTION IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN WITNESS LADDER, ONE LEVEL UP, AND I WALKED PAST IT. ***  The ladder's whole rung-2 clause says machine CONSTRUCTION proves presence and NOT reachability, and is a reproduction only for defects that construction itself executes.  I applied that rule carefully to witnesses all day and then made exactly the error it warns about when reasoning about GATES.  A gate that constructs a CPU is a rung-2 gate; these defects need a rung-3 one.

THE PRESCRIBED CLOSURE IS SMALLER THAN MY FRAMING SUGGESTED: wire the existing 19-row regress/ppc_rldicl_probe.py into gate_ppc.sh, asserting its score AND its completion sentinel.  That closes the missing instruction-result check.  **It does NOT close all 64-bit PowerPC coverage**, and the seat says so explicitly rather than letting the round claim it does.

*** DESIGNED 2026-09-10 (ppcrldimimask/codex_repair_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, ZERO cyber flags), AND IT FOUND A SECOND DEFECT AT THIS SITE THAT I HAD NOT SEEN.  MY 'ONE-TOKEN CAST' PREMISE IS REFUTED. ***

The width contamination is confirmed exactly as filed: for `1 <= SH <= 31' the erroneous expression's low word is `correct_rot32(L, SH) | ((H << SH) & 0xffffffff)', and the existing low-word mask can select those bits.  `SH == 0' bypasses the shift expression and is clean.

*** THE SECOND DEFECT: WHEN `MB > ME' THE ARCHITECTURAL MASK WRAPS ACROSS THE 64-BIT BOUNDARY AND COVERS THE ENTIRE HIGH HALF, so RA's high 32 bits must be REPLACED with the rotated word -- and this implementation preserves them unconditionally. ***  `ROTL32(x, y)' is defined as rotating `x || x', the low word DUPLICATED (`ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:17143'), and the rlwimi RTL at `:29989' combines that with `MASK(MB+32, ME+32)'.  The wrapping mask visits `MB+32..63, 0..ME+32' -- which includes every architectural position `0..31'.

    MB <= ME   high 32 mask bits all ZERO  -> preserve old RA      (what the code does)
    MB >  ME   high 32 mask bits all ONE   -> replace with rot word (what the code never does)

**So the repair is narrowing AND a high-word insertion**, and it must sit after the rotation and before the loop mutates `mb':

        uint32_t tmp = (uint32_t)reg(ic->arg[0]);
        MODE_uint_t ra = reg(ic->arg[1]);
        ...
        tmp = sh ? ((tmp << sh) | (tmp >> (32-sh))) : tmp;
        /*  A wrapping MASK(MB+32, ME+32) includes the high word.  */
        if (mb > me)
                ra = (ra & 0xffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)tmp << 32);

In the 32-bit compilation the conversion back to `MODE_uint_t' discards that high half, so the existing behaviour there is unchanged.

MUTANT, one character: `>' -> `<' in the new condition.  `rlwimi r4,r3,0,31,0' = **0x506407c0**, `r3 = 0xaaaaaaaa0000000f', `r4 = 0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a' gives correct `0x0000000f5a5a5a5b' and mutant `0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5b' -- the low-word insertion succeeds and the high-word replacement is skipped.

TERMINATION PROVED rather than assumed: both fields are masked `& 31', `mb' is reset to 0 on reaching 32, positions are `(b+k) mod 32', and ME is processed after `((ME-b+32) % 32) + 1' bodies -- between 1 and 32.  Every shift count `31-mb' is in range.

rows.title: cpu_mips_instr.c X(ext): EXT requires a properly sign-extended 32-bit source and nothing checks it -- a SECOND restriction, independent of the shift-count range that [[mipsextshift]] closes
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[mipsextshift]] design review (mipsextshift/codex_guards_RETRY_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max), which found it while answering a question about something else and said so explicitly: *"The proposed range checks do not address that separate condition."*

MIPS64 Volume II states the restriction on EXT's page (mips64_volII.txt:746) and reflects it in the instruction's operation section (`:750'): the source register must hold a properly sign-extended 32-bit value.  `X(ext)' reads `uint32_t rs = reg(ic->arg[1]);' -- it TRUNCATES to 32 bits and asks nothing about the upper half, so a 64-bit register holding a value that is not a sign-extension of its low word is accepted and extracted from silently.

**WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO [[mipsextshift]]:** that row's guards are a DECODE-time predicate over two instruction fields, decidable when the instruction is translated. This one is a RUN-time property of a register value, so it cannot be checked in the decoder at all and needs a different fix shape.  Same instruction, different site, different mechanism -- the round-scope rule's same-fix-design condition fails.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING: this is UNPREDICTABLE-on-violation like the range case, but unlike the range case it causes **no undefined behaviour in the host** -- the truncation is well-defined C.  The cost is a wrong guest answer in a state a correct guest does not reach, not a host fault.

NOT MEASURED, no witness, and it inherits [[mipsextshift]]'s blocker: EXT is MIPS32 Release 2, so no machine in this tree has yet been named that executes it.

*** DROPPED 2026-09-11 -- NOT A DEFECT, and the disposition I asked for explicitly rather than having a check invented for its own sake. ***

**THE RESTRICTION IS REAL AND EXPLICIT** -- it is in BOTH the Restrictions block and the architectural pseudocode, not a programming note.  `mips64_volII.txt:746`:

    "If GPR rs does not contain a sign-extended 32-bit value (bits 63..31 equal), then the
     result of the operation is UNPREDICTABLE."

and `:750` checks it in the Operation itself -- `if ((lsb + msbd) > 31) or (NotWordValue(GPR[rs])) then UNPREDICTABLE endif` -- with `NotWordValue` defined at `:117` as bits 63..32 not equalling 32 copies of bit 31.

*** BUT UNPREDICTABLE DOES NOT REQUIRE VARIATION, AND THAT IS WHAT DECIDES IT. ***  The architecture's own definition (`:44`) says results *"MAY vary from processor implementation to implementation, instruction to instruction, or as a function of time"*, and that software can never depend on them.  **May vary is not must vary.**  An implementation is free to produce the nominal extraction consistently, which is exactly what the truncation does -- so the model selects a PERMITTED result in a state where the architecture specifies none.  No detector, randomisation or exception is owed.

**MY SCOPE WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the correction is worth keeping even though the row is dropped:**
  * the requirement ALSO governs **`INS`**, and there it applies to **both `rs` AND the existing `rt` value** (`:770`) -- I filed it as an `EXT`-only property;
  * it does **NOT** govern `DEXT`/`DEXTM`/`DEXTU` or `DINS`/`DINSM`/`DINSU` at all (`:554`, `:562`, `:570`, `:586`, `:594`, `:602`).  The doubleword forms carry their own ENCODING restrictions and the word-value restriction does not carry over.

*So a round that had 'generalised' this across the family would have added checks to six instructions the architecture does not restrict.*

**NOTHING IS OWED TO [[mipsextshift]]**, which remains live and separate: that row is the SHIFT-COUNT range, where the C is genuinely undefined in the host, not merely unpredictable in the guest.  The two were filed apart for exactly this reason and the split held.

closure.note: DROPPED as NOT A DEFECT on a sourced reading of MIPS64 Volume II (mipsextsignext/codex_signext_20260911.txt).  The architecture declares the violated state UNPREDICTABLE, and UNPREDICTABLE permits a consistent nominal result -- so the model's truncation selects a PERMITTED answer rather than a wrong one.  Author self-review disclosed: I filed the row and I am closing it.

rows.title: dev_dreamcast_maple.c maple_do_dma_xfer(): the DMA address is advanced past the command list and the file flags its own uncertainty about it in a comment -- `// TODO: Should the DMA address be updated?'
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10, split out of [[mapledmaaddr]] so that row can proceed.  **The two are on DIFFERENT SITES and only one of them is that round's.**

`maple_do_dma_xfer()' walks the command list accumulating `addr += datalen_cmd * 4;' per command, and at its tail -- immediately before asserting SYSASIC_EVENT_MAPLE_DMADONE -- does:

        // TODO: Should the DMA address be updated?
        d->dmaaddr = addr;

So an advancing cursor IS modelled, and the author recorded that they did not know whether it should be.  **The comment is the finding**: this is not a defect anyone has established, it is an unresolved semantic question sitting in shipped code with no test either way.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: real Maple hardware behaviour for a read of the DMA address register after a completed transfer.  No Dreamcast or Maple documentation is present in `_scratchpad/` -- checked by `ls`, not assumed -- so this needs a source obtained first, on the vmesbcp2 / 21066 / ddi0406 precedent where a seat's citation was fetched and then VERIFIED LOCALLY rather than trusted.

**TWO EARLY RETURNS LEAVE THE FUNCTION BEFORE THE TAIL** and are part of the same question: the `!d->enable' path and the `addr & 0x1f' alignment refusal both return without touching `d->dmaaddr', so after an aborted transfer the field holds the PROGRAMMED address while after a completed one it holds the advanced address.  Whatever contract is settled has to cover both.

*** DO NOT LET THIS BLOCK [[mapledmaaddr]]. ***  That round deletes a terminating call in the register's READ arm, which is a pure reporter of this field -- it neither creates nor resolves the question above, and the same unverified address is ALREADY handed to the DMA engine on every transfer whether or not a guest ever reads it back.  The dependency runs the other way: whatever is settled here becomes the expected value of that round's disclosed after-DMA row, which is why that row is written to pin the READ ARM'S contract rather than to certify the advanced value.

*** ARITHMETIC CORRECTED 2026-09-10 (mapledmaaddr/codex_readarm_20260910.txt) BEFORE ANYONE BUILT ON IT. ***  This row first described the advance as `addr += datalen_cmd * 4' per command.  **That is one of three terms.**  Each descriptor advances the local cursor by 8 bytes of control words, 4 bytes of command word, and `4 * datalen_cmd' of data, so the committed value is

        C = (P + SUM over descriptors of (12 + 4*D_i))  mod 2^32

Two consequences for whoever settles the hardware contract: **the sum is modulo 2^32, so "advanced" does not imply numerically larger**, and `C != P' is not guaranteed in general -- so a test asserting merely that the value CHANGED is weaker than it looks.

**AND THE EARLY-EXIT DESCRIPTION IN [[mapledmaaddr]] WAS WRONG in a way that matters here:** an early return preserves the field's ENTRY value, which may be a PRIOR transfer's cursor -- it does not restore a programmed address.  The `!d->enable' test also precedes the alignment test, so a disabled and unaligned address never reaches the alignment diagnostic.  Any contract settled for this row has to cover the entry-value case, not just "programmed" versus "advanced".

Also relevant to the eventual policy: an alternative length calculation from the CONTROL word sits COMMENTED OUT beside the executable one, so the file records that its author considered a second arithmetic and chose this one.

rows.title: cpu_ppc_instr.c X(rlwinm) and X(rlwnm): a WRAPPING mask (MB > ME) selects the whole high half under the manual's RTL, and both handlers zero it instead -- a DEFECT (resolved 2026-09-10 against PowerPC Book I v2.01; until 2026-10-09 this title read 'but the manual CONTRADICTS ITSELF on this point and the dispute is unresolved', an L4 per 7n-3); rung-3 witness on committed HEAD 2026-10-09
rows.note:
[2026-10-09] WITNESSED ON COMMITTED HEAD, and the stale DISPUTE wording corrected.  (1) Fable 5.1's 7n-3 ruling (regress/artifacts/fablequeue7n_20261009/fable5_rule7n_35.md; GPT-6 Astra CONFIRM WITH CHANGES (8), codex_astra_confirm.txt beside it): the rlwinm/rlwnm handlers are still committed-defective (a masked uint32_t assigned into the 64-bit reg()), so the order discriminator for the re-pinned oracle is runnable today -- a red on committed HEAD -- and a divergence or provenance argument is corroboration, never that red.  (2) OWNER 2026-10-09: WITNESS ONLY -- the fix round stays UNSCHEDULED.  (3) THE WITNESS, regress/artifacts/ppcrlwhighhalf/witness_committed_20261009/: agy (gemini-3.8-flash-high, measuring seat) ran a probe copied from regress/ppc_rlwimi_probe.py's cold-debugger harness (kept as ppc_rlwhigh_witness.py.txt; rename to .py to run) against a binary built from `git archive 200671b6` (cpu_ppc_instr.c md5 87a766e0 = HEAD's), unmodified -E bareppc -M 64 (PPC970).  rlwinm. r4,r3,1,31,0 with r3 = 1 gave r4 = 0x0 and CR0 = 2 (EQ) where Book I gives 0x0000000200000000 and CR0 = 4 (GT); rlwinm (Rc=0) and rlwnm with RB = 1 and RB = 33 gave the same 0x0.  Controls all green: PVR 0x00390000 through mfspr (the device-signature equivalent), li r9 after the target (liveness), the tree's own unassemble of 0x54640fc1 = rlwinm. r4,r3,1,31,0 (instruction control), and the non-wrapping rlwinm r4,r3,1,0,31 = 0x2 (the small-nonzero row).  witness.out ends PPCRLWHIGH_WITNESS_DONE.  The probe was read by the main loop before this record: r4 is seeded 0x5A5A5A5A5A5A5A5A in every session, so a 0x0 is a real write, and a dead session would read None, not 0x0.  This ONE artifact is the order discriminator for ppcwitnessmaskoracle's re-pinned oracle, this row's witness, and reproduce-before-edit for the fix round, and its mtime predates any handler edit.  (4) AN UNREAD REVIEW, recorded now: regress/artifacts/codexfarm_20260926/codex_ppcrlwhighhalf.txt (GPT-6 Astra, 2026-09-26, tracked since 1202d342) carried the witness spec used above, the stale-title/MED findings and line drift, and was cited by no ledger row, CHANGELOG block, queue entry or receipt until Fable's 7n-3 answer found it -- the unread-review class, fourth instance.  (5) The oracle repair (regress/ppc_rldicl_probe.py + regress/artifacts/ppcwitnessmaskoracle/) is committed ALONE in the same commit as this note, before any rlwinm/rlwnm handler edit.  ||  FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrlwimiwidth]] design review (ppcrldimimask/codex_repair_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max).  **It arrived as a refutation of MY OWN premise**: I had told the seat that these two siblings are the CORRECT idiom that `rlwimi' fails to follow.  They are correct about the low word and, on the RTL reading, wrong about the high one.

THE MECHANISM, verified locally by reading both the decoder and the handlers rather than taking the seat's word:
  * the decoder (`case PPC_HI6_RLWNM: case PPC_HI6_RLWINM:') builds a **32-bit** mask with a correct wrap -- `mask |= ((uint32_t)0x80000000 >> mb); ... mb ++; mb &= 31;' -- so the LOW word is right including the `MB > ME' case;
  * `X(rlwinm)' holds `tmp' as `uint32_t' and ends `reg(ic->arg[0]) = tmp;'.  **Assigning a uint32_t into a 64-bit register ZERO-EXTENDS**, so the high half is unconditionally 0.

Under the RTL the high half is not free to be zero: `ROTL32(x, y)' is defined as rotating `x || x' -- the low word DUPLICATED (`ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:17143') -- and `MASK(MB+32, ME+32)' with `MB > ME' wraps to cover `MB+32..63' AND `0..ME+32', the second range including every architectural position `0..31'.  So the high half should receive the rotated word.  Worked case from the seat: `rlwinm' with source `0xaaaaaaaa0000000f', SH=0, MB=31, ME=0 gives RTL `0x0000000f00000001' against the tree's `0x0000000000000001'.  The same applies to `rlwnm' when the register shift's low five bits are zero.

*** THE REASON THIS IS FILED AS A DISPUTE AND NOT AS A DEFECT: THE MANUAL CONTRADICTS ITSELF, AND THE SEAT SAID SO ITSELF RATHER THAN LETTING ITS READING STAND UNQUALIFIED. ***  `ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:30065' asserts blanket upper-half CLEARING for `rlwinm', which conflicts with that instruction's own RTL and with the general duplicated-rotation / wrapping-mask definitions when `MB > ME'.  The seat followed the RTL and flagged the conflict; **this row does not adopt either reading.**

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, in preference order: a second PowerPC manual in `_scratchpad/` (three more are present -- `ppc_oea_book3_v201', `ppc_pem32_rev2_2001', `ppc_vea_book2_v201' -- and none has been consulted on this point); then real hardware behaviour; then what other emulators and compilers assume.  **Compiler output is the strong practical argument either way**: if compilers emit wrapping-mask `rlwinm' expecting the high half cleared, the tree's behaviour is what software depends on whatever the RTL says.

*** DO NOT LET THIS BLOCK [[ppcrlwimiwidth]]'s NARROWING HALF. ***  That round's FIRST defect -- high-half SOURCE bits leaking into the low word through `tmp >> (32-sh)' at 64-bit width -- is independent of this dispute and is wrong under every reading.  Only its high-half INSERTION half depends on how this resolves.

*** ADJUDICATED AGAINST THE FOUR LOCAL MANUALS 2026-09-10 (ppcrlwhighhalf/codex_dispute_20260910.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, ZERO cyber flags).  THE DISPUTE STANDS, AND THE DOCUMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT IS NOT HERE. ***

**THE DERIVATION IS CONFIRMED, with a worked evaluation of the specification:**

        rS = 0x0000000012345678, SH = 0, MB = 31, ME = 0
        r  = 0x1234567812345678        (ROTL[32] duplicates the low word -- :17143)
        m  = 0xFFFFFFFF80000001        (MASK wraps when MB > ME -- :17137, :6879)
        rA = 0x1234567800000000        <-- upper half NONZERO

Because `ME+32 >= 32', the wrapped interval `0..ME+32' contains EVERY position 0..31, so the RTL puts the complete rotated word into the upper half.  For `MB <= ME' the mask lies wholly within 32..63 and the upper half is cleared.

*** THE CONTRADICTING SENTENCE IS GENUINELY UNCONDITIONAL, AND THE OBVIOUS ESCAPE ROUTE DOES NOT WORK. ***  At `:30065', in the main instruction description immediately after the RTL -- not a programming note, not a simplified-mnemonics table -- the 2005 PEM says flatly *"The upper 32 bits of rA are cleared."*  Nothing in that paragraph restricts it to `MB <= ME'.

**A SECOND, SIMILAR-LOOKING SENTENCE AT `:30074' IS QUALIFIED AND AGREES WITH THE RTL** -- *"For all uses mentioned, the high-order 32 bits of rA are cleared"*, where the listed extraction, rotation, shift and clear uses all employ NON-WRAPPING masks.  So it does not explain away the unconditional one; the same goes for Appendix E.4.2 at `:50520', scoped to its own simplified-mnemonics table.  *That is worth recording because finding the qualified sentence looks like a resolution and is not.*

*** THE THREE UNCONSULTED MANUALS SUPPLY NO RULING AT ALL -- so this is an INTERNAL disagreement in ONE document, not four sources disagreeing. ***
  * **2001 PEM rev 2**: its own computation-modes section says *"all pseudocode examples provided in this chapter are for 32-bit implementations"* (`:15668'), and its rotate section specifies a **32-bit** mask wrapping from position 31 (`:7535').  Its `rlwinm' RTL uses `MASK(MB, ME)' with no `+32'.  It describes registers with no upper half.  *A trap the seat flagged itself: its notation table DOES carry the duplicated 64-bit `ROTL[32]' definition at `:15558', which does not override the chapter's stated scope.*
  * **OEA Book III v2.01** and **VEA Book II v2.01**: **ZERO occurrences** of `rlwinm', `rlwnm' or `rlwimi'.  Their subjects are the operating environment and the storage model.  Being architectural specifications does not help if they do not address the operation.

*** WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: **PowerPC Architecture Book I (UISA), version 2.01** -- and the 2005 PEM NAMES IT AS THE AUTHORITY OVER ITSELF at `:302': "This book does not attempt to replace the PowerPC Architecture specification (version 2.01) ... which remains the defining manual."  The PEM classifies integer rotate and shift as UISA instructions (`:633'), and Book III's preface identifies Book I as defining the base instruction set.  **Book I is ABSENT from `_scratchpad/'.** ***  This project has fetched a cited manual three times before -- `vmesbcp2', `21066_66a_hrm', `ddi0406' -- each time verifying the load-bearing claims LOCALLY rather than trusting the seat's page anchor, which is the rule that would apply here.

**THE UPPER-HALF RESULTS IMPLIED BY THE RTL, for all three instructions**, since a round on any of them inherits this question:

        instruction   MB <= ME                      MB > ME
        rlwinm        cleared                       replaced by the rotated word
        rlwnm         cleared                       replaced by the rotated word
        rlwimi        previous upper half preserved replaced by the rotated word

`rlwnm' transfers directly (same rotation, mask and final AND at `:30142').  `rlwimi' differs only in the insertion form `rA <- (r & m) | (rA & !m)' (`:29989'): a zero mask bit PRESERVES the old bit, and a wrapping mask has ones throughout the upper half, so it replaces all of them.

**THE SEAT'S OWN CONFIDENCE, recorded rather than rounded up: it FAVOURS the RTL reading and says it cannot establish it conclusively from these files.**  That is the honest answer and it is why [[ppcwitnessmaskoracle]]'s `mask32' was deliberately left unchanged today -- correcting it would have adopted one side of this inside a test oracle.

*** RESOLVED 2026-09-10 BY FETCHING THE DOCUMENT THE PEM DEFERS TO.  IT IS A DEFECT, NOT A DISPUTE, AND THIS ROW IS RAISED TO HIGH. ***

`_scratchpad/ppc_uisa_book1_v201.pdf` / `.txt` -- **PowerPC User Instruction Set Architecture, Book I, Version 2.01, September 2003** (IBM; Wetzel / May / Frey / Silha), 997 KB -> 784 KB of text, 12,586 lines.  Fetched with the owner's approval on this project's own vmesbcp2 / 21066 / ddi0406 precedent, and then **verified locally rather than taken from any seat's page anchor.**  *(`file` reports "10 page(s)" and is wrong, exactly as it was for the 21066 manual -- the real count is in a linearized trailer.)*

**BOOK I's `rlwinm`, at `ppc_uisa_book1_v201.txt:4125-4137`:**

        n   <- SH
        r   <- ROTL32((RS)32:63, n)
        m   <- MASK(MB+32, ME+32)
        RA  <- r & m

    "The contents of register RS are rotated32 left SH bits.  A mask is generated having 1-bits
     from bit MB+32 through bit ME+32 and 0-bits elsewhere.  The rotated data are ANDed with the
     generated mask and the result is placed into register RA."

**And Book I's own MASK definition, `:578-580`: "Mask having 1s in positions x through y (WRAPPING IF x > y) and 0s elsewhere."**

*** THE DECIDING FACT IS THAT BOOK I's CLEARING SENTENCE IS **SCOPED** WHILE THE PEM's IS **UNCONDITIONAL**. ***  A first grep for *upper 32 bits* and *high-order 32 bits of* returned hits only in branch and addressing contexts, hundreds of lines away.  A second pass over the `rlwinm` page span itself (`:4170-4190`) did return several *clearing* mentions -- **and reading them shows every one is a PROGRAMMING NOTE about clearing "the remaining bits of THE LOW-ORDER 32 BITS of RA"**, each for an explicitly NON-WRAPPING (MB, ME) choice: `MB=32-n, ME=31`; `MB=0, ME=n-1`; `MB=0, ME=31`; `MB=n, ME=31`.  *Those hits are exactly the false positive that would have made a grep-only negative wrong, which is why the span was read.*

**SO THE 2005 PEM's UNCONDITIONAL SENTENCE (`:30065`, "The upper 32 bits of rA are cleared") IS A PEM-ONLY CLAIM, ABSENT FROM THE MANUAL THE PEM ITSELF NAMES AS DEFINING** (`:302`: *"This book does not attempt to replace the PowerPC Architecture specification (version 2.01) ... which remains the defining manual"*).  The RTL reading wins on the authority the PEM nominates.

**THE DEFECT, restated now that it is one:** `X(rlwinm)` holds `tmp` as `uint32_t` and assigns it into a 64-bit register, which zero-extends -- so for `MB > ME` the upper half reads 0 where the architecture requires the rotated word.  Same for `X(rlwnm)` when the register shift's low five bits are zero.  Worked case: source `0xaaaaaaaa0000000f`, SH=0, MB=31, ME=0 gives `0x0000000f00000001` against the tree's `0x0000000000000001`.

**A COROLLARY THAT WAS ALSO A TRAP:** Book I's left-hand column on the same page gives `rldic`'s mask as `MASK(b, !n)`, confirming the complement notation `!n = 63-SH` that [[ppcrldimimask]] depends on -- so that row's endpoint reasoning is corroborated by the defining manual too.

*The honest note on what changed the answer: the design review said it FAVOURED the RTL reading and could not establish it from the four local manuals, and it was right on both counts.  What settled it was one download and twenty minutes of reading -- not a better argument.*

*** CORRECTED WITHIN HOURS, AND THE ERROR WAS MINE: I WROTE THAT BOOK I 'NEVER SAYS' THE UPPER 32 BITS ARE CLEARED, HAVING READ `:4170-4190' AND STOPPED **FIVE LINES SHORT** OF THE SENTENCE. ***

**Book I `:4195-4196`: "For all the uses given above, the high-order 32 bits of register RA are cleared."**  Found by the Book I verification pass, then confirmed here by opening those lines.

**THE CONCLUSION IS UNAFFECTED AND THE SENTENCE WAS STILL WRONG**, which is the combination that let it survive a first reading.  The corrected statement:
  * Book I's clearing sentence is QUALIFIED -- *"for all the uses given above"* -- to the programming-note uses enumerated immediately above it, **every one of which fixes a NON-WRAPPING `(MB, ME)`**;
  * the 2005 PEM carries that SAME qualified sentence at `:30074` **and** an UNCONDITIONAL one at `:30065`, inside its instruction description;
  * so it is the UNCONDITIONAL claim that is absent from Book I, **neither qualified sentence reaches the wrapping case**, and Book I's normative RTL governs it.

*** THE PROCESS LESSON, and it lands on the instruction I had JUST WRITTEN INTO THE CARRIER: I told the next reader to check that absence BY READING RATHER THAN BY ONE GREP -- and then read a span five lines too short. ***  The instruction was right; my execution of it was not.  **An absence claim is only as good as the span actually read, and the span has to be chosen to CONTAIN the thing being denied rather than to end where the interesting text appears to stop.**  Corrected in the carrier, the tracked copy, this row, [[ppcwitnessmaskoracle]] and the witness docstring -- five sites, found by grepping for siblings, which is the rule that exists for exactly this.

*** REPAIR DESIGNED 2026-09-11 (ppcrlwhighhalf/codex_repair_20260911.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, ZERO cyber flags).  THE DEFECT IS CONFIRMED AND MY PREFERRED REPAIR IS REFUTED. ***

I expected the cheap fix to be **widening the decoder's precomputed mask**, since the decoder runs once per translated instruction and both handlers consume it every execution.  **That is not supported, for two independent reasons:**

  1. **A widened mask alone does not repair anything.**  The handlers would still have to DUPLICATE the rotated word into both halves and retain it through the AND -- execution-time work either way.  Precomputing the mask avoids building it at run time and nothing else.  *"Widen the decoder mask and fix both for free" is not supported.*
  2. *** THE ARGUMENT SLOT'S CAPACITY FOLLOWS THE HOST, NOT THE GUEST MODE -- AND I FOUND THE DECLARATION THE REVIEW COULD NOT REACH. ***  It was confined to two files that do not define `struct ppc_instr_call', said so plainly, and reasoned that IF the member were `size_t' its width would follow the host.  **`src/include/cpu.h:76` declares `uintptr_t arg[ARCH ## _N_IC_ARGS]`** -- which also follows the host.  So on a 32-bit HOST the slot is 32 bits and a 64-bit mask would be silently truncated, whatever the guest is doing.  **The conclusion is confirmed and its warrant is now stronger than the review's own.**

*The translator's local `mask' is demonstrably `uint32_t' (`:4051'; lines of 030e961f, at 987cb596 :4074), and the shared decode arm at `:4512-4534' (lines of 030e961f; at 987cb596 :4564-4586) serves exactly `PPC_HI6_RLWNM` and `PPC_HI6_RLWINM` including their record forms -- `rlwimi` has a SEPARATE arm and a separate argument contract and does not consume this mask.*

**ADOPTED: dedicated WRAPPING handlers selected at DECODE time** -- `rlwinm_wrap` / `rlwnm_wrap` beside the existing bodies, chosen when `mb > me`, and guarded `#ifndef MODE32` so the 32-bit compilation does not carry them at all.  That keeps the ordinary non-wrapping path byte-unchanged and byte-identical in both compilations, which is the property that makes this cheap to verify: **every encoding that works today must still take the same code.**

SCOPE CAVEAT THE REVIEW STATED ITSELF, kept because it bounds what was checked: it audited the VISIBLE consumers of `arg[1]` in this file, and a translation tail at `:5408` (lines of 030e961f; at 987cb596 :5460) was outside its permitted reads.  So the no-other-consumer finding is file-scoped.

*** THE ADOPTED REPAIR WOULD HAVE SHIPPED **INERT**, AND THE DECODER IS WHY.  Found 2026-09-11 (ppcrlwhighhalf/codex_witness_20260911.txt), CONFIRMED HERE BY READING THE LINES. ***

The design adopted yesterday selects dedicated wrapping handlers **at decode time, when `mb > me`**.  `cpu_ppc_instr.c:4515-4529` (lines of 599a7a82; at 987cb596 :4567-4581):

        mb = (iword >> 6) & 31;
        ...
        for (;;) {
                mask |= ((uint32_t)0x80000000 >> mb);
                if (mb == me)
                        break;              <-- exits ONLY when mb == me
                mb ++; mb &= 31;            <-- and it MUTATES mb to get there
        }
        switch (main_opcode) {              <-- handler selection happens HERE
                ... ic->f = rc? instr(rlwinm_dot) : instr(rlwinm); ...

*** BY THE TIME THE HANDLER IS CHOSEN, `mb == me` ALWAYS.  A `mb > me` TEST THERE IS ALWAYS FALSE, SO THE WRAPPING HANDLER WOULD NEVER BE SELECTED AND THE REPAIR WOULD CHANGE NOTHING. ***

**THE FIX IS TO CAPTURE THE ORIGINAL `mb` BEFORE THE MASK LOOP**, or to test `((iword >> 6) & 31) > me` directly from the instruction word at the selection point.  Either way the ORDER is load-bearing and the design must say so.

*This is the identical trap the same review found in `rlwimi` one day earlier -- there the `if (mb > me)` conditional had to PRECEDE the insertion loop, because the loop walks `mb` around to `me`.  **The same mutation, in the decoder instead of the handler, and I did not transfer the lesson.**  A warrant that is true in one function is not thereby true one call earlier.*

**AND IT WOULD HAVE BEEN AN INERT REPAIR SHIPPED WITH A GREEN TABLE** -- every non-wrapping encoding takes byte-identical code, which is the property the design leaned on for safety, and every wrapping encoding would have kept the defect.  A detector built from the same wrong premise would have agreed.

TWO MORE AXES NAMED IN THE SAME ANSWER, both outside my four: **register indices** and **aliasing**.  My axes were `mb`, `me`, the shift, and the compilation width.  *That is the second time in two days an enumeration of mine has named the containers and missed what indexes them -- the first cost `#519` its close.*

*** THE INERT FINDING IS CONFIRMED BY THE SEAT, AND IT CORRECTED MY SCOPE IN THE SAME BREATH.  2026-09-11 (ppcrlwhighhalf/codex_redesign_20260911.err -- see the apparatus note below for why the answer is in the `.err`). ***

**CONFIRMED:** *"The loop does guarantee `mb == me` at selection."*  So the adopted design would indeed never select the wrapping handler, and the repair as recorded yesterday would have shipped doing nothing.

*** AND A SCOPE CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTE: I wrote that `rlwnm` has the high-half gap *"when the register shift's low five bits are zero"*.  THAT IS TOO NARROW. ***  *"In this exact file, `rlwnm` uses `uint32_t tmp` for every shift count, so the wrapping defect extends beyond zero shifts."*  The zero-shift case was one WORKED EXAMPLE in an earlier answer and I generalised it into a condition.  **The high half is zeroed by the final assignment for EVERY shift**, so the defect is universal over wrapping masks and not conditioned on the shift at all.

**THE CHOSEN DESIGN IS CANDIDATE (b): re-derive `MB` from `iword` in the DECODER, and leave the existing execution handlers unchanged.**  That keeps the hot path untouched and puts the only new work at translation time.

**IT RE-CONFIRMED THE PARTITION INDEPENDENTLY: 496 wrapping and 528 non-wrapping mask pairs**, and that the proposed calculation matches Book I across all 32 shifts with **every low-word result unchanged**.

*** AN HONEST LIMIT ON MY OWN SAFETY ARGUMENT, WHICH THE SEAT VOLUNTEERED: *** I have been defending this design on the property that *every encoding that works today takes byte-identical code*.  The seat's qualification: *"retaining the old handlers preserves their SOURCE and EXECUTION PATH, but byte-for-byte NATIVE-CODE identity would still need a build comparison."*  **Source identity and object identity are different claims and I had been asserting the stronger one.**  A round shipping this owes the build comparison or a narrower sentence.

*** 2026-09-11, VERIFIED BY READING: THE DECODER'S MASK LOOP LEAVES `mb == me` ALWAYS, AND -- CORRECTING THIS ROW'S OWN FRAMING -- **NO WRAPPING DISPATCH EXISTS IN THE COMMITTED TREE AT ALL.** ***

`cpu_ppc_instr.c:4523-4529` [at 987cb596: the loop is :4571-4576] breaks on `if (mb == me)` and mutates `mb` to get there.  So a decode-time test of `mb > me` selects NOTHING and `mb >= me` selects EVERYTHING.  Any fix must capture `wrap = mb > me` BEFORE the loop, or re-derive MB from `iword`.

**The framing correction matters for the disposition:** `:4530-4535` [at 987cb596: :4577-4582] is still a bare `rc ? _dot : plain`, and `git log` shows the rlwinm repair was refuted at RECORDS level (`030e961`, `576c168`) and never shipped as code.  **So this is a constraint on the NEXT edit, not an inert repair sitting in the tree** -- there is nothing to un-break.

THE CONTRAST THAT MAKES IT CONCRETE: `rlwimi`'s shipped fix at `:2608-2638` [at 987cb596: :2608-2656] works PRECISELY BECAUSE its test lives in the HANDLER, where `mb` is freshly decoded at `:2614`, so `if (mb > me)` at `:2621` [at 987cb596: :2639] is evaluated against an unmutated value.  Transplanting that pattern into the DECODER is what is inert.  *That is the scope-transfer class again: a premise true at one call level and false one level up.*

SCOPE CORRECTION, and it narrows in the DANGEROUS direction: the defect is **not** limited to zero shifts.  `rlwnm` at `:2567-2577` and `:2588-2598` holds `uint32_t tmp` through `reg(ic->arg[0]) = tmp;` for EVERY shift count.  **A zero-shift-only witness under-covers the defect.**

*** 2026-09-11 -- THE UNREAD 16,029-BYTE ANSWER, HARVESTED.  **Nine findings sit below its verdict line and at least four would change an edit.**  It refuted one brief premise outright and narrowed three more. ***

*** 1. THE GUARD IS `MODE32`, NOT `DYNTRANS_DUALMODE_32`, AND AN EDIT USING THE WRONG ONE IS A DEAD GUARD. ***  `grep -c DYNTRANS_DUALMODE_32 src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c` is **0** -- the symbol is defined in `cpu_ppc.c:53`, while `generate_tail.c:139` gates the second pass on it and `:151` emits `#define MODE32`.  **So `#ifndef DYNTRANS_DUALMODE_32` would compile the 64-bit path silently into the 32-bit build.**  My brief's framing was true of the build DRIVER and wrong about the symbol to guard on.

*** 2. TWO HANDLER EDITS COVER ALL FOUR FORMS -- this halves the work. ***  `DOT0` (`:208-209`) is a macro wrapper that CALLS THE BASE and then `update_cr0` on the destination, so an early `return` in the base returns to the wrapper, which reads the corrected value.  In the non-`MODE32` pass `reg()` is `*((uint64_t*)(x))`, **so CR0 sees the full corrected 64-bit result for free.**  *Caveat stated by the seat: this holds for the IN-HANDLER route only -- specialised wrapping bases would need the Rc=1 encodings routed to wrappers calling THOSE bases, or the defect stays live.*

*** 3. YOU CANNOT INFER WRAPPING FROM THE EXISTING 32-BIT MASK -- this kills the cheapest-looking option. ***  `(MB,ME) = (1,0)` and `(0,31)` BOTH produce `mask32 == 0xffffffff`.  Since `ic->arg[1]` is already in the handler a future round will reach for it; **the low mask has lost the distinction.**

*** 4. THE HIGH HALF TAKES THE **UNMASKED** ROTATED WORD, so widening `tmp` is a HALF-FIX. ***  `RA64 = ((MB > ME ? uint64(r) : 0) << 32) | (r & mask32)`.  When `MB > ME` the wrap makes the high-word mask all-ones.  *"Merely widening `tmp`, while retaining the existing 32-bit AND, does not accomplish this"* -- the obvious wrong fix, named.

**5. `iword` IS ALREADY IN SCOPE IN BOTH HANDLERS** (`:2569`, `:2590`; the decoder already stores it at `:4538` [at 987cb596: :4585]), so the in-handler test needs **no new argument slot, no decoder change, no flag**.  That is the load-bearing feasibility fact for the recommendation, and it holds.

=== MY PREMISES, ONE REFUTED AND THREE NARROWED ===
* **REFUTED: `:2588-2598` is NOT a second `rlwnm` site -- it is `rlwinm`.**  The file carries `rlwnm` FIRST at `:2567` and `rlwinm` SECOND at `:2588`, the reverse of the natural order, **which is almost certainly how I mislabelled it.**
* **NARROWED: "only `MB=ME=0` catches an `mb >= me` error" is SITE-DEPENDENT.**  If the erroneous `>=` sits AFTER the destructive loop, `mb == me` always, so the comparison is universally true and `(0,31)` catches it too.  **Which witness rows are load-bearing depends on which option is chosen.**
* **STRENGTHENED, into a proof: NO wrapping witness can EVER separate the correct repair from an unconditional high-half write** -- the two formulas agree throughout the wrapping domain, because the high-word mask is all-ones for every wrapping mask.  *But unconditional replication of the MASKED word IS catchable*, and it supplies the case: SH=1, `r4=0x80000001`, `(31,0)` gives correct `0x0000000300000001` against masked-replication `0x0000000100000001`.
* **CORRECTED: `ROTL32` is at Book I `:501-504`** (the RTL notation table), not `:4126` -- and there is a SECOND prose definition at `:4008-4012` giving the bit ranges explicitly.

*** 6. `rlwnm` HAS ITS OWN SCOPED CLEARING SENTENCE at Book I `:4291-4292`, preceded by uses (`:4286-4289`) that fix `MB=0, ME=31` -- NON-WRAPPING. ***  **So the scoping argument is independently established for `rlwnm` rather than transferred from `rlwinm` by symmetry.**  Worth adding to the carrier's Book I entry, which records only the `rlwinm` sentence.

**7. THE ALIAS HAZARD KILLS THE WRAPPER-REPAIR DESIGN OUTRIGHT.**  A wrapper that calls the old handler then re-reads registers to patch the high word is broken for **RA=RS** (source already overwritten), **RA=RB** (shift register overwritten) and **RA=RS=RB**.  The in-handler repair needs no alias branch: `:2571-2572` reads the shift register, `:2573` the source, and the insertion stores only after both.

**8. TEN OPTIONS ENUMERATED against my five**, with a closure claim -- *recover or preserve the endpoint information, carry its classification, or carry the full mask* -- and two explicitly refuted shortcuts.  The genuinely new cheapest one: **select the handler BEFORE the destructive loop**, which needs no saved Boolean at all.  **And option 8 (a full 64-bit mask at translation) is HOST-WIDTH-DEPENDENT**: `cpu.h:76` is `uintptr_t arg[...]`, so it fits on a 64-bit host and not a 32-bit one -- a portability regression under this fork's C99 ethos, which strengthens the in-handler recommendation.

*** 9. A GAP THE SEAT DID NOT NAME, found by the harvest: THE SHIPPED `rlwimi` FIX IS NOT `MODE32`-GUARDED. ***  `:2620-2622` is bare.  In `MODE32`, `MODE_uint_t ra` is `uint32_t` so the statement is arithmetically a no-op -- **but the `if` and the statement are still compiled into the 32-bit pass.**  Codex proposes a `#ifndef MODE32` guard the sibling precedent does not have.  **Both are defensible; the round must pick DELIBERATELY rather than discover the asymmetry later**, and the seat's claim that *"the sibling's placement transfers directly"* is silent on it.

**10. NO FUSED/COMBINED CONSUMERS EXIST** -- `grep rlwinm|rlwnm` over the whole file returns exactly 8 lines: two comments, two `X()`, two `DOT0()`, two decoder assignments.  *Checked because a missed fused handler would be a silent half-fix.*

**EVIDENCE BASIS, stated twice by the seat and honest:** source inspection, an in-memory text diff, and arithmetic models over 1,024 masks x 32 shifts x 32 basis bits plus all 32^3 register-index combinations -- **"not compiled-handler or emulator measurements."**  All fourteen encodings were re-derived independently by the harvest and every one is correct.  It ratified NOTHING it was told: previous measurements, the rejected proposal and the commit history were outside its permitted files and it said *"cannot be independently verified"* rather than agreeing.

*Two derived notes worth keeping: **`RB=0` means read GPR0, not a constant zero** (`:2571-2572`), so a witness must INITIALISE r0; and the RB INDEX must stay distinct from its CONTENTS -- values 1 and 33 must give the same shift, as must 0 and 32.*
