rows.title: harness: the #522 witness's rldimi oracle returns ZERO for every wrapping mask and its mask32 omits the high half -- so the two filed sibling rows rest on oracles that cannot certify their own repairs
rows.note:
[2026-10-09] THE ORACLE REPAIR IS COMMITTED ALONE, by owner ruling (Fable 5.1's 7n-3 consequence 2; GPT-6 Astra confirmed with changes, regress/artifacts/fablequeue7n_20261009/codex_astra_confirm.txt): regress/ppc_rldicl_probe.py's mask_range(), corrected want_rldimi() and 64-bit mask32() -- uncommitted since 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-17.  Re-derived 2026-10-09 from BOTH helper versions, lifted by ast from HEAD's and the working file (regress/artifacts/ppcwitnessmaskoracle/enumcheck_20261009.out, script enumcheck_20261009.py.txt): mask32 528 of 528 non-wrapping pairs identical and 496 of 496 wrapping pairs differing only by an all-ones high half with the low word unchanged; the old want_rldimi mask all-zero on 2016 of 4096 (MB, SH) pairs, the new one on none, the 2080 non-wrapping pairs identical; want_rldicl and want_rldicr -- the ONLY helpers that file's rows call -- unchanged.  So NO ROW in that file consumes the corrected helpers, and the carrier's oracle-correction bound (one measured red per oracle a ROW consumes) owes nothing there; the probe now says so in a CONTRACT comment.  The order discriminator for the re-pinned rlwinm mask is ppcrlwhighhalf's rung-3 witness on committed HEAD, regress/artifacts/ppcrlwhighhalf/witness_committed_20261009/.  One definition per semantics: the committed mask32 in ppc_rldicl_probe.py and ppc_rlwimi_probe.py are now the same Book I form.  The same commit corrects the probe's TRUNCATION note, which told a reader to recover the lost 2026-09-11 clause with `git show' -- false, that revision was never committed; the clause is quoted back into the file from the brief that inlined the 2026-09-17 diff.  Stays IN WORK until a later records commit names this commit in `commits' and a Fable regress review rules on closure.  ||  FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrldimimask]] design review, which named the defect and the line; **both halves were then verified locally by opening the file before this was written.**

`regress/artifacts/ppcrldiclzero/opus_ppc_rldicl_witness_20260910.py' is a COMMITTED artifact of `#522' (`e777ff0').  Two of its model oracles are wrong for WRAPPING masks:

  * `want_rldimi()' computes `m = mask_b_63(mb) & mask_0_e((63 - sh) & 63)' -- the INTERSECTION of `bits mb..63' with `bits 0..63-sh'.  That is the correct mask when `mb <= 63-sh'.  When `mb > 63-sh' **the two ranges are disjoint and the intersection is EMPTY**, so the oracle returns the untouched destination for every wrapping encoding.  Its own docstring shows how it happened: it cites the manual's PROSE (*"1 bits from bit MB through bit 63 - SH"*), which describes the non-wrapping reading, rather than the `MASK' definition that wraps.
  * `mask32()' is documented *"confined to the low 32 bits"* and sets only `1 << (31 - b)'.  Its companion `rotl32()' correctly returns the DUPLICATED `(r32 << 32) | r32', so the model has the duplication and then masks it away -- the high half a wrapping word mask requires is never selected.

*** THIS DOES NOT INVALIDATE `#522'. ***  That round is `rldicl', which uses neither oracle, and its 190-cell census and 24-row detector are untouched.  The exposure is FORWARD: [[ppcrldimimask]] and [[ppcrlwimiwidth]] are filed on measurements this witness produced, and **the wrapping encodings are exactly where both repairs do their new work** -- so an uncorrected oracle would score a correct repair as wrong, or agree with a repair that fixes only the non-wrapping half.

**THE SHAPE IS ONE THIS PROJECT HAS NAMED BEFORE: a check that cannot fail.**  A wrapping-mask row scored against `want_rldimi()' compares an implementation that omits the wrap against an oracle that omits the wrap, and passes.  *The oracle and the defect share the same misreading of the same sentence.*

OWED BEFORE EITHER SIBLING ROUND MEASURES ANYTHING: correct both oracles to the wrapping `MASK' definition, and add a row at a wrapping encoding that is RED on the committed build -- the order discriminator, so the correction cannot be mistaken for fitting the oracle to a repair.

*** HALF FIXED 2026-09-10, AND THE MANUAL SUPPLIED A SHARPER PROOF THAN THE REVIEW DID. ***

**`want_rldimi' IS CORRECTED.**  The decisive sentence is not the RTL but the mask generator's own definition at `ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:6879-6882', verified by opening it rather than taking the seat's citation:

    :6879  "consists of `1' bits from a start bit, Mstart, through and INCLUDING a stop bit,
            Mstop ... If Mstart > Mstop, the `1' bits WRAP AROUND from position 63 to position 0"
    :6880  if Mstart <= Mstop:  mask[mstart..mstop] = ones
    :6881  else:                mask[mstart..63] = ones ; mask[0..mstop] = ones
    :6882  *** "It is not possible to specify an all-zero mask." ***

**THE WRAPPING BRANCH IS A UNION AND THE FILE COMPUTED AN INTERSECTION**, so it produced exactly the all-zero mask `:6882' says cannot exist.  That sentence turns the defect from an argument about readings into a flat contradiction, and it is now an ASSERTION inside the new `mask_range()' helper -- the architecture's own impossibility claim doing duty as a self-check that would have caught this on the day it was written.

*** THE SCALE WAS MUCH LARGER THAN 'wrapping encodings': 2016 OF 4096 (MB,SH) PAIRS -- 49% OF THE SPACE -- YIELDED AN ALL-ZERO MASK. ***  Enumerated, not estimated.  After the correction: ZERO.  And it is CONSERVATIVE -- all **2080** non-wrapping pairs are byte-identical to the old formula, and 2016 + 2080 = 4096, so the two sets partition the space exactly.  At the review's worked encoding (`MB=40, SH=40', Mstop = 23) the old mask is `0x0000000000000000' and the new one is `0xffffff0000ffffff'.

**THE PROSE THAT CAUSED IT IS NAMED IN THE NEW DOCSTRING**, because a wrong reason gets reused: the old code quoted `:29909' (*"1 bits from bit MB through bit 63 - SH"*), which is the NON-WRAPPING reading, and `:6879' is the definition that governs.  *Citing the prose beside a formula is how a reader is persuaded the formula matches it.*

*** `mask32' IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED, AND THAT IS RECORDED IN THE FILE ITSELF. ***  Its high-half behaviour is the live dispute in [[ppcrlwhighhalf]] -- the same manual asserts blanket upper-half clearing for rlwinm while its RTL and the `:6878' two-copies definition imply otherwise, and three further PowerPC manuals are unconsulted.  **Changing it would adopt one side of an unsettled reading INSIDE A TEST ORACLE**, which is the worst place to do it; the helper carries a docstring saying so and pointing at the row.

STILL OWED BEFORE EITHER PowerPC ROUND MEASURES ANYTHING: a witness ROW at a wrapping encoding that is RED on the committed build -- the order discriminator, so the correction cannot be mistaken for fitting an oracle to a repair.  **The correction above is a MODEL fix verified by enumeration against the manual's definition; no emulator was run.**

*** THE HOLD ON `mask32' IS LIFTED, SAME DAY: [[ppcrlwhighhalf]] IS RESOLVED AGAINST IT. ***  `mask32' was deliberately left wrong this morning because changing it would have adopted one side of an open dispute inside a test oracle.  **PowerPC Book I v2.01 -- the manual the 2005 PEM names as defining -- states `rlwinm` as `m <- MASK(MB+32, ME+32)` with MASK explicitly "wrapping if x > y", and whose only upper-half clearing sentence (`:4195-4196`) is SCOPED to the non-wrapping programming-note uses, never unconditional as the PEM's `:30065` is.**  So the wrapping reading is the architecture's, `mask32` must cover the high half when `mb > me`, and its docstring's deferral note is now superseded and must be rewritten rather than left standing.

*** BOTH CORRECTIONS VERIFIED AGAINST BOOK I, 2026-09-11 (ppcwitnessmaskoracle/codex_oraclecheck_20260911.txt, GPT-6 Astra at max, ZERO cyber flags): **PASS.** ***

*"Both corrections match Book I v2.01 for the stated input ranges and helper semantics.  The assertion and all reported counts hold."*

**WHAT WAS CHECKED, because a bare PASS is worth little:** that `mask_range` implements the architecture's `MASK` with both endpoints inclusive and the wrap in the right direction; that `b == e` yields exactly one bit; that `MASK(MB, 63-SH)` is right for `rldimi` and `(63 - sh) & 63` computes it for all SH; that `mask32(mb, me) = mask_range(mb+32, me+32)` is right for the word forms given `ROTL32`'s duplication; that there is no off-by-one in `mask_b_63`, `mask_0_e`, the `+32` offsets or the `& 63`; and that the partitions **2016 + 2080 = 4096** and **528 + 496 = 1024** hold when derived independently.

*** AND THE ASSERTION IS LEGITIMATE, WHICH WAS THE QUESTION I MOST NEEDED ANSWERED. ***  I made *"It is not possible to specify an all-zero mask"* an `assert` inside the helper.  **An assert built on a NON-normative sentence would fire on a legal encoding -- worse than the defect it replaced.**  It holds.

**SO THE PowerPC MEASUREMENT CAN PROCEED ON TRUSTWORTHY ORACLES.**  That was the point of asking before the build rather than after: the wrapping encodings are exactly where both repairs do their new work, so a wrong oracle would have produced numbers that were wrong in the same direction as the repair and LOOKED perfectly consistent.

*** 2026-09-11: THIS ROW NAMES ONLY THE ARTIFACT COPY.  THE LIVE PROBE IS AFFECTED TOO, AND ITS SECOND HELPER IS WRONG IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION -- WHICH WOULD SCORE CORRECT CODE **RED**. ***

The row cites `regress/artifacts/ppcrldiclzero/opus_ppc_rldicl_witness_20260910.py`.  The LIVE probe `regress/ppc_rldicl_probe.py` carries the same defect at `:158-171` and is named nowhere: `mask32()` is low-32-confined, `rotl32()` at `:150-155` correctly returns `(r32 << 32) | r32`, and `want_rlwinm` then ANDs the duplication away.  Remediation must touch the live probe, not only the artifact.

**AND `want_rlwimi` AT `:174-176` HAS THE IDENTICAL DEFECT WITH OPPOSITE POLARITY, WHICH NOBODY HAD NAMED.**  `m = mask32(mb, me)` is low-32-only, so `ra_val & (~m & M64)` preserves ALL of RA's high half -- which **contradicts the shipped, correct `rlwimi` fix** at `cpu_ppc_instr.c:2621-2622`, where a wrapping mask replaces the high half with the rotated word.

> **So a wrapping `rlwimi` row written against this oracle would score the CORRECT implementation as a FAILURE.**  That is the oracle-correction rule's hazard arriving from the dangerous side: not a detector that misses a defect, but one that manufactures a phantom regression against a fix this project has already measured and shipped.

MITIGATING, and it bounds the exposure rather than excusing it: both helpers are currently UNCALLED in the live probe, and `ppc_rldicl_probe.py` appears in NO gate (`regress/run.sh` GATES list).  **Forward exposure only** -- nothing green today rests on them.  That is why this is filed rather than repaired in-round.

Found by a harvest of unread seat answers, which is the third time this project has found a real defect in an answer nobody had opened.  *Two of the five answers harvested were ZERO BYTES with no quota or wall text -- lost answers, not walls: `wdcaltdigin/codex_impl_20260911.txt` (recovered by a retry that exists) and `ppcrlwhighhalf/codex_redesign_20260911.txt` (NOT recovered, no retry).*

*** 2026-09-11: MY CENTRAL PREMISE WAS FALSE, AND THE CORRECTION MAKES THE POSITION STRONGER. ***

I briefed a seat that the `rlwimi` fix is *"shipped, measured, correct"* and that this therefore INVERTS the oracle-correction rule -- code already right, only the oracle moving, so the order discriminator is unavailable.  **`git show HEAD:src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c` has neither repair.**  Both the `uint32_t tmp` cast and the `if (mb > me)` prologue are UNCOMMITTED working-tree edits, and both sibling rows are `in work`.

> **So the ordinary rule applies verbatim and is fully satisfiable: correct the oracle, measure HEAD RED under the new expectations, THEN land the code.**  No special case, no weakened discriminator.  *Asserting the inversion would have thrown away the strongest evidence available.*

**A THIRD WRONG HELPER, AND IT IS THE LARGEST.**  `want_rldimi` in the LIVE probe still computes `mask_b_63(mb) & mask_0_e((63-sh)&63)` -- the INTERSECTION -- where Book I `:4319` is `MASK(b, not n)`, which WRAPS.  **2016 of 4096 (MB,SH) pairs yield the all-zero mask Book I `:4031` declares impossible** (*"There is no way to specify an all-zero mask"*).  The witness copy was corrected 2026-09-10; the live probe never was.

**THE SHARPEST NUMBER IN THE WHOLE AUDIT:** old `want_rlwinm` agrees with the shipped `X(rlwinm)` on **131,072 of 131,072 cells** -- every source, every encoding.  It is not *usually* green against `ppcrlwhighhalf`; **it is INCAPABLE of red.**  That is this project's check-that-cannot-fail shape in its purest recorded form, and it sits in a test oracle.

THE DIFFERENTIAL, with the space corrected: `mask32`'s domain is **1024**, not 4096 -- MB and ME are 5-bit M-form fields (Book I `:4311-4313`).  *The 4096 I gave is `want_rldimi`'s (MB,SH) space transposed onto the wrong helper.*  Non-wrapping 528 pairs IDENTICAL under both (528/528, as required); wrapping 496 pairs DIFFER in exactly the high 32 bits (496/496).  The correction is precisely *add the high half, change nothing else*.

**A NINE-DAY FUSE, and it is the reason this is repaired now rather than filed:** `check_probe_wiring.py` grants this probe an exemption **expiring 2026-09-20**, and `grep -rn 'def mask32' regress/` now returns **TWO live definitions with opposite semantics** -- one committed and wrong, one untracked and right (`regress/ppc_rlwimi_probe.py:145-148`).  *That is not forward exposure; it is a live contradiction inside one directory with two rounds walking toward it.*  Mitigating and worth recording: the sibling rounds did NOT copy the broken helper -- they independently re-derived the right one three times.  **The trap did not spring by diligence, not by design.**

**REPAIR AS ITS OWN EARLIER COMMIT, NOT AS A RIDER ON EITHER SIBLING ROUND** -- and the reason is the order rule rather than tidiness: *the sibling rounds are the CONSUMERS of this oracle.  An author who corrects the oracle inside the round that consumes it destroys the order discriminator*, because oracle and row land in one commit and no reader can separate *derived from Book I* from *fitted to the repair I just wrote*.

**THE HONEST LIMIT, written down rather than glossed:** for `want_rlwimi` taken ALONE no measurement can distinguish a correct derivation from a fit, because the repair is correct and the corrected oracle agrees with it.  The distinguishing evidence is entirely (i) the SHARED `mask_range` helper -- correcting it simultaneously makes `want_rlwimi` agree with the repair AND makes `want_rlwinm` DISAGREE with shipped code on 47,616 of 131,072 cells (DERIVED by algebra over the enumeration, not an emulator measurement -- labelled 2026-10-09 per 7n-3), a red on a defect filed before this correction, in a handler nobody was fitting to -- and (ii) provenance: `mask_range` was written 2026-09-10 for `want_rldimi`, whose implementation is STILL WRONG [L4 2026-10-09, 7n-3: FALSE since 2026-09-12 -- rldimi was fixed by #527; the helper predates BOTH repairs, which is the stronger provenance], so the helper predates and outlives the repair it is accused of matching.  **A fitted oracle cannot produce a red on a sibling handler it was never fitted to.**

> **STRUCTURAL COROLLARY, not a remark: KEEP ONE MASK HELPER SHARED BY ALL FOUR `want_*`.**  The only way to fit `rlwimi` while staying green on `rlwinm` is to give the two instructions DIFFERENT masks -- which Book I gives identically at `:4127` and `:4317`.  A per-instruction split would be the tell and it would be visible in the diff.

*** CORRECTION 2026-09-11: "Book I's ONLY upper-half clearing sentence" IS FALSE.  **THERE ARE TWO.** ***

The second is at `ppc_uisa_book1_v201.txt:4291-4292`, in the **`rlwnm`** Programming Note (`:4265-4296`), and it is the same sentence: *"For all the uses given above, the high-order 32 bits of register RA are cleared."*  Its three enumerated uses are **also all non-wrapping**, so **the conclusion survives intact and is STRENGTHENED** -- the scoped-to-non-wrapping pattern now holds twice rather than once.

*This row was already corrected once for under-reading this exact span (`38040ac`: "Book I DOES have an upper-half clearing sentence, five lines past where I stopped reading").  The word ONLY is that overclaim's residue, and it is a fresh absence claim of the same kind -- an absence claim is only as good as the span you actually read.*

**AND THE DECIDING FACT NOBODY HAD STATED: Book I has NO clearing sentence for `rlwimi` AT ALL**, scoped or otherwise -- its entry (`:4304-4358`) is RTL only.  So the two oracles rest on different strengths of warrant and must not be recorded as one: `rlwimi` rests on RTL with no contrary text anywhere, while `rlwinm` must overcome the PEM's unconditional `:30065`.

**A SENTENCE THAT LOOKS LIKE A COUNTER-TEXT AND IS NOT, uncited anywhere in this project until now:** `:4033-4035`, *"the mask start and stop positions are always in the low-order 32 bits of the mask."*  A skeptic will reach for it to argue `mask32` should stay low-32-confined.  It speaks of the **start and stop POSITIONS** (`MB+32`, `ME+32`, which are indeed 32..63) and says nothing about where the mask's 1-BITS reach; `:4015` says the mask is 64 bits long and `:4026-4028` gives the wrap explicitly.  **Pre-empt it in the docstring** -- it is the strongest-looking objection and costs one sentence to disarm.

rows.title: cpu_ppc.c update_cr0(): the comparison width is chosen from the CPU MODEL width (cpu->cd.ppc.bits) rather than from the current operating mode, so a 64-bit CPU running with SF=0 records 64-bit condition bits
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-10 from the [[ppcrldimimask]] design review, which raised it as a limitation on its own repairs rather than as the thing it was asked about.  **Verified locally by opening the function.**

`update_cr0()' branches on `if (cpu->cd.ppc.bits == 64)' and compares `(int64_t)value', else `(int32_t)value'.  `cpu->cd.ppc.bits' is a property of the configured CPU MODEL and does not change while the guest runs.  The manual requires the comparison to follow the current MODE (`ppc_pem_32and64_2005.txt:6357'), which on a 64-bit implementation is selected by the MSR SF bit and CAN change at run time.

So on a 64-bit CPU executing in 32-bit mode, a record-form result whose low word is negative but whose full 64-bit value is positive records GT where the architecture requires LT.

**SCOPE IS THE WHOLE RECORD FORM, NOT ONE INSTRUCTION**: every `_dot' handler in the tree routes through this one function, which is why it is filed on its own rather than inside either PowerPC rotate row.  The seat's own statement of the consequence is the honest bound to carry forward: *those repairs do not establish correct record-form behaviour on a 64-bit CPU operating with SF=0.*

LOW because reachability is unestablished in the sharpest way: it needs a 64-bit PowerPC CPU running with SF clear, and this tree has no gate that executes ANY 64-bit PowerPC instruction and checks the result -- see [[wiringcliff]]. [2026-11-02, records: true when filed (6784f9bf, 2026-09-10); since #565 (8d038908, 2026-10-18) gate 13 runs ppc_rldicl_probe.py on -E bareppc -M 64 (PPC970) and checks its rows (gate_ppc.sh:182-183 at 987cb596), and the state_note records the 2026-10-02 re-grade from LOW to MED]  A round here owes the mode plumbing first, and should check whether `cpu->cd.ppc.bits' is consulted this way anywhere else.

*** CORRECTION 2026-09-11: **"EVERY `_dot` HANDLER IN THE TREE ROUTES THROUGH THIS ONE FUNCTION" IS FALSE**, and that sentence is this row's stated warrant for filing separately ("SCOPE IS THE WHOLE RECORD FORM"). ***

`cpu_ppc_instr.c:205-206`:

    #define FDOT(n) X(n ## _dot) { CHECK_FOR_FPU_EXCEPTION; \
            instr(n)(cpu,ic); update_cr1(cpu); }

`grep -c '^FDOT('` = **25 `_dot` handlers routing through `update_cr1()`**, not `update_cr0()`.  The real population is the 33 `DOT0`/`DOT1`/`DOT2` uses plus 6 explicit `update_cr0` call sites [corrected 2026-11-02, records: said 4; outside the DOT macros the calls are cpu_ppc_instr.c:280, :338, :2499, :2525, :2556 and :2632 at 599a7a82, which wrote this count (the last is :2655 at 987cb596)].

**The CODE is right** -- floating-point record forms SHOULD set CR1 -- and the defect itself is unaffected.  What is wrong is the SCOPE sentence, and it is wrong in the expensive direction: *a round scoping its work from that sentence would sweep in 25 handlers the defect cannot touch.*

rows.title: codexfarm.py writes its answer only after the call returns, so a MISSING answer file is its normal mid-run state -- the carrier's 'log missing => never started' discriminator reads that as dead and I destroyed a finished answer acting on it
rows.note:
MEASURED 2026-09-11, and it cost a completed 12,032-byte codex answer.

`codexfarm.py` calls `subprocess.run()`, which BLOCKS for the whole call, and writes its answer file only AFTERWARDS.  So for the entire run -- 6m41s here -- there is no answer file at all.

The carrier's discriminator is *log MISSING -> the command NEVER STARTED*.  **That rule is correct for a SHELL REDIRECT, which creates the file before it execs, and exactly wrong for a tool that writes at the end.**  I applied it to a codexfarm job, concluded the VME run had never started, and re-fired codex at the SAME output path with a `>` redirect -- which truncates at launch.  The finished answer was destroyed by its own replacement.

**TWO APPARATUS CHECKS, BOTH BLIND, BOTH FAILING IN THE SAME DIRECTION**, which is the stacked-error shape the carrier already names.  The process check that should have caught it is the one this project has ALREADY recorded as blind on this machine: git-bash `ps -ef` prints the executable path and no arguments, so `grep -c -i codex` returns 0 whether or not anything is running.  Nothing in the harness could have reported the truth, and the empty artifacts directory looked exactly like a launcher failure.

*The one signal that WAS available and that I did not consult: the background task had not yet notified.  The harness tracks `run_in_background` jobs and notifies on exit -- so 'has it finished?' was answerable without touching the filesystem at all.*

FIXED STRUCTURALLY, because *remember that codexfarm writes late* is exactly the prose this project has measured does not fire:
  1. a `<out>.RUNNING` sentinel written BEFORE the call and removed after the answer lands, so mid-run and never-started stop rendering the same;
  2. a REFUSAL to launch when a live sentinel or a NON-EMPTY answer already exists at the target path -- the duplicate-writer race becomes unavailable rather than discouraged.

NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS the same hour: a non-empty answer refuses and is left intact at its original byte count; a live sentinel refuses and names the owning pid; a CLEAN path is NOT refused (it proceeds to the brief read); and `CODEXFARM_FORCE=1` overrides both.  Escape hatch is deliberate -- a genuinely stale sentinel must not need an edit to clear.

SCOPE: the tool lives in the session scratchpad, not in `GXEMUL-SEC/tools/`, so nothing is owed to the repo for this.  Recorded because the DISCRIMINATOR is a carrier-level fact -- *a missing output file means 'never started' only for tools that create it at launch* -- and the carrier currently states the rule without that qualifier.

rows.title: landisk: SH7751R extended-INTC registers 0xfe080000 and 0xfe080040 are UNMAPPED, so six guest accesses per boot from intc_init and intpri_intr_priority reach no device at all
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-11 from the `landiskaux` boot census.  **MEASURED, not read.**

OpenBSD 7.6 on landisk touches **`0xfe080000` five times per boot** (from `intc_init`) and **`0xfe080040` once per boot** (from `intpri_intr_priority`).  Both are SH7751R **extended-INTC** registers, and **neither is claimed by any device in the constructed machine** -- so every one of those six accesses goes nowhere.

**WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the whole severity question:** whether the guest's interrupt priority configuration is thereby wrong, or whether the writes are redundant with the base INTC registers the model DOES implement.  *A write that lands nowhere and a write that lands nowhere AND MATTERS are different defects, and only the second earns a round.*  The census counts accesses; it does not test consequences.

FIRST STEP: read `dev_sh4.c`'s INTC handling and the SH7751R manual (`_scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt`) for what the extended block adds over the base one.  **The manual is present** -- do not reason about SH interrupt priority from the source alone, which this project did for four rounds on a false "there is no SH documentation" note.

Measured in `regress/artifacts/landiskaux/census_20260827/RESULTS.txt`, which prints an "ALL paddrs" section; the write-up there originally presented only the `0x14000000..0x14000040` window and **corrected itself** to name all five unmapped sites per boot.  *This row exists because that correction was made and then filed nowhere -- the addresses appeared in no ledger row until 2026-09-11.*

rows.title: landisk: board registers 0x10000003 (rtc_ce) and 0x10000005 (intr_init / extintr_establish) are UNMAPPED, so eight guest accesses per boot reach no device
rows.note:
FILED 2026-09-11 from the `landiskaux` boot census.  **MEASURED, not read.**

OpenBSD 7.6 on landisk touches **`0x10000003` five times per boot**, from **`rtc_ce`** -- the RTC chip-enable line -- and **`0x10000005` three times per boot**, from `intr_init` and `extintr_establish`.  **Neither address is claimed by any device in the constructed machine.**

*** THE RTC ONE IS THE INTERESTING HALF, AND IT IS A TESTABLE PREDICTION RATHER THAN A GUESS. ***  The machine DOES construct an `rs5c313` RTC at `0x110000000` (it appears in the debugger's device list).  **If `rtc_ce` is the chip-select the guest drives to talk to that RTC, then the RTC conversation is happening with the select line going nowhere** -- which either works by accident, because the model ignores chip-select, or does not work at all.  **Check which before assigning severity; both outcomes are informative and they differ by a lot.**

*Note `0x10000003` also appears in the `wdcstandby` row.  I have NOT established that the two are the same subject -- it may be an unrelated coincidence of a common constant -- and a future round should check rather than assume they are related.*

rows.title: a MODEL wall on the Agent tool is not a TRANSPORT outage: subagents on sonnet ran normally while opus and fable were both walled, and the carrier's shared-service note does not distinguish the two
rows.note:
MEASURED 2026-09-11, during a real double outage.

**Opus 5 hit a session limit** (`You have hit your session limit, resets 6:10am`, HTTP 429) and **killed four in-flight subagents at once**.  **Fable 5 was already walled** on its own quota, tested three times the same day.  Both are Anthropic seats **behind the same Agent-tool transport**, and both are compile-and-measure front ends -- which is the roster weakness the carrier records from `#462`.

*** BUT THE TRANSPORT WAS NEVER DOWN.  TWO SUBAGENTS LAUNCHED ON `model: sonnet` STARTED NORMALLY IN THE SAME MINUTE. ***

> **A MODEL WALL AND A TRANSPORT OUTAGE PRESENT IDENTICALLY -- an Agent call that fails -- AND THEY HAVE DIFFERENT REMEDIES.**  `#462`'s outage was `API Error: 529 Overloaded` on the PATH, and nothing could be done but wait.  A per-model rate limit leaves the path healthy and **the other models on it reachable**.

**THE DISCRIMINATOR IS IN THE ERROR TEXT AND COSTS NOTHING TO READ:** a `529 Overloaded` names no model and is the transport; a `429 rate_limit` naming `model sent to the API: claude-opus-5` is that MODEL only.  *The four dead subagents all carried the second form, and I read it as the roster losing its Agent capacity when it had lost two models out of four.*

**WHAT IS RECOVERABLE AND WHAT IS NOT, stated separately because they are not the same:**
  * **READING capacity is fully recoverable** -- a sonnet subagent has the same repo tools and can do records audits, source tracing and harvests, which is most of what the dead agents were doing.
  * **MEASURING capacity is NOT equivalent.**  The carrier's claim for Opus is that it is *the seat most likely to COMPILE AND MEASURE* -- a statement about judgement, not permission.  A sonnet subagent may build; whether its measurements carry the same weight is **not established here and must not be assumed.**  *Do not silently substitute it for a measuring seat and report the result as if the flagship had produced it -- that is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape wearing a model name.*

**OPERATIONAL RULE:** when an Agent call fails, **read which model the error names before concluding the transport is gone**, and try another model on the same path.  One invocation settles it, exactly as the wall rule already says for CLI seats.

*Recorded because the practical cost was real: for about ten minutes I treated subagent capacity as lost and stopped launching them, while the capability was available the whole time.  That is the same shape as the kimi substitute sitting unfired for days -- a seat answerable right now, on a different road, that nobody asked.*

*** FILED 2026-09-11.  **Named in `regress/artifacts/lcaisalane/RULING_20260910.md:72` as FILED, and nothing filed it** -- a contract that says FILED while nothing files it is false on arrival. ***

**THE MECHANISM.**  `dev_lca.c:280` is `relative_addr >>= 5`, which throws bits 4:0 away.  HRM `_scratchpad/21066_66a_hrm.txt:8850` (S6.2.6.1): *'Physical address bits <4:3> also specify transfer size'*, and `:9198-9199` (S6.2.8) confirms the I/O region *'supports all masked and unmasked transfers that are supported in sparse space.'*  **The model implements the BYTE row only -- 4 of the 11 legal encodings Table 6-3 enumerates at `:8857-8891`.**

*** A PANEL SEAT CALLED THIS A PHANTOM AND WAS REFUTED BY READING, which is why the refutation is recorded here rather than the claim: *** minimax argued *'the sparse window forces a<4:3> = 00'*.  The ruling refutes it -- **the window is registered `0x10000 << 5` bytes wide with NO alignment restriction**, so a guest LDL at `(0x3fd << 5) | (1 << 3)` (the HRM's WORD encoding) reaches the handler with the size bits already gone.

> **The guard at `:283` never fires on this path, so unlike its siblings this defect is SILENT AND TOTAL, and it is on the CANONICAL `LDL` path a real guest uses.**  *On reachability-by-a-real-guest it outranks the host-kill row it was found under, because that kill needs `ldbu`/`stb` -- BWX instructions a genuine EV4 guest never emits.*

**Disposition: member 7 (IMPLEMENT)** -- capture `(relative_addr >> 3) & 3` BEFORE the shift, transfer every enabled byte, pack lanes.  *Its own round: different semantic class from the refusal guard, different member, new oracles.*  Siblings: [[lcaisaphys]], [[lcaisaqword]].  Parent: [[lcaisalane]].

*** 2026-09-11 DESIGN (codex GPT-6 Astra at max).  **CONFIRMED, NARROWED -- 7/11 HOLDS, 'SILENT AND TOTAL' DOES NOT, AND IT LANDS AT MEDIUM TOO.** ***

*VERDICT: CONFIRMED, NARROWED -- 7/11 encodings request too few bytes, silently at canonical access widths.  MEDIUM pending evidence of guest use.*

**THE COUNT HOLDS: four encodings have the correct transfer width, seven are under-copied**, read off Table 6-3 at `21066_66a_hrm.txt:8857`.  *And the seat bounded even that: it is a statement about transfer size and lane handling CONDITIONAL ON SUCCESSFUL DOWNSTREAM ACCESS, and it does not certify the four BYTE cases end to end, because [[lcaisaphys]] sits under all of them.*

=== MY 'SILENT AND TOTAL' WAS TOO STRONG, IN A WAY WORTH KEEPING ===
*'The guard cannot detect it on the canonical path, but the handler is not universally silent, and actual guest use is not established by these files.'*  **So the SILENCE claim survives only where it was argued -- on the canonical `LDL` path -- and the TOTALITY claim does not.**

*** SEVERITY: MEDIUM, pending the same missing evidence that downgraded its sibling -- GUEST USE. ***  This row was already `med`, so no change is applied; what changes is that **the pass-1 seat's instruction to 'rank it above `lcaisasize`' is now MOOT** -- [[lcaisaphys]] came down to `med` on its retry and this one is confirmed at `med`.  **They are level, and they are level for the same reason: both are real defects whose reachability by an actual guest is unestablished.**  *I recorded earlier that this row 'plausibly outranks' its sibling; that was my inference from a partial answer and it is withdrawn -- the evidence puts them equal, not ordered.*

=== *** A VACUITY WARNING AT DESIGN TIME, which is the most valuable line in the answer *** ===
> *'For nonquadword accesses, both the OLD handler and a CORRECT handler can make exactly ONE nested call.  A detector that checks only CALL COUNT, SUCCESSFUL EXIT, or ABSENCE OF DIAGNOSTICS cannot establish this repair.'*

**That rules out three oracle shapes before a single row is written** -- and they are the three a detector for this row would naturally reach for.  *The channel must be the DATA transferred or the transaction trace, not the fact that a transfer happened.*

**Two non-vacuity checks the seat ran in its own model and reports as passing:** restoring the old read tail changed **only returned data**; replacing proper-width transfers with byte calls changed **only the transaction trace** for an ordinary memory mock.  *Both are arithmetic/model checks, not emulator runs, and are labelled as such.*

**STATUS: specified, MEDIUM, and its detector's admissible channels are now bounded.**  Landing held by owner ruling; nothing in this row is committed.

rows.title: dev_lca.c DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_isa): for the QUADWORD encoding a<6:5> is NOT ad<1:0>, so a quadword I/O access to port P is forwarded to port P+3 -- an ADDRESSING defect, and a fix for the width defect does not imply a fix for this
rows.witness: none -- filed from a pass-1 panel finding; the rung-3 attempt is owed.
rows.note:
*** FILED 2026-09-11 to give a homeless finding a carrier.  **Named by the `lcaisalane` pass-1 panel and by the Opus seat as needing SEPARATE filing, and never filed.** ***

**THE SEAT'S REASON FOR SEPARATING IT** (`regress/artifacts/lcaisalane/opus_pass1_20260910.md:77-79`): a separate row *'because it is an addressing defect, not a width defect, and a fix for the first does not imply a fix for the second.'*

**THE MECHANISM.**  `((port << 5) | 0x78) >> 5` = `port | 3`, so the access lands three ports high.

*** THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THE MANUAL'S PROSE AND ITS TABLE DISAGREE, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE FINDING. ***  `21066_66a_hrm.txt:9192-9193` (S6.2.8) states flatly that *'PCI address bits ad<1:0> come directly from physical address bits a<6:5>'*.  **But Table 6-3 at `:8884` reads `11 11 Quadword 0000 00 00 Unmasked` -- `a<6:5> = 11` with I/O `ad<1:0> = 00`.**

**The table is taken, on two grounds:** it is the more specific statement, and its own footnote at `:8888` corroborates it (*'ad2 is 0 for the first longword and 1 for the second longword of the quadword'* -- `ad<1:0>` is `00` throughout).

*** AND THE READING IS CALIBRATED RATHER THAN TRUSTED, which this project requires of any extracted table: *** the `c_be_l` column is vertically compressed, so it was calibrated on **two independent columns STRADDLING the block** rather than one point -- the `a<6:5>` -> `ad<1:0>` pairs run `00->00, 01->01, 10->10, 11->11` on the same lines, and the byte enables read `1110, 1101, 1011, 0111` = lanes 0,1,2,3 in order, with the word and tribyte blocks agreeing.  *A single calibration point is only valid for a UNIFORM stagger and you cannot tell which kind you have from one point.*

Collides with `IOC_HAE`, which the model ignores entirely.  Siblings: [[lcaisaphys]], [[lcaisasize]].  Parent: [[lcaisalane]].

rows.title: fread_helper()'s in-place zero-fill can be narrowed by a FITTED THRESHOLD on totallenread and NO FINITE ROW SET CLOSES THE CLASS -- filed by #488 as a class, and the bug file has carried it since 2026-08-27 with no ledger row
rows.witness: none -- documented-only.  A CLASS filing, not an escape: what would close it is a different KIND of oracle, and nobody has designed one.
rows.note:
*** FILED 2026-09-11.  **`OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md:611` has carried this entry since 2026-08-27 and there was NO LEDGER ROW** -- so the machine source of truth did not know it existed. ***

*** THIS IS THE `es438`/`lunafuse` SHAPE RECURRING, AND `check_bugfile_sync.py` RECORDS THAT SHAPE IN ITS OWN HEADER. ***  `:13-15` reads *'filed in OUTSTANDING_BUGS and given no ledger row -- so the fix reproduced the defect one layer in'*.  **The gate checks ledger -> bug file and nothing checks bug file -> ledger**, which is precisely the direction this needed.  *The bug-file entry even names the class it is an instance of.*

**THE CONTENT, quoted from the entry rather than paraphrased:** `fread_helper()`'s in-place zero-fill can be narrowed by a fitted threshold on `totallenread` (`&& totallenread < 1024`).  `#488`'s ROW S kills the `< 1024` INSTANCE by shorting twice in one call, with the second short landing at exactly `totallenread == 1024` -- **but `< 2048` escapes, and so on up.  The ladder's limit is the fix itself.**

> **Filed as a CLASS rather than as an escape, deliberately.  Chasing it row by row is the unbounded fix-of-fix shape this project has already paid for once.**  What would close it is a different KIND of oracle -- one asserting the fill happened on EVERY short rather than at enumerated positions -- and nobody has designed one.

*The id currently appears in `ledger.json` only inside the prose note of the CLOSED row [[shortread]].  Found by an Opus audit of the sync gate; the entry text above is the bug file's, unedited.*

*** AND THE SAME PASS CORRECTED ITSELF TWICE, both worth recording because both are classes this project already names: *** its first wording claimed the string `SM_COVERED` appears nowhere else -- **false**, it occurs in several rows -- rewritten to claim only what was measured (the PROPOSAL is unique); and a `grep -c $'\r'` reporting CRLF matched **every line under MSYS**, a vacuous pattern on a check about vacuity, refuted by a raw byte check showing the file was LF-only before and after.  *A correction is not safer than the thing it corrects.*

rows.title: cpu_arm_instr.c: the netbsd_memset and netbsd_memcpy COMBINED handlers replace LDM/STM outright and copy through raw `& 0xfff` page offsets, bypassing the generic BDT helpers entirely -- so #524's word-rounding does not reach them, and netbsd_memcpy uses TWO DIFFERENT address rules in one handler
rows.witness: none -- filed from [[armbdt]]'s pass 2.  The rung-3 fixture for the generic helpers already exists (regress/artifacts/armbdt/agy_armbdt_witness_20260911.py, unmodified `testarm`); reaching a COMBINED handler additionally requires driving the instruction pattern its matcher recognises, which is not yet attempted.
rows.note:
*** FILED 2026-09-11 by [[armbdt]]'s pass 2, which refuted that round's 'only two sites' premise. ***

**`#524` masks the two `memory_rw` calls in the generic `arm_pop()`/`arm_push()` helpers.  These two handlers never reach those calls** -- they are combined-instruction replacements that do the transfer themselves:

  * **`netbsd_memset`** (`:2093`, replaces STM): `memset(page + (addr & 0xfff), 0, 128);` at `:2127`.  **Raw page offset, no word rounding.**  Its guards check page bounds, zero source values and page availability -- *none rejects an unaligned address.*
  * **`netbsd_memcpy`** (`:2274`, replaces LDM/STM): `memcpy(page_0 + (addr_r0 & 0xfff), page_1 + (addr_r1 & 0xfff), 32);` -- **raw offsets on BOTH source and destination**, *while its register-publication reads use `& 0xffc`.*

> *** THE SHARPEST PART IS THE INTERNAL DISAGREEMENT: `netbsd_memcpy` ROUNDS THE ADDRESS IT PUBLISHES TO REGISTERS AND DOES NOT ROUND THE ADDRESS IT COPIES FROM.  One handler, two address rules. ***

**Their matchers (`:3428`) recognise instruction patterns without establishing address alignment**, so an unaligned base reaches the combined body with nothing in the way.

*The file already half-knows: `netbsd_memcpy`'s own comment at `:2252` acknowledges 'the overlap and unaligned-copy divergences'.  **The knowledge was present and the rounding was not** -- which is this project's recurring shape of a fact living where nobody consults it at edit time.*

**PRE-EXISTING, not a regression of `#524`** -- filed under the stopping rule rather than repaired in-round, because it is neither a measured false pass against `#524`'s detector nor a wrong record in it.  **But it bounds what that round may claim: the generic helpers are closed, the BDT ACCESS RULE is not.**

*Every quote above was re-read from the file here before filing, not taken from the seat's report.*

rows.title: a kill-table driver took its baseline from the MUTABLE working tree while a comment claimed it verified the commit, and its HEAD leg is the ONE leg with no presence pin -- so a re-run today silently measures the FIXED file and labels it HEAD
rows.witness: harness:the driver's own text -- `killtable.sh:15-18` and `mutate_armbdt.py:46-48`, plus a grep showing the mutator's anchor text now occurs ZERO times in the tree it would read.
rows.note:
*** FILED 2026-09-11, found by the GROK seat on the `#524`/`#525` panel and verified here line by line before filing. ***

**`regress/artifacts/armbdt/killtable_20260911/killtable.sh` reads:**

    15: # Verify SEC cpu_arm_instr.c matches pure HEAD commit 8d372aa
    16: git -C "$SEC_DIR" log --oneline -1
    17: # Save head file
    18: cp "$SEC_DIR/src/cpus/cpu_arm_instr.c" "$HEAD_FILE"

> *** THE COMMENT SAYS *VERIFY*.  LINE 16 PRINTS A COMMIT AND GATES ON NOTHING.  LINE 18 THEN COPIES FROM THE **WORKING TREE**, WHICH IS A MOVING REFERENCE. ***

**This is [[makercfalse]]'s defect in a different script, found the same day** -- *a build that FAILED reported MAKE_RC=0 because the script captured the right number and acted on none of it.*  Here the script prints the right commit and compares it to nothing.

=== WHY IT DID NOT BITE, AND WHY IT WOULD NOW ===
When the table ran (~06:45) the working tree was PRE-FIX, so the copy genuinely was HEAD and **the measurement is valid**.  `#524` landed in the tree at ~10:1x.  **Re-running the identical script today would:**
  * copy the **FIXED** file as `$HEAD_FILE`;
  * **`M_NULL_EFFECT`-style legs fail LOUDLY** -- `mutate_armbdt.py` exits 1 on MUTANT-TEXT-NOT-FOUND at `:50`, `:62`, `:67`, and the anchor `if (!cpu->memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem, addr, data,` now occurs **ZERO times** in the tree (measured);
  * *** but the **HEAD** leg is `pass` at `:46-48` with the comment `# Verbatim pre-fix HEAD` and **NO TEXT CHECK AT ALL** -- so it would measure the FIXED code and label it HEAD. ***

> **THE ONE LEG WITHOUT A PRESENCE PIN IS THE ONE THAT WOULD LIE.**  Every mutant leg is protected by its find-text acting as a presence pin -- which is the property this project already praises -- and the BASELINE leg, which asserts nothing, is unprotected.  *A driver that treats MUTANT-TEXT-NOT-FOUND as a FAIL pins every feature it edits, and pins nothing about the file it starts from.*

**AND THE RULE WAS IN THE BRIEF.**  The measuring seat's own brief said, verbatim: *'NAME THE BASELINE BY COMMIT, never by a moving reference: a `git show HEAD:` baseline here once advanced past the fix and produced a pre-fix leg scoring identical to BASE.'*  **It was given, and the script used `cp` from the working tree anyway.**  *This file's own structure-first finding, again: knowing a rule and having it fire on the right object are different problems.*

**THE REPAIR IS TWO LINES AND IT IS NOT A NEW RULE:** take the baseline with `git -C "$SEC_DIR" show <commit>:src/... > "$HEAD_FILE"`, and give the HEAD leg a presence pin of its own so it refuses a file that does not match the baseline it names.  **Filed, not fixed:** changing a kill-table driver owes negative controls in both directions, and landing is held by owner ruling.

*Scope note: this is a per-round artifact driver, not a committed gate, so nothing in the harness reads it today.  It is filed as a CLASS because the next round copies the last round's driver.*

*** 2026-09-11 FABLE 5 ADJUDICATION (`FABLE_ADJ_20260911`).  **SEAT ALIVE -- token AND a verbatim `CHECKPOINT.md` HEAD quote returned, and it re-ran `git log --oneline -1` itself to confirm the checkpoint is not stale.**  Fired ONLY after all seven other scriptable seats had spoken, per owner sequencing, and via a subagent rather than Opus. ***

*** PROMOTED FROM FILED DEBT TO **THE FIRST STEP OF THE NEXT ROUND**. ***

**It stops being a filed item because `#524`'s clause-(d) repair FORCES A RE-TABLE, and the tree now holds the fix** -- so the very next kill-table run is the one that would copy the FIXED file as its baseline and score it 25/25 as HEAD.

**The adjudicator independently verified all three defects** (`killtable.sh:16` gates nothing, `:18` copies from the working tree, `mutate_armbdt.py:46-47` HEAD leg has no presence check) and prescribed the repair: **`git show 8d372aa:src/cpus/cpu_arm_instr.c > $HEAD_FILE`, and pin the HEAD leg on the unmasked `memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem, addr, data,` text occurring EXACTLY TWICE.**  *Five lines.*

*A presence pin that counts occurrences is stronger than one that merely finds the text: it also catches a file where one site was fixed and the other was not.*

rows.title: a probe's read_mem32() indexed dump columns by 16-byte offset while ISSUING an unaligned dump -- the line label still matched, the leading groups were blank-padded, and split() shifted every index so it silently returned a NEIGHBOURING word
rows.witness: harness:measured directly -- `dump 0x21000 0x21008` renders `0x00021000  00000000 44332211` while `dump 0x21004 0x2100c` renders `0x00021000           44332211 00000000`, same label, shifted columns.
rows.note:
*** FILED 2026-09-11 from [[armbdt]]'s table 4, where it made the FIX look broken. ***

**THE SHAPE.**  `read_mem32(addr)` dumped from `addr`, searched for the line labelled `(addr & ~0xF)`, then indexed `line[12:48].split()` by `(addr & 0xF) // 4`.  **The label matches whether or not the dump start is aligned** -- so every sanity check that looked for the right line passed -- **but an unaligned start BLANK-PADS the leading word groups, `.split()` collapses the padding, and every index shifts by the number of omitted groups.**

**MEASURED COST: 8 of 10 kill-table legs changed value when it was repaired**, including the pre-fix `HEAD` leg, and it made a CORRECT fix report a red BASE row.  *It cost four rounds of inference before anyone dumped the memory and looked.*

> **THE GENERAL FORM IS THIS PROJECT'S PADDED-COLUMN TRAP IN A NEW PLACE: the ROW was found and the COLUMN was wrong.**  A checker that verifies it located the right line learns nothing about whether it read the right field, and positional parsing of a human-formatted dump has no way to tell the difference.

**REPAIR (applied in `armbdt`'s probe): dump from `(addr & ~0xF)` for 16 bytes, so all four groups are always present -- which is what the index arithmetic already assumed.  One line.**

*Filed as a CLASS rather than closed with that round: any future probe that parses `dump` positionally inherits it, and the next probe is usually copied from the last one.*  **Censused: no other probe in the tree shares the shape today** (`grep -rln 'offset_in_16' regress/`), so the population is one and this row exists to keep it there.

rows.title: regress/ carries TWO INCOMPATIBLE PROBE-EXIT IDIOMS -- 26 probes key their exit status on the pass tally and 41 always exit 0 with failed rows -- and nothing tells a gate author which idiom the probe they are wiring follows
rows.note:
*** MEASURED 2026-09-11, AND THE MEASUREMENT REFRAMED THE ROW. I FILED THIS AN HOUR AGO AS A
SINGLE-FILE DEFECT WITH AN UNMEASURED POPULATION; THE CENSUS SAYS THE POPULATION IS 41 AND THAT
EXITING 0 IS THE HOUSE IDIOM, NOT THE DEFECT. ***

Raised by the GPT-6 Astra seat (unasked) about `ppc_rldicl_probe.py': *"prints `SCORE', `FAILING',
and its token without setting a failure exit status. Normal execution therefore exits successfully
even with failed assertions."*  **That reading is CORRECT** -- its only `sys.exit(2)' is an
apparatus guard at `:89', not a failed-row path.  Cited: 
regress/artifacts/ppcrlwimiwidth/codex_detector_20260911.txt

THE DERIVER (run it; do not quote the numbers), against the WORKING TREE 2026-09-11:
  for each regress/*_probe.py that prints a SCORE or _RESULT tally, take the text FROM the tally
  onward and ask whether any `sys.exit'/`raise SystemExit' in it carries a nonzero status.

    probes printing a SCORE/_RESULT tally : 67
    exit status KEYED on the tally        : 26
    exit ALWAYS 0 despite failed rows     : 41

*** MY FIRST DERIVER RETURNED **3**, AND IT WAS WRONG FOR THE EXACT REASON THIS ROW'S OWN CLOSING
PARAGRAPH WARNED AGAINST. ***  It asked *"does the file contain a nonzero `sys.exit' anywhere?"* --
a CORRELATE -- so `ppc_rldicl_probe.py' scored CLEAN on the strength of its apparatus guard, and
the subject of the finding was excluded from the census of the finding.  **Keyed on what defines
the class -- an exit keyed on the tally, searched only AFTER the tally is computed -- the answer is
41.  Wrong by 13x.**  *The row telling the next person not to key on a correlate was filed with a
count derived from a correlate.*

**SO THE DEFECT IS NOT THE 41. IT IS THE SPLIT.**  The house idiom in this tree is that a probe
PRINTS result lines and the GATE greps them -- which is why no gate has ever been misled, and why
41 probes exiting 0 has cost nothing.  But 26 probes do the opposite, several with the identical
`sys.exit(0 if ok == len(rows) else 1)' shape.  **A gate author who has read those 26 reasonably
concludes that exit status is a supported channel, and wiring any of the 41 that way yields a check
that CANNOT FAIL** -- green whether or not every assertion failed.  That is the dangerous direction:
it reassures.

*** THE HOUSE IDIOM DOES NOT MERELY AVOID THE EXIT-STATUS CHANNEL -- IT **REFUSES** IT IN WRITING,
AND I ONLY FOUND THAT BY OPENING THE GATES AFTER RECORDING `verified' FROM MEMORY. ***

    gate_arm.sh:672          python3 arm_bdt_probe.py "$PMAX" > "$BDTLOG" 2>&1 || true
    gate_arm.sh:674          if ! grep -q "ARMBDT_RESULT=" "$BDTLOG"; then        <- PARSE BEFORE SCORE
    gate_arm.sh:687          check "bdt rows run"     "$bwant" 32                 <- denominator pinned
    gate_arm.sh:688          check "bdt rows correct" "$bgot"  "$bwant"

    gate_sh_rounding.sh:1457 python3 -u wdc_altdigin_probe.py ... > "$ADLOG" 2>&1 || true
    gate_sh_rounding.sh:1459 if ! grep -q "WDC_ALTDIGIN_RESULT=" "$ADLOG"; then
    gate_sh_rounding.sh:1485 check "wdc_altdigin rows run"     "${adres#*/}" 16
    gate_sh_rounding.sh:1486 check "wdc_altdigin rows correct" "${adres%/*}" "${adres#*/}"

**`|| true` is a DELIBERATE discard of rc, and the `grep -q ..._RESULT=` guard is what catches a
probe that crashed or printed nothing** -- so absence reds and a malformed result line cannot reach
an empty-variable `check "" ""` that would pass.  Both halves are present in both gates.

*That is the strongest available evidence for repair (1) below: the tree has already CHOSEN the
result-line channel, twice, explicitly.  The 41 probes that exit 0 are not 41 latent defects -- they
are 41 probes following the channel the gates actually read.  The 26 that key exit on the tally are
the ones carrying an idiom no gate consumes.*

NOT A LIVE DEFECT TODAY, verified: `arm_bdt_probe.py' and `wdc_altdigin_probe.py' are both in the
41, and both of their gate sections grep RESULT LINES with pinned denominators (`bdt rows run' 32,
`wdc_altdigin rows run' 16) rather than testing rc.  See [[armbdt]] and [[wdcaltdigin]].

DISPOSITION QUESTION, unresolved and put to the adjudicating seat as Q-G2: `ppc_rldicl_probe.py'
belongs to the CLOSED `#522', so a change there is an L4 in a closed round, a MEASURED FALSE PASS
(L2, follow-up commit), or a new filed row -- the late-dissent rule gives exactly those three.

THE REPAIR IS NOT `fix 41 probes'.  A sweep of that size is the `#392' shape and would be switched
off.  The cheap forms, in order of cost: **(1)** every NEW gate section greps result lines, never
rc -- which is already the practice; **(2)** a probe whose exit is keyed says so in its header, so
a reader can tell the idioms apart; **(3)** forward-only, a new probe picks ONE idiom and the
round that adds it says which.  See [[ppcprobescorestale]], same file.

rows.title: gate_ppc.sh requires a NetBSD image before it launches its probe, so a missing image turns integer-instruction coverage into a gate_skip -- silent coverage loss scored as SKIP
rows.note:
*** FILED 2026-09-11 by the GPT-6 Astra seat, unasked. *** Cited: regress/artifacts/ppcrlwimiwidth/codex_detector_20260911.txt

*"`gate_ppc.sh' requires a NetBSD image before launching its current probe. The bareppc integer
groups must run independently of that prerequisite -- through a separately invoked gate, or through
restructuring that prevents the image check from skipping them."*

**This is the documented `gate_skip' class: coverage that disappears without reddening anything.**
The tree already has a measured instance -- `gate_build.sh' withdraws `/tmp/gxsec-gxemul' at gate
start and `gate_mips.sh' `need_exec's it, so concurrent runs make gate 4 skip on a missing binary.

**LIVE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TWO HELD POWERPC ROUNDS:** the rldimi and rlwimi detectors are
bareppc-only -- register-to-register instructions observed through the cold debugger, needing no
guest OS and no image at all.  **Wiring them behind this gate's image prerequisite would couple a
detector that needs no image to an image that may be absent**, and the failure renders as SKIP
rather than as red.  See [[ppcrldimimask]] and [[ppcrlwimiwidth]].

rows.title: regress/ppc_rldicl_probe.py: its row-count comments say 19 while it makes 24 row calls, and `naive fix wrong' contributes to SCORE despite being documented carried-not-counted
rows.note:
*** FILED 2026-09-11 by the GPT-6 Astra seat, unasked. *** Cited: regress/artifacts/ppcrlwimiwidth/codex_detector_20260911.txt

*"That is **24 row calls**, with census cells aggregated into rows. The comments claiming 19 rows
are stale. Also, `naive fix wrong' still contributes to `SCORE' through `row()', despite its
'carried-not-counted' description."*

Two defects of one family and both are the FROZEN-NUMBER class this project keeps paying for:
a count transcribed into a comment and outlived by the code, and a row whose prose says it is
excluded from the score while the code includes it.

**THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT CAN MISLEAD A MEASUREMENT**, not merely a reader: a denominator that
silently includes a row the record says is excluded makes every `n/N' from this probe ambiguous
between two N.  Any kill table citing this probe's scores inherits that ambiguity.  **The repair is
to make the code and the prose agree, in whichever direction the round that owns it decides -- and
to pin the denominator with a `check' row against a literal, which is the idiom the gates already
use.**

LOW because no shipped decision is known to rest on it; filed because [[probeexitzero]] is in the
same file and a round touching one should close both.

rows.title: a probe row that tests a SLOW-PATH fix with a MULTI-ACCESS instruction is vacuous from the second access onward -- the first cold access WARMS the page and every later access takes the FAST path, so the row cannot observe a slow-path mutant at all
rows.note:
*** MEASURED 2026-09-11 by the kimi seat on `#524` pass D, and INDEPENDENTLY SUSPECTED by glm from
the same table without knowing the cause. ***  Cited: `_scratchpad/panel_20260911_193940/kimi.txt`
and `ollama_glm.txt`.

`#524` fixes the SLOW path of `arm_pop`/`arm_push` (the fast path already masked the address).  A
closure row was built as `LDMIA r0!,{r1,r2}` from a cold page at residue 2, asserting BOTH loaded
registers -- one leg, three assertions, deliberately cheap.

**THE SECOND ASSERTION CANNOT FAIL.**  The first access misses and goes through the slow path,
which is what the row is for -- *and in doing so it WARMS THE PAGE*.  The second register's access
then takes the FAST path, which the fix does not touch and a slow-path mutant does not alter.
kimi demonstrated it with a mutant that deviates at the second access and still left that row
GREEN; glm reached the same place from the other end, calling the published kill table
*"internally impossible as stated"* because a row it expected to red did not.

**IT IS THE CHANNEL CHECK'S OWN SHAPE -- *a row whose named channel cannot vary under its named
mutant is vacuous BY CONSTRUCTION* -- and it is knowable at WRITING time**, which is the point of
that check.  I missed it because I reasoned about the ARITHMETIC of the second access (which is
genuinely different) and not about WHICH PATH SERVICES IT.

*** WHY IT IS A CLASS AND NOT A ONE-OFF: the cheap way to get more assertions per session is to
load or store MORE REGISTERS, and that is exactly the edit that silently moves every assertion
after the first onto the fast path. ***  Any round fixing a slow path -- and this tree has several
-- will find the same bargain attractive and inherit the same vacuity.

**THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS: a row testing a SLOW-PATH repair must drive ONE access per cold page.**
More assertions mean more sessions, not more registers.  Where a multi-register transfer is wanted
for its own sake (register-list-length coverage), its later assertions are FAST-path observations
and must be labelled as such rather than counted as slow-path coverage.

CENSUS OWED, and it must key on what DEFINES the class rather than a correlate: not *"does the
probe use a multi-register instruction"* but *"does an assertion after the first in one session
claim to observe a SLOW-PATH property"*.  See [[armbdt]], [[probereadalign]].

rows.title: A READ of PCI ADDR (0xcf8) decomposes idata=0 and clobbers the latched address -- in ALL THREE PCI bridges, so an upstream idiom rather than a macepci bug
rows.state_note: filed 2026-09-17 while triaging macepciwidth severity; LATENT, NO WITNESS and none attempted; a CLASS across three files, fix all or none

entries.grader: main-loop (Opus 5), by reading the three handlers and bus_pci_data_access
entries.ev: src/devices/dev_sgi_ip32.c DEVICE_ACCESS(macepci) case 0xcf8; src/devices/dev_cpc700.c case 0; src/devices/dev_eagle.c case 0; src/devices/bus_pci.c bus_pci_data_access
entries.note: A READ of the PCI ADDR register runs the WRITE path.  idata is declared = 0 and assigned ONLY inside if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE), and the 0xcf8 arm tests writeflag NOWHERE -- so a read decomposes ZERO, latches bus 0 / device 0 / function 0 / register 0, and returns 0.  It both answers wrongly and CLOBBERS the address a previous write latched.  *** THE SIBLING CENSUS IS THE FINDING AND IT REVERSES THE OBVIOUS READING. ***  This looked like a macepci outlier; it is not.  ALL THREE PCI bridges in the tree share the shape -- dev_sgi_ip32.c (macepci, case 0xcf8), dev_cpc700.c (cpc700_pci, case 0) and dev_eagle.c (eagle, case 0) -- so it is an UPSTREAM IDIOM rather than damage this fork did, and a round fixing macepci alone would leave the class open in two files while making the tree inconsistent.  The fix lands in all three or in none.  LOW because the damage needs a guest that READS 0xcf8 between writing it and reading 0xcfc; the common driver idiom is write-ADDR then read-DATA, which never touches this path.  NO WITNESS EXISTS AND NONE WAS ATTEMPTED -- recorded as not-yet-attempted rather than as absence, because those are different states.  Found while triaging macepciwidth's SEVERITY, not while looking for it.  *** AND THE TRIAGE ITSELF CAME BACK NEGATIVE, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF OF THIS ENTRY: macepciwidth STAYS MED. ***  Its len != 4 fall-through is NOT memory-unsafe, now CHECKED rather than assumed -- memory_readmax64 and memory_writemax64 are both bounded by len, the only array index reachable through bus_pci_data_access is masked (cfg_base[ofs & (PCI_CFG_MEM_SIZE - 1)]), and config writes go through the dev->cfg_reg_write callback rather than a direct index.  The cost is an unlatched flood plus wrong-value semantics, which is correctness and not memory safety.  The macepciwidth entry's phrase 'the sibling is WORSE' is true of the DECLINE BEHAVIOUR and FALSE of severity; recorded so a future round does not read it as grounds to escalate.

rows.title: dev_8253.c one-byte formats: BOTH arms keep the other byte stale against the datasheet, and the LSB arm additionally installs no timer -- wrong host rate on counter 0
rows.state_note: filed 2026-09-17 by the kimi-k3 seat, WIDENED the same day by Fable 5.1's adjudication from a datasheet passage I read past

entries.grader: main-loop (Opus 5) verified the seat's claim by reading dev_8253.c
entries.note: A counter programmed in LSB-ONLY mode (RW=01) is SILENTLY DEAD: the LSB arm updates counter[] and nothing else -- no hz[] recompute, no timer_add, no timer_update_frequency, and no diagnostic -- while the MSB arm does all three.  RW=01 is a LEGITIMATE 8253 mode (I8253_TIMER_LSB 0x10), so this is not a refusal decision: the model implements one half of a two-half register and not the other.  It is option-set member 7 (IMPLEMENT), not a latch question.  TWO consequences and the second is arguably worse: a counter programmed LSB-only never starts, silently, and for counter 0 that is the interrupt source; and if a timer was ALREADY installed by an earlier MSB write, a later LSB-only write changes counter[] while the running timer keeps the OLD frequency, so recorded counter and actual rate DIVERGE with no diagnostic.  *** FOUND BY A PACKET-FED SEAT (kimi-k3:cloud) FROM THE INLINED FUNCTION ALONE, while answering a brief about the flood. ***  Verified by reading before filing; the seat's claim was exact.  The design question -- should the LSB arm install the timer by symmetry, or does the real 8253 defer until both halves are written in 16-bit mode -- is a DATASHEET question, and _scratchpad/i8254.pdf and i8254.txt are present locally, so it is answerable without guessing.  Caution for the row author: an MSB write to counter 0 calls timer_add with hz = 1193182/counter, so a SMALL counter installs a HIGH-FREQUENCY host timer; keep it large.

entries.grader: main-loop (Opus 5), by reading the datasheet text
entries.note: PRIMARY SOURCE MAKES THIS WORSE THAN FILED.  _scratchpad/i8254.txt :219 lists RW1 RW0 = 0 1 as 'Read Write least significant byte only', a first-class mode beside MSB-only and 16-bit.  And :528 states the conventions for ALL mode timing diagrams: 'Counters are programmed for binary (not BCD) counting and for reading writing least significant byte (LSB) only'.  *** EVERY MODE TIMING DIAGRAM IN THE INTEL DATASHEET IS DRAWN IN LSB-ONLY MODE. ***  It is the manufacturer's canonical illustration case, not an exotic corner -- and it is the one programming mode in which this model never starts a timer.

entries.grader: main-loop (Opus 5) verified Fable's citation and both masks by reading
entries.note: *** THIS ROW WAS UNDER-SCOPED AND THE DATASHEET QUESTION IT FILED AS OPEN IS ANSWERED LOCALLY. ***  Fable found the governing sentence at _scratchpad/i8254.txt:168-172: 'CRM and CRL are cleared when the Counter is programmed.  In this way if the Counter has been programmed for one byte counts (either most significant byte only or least significant byte only) the other byte will be zero.'  THE MODEL DOES THE OPPOSITE IN BOTH ONE-BYTE ARMS -- :175 masks with 0xff00 and keeps a STALE MSB, :179 masks with 0x00ff and keeps a STALE LSB -- where the datasheet requires the other byte to be ZERO.  So the defect is not only 'the LSB arm starts no timer': THE COMPOSED COUNT IS WRONG IN BOTH ARMS, and the MSB-only arm is the one that DOES compute hz and call timer_add/timer_update_frequency, so a stale low byte yields a WRONG HOST TIMER RATE ON COUNTER 0 -- the same consequence as pit8253bcdbinary, reached by a different route.  Severity raised MED -> MED-HIGH accordingly: the original filing described the weaker half.  The datasheet also names the FIX SHAPE rather than leaving it to design: clear counter[sel] at the CONTROL WORD (dev_8253.c:310-312), which is exactly where the datasheet says the CR is cleared.  *** I HAD READ THIS DATASHEET AN HOUR EARLIER, FOR THIS ROW, AND WALKED PAST THE PASSAGE. ***  I grepped for 'BCD' and read the hits; the CR-clearing rule is 500 lines away and mentions neither BCD nor LSB in terms my grep matched.  A targeted grep over a primary source answers the question you asked it, not the question you should have asked.

rows.title: dev_8253.c accepts a BCD control word then reads the count as BINARY -- a BCD counter runs at the wrong rate, and for counter 0 that is the host timer (~4x)
rows.state_note: filed 2026-09-17 from pit8253flood pass 1; LIVE and guest-visible.  Severity corrected MED-HIGH -> MED by Fable 5.1 on REACH: no real-guest driver found.

entries.grader: main-loop (Opus 5) verified every element by reading dev_8253.c and i8253reg.h
entries.note: THE 8253 ACCEPTS A BCD CONTROL WORD AND THEN INTERPRETS THE COUNT AS BINARY.  Verified by reading before filing, every element: I8253_TIMER_BCD occurs EXACTLY TWICE tree-wide -- the define in i8253reg.h and one if at dev_8253.c:339 -- so there is NO BCD arithmetic in the fork; the bit is nevertheless ACCEPTED at :310 (d->mode_byte = idata, unmasked); and :181-184 computes hz = I8253_TIMER_FREQ / (float) counter, treating the stored bytes as binary.  Worked arithmetic rather than an assertion: BCD 0x9999 means decimal 9999 (~119.3 Hz); the model reads 39321 and computes 30.3 Hz, which is 3.93x wrong.  For counter 0 that hz[0] is what timer_add and timer_update_frequency install at :192-196, so the error is the REAL HOST TIMER FREQUENCY and guest timekeeping is wrong by up to ~4x.  *** THE REASON THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN MERELY TRUE: pit8253flood WAS ABOUT TO LATCH THE ONLY SURVIVING SYMPTOM. ***  The fatal() at :342 is the single signal that this defect is live, and a warn-once latch turns a loud recurring signal into one line then silence -- option-set member 3 used to suppress a REAL EVENT, which is what the flood-versus-event distinction exists to prevent.  CONSEQUENCE, recorded on both rows so it cannot be lost by reading only one: DO NOT LATCH :342 in pit8253flood.  Found by the Opus 5 seat; no other seat of the eight reached it.

entries.grader: main-loop (Opus 5), by reading the datasheet text
entries.note: PRIMARY SOURCE, read the same day rather than cited from a paragraph: _scratchpad/i8254.txt :213-216 gives the control word's BCD bit as 0 = Binary Counter 16-bits and 1 = Binary Coded Decimal (BCD) Counter (4 Decades); :671-673 says the largest initial count 0 is equivalent to 2^16 binary and 10^4 BCD; :677-678 says the counter wraps to FFFF hex for binary or 9999 for BCD.  THE DATASHEET THEREFORE STATES THE DEFECT DIRECTLY -- a BCD counter is a 4-decade counter and the model applies 16-bit binary arithmetic to the same bytes.  The Opus seat's 0x9999 example is the datasheet's own maximum BCD count, not an arbitrary worst case.  A round taking this row does not need to reason about what BCD means.

The SHARED-mode_byte-ACROSS-COUNTERS defect, which codex's witness-ordering constraint depends on and which the panel packet called 'pitclobber', had NO LEDGER ROW AT ALL -- it survived only as a residual bullet at OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md:6693 under #440's block.  **Closing the pitclobber row would therefore have buried a live defect that no row carried.**  THE DEFECT ITSELF: mode_byte is ONE field (dev_8253.c:78) written at exactly one site (:310), so a control word programming ANY counter replaces the RW format of all three.  That is why :204/:270 fire only before the first non-latch control word, and it is why a device-signature control word on another counter is NOT neutral for a witness -- the constraint codex raised.  It needs its own id before any round is built on it, which is what this row is.

rows.title: dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c's 'Transfering %i bytes' fatal() is UNLATCHED on the NORMAL DMA path, so it floods on every legal guest transfer
rows.state_note: filed 2026-09-17 by the agy seat during the late-review panel on the six unreviewed fixes -- found while auditing a DIFFERENT question, the standing license working as intended.  *** DISPOSITION IS LATE-DISSENT 3 (file as a new item), NOT an L2 against #462, and the reason is MEASURED not procedural: `git show 7c9dd9e^:src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c | grep -n Transfering` returns the identical unlatched fatal() at :825.  #462 MOVED and re-pointed it (at d->data_len rather than `length`); it did not introduce it. ***  NOT the one-line change it looks like: the flood is on the SUCCESS path, so the (once) idiom is the wrong shape -- latching would suppress genuinely per-transfer information, and the row `nodata notx` PINS this line MEASURED RED at 50/51 (probe_pre51.raw), so a latch MOVES that row.  The option set needs naming before a fix is designed.  The file already carries 12 correctly latched sites and an enumerated GDROM_W_* bit-position scheme built for this.  *** UPHELD MED by the Fable adjudication 2026-09-17 (9 of 9), which verified the parent at `7c9dd9e^:825' shows the same unlatched fatal() above the NULL test -- #462 MOVED it and CHANGED ITS ARGUMENTS.  ***  AND A COUPLING THAT MUST BE WRITTEN INTO ANY FIX FOR THIS ROW: the Opus seat's finding (b) proposes making `accept dma' PARSE THE NUMBER on this very line (`Transfering (\d+) bytes' asserting 408), because no row reads it today.  **So whoever later LATCHES or DEMOTES this line must re-pin that row IN ORACLE-CORRECTION ORDER** -- re-pin first, measure the committed build RED under the new expectation, then change the code.  Fable calls this 'the crimectlflood coupling again'.  Two rows, one line, and they move in opposite directions: one wants the line QUIETER, the other wants it PARSED.

AND THE ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG TOO: **#472, not #491, is the round whose detector covers this line.**  *** THE ERROR IN ONE SENTENCE: a packet-fed seat reading an inlined diff hunk CANNOT SEE a detector that lives in another file, and I filed HIGH on its coverage claim without opening the tree. rows.title: exitsweep censused terminating sites across src/devices/ ONLY -- src/cpus/ was never covered, and cpu->running = 0 is a second shape an exit(-keyed sweep cannot see
rows.state_note: filed 2026-09-17.  The gap is in the CLOSED exitsweep row's own title: 'terminating sites across src/devices/'.  src/cpus/ holds 111 exit( across 23 files, 1 abort(, and 52 `cpu->running = 0' across 10 files (deriver: grep -roh over src/cpus/*.c; RE-RUN, do not quote). *** THE COUNT IS AN UPPER BOUND AND NOT THE CLASS -- PAL_halt is a legitimate halt; what defines the class is reachability from a GUEST-SUPPLIED SELECTOR, which no regex tests. ***  Verified instances: alpha_prom_call() reads a0-a3 from guest registers and BOTH its default: arms do fatal() + cpu->running = 0, so a guest setting a register and making a PAL call stops the emulator.  Ranked HIGH for the CENSUS, not for any single site.  Owes a src/cpus/ census on the same footing exitsweep gave src/devices/, keyed on guest reachability, each site triaged under the seven-member option set.  *** FIGURES CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR: the filed 111 exit( / 52 running=0 were the RAW STRING COUNT and included this project's OWN COMMENTS about the pattern.  Stripping block comments, line comments and string literals gives **73 exit( and 41 running=0 IN CODE**.  FOUR files (cpu_mips_instr.c 5, cpu_sh_instr.c 2, cpu_ppc_instr.c 1, cpu_m88k_instr.c 1) have ZERO real sites and were listed as having them.  Caught because cpu_alpha_palcode.c:413 enumerated as a site and is the COMMENT that documents the other sites -- the census counted its own documentation.  THE CLASS IS SHARPER THAN 'keyed on a correlate': a string-keyed census is inflated by its own prose whenever the codebase comments on the pattern being counted, and a de-fatalisation fork is the worst case for that.  The SUBSTANCE is unchanged -- src/cpus/ is still uncensused and both palcode arms are still guest-drivable halts. ***  *** RELABELLED RESEARCH (was HIGH) by the Fable adjudication 2026-09-17: 'HIGH is a defect severity; a census has no witness and is a research item that generates rows.  Label it RESEARCH with a priority, not a severity.'  The deriver being stated is right and is kept.  STILL OWED: the FOUR->FIVE L4 at cpu_alpha_palcode.c -- the in-file comment still says FOUR sites and the triage found FIVE. ***  *** `cpusexitsweep`'s CENSUS IS SPELLING-KEYED AND CANNOT SEE A THIRD OF ITS OWN POPULATION. The concealment is THREE-LAYERED, and I verified all three myself. ***  **(1) `running = 0` vs `running = false`.**  Measured in `src/cpus/`: **`= 0` gives 54 hits across 11 files; `= false` gives 20 hits across 10 files.**  A `= 0`-keyed census misses every one of the 20 -- and the files it misses include `cpu_dyntrans.c`, `cpu_mips_instr_loadstore.c`, `cpu_ppc_instr_loadstore.c` and `cpu_sh_instr.c`, which is **four files the sweeping seat's own table did not list either**.  The `= false` population is the m88k / i960 / RISC-V / MIPS-reboot family. **(2) `ABORT_EXECUTION` IS A MACRO, so neither spelling appears at the USE sites.**  It is defined three times -- `cpu_i960_instr.c:45`, `cpu_m88k_instr.c:45`, `cpu_sh_instr.c:45` -- and every invocation is a bare `ABORT_EXECUTION`.  A grep for either assignment spelling finds the three definitions and none of the uses. **(3) COMMENTS AND `#if 0` INFLATE BOTH SPELLINGS**, so the raw hit counts above are an upper bound, not the live population -- the seat stripped them programmatically and found, for example, that `cpu_dyntrans.c` has ONE live `= 0` (the `bad` label) with the other two commented out, and that `cpu_m88k_instr_loadstore.c`'s alignment halt sits in the `#else` of an `#if 1`. **THIS IS THE SESSION'S DOMINANT FAILURE FAMILY ARRIVING IN A SHIPPED CENSUS ROW:** the deriver measured a CORRELATE -- one way of spelling the assignment -- rather than the thing, which is *does this code path stop the emulated CPU*.  The carrier already states the rule (*'before writing a deriver, ask what makes a member a member'*) and `staticlatchscope` is the recorded precedent where three name-keyed censuses of one class all came back wrong. **THE FIX IS A RE-DERIVATION, NOT A SWEEP.**  `cpusexitsweep`'s number is owed a re-run keyed on the three spellings together, with comments and `#if 0` stripped and macro uses expanded. No code changes; the row's count is the deliverable.  *** `abort()` IS ABSENT FROM `src/cpus/`: ZERO CALLS.  An empty result with its denominator, and it CLOSES that class for this domain. ***  The only hit is a COMMENT at `memory_alpha.c:195` -- *'must not abort()/exit() the host'* -- which documents a host death `#194` REMOVED, not a live one.  `cpu_mips_instr.c` has a second comment, prose about `cpu->running = 0`.  Lookalikes that a careless grep counts: `abortdyntrans` (an ARM dyntrans helper), `abort_dump:` (an m88k `rte` label), and 'abort execution' in prose. *** AND I REPORTED '1' FOR THIS EARLIER TODAY BY GREPPING `abort(` AND COUNTING A LINE OF PROSE.  Same correlate-keying failure, mine, in the same session that keeps finding it. *** Denominator: every `.c`/`.h` under `src/cpus/`, including the `#include`d `.c` files and the generated `tmp_*`.  Also checked and absent: `raise(`, `SIGABRT`, `__builtin_trap` (the `raise` hits are `ppc_fpscr_raise` and `*_interrupt_assert`). Related but NOT this class: `cpu_dyntrans.c`'s two `assert()`s on page-aligned translation inserts, which can only abort with `NDEBUG` off -- and this tree builds with it on -- and which pin a HOST invariant rather than a guest opcode. **NO MAPLE-STYLE UNBOUNDED INSTRUCTION-PATH LOOP EXISTS in `src/cpus/`** either.  The one shared 'I do not know this instruction' halt is `cpu_dyntrans.c`'s `bad` label, which is included into every dyntrans CPU -- so it is one site with many faces rather than many sites.
