entries.grader: main-loop (Opus 5); every site opened, the #if 0 boundaries controlled, the deriver corrected three times
entries.note: *** TRIAGE OF THE MOTIVATING FILE: FIVE LIVE SITES, ALL FIVE GUEST-DRIVABLE. ***  :138 (a1, GETENV id), :149 (a0, PROM call number), :189 (palcode called in userMode), :443 (a1, wrent kentry selector), :500 (palcode, top-level dispatch default).  a0-a3 come straight from cpu->cd.alpha.r[] and palcode is an instruction field, so each is reachable by a guest setting a register or executing call_pal.  *** THE CENSUS NEEDED A FOURTH REFINEMENT: `#if 0' REGIONS ARE NOT COMPILED. ***  :474 (PAL_bugchk), :478 (PAL_OSF1_syscall) and :487 (KENTRY not set) sit inside #if 0...#endif -- controlled by reading the boundaries at :472/:480.  Tree-wide the progression is 53 raw -> 41 code -> **38 LIVE** for running=0, and 111 -> 73 -> **73** for exit( (no #if 0 effect there).  ALL THREE #if 0 LOSSES ARE IN THIS FILE.  *** AND THE FILE'S OWN COMMENT NAMES FOUR, NOT FIVE -- it omits :500, the top-level PALcode default, which meets an unrecognised selector in exactly the sense its sentence describes.  Whether that was a deliberate scoping of 'selector' to the PAL-call ARGUMENTS or an omission is NOT established, and this claims only what was counted -- but a reader trusting 'four' misses a live guest-drivable halt, and that comment was the only record of the class until today. ***  WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: that any of the five is a BUG (halting on an unimplemented PAL code may be right; DELETE is one of seven options), that the other 33 live sites are reachable (untriaged; cpu_arm.c alone has 16), or any severity ranking.

entries.grader: grok 4.6 xhigh; it opened EVERY match in cpu_arm.c rather than trusting the brief's count, and corrected a sibling figure
entries.note: *** SITE-BY-SITE TRIAGE OF cpu_arm.c: 16 live sites; FIVE ARE ONE DEFECT; NINE ARE LEGAL THUMB ENCODINGS THAT STOP THE EMULATOR; TWO ARE NOT GUEST-REACHABLE; ONE CANNOT FIRE AT ALL. ***  It confirmed 16 (no #if 0 in this file, no comment/string hits) and CORRECTED my sibling figure: cpu_m88k_instr_loadstore.c is 2 live + 1 preprocessor-dead, NOT 3.  *** MEMBER 5 IS AVAILABLE ON ARM, which the option-set rule says to check before reaching for it: arm_exception() already delivers UND (X(und), arm_cdp), PREF_ABT (memory_arm.c I-fault, X(bkpt)), DATA_ABT, SWI and IRQ.  RESET is the one vector that itself halts -- do NOT reach for FAULT there until RESET is implemented. ***  **THE SHARPEST FINDING, and it is a FUNCTIONAL defect rather than merely a halt: sites 1227, 1557, 1600, 1629, 1653 are ONE defect, member 1 DELETE.  On an MMU fault the abort is ALREADY DELIVERED and T is ALREADY CLEARED -- so the halt PREVENTS THE ABORT HANDLER FROM RUNNING.**  Keep the `return 0'; do NOT fall through to `pc += 2'.  Precedent in-tree: #312 said of the ARM-mode analogue that 'halting was never right'.  DISPOSITIONS for the rest: 1510 (MOV Rd,PC) member 7, value is (pc & ~1) + 4 with bit 0 CLEAR, not +8; 1495/1541/1810 member 7 -- real ARMv4T instructions where UND would be the #312 APPROXIMATION and wrong for NEG/ADR/STMIA/hi-ADD; 1757 (0xDE**) member 5 UND, A6.8's own 'use this if you want UNDEFINED' and the cleanest FAULT in the file; 1690 SPLIT (5 for A6.8, 7 for BKPT -- do not UND a defined BKPT on an ARMv5 model); 1535 member 7 for BLX Rm on v5 and 5 UND for the rest of the BX hole; 1769 member 5 or UNPREDICTABLE, not first.  KEEP AND DO NOT FILE: :659 RESET (not guest-reachable; but its extra exit(1) is NOT an honest stop -- process death if that arm ever becomes reachable) and :1219 not-in-Thumb (an emulator invariant; a privileged MSR CAN manufacture the desync via CPSR bits 7:0, but that is an MSR modelling hole, not an ISA defect).  **:1571 CANNOT FIRE -- not a halt, not a row.**

Built to that decision, with the rejected reasoning recorded IN THE FILE rather than quietly softened -- the carrier's finding that a retro-failing rule gets switched off is the COST of the decision, not a veto on it.  TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS, both run: against the real ledger it EXITS 1 and names 34 rows; with the gaps synthetically closed it EXITS 0 and prints FIX_SEATS_PASS.  Ledger restored and the restore verified BY CONTENT (0 synthetic entries remaining, 488 rows), not by the backup's existence.  *** A CLOBBER WAS AVERTED IN THE BUILD: the parked draft's docstring named it `check_seat_coverage.py', which ALREADY EXISTS and does a different job (per-seat answers-on-disk vs ledger coverage). rows.title: cpu_arm.c: FIVE Thumb sites halt the emulator AFTER the abort is already delivered and T cleared -- the halt PREVENTS THE GUEST'S ABORT HANDLER FROM RUNNING
rows.witness: none -- documented-only.  ATTEMPT RECORDED: a rung-3 probe was specified in full (regress/artifacts/armthumbabortkill/WITNESSSPEC_grok_20260917.txt) and then condemned against the tree across 13 holes (HOLES_grok_20260917.txt), two of which are unfixable as specified -- the t ifetch row is vacuous by construction, and the TLB flush the ARM control needs is the same flush that makes site 1227 unreachable.  Reopen if an MMU-on ARM vehicle is built for a higher-ranked defect.
rows.state_note: [2026-11-02, records] #562 as landed (4f908ad5) shifts cpu_arm.c by +50, not +42: the five filed sites are :1277, :1607, :1650, :1679, :1703 at 987cb596.  ||  2026-10-07 pre-brief READING (Opus 5.5, read-only, nothing run; brief not written -- the seat's response was classifier-stopped at the witness-design step): (1) the row's own reopen condition (an MMU-on ARM vehicle) is NOT met by arm_msrmode_probe.py; owner asked whether to reopen anyway.  (2) on ARM a failing DEVICE read raises no exception (memory_rw.c's exception arms are MIPS/M88K only), so a bare delete of running=0 with `return 0` would re-run the Thumb instruction forever with an unlatched fatal() -- argues for a conditional decline; unreachable on testarm (all seven devices return 1).  (3) candidate siblings, UNVERIFIED: the PC-relative site passes CACHE_INSTRUCTION -> Prefetch Abort where Thumb LDR(3) is a Data Abort (ddi0100i.txt:23050-23051); Thumb pc bit 0 may make the saved abort return address 1 low; testarm's default SA1110 is ARMv4 with no Thumb (seat's recollection, unchecked) -- ANSWERED 2026-10-09 (Fable 5.1's regress review of #562, finding 2, regress/artifacts/armmsrmodekill/regress_20261009/fable5_regress562.md): src/include/arm_cpu_types.h has NO Thumb capability field and cpu_dyntrans.c selects arm_cpu_interpret_thumb_SLOW on ARM_FLAG_T alone, as the armmmuvehicle record already says from agy's research -- T alone selects the Thumb interpreter on any ARM CPU here.  Cite sites by grep anchor: #562 shifts cpu_arm.c by +42.  ||  filed 2026-09-17 from the grok seat's site-by-site triage of cpu_arm.c (the cpusexitsweep research row).  **FIVE SITES, ONE DEFECT: 1227, 1557, 1600, 1629, 1653.**  *** IT IS A FUNCTIONAL DEFECT, NOT MERELY A HALT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HIGH AND IS NOT PART OF THE CENSUS: on an MMU fault the abort is ALREADY DELIVERED and T is ALREADY CLEARED, so the `cpu->running = 0' that follows PREVENTS THE GUEST'S OWN ABORT HANDLER FROM EVER RUNNING.  A guest that would have recovered instead stops. ***  DISPOSITION: option-set member 1 DELETE -- match the ARM load/store path.  **KEEP the `return 0'; do NOT fall through to `pc += 2'.**  IN-TREE PRECEDENT: #312 said of the ARM-mode analogue that 'halting was never right'.  SELECTOR: a guest-supplied instruction or address in arm_cpu_interpret_thumb_SLOW, which is the PRODUCTION Thumb path -- cpu_dyntrans.c calls it whenever ARM_FLAG_T is set and ignores its return value -- so these are reachable by any Thumb guest taking a memory fault.  NOT YET WITNESSED: no probe has been built.  This is a READING by a file-reading seat, and the round that takes it owes the rung-3 ATTEMPT the 2026-08-27 lifecycle ruling requires.  *** WITNESS DISPOSITION: DOCUMENTED-ONLY, WITH THE ATTEMPT RECORDED.  DO NOT BUILD `regress/arm_thumbabort_probe.py` FROM THE SPEC, AND DO NOT BUILD A PATCHED COPY IN THIS CAMPAIGN. ***  The lifecycle ask is satisfied in the form it was written for: a seat WAS asked to try a rung-3 probe, DID specify one, and then condemned its own spec against the tree.  So `none` here means 'tried; the vehicle costs a new MMU-on ARM harness that this row does not outrank', NOT 'did not think to' -- which are different states and must not render the same. THIRTEEN HOLES, derived against source rather than restated.  **The two that end the question:** *** HOLE 3 -- THE `t ifetch` ROW (site 1227) IS VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION AND THE SPEC'S OWN SCORE IS THEREFORE A WRONG RECORD. ***  `X(bx)` sets T before `quick_pc_to_pointers_arm` short-circuits, so the BX itself does not translate the hole -- but the NEXT `run_instr` does: `arm_run_instr` calls the GENERIC `arm_pc_to_pointers` FIRST and checks T only afterwards, so the prefetch abort is taken with T already cleared and PC already at 0x0C, the ARM prefetch handler runs, and **site 1227 never executes**.  The row wants `SENT` (handler did not run); the handler DID run; so the row is GREEN on HEAD and GREEN post-fix.  It never reds -- and it inflates the spec's claimed HEAD from 7/12 to 8/12.  A 'Thumb ifetch' row built as specified is an ARM dyntrans prefetch-abort row wearing a Thumb name.  1227 is DISCLOSED, not rowed. *** HOLE 2 -- A GENUINE CONTRADICTION THE SPEC CANNOT SEE: the c8 flush that makes the `arm abt` control honest is the SAME flush that makes 1227 unreachable.  You cannot have both on one hole. ***  And the seat CORRECTED ITS OWN EARLIER SPECSET CLAIM here: stale VPH does NOT hide a Thumb abort (the five Thumb sites go through `memory_rw` -> `translate_v2p` and never read `host_load`); it hides the ARM SIBLING CONTROL instead.  My own brief had stated this as a QUESTION rather than a fact, which is why no wrong record of mine needs correcting. THE REMAINING ELEVEN, kept because they are reusable if an MMU-on ARM vehicle is ever built: (1) the TTB plant explodes three different ways -- 4096 `put w` of zeros onto already-zero anonymous mmap is 4096 pty round-trips against a 45 s wait, `put w` warms `host_load` because it does NOT use NO_EXCEPTIONS, and any `put w` after the M bit makes THE DEBUGGER take the abort; (4) the row set splits DATA {1600,1629,1653} / PREF {1557 only}, one probe, and PREF must NOT pin FAR/FSR because prefetch does not write them and a leftover FAR would lie; (5) `-T` is not host death, is IRRELEVANT at UNMAP=0x100000 under `-M 64`, and `-K` is redundant with `-V`; (6) LIVE must be a named constant, never 'UNIQUE's neighbour', which plants next to the hole; (7) `mmu bit`/`ttb sent`/`thumb T` have NO observation channel as specified -- Thumb has no MRS; (8) rows 1-6 CANNOT share a session, because `arm abt` leaves the CPU in ABT32 at the handler -- three control processes, not one; (9) no `enc ok` for the planted Thumb halfwords, and a wrong halfword hits `:1808 default:` `running = 0` which LOOKS exactly like the abort defect on HEAD and false-reds POST; (10) the two vector `B` words are not in the spec (given: `0xEA0020FB` at 0x0C, `0xEA00213A` at 0x10); (11) after the M bit **testarm's own LR stub is unmapped**, so `continue` or an oversized `step N` falls into it and takes a prefetch abort -- which is the POST colour of a PREF row; (12) flags `session()` is the wrong wrapper to copy even though a trailing dump IS legal for Thumb; (13) `return 0` is load-bearing -- DELETE only `cpu->running = 0`, because dropping the whole `if` body falls through to `cpu->pc += 2` on a PC `arm_exception` already set, making the vector 0x0E/0x12. **THE BILL IF BUILT AFTER REPAIRS: 7 sessions minimum, not 6, plus the first in-tree ARM MMU-on probe** -- no `regress/arm_*` probe enables the M bit today -- meaning CP15 c1/c2/c3/c8, a 1 MB section table, two abort handlers and architectural BX.  That is a round of its own spent on a FUNCTIONAL HALT (`cpu->running = 0` AFTER `arm_exception` already delivered and T already cleared; the abort handler never runs; the host does not die) while a PROCESS-DEATH row (`armmsrmodekill`) is unbuilt. **REOPEN CONDITION, NAMED SO THIS IS NOT A QUIET DROP:** reopen if an MMU-on ARM vehicle is ever built for a higher-ranked defect -- Thumb is then a RIDER on it, not its first customer. **THE HONEST COST, stated rather than glossed:** documented-only means the fix does not ship, so the five `cpu->running = 0` lines STAY.  The fix is known and is member 1 DELETE with `return 0` KEPT; it is unshippable under test-first without a witness. Seat's own reservations, kept because they bound the answer: it would not claim without a run that 1557's PC-relative load takes PREF rather than DATA on this binary, that `step N` under `-V` leaves DEST dumpable as SENT, or that `dump UNMAP` prints '(memory access failed)' rather than zeros a sloppy regex would read as UNIQUE.  ||  [2026-10-09, armmmuvehicle pass 1] Fable 5.1 MEASURED the vehicle shape on unmodified testarm with the MMU on: a Thumb LDR to an unmapped VA reaches a stop site (logs 'could not load with immediate offset', DEST stays poison, pc stuck at 0x10 with LR/SPSR already written) -- this row's symptom; a Thumb BX to an unmapped VA goes through the generic pc_to_pointers prefetch abort and never reaches the Thumb fetch stop (the 1227 site is reachable only through a stale warm entry).  The return-address defects are filed as armthumbabtlr.

entries.note: *** WITNESS SPECIFIED: regress/arm_thumbabort_probe.py, 12 rows (11 data + identity), on UNMODIFIED testarm.  Expected 7/12 on HEAD -> 12/12 after member 1 DELETE. ***  TWO PIECES OF ITS OWN EARLIER CORRECTION ARE WRONG AS STATED, both found by being asked which part was weakest:  (1) *** 'MMU IS OFF' IS TRUE OF arm_cpu_new AND FALSE AS A CLAIM ABOUT THE THREE ARM MACHINES. ***  The seat caught itself mid-answer on the absence-claim trap -- cpu_arm.c:231 ORs in ARM_CONTROL_MMU but that line is arm_setup_initial_translation_table, NOT create.  testarm and barearm never call it (MMU off, identity translate); **cats DOES**, so cats starts MMU-ON -- and worse, that table writes a 1 MB section for EVERY 1 MB of the 4 GB VA space (sixteen aliases of the low 256 MB), so *** THERE IS NO UNMAPPED VA ON cats AT ALL. ***  'Enable the M bit and LDR an unmapped VA' on unmodified cats is a GREEN RUN THAT MEANS THE TABLE MAPPED THE ACCESS, not that the defect is absent -- the same fake-green trap as the MMU-off one, at the opposite polarity.  barearm is also unusable: its setup forces BIG-ENDIAN, so LE encodings would be silently swapped.  **testarm is the vehicle, and it is the only one.**  (2) TWO OF THE FIVE SITES TAKE **PREFETCH** ABORT, NOT DATA ABORT -- a correction to its own earlier one-class characterisation.  (3) THE FIX SURVIVES THE SKETCH RULE, NARROWED: DELETE of `cpu->running = 0' is right ONLY IF `return 0' IS KEPT -- `return 0' is load-bearing, and the 'next run_instr executes ARM at the abort vector' half holds only where arm_exception has ALREADY run.  The caller ignoring the return value is confirmed true.  *This is the third time today that asking this seat to attack its own finding returned a defect in it, and the second where the defect would have produced a probe that goes GREEN ON A LIVE DEFECT.*

entries.note: *** CROSS-SPEC REVIEW OF ALL THREE WITNESS SPECS AS A SET -- none had been reviewed against the others, each was written in isolation.  VERDICT: DO NOT BUILD THE THUMB SPEC AS WRITTEN ('the TTB plant is a session bomb').  BUILD ORDER: MSR first, then Alpha with one added stop, then Thumb. ***  IT CORRECTED ITS OWN EARLIER SPEC TWICE MORE.  (1) THE `printed()' INSTRUCTION WAS FALSE: it had told me to shun arm_bfx_width_probe.py because 'the debugger prints r0 = 0x...'.  debugger_parse_expression returns PARSE_NUMBER, so `print <reg>' emits a BARE 0x... line; `reg' is the command with the prefix.  A builder who 'fixed' the regex would score EVERY print as ABSENT -- and arm_flags_probe.py has NO printed() at all, so the advice was unfollowable.  Copy verbatim from lca_isalane_probe.py:397-399.  (2) THE MSR FAKE-GREEN MECHANISM WAS THE WRONG ONE: already-USR32 gives m=10 alive, which reds honestly (wrong-reason FAIL), NOT a kill-row green.  The real fake-green is encoding-nop / c-bit-off / MSR-never-stepped -> still SVC32, alive -> GREEN, because that IS the post-fix decline appearance.  Guarding USR32 would have guarded the path that reds.  NEW BUILD TRAP: DO NOT COPY arm_flags_probe.py's session() wrapper -- it dumps ONCE AT THE END, and this guest calls exit(1), so the arming word must be dumped BETWEEN step 2 and the killing step.  That is also why MSR is built FIRST: it is the only one of the three that forces the mid-session dump, so Thumb inherits proven machinery.  ALPHA GAP: lcaisaphys states its stop in PROSE and emits no CONTROL=DEAD / RESULT=0/0, so a failed swpctx yields ~10/13 with defect rows GREEN that a RESULT grep will not refuse -- copy the ARM token.  ONE GUARD FOR ALL THREE: a positive un-fakeable observable that the bad path is ARMED, on the SAME PROCESS that issues the stimulus, before any defect row is read; red there is SETUP-FAILED.  Do NOT share an MMU-arming prologue between the ARM probes; share only pty/wait/send/sw()/-A.  `-T' is a silent coupler (turns a physical miss into host death); `-K' is redundant with `-V'.  All of this is in regress/artifacts/armmsrmodekill/SPEC_AMENDMENTS_READ_BEFORE_BUILDING.md, beside the spec rather than in this row, per the #490 lesson.

The underlying worry stands: without a scored two-write row a Load-only skip-memcpy POSTs clean and still dies on the write OUT of reserved mode (16/17, `save 2s` red on the second MSR -- that is the point of the row). **AMENDMENT 5 IS TRUE OF THE ENCODING AND INERT FOR THIS PROBE, VERIFIED LOCALLY BY ME AND NOT TAKEN FROM THE SEAT:** `#0x14` does clear I and F, and testarm does hang cons/ether/rtc off `irqc` -- but ARM IRQ dispatch sits inside `if (!single_step) {` at `cpu_dyntrans.c:206` with the ARM arm at `:208-209`, and `-V` sets single_step; **`fiq_asserted` has ZERO occurrences across all of `src/`** and `ARM_FLAG_F` zero in `cpu_dyntrans.c`, so there is no ARM FIQ dispatch to enable; and debugger interaction `timer_stop()`s so `step N` runs no host-timer callback.  **The pin is STAY ON `step`, NEVER `continue`** -- a `continue` after a LANDED `#0x14` can take `arm_exception` and run Save on the reserved current mode, which is a free-run hazard and not a step hazard.  DO NOT change the filed stimulus to `#0xD4`. **BOTH KILL ARMS CONFIRMED AT HEAD BY READING:** `cpu_arm.c:559-561` `arm_save_register_bank: unimplemented mode %i` + `exit(1)`, and `:606-608` the same for `arm_load_register_bank`. Amendment 8 belongs on the ALPHA spec, not this one. **CLAUSE (e), DISCLOSED NOT ROWED:** register-form MSR (`X(msr)` copies rm into arg[0] and calls msr_imm); the 26-bit holes; the other 32-bit holes 0x16/18/19/1a/1c/1d/1e (`kill 14` + `kill 15` catch a ONE-VALUE special case, not a two-value one); SPSR-then-`MOVS pc`; free-run IRQ after a landed reserved write, pinned by stay-on-step. **BUILD FROM THE ARTIFACT, NOT FROM THIS NOTE** -- the complete 17-row table, the 13-session schedule, the CONTROL=DEAD set, the plant layouts and the tally live verbatim at `regress/artifacts/armmsrmodekill/WITNESSSPEC_REWRITE_grok_20260917.txt`.  Transcribing a row table into a ledger note is the frozen-number class waiting to happen. **ONE BUILD REQUIREMENT I FOUND MYSELF AND THE SPEC DOES NOT STATE:** the launch line uses `regress/arm_bfx_stub.bin`, which is on the NEVER-STAGE list and is UNTRACKED.  That is safe, and the reason matters -- **all 11 top-level committed probes referencing such a stub CREATE IT IF ABSENT** (e.g. `alpha_harness_probe.py:169-173`).  `arm_msrmode_probe.py` MUST carry the same self-create block, or it will be the one committed probe that cannot run on a fresh clone.  *** THE PROBE WAS ATTACKED BEFORE IT WAS EVER RUN, AND IT HAD THREE INDEPENDENT DEFECTS. Verdict: 'It runs.  It does not score.' ***  (1) **LINE LABELS ARE 16-BYTE ALIGNED** -- `debugger_cmds.c:709` is `addr = addr_start & ~0xf`, so `dump 0x9004` labels the line `0x00009000` AND BLANK-PADS the leading word groups, shifting every group index.  (2) **THE DUMP RENDERS LITTLE-ENDIAN BYTES, NOT A WORD** -- 0x2a prints as `2a000000`.  (3) **`save 2s` READ A SLOT NOTHING WROTE**: its plant put SP at DEST+16 via `str_sp_10` while `classify()` read DEST+8, so ` sp` could NEVER appear and **the row was ALWAYS RED, pre-fix and post-fix alike** -- not a witness of Save at all. *** THE REMEDIES FOR (1) AND (2) ALREADY EXISTED IN THIS TREE AND I DID NOT USE THEM: `arm_bdt_probe.py:123-149` records the alignment measurement from 2026-09-11 in a seven-line comment, and `arm_flags_probe.py:191-193` carries `sw()` for the byte order. Knowledge present, unconsulted at the moment of use -- the carrier's own recurring finding.  The repair COPIES both rather than inventing. *** **AND THE FAILURE MODE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN A FALSE GREEN, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.**  `live` wants 0x2a and would have got 0x2a000000; `armed` would have given `?/?`.  Both sit in the CONTROL=DEAD set, so the probe would have printed `ARMMSRMODE_CONTROL=DEAD`, `RESULT=0/0` and 'SETUP FAILED -- NOT no defect'.  **The vehicle-kill design worked exactly as intended: it would have REFUSED TO SCORE rather than lying.**  That is the difference between a wasted run and a wrong record, and it is why the CONTROL=DEAD set is not decoration. *A self-check while repairing it showed why `arm_flags_probe.py` warns as it does: `deadbeef` read RAW yields 0xdeadbeef, so the POISON comparison would have MATCHED under the broken parser while every real value was wrong -- the sentinel's own byte pattern hiding the defect.* **ONE CORRECTION RUNNING THE OTHER WAY, against the SPEC rather than the probe:** `print pc` wanting CODE+8 after `step 2` is RIGHT; the spec table's CODE+4 is the wrong half, and a builder must not 'fix' the probe down to it.  REPAIRED, AST clean, zero raw `dump` commands left.  **STILL NOT RUN** -- the adjudicated ship order puts the commit first, then this.  *** THE RANKING IS SETTLED BY READING WITH A DENOMINATOR: `ip30abortkill` FIRST. ***  And the distinction that settles it is worth more than the verdict: **the gap on ip30 is 'we do not run that OS here'; the gap on armmsr is 'that OS would not do this.'  Only the second kind of gap demotes a defect.**  A process death on the documented interrupt path of the guest the machine exists to run outranks a process death that requires the guest to program a reserved mode. **Q1 -- CAN A REAL ARM GUEST REACH `armmsrmodekill`?  NO.**  `arm_save_register_bank` / `arm_load_register_bank` switch on `cpsr & 0x1f`: **7 arms handled, 25 of 32 unhandled.**  Handled: USR32 0x10, FIQ32 0x11, IRQ32 0x12, SVC32 0x13, ABT32 0x17, UND32 0x1b, SYS32 0x1f. The unhandled 25 break down as: **26-bit modes 0x00-0x03** (`cpu_arm.h` names them and `grep -c 'case ARM_MODE_USR26'` across src/ is ZERO; CATS/testarm/barearm are SA-110/SA1110 and the in-tree NetBSD `armreg.h` does not even define 26-bit modes); **0x04-0x0F unused**; **0x14/0x15/0x18/0x19/0x1c/0x1d/0x1e reserved** -- DDI 0100I A2.5.7 says *'If any other value is programmed into the mode bits M[4:0], the result is UNPREDICTABLE'*, and there are NO MSR exceptions; **0x16 Monitor** (TrustZone, not on any in-tree CPU); **0x1a Hyp** (ARMv7-A virt, likewise). A real kernel writes the named constants plus I/F -- `msr cpsr_c, #PSR_SVC32_MODE|I32_bit|F32_bit` (0xD3), IRQ 0x12, USR on process start, SYS for some copy paths -- and locore is `bic r0,r0,#0x1f ; orr r0,r0,#<legal> ; msr cpsr_c,r0`.  **Userspace cannot do it at all**: `X(msr_imm)` strips the c-byte in USR32 (`mask &= 0xff000000`). **Q2 -- THE SECOND PATH, which I had not considered and which is the one that could have been worse:** `MSR SPSR` is UNVALIDATED, and `MOVS PC, LR` / `LDM {..,pc}^` copies SPSR into CPSR **with no mode check**, after which Load dies identically.  But a correct kernel's SPSR is either the CPSR saved at exception entry (a legal mode) or a sigreturn frame, and Linux's `valid_user_regs` rejects anything whose MODE_MASK is not USR/USR26 and forces USR32.  **So the path exists and no correct kernel drives it.** **CONSEQUENCE FOR `armmsrmodekill`:** it stays a real process death and a real fix -- a hostile or buggy guest reaches it, and 25 of 32 encodings are unhandled -- but its SEVERITY is now measured rather than assumed, and it does NOT outrank ip30.  **`highrankunmeasured` is answered on the armmsr side by READING; the ip30 side stands as measured (gate_asan_sweep runs ip30 green, so the aborts are on no in-tree path).**

entries.note: *** THE ORACLE IN THE WITNESS SPEC IS BACKWARDS IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION.  SINGLE-SEAT FINDING, UNCORROBORATED -- deepseek and minimax did not reach it, and that is stated rather than glossed. ***  The spec makes an armed kill row RED only on EOF **AND** the exact text `arm_load_register_bank: unimplemented mode 20'.  glm names the mutant the AND cannot see: A BUILD THAT STILL exit(1)s WITH A REWORDED MESSAGE -- and the packet itself spotlights the %i-vs-0x14 confusion, which makes 'fix the format string, forget the exit' THE MOST PLAUSIBLE NEAR-MISS FIX.  That mutant gives EOF and no matching text, the AND never fires, THE ROW GOES GREEN, and the witness certifies a build where a guest MSR still kills the emulator.  *** THE AND GUARDS THE SAFE DIRECTION (a false-RED from an unrelated crash) AT THE COST OF A FALSE-GREEN, which is the wrong trade for a CERTIFICATION witness. ***  CORRECTION TO ADOPT: on an armed kill row, **EOF ALONE => RED; the text is the DIAGNOSIS, not half the trigger.**  Under that rule the feared cases still close: crash-elsewhere => RED (conservative, acceptable); print-without-exit => no death => GREEN, which is CORRECT because the defect IS the process death.  Buffering fear answered separately: exit() flushes stdio and a pty is line-buffered at the trailing newline, so the defect's own death preserves its text; buffering only threatens SIGNAL deaths, i.e. mutant territory.  THREE MORE DEFECTS, all correctable: (C4) the spec SELF-CONTRADICTS -- 'one fresh process per data row' AND '12 guest sessions' for 15 data rows, and 12 < 15, so either three sessions host two rows (reintroducing the sharing hazard the rule exists to avoid) or the count is wrong; the row->session schedule is missing.  (Q5) if BOTH red rows are a single MSR #0x14 they are DUPLICATES -- a load-only fix turns both green and the witness certifies a build that still dies on the write OUT of the reserved mode.  (Q4) the SVC32 accept row is incoherent as stated: a same-bank switch cannot change SP, so 'SP changed from boot to 0' is unsatisfiable there; and a fix repairing both LOAD arms while no-opping the SAVE arm passes every accept row, because nothing checks PRESERVATION -- a canary write to r13/r14 before the switch, verified after return, is owed for every mode but USR32.  FREE FINDING: the stimulus writes the whole control byte, and bits 6-7 of 0x14 are ZERO, so it UNMASKS IRQ AND FIQ; post-fix the guest sits in a reserved mode with interrupts enabled and any pending source takes an exception whose bank-save runs with the reserved mode current -- the store arm walks in ASYNCHRONOUSLY, making row timing nondeterministic.  It also HAND-DECODED 0xE321F014 independently and confirmed it, and confirmed 0x14 = 20 decimal.

VERDICT: DO NOT BUILD THE THUMB SPEC AS WRITTEN ('the TTB plant is a session bomb').  BUILD ORDER: MSR first, then Alpha with one added stop, then Thumb. ***  IT CORRECTED ITS OWN EARLIER SPEC TWICE MORE.  (1) THE `printed()' INSTRUCTION WAS FALSE: it had told me to shun arm_bfx_width_probe.py because 'the debugger prints r0 = 0x...'.  debugger_parse_expression returns PARSE_NUMBER, so `print <reg>' emits a BARE 0x... line; `reg' is the command with the prefix.  A builder who 'fixed' the regex would score EVERY print as ABSENT -- and arm_flags_probe.py has NO printed() at all, so the advice was unfollowable.  Copy verbatim from lca_isalane_probe.py:397-399.  (2) THE MSR FAKE-GREEN MECHANISM WAS THE WRONG ONE: already-USR32 gives m=10 alive, which reds honestly (wrong-reason FAIL), NOT a kill-row green.  The real fake-green is encoding-nop / c-bit-off / MSR-never-stepped -> still SVC32, alive -> GREEN, because that IS the post-fix decline appearance.  Guarding USR32 would have guarded the path that reds. entries.note: *** REWRITE, NOT PATCH.  THE 16-ROW SPEC PLUS EIGHT AMENDMENTS DOES NOT CLOSE, AND THE SEAT THAT WROTE THE ORIGINAL SPEC RULED AGAINST ITS OWN WORK WHEN ASKED TO BE HARDER ON IT. ***  I asked plainly whether eight amendments on a 16-row spec meant the spec should be rewritten rather than patched, and named the `#392` shape as the thing I feared.  Answer: yes.  'A builder applying them in order will get 1+6 wrong and will either treat `save 2s` as a duplicate of `kill 15` or REPLACE `kill 15` with it, losing the `== 0x14` pin.'  *** AND THE TALLY ITSELF WAS A FROZEN NUMBER: it is 14/17 -> 17/17 over THIRTEEN sessions, not 14/16 -> 16/16 over twelve.  The original 12 was already false -- 16 scored minus `enc ok` minus the identity row minus one for live/pc/armed sharing S1 is 13, and the spec wrote 12. ***  THE VEHICLE STANDS and is unchanged: `-V -A -E testarm -M 64`, `0xE321F014`, member 3 at BOTH `default:` arms, one fresh process per scored row that executes a guest instruction, mid-stream dump.  The ROW LIST, the ORACLES and the SESSION ARITHMETIC are replaced. **ANSWER TO MY INTERACTION QUESTION 1+6, AND IT REFUTES MY FRAMING.**  I asked whether, once amendment 1 makes EOF-alone the kill trigger, the `enc ok` / `no cbit` / dump-before-MSR machinery becomes THE ONLY THING between the witness and a false green.  The answer is that those three are **NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT** -- each has a smallest defeat: dump-DEST proves MRS ran, not that the MSR word was planted or stepped; `no cbit` is greened by a decoder that never writes the mode field AT ALL, which greens every kill row too; and `enc ok` walking a constructor instead of the planted literal is the BFX incident repeating.  What actually closes false-green, all four required: (1) **POST want is `m=13 sp once`, not `m=13`** -- member 3 prints `(once)`, and encoding-nop, skipped-step and a silent member-2 all print nothing, so the latch must be IN the got string or its absence is a comment rather than a FAIL; (2) **poison `DEST+4` with 0xdeadbeef** and dump DEST+4, never DEST+0, so a never-fired post-MSR store reds; (3) **one `WORDS` dict**, with every `put w` drawn from it and a per-session plant-dump of the MSR slot -- this is the load-bearing anti-false-green that amendment 6 hoped `enc ok` was; (4) **named-red tally** -- HEAD must be EXACTLY the three named reds, because 17/17 on HEAD is not success. **ANSWER TO INTERACTION 3+5, AND AMENDMENT 3 IS HALF-RIGHT AND MISREADS ITS OWN CASE.**  The original two reds were `kill 14` and `kill 15` -- TWO LOAD HOLES catching the `== 0x14` special case -- **not** Load vs Save, which is what amendment 3 assumed.  So: SCORE `save 2s`, KEEP `kill 15`, do NOT replace one with the other.  The underlying worry stands: without a scored two-write row a Load-only skip-memcpy POSTs clean and still dies on the write OUT of reserved mode (16/17, `save 2s` red on the second MSR -- that is the point of the row). **AMENDMENT 5 IS TRUE OF THE ENCODING AND INERT FOR THIS PROBE, VERIFIED LOCALLY BY ME AND NOT TAKEN FROM THE SEAT:** `#0x14` does clear I and F, and testarm does hang cons/ether/rtc off `irqc` -- but ARM IRQ dispatch sits inside `if (!single_step) {` at `cpu_dyntrans.c:206` with the ARM arm at `:208-209`, and `-V` sets single_step; **`fiq_asserted` has ZERO occurrences across all of `src/`** and `ARM_FLAG_F` zero in `cpu_dyntrans.c`, so there is no ARM FIQ dispatch to enable; and debugger interaction `timer_stop()`s so `step N` runs no host-timer callback.  **The pin is STAY ON `step`, NEVER `continue`** -- a `continue` after a LANDED `#0x14` can take `arm_exception` and run Save on the reserved current mode, which is a free-run hazard and not a step hazard.  DO NOT change the filed stimulus to `#0xD4`. **BOTH KILL ARMS CONFIRMED AT HEAD BY READING:** `cpu_arm.c:559-561` `arm_save_register_bank: unimplemented mode %i` + `exit(1)`, and `:606-608` the same for `arm_load_register_bank`.  Two arms, two kills -- which is exactly why member 3 is owed at both and why `save 2s` is independent rather than a duplicate. **DROPPED FROM THE ORIGINAL SPEC:** EOF-AND-text as the kill trigger; the 12 sessions; 'two reds because two default: arms'; POST `0xd3` on `kill 14` (member 3 refuses the MODE FIELD, so I|F stay clear at `0x13` -- record I|F, do not want them); already-USR32 as the fake-green mechanism; copy-flags-`session()`; copy-flags-`printed()` (arm_flags_probe.py has none).  Amendment 8 belongs on the ALPHA spec, not this one. **CLAUSE (e), DISCLOSED NOT ROWED:** register-form MSR (`X(msr)` copies rm into arg[0] and calls msr_imm); the 26-bit holes; the other 32-bit holes 0x16/18/19/1a/1c/1d/1e (`kill 14` + `kill 15` catch a ONE-VALUE special case, not a two-value one); SPSR-then-`MOVS pc`; free-run IRQ after a landed reserved write, pinned by stay-on-step. **BUILD FROM THE ARTIFACT, NOT FROM THIS NOTE** -- the complete 17-row table, the 13-session schedule, the CONTROL=DEAD set, the plant layouts and the tally live verbatim at `regress/artifacts/armmsrmodekill/WITNESSSPEC_REWRITE_grok_20260917.txt`.  Transcribing a row table into a ledger note is the frozen-number class waiting to happen. **ONE BUILD REQUIREMENT I FOUND MYSELF AND THE SPEC DOES NOT STATE:** the launch line uses `regress/arm_bfx_stub.bin`, which is on the NEVER-STAGE list and is UNTRACKED.  That is safe, and the reason matters -- **all 11 top-level committed probes referencing such a stub CREATE IT IF ABSENT** (e.g. `alpha_harness_probe.py:169-173`).  `arm_msrmode_probe.py` MUST carry the same self-create block, or it will be the one committed probe that cannot run on a fresh clone.

entries.note: *** THE PROBE WAS ATTACKED BEFORE IT WAS EVER RUN, AND IT HAD THREE INDEPENDENT DEFECTS. Verdict: 'It runs.  It does not score.' ***  (1) **LINE LABELS ARE 16-BYTE ALIGNED** -- `debugger_cmds.c:709` is `addr = addr_start & ~0xf`, so `dump 0x9004` labels the line `0x00009000` AND BLANK-PADS the leading word groups, shifting every group index.  (2) **THE DUMP RENDERS LITTLE-ENDIAN BYTES, NOT A WORD** -- 0x2a prints as `2a000000`.  (3) **`save 2s` READ A SLOT NOTHING WROTE**: its plant put SP at DEST+16 via `str_sp_10` while `classify()` read DEST+8, so ` sp` could NEVER appear and **the row was ALWAYS RED, pre-fix and post-fix alike** -- not a witness of Save at all. *** THE REMEDIES FOR (1) AND (2) ALREADY EXISTED IN THIS TREE AND I DID NOT USE THEM: `arm_bdt_probe.py:123-149` records the alignment measurement from 2026-09-11 in a seven-line comment, and `arm_flags_probe.py:191-193` carries `sw()` for the byte order. Knowledge present, unconsulted at the moment of use -- the carrier's own recurring finding.  The repair COPIES both rather than inventing. *** **AND THE FAILURE MODE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN A FALSE GREEN, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.**  `live` wants 0x2a and would have got 0x2a000000; `armed` would have given `?/?`.  Both sit in the CONTROL=DEAD set, so the probe would have printed `ARMMSRMODE_CONTROL=DEAD`, `RESULT=0/0` and 'SETUP FAILED -- NOT no defect'.  **The vehicle-kill design worked exactly as intended: it would have REFUSED TO SCORE rather than lying.**  That is the difference between a wasted run and a wrong record, and it is why the CONTROL=DEAD set is not decoration. *A self-check while repairing it showed why `arm_flags_probe.py` warns as it does: `deadbeef` read RAW yields 0xdeadbeef, so the POISON comparison would have MATCHED under the broken parser while every real value was wrong -- the sentinel's own byte pattern hiding the defect.* **ONE CORRECTION RUNNING THE OTHER WAY, against the SPEC rather than the probe:** `print pc` wanting CODE+8 after `step 2` is RIGHT; the spec table's CODE+4 is the wrong half, and a builder must not 'fix' the probe down to it.  REPAIRED, AST clean, zero raw `dump` commands left.  **STILL NOT RUN** -- the adjudicated ship order puts the commit first, then this.

It was given explicit licence to demote the row -- 'not reachable by any real guest, here is the denominator' was named as a real answer -- and it enumerated 7 handled vs 25 unhandled modes rather than asserting.
entries.note: *** THE RANKING IS SETTLED BY READING WITH A DENOMINATOR: `ip30abortkill` FIRST. ***  And the distinction that settles it is worth more than the verdict: **the gap on ip30 is 'we do not run that OS here'; the gap on armmsr is 'that OS would not do this.'  Only the second kind of gap demotes a defect.**  A process death on the documented interrupt path of the guest the machine exists to run outranks a process death that requires the guest to program a reserved mode. **Q1 -- CAN A REAL ARM GUEST REACH `armmsrmodekill`?  NO.**  `arm_save_register_bank` / `arm_load_register_bank` switch on `cpsr & 0x1f`: **7 arms handled, 25 of 32 unhandled.**  Handled: USR32 0x10, FIQ32 0x11, IRQ32 0x12, SVC32 0x13, ABT32 0x17, UND32 0x1b, SYS32 0x1f. The unhandled 25 break down as: **26-bit modes 0x00-0x03** (`cpu_arm.h` names them and `grep -c 'case ARM_MODE_USR26'` across src/ is ZERO; CATS/testarm/barearm are SA-110/SA1110 and the in-tree NetBSD `armreg.h` does not even define 26-bit modes); **0x04-0x0F unused**; **0x14/0x15/0x18/0x19/0x1c/0x1d/0x1e reserved** -- DDI 0100I A2.5.7 says *'If any other value is programmed into the mode bits M[4:0], the result is UNPREDICTABLE'*, and there are NO MSR exceptions; **0x16 Monitor** (TrustZone, not on any in-tree CPU); **0x1a Hyp** (ARMv7-A virt, likewise). A real kernel writes the named constants plus I/F -- `msr cpsr_c, #PSR_SVC32_MODE|I32_bit|F32_bit` (0xD3), IRQ 0x12, USR on process start, SYS for some copy paths -- and locore is `bic r0,r0,#0x1f ; orr r0,r0,#<legal> ; msr cpsr_c,r0`.  **Userspace cannot do it at all**: `X(msr_imm)` strips the c-byte in USR32 (`mask &= 0xff000000`). **Q2 -- THE SECOND PATH, which I had not considered and which is the one that could have been worse:** `MSR SPSR` is UNVALIDATED, and `MOVS PC, LR` / `LDM {..,pc}^` copies SPSR into CPSR **with no mode check**, after which Load dies identically.  But a correct kernel's SPSR is either the CPSR saved at exception entry (a legal mode) or a sigreturn frame, and Linux's `valid_user_regs` rejects anything whose MODE_MASK is not USR/USR26 and forces USR32.  **So the path exists and no correct kernel drives it.** **CONSEQUENCE FOR `armmsrmodekill`:** it stays a real process death and a real fix -- a hostile or buggy guest reaches it, and 25 of 32 encodings are unhandled -- but its SEVERITY is now measured rather than assumed, and it does NOT outrank ip30.  **`highrankunmeasured` is answered on the armmsr side by READING; the ip30 side stands as measured (gate_asan_sweep runs ip30 green, so the aborts are on no in-tree path).**

A `git checkout` or `stash` loses it with nothing saying so, and the ledger has already recorded the obligation as discharged. **THE DISCHARGE IS CHEAP AND OWES NO NEW MEASUREMENT.**  The three legs are preserved and the seat read them: base with the tightened oracle `accept dma ok`; the `M_lenrev` mutant with the tightened oracle `SOLE RED`; the same mutant with the SHIPPED oracle `ok` -- **that third leg is the escape, and it is a real negative control with abort-guards in both directions.**  COMMIT THE PROBE AND THE ROW CLOSES. *The brief asked "can a closure rest on a repair that was named and not applied?"  The question was moot; the live one is whether a closure can rest on a repair that exists only in an uncommitted working tree, and the answer is no.  **A premise stated as fact in a brief came back refuted with a `git show` -- the third trial of the premise-audit opener and its third catch.**  This is also the CHECK THE SEAT RECOMMENDS TO EVERY FUTURE BATCH: for each closed row, is the thing the witness names present at HEAD, or only in your working tree?*  *** NINE-ROW CLOSURE PANEL, 2026-09-17 -- AND IT CONVERGED ONCE SEAT CLASS WAS RESPECTED, WHICH IS THE DOCTRINE WORKING RATHER THAN A DISAGREEMENT. ***  Seven seats answered; the kimi CLI hit its weekly wall and its `kimi-k3:cloud` substitute COVERED the seat (not lost). **THE SPLIT IS BY SEAT CLASS, NOT BY OPINION.**  The four FILE-READING seats (opus5, grok, agy, codex) each verified against HEAD and the preserved artifacts, and reached **CLOSE on rows 1-8, KEEP-OPEN on row 9**.  The four PACKET-FED seats kept rows open where the packet could not show them a witness -- and glm stated that standard explicitly: *"I CLOSE where the packet is internally coherent and the witness shape matches the recorded defect; I KEEP-OPEN only where the packet"* cannot.  **deepseek kept all nine open "on packet-only review", which is an honest not-checkable and is NOT a vote on repo fact** -- exactly the distinction PIPELINE.md draws. *** ROW 9 IS UNANIMOUS KEEP-OPEN ACROSS EVERY SEAT THAT GAVE A PER-ROW VERDICT, AND THE ROW WAS RE-OPENED. ***  Two file-reading seats reached it by DIFFERENT EVIDENCE: opus5 diffed the working tree against HEAD and found the tightened oracle uncommitted; grok checked the `commits` field and the file's last-commit history.  codex reached it a third way -- *"row 9's 'not applied' and 'unproven' descriptions are stale locally"* -- and characterised the disposition precisely: *"an oracle repair of its own, rather than an OVERTAKEN disposition; its remaining issue is landing the validated work."* *** THE BRIEF'S OWN PREMISE ABOUT ROW 9 WAS FALSE AND TWO SEATS INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED IT SO. ***  It asserted the repair was *"named and deliberately not applied"*; it was applied and is uncommitted.  **Third trial of the premise-audit opener, third catch.** **ROW 5's LABEL DEFECT WAS FOUND BY TWO FILE-READING SEATS INDEPENDENTLY** -- opus5 and codex both report OVERTAKEN condition (2) unmet, codex putting it flatly: *"'#481's rows' is insufficient"*.  Corrected in the witness field. *** AND deepseek's HYPOTHETICAL MUTANT FOR ROW 9 IS WHAT HEAD ACTUALLY CONTAINS. ***  It proposed, as the smallest edit that breaks the fix and still passes: *"edit the oracle back to substring `Transfering`; all 62 rows stay green."*  **That is the committed state.**  A packet-fed seat with no file access described the real defect as a thought experiment -- which is the strongest possible corroboration of the two file-reading seats, precisely because it could not have been copied from the tree. **CODEX ALSO ANSWERED THE OPTION-SET QUESTION WITH FIVE IN-TREE IDIOMS THE BRIEF DID NOT NAME**, including *"combine page base with a masked virtual offset, as the MIPS translator does"* (`memory_mips_v2p.c`) -- the option-set rule working as designed, by grepping the fork rather than reasoning.  Its per-row coverage predictions are recorded as PREDICTIONS, which it said plainly: *"these are coverage predictions, not newly run mutants."*  *** F5 WITHDRAWN 2026-09-17: deepseek's 'hypothetical mutant' IS NOT CORROBORATION, and the Fable seat is right that my own rule scores it at ZERO. ***  I recorded that deepseek proposing *"edit the oracle back to substring `Transfering`; all 62 rows stay green"* was striking because it described the real committed state without file access. **The brief handed it every element**: that the old oracle was the word `Transfering`, that the repair tightens it to the COUNT, and (falsely) that the repair was not applied.  A packet-fed seat answering the smallest-edit question from those three sentences produces that mutant BY CONSTRUCTION. *"It could not have been copied from the tree" is true and IRRELEVANT: it was copied from the packet.*  The standing rule -- score agreement only where a seat re-derived something the brief did NOT give it -- scores this at zero.  **The evidence for the breach is leg 3 of the preserved three-leg measurement (`probe_M_lenrev_SHIPPED.raw`, 62/62, `accept dma ok`), not deepseek.** *I found the coincidence striking and wrote it up as corroboration without asking what the packet had already told the seat -- which is the unanimity-is-worth-nothing rule landing on me, one level up.*  *** L4 -- I RECORDED THE BRIEF'S OWN HEADINGS AS CODEX'S ANSWER ON ALL NINE ROWS.  Found by the Fable seat, corrected 2026-09-17. ***  My extraction matched the first line containing the row id and a word from `CLOSE|KEEP-OPEN|NOT CHECKABLE` -- and **`CLOSE` matched the word `closed` inside the brief's own heading**, which codex echoes.  So nine cells read `### N. <id> (SEV, closed) -- <title>`: the packet, handed back as the seat's verdict. *** IT IS WORSE THAN AN UNREAD REVIEW AND FABLE SAID WHY: "an unread review filed under a RECORDED seat -- section G cannot see it because an entry exists." ***  The blank that would have been caught was filled with something that looks like an answer. **AND MY OWN AUDIT OF IT UNDER-COUNTED 9 AS 6**, because the pattern I checked required a severity token `(LOW|MED|HIGH)` and three headings carry only `(closed)`.  *Sixth correlate-keyed check of this session, committed inside the audit of the fifth.* Codex's real verdict, recorded now: **CLOSE 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8; KEEP-OPEN 3, 5, 9.**  *** L4 -- MY 'SPLIT BY SEAT CLASS' ADJUDICATION IS A WRONG RECORD, AND THE FABLE SEAT SHOWED IT IS FALSE ON THE PACKET'S OWN DATA. The carriers that do the GDROM work are `impl ok` (CNTHI store/readback -- the row this file ALREADY added after measuring a value-only device row vacuous) and `scan uniq`.**  The project's own CHANGELOG had already ruled `live` "is a liveness control and CANNOT DO MORE", so my list repeated a mislabel the record had corrected once. **THE MEASURED ANSWER, per medium:** garbage BIN -> every session dies, `live` wants 0x12345678 and gets "died", `GDROM_DEF_CONTROL=DEAD`, result 0/62 or no `_RESULT=` line at all; comment-only product source -> does not COMPILE (the `Mc_null` form); GDROM removed or emptied -> `impl ok` and `scan uniq` red, DMA rows red with them.  **Not green on any medium clause (c) has ever been scored on.** **Q3, THE GATE PIN:** it is neither sufficient nor necessary, and the honest statement is both halves.  Not sufficient -- kill tables grep `GDROM_DEF_RESULT=n/n` without asserting `n==62`, and a gate can `gate_skip`. A hygiene self-pin (`if len(rows) != 62: n = 0` before the `_RESULT=` print) is available, moves no row, and is NOT owed. **ONE REAL SHAPE THE SEAT NAMED AND DID NOT DISMISS:** a STALE detector -- 58 rows, all green, reporting `58/58` -- WOULD look clean standalone. rows.title: adjudicate.sh's seat-check loop kept the superseded glm-5.3-flash tag after the fire loop migrated to glm-5.3, so a LIVE seat was reported as NO ANSWER and its 8.7 KB answer was nearly discarded
rows.state_note: *** A LIVE SEAT WAS REPORTED MISSING, AND THIS FILE'S OWN COMMENT PREDICTED IT IN THOSE WORDS. ***  `adjudicate.sh' fires its cloud seats in one loop and CHECKS them in a second, and the second must carry the ${m%%:*} SHORT FORM of the first because that is how the output filenames are built.  The 2026-08-29 migration glm-5.3-flash -> glm-5.3 changed the FIRE loop and not the CHECK loop.  So the run wrote glm-5.3.txt while the check hunted glm-5.3-flash.txt, and it printed `glm-5.3-flash: NO ANSWER (0b)' and `ADJUDICATORS: 2/3'.  *** glm HAD ANSWERED WITH 8,693 BYTES, FOUR DEFECTS AND THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IN THE ADJUDICATION -- an oracle that would have certified a live defect GREEN. ***  The comment immediately above the broken line reads: 'Updating the fire loop alone would leave this one looking for glm-5.2.txt, which the run never writes -- so a LIVE seat would be reported as a missing one.  That is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape arriving through a rename rather than through a wall.'  The structure knew; the edit did not.  FIXED 2026-09-17: both loops now agree on glm-5.3.  [2026-11-02, records: not true of any commit -- at 987cb596 tools/adjudicate.sh:103 still reads `for m in glm-5.3-flash deepseek-v4-pro minimax-m3; do` while the fire loop (:89) is on glm-5.3, and the file's last commit is 55ef9db5 (2026-08-29); the fix this sentence records is not committed.]  Note the fix is a RETYPE and therefore has the same failure mode next migration -- deriving the check list from the fire list with ${m%%:*} is the structural form and is NOT done here, because it changes a script every adjudication runs and owes its own negative controls.

A LIVE seat was reported `NO ANSWER (0b)` and its 8.7 KB answer -- carrying the adjudication's single most important finding -- was nearly discarded.  The comment directly above the broken line had predicted this exact failure in those words. rows.title: check_probe_wiring.py's MANIFEST governs the EVIDENCE ARCHIVE as well as live instruments, so 148 artifact ghosts drown the 2 real findings -- and 3 keys are GHOST by construction because domain() only lists *.py
rows.state_note: *** TWO JOBS GLUED TOGETHER: a WIRING check (detectors/witnesses) and a CENSUS (every *.py domain() returns).  The 148 artifact ghosts are the CENSUS firing on files the WIRING job does not care about, and they hid the 2 real findings. ***  Measured: 692 MANIFEST keys, 582 under artifacts/, 110 top-level; 150 GHOST of which 148 artifacts/ and 2 top-level.  *** THREE KEYS ARE GHOST BY CONSTRUCTION AND CAN NEVER PASS: laneP.sh, laneQ.sh, mkfreeze.sh -- domain() is `git ls-files -- *.py' and a .sh can never be in that set. ***  MY PROPOSED FIX (scope to top-level) WAS REFUTED BY ONE MEASURED FACT: exactly one artifacts/**.py IS gate-executed -- gate_sh_rounding.sh:1029 [at 987cb596: :1028] GPNPROBE=artifacts/gdrompionull/gdrom_pio_null_probe.py, a live CLASS_DETECTOR whose absence guard is `gate_skip' (silent coverage loss scored as a SKIP), and #471's M13/M14/M15 exist so that path cannot go invisible.  Flattening re-opens #465.  Option (b) is ALREADY SHIPPED as CLASS_RESEARCH and did not help, because GHOST tests TRACKEDNESS not class.  Option (c) would make 148 immortal exemptions, i.e. a switched-off check.  ADOPT (a'): domain() excludes artifacts/ as gate_hygiene.sh already does, EXCEPT gate-invoked paths.  NOT BUILT -- it changes a checker every commit runs, owes two negative controls (prove the exception fires; prove a frozen copy is not demanded), and ships as its own HARNESS ROUND.  Same round owes the docstring fix: it still claims 'a few dozen files in ONE FLAT DIRECTORY' while domain() has been recursive since #471.

The shipped 33-row instrument's matched pair: PRE-FIX 10/33 (23 rows red, every abort site among them) -> POST-FIX 33/33, one instrument, HEAD's sources in a scratch clone (regress/artifacts/ip30abortkill/gatewire_20261018/legs/).  Still owed before close (target: before the 2026-10-25 battery): the witness field still leads with the 21-row pair; clause (b) -- abort() re-inserted at each fixed site of the FIXED file, re-run at 33 rows -- is held by no kill table; and a ruling on whether V7_nocounter and V8_len4 need a carrier that survives the close (Grok 4.7: no).  A load stall can read green in gate 14: ip30stallgreen.  ||  *** ONE GUEST LOAD OR STORE AT 0x0ff10020 ON THE ADVERTISED `-E sgi -e ip30` RAISES SIGABRT. AN `exit(` SWEEP CANNOT SEE IT, BECAUSE `abort()` CONTAINS NO `exit(`. ***  FOUR abort() SITES IN ONE FILE, all verified by reading dev_sgi_ip30.c at HEAD:  (1) :127 `case 0x10020` Set ISR; (2) :135 `case 0x10028` Clear ISR; (3) :145 `case 0x10030` write arm; (4) :78 the DEVICE_TICK. REACHABILITY: `DEV_SGI_IP30_LENGTH` is 0x80000 (:44) registered at :387, the device is added at `machine_sgi.c:417` as `sgi_ip30 addr=0x0ff00000`, and the subtype is ADVERTISED at `machine_sgi.c:744` -- `machine_entry_add_subtype(me, "IP30", 30, "ip30", "octane", NULL)`. 0x10020/0x10028/0x10030 all fall inside the window. *** TWO FACTS THE HUNTING SEAT DID NOT STATE, FOUND BY READING THE ARM, AND BOTH RAISE THE SEVERITY: ***  (A) **`case 0x10020` HAS NO `writeflag` TEST AND EXECUTES `d->isr = idata;` FIRST.**  `idata` is initialised to 0 at :87 and assigned ONLY under `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE)` at :89-90, so a guest **LOAD** at 0x0ff10020 ZEROES THE INTERRUPT STATUS REGISTER and *then* aborts.  That is GUEST-STATE CORRUPTION AND A HOST DEATH IN THE SAME ARM, and it means the defect is not write-only as a reader would assume from the `Set ISR` comment.  `case 0x10028` shares the missing test (its `d->isr &= ~idata` is a no-op at idata==0, then aborts).  `case 0x10030` IS writeflag-tested and reads return `d->isr` correctly -- so the three arms are NOT uniform, and a detector must row them separately.  (B) **THE TICK ABORT IS ARMED BY A LEGAL WRITE TO AN IMPLEMENTED REGISTER.**  `case 0x10000` (:99-105) implements imask0 and ACCEPTS the write; the tick at :74-78 then aborts whenever `d->imask0 & (1<<50)`.  So the guest makes an accepted, unremarkable register write and the host dies LATER, from a different code path, with no access in flight.  That is the de-escalation shape at its worst: the announcing access succeeds. OPTION SET: member **7 IMPLEMENT** is the strong candidate -- every one of the four sites has the intended model sitting beside it as a commented-out `cpu_interrupt(...)` call, so this is a stubbed path (no predicate refusing a value), which is exactly the tell member 7 was minted for. Member **3 DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE** is the fallback if the interrupt rewrite stays out of scope.  Member 5 FAULT is architecturally available here (MIPS dispatches on a failed device access) but is INERT as the code stands, because `abort()` fires before any `return 0`. GATE COVERAGE: NONE.  No ip30 probe exists under `regress/`.  Gate 9 may CONSTRUCT the machine, but nothing feeds 0x10020 -- the same blind spot as `armmsrmodekill`. SEVERITY HIGH: `abort()` is strictly worse than `exit(1)` (SIGABRT plus a core dump), it is on an advertised subtype, and one of the four paths corrupts guest state before dying.  Honest limit: there is NO in-tree Octane boot image, so this ranks probe-HIGH and not boot-HIGH -- the same standing as `mapledmaaddr` and `vmedefaultkill`.  Reachability is CONFIRMED BY READING and is NOT YET MEASURED; the round owes a rung-3 probe on unmodified `-E sgi -e ip30` (`ld`/`sd` at 0x0ff10020), plus a separate row for the armed-tick path, before any edit. NO EXISTING ROW COVERS THIS.  Nine ledger rows mention ip30 or abort(): `exitsweep` is CLOSED and counts `exit(` sites, not `abort()`; `ctorabortclass` is HELD and is the CONSTRUCTION abort class (nine subtypes across five families, none of them ip30 -- ip30 constructs fine, which is why this one is guest-reachable rather than construction-time); `hpcabort` is CLOSED and is hpcmips construction; `asansweepblind` is DROPPED and is about gate 9's blindness to construction aborts.  `exitunowned76` counts `exit(`.  `cpusexitsweep` is src/cpus/ only.  The site was NAMED ONCE, in the 2026-08-17 `exitsweep` correction in OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md ("No abort() is guest-reachable is FALSE"), and never given an id -- so it has been a known-but-unqueued exposure for a month.  *** RUNG-3 WITNESS BUILT AND MEASURED 2026-09-17.  THE DEFECT IS NO LONGER CONFIRMED-BY-READING; IT IS MEASURED. ***  `IP30ABORT_CONTROL=OK`, `IP30ABORT_RESULT=6/9` on the committed build, with the three kill rows RED -- which IS the reproduction, since the house polarity is WANT = POST-FIX CORRECT.  Measured, on unmodified `-E sgi -e ip30' with no `device_add' introduced to reach the site: **a guest LOAD at 0x0ff10020 kills the host** (`kill 20 rd' DEAD); so does a load at 0x10028; so does a WRITE at 0x10030 -- while a READ at 0x10030 is SERVICED (`acc 30 rd' alive).  **The three arms are provably NOT uniform**, which was a reading and is now a measurement.  The raw disposition was captured separately: `KILLED BY SIGNAL 6 (SIGABRT) after 0.6 s`, and the tree installs no SIGABRT handler. *** AND THE FIRST RUN OF THAT PROBE REPORTED `alive' FOR ALL THREE KILL ROWS -- A FALSE GREEN ON A LIVE HOST DEATH -- FOR A REASON WORTH CARRYING INTO EVERY EOF-ORACLE PROBE IN THIS TREE. ***  `rd()` RETURNS IMMEDIATELY ON EOF instead of waiting out its timeout, so the `spin` that exists to give a dying child time to die is SKIPPED EXACTLY WHEN THE CHILD DIES.  A single `waitpid(WNOHANG)` then samples ~0 s after EOF while the kernel is still writing a 6 MB core, reports 'still running', and the kill row goes GREEN.  **The fix is to POLL with a deadline, never to sample once** -- and `arm_msrmode_probe.py`, whose every kill row is an EOF oracle, MUST carry the polling form or its witness will certify the MSR defect fixed while it is live. *A second apparatus error in the same run, caught by the same disagreement: my `devsig` and `acc 18` oracles wanted truncated values, but `lw` SIGN-EXTENDS on this 64-bit R10000, so a CORRECT device reddened.  The apparatus was wrong, not the model.* ## FIX DESIGN, ADJUDICATED -- **MEMBER 3 + MEMBER 4, AND THE writeflag TEST IN THE SAME DIFF.** *** MY MEMBER-7 PREMISE WAS REFUTED BY A REPO FACT, NOT BY ARGUMENT. ***  I filed that member 7 IMPLEMENT was the strong candidate because every site carries its intended model beside it as a commented-out `cpu_interrupt(...)`.  **THAT API NO LONGER EXISTS.**  Verified locally: `cpu_interrupt(` occurs FIVE times in the entire tree -- one warning comment in `dev_lca.c` and the four commented-out calls here -- with no definition and no declaration; the live API is `interrupt_assert` through `struct interrupt` (`cpu_mips.c:1884`).  **Uncommenting does not compile.**  The tell was right (a stubbed path with no predicate); the inference that it was cheap was wrong. Further, `machine_sgi.c:415` for case 30 is literally `// TODO: Interrupts!` -- no INTERRUPT_CONNECT, no HEART lines -- and the serial is already routed AROUND HEART onto `cpu.2`.  The fossil literals use a DELETED numbering scheme (`8 + x`, so the tick's `cpu_interrupt(cpu, 8+1+50)` is 59), so translating them onto `INTERRUPT_ASSERT(cpu.2)` would be a WRONG MODEL, not a restore.  A cheap HEART sharing `cpu.2` with the 16550 breaks on deassert (assert ORs, deassert ANDs off), which is exactly why CRIME exists.  **`#516` refused member 7 on `lca_interrupt_assert` after naming the same tell -- the precedent is in-tree.** **MEMBER 7 IS THE FOLLOW-UP ROW** (implement HEART the way `dev_sgi_ip32.c` implements CRIME: INTERRUPT_CONNECT to cpu.2, named child lines, a reassert function), NOT this de-fatalisation. **MEMBER 5 FAULT is AVAILABLE and WRONG.**  `memory_rw.c` turns a device `return 0` into `EXCEPTION_DBE` on MIPS, so it works -- but these offsets are NOT unmapped space: they have storage, comments, and a PROM that already talks to the neighbour at 0x10018.  `dev_unreadable.c` is the FAULT idiom and is for holes.  *Note the brief's own framing was weak here and the seat said so: `abort()` firing before any `return 0` is a description of the current kill, not a design warrant either way.* **Q3 -- THE writeflag TEST IS A SEPARATE DEFECT AND IS NOT OPTIONAL.**  This is the `asicindexcase` / `mvme187memcoob` shape: the kill is currently also the direction check.  De-fatalise 0x10020 without adding the test and **the host lives on with a guest-clobbered ISR** -- worse than today.  0x10028 shares the missing test and does not corrupt today (`&= ~0` is a no-op) but gets it anyway, so the twins stay twins.  0x10030 already has it and its reads work NOW -- an existing accept-side channel that must not break. entries.grader: grok 4.6 xhigh, fired on an open critical-bug hunt asking what guest-reachable host death or guest-state corruption an `exit(` grep CANNOT find, with an honesty clause that an empty result with its denominator is a real answer. EVERY load-bearing claim re-derived locally before filing; two facts were added by that re-derivation and one citation (machine_m88k.c) corrected.
entries.note: *** ONE GUEST LOAD OR STORE AT 0x0ff10020 ON THE ADVERTISED `-E sgi -e ip30` RAISES SIGABRT. AN `exit(` SWEEP CANNOT SEE IT, BECAUSE `abort()` CONTAINS NO `exit(`. ***  FOUR abort() SITES IN ONE FILE, all verified by reading dev_sgi_ip30.c at HEAD:  (1) :127 `case 0x10020` Set ISR; (2) :135 `case 0x10028` Clear ISR; (3) :145 `case 0x10030` write arm; (4) :78 the DEVICE_TICK. REACHABILITY: `DEV_SGI_IP30_LENGTH` is 0x80000 (:44) registered at :387, the device is added at `machine_sgi.c:417` as `sgi_ip30 addr=0x0ff00000`, and the subtype is ADVERTISED at `machine_sgi.c:744` -- `machine_entry_add_subtype(me, "IP30", 30, "ip30", "octane", NULL)`. 0x10020/0x10028/0x10030 all fall inside the window. *** TWO FACTS THE HUNTING SEAT DID NOT STATE, FOUND BY READING THE ARM, AND BOTH RAISE THE SEVERITY: ***  (A) **`case 0x10020` HAS NO `writeflag` TEST AND EXECUTES `d->isr = idata;` FIRST.**  `idata` is initialised to 0 at :87 and assigned ONLY under `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE)` at :89-90, so a guest **LOAD** at 0x0ff10020 ZEROES THE INTERRUPT STATUS REGISTER and *then* aborts.  That is GUEST-STATE CORRUPTION AND A HOST DEATH IN THE SAME ARM, and it means the defect is not write-only as a reader would assume from the `Set ISR` comment.  `case 0x10028` shares the missing test (its `d->isr &= ~idata` is a no-op at idata==0, then aborts).  `case 0x10030` IS writeflag-tested and reads return `d->isr` correctly -- so the three arms are NOT uniform, and a detector must row them separately.  (B) **THE TICK ABORT IS ARMED BY A LEGAL WRITE TO AN IMPLEMENTED REGISTER.**  `case 0x10000` (:99-105) implements imask0 and ACCEPTS the write; the tick at :74-78 then aborts whenever `d->imask0 & (1<<50)`.  So the guest makes an accepted, unremarkable register write and the host dies LATER, from a different code path, with no access in flight.  That is the de-escalation shape at its worst: the announcing access succeeds. OPTION SET: member **7 IMPLEMENT** is the strong candidate -- every one of the four sites has the intended model sitting beside it as a commented-out `cpu_interrupt(...)` call, so this is a stubbed path (no predicate refusing a value), which is exactly the tell member 7 was minted for. Member **3 DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE** is the fallback if the interrupt rewrite stays out of scope.  Member 5 FAULT is architecturally available here (MIPS dispatches on a failed device access) but is INERT as the code stands, because `abort()` fires before any `return 0`. GATE COVERAGE: NONE.  No ip30 probe exists under `regress/`.  Gate 9 may CONSTRUCT the machine, but nothing feeds 0x10020 -- the same blind spot as `armmsrmodekill`. SEVERITY HIGH: `abort()` is strictly worse than `exit(1)` (SIGABRT plus a core dump), it is on an advertised subtype, and one of the four paths corrupts guest state before dying.  Honest limit: there is NO in-tree Octane boot image, so this ranks probe-HIGH and not boot-HIGH -- the same standing as `mapledmaaddr` and `vmedefaultkill`.  Reachability is CONFIRMED BY READING and is NOT YET MEASURED; the round owes a rung-3 probe on unmodified `-E sgi -e ip30` (`ld`/`sd` at 0x0ff10020), plus a separate row for the armed-tick path, before any edit. NO EXISTING ROW COVERS THIS.  Nine ledger rows mention ip30 or abort(): `exitsweep` is CLOSED and counts `exit(` sites, not `abort()`; `ctorabortclass` is HELD and is the CONSTRUCTION abort class (nine subtypes across five families, none of them ip30 -- ip30 constructs fine, which is why this one is guest-reachable rather than construction-time); `hpcabort` is CLOSED and is hpcmips construction; `asansweepblind` is DROPPED and is about gate 9's blindness to construction aborts.  `exitunowned76` counts `exit(`.  `cpusexitsweep` is src/cpus/ only.  The site was NAMED ONCE, in the 2026-08-17 `exitsweep` correction in OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md ("No abort() is guest-reachable is FALSE"), and never given an id -- so it has been a known-but-unqueued exposure for a month.

entries.grader: main loop, rung-3 witness BUILT AND RUN against the committed build/gxemul (itself freshly two-part-cleared the same hour).  Two apparatus errors of mine were caught inside the run and are recorded rather than quietly fixed.
entries.note: *** RUNG-3 WITNESS BUILT AND MEASURED 2026-09-17.  THE DEFECT IS NO LONGER CONFIRMED-BY-READING; IT IS MEASURED. ***  `IP30ABORT_CONTROL=OK`, `IP30ABORT_RESULT=6/9` on the committed build, with the three kill rows RED -- which IS the reproduction, since the house polarity is WANT = POST-FIX CORRECT.  Measured, on unmodified `-E sgi -e ip30' with no `device_add' introduced to reach the site: **a guest LOAD at 0x0ff10020 kills the host** (`kill 20 rd' DEAD); so does a load at 0x10028; so does a WRITE at 0x10030 -- while a READ at 0x10030 is SERVICED (`acc 30 rd' alive).  **The three arms are provably NOT uniform**, which was a reading and is now a measurement.  The raw disposition was captured separately: `KILLED BY SIGNAL 6 (SIGABRT) after 0.6 s`, and the tree installs no SIGABRT handler. *** AND THE FIRST RUN OF THAT PROBE REPORTED `alive' FOR ALL THREE KILL ROWS -- A FALSE GREEN ON A LIVE HOST DEATH -- FOR A REASON WORTH CARRYING INTO EVERY EOF-ORACLE PROBE IN THIS TREE. ***  `rd()` RETURNS IMMEDIATELY ON EOF instead of waiting out its timeout, so the `spin` that exists to give a dying child time to die is SKIPPED EXACTLY WHEN THE CHILD DIES.  A single `waitpid(WNOHANG)` then samples ~0 s after EOF while the kernel is still writing a 6 MB core, reports 'still running', and the kill row goes GREEN.  **The fix is to POLL with a deadline, never to sample once** -- and `arm_msrmode_probe.py`, whose every kill row is an EOF oracle, MUST carry the polling form or its witness will certify the MSR defect fixed while it is live. *A second apparatus error in the same run, caught by the same disagreement: my `devsig` and `acc 18` oracles wanted truncated values, but `lw` SIGN-EXTENDS on this 64-bit R10000, so a CORRECT device reddened.  The apparatus was wrong, not the model.* ## FIX DESIGN, ADJUDICATED -- **MEMBER 3 + MEMBER 4, AND THE writeflag TEST IN THE SAME DIFF.** *** MY MEMBER-7 PREMISE WAS REFUTED BY A REPO FACT, NOT BY ARGUMENT. ***  I filed that member 7 IMPLEMENT was the strong candidate because every site carries its intended model beside it as a commented-out `cpu_interrupt(...)`.  **THAT API NO LONGER EXISTS.**  Verified locally: `cpu_interrupt(` occurs FIVE times in the entire tree -- one warning comment in `dev_lca.c` and the four commented-out calls here -- with no definition and no declaration; the live API is `interrupt_assert` through `struct interrupt` (`cpu_mips.c:1884`).  **Uncommenting does not compile.**  The tell was right (a stubbed path with no predicate); the inference that it was cheap was wrong. Further, `machine_sgi.c:415` for case 30 is literally `// TODO: Interrupts!` -- no INTERRUPT_CONNECT, no HEART lines -- and the serial is already routed AROUND HEART onto `cpu.2`.  The fossil literals use a DELETED numbering scheme (`8 + x`, so the tick's `cpu_interrupt(cpu, 8+1+50)` is 59), so translating them onto `INTERRUPT_ASSERT(cpu.2)` would be a WRONG MODEL, not a restore.  A cheap HEART sharing `cpu.2` with the 16550 breaks on deassert (assert ORs, deassert ANDs off), which is exactly why CRIME exists.  **`#516` refused member 7 on `lca_interrupt_assert` after naming the same tell -- the precedent is in-tree.** **MEMBER 7 IS THE FOLLOW-UP ROW** (implement HEART the way `dev_sgi_ip32.c` implements CRIME: INTERRUPT_CONNECT to cpu.2, named child lines, a reassert function), NOT this de-fatalisation. **MEMBER 5 FAULT is AVAILABLE and WRONG.**  `memory_rw.c` turns a device `return 0` into `EXCEPTION_DBE` on MIPS, so it works -- but these offsets are NOT unmapped space: they have storage, comments, and a PROM that already talks to the neighbour at 0x10018.  `dev_unreadable.c` is the FAULT idiom and is for holes.  *Note the brief's own framing was weak here and the seat said so: `abort()` firing before any `return 0` is a description of the current kill, not a design warrant either way.* **Q3 -- THE writeflag TEST IS A SEPARATE DEFECT AND IS NOT OPTIONAL.**  This is the `asicindexcase` / `mvme187memcoob` shape: the kill is currently also the direction check.  De-fatalise 0x10020 without adding the test and **the host lives on with a guest-clobbered ISR** -- worse than today.  0x10028 shares the missing test and does not corrupt today (`&= ~0` is a no-op) but gets it anyway, so the twins stay twins.  0x10030 already has it and its reads work NOW -- an existing accept-side channel that must not break.  Owed row: a load at 0x10020 leaves ISR unchanged (seed via a write, `lw`, read back at 0x10030). **Q4 -- YOU DO NOT DECLINE A TICK; YOU STUB THE CALLBACK.**  Members 1-6 presume an access with a value to refuse, and the `:78` abort has none -- the guest already completed a LEGAL write to an IMPLEMENTED register.  No new option-set member is minted: this is member 3 applied to a callback, exactly as `#516` did for `lca_interrupt_assert`.  The tick also does not implement its own comment (no compare of 0x20000 against 0x30000), so a member-7 timer would have to ADD that, not merely delete the abort. **Q5 -- DE-ESCALATION ACCEPT ROWS.**  `0x10000` is not 'maybe an accept row' -- for the tick it IS the accept row, because that write is what used to arm the host death; it owes a companion row that the host SURVIVES the next tick.  Neighbours to pin: 0x20, 0x10000, 0x10018, 0x10030 READ, 0x20000, 0x30000.  **The latch must be TWO BITS, not one** (tick vs ISR-recalc): a shared bit lets the first shape silence the second, which is LCA's assert/deassert lesson. **Q6 -- SIBLINGS, GREPPED.**  `dev_sgi_ip19.c` and `dev_sgi_ip20.c` use `debug()` + `return 1` for unknown offsets; **this file's OWN `default:` does the same**.  So the ISR arms are the file's outliers, not the house idiom -- the same upstream-residue finding that settled `sgireunmapped`. **WITNESS LIMIT, STATED:** the probe covers the three ACCESS kills and does NOT cover the TICK kill.  `tickshift` is 16, so the tick fires every 65536 cycles and a handful of `step`s cannot reach it -- that needs `continue`/free-run, which is the same step-vs-free-run distinction the carrier already records for host-timer paths.  The tick row is OWED and is not claimed.

entries.note: *** THE TICK ROW IS BUILDABLE AND IS MEASURED: `step 1' KILLS THE HOST.  The codex/agy split is settled BY MEASUREMENT, and BOTH SEATS WERE HALF RIGHT WHILE THE DECISIVE FACT WAS NAMED BY NEITHER. ***  codex was right that stepping alone is insufficient -- the guard must be ARMED (measured: no store + 70000 steps -> alive; bit 49 + 70000 steps -> alive).  agy was right that free-run is NOT needed, but its stated reason -- a 65536-cycle period implying `step 70000' -- is not why the cheap row works.  **THE MECHANISM, verified by me in the source and not taken from the seat:** `machine_add_tickfunction' sets `ticks_till_next[n] = 0' (`machine.c:354') while `ticks_reset_value[n] = 1 << tickshift' (`:355'), and `machine_run()' decrements then fires while `<= 0' (`:727').  **So the FIRST `machine_run()' of any session drives it to -1 and fires EVERY tick function immediately** -- `step 1' executes the store and then runs the tick in that same `machine_run()'.  *** A THIRD FACT NEITHER SEAT NAMED, AND IT IS A FALSE-GREEN TRAP I WOULD HAVE WALKED INTO: **BIT 50 CANNOT BE SET BY `sw'.** ***  `case 0x10000' does `d->imask0 = idata' with `idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len)', so a FOUR-BYTE store caps idata below 2^32 -- measured, `sw 0xffffffff' + 70000 steps -> ALIVE.  Arming requires **`sd' = 0xFCE80000** (readback `ld' = 0xDC220000).  **`OP_SW_T0_A3' IS THE ONLY STORE HELPER IN `ip30_abort_probe.py'**, so a tick row copy-pasted from it would arm nothing, stay alive, and SCORE GREEN ON A LIVE HOST DEATH.  **PERIODICITY IS NOT A STARTUP ARTIFACT** -- the boundary was measured from TWO different warm offsets, both sides: warm=10 gives alive at N=65525 and DEAD at 65526; warm=100 gives alive at 65435 and DEAD at 65436.  Both put tick #2 at `machine_run' #65536 exactly, so ticks fire at MR #1, #65536, #131072.  **A guest arming bit 50 at ANY moment dies within 65536 instructions, with no access in flight.**  *The seat's own first derivation said #65537 and its boundary run measured that false -- it recorded the measurement over its derivation, which is the right way round.*  STABILITY: run 1 and run 2 are BYTE-IDENTICAL across all 13 scored rows (9/13, same four FAILs), `IP30TICK_CONTROL=OK` both times.  CONTROLS ALL GREEN, including the two that make the positive attributable: **`tick49 s70k'** (same store, same step count, bit 49 not 50 -> alive) is the discriminator, and **`late s1'** (armed AFTER tick #1 was consumed, one step -> alive) is what proves `tick50 s1' measured THE TICK and not something else about the first instruction.  **L4 APPLIED TO MY OWN PROBE:** `ip30_abort_probe.py`'s `acc imask' row claimed "a handful of steps cannot reach it".  MEASURED FALSE.  The row is still safe, for two reasons it did not state (bit 18, and `sw' cannot set bit 50 anyway), and the comment now says so.  **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUND:** codex's constraint is DISCHARGEABLE rather than blocking -- the four-site closure is available because the tick row exists and is measured.  Artifacts at `regress/artifacts/ip30abortkill/tick_20260917/`, all four carrying their completion sentinel, copied off the volatile scratch path the measuring seat itself flagged.

entries.grader: main loop, after the owner authorised fetching an IP30/HEART reference.  The source was chosen because THE CODE CITES IT, not because it was findable, and every offset was re-verified against the fork before citation.
entries.note: *** Q3 IS SETTLED BY THE DOCUMENT THE CODE ITSELF CITES, AND THE ANSWER ARRIVED WITH A NEW FINDING. ***  `dev_sgi_ip30.c` says "according to Linux/IP30" three times, so the reference is Linux's `arch/mips/include/asm/sgi/heart.h` -- fetched with the owner's approval on this project's vmesbcp2 / 21066 / ddi0406 precedent, then VERIFIED LOCALLY offset by offset before anything was cited.  **Every offset matches the fork exactly**, base included (0x0ff00000 vs `machine_sgi.c:417`). **THE ANSWER: `set_isr` (0x10020) and `clear_isr` (0x10028) are WRITE-SIDE registers.**  The architectural triple is set / clear / status -- write set_isr to set, write clear_isr to clear, READ `isr` for status.  A read of set_isr has NO defined meaning, so **do not mirror `d->isr` there** (that fabricates semantics, which the addition licence forbids) and **DECLINE the read** -- now a TRANSFERRED WARRANT rather than the conservative guess it was when minimax said the packet could not settle it. *** AND IT UPGRADES THE `writeflag` TEST FROM DEFENSIVE TO CORRECT: *** it was argued as a direction guard; the reference makes it ARCHITECTURE, because executing a write-side register's store arm on a READ is wrong on its own terms, independently of the host death. *** NEW FINDING, AND THE CODE ASKED FOR IT IN ITS OWN COMMENT: heart.h documents `isr` (0x10030) as READ-ONLY, and the fork implements a WRITE arm -- `/* Clear-on-write (TODO: is this correct?) */  d->isr &= ~idata;`.  The cited document answers that TODO: NO. ***  Clearing goes through `clear_isr` at 0x10028, which this same file already implements, so the model has TWO clear paths where the architecture has ONE, and the fabricated one is the one carrying the self-doubting comment.  IN SCOPE for this round (same case labels, same function, same detector); it is a member 6 BACKED ACCEPT standing WITHOUT a warrant, which the addition licence does not permit.  Disposition deliberately NOT decided here. **HONEST LIMIT, STATED:** a Linux header is a driver author's model, NOT SGI's specification. It is strong evidence about what the registers ARE and about what this emulator MEANT -- because this emulator cites it -- and it is not a hardware contract.  No claim above depends on the difference: declining a read is safe under either reading.  Preserved at regress/artifacts/ip30abortkill/HEART_reference_20260917.txt.
