entries.note: *** FABLE 5.1 ADJUDICATION, 2026-09-17.  IDENTITY VERIFIED -- `claude-fable-5-1`, the nonce, AND the verbatim first line of CHECKPOINT.md, so prompt delivery and file access are proven rather than assumed.  Fired LAST, after all 8 scriptable transports and the Opus measurement. *** **SHIP ORDER: (c) commit the reviewed working set -> (b) run `arm_msrmode_probe.py` -> (a) the ip30 fix as its OWN round.**  Serialisation note it supplied and I had not: (b) runs the emulator and (c) runs a gate, and they contend on CPU but NOT on the tree -- so run (b) to completion, THEN (c)'s gate alone. **A2 -- Q3 IS ALREADY ANSWERED AND THE FIX DOES NOT WAIT.**  DECLINE the read at 0x10020; do not mirror `d->isr`, do not return 0-as-a-value.  *** AND IT RULED ON A SECOND DISPOSITION MY FIVE QUESTIONS NEVER REACHED: DECLINE THE 0x10030 **WRITE** ARM TOO. ***  heart.h documents `isr` as read-only and the fork's clear-on-write is a member-6 BACKED ACCEPT standing without a warrant, which the addition licence does not permit -- Linux/IP30 clears via 0x10028, which the file already implements.  Same function, same case labels, same detector family, so same round.  It owes a STATE row (write declined AND `isr` unchanged), not merely an `alive' row. **A3 -- MY FRAMING WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART.**  These are not four defects competing to join a round under the reopening rule.  **They are ONE ABANDONED FEATURE** -- the identical `fatal("IP30 legacy interrupt rewrite: TODO"); abort();` at every reachable exit of a rewrite nobody finished.  The unit of work is the FEATURE, not the site, and splitting it would de-fatalise three of four exits and leave the fourth a live host death, which is the de-escalation clause's own hazard.  *** AND IT REFUSED TO LET ME GLOSS THE COST: the 'no new oracle' criterion IS genuinely violated -- the tick needs its own periodicity oracle and its own latch bit, so THE ROUND SHIPS TWO DETECTORS, and the round record must NAME that deviation rather than let a two-probe structure read as an accident. *** **A4 -- IT FOUND MY WEAKEST CORRECTION AND IT IS RIGHT.**  My (iv) said the `acc imask' row is safe *because it writes bit 18 AND because `sw' cannot set bit 50*.  Both clauses are true and **clause (2) MISDIRECTS**: the row's value `1<<18` has no high bits at any width, so width is irrelevant to THIS row -- while 'sw cannot set bit 50' reads as a general safety invariant for imask0, and **the death IS reachable, by `sd 1<<50`**.  *** MY OWN PROBE'S COMMENT IS STRONGER AND MORE HONEST THAN MY SUMMARY OF IT: it calls that row a documented HAZARD and warns that copy-pasting it as a kill row would 'arm NOTHING, stay ALIVE, and score green on a live host death'.  My correction re-labelled a HAZARD as a SAFETY PROPERTY. ***  That is the a-correction-is-not-safer-than-what-it-corrects rule landing on me. **A4(i) -- MY WARRANT OVERCLAIMED TRANSFERABILITY, verified locally:** `dev_sgi_ip32.c` has 6 INTERRUPT_CONNECT/ASSERT sites; **`dev_sgi_ip30.c` has ZERO, and zero `struct interrupt` members.**  'CRIME uses it' proves the IDIOM exists on MIPS; it does not prove member 7 is BUILDABLE for ip30, which has no interrupt topology at all.  The correct statement is *member 7's idiom is available; its application to ip30 requires building the HEART topology and is substantial* -- which is the carrier's own 2026-09-06 lesson (check the member is available on THIS CPU; a precedent real elsewhere is not thereby transferable). **A5 -- THE QUESTION I WAS NOT ASKING, AND IT IS THE RIGHT ONE: DOES `ip30abortkill` ACTUALLY OUTRANK `armmsrmodekill`?**  Rung is a FLOOR ON ADMISSIBILITY; SEVERITY orders the queue, and severity rests on real-guest reachability **that is measured for NEITHER**.  Verified locally: `gate_asan_sweep.sh:593` runs `for s in ip12 ip28 ip30 ip32 ip35` and is GREEN, so **the ISR aborts are on no path anything in-tree travels today**; only one gate names ip30 at all, and the device's own header says it is 'just comprised of hardcoded guesses so far.'  Meanwhile `armmsrmodekill` kills the PROCESS on ARM, whose decode IS exercised across testarm/barearm/cats.  **So the order between the two HIGHs was set without the measurement that would settle it** -- which is itself the argument for running the arm probe BEFORE the larger ip30 build: the cheap measurement informs the order of the expensive work.

entries.note: *** THE FIX DIFF IS WRITTEN AND PRESERVED, AND IT FOUND A HOLE IN MY OWN DETECTOR. ***  `regress/artifacts/ip30abortkill/FIXDIFF_grok_20260917.txt`.  NOT APPLIED -- the adjudicated ship order puts the ip30 round LAST, after the commit and the arm probe. The diff honours every ruling: TWO latch bits (`IP30_W_TICK` 1<<0, `IP30_W_ISR` 1<<1, 'one bit per site, never shared'), the `(once)` house marker, `break` and never an early `return` so the common tail at :180-183 still runs, the `writeflag` test at 0x10020/0x10028, and on a READ it DECLINES rather than mirroring -- *'odata stays the function's 0 initializer; that is not a modelled value'*.  It also declines the 0x10030 WRITE arm per the Fable ruling, with the comment *'the TODO answers no.  Clearing goes through clear_isr at 0x10028'*.  It carries a control-flow table showing every path lives. *** THE DETECTOR FINDING, AND IT IS FLOOR-RELEVANT: `kill 30 wr` IS SURVIVE-ONLY AND THEREFORE CANNOT SEE THIS REPAIR. ***  Post-fix the host lives on a 0x10030 write whether or not the store is applied, so an `alive` oracle is invariant under the very edit the row exists to pin.  **That row owes a STATE oracle -- write declined AND `isr` unchanged** -- which is the CHANNEL check's vacuous-by-construction shape, knowable now, before any table runs. **AND THE ISR-UNCHANGED ROW MUST COVER BOTH LOADS, with a twist at 0x10028:** `&= ~0` is a no-op today, so a row that only checks the ISR CELL cannot fail there.  Pin **`odata` is not `d->isr`** instead, seeding ISR to a distinctive value first.  Without that, the 0x10028 writeflag repair ships unpinned.

entries.grader: grok 4.6 xhigh, fired to attack the witness probe BEFORE it becomes the round's detector, with the full probe inlined and an explicit warning that a manufactured breach costs an in-round repair on a detector that did not need one.  It returned five real misses AND two honest non-breaches, and it applied the DEPENDS-ON enclosing-function bound against one of its own findings.
entries.note: *** THE DETECTOR WAS ATTACKED BEFORE THE FIX SHIPPED, AND IT HAS CLEAN-SWEEP (d) MUTANTS. Every one is L1 CONSTRUCTION -- pre-ship material still being built -- NOT an L2 breach, because nothing has been committed. ***  That is the whole point of attacking a detector while it is still a draft. **THE MISSES, each 12/12 against the current 12-row probe:** **(1) `M_tick_abort` -- keep the `if`, put `abort()` back.**  MISS.  No session sets imask0 bit 50, so nothing in the probe visits the tick guard at all.  *** THIS IS CLAUSE (b) AT SITE 4 AS WELL AS (d): a VERBATIM REINSTATEMENT of the removed defect that the detector cannot see. ***  **(2) `M_tick_bit49`** -- `(1<<50)` -> `(1<<49)`.  MISS: `acc imask` deliberately writes bit 18, and `tick49 s70k` was ALREADY MEASURED alive.  **(3) `M_tick_swap`** -- `imask0` -> `reg_0x20000`, a field the body writes every tick.  MISS: `acc 20000` stores 0x1234 so bit 50 stays clear. **(4) `M_wf20_store_out` -- the `writeflag` wraps only the ANNOUNCE while `d->isr = idata` still runs on a LOAD.**  MISS.  **This is the `asicindexcase` (d) shape exactly: the guard is kept and the repair that stops the clobber is nulled** -- the host lives and the guest's load still zeroes the ISR.  *** AND PASS 1 ALREADY ASKED FOR THIS ROW (Q5) AND IT IS STILL NOT THERE -- which is the `#490` lesson repeating: a prescribed row lost between the pass that prescribed it and the list that was written. ***  **(5) `M_wf20_abort_wr` / `M_wf28_abort_wr`** -- `writeflag` present, `abort()` kept INSIDE the write arm.  MISS, because there is no `kill 20 wr` and no `kill 28 wr` row: the probe only ever LOADS at those two offsets. **TWO HONEST NON-BREACHES, and recording them matters as much as the misses:** `M_wf28_store_out` is **EQUIVALENT, not a breach** -- `idata` is 0 on reads (`:87-90`) so `&= ~0` is a no-op, and *a mutant that will not die is a RESULT*.  `M_one_latch_bit` (tick and ISR sharing one `warned`) is **NOT a (d) floor cell**, because the two guards live in DIFFERENT FUNCTIONS and DEPENDS-ON is walked only to the enclosing function boundary, never into callers -- so it is **L3 / contract disclosure, not L2**.  *That bound is what stops this becoming `#392`, and the seat applied it against its own finding.* **ROWS OWED BEFORE THE FIX SHIPS:** a TICK row (arm bit 50 with `sd`, step, expect the announce -- note the existing tick witness is a SEPARATE probe, so either it folds in or the contract must state the round ships TWO detectors); **`kill 20 wr` and `kill 28 wr`**; the **ISR-UNCHANGED** row (seed ISR, load at 0x10020, read back at 0x10030); and a `txt` sibling for the 0x10030 write so `M_latch_silent_30` cannot delete the diagnostic silently. **AND ONE FORWARD-LOOKING MUTANT WORTH THE CONTRACT:** `M_wf20_len8` -- `writeflag == MEM_WRITE && len == 8` -- misses today only because there is no write row at 0x10020, and **HEART registers are `u64`, so it becomes real the moment a write row is added using `sw`**.  That is the `sd`/`sw` trap from the tick measurement arriving in the detector.

entries.note: *** THE OWED ROWS ARE WRITTEN (L1 CONSTRUCTION, NOT YET RUN). ***  Five mutants that scored 12/12 against the probe are now closed by construction: **`tick 50`** (closes M_tick_abort -- which is ALSO clause (b) at site 4, a VERBATIM REINSTATEMENT the probe could not see -- and M_tick_swap); **`tick 49`**, its DISCRIMINATOR, so `tick 50` cannot pass for an unrelated reason and M_tick_bit49 cannot walk free; **`kill 20 wr` / `kill 28 wr`**, because the probe only ever LOADED at those offsets so an abort() kept inside the WRITE arm was invisible; **`isr keep`**, the `asicindexcase` row that closes M_wf20_store_out -- the writeflag wrapping only the ANNOUNCE while `d->isr = idata` still runs on a load, which leaves the host ALIVE and the ISR CLOBBERED, worse than the defect being fixed; and **`kill 30 txt`**, a diagnosis sibling for the 0x10030 write arm so M_latch_silent_30 cannot delete its announce silently. *** THE TICK ROW REQUIRED A NEW OPCODE, AND THAT IS THE TRAP, NOT A DETAIL: the probe had ONLY `sw`, and a 4-byte store CANNOT SET imask0 BIT 50 because `case 0x10000` reads through `memory_readmax64`.  A tick row written with the existing helper would arm NOTHING, stay alive, and SCORE GREEN ON A LIVE HOST DEATH. ***  Added `OP_SD_T0_A3` (0xFCE80000) and `OP_LD_V0_AT` (0xDC220000), and **DECODED BOTH FROM OUTSIDE THE CODE before trusting them** -- opcode 63 = sd with base $7/rt $8, opcode 55 = ld with base $1/rt $2 -- because this project's hand-assembled-encoding trap is that a wrong constant is invisible when the probe reads the same constant. **`isr keep` READS `died` PRE-FIX AND THAT IS CORRECT**: its seeding write at 0x10020 itself aborts on the committed build.  That is part of the reproduction, not an apparatus failure, and the row comment says so. **NOT YET RUN** -- five grok seats are loading the machine and this probe's settle/spin are LOAD-SENSITIVE oracles.  The new rows are CONSTRUCTED, not MEASURED, and the pre-fix run owes a re-run with this instrument (a comparison owes ONE instrument).

entries.note: *** THE 15-ROW INSTRUMENT'S PRE-FIX BASELINE WAS RUN 2026-09-17, AND IT CAUGHT A ROW THAT WAS RED ON A CORRECT BUILD.  L1 construction repair, in-round. ***  **FIRST, THE COUNT WAS WRONG IN MY OWN NOTE:** the probe emits **18** rows, not the 15 a `grep -c '^\s*row('` reported -- the probe's own `IP30ABORT_RESULT` line is the authority, and the grep was another correlate.  Baseline: **`IP30ABORT_RESULT=10/18`**, sentinel `IP30ABORT_DONE`, preserved at `probe_HEAD_preaccfix_20260917.out`. **SEVEN OF THE EIGHT FAILURES ARE THE DEFECT REPRODUCING**, at both directions of all three offsets plus the tick and the ISR clobber: `kill 20 rd`, `kill 28 rd`, `kill 30 wr`, `kill 20 wr`, `kill 28 wr`, `tick 50`, `isr keep`.  **Every control is GREEN** -- `live` returns `0x11223344`, the accept rows are serviced, and *** `tick 49` STAYS ALIVE WHERE `tick 50` DIES ***, which is the discriminating pair proving it is bit 50 rather than the tick path generally. *** THE EIGHTH FAILURE WAS NOT THE DEFECT AND NOT A SECOND ONE: `acc 20000` EXPECTED A COUNTER NOT TO COUNT. ***  It stored `0x1234` and wanted it back; it read `0x161c`.  **`0x161c - 0x1234 = 0x3e8 = 1000` EXACTLY**, which is `d->reg_0x20000 += 1000` in `DEVICE_TICK` -- one tick between the store and the load.  *The DEVICE was right and the ROW was wrong.*  The access arm alone reads like a plain r/w register; only the file's own `/*  A counter  */` comment and the tick body say otherwise. **AS WRITTEN IT MANUFACTURED A PHANTOM FAILURE ON A CORRECT BUILD, so it could never signal the defect this probe exists for** -- the vacuity class inside the round's own witness, and the reason it is L1 (pre-ship construction) rather than filed. **THE REPLACEMENT ORACLE IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN THE ONE IT REPLACES.**  The counter is always a multiple of 1000 (it starts at 0 and only ever `+= 1000`) and `0x1234` = 4660 is NOT, so `readback - 0x1234` is an exact multiple of 1000 **iff the store landed**, and is never one if the store was lost.  The row now pins THAT THE STORE REACHED `reg_0x20000` -- which the old literal compare only did by accident on a tickless run -- while tolerating any number of ticks. *Found by doing the test-first step the round already owed: re-running the pre-fix baseline on the CURRENT instrument, because the last recorded figure (6/9) came from a retired nine-row one.  That is the same two-instrument defect found in `sgirergbroundtrip` (4/6 vs 10/10) an hour earlier, caught here BEFORE it became a record rather than after.*

THE ROUND'S FIGURES ARE 8/21 PRE-FIX (PREFIX_21row_20260917.out) AND 21/21 POST-FIX (probe_FIX531_21row_20260917.out), both on that one instrument. Witness 13/21 on the committed build; the 213-row detector in gate 14 (HEAD 29/213, fix 213/213, /bin/true 28/213, an absent binary 4/213, /bin/false 5/213 with CONTROL=FAIL); six test-variant tables; pass 5's ruling CLOSE-AFTER-RECORDS and four records readings (10, 3, 1, 0 to fix); the regress review's floor breach (eight own-latch variants) closed by repair 6's session R18 (each 212/213 in table 6), repair 6's pass 2 zero breaches over 693 cells; the regress follow-up REGRESS-WITH-FINDINGS.  Coverage debt filed as memccoverdebt.  || [2026-10-22] QUEUE: external-research batch 8 of 10 (regress/artifacts/research_20261022/adj_20261022/ADJ_RULINGS.md D; regress/artifacts/research_20261022/TRIAGE.md T7): the bounds repair FIRST, the exits' disposition after -- the dev_mvme187.c:80 and :90 exits are census line 97 of `exitunowned76`.  Port: ajfa/mvme187-sysv88-gxemul 4a01173 patch 06 supplies the bound, and the recipe shows 187Bug writes memconf, reaching the :80 exit (report row A7-49; https://github.com/ajfa/mvme187-sysv88-gxemul/commit/4a01173afc4beafabbd61ca385bd158d07d4a415).  ||  `dev_mvme187.c:68` indexes a 124-byte struct with a guest-supplied offset of up to 255, **BEFORE the switch and unconditionally on every access including reads**:  `odata = ((uint8_t*)&d->memcreg)[relative_addr];`  The device is registered with length **0x200** at `:127-129`, and `:63-66` folds the high half down (`if (relative_addr & 0x100) { controller = 1; relative_addr &= ~0x100; }`), so the index domain is 0..255.  **sizeof(struct memcreg) is 124** -- DERIVED LOCALLY by counting the 62 `volatile u_char` declarations in `src/include/thirdparty/mvme_memcreg.h` (31 registers, each followed by a 3-byte `xxN[3]` pad), which independently reproduces the hunting seat's figure.  **So offsets 124..255 are a 132-byte host OUT-OF-BOUNDS READ past the struct**, into whatever follows it inside the malloc'd `struct mvme187_data`. REACHABILITY: `machine_mvme88k.c:88` `device_add(machine, "mvme187")` -- note this is `machine_mvme88k.c`, NOT `machine_m88k.c`, which the hunting seat named loosely and where my first grep found nothing; I corrected it by locating the constructor rather than by trusting the citation. *** THE REASON THIS IS A RIDER AND NOT A SECOND KILL: the `default:` arm already `exit(1)`s, so TODAY THE OOB VALUE NEVER ESCAPES TO THE GUEST -- the read happens, the process dies, and the kill is already inside `exitunowned76`. ***  **The exposure is what a DE-FATALISATION of that arm would create**, and it is the `asicindexcase` shape exactly: the `exit(1)` is doing duty as the bounds check, so removing the kill without clamping the index converts a host death into a SILENT heap over-read served to the guest as register data.  A round that de-fatalises this file owes the clamp IN THE SAME DIFF -- a bound, not a `case`.  Filed MED so it is queued BEFORE the de-fatalisation round rather than discovered inside it.

rows.title: the tightened `accept dma` oracle still cannot distinguish data_len from cnt or a literal 408, and its kill DEPENDS on the guest never writing the DMA length register -- plus `accept byte` still carries the old substring form
rows.state_note: *** COVERAGE DEBT ON THE CLAUSE-(b) REPAIR THAT SHIPPED 2026-09-17.  NOT A FLOOR BREACH -- the clause-(c) question was adjudicated the same day and came back DISCHARGED, and none of these re-opens clause (b) as measured. ***  The repair tightened `accept dma`'s oracle from SUBSTRING PRESENCE (`"Transfering" in t`) to COUNT-BEARING (`"Transfering 408 bytes" in t`), and three legs proved the breach was real (leg 3: SHIPPED oracle + M_lenrev = 62/62, the escape).  What the tightened form still cannot see, enumerated by the reviewing seat and verified here: **(1) `d->data_len` -> `d->cnt` or a hardcoded `408`.**  On this staging those three are the SAME VALUE -- TOC `case 0x14` accepts only `d->cnt != 408` as the decline and `alloc_data()` does `d->data_len = d->cnt` -- so the mutant still prints `Transfering 408 bytes` and BOTH the old and new oracles stay green.  The oracle distinguishes that cluster from `length` (`dma_reg[+0x08]`), which this session never writes, and not from its own members. **(2) THE KILL DEPENDS ON LEAVING THE DMA LENGTH REGISTER UNWRITTEN, and that is the sharpest one.**  Write `+0x08 = 408` and `length == data_len`, so `M_lenrev` prints `Transfering 408 bytes` again and leg 2's SOLE RED disappears.  The device comment's own example is `0x3800`, so a guest that programs a length is ordinary, not exotic.  **The stronger session programs a DISTINCT length and pins BOTH halves of `Transfering %i bytes ... (guest asked for %i)`** -- that is the repair if this is ever bought, and it is a new session rather than an oracle edit. **(3) `accept byte` STILL USES THE SUBSTRING FORM.**  Verified at `regress/gdrom_default_probe.py:1608`: `"ran" if "Transfering" in t else "no"`.  It is a DIFFERENT cell (the SUCCESS arm's shadow-clear pair-oracle) and `accept dma` is the print site clause (b) was measured against, so this is not a (b) hole -- **but it is the old form left sitting beside the repair of it**, which is the shape a future reader mistakes for a decision. **(4) `nodata notx` counts `t.count("Transfering")`** -- harmless for a decline row wanting 0, and NOT a pin of the number. **(5) THE ROW STILL DOES NOT PROVE 408 BYTES MOVED.**  `accept data` (want `0x10` at the destination) remains the movement oracle; the tightened `accept dma` proves the LOG LINE carries the count.  The contract must not be read as claiming otherwise. DISPOSITION: FILED, not fixed.  The stopping rule takes in-round only a MEASURED FALSE PASS or a WRONG RECORD; the wrong record in this family was the `EXPECT_ROWS`/clause-(c) conflation and it was corrected in place the same day.  (1) and (2) are contract-honesty items -- they matter exactly if the probe header's "prints data_len" bullet is read as "UNIQUELY data_len", which it should not be.

rows.title: dev_8259.c halts the emulated CPU on an unimplemented PIC command at the command port and then returns 1, so the access succeeds while the strand stops -- invisible to both an exit( and an abort() sweep
rows.state_note: READ at the arm by #574's panel (2026-10-25, Astra/Grok/GLM and the main loop): the specific-EOI arm captures 0x21-0x27 (non-specific on the chip) and 0xe0-0xe7 (rotate not performed); 0xa0-0xa7 (rotate on non-specific EOI), 0x00, 0x40, 0x48, 0x80 and a slave-line EOI byte such as 0x6c reach `cpu->running = 0`.  Reachability no longer BELIEVED: the arm's condition was read.  Still HELD with the host-stop class.  ||  `dev_8259.c` turns an unimplemented PIC command into a GUEST-VISIBLE HALT: the command-port arm does `fatal("[ 8259: unimplemented command 0x%02x ]")` and then `cpu->running = 0`, and **then still returns 1** -- so the access 'succeeds' while the strand stops.  Sites verified by grep at HEAD: `:140`, `:231`, `:235` (`:173` is inside a comment and is NOT a site). **DISTINCT FROM A HOST DEATH, and the ranking matters:** `cpu->running = 0` is a FUNCTIONAL HALT -- the process lives, the emulated CPU stops.  That ranks BELOW a SIGABRT/exit(1) and ABOVE a silent wrong value, and it is invisible to BOTH an `exit(` sweep and an `abort()` sweep, which is why the class survived three censuses. REACHABILITY **BELIEVED, NOT CONFIRMED** -- the seat's claim is that `DEV_8259_LENGTH` is 2 so the `default:` arm is dead, and the live door is OFFSET 0, the command port, taking any OCW that is not ICW1 / 0x0a / 0x0b / 0x0c / an EOI form -- i.e. `strb r0,[pic]` with r0 = 0 would be enough on CATS, where `bus_isa.c` installs it.  **NONE of that is re-verified here and it is explicitly not claimed.**  A census job is auditing it; this row exists so the finding cannot be lost again while that runs. *** PROVENANCE, AND IT IS A RECORDS FAILURE OF MINE: this was named by the 2026-09-17 `exithunt' seat, which returned FOUR findings.  I filed TWO (`ip30abortkill`, `mvme187memcoob`), acted on the abort() one -- which produced a measured rung-3 witness and a real HIGH -- and LEFT THESE TWO UNQUEUED.  `lunafb` had ZERO mentions anywhere in the ledger, so that file had never been queued at all.  **That is the UNREAD-REVIEW class, which this project has three times found real defects sitting in**, and here the review was read and then half-acted-on, which is the same shape one step later. *** *** CORRECTED 2026-09-17 BY THE HALT-CLASS CENSUS, AND TWO OF THE THREE SITES I LISTED CANNOT RUN. ***  I filed `:140`, `:231`, `:235`.  **`DEV_8259_LENGTH` is 2** (`dev_8259.c:47`, registered `:278`), and `memory_rw` only calls a handler for `paddr` in `[base, endaddr)` then subtracts the base -- so `relative_addr` is 0 or 1, both have `case` labels, and **the `default:` arm at `:228-236` is DEAD BY WINDOW SIZE.**  **THE LIVE SITE IS `:140` ALONE.**  *** AND MY 'the access still returns 1, so it SUCCEEDS' CLAIM IS ALSO WRONG. ***  `memory_rw.c` SNAPSHOTS `cpu->running` around the handler and, if it dropped, returns `MEMORY_ACCESS_FAILED` **before** it looks at `res` -- so the access does NOT report success.  What is true, and is the part worth keeping, is that there is **no `MEM_ARM` case** in that block, so ARM gets no device-fail abort: it is a HALT, not a FAULT, and member 5 is not wired for ARM device failures. **THE DOOR IS CONFIRMED AND THE CHAIN IS LONGER THAN I WROTE:** `machine_cats.c` adds footbridge -> `bus_pci_add(..., "ali_m1543")` -> `PCIINIT(ali_m1543)` for MACHINE_CATS calls `bus_isa_init(..., 0x7c000000, 0x80000000)` with NO `BUS_ISA_EXTERNAL_PIC`, putting the 8259 at **0x7c000020 / 0x7c0000a0** -- the same mapping the `isaorder` row already measured.  NetWinder gets the same ports via `symphony_83c553`.  A command-port write that is not ICW1 / 0x0a / 0x0b / 0x0c / an EOI form / the two non-halting TODOs (0x68, 0xc0-0xc7) falls to `:140`, and **`idata = 0` is enough -- a legal OCW2 NOP on real hardware.**  RANKED #2 of the guest-reachable halts.

rows.title: dev_lunafb.c halts the CPU from four sites on ordinary framebuffer offsets, on a machine this project actually boots -- and the file had never been queued at all
rows.state_note: `dev_lunafb.c` halts the CPU on ordinary framebuffer offsets: the `lunafb_a` and `lunafb_b` `default:` arms and a ROP-not-all-ones write all do `cpu->running = 0`.  Sites verified by grep at HEAD: `:93`, `:160`, `:166`, `:185`. *** THIS FILE HAD NEVER BEEN QUEUED -- `lunafb` had ZERO mentions in the entire ledger before this row. ***  It is installed unconditionally from `DEVINIT(luna88k)`, and luna88k is a machine this project HAS a rig for and DOES boot, which is what separates it from the ip30 case (advertised but no in-tree boot image). REACHABILITY **BELIEVED, NOT CONFIRMED**: the seat's claim is that `lunafb_a` is 512 KB (`0x80000`) implementing only `BMAP_RFCNT` and `BMAP_BMSEL`, so every other offset in that window stops the CPU, and that a comment naming `0xb1000000` for BOTH is wrong while the `#define`s are right.  It also claims OpenBSD's `omfb_clear_framebuffer` uses BMSEL, which IS implemented, so the boot path is BELIEVED clear of the halt.  **None of that is re-verified here.**  FAULT (member 5) is architecturally available on M88K and `return 0` would deliver it -- today the halt runs first. *** PROVENANCE, AND IT IS A RECORDS FAILURE OF MINE: this was named by the 2026-09-17 `exithunt' seat, which returned FOUR findings.  I filed TWO (`ip30abortkill`, `mvme187memcoob`), acted on the abort() one -- which produced a measured rung-3 witness and a real HIGH -- and LEFT THESE TWO UNQUEUED.  `lunafb` had ZERO mentions anywhere in the ledger, so that file had never been queued at all.  **That is the UNREAD-REVIEW class, which this project has three times found real defects sitting in**, and here the review was read and then half-acted-on, which is the same shape one step later. *** *** CORRECTED 2026-09-17: NOT UNCONDITIONAL, AND NOT ON THE DEFAULT LUNA BOOT.  MY ROW'S FRAMING WAS THE WRONG WAY ROUND. ***  I filed it as being on 'a machine this project ACTUALLY BOOTS', implying boot reachability.  **`dev_luna88k.c:1098-1101` [at 987cb596: :1102-1105] adds lunafb ONLY `if (devinit->machine->x11_md.in_use)`** -- so **default `-E luna88k`, the serial `login:` rig, does NOT install it at all**, and the hunt's 'CONFIRMED probe on unmodified -E luna-88k' is FALSE. The rest of the reading HOLDS and is sharper than I filed it: `lunafb_a` is 512 KB (`0x80000`) at 0xB1000000 implementing only `BMAP_RFCNT` (offset 0) and `BMAP_BMSEL` (offset 0x40000), so everything else in it stops the CPU; **the comment naming `0xb1000000` for BOTH arms is wrong while the `#define`s are right**; and `lunafb_b` is far LARGER than I stressed -- 0xB1100000..0xE1000000, roughly **767 MB**, implementing only plane-1 detect, 16 bytes of PALLET2, and `BMAP_FN + 4*ROP_THROUGH` **only when the write is 0xffffffff**. **OpenBSD's `omfb_clear_framebuffer` is CLEAR of the halt**, traced step by step (RFCNT write, PLANEMASK 0xff, `ROPFUNC[5] = ~0` which is exactly the one implemented all-ones slot, bitmap zeros, PLANEMASK 0x01).  What DOES halt under `-X` is later console drawing writing `ROPFUNC[5] = lmask` with `lmask != 0xffffffff` -- putchar, not the clear path. **DEMOTED to LOW-MED and RANKED #4**: real, but X11-only.  FAULT is the available member on M88K and is not what ships, because `#220`'s running-latch returns MEMORY_ACCESS_FAILED first.

Sites verified by grep at HEAD: `:93`, `:160`, `:166`, `:185`. *** THIS FILE HAD NEVER BEEN QUEUED -- `lunafb` had ZERO mentions in the entire ledger before this row. ***  It is installed unconditionally from `DEVINIT(luna88k)`, and luna88k is a machine this project HAS a rig for and DOES boot, which is what separates it from the ip30 case (advertised but no in-tree boot image). REACHABILITY **BELIEVED, NOT CONFIRMED**: the seat's claim is that `lunafb_a` is 512 KB (`0x80000`) implementing only `BMAP_RFCNT` and `BMAP_BMSEL`, so every other offset in that window stops the CPU, and that a comment naming `0xb1000000` for BOTH is wrong while the `#define`s are right.  It also claims OpenBSD's `omfb_clear_framebuffer` uses BMSEL, which IS implemented, so the boot path is BELIEVED clear of the halt.  **None of that is re-verified here.**  FAULT (member 5) is architecturally available on M88K and `return 0` would deliver it -- today the halt runs first. *** PROVENANCE, AND IT IS A RECORDS FAILURE OF MINE: this was named by the 2026-09-17 `exithunt' seat, which returned FOUR findings.  I filed TWO (`ip30abortkill`, `mvme187memcoob`), acted on the abort() one -- which produced a measured rung-3 witness and a real HIGH -- and LEFT THESE TWO UNQUEUED.  `lunafb` had ZERO mentions anywhere in the ledger, so that file had never been queued at all.  **That is the UNREAD-REVIEW class, which this project has three times found real defects sitting in**, and here the review was read and then half-acted-on, which is the same shape one step later. ***

entries.grader: grok 4.6 xhigh halt-class census; the x11 conditional verified locally
entries.note: *** CORRECTED 2026-09-17: NOT UNCONDITIONAL, AND NOT ON THE DEFAULT LUNA BOOT.  MY ROW'S FRAMING WAS THE WRONG WAY ROUND. ***  I filed it as being on 'a machine this project ACTUALLY BOOTS', implying boot reachability.  **`dev_luna88k.c:1098-1101` adds lunafb ONLY `if (devinit->machine->x11_md.in_use)`** -- so **default `-E luna88k`, the serial `login:` rig, does NOT install it at all**, and the hunt's 'CONFIRMED probe on unmodified -E luna-88k' is FALSE. The rest of the reading HOLDS and is sharper than I filed it: `lunafb_a` is 512 KB (`0x80000`) at 0xB1000000 implementing only `BMAP_RFCNT` (offset 0) and `BMAP_BMSEL` (offset 0x40000), so everything else in it stops the CPU; **the comment naming `0xb1000000` for BOTH arms is wrong while the `#define`s are right**; and `lunafb_b` is far LARGER than I stressed -- 0xB1100000..0xE1000000, roughly **767 MB**, implementing only plane-1 detect, 16 bytes of PALLET2, and `BMAP_FN + 4*ROP_THROUGH` **only when the write is 0xffffffff**. **OpenBSD's `omfb_clear_framebuffer` is CLEAR of the halt**, traced step by step (RFCNT write, PLANEMASK 0xff, `ROPFUNC[5] = ~0` which is exactly the one implemented all-ones slot, bitmap zeros, PLANEMASK 0x01).  What DOES halt under `-X` is later console drawing writing `ROPFUNC[5] = lmask` with `lmask != 0xffffffff` -- putchar, not the clear path. **DEMOTED to LOW-MED and RANKED #4**: real, but X11-only.  FAULT is the available member on M88K and is not what ships, because `#220`'s running-latch returns MEMORY_ACCESS_FAILED first.

ANSWERED BY READING WITH A DENOMINATOR on both sides: armmsr's reachability by mode enumeration (7 handled, 25 unhandled, none producible by a correct in-tree kernel), and ip30's by gate_asan_sweep.sh:593 running ip30 green. rows.title: the order between the two open HIGHs rests on real-guest reachability measured for neither -- ip30's aborts are on no in-tree path, and armmsr's probe is built but unrun
rows.state_note: *** BOTH OPEN HIGHs' SEVERITIES REST ON REAL-GUEST REACHABILITY THAT IS MEASURED FOR NEITHER, AND THE ORDER BETWEEN THEM WAS SET WITHOUT IT.  Named by the Fable adjudicator 2026-09-17 as the question the adjudication was not being asked. ***  RUNG IS A FLOOR ON ADMISSIBILITY; SEVERITY ORDERS THE QUEUE -- that is settled carrier doctrine.  What is not settled is the severity input.  **`ip30abortkill`:** rung-3 probe witness, measured SIGABRT.  But `gate_asan_sweep.sh:593` runs `for s in ip12 ip28 ip30 ip32 ip35` and is GREEN, so **the ISR aborts are on no path anything in-tree travels**; only one gate names ip30 at all; there is no in-tree Octane boot image; and the device header says it is 'just comprised of hardcoded guesses so far.'  The defect is real for a guest that touches those addresses -- which a booting Linux/IP30 would, since the code cites that very driver -- and hypothetical for anything running here today.  **`armmsrmodekill`:** kills the PROCESS (not a halt, not a probe-only path) on ARM, whose decode IS exercised across testarm/barearm/cats.  Its real-guest reachability is ALSO unmeasured -- and `regress/arm_msrmode_probe.py` is BUILT and unrun, so that measurement is one run away.  **DISPOSITION: do not re-rank on argument.  Run the arm probe; it is the cheap measurement that informs the order of the expensive work.**  This row exists so the ranking is not silently decided by which defect was found most recently.  *** THE RANKING IS SETTLED BY READING WITH A DENOMINATOR: `ip30abortkill` FIRST. ***  And the distinction that settles it is worth more than the verdict: **the gap on ip30 is 'we do not run that OS here'; the gap on armmsr is 'that OS would not do this.'  Only the second kind of gap demotes a defect.**  A process death on the documented interrupt path of the guest the machine exists to run outranks a process death that requires the guest to program a reserved mode. **Q1 -- CAN A REAL ARM GUEST REACH `armmsrmodekill`?  NO.**  `arm_save_register_bank` / `arm_load_register_bank` switch on `cpsr & 0x1f`: **7 arms handled, 25 of 32 unhandled.**  Handled: USR32 0x10, FIQ32 0x11, IRQ32 0x12, SVC32 0x13, ABT32 0x17, UND32 0x1b, SYS32 0x1f. The unhandled 25 break down as: **26-bit modes 0x00-0x03** (`cpu_arm.h` names them and `grep -c 'case ARM_MODE_USR26'` across src/ is ZERO; CATS/testarm/barearm are SA-110/SA1110 and the in-tree NetBSD `armreg.h` does not even define 26-bit modes); **0x04-0x0F unused**; **0x14/0x15/0x18/0x19/0x1c/0x1d/0x1e reserved** -- DDI 0100I A2.5.7 says *'If any other value is programmed into the mode bits M[4:0], the result is UNPREDICTABLE'*, and there are NO MSR exceptions; **0x16 Monitor** (TrustZone, not on any in-tree CPU); **0x1a Hyp** (ARMv7-A virt, likewise). A real kernel writes the named constants plus I/F -- `msr cpsr_c, #PSR_SVC32_MODE|I32_bit|F32_bit` (0xD3), IRQ 0x12, USR on process start, SYS for some copy paths -- and locore is `bic r0,r0,#0x1f ; orr r0,r0,#<legal> ; msr cpsr_c,r0`.  **Userspace cannot do it at all**: `X(msr_imm)` strips the c-byte in USR32 (`mask &= 0xff000000`). **Q2 -- THE SECOND PATH, which I had not considered and which is the one that could have been worse:** `MSR SPSR` is UNVALIDATED, and `MOVS PC, LR` / `LDM {..,pc}^` copies SPSR into CPSR **with no mode check**, after which Load dies identically.  But a correct kernel's SPSR is either the CPSR saved at exception entry (a legal mode) or a sigreturn frame, and Linux's `valid_user_regs` rejects anything whose MODE_MASK is not USR/USR26 and forces USR32.  **So the path exists and no correct kernel drives it.** **CONSEQUENCE FOR `armmsrmodekill`:** it stays a real process death and a real fix -- a hostile or buggy guest reaches it, and 25 of 32 encodings are unhandled -- but its SEVERITY is now measured rather than assumed, and it does NOT outrank ip30.  **`highrankunmeasured` is answered on the armmsr side by READING; the ip30 side stands as measured (gate_asan_sweep runs ip30 green, so the aborts are on no in-tree path).**

rows.title: dev_luna88k.c:923 stops the CPU on any unimplemented address in a ~1.76 GB always-installed window -- named by seats three times since 2026-09-06 and never given a ledger id
rows.state_note: *** NAMED BY SEATS THREE TIMES AND NEVER QUEUED UNTIL NOW.  This is the records finding as much as the defect. ***  It was named `lunadefaultstop` on 2026-09-06 in the `lunaabsentcpu` pass-2/pass-3 panels with an explicit 'file as a row'; the CHANGELOG still uses the name (**one** occurrence); the 2026-09-17 exithunt table named the same site with NO id; and the halt-class census named it again.  **Verified: `lunadefaultstop` was ABSENT from ledger.json and had ZERO occurrences in OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md.** THE DEFECT: `src/devices/dev_luna88k.c:923`, in the unimplemented-address arm -- `// Stop the emulation immediately.` then `cpu->running = 0; return 0;`.  **The device is ALWAYS INSTALLED** (no x11 conditional, unlike lunafb), and its window runs from 0x3ffffff0 to BMAP_START -- **roughly 1.76 GB**.  One supervisor store to any unimplemented offset in that range stops the CPU **on the machine this project actually boots**. **RANKED #1 of the guest-reachable halts** by the census, above `8259cmdhalt`, precisely because it is unconditional on a booted machine where `lunafbhalt` is X11-only.  Boot to `login:` is clear -- or the rig would not boot -- so the door is a probe, not the PROM path. CLASS: a FUNCTIONAL HALT, not a host death; the process lives and the strand stops.  That ranks BELOW a SIGABRT/exit(1) and ABOVE a silent wrong value, and it is invisible to an `exit(` sweep AND to an `abort()` sweep, which is how the class survived three censuses.  *** MY '~1.76 GB WINDOW' IS THE MAP, NOT THE DEFECT, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS BECAUSE I USED THE BIG NUMBER AS THE SEVERITY ARGUMENT. ***  The window really is 1,897,267,216 bytes (`0x3ffffff0` .. `BMAP_START`), and the implemented mass inside it is about **148 KB** -- four range handlers (FUSE_ROM 1 KB, NVRAM 0x1FDC, NVRAM_ADDR_88K2 0x1FDC byte-only, TRI_PORT_RAM ~128 KB) plus **34 exact switch addresses**.  But the set that MATTERS is three nested sets, not one: **(1) COLD DEBUGGER, TRANSLATION OFF** -- `APR_V` clear means VA==PA, which is exactly why `luna_intmask_probe.py` already reaches `0x65000000`.  Almost the whole window kills.  **This is the WITNESS population.**  **(2) AFTER THE MMU, THE PAGES OpenBSD ACTUALLY MAPS THAT THIS FILE DOES NOT IMPLEMENT** -- and this is the finding my row did not have.  `pmap_table.c` identity-maps **RW** inside this device's window: `OBIO_TAS 0x61000000` (4 KB, nothing implemented), `SOFT_INT_FLAG0 0x6B000000` (4 KB, nothing), `RESET_CPU0 0x6D000000` (4 KB, of which only `+0x10` is serviced), `PIO0C`, and **`PC_BASE 0x90000000` -- 32 MB, nothing implemented**.  So the guest-kernel-reachable unimplemented set is **~32 MB, and 32 MB of it is ONE mapping**.  **(3) THIS IMAGE'S LOGIN PATH: EMPTY**, as my row said. **So 'the #1 guest-reachable halt on a machine we boot' is true of (1) and (2) as CAPABILITY and false of (3) as TRAVELLED PATH** -- which is the distinction the ranking rests on and my row blurred.  *`PROM_SPACE` is the sharpest illustration of map-versus-defect: 256 KB of PROM, **one** word implemented, and that one word IS on the boot path.* **FAULT (member 5) BECOMES MECHANICALLY AVAILABLE IF THE HALT GOES, AND IS STILL NOT RIGHT.** Today the halt wins because `#220`'s latch in `memory_rw.c` -- `if (running_before_device_access && !cpu->running) return MEMORY_ACCESS_FAILED;` -- fires BEFORE the `res == 0` -> `m88k_exception(DATA_ACCESS)` block is ever reached.  Delete the halt, keep `return 0`, and `#502`'s implemented DATA_ACCESS vector does fire.  Four reasons from the TREE not the menu: **(a) this file already models 'illegal address' and it is NOT `return 0`** -- `case 0x3ffffff0` pokes `CMMU_PFSR_BERROR` into the data CMMU and `break`s, i.e. the access SUCCEEDS, thirty lines above the defect; **(b) the failed-device arm never sets PFSR** while OpenBSD's `trap.c` READS `CMMU_PFSR_FAULT(tf_dpfsr)` -- so a naked `return 0` is a HALF-FAULT, an exception without the bus-error status the guest inspects; **(c) the same CPU and the same class were already adjudicated the other way** -- `pcc2defaultkill` `#501` declined unimplemented offsets with a latched `(once)` and `return 1`, and `dev_m8820x.c` `#433` says it in product comments, complain-and-continue, because `#220` assigned HALT to 'the guest asked the machine to halt' and CONTINUE to 'model gap'; **(d) FAULT on a MAPPED hole is a kernel PANIC, not a clean probe** -- OpenBSD `T_DATAFLT` with no `pcb_onfault` goes to `panictrap`, and TAS / RESET_CPU0 / PC_BASE are all mapped.  A driver that stores without `badaddr()` dies. *** AND THE WARNING THAT REFRAMES THE WHOLE FIX: deleting the halt and leaving `return 0` would SILENTLY CHANGE EVERY UNIMPLEMENTED ACCESS from 'stop the emulator' to 'inject DATA_ACCESS'.  **That is a behaviour change to the guest, not a de-fatalisation** -- and it is precisely the kind of change the addition licence refuses without a measured delta. *** **THE SHIPPING TABLE (proposed, not ratified):** `RESET_CPU_ALL` **KEEPS THE HALT** -- OpenBSD `boot()` writes it to reboot, so the guest asked, which is `#220`/footbridge_reset; the `default:` arm gets **member 3**, latched announce plus **`break` and never an early `return`** because the common tail writes `odata` on reads; TAS / `RESET_CPU0..3` / `SOFT_INT_FLAG` / `PIO0C` are **member 7 FILED, not in-round**, being real registers whose implementation needs a measured delta or a transferred warrant; and FAULT stays **available-but-not-chosen** unless someone measures OpenBSD's `badaddr()` against both a `return 0` and a `PFSR_BERROR` poke. *** `RESET_CPU_ALL` IS THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT MAKES THE SIBLING TEST WORK: it proves this file ALREADY distinguishes a deliberate halt from an accidental one, so the `default:` arm is not 'how this file does things' -- it is the outlier. ***

rows.title: maple_do_dma_xfer() is for(;;) with its only exit gated on a bit read from guest RAM, so a guest that never sets it hangs the emulator inside a register write -- alive, running, and never coming back
rows.state_note: *** AN UNBOUNDED, GUEST-TRIGGERABLE LOOP INSIDE A DEVICE ACCESS HANDLER.  THE EMULATOR NEVER DIES -- IT NEVER COMES BACK. ***  `maple_do_dma_xfer()` is `for (;;)` at `dev_dreamcast_maple.c:409`, and its ONLY exit is `:535` `if (last_message) break;` where `last_message = buf[3] & 0x80` (`:429`) is read **from guest RAM** at `d->dmaaddr`.  A guest that never sets bit 7 of that byte loops forever; `:532` only advances `addr`.  Triggered by an ordinary register write -- `case 0x18 MAPLE_STATE`, `case 1: maple_do_dma_xfer(cpu, d)` at `:588` -- after MAPLE_ENABLE and MAPLE_DMAADDR.  Machine: **dreamcast**. **THIS IS A THIRD CLASS AND THE TREE HAS NO NAME FOR IT.**  An `exit(`/`abort()` is a HOST DEATH; `cpu->running = 0` is a FUNCTIONAL HALT where the process lives and the strand stops. **This is neither: the process is alive, the strand is running, and the user's machine is gone.**  No sweep in this project looks for it, because there is no keyword -- which is exactly the property that let the `abort()` class survive three censuses. **NOT A DUPLICATE, verified:** `mapledmaaddr` is about the DMAADDR read value and `mapledmaadvance` about address advancement past the command.  Neither is the loop bound. There IS an `exit(1)` at `:426` inside the loop, on a different condition -- so the function has a terminating path and still has no trip cap. DISPOSITION NOT DECIDED HERE.  The obvious shape is a trip cap with a latched announce (member 3 applied to a loop), but the bound is a design question: a legitimate maple chain has a real maximum and picking it needs the Comstedt reverse-engineering note the function header cites, not a guess.  **The addition licence wants a measured delta or a transferred warrant, never a number that feels safe.**  *** THE BOUND IS NOT DERIVABLE FROM THIS TREE, AND THAT IS THE ANSWER RATHER THAN A FAILURE TO FIND ONE. ***  Comstedt's own DMA paragraph -- the page this file's header names -- says the controller *'will send ANY NUMBER of requests'*.  The 'configurable amount of time' in that sentence is **per request**, and it is ALREADY in the model as `d->timeout` (MAPLE_SPEED bits 16-31), **stored and never read inside `maple_do_dma_xfer`**.  On hardware a timeout writes 0xFFFFFFFF at the result address and CONTINUES to the next descriptor -- it does not end the list.  **`d->timeout` therefore cannot be turned into a frame cap without inventing a meaning the register does not have.** **24 IS THE ENDPOINT CENSUS, NOT THE LIST CEILING** (4 ports x 6 units): a legal DMA may send DEVINFO *and* GETCOND to the same unit, or a burst of VMU BWRITEs.  Linux's `MAPLE_MAXPACKETS 8` and the 16 KiB `MAPLE_DMA_SIZE` that Linux and KallistiOS both allocate are **SOFTWARE** batching, not ASIC limits, and neither is in this tree's model. *** AND IT CORRECTED THE DISPOSITION I WROTE INTO THIS ROW WHEN I FILED IT. ***  I wrote *'the obvious shape is a trip cap with a latched announce (member 3 applied to a loop)'*.  **The seven-member option set is the WRONG MENU here: every member presumes an ACCESS with a value to refuse, and this is a LIST WALK whose only exit is a guest bit.**  Bounding the walk is a NEW member -- *'do not dress it up as member 3 applied to a loop and then pick 24'*. **THE IN-TREE PRECEDENT, GREPPED RATHER THAN ARGUED, AND IT DOES NOT TRANSFER:** `dev_sgi_mec.c`'s `for (;;)` IS bounded -- by `dma_ptr_nr >= 4` (the hardware has four DMA pointers) AND `j >= MAX_TX_PACKET_LEN`, and `#203` added the outer cap after an inner `break` left the outer loop writing past the array.  **But that bound comes from the HOST STORAGE the fill writes into, and maple writes GUEST RAM at `receive_addr` -- there is no host buffer to cap against.**  *And that answers the sighunt's open question: there is NO other `for (;;)` and no `while (1)` in `src/devices/*.c`; the sighunt's second one is mec, and mec is bounded.* **THE DISPOSITION, WITHOUT INVENTING N:** detect the **MISSING LAST**, not 'too many devices' -- the defect is a list that never terminates, not a list longer than 24.  **DECLINE THE WHOLE DMA**, which is the shape this same function already uses for a malformed DMA: the unaligned `addr & 0x1f` check prints and RETURNS with no `SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT`.  *** TRUNCATING MID-LIST AND THEN FIRING DMADONE WOULD HAND THE GUEST A SILENT PARTIAL TRANSFER, and the unaligned path pointedly does not do that. ***  Latch the announce with `(once)` -- the unaligned path `fatal()`s EVERY time with no latch, which is floodclass.  **Do NOT `exit(1)`** (that converts a hang into a host death, the thing this queue is removing).  **Do NOT `cpu->running = 0`** (wrong class -- that is `lunafbhalt`/`8259cmdhalt`).  Do not make the DMA asynchronous in this round: that IS the hardware shape and would stop taking the host away, but it is a rewrite, and on real silicon a no-LAST list may still hang the Maple ASIC. **`:426` IS NOT A MODEL FOR MISSING LAST.**  All four `exit(1)`s in this function (`:426` GUN bit, `:459` multiple units, `:520` GETCOND function, `:529` unknown command) are UNIMPLEMENTED-PATH TRIPWIRES -- member 7's tell, a stub with no predicate refusing a value. *** BWRITE IS THE TELL: it is `fatal` + `break` OF THE SWITCH, and then the loop CONTINUES. So a no-LAST list of BWRITE HANGS while a no-LAST list of an unimplemented command DIES -- the same loop, two different classes, decided by `cmd`. ***  The author used `exit(1)` for 'I have not written this opcode', not for 'this list is malformed'. **Q4 -- IT CAN BE WITNESSED, AND AN EXISTING PROBE IS A LIVE HAZARD.**  Death-keyed oracles are all blind here: `exit(`, `abort()`, WIFSIGNALED and EOF-on-pty none of them fire.  *** AND `regress/maple_dmaaddr_probe.py`'s `os.waitpid(pid, 0)` AFTER `rd(10.0)` WOULD BLOCK FOREVER ON THIS BUG -- that probe cannot be the detector, and if it ever reaches this path it hangs the harness rather than reporting anything. ***  The instrument is SIGKILL-after-deadline plus a LAST-set control; the enable and alignment checks both return before the loop, so they are the liveness controls. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE N:** measuring the real ASIC with lists of 24, 25 and 512 frames and one with LAST never set -- noting that on hardware Maple DMA is **ASYNCHRONOUS** (STATE=1 while in progress, the SH4 keeps running), so the question is what the ASIC does with no LAST, not what feels safe on the host.  **The synchronous modelling is itself part of why this presents as a host hang.**

rows.title: four guest-controlled loop bounds at denial scale across sgi/ip32, dreamcast and mvme88k -- bounded, but 16M-to-4GiB of host traffic inside a single guest access
rows.state_note: *** FOUR GUEST-CONTROLLED TRIP COUNTS LARGE ENOUGH TO DENY THE EMULATOR, ACROSS THREE MACHINES.  Bounded -- so not the `mapledmahang` class -- but bounded at denial scale. ***  Found by the signal-death hunt with an explicit denominator: `for (` 289, `while (` 60, `do {` 6, `for (;;)` 2 across `src/devices/*.c`. **(1) SGI MTE linear fill, `dev_sgi_re.c:1477`** -- `dstlen = dst1 - dst0 + 1` on uint32, so `dst1 < dst0` UNDERFLOWS to ~2^32; the loop at `:1639-1677` subtracts at most 4096 per pass, giving ~2^20 passes of up to 4 KiB of `memory_rw` -- **roughly 4 GiB of traffic** from guest `mte_reg[]` values plus a CRIME_DE_START access.  Machine sgi/ip32. **(2) SGI MTE tiled fill/copy, `:1516-1574`** -- `for (y = y1; y != y2+dy; y += dy)` with 12-bit coordinates and no trip cap: **4096 x 4096 = 16,777,216** `horrible_getputpixel` calls, often two `memory_rw` each.  Same trigger. **(3) PVR / SH4 DMAC, `dev_pvr.c:171-204`** -- the hardware convention that TCR 0 means 16M is modelled faithfully (`:202-204`), so a guest programming DMAC ch2 with count 0 and writing PVR_MODE gets **16,777,216 transfers, one `memory_rw` each, inside one store**.  Machine dreamcast. **(4) osiop SCRIPTS MOVE, `dev_osiop.c:433`** -- `xfer_byte_count` is a 24-bit guest field, so ONE MOVE is up to **16,777,215** byte-at-a-time host accesses.  `MAX_SCRIPTS_PER_CHUNK` 256 caps how many MOVEs run per tick and does nothing about the size of one.  Machine mvme187/mvme88k. **WHY THIS IS ONE ROW AND NOT FOUR:** they are the same defect shape -- a guest-supplied count or coordinate pair used directly as a loop bound with no cap and no yield -- and the disposition is the same question for all four (cap, yield, or accept as faithful).  **(3) is the interesting one because the 16M IS the hardware contract**, so a cap there would be a deliberate divergence from the spec rather than a fix, and that is a different argument from the other three.  Filed as a class so the argument happens once.  *** THE HEAP-OVERFLOW CLASS IS CLOSED AS EMPTY, WITH ITS DENOMINATOR, AND THE SEAT REFUSED THE FINDING MY OWN BRIEF SUGGESTED. ***  I pointed it at `512 * count` on a 32-bit `int`, which overflows at count 8,388,608 and would give a SMALL allocation followed by a LARGE write -- a heap overflow, far worse than a denial.  **Measured: `count` is 1-256, so `512*256 = 131072` and the wrap is UNREACHABLE.**  Its own words: *'a manufactured WDC heap overflow would be a wrong record.'* **DENOMINATOR:** 130+ `malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`/`zeroed_alloc` calls in `src/devices/` and ~15 in `src/cpus/` production code, the large majority `malloc(sizeof(struct ..._data))` at DEVINIT or init-time name buffers -- host/config, not guest.  **16 guest-derived sizes across 10 files**, every one traced to its writer.  Result: **0 overflow, 15 capped or field-width bounded, 1 unbounded growth** (the mp IPI queue, filed as `mpipirealloc`). Each cap named rather than asserted: le is a 12-bit field plus a 12-1900 reject and a `size_t` aggregate check; 21143 an 11-bit field with an `int` sum clamped to 65536; gdrom a 16-bit `cnt` / 24-bit sector count with an explicit 64 KiB cap before `alloc_data()`; ps2 `0xffff * 16`; pvr Z 10-bit geometry gated by the 8 MiB VRAM check; pvr TA a doubling allocator; and `dev_fb.c` carries `#156`'s `size_t` overflow check **before** the malloc.

rows.title: census of probes that could report `alive' for a process that already died -- 0 shipped live probes mis-score; the class was born and closed the same day
rows.state_note: *** CENSUSED 2026-09-17 AND THE CLASS IS CLOSED WITH ITS DENOMINATOR: **0 shipped live probes still mis-score this way.**  The defect was born today and died today. ***  The founding case is `regress/artifacts/ip30abortkill/ip30_abort_probe.py`, which had the exact shape, was MEASURED reporting `alive` for a process that had SIGABRT'd, and was rewritten to poll the same hour.  `arm_msrmode_probe.py` was built with the polling form from the start. **METHOD, keyed on MECHANISM rather than on names** -- and it explicitly refused to count `artifacts/**` frozen copies, which would have inflated the class about FIFTEENFOLD by re-counting the same five files: live population is `regress/*.py` = **99 files**, minus 10 harness/selftest/census scripts and one source-only probe = **88 launchers**. **THE DEATH-AS-ORACLE FAMILIES, with counts:** EOF-as-alive (`alive = rd(...)`) **33**; sessions borrowed from those 33 **11** (pcc2_default execs pcc2_width's session; ten SH4 probes import sh4_pcic_probe); prompt/dump still-answering **3**; `subprocess.run` wait-status **6**; **`WNOHANG` at all: 5** (4 at HEAD plus the uncommitted arm_msrmode). **OF THOSE FIVE, HOW MANY SAMPLE waitpid ONCE?**  `pcc2_width_probe.py` polls 30x0.1s and waitpid only fills `how`; `pcc2_c040_probe.py` the same; `xscale_inten_probe.py` polls 2s in `close()` and sets `self.dead` on EOF during `send()`; `arm_msrmode_probe.py` polls 12s. `luna_absentcpu_probe.py` **does sample once -- and it is NOT the alive oracle**, being called from `died()` only after `step_at` has already failed on EOF.  **ONCE-ONLY IN THE LIVE TREE: 1.  WAITPID-ONCE AS THE SURVIVE ORACLE: 0.** *** AND THE SEAT NAMED THE CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN THE KEYWORD, which is what makes this reusable: the bug is NOT 'has WNOHANG'.  It is the three-part combination -- `rd()` returns on an empty `os.read` so the spin is skipped exactly on death; that return is IGNORED; and `alive` is then taken from a single `waitpid(WNOHANG)`.  Any one of the three alone is harmless. ***  **DISPOSITION: NO TREE-WIDE EDIT.**  The seat's own words -- *'a tree-wide rewrite would manufacture findings'* -- and this project's addition licence agree: 33 EOF-as-alive probes consume `rd()`'s return and are correct as written.  The boundary is recorded so a future round does not rediscover the class and sweep it.

rows.title: three grok seats lost to a trailing & inside a Bash-tool wrapper -- the documented hazard, hit after nine correct launches, detected by MTIME rather than by size or process count
rows.state_note: *** THREE GROK SEATS WERE LOST TO THE DOCUMENTED PLAIN-`&` HAZARD ON 2026-09-17, AND THE CARRIER DESCRIBES IT EXACTLY. ***  A trailing `&` inside a Bash-tool invocation does not survive: the child is torn down when that invocation's shell exits.  I used the correct form -- the grok command in the FOREGROUND of a `run_in_background` wrapper -- for the first nine jobs, then broke it on the tenth by trying to fire TWO seats from ONE wrapper with `&`.  **Knowing the rule and having it fire on the right object are different problems**, which is the carrier's own structure-versus-memory thesis arriving against me. **HOW IT WAS DETECTED, because the obvious check is the wrong one:** the files were SMALL but not empty, which the carrier warns is indistinguishable between a stall, a wall and a dead run.  `tasklist` showed 3 live grok processes against 5 jobs, which is suggestive and not decisive because grok spawns more than one process per job.  **The decisive observable was MTIME**: `allocsize` and `records` had been written 61 s and 80 s earlier (alive), while `lunadefault`, `maplebound` and `cpusweep` had not been touched for 338-675 s.  A killed job's redirect target stops growing; a live one does not. **AND THE TAIL CONFIRMED IT**: `grok_lunadefault.txt` ended mid-sentence in streaming reasoning -- *'next I will list every exact `case` versus the board map'* -- with no verdict line.  That is a STOPPED SEAT, and the standing rule is that **a stopped seat is a SEAT FAILURE, never agreement**: re-fire once, preserve the partial rather than deleting it. All three partials are preserved as `grok_<job>.STOPPED_partial.txt` and all three were re-fired one per wrapper, command in the foreground. *Two jobs fired the same way SURVIVED (`allocsize`, `records`), which is worth recording because it makes the hazard INTERMITTENT rather than deterministic -- and an intermittent failure that leaves a plausible-looking partial is exactly the shape this project keeps misfiling as a seat problem rather than a launcher one.*

rows.title: maple_dmaaddr_probe.py uses a BLOCKING waitpid, so on the mapledmahang path it would hang the harness forever instead of reporting -- the mirror of the false-green class, and outside probedeathoracle's WNOHANG-keyed census
rows.state_note: *** `regress/maple_dmaaddr_probe.py` CALLS `os.waitpid(pid, 0)` -- A BLOCKING WAIT -- AFTER `rd(10.0)`, AND `mapledmahang` IS A PATH ON WHICH THE EMULATOR NEVER EXITS. ***  If that probe ever drives a maple DMA list with no LAST bit, the blocking wait **never returns and the harness hangs**, reporting nothing at all.  **This is the mirror of the false-green class closed today as `probedeathoracle`.**  That one was about a probe reporting ALIVE for a dead process; this is a probe that cannot report anything because it waits forever on a process that will not die.  Both come from keying an oracle on process death without a deadline -- and `probedeathoracle`'s census keyed on `WNOHANG`, so a BLOCKING `waitpid` was outside its population by construction. **The remedy is the same shape as the one already applied: a DEADLINE.**  A blocking `waitpid` in a harness that can drive a non-terminating guest path needs SIGKILL-after-N rather than patience.  Filed rather than fixed: it is a real hazard on a path nothing currently drives, and the fix belongs with whichever round builds the `mapledmahang` witness, because that round is the one that will first make the path reachable.

rows.title: dev_mp.c reallocs the IPI queue larger on every IPI write with no cap, and only the target CPU's own read drains it -- host heap grows by accretion
rows.state_note: *** AN UNCAPPED HOST ALLOCATION THAT A GUEST GROWS BY ACCRETION -- THE SUCCESS-CASE DENIAL, NOT A FAILED MALLOC. ***  `dev_mp.c:198-200`: a write to `DEV_MP_IPI_ONE` or `DEV_MP_IPI_MANY` does `d->n_pending_ipis[i]++` and then `CHECK_ALLOCATION(d->ipi[i] = realloc(d->ipi[i], d->n_pending_ipis[i] * sizeof(int)))` -- **with no cap of any kind**.  Verified at HEAD. **NOTHING DRAINS THE QUEUE EXCEPT THE TARGET CPU READING IT.**  The only consumer is `DEV_MP_IPI_READ` at `:211`, which decrements `n_pending_ipis[cpu->cpu_id]` -- i.e. the *receiving* CPU's own read.  A guest that sends IPIs and never reads them grows the host heap four bytes at a time, **with a `realloc` on every single write**, so the cost is both resident memory and repeated copying. REACHABILITY: **the test machines ALWAYS add it** -- `machine_test.c:148` and `:333` both `device_add("mp addr=... irq=...")`.  So this is not a device nobody installs. **SEVERITY LOW, RANKED BELOW `guestloopdenial`, and the reason is the shape rather than the size:** this is not a 2 GB one-shot allocation.  It is growth by accretion -- many writes, four bytes each -- so it is slower to matter than a tight loop and needs sustained guest cooperation.  It sits in the same family as `guestloopdenial` (the guest takes the host away without killing it) but arrives by a different road: **resident memory grows instead of a loop spinning.** *** NOTE WHAT `CHECK_ALLOCATION` DOES AND DOES NOT BUY HERE.  It turns a FAILED realloc into a clean `exit(1)`, which is why this is not a crash -- but it does nothing at all about a long run of SUCCESSFUL ones, which is the whole defect.  A guard against failure is not a guard against growth. ***  **ADJACENT, AND FLAGGED HONESTLY AS OUTSIDE THE DIRECTORIES THE HUNT WAS ASKED ABOUT:** `scsi_transfer_allocbuf()` in `src/disk/diskimage_scsicmd.c` is the malloc that SCSI controllers actually use, and devices pass guest lengths into it.  READ/WRITE is capped at **64 MiB** by `#163`'s `SCSI_MAX_XFER_BYTES` with a 64-bit multiply from `#133`.  But `dev_mb89352.c`'s `transfer_count` (a `size_t` fed from the 24-bit TCH/TCM/TCL register triple) is used as `want_len` for DATA OUT **and for the CDB**, giving a command buffer of up to **16,777,215 bytes** on a FIELD-WIDTH cap with no software cap behind it.  Machine: luna88k.  Recorded here rather than filed as its own row because it is a bound, not an overflow, and it belongs with whoever next touches mb89352 -- which `b120` already owns.

rows.title: seven rounds shipped code with no CHANGELOG round block -- four unmentioned anywhere in the file, and two of them are the rounds the vacuity floor was minted from
rows.state_note:
*** SEVEN ROUNDS SHIPPED CODE WITH NO CHANGELOG ROUND BLOCK, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE UNMENTIONED ANYWHERE IN THE FILE.  Measured 2026-09-17 against a live denominator of 293 round-block headings. ***  The ethos line is *'a CHANGELOG.md round block per correction'*, and `#436 #439 #441 #443 #466 #487 #493` each have **zero** headings matching their number.  Twelve commits across the seven, every one verified present in `refs/heads/main`. *** NONE IS A VOID NUMBER, WHICH IS THE CHECK THAT MAKES THIS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A GAP IN A COUNTER. ***  This project HAS a void number (`#289`), so a skipped heading is not automatically a breach -- it is one only if the number shipped.  All seven did, and three are ordinary defect fixes: **`#441 sh4bcr`** (*two guest instructions ended the emulator process*), **`#443 sh4pcicexit`** (*one guest LOAD ended the host, on 116 of 137 offsets*), and **`#493 wdcaltoffset`** (*a rung-3 witness for a live sev-high defect*). *** AND THE SHARP PART: `sh4bcr` AND `sh4pcicexit` ARE THE TWO ROUNDS THE VACUITY FLOOR WAS MINTED FROM. ***  The carrier cites them by name as its founding evidence -- *"sh4bcr's first detector passed a mutant reinstating the very host kill its round removed; sh4pcicexit's passed the original kill verbatim"* -- so **the most-cited exemplars in the whole rule set have no round block in the file a reader would go to.**  A future reader re-deriving the floor's warrant finds the rule, finds the rounds named, and finds nothing in the CHANGELOG under either number. **THE GAP IS DIRECTIONAL AND IT IS THE INVERSE OF THE USUAL ONE.**  This session's other records findings are all *written down but wrong*; this one is *shipped but not written down*, which no gate looks for -- section H checks seats were fired, G checks an answer was recorded, and `check_cited_artifacts.py` checks a cited path exists.  **Nothing asks whether a round that shipped has a block at all.** **DISPOSITION: recorded, NOT reconstructed.**  Writing seven retroactive round blocks from commit messages would manufacture records, which is worse than the gap -- so ONE consolidated *assessed-not-changed* entry names every round and its commits, and the reconstruction is filed for a round that can do it from the rounds' own artifacts. *The checker that would close this is a ledger-row-to-CHANGELOG-heading existence test, forward-only from a cutoff -- the `check_bugfile_sync.py` idiom.  FILED, not built: it is a tooling change owing two negative controls, and this file's own rule is that such a change ships as its own harness round rather than as a rider.*  DERIVER, because a count in a durable record names the command that made it and the tree it ran against (HEAD at the time of writing, working tree clean of CHANGELOG edits):

    for n in 436 439 441 443 466 487 493; do
        printf '#%-4s heading=%s any=%s\n' "$n" \
            "$(grep -cE "^#+ .*#$n\b" CHANGELOG.md)" \
            "$(grep -cE "#$n\b" CHANGELOG.md)"; done
    grep -cE '^#+ .*#[0-9]+' CHANGELOG.md      # the denominator: 293

*** AND THE FIRST FORM OF THAT DERIVER WAS KEYED ON A CORRELATE, WHICH I CHECKED BEFORE TRUSTING IT. ***  `^#+ .*#NNN\b` tests the LITERAL number, while the class is *is this round documented* -- and a RANGE heading (`## #89-#94`, which this file really does use) reports 0 for a round it documents.  Checked: no range heading covers any of the seven, and the bracketing headings confirm each gap (R9=#435, R10=#437 straddle #436; R12=#440, R13=#442 straddle #441).  *The correlate would have produced a plausible wrong answer in the direction that manufactures a finding.*

Its four named rounds were verified here and THREE MORE were found; the void-number check and the range-heading control are mine, run before recording.

rows.title: 297 ev citations across 27 rows name tools/pipeline/evidence/, a directory that was never tracked in any commit -- the answers survive in the panel dirs, so the remedy is a re-point, not a recovery
rows.state_note: *** 297 `ev` CITATIONS NAME `tools/pipeline/evidence/`, AND THAT DIRECTORY WAS NEVER BUILT -- NOT DELETED, NEVER TRACKED.  Measured 2026-09-17. ***  `git log --all -- 'tools/pipeline/evidence'` returns **0 commits**, and `--diff-filter=A` over `*evidence*` returns **nothing ever added to the index**.  So these are not decayed citations; they are citations to an ARCHIVE SCHEME THAT WAS PRESCRIBED AND NEVER IMPLEMENTED -- the PIPELINE.md doctrine's layout, written into rows at its 2026-08-15 adoption (`pipeline/evidence/d1/assess/codex_2026-08-15.md` and siblings). **27 distinct rows**: a1a2 a4 b101 b115 b118 b120 b122 b126 b1w b27 b47 b75 b82 d1 devexit gateflr hlen n1 n2 n3 n4 n5 n6 pkbrief + 3 more. *** THE ANSWERS SURVIVE, WHICH CHANGES THE DISPOSITION FROM RECOVERY TO RE-POINT. ***  `_scratchpad/panel_20260815_*` holds ten panel dirs for that date, each carrying `agy.txt codex.txt grok.txt kimi.txt ollama_{deepseek,glm,minimax}.txt`.  **The seat answers were written; only the path they are cited at is fictional.**  A round closing this re-points the 297 fields at the real panel dirs (and, per the durable-path rule, copies them under `regress/artifacts/` -- `_scratchpad/` is itself volatile). **SCALE, DERIVED BY WALKING THE DECODED LEDGER RATHER THAN BY GREP:** **3222 `ev` fields** (row-level + entry-level), 3209 non-empty; **1923 cite `_scratchpad/`**; 297 cite the dead archive; 989 cite neither. *** AND THE AUDIT'S OWN NUMBERS WERE TRUNCATED GREPS THAT SAID SO -- WHICH IS WHY THEY WERE RE-DERIVED AND NOT TRANSCRIBED. ***  It reported `>=1999` ev fields and `>=999` _scratchpad citations, flagging both as cut off, and gave 297 as COMPLETE.  The walk reproduces **297 exactly** and shows the two lower bounds were low by ~1.6x and ~1.9x.  *An honest lower bound is a good record and a bad number: it is indistinguishable from a measurement once it is quoted one hop away from the tool that produced it*, which is this project's frozen-number class arriving through the seat rather than through the author. **WHY NO CHECKER SEES IT, and it is a scope boundary rather than a checker defect.**  `check_cited_artifacts.py` exists and does exactly this job -- but its own header sets the altitude deliberately: *"checks committed records, never scratchpad state"*, per the fable5 `#462` Decision 4c.  It reads CHANGELOG ROUND BLOCKS, not ledger `ev` fields.  So the 297 are outside it BY DESIGN, and widening it is a scope change the adjudication that created it explicitly bounded. **RANKED LOW, and the reason is the same one the carrier's own citation-form ruling gives: NO GATE, PROBE OR SCRIPT READS AN `ev` FIELD FUNCTIONALLY.**  It is consumed by a reader, and a reader following a `pipeline/evidence/...` path gets an immediate, loud failure -- not a wrong answer.  That is the SAFE direction.  The cost is audit expense and the fact that 27 rows cannot be verified from their own fields.

So these are not decayed citations; they are citations to an ARCHIVE SCHEME THAT WAS PRESCRIBED AND NEVER IMPLEMENTED -- the PIPELINE.md doctrine's layout, written into rows at its 2026-08-15 adoption (`pipeline/evidence/d1/assess/codex_2026-08-15.md` and siblings). **27 distinct rows**: a1a2 a4 b101 b115 b118 b120 b122 b126 b1w b27 b47 b75 b82 d1 devexit gateflr hlen n1 n2 n3 n4 n5 n6 pkbrief + 3 more. *** THE ANSWERS SURVIVE, WHICH CHANGES THE DISPOSITION FROM RECOVERY TO RE-POINT. ***  `_scratchpad/panel_20260815_*` holds ten panel dirs for that date, each carrying `agy.txt codex.txt grok.txt kimi.txt ollama_{deepseek,glm,minimax}.txt`.  **The seat answers were written; only the path they are cited at is fictional.**  A round closing this re-points the 297 fields at the real panel dirs (and, per the durable-path rule, copies them under `regress/artifacts/` -- `_scratchpad/` is itself volatile). **SCALE, DERIVED BY WALKING THE DECODED LEDGER RATHER THAN BY GREP:** **3222 `ev` fields** (row-level + entry-level), 3209 non-empty; **1923 cite `_scratchpad/`**; 297 cite the dead archive; 989 cite neither. *** AND THE AUDIT'S OWN NUMBERS WERE TRUNCATED GREPS THAT SAID SO -- WHICH IS WHY THEY WERE RE-DERIVED AND NOT TRANSCRIBED. ***  It reported `>=1999` ev fields and `>=999` _scratchpad citations, flagging both as cut off, and gave 297 as COMPLETE.  The walk reproduces **297 exactly** and shows the two lower bounds were low by ~1.6x and ~1.9x.  *An honest lower bound is a good record and a bad number: it is indistinguishable from a measurement once it is quoted one hop away from the tool that produced it*, which is this project's frozen-number class arriving through the seat rather than through the author. **WHY NO CHECKER SEES IT, and it is a scope boundary rather than a checker defect.**  `check_cited_artifacts.py` exists and does exactly this job -- but its own header sets the altitude deliberately: *"checks committed records, never scratchpad state"*, per the fable5 `#462` Decision 4c.  It reads CHANGELOG ROUND BLOCKS, not ledger `ev` fields.  So the 297 are outside it BY DESIGN, and widening it is a scope change the adjudication that created it explicitly bounded. **RANKED LOW, and the reason is the same one the carrier's own citation-form ruling gives: NO GATE, PROBE OR SCRIPT READS AN `ev` FIELD FUNCTIONALLY.**  It is consumed by a reader, and a reader following a `pipeline/evidence/...` path gets an immediate, loud failure -- not a wrong answer.  That is the SAFE direction.  The cost is audit expense and the fact that 27 rows cannot be verified from their own fields.

touches tools/pipeline/check_score_claims.py.  *** FIXED 2026-09-17 BY OWNER DECISION, WITH A SIBLING AUDIT RATHER THAN A ONE-INSTANCE PATCH. ***  `check_score_claims.py`'s `SCORE` regex was `(?<![\dx/])(\d+)\s*/\s*(\d+)(?![\d/%])` -- a lookbehind excluding a digit, `x` and `/` **but not a hyphen** -- so the ORDINAL PAIR `entries-4/8` was reported as a stale score claim of 4/8 against a pin of 188. *** THE REASON THIS WAS NOT LEFT ALONE: THE CHECKER'S OWN PRESCRIBED REMEDY WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A FALSE STATEMENT. ***  Its message reads *"if that is a deliberate historical quote, write '8-row' on the same line"* -- and on a line about ARRAY ENTRIES that silences the check by writing something untrue into a probe.  **A check whose repair corrupts the thing it guards** is the shape the carrier already records for the build-tree clearance recipe, arrived at from a new direction. **THE AUDIT, with a denominator, because a correlate-keyed matcher usually has more than one victim:** 710 N/M matches across 121 `regress/` files; the hyphen-aware form keeps **706** and drops exactly **FOUR**, every one an ordinal pair and none a score -- `entries-4/8` (`crime_width_probe.py`), `len-3/5` (`lca_isalane_probe.py` comment 96), `opcode-59/63` (`ppc_halt_probe.py` comment 238), `pass 2-3 / 6-7` (`sgi_de_primop_probe.py` comment 985).  *** THREE OF THE FOUR WERE LATENT: they fire only once their probe gains a gate pin, so the class had four members and one visible face. *** **CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE LANDING:** eight real score claims still match (13/13, 26/26, 8/32, `52 / 52`, 16/16, `scored 27/29`, `base 29/29`, `RESULT=6/9`); six non-scores rejected (the four hyphen pairs plus the two pre-existing hex lists).  `SCORE_CLAIMS_PASS` at 30 pinned probes. *The fix is one character in a lookbehind.  What made it worth a round is that the audit converted an anecdote into a population -- and the population was four.*

rows.title: ledger `commits` is a space-separated string in 382 rows and a list in 37, so a consumer that assumes a list silently yields CHARACTERS and renders one SHA as seven commits
rows.state_note: *** THE LEDGER'S `commits` FIELD IS A SPACE-SEPARATED STRING IN 382 ROWS AND A LIST IN 37, AND A CONSUMER THAT ASSUMES A LIST FAILS SILENTLY BY YIELDING CHARACTERS.  Measured 2026-09-17 -- by falling into it. ***  `", ".join(row["commits"])` on a string row renders `7a41b3f` as `7, a, 4, 1, b, 3, f`, which **looks like a list of seven commits** rather than like an error.  Census over 512 rows: `str` 382, `NoneType` 93, `list` 37; 132 of the strings are non-empty. **IT IS NOT A DATA DEFECT -- both shapes are parseable and the shipped tools handle them** (`gen_dashboard.py` and the checkers all work today).  It is a SCHEMA INCONSISTENCY that makes every new consumer a coin-flip, and the failure mode is the one this project keeps naming: **a plausible wrong answer that does not look like a failure.**  The records audit's own Q1 had to count "hash-bearing rows" precisely because the field has two shapes. **DISPOSITION: FILED, NOT NORMALISED.**  Rewriting 382 rows to lists is a mechanical edit to the single source of truth with no measured defect behind it -- the ADDITION LICENCE refuses "cannot hurt", and this is its records-side twin.  The cheap durable fix is a one-line accessor (`commits_of(row)` returning a list from either shape) adopted where consumers are written, which is FILED as a tooling change owing its own negative controls. *Recorded because the near-miss is the instructive part: the wrong output was nine rows of single letters in a brief-building extraction, and it was obvious ONLY because a SHA is recognisable.  A field of short tokens would have rendered the same way and read as real.*

rows.title: sh4_dmac_transfer signals transfer end through no channel -- it never sets CHCR_TE nor clears DE, while dev_pvr.c does; a guest polling CHCR on the generic DMAC path would never see completion, IF such a path transfers
rows.state_note: *** THE COMMENT IS WRONG; WHETHER THE BEHAVIOUR IS WRONG IS **NOT** MEASURED, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ROW. ***  `sh4_dmac_transfer` never sets `CHCR_TE` and never clears `CHCR_DE`, while `dev_pvr.c` sets TE on its own DMA path.  A guest that polls CHCR for transfer end on the GENERIC DMAC path would therefore never see it. **WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT CLAIMED:** `#453`'s own analysis records that the only RS encoding reaching this point is the SINGLE-ADDRESS EXTERNAL case, **which performs no transfer** -- so "never signals completion" may be exactly right for the one path that arrives.  *Not signalling the end of a transfer that did not happen is not a defect.* **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is the ordinary ladder question:** a rung-3 probe that drives the generic DMAC on a path which DOES transfer, then reads CHCR back through `DEVICE_ACCESS` and asks whether TE is set.  If no such path is reachable, the honest answer is that the arm is unreachable and the row closes as documented-only -- which is a real answer, not a failure. *Ranked LOW: it is a HANG-class candidate (the third defect class this queue tracks) with no witness and a named reason to think it may be vacuous.  It ranks below every measured defect and is recorded so the question is not lost a second time.*

rows.title: dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c prints an UNLATCHED guest-drivable fatal() on the ACCEPTED-DMA path, so ordinary correct guest traffic floods the log and -q cannot silence it -- a floodclass site the floodclass row does not name
rows.state_note: *** AN UNLATCHED GUEST-DRIVABLE `fatal()` ON THE **SUCCESS** PATH -- IT FIRES ON EVERY ACCEPTED DMA, NOT ON A REFUSAL.  Verified 2026-09-17 by brace depth, not by eye. ***  `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` prints `[ dreamcast_gdrom_dma: Transfering %i bytes to 0x%08x (guest asked for %i) ]` on the accepted-transfer path with **no latch of any kind**. **HOW IT WAS SETTLED, because the obvious check is misleading here:** the enclosing function DOES contain a latch -- `if (!(d->warned & GDROM_W_DMANODATA))` -- about thirty lines above the print, so a reader scanning for *"is there a `d->warned` test nearby"* finds one and stops.  **Brace depth settles it: that block CLOSES before the print**, which sits outside it (depth -1 relative to the latch's `if`).  *A latch in the same function is not a latch on this line, and the two are indistinguishable without counting braces.* **WHY THE SUCCESS PATH IS THE BAD PLACE FOR IT.**  Every other flood this queue tracks is on a REFUSAL arm, where the guest has to do something unusual to provoke it.  This one is on the path a working driver takes, so **ordinary correct guest behaviour produces the flood** -- and `fatal()` has no `-q` early-out, so it cannot be silenced by verbosity. **NOT INTRODUCED BY `#462`, AND THE SEAT SAID SO ITSELF** (*"This is not introduced by the diff -- the original also had it"*).  `#462` MOVED the print below the `d->data == NULL` check and changed it to print `d->data_len` rather than the guest's register, which is why the line is correct about its CONTENT and still unlatched about its FREQUENCY. *** `floodclass` DOES NOT COVER THIS SITE: checked, and the row mentions neither `gdrom`, `dreamcast` nor `Transfering`. ***  So it is a genuinely new member of a class this project already tracks, rather than a duplicate. **DISPOSITION IS NOT OBVIOUS AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHOSEN HERE.**  The house idiom is member 3, DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE -- but this is not a decline, it is a SUCCESS, and a `(once)` latch on a success path silences the transfer log after the first DMA, which may be the diagnostic someone wants.  The option set for a NOISY-BUT-CORRECT print is not the de-fatalisation set, and naming the right menu is the first job of whoever takes this. *Provenance: the deepseek seat, `panel_20260917_100431`, in an answer STAMPED ACROSS SIX ROWS -- so the finding had no cell of its own.  Third real defect recovered today from a review that was written, delivered and never read as its own answer.*
