rows.title: check_boilerplate.py keyed on note[:60], so it clustered on the opening sentence -- 20 of 64 clusters were false positives AND it hid ten genuine stamps by merging them into mixed buckets
rows.state_note: [2026-10-02] the repair (the full-note comparison key) sat UNCOMMITTED in the working tree from 2026-09-17 while this row read closed; the census found it (Astra, overturning grok, who had read the working copy).  #557 commits it, with its comment corrected per Astra's review (the preamble is 81 characters, not 66; the landing language; the recall overstatement; the stale header) and its controls re-run on the day (regress/artifacts/closeassess_20261002/draft/boilerplate_controls_20261002.out); the commits field is filled with #557's sha by its post step.  *** `check_boilerplate.py` COMPARED THE FIRST 60 CHARACTERS OF A SEAT NOTE, SO IT CLUSTERED ON THE OPENING SENTENCE RATHER THAN ON THE NOTE.  Fixed 2026-09-17 by owner decision, with the audit run first. ***  Cells that carried each seat's OWN finding but shared an identifying preamble -- `LATE REVIEW of the six rows the seat audit flagged (panel panel_20260917_100431).` is 66 characters before the first seat writes a word -- were reported as boilerplate **while satisfying this check's own stated rule**, which asks for *"each seat its own sentence from its own file"*.  They had their own sentence. **MEASURED OVER EVERY CLUSTER IN THE LEDGER, BOTH KEYS, SAME RUN:**  OLD `note[:60]` -- 64 clusters, 44 genuine, **20 NOTES DIFFER**; NEW full note -- 54 clusters, **54 genuine, 0 notes differ**. *** IT FAILED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE SECOND HALF IS THE SURPRISE: GENUINE STAMPS ROSE 44 -> 54. ***  A 60-character bucket holding a real stamp ALONGSIDE other notes scored as one mixed cluster, so **the prefix key was HIDING TEN REAL STAMPS BY MERGING THEM**.  Truncation cost recall as well as precision; it never bought either. **ALL SEVEN LIVE REDS WERE FALSE**, each with seven genuinely distinct notes -- so section O was blocking commits on nothing. **CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS:** `BOILERPLATE_PASS` with the seven gone; an INJECTED identical paragraph across four seat cells post-cutoff turns it red and names the row; removing the injection restores green. *** AND A HARNESS BUG OF MINE IS RECORDED IN THE FILE, because it produced a wrong number first: `shared_notes` returns its key with NEWLINES REPLACED BY SPACES for display, so a verification that compares a recomputed key against the RETURNED one silently matches nothing for any note containing a newline -- and then reports the cluster as non-identical. ***  It made one cluster (`wdcnoirq`) look like a survivor when the fix had worked.  *Recompute the bucket; never compare against the display key.*  **Third time this session that a check of mine keyed on a correlate of the thing rather than the thing.**

rows.state_note: *** `seat_verdicts.py` CAN SCORE A GENUINE WALL AS `answered` WHEN THE SEAT STREAMED ENOUGH TEXT TO YIELD A VERDICT-SHAPED PHRASE.  Measured 2026-09-17. ***  `is_walled = _is_wall(t[-600:], t[-4000:]) and not v`.  The tail test is right and fires; `and not v` suppresses it. **IT CONTRADICTS THE FILE'S OWN DOCUMENTED RULE**, which distinguishes *"STRONG ones are a notice on their own; WEAK ones (`quota`, `rate limit`) need"* the extra condition -- and then applies the extra condition to both.  `usage limit` and `quota will reset` are both in `WALL_STRONG`. **MEASURED POPULATION, not generalised from the instance:** 2,369 seat files / 356 panel dirs; **166 walls by the tail test; 2 hidden** -- `panel_20260917_085545/kimi.txt` (2.4 MB, today, on the in-flight `#530`) and `panel_20260820_005715/codex.txt` (21 KB). **WHY THE GUARD EXISTS, so nobody removes it blindly:** the file records that the wall test twice fired on LIVE seats that were merely DISCUSSING rate limits.  The fix for that was the TAIL RESTRICTION (`t[-600:]`), which is the real discriminator; `and not v` is belt-and-braces that now costs more than it buys for STRONG patterns. **THE SHAPE OF A FIX, filed rather than applied:** report WALLED on a STRONG pattern in the tail regardless of `v`, and keep `and not v` for WEAK patterns only -- which is exactly what the file already says it does.  It owes two negative controls (a live seat discussing quotas must NOT be walled; a strong-notice tail with a verdict in the stream MUST be) and it is a third checker change in one session, so it ships as its own harness round rather than as a rider.

rows.title: ten ledger cells recorded the BRIEF back as the seat's answer -- a substring match on CLOSE fired on `closed` in the brief's headings -- and section G cannot see it, because an entry exists
rows.state_note: *** TEN OF SIXTY-THREE LEDGER CELLS RECORDED THE BRIEF BACK AS THE SEAT'S ANSWER, AND NO GATE CAN SEE IT.  Found by the Fable seat 2026-09-17; measured and repaired the same day. ***  **ROOT CAUSE, and it is one character class:** the extraction matched `CLOSE|KEEP-OPEN|NOT CHECKABLE` as a SUBSTRING, so **`CLOSE` fired on the word `closed`** -- which appears in the brief's own headings (`### 1. \`lcashiftub\` (LOW, closed) -- ...`) and in seat narration (*"I'll verify each closed row"*).  It then took the FIRST matching line, which for a seat that ECHOES the brief (codex) or NARRATES ITS PLAN (grok) is not its verdict. **MEASURED: 9 codex cells were brief headings; 1 grok cell was a 926-character opening narration.  53 of 63 were genuine.**  All ten repaired -- codex's from its real per-row verdict table, grok's from its row-9 table line. *** WHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN UNREAD REVIEW, in the Fable seat's words: "an unread review filed under a RECORDED seat -- section G cannot see it because an entry exists." ***  Section G's whole question is *did a seat that answered get recorded*; a cell containing the BRIEF answers yes.  **The blank that would have been caught was filled with something shaped like an answer** -- the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement family, one step further along than any instance this project has recorded. **AND MY OWN AUDIT OF IT UNDER-COUNTED 9 AS 6**, because the pattern I checked required a severity token `(LOW|MED|HIGH)` and three headings carry only `(closed)`.  *Sixth correlate-keyed check of the session, committed inside the audit of the fifth -- which is why the repair was done by RE-EXTRACTING ALL 63 with a corrected key and DIFFING, rather than by patching the rows the audit named.* **THE STRUCTURAL LANDING SPOT, FILED NOT BUILT:** a checker that flags a ledger cell whose text appears verbatim in the `brief_sent.md` of the panel dir the entry cites.  Both files are already on disk and already linked by the `ev` field, so the comparison is cheap and needs no new convention.  It owes two negative controls (a genuine cell quoting a short phrase from the brief must NOT fire; a pasted heading MUST) and is a tooling change, so it ships as its own harness round rather than as a rider.

rows.title: eleven probe exemptions in check_probe_wiring.py all expire 2026-09-20 -- a deliberate alignment of TWO debts that nine later exemptions copied, so the checker reds on eleven unrelated probes at once
rows.state_note:
*** STATUS 2026-09-25 (GXEMUL): #550 DISPERSES the block -- ten dates, 2026-10-08 to 2026-12-03, each with its reason (regress/artifacts/exemptredate_20260925/).  CLOSED. ***

*** STATUS 2026-09-18 (GXEMUL): #536 SHIPS under `wiringcliff`.  Two probes wired (mk48_nvram, hpcmips_ctor); the other ELEVEN re-dated to 2026-09-27 BY OWNER RULING -- one block again, valid on the 27th, RED from 2026-09-28.  That is the cliff this row names, re-created on purpose; the row stays open until it is dispersed or discharged. ***

*** ELEVEN PROBE EXEMPTIONS FALL DUE ON THE SAME DAY, 2026-09-20 -- THREE DAYS FROM THIS FILING.  Measured 2026-09-17 by the Opus 5 seat and verified here. ***  A date histogram over `check_probe_wiring.py`'s `EXEMPT` table: **11 entries dated `2026-09-20`**, plus one `2026-09-19` and one `2026-09-21` -- so **thirteen exemptions expire inside three days**, eleven of them together. *** AND THE PILE-UP IS AN ACCIDENT OF A DELIBERATE CHOICE, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. ***  The file's own comment explains the date: *"2026-09-20 matches the fbpending_bound:2026-09-20 deadline already standing in gate_offline.sh's SM_EXEMPT, so `#442`'s two debts fall due together."*  **Aligning TWO debts was a good idea; nine more have since been written to the same date, and nobody chose that.**  Each new exemption copied the date it found. **WHAT IT COSTS IF NOTHING IS DONE:** on 2026-09-20 the checker reds on eleven probes at once, and a gate that reds on eleven unrelated things is the shape this project already names -- *a rule that retro-fails at scale gets switched off, and a disabled rule is worse than no rule*.  The honest options are to WIRE them, to RE-DATE them individually with their own warrants, or to retire the ones whose rounds are closed -- but **not** to push the whole table forward as one edit, which is how the pile-up formed. *Note one of the eleven is `ppc_rldicl_probe.py`, whose repair is uncommitted and whose row (`ppcwitnessmaskoracle`) is open -- so that debt is about to come due on an oracle nothing executes.*

rows.title: dev_sgi_ip30.c DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_ip30_2) case 0x114+0x40*(12-8) carries an UNLATCHED guest-drivable fatal() whose message is a keyboard mash (asdvasdvnb), on an arm that is actually implemented and returns the documented 0x80000000 alive value
rows.state_note: FILED 2026-09-17 by the #531 pass-2 grok seat; every element verified here before filing.  NOT one of #531's four sites -- it carries no abort() and no exit(, so it kills nothing.  The round-scope rule takes ONE site, and a second joins only in the SAME semantic class; a host kill and a log flood are different classes, which is why this is filed rather than folded in.  UPSTREAM RESIDUE, checked against HEAD rather than assumed: present before #531 and never touched by the fork.  TWO defects in one line -- UNLATCHED (every guest read prints; floodclass already records guest-drivable log floods as a CLASS, and the house idiom is N=1 per device instance with an unqualified '(once)' marker) and a MEANINGLESS MESSAGE that tells a reader nothing.  DISPOSITION when it is taken: member 1 DELETE, not member 3.  The arm computes the right value and refuses nothing, so there is no event to announce, and a bounded announce would ship a wrong record in product code -- exactly what the footbridge +0x188 case established.  WITNESS when it is taken: a rung-3 probe reading that offset and counting emissions.  The #531 probe's vehicle already reaches this device, so the cost is one session, not a new rig.  *** WARRANT CORRECTED 2026-09-18 after the kimi seat named it in the §F2 adjudication: 'a host kill and a log flood are different classes' KEYS ON IMPACT, which is a CORRELATE of the defect -- committed in the very sentence excluding a row, during a session spent cataloguing that error. ***  The reopening rule's test is its own parenthetical, SO ONE FIX DESIGN COVERS BOTH.  The filing stands and is stronger than the reason given: (1) NOT the same device -- sgi_ip30_2 is a separate DEVICE_ACCESS and registration, and sharing a .c file is not sharing a device; (2) NOT one fix design -- #531 de-fatalises, while this arm computes the right value and needs member 1 DELETE; (3) NOT the same detector -- no row reaches that offset, so it needs a NEW ORACLE, which the rule excludes outright.

rows.title: dev_sgi_ip30.c set_isr (0x10020) ASSIGNS where the set/clear register pair implies OR: d->isr = idata clobbers every other pending interrupt bit, while the sibling clear_isr at 0x10028 is a correct AND-NOT
rows.state_note: FILED 2026-09-17 from the #531 pass 2.  *** FLAGGED BY grok AT DESIGN TIME AND CARRIED BY NO QUEUE ROW UNTIL NOW -- the unread-review class, which this project has paid for three times. ***  MEASURED by the opus5 seat on the shipped build: set 0x00ff then 0x5a00 gives ISR 0x5a00, NOT 0x5aff; while set 0x00ff then clear 0x000f correctly gives 0x00f0.  A set/clear register PAIR exists precisely because the set is an OR -- otherwise the clear register would be redundant -- so `d->isr = idata' loses every bit a concurrent source has raised.  #531 invokes heart.h's authority for two decisions in these very arms (write-side at 0x10020/0x10028, read-only at 0x10030) and leaves this third one untouched.  NOT folded into #531 deliberately: it is a BEHAVIOUR change to a path #531 only de-fatalises, and the addition licence wants a measured delta or a transferred warrant rather than 'while we are here'.  #531 records it as ASSESSED, NOT CHANGED.  WITNESS when taken: the #531 probe's vehicle reaches this arm already -- seed via 0x10020, set a disjoint mask, read back at 0x10030.  One session.

Two structurally identical `fatal("TODO: ip22 legacy interrupt rewrite!"); abort();' pairs in dev_sgi_ip22.c, in the WRITE arms of the local0 and local1 interrupt masks.  *** THE CENSUS LESSON RECURS: these carry no `exit(', so the same three exit( sweeps that walked past #531's four sites walk past these too.  A census keyed on `exit(' cannot see a host death spelled abort(). ***  Ranked HIGH on the same warrant as #531: guest-reachable host death on an advertised machine. The disposition is likely the same as #531's -- heart.h has no ip22 equivalent, so the option-set work starts from the file's own sibling handlers.  LINE NUMBERS VERIFIED 2026-09-17 by opening the file: :314 and :338 exactly, 2 abort() and 0 exit( in dev_sgi_ip22.c.  Grade upgraded BELIEVED -> CONFIRMED.  *** SEVERITY CORRECTED HIGH -> LOW THE SAME DAY IT WAS FILED, AND THE CORRECTION IS MINE TO OWN: I RANKED IT AS A SIBLING OF #531 WITHOUT CHECKING THE ONE FACT THAT MADE #531 LIVE. ***  #531's warrant is that `-E sgi -e ip30' is an ADVERTISED machine AND the device is actually installed -- its rung-3 probe reached the code and killed the host, empirically.  dev_sgi_ip22 is DIFFERENT and the difference is decisive:  (a) `dev_sgi_ip22_init' has exactly TWO call sites in the whole tree, machine_sgi.c:270 and :278, and BOTH ARE COMMENTED OUT;  (b) the file defines DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_ip22) but NO DEVINIT(sgi_ip22), so the autodev / device_add route cannot register it either;  (c) it still COMPILES IN (Makefile.skel lists dev_sgi_ip22.o), which is why an abort()-census finds it and a reachability question does not get asked.  *** THE DEVICE IS NEVER IN ANY MACHINE'S MEMORY MAP, SO NO GUEST CAN REACH EITHER abort(). ***  CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WITNESS LADDER, and it is why this cannot simply be 'done later': NO WITNESS EXISTS OR CAN EXIST AT RUNGS 2-4 while the device is uninstalled, and installing it to reach the site is exactly what the ladder names as LAUNDERING -- 'a machine or device_add introduced IN ORDER TO reach the site is laundering, not witnessing'. rows.title: a row prescribed BY NAME in a seat's fix-design answer can be lost even when #490's diff-against-the-PRETABLE rule is obeyed, because the prescription never entered the PRETABLE -- and a PRETABLE that mis-classifies the cell CERTIFIES the omission
rows.state_note: *** THE FOURTH RECORDED INSTANCE OF THE UNREAD-REVIEW CLASS, AND THE MOST PRECISE: THE MISSING ROW WAS PRESCRIBED BY NAME, IN ONE LINE, IN A DURABLE ARTIFACT, BEFORE THE FIX SHIPPED. ***  regress/artifacts/ip30abortkill/FIXDIFF_grok_20260917.txt:239 reads: '5. `isr 20 rd' / `isr 28 rd' -- load does not clobber ISR; load's VALUE is not the seeded ISR (don't-mirror)'.  BOTH rows, explicitly.  The round shipped `isr 20 rd val' and not its sibling, and it then cost a full extra kill table and a nine-seat adjudication pass to rediscover -- with agy REQUIRING it and grok having to point at its own earlier answer.  The opus5 seat independently reported the same pattern: grok's design pass prescribed six closing rows and items 1, 2, 4 and 5 did not ship.  *** THE STRUCTURAL GAP, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: THE CARRIER'S EXISTING RULE CANNOT CATCH THIS. ***  After #490 the rule is 'a row list rewritten from a panel's findings is DIFFED against the pre-table block's own prescribed rows, not merely extended with the new ones.'  That binds the PRETABLE.  Here the prescription NEVER ENTERED A PRETABLE -- it lived in a SEAT'S FIX-DESIGN ANSWER, and nothing diffs a row list against that.  So the #490 rule was obeyed and the row was still lost: the diff ran against the wrong source document.  AND THE PRETABLE MADE IT WORSE RATHER THAN NEUTRAL: PRETABLE.out listed BOTH read arms as 'decline, no value to pin', so the one artifact #490 DOES mandate diffing against positively asserted that neither row was owed.  *A pre-table block that mis-classifies a cell does not merely fail to catch the omission; it CERTIFIES it.*  grok's correction is one sentence: A DECLINE HAS A VALUE, AND IT IS 0.  PROPOSED REMEDY, FILED NOT BUILT (a harness change owing two negative controls): a round whose fix design was reviewed by a seat DIFFS ITS FINAL ROW LIST AGAINST THAT SEAT'S PRESCRIBED ROWS, as #490 mandates for the PRETABLE -- and the PRETABLE should CARRY those prescriptions forward so the two documents cannot disagree silently.  Cheapest mechanical form is existence-only: if a FIXDIFF_<seat>_*.txt sits beside the killtable dir, each of its numbered prescriptions must map to a shipped row or an explicit no-row sentence.  *** THE LAST FIVE UNREAD ANSWERS READ 2026-09-18 (panel_20260827_134019).  23 OF 23 NOW READ -- the section-G backlog is CLEARED. ***  This was a pass-1 DESIGN panel on a now-CLOSED row, so it was read for the question `seatprescriptiondiff' exists to ask: DID THE PRESCRIPTIONS SURVIVE INTO THE SHIPPED WORK?  *** AND THE ANSWER IS YES -- A NEGATIVE RESULT THAT BOUNDS THE ROW I FILED THIS MORNING. ***  agy prescribed three items.  (1) the predicate fix -- SHIPPED, dev_wdc.c now triggers on WDCTL_RST (0x04) and not WDCTL_4BIT (0x08), with the rising-edge `prev_ctl' machinery and a recorded brace hazard beside it.  (2) the MACHINE_LANDISK alt-status mapping -- NOT in dev_wdc.c, and NOT a silent drop: it was SPLIT INTO ITS OWN ROW `landiskaux', which is open, and OUTSTANDING_BUGS carries the coupling in full.  (3) acceptance rows -- folded, per the kimi/deepseek rulings in the same panel.  *** SO `seatprescriptiondiff' HAS A POPULATION OF ONE (the #531 case), NOT A PATTERN.  A class filed from a single instance is a hypothesis, and this is the first test of it -- it did not generalise.  Recorded as such rather than left looking systemic. ***  AND THE COUPLING WAS HANDLED IN THE SAFE ORDER, which is worth keeping because the unsafe one was live: mapping the landisk register WHILE the predicate still triggered on 0x08 would have latched COMMAND_RESET on SIX routine Device Control writes per probe (a seat measured twelve writes, six of them 0x08, currently all landing on unmapped memory).  The round fixed the PREDICATE first, so `wdcaltctrlbit' is CLOSED as overtaken and `landiskaux' is now OPEN AND UNBLOCKED.  *** THAT MAKES `landiskaux' A ONE-LINE FIX THAT IS NOW SAFE TO TAKE -- a strong critical-and-easily-resolvable candidate for the next round. ***  The other seats' content was design judgement, no live defects: glm listed SEVEN uninlined premises and ranked them by load-bearingness (the premise-audit discipline working as intended); minimax named an option-set hole (C4/B5, 'the brief's C-options jump'); deepseek ruled that a channel reset must clear in-flight transfer, FIFO, phase and interrupt state but NOT per-device-life diagnostics like `warned_*' -- and dev_wdc.c carries 43 `warned_' references, so that distinction is load-bearing there.

rows.title: check_probe_wiring.py's manifest named three .sh paths while its domain() is .py-only by construction -- three permanently unsatisfiable GHOST rows holding the pre-commit gate red
rows.state_note: [2026-10-02] COMMITS FIELD LEFT EMPTY by #557, on purpose: no commit shipped the deletion of the three .sh manifest keys -- they existed only in a working tree and were never committed (686d179c's parent 9c91999a has none of them); 686d179c RECORDS the resolution, adding the explanation at tools/pipeline/check_probe_wiring.py:1157-1176, and is kept here as provenance only.  The attribution rule distinguishes shipped work from records about it (check_commit_attribution.py) and permits a documented-only closure with an empty field (Astra, aconf_557b item 2, correcting its census line and the first draft of this unit).  *** A CHECK THAT CANNOT PASS -- the mirror of the check-that-cannot-fail, and it had been holding the pre-commit gate RED. ***  check_probe_wiring.py's MANIFEST named three `.sh' paths (opus_close7_20260915/scripts2/{laneP,laneQ,mkfreeze}.sh, CLASS_TOOL, #529's lane runners and instrument freezer).  Its `domain()' is `.py'-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: it runs `git ls-files -- "*.py"' and filters `f.endswith(".py")' in two further places.  A `.sh' path can therefore NEVER enter the domain, so a `.sh' manifest entry reports GHOST *whatever its git state*.  MEASURED, which is how it was found rather than reasoned: all three were `git add'ed, `git ls-files' listed all three, and the checker still called them ghosts -- while the FIVE `.py' files in the SAME DIRECTORY cleared.  That asymmetry is the tell.  FIXED by DELETING the three entries and preserving their descriptions as a comment in place.  The alternative -- widening domain() to `.sh' -- was rejected on a stated measurement risk: every unclassified shell driver under regress/ would go newly red, a flood this check was never scoped for.  TWO CONTROLS, both run: (1) the checker goes 3 GHOSTs -> 0 and PROBEWIRING_PASS; (2) the three files remain TRACKED, so the record is preserved and only an undischargeable obligation was removed.  A backup of the pre-edit checker is at /tmp/cpw.before.py for this session.

Measured 2026-09-18 by testing every one of the 25 for an empty `response' field, which is the burn discriminator this project already uses. ***  TWO ARE THINKING BURNS -- SEAT FAILURES, NOT UNREAD REVIEWS: panel_20260826_222557/ollama_deepseek (response 0 chars, thinking 142,280, done_reason=length, eval_count=65536 -- THE burn the carrier documents by its byte count) and panel_20260907_104814/ollama_glm (response 0, thinking 114,797, done_reason=**stop**, eval_count=None -- the variant where BOTH signature fields read NORMAL and only the empty response is diagnostic).  There is nothing to read in either; the honest record is SEAT DOWN.  TWENTY-THREE ARE REAL ANSWERS AND ARE GENUINELY UNREAD, totalling roughly 400 KB.  The largest is panel_20260907_184039/ollama_glm at 243,346 chars -- and it is a burn that panel_ollama.py RECOVERED by re-firing with think=False, so the tooling saved a 121 KB answer that nobody then opened.  *** THE CHECKER GAP: check_seats_read.py counts a BURN and an UNREAD ANSWER identically, and their dispositions are opposite -- one is a seat failure to record, the other is content to read that may hold a defect.  That is this project's own 'a blank cell and a seat failure must not look alike' rule, and the checker enforcing it is itself blind to the distinction. ***  FILED as `seatsreadburnsplit'.  TRIAGED, NOT READ -- stated plainly so the record does not overclaim: this cycle established WHICH of the 25 are readable and which are dead, and read none of the 23.

rows.title: TWENTY-THREE real seat answers (~400 KB) across six panels of 2026-08-27 and 2026-09-07 are recorded nowhere and have never been read
rows.state_note: [2026-10-02] A MEMBER OF `closeassessrows` (#557, from the census: regress/artifacts/closeassess_20261002/grok/grok_closedcensus.txt; confirmed regress/artifacts/closeassess_20261002/aconf_census/codex_aconf_census.txt).  Work still alive: the 23 answers were read, and the same note leaves four checks undone (a gate that matches the probe's printed strings; the PUT@8 contract overclaim; the `rgb not corrupt` inequality; no ABGR row) -- pending checks, not established defects (Astra: sgi_re_rgb_probe.py:343 already asserts the exact value).  The row is NOT re-opened here: that decision is the class row's work.  Split out from the gate's section-G count once the two THINKING BURNS were separated (see `seatsreadburnsplit').  These 23 are REAL ANSWERS with non-empty response fields.  *** THIS PROJECT HAS NOW FOUND REAL DEFECTS IN AN UNREAD REVIEW FOUR TIMES -- most recently on 2026-09-18, when grok's FIXDIFF prescription of `isr 28 rd val' turned out to have been written down before #531 shipped and cost an extra kill table to rediscover. ***  The single largest is panel_20260907_184039/ollama_glm at 243,346 chars, which is notable twice over: panel_ollama.py DETECTED a thinking burn on the first shot and re-fired with think=False to recover a 121 KB real answer -- so the tooling did its job and the answer was still never opened.  TRIAGED, NOT READ: this row exists because the 25-count was measured and split, not because the content was reviewed.  Reading them is the work.  Panels: 20260827_050852 (4), 20260827_134019 (5), 20260907_051055 (4), 20260907_104814 (3), 20260907_184039 (4), 20260907_221353 (3).  *** FOUR UNREAD SEAT ANSWERS FROM _scratchpad/panel_20260907_051055 READ 2026-09-18 -- the FIRST of the 23 to be opened, chosen because this panel is cited by a LIVE HIGH row. ***  They contain real content, which is the fifth time this project has found something in an unread review.  (1) *** THREE SEATS INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED THAT `+' -> `|' IS AN UNCATCHABLE NULL MUTANT in the RGB pack: every term is a uint8_t shifted into DISJOINT bit ranges, so sum == OR always. ***  glm: 'No test can or should catch it.'  kimi: 'Uncatchable by construction.'  minimax: 'NOT caught by behavioral tests.'  That is an EQUIVALENT mutant and therefore a RESULT, not a coverage gap -- the same disposition #531 reached for its latch-macro renumbering.  Three independent derivations is the one kind of agreement that IS evidence.  (2) glm AND kimi independently named a CLEAN-SWEEP mutant: the MIRROR EDIT IN THE PUT ARM (make PUT write [0,R,G,B]).  It round-trips perfectly against the corrected GET, so every round-trip row passes while the on-the-wire byte order is inverted.  A clause-(d) concern for whatever detector shipped.  (3) deepseek challenged a MEASURED VALUE and the resolution is PATH-DEPENDENT, which is worth more than either claim: it derived that an RGB PUT->GET round-trip on 0xaabbccdd yields **0xbbcc0000**, not the 0xbbccdd00 the records carry.  BOTH ARE CORRECT FOR DIFFERENT PATHS, verified here against dev_sgi_re.c: a COPY reads its source as four REAL bytes from guest memory (buf = {aa,bb,cc,dd}) so GET-reads-buf[1..3] gives 0xbbccdd00; a PUT->GET round-trip writes an explicit PAD at buf[3]=0 (the PUT arm sets it) so the same GET gives 0xbbcc0000.  **The defect, if any, is a record that quotes one path's value while describing the other's** -- NOT verified here which way #505's brief put it, and deliberately NOT asserted.  Filed for checking.  (4) CORROBORATION OF TWO OPEN ROWS, from seats that had never been read: glm found 'no arm initializes buf[4..7] -- a bufdepth-8 PUT transmits four uninitialised bytes' (= `sgirebufuninit'), and kimi found 'all three 32-bit arms pack/unpack four bytes regardless of bufdepth, which can be 1, 2, 4 or 8' (= `sgirebufshiftub').  kimi also independently re-found the YCRCB default writing four bytes of host random() (= `sgirandomcolour', HIGH).  *** PROGRESS: 4 of 23 READ (panel_20260907_051055). NINETEEN REMAIN. ***  *** AN UNREAD REVIEW IS TIME-INDEXED, AND READING ONE LATE CAN MANUFACTURE PHANTOM WORK AS EASILY AS IT RECOVERS A DEFECT.  Measured 2026-09-18 on the second panel opened. ***  panel_20260907_184039: TWO seats independently (kimi and glm) flagged #507's comment claim 'here and three lines up' as FALSE, and glm named the actual lines it should cite.  glm went further -- 'Q2: not shipped: #507 as written (comment)'.  A live L4 in a closed round, found by two seats, in an answer nobody had opened.  *** IT WAS ALREADY FIXED. ***  cpu_alpha_palcode.c now reads 'four lines above' and carries its own correction note: '"three lines up" until 2026-09-07' -- the SAME DAY as that panel.  Verified here: `apcb_ptbr = new_ptbr' is at :296 and the #507 comment block begins at :300, so FOUR is right and THREE was wrong.  The seats were correct when they wrote it and the defect was discharged, almost certainly by a sibling answer that WAS read.  *** THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMAINING 19, AND IT CHANGES HOW THEY MUST BE PROCESSED: these answers are up to THREE WEEKS OLD (2026-08-27 and 2026-09-07).  Every finding in them must be RE-CHECKED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE before it is recorded as live.  The unread-review hazard is usually stated as 'you miss real defects'; its mirror is 'you re-raise fixed ones', and a phantom row costs a round. ***  *Method for the rest, therefore: read for findings, then CHECK each against HEAD before filing -- exactly as the #507 claim was checked here rather than recorded on two seats' agreement.*  ALSO CAPTURED from that panel, still to check: kimi's #506 `relative_addr' question, glm's four per-round 'single settling fact' items, and minimax's observation on #508 that `return 2' reports every walked page writable.  *** PROGRESS: 8 of 23 READ.  FIFTEEN REMAIN. ***  *** THREE MORE UNREAD ANSWERS READ 2026-09-18 (panel_20260907_104814; its glm is one of the two THINKING BURNS and has nothing to read).  THE TIME-INDEXING LESSON LANDED A SECOND TIME AND MORE SHARPLY. ***  deepseek's Q6 claimed the gate's `^$v  .*ok$' row pattern CANNOT MATCH, because the probe pads `%-16s' plus a space so only a 15-char name leaves exactly two.  **MEASURED FALSE HERE**: the `.*' after the two literal spaces absorbs the extra padding, so every name of <= 15 chars matches -- `rgb chan' (9 trailing spaces) matches True; only a name of 16+ fails.  kimi, in the SAME unread panel, had already corrected deepseek: an unsatisfiable pattern makes `count' return 0 against a wanted 1 and FAILS LOUDLY rather than greening.  *** AND gate_arm.sh ALREADY CARRIES THAT CORRECTION IN ITS OWN COMMENT, measured at name lengths 15/16/17, INCLUDING the note that an earlier draft had copied the wrong 'silently stops testing while staying green' sentence from a sibling block and that the pass-2 panel caught it. ***  So the gate was already right and already knew.  **Had I recorded deepseek's claim as a finding I would have filed a false defect against a gate that documents the opposite, with a measurement.**  Checked instead of recorded, per the method this row adopted after the #507 case.  WHAT SURVIVES, none of it yet checked against HEAD and all of it flagged as such: (1) kimi -- *** THE GATE BLOCK GREPS STRINGS THE PROBE ITSELF PRINTED (row verdicts, SGIRGB_WITNESS=PASS), so it validates the probe's SELF-REPORT rather than independent behaviour -- 'the probe grades its own homework'. ***  Real, but ARCHITECTURAL: it is how every probe-backed gate in this tree works, and the mitigation is that the probe's rows are themselves measured against mutants.  Worth a row of its own rather than a #531 rider.  (2) deepseek -- CONTRACT OVERCLAIM: the row set has `rgb chan' (GET@4), `rgb depth64' (GET@8) and `rgb samemode' (PUT@4), and NO row for PUT@8, while the contract claims 'both directions at widths 4 and 8'.  Its M9_put8 mutant corrupts the RGB PUT arm only when bufdepth == 8 and is predicted to sweep clean.  CHECKABLE.  (3) kimi -- `rgb not corrupt' is an INEQUALITY against one specific value (0xbbccdd00), so it greens on ANY other wrong value, including a different corruption.  (4) kimi -- value-conditioned and location-conditioned mutants; and NO ABGR row exists, so a reader assuming sibling coverage would be wrong.  *** PROGRESS: 11 of 23 READ.  TWELVE REMAIN. ***  *** FOUR MORE UNREAD ANSWERS READ 2026-09-18 (panel_20260827_050852).  THIS ONE IS A RATIFICATION, AND THAT IS RECORDED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN LEFT BLANK -- the gate's own rule: if a seat truly had nothing new to say, record THAT, because a blank cell and a seat failure must not look alike. ***  agy: VERDICT GO, 'all premises, calculations, diff hunks and test oracles are verified against the repository'.  glm, minimax and deepseek concur.  NO live defect found, and none of the four raised a floor or coverage breach.  *** THE ONE SUBSTANTIVE CONVERGENCE, reached INDEPENDENTLY by agy and deepseek, and it is a warrant the round should keep: THE TWO DEFECTS WERE NOT SEPARABLE AND SHIPPING THEM TOGETHER WAS MANDATORY. ***  Bounding the initial push WITHOUT the re-arm refill would have made every transfer in (32768, 65536] worse than pre-fix: the initial push queues only 32768, the guest drains it, atapi_len goes 0, the re-arm then sets atapi_len = remaining while THE RING IS EMPTY -- so the guest is told bytes remain and none do.  That band WORKED pre-fix by accident (the whole transfer was pushed on the initial arm), so a half-fix would have INJECTED corruption into a working band.  glm's one nit, a RECORDS point: the commit message states the re-arm fix is for the >32768 remaining case and separately that bounding is for the >262656 wrap, which reads as two independent fixes when the coupling is tighter than that.  Commit messages are immutable history, so this is noted rather than edited.  ALL FOUR independently confirmed the round's SCOPE BLOCK is honest: a rung-1 direct-call harness is a DETECTOR and never a witness; only the FIRST re-arm is pinned; wdc_addtoinbuf() remains unbounded (filed); and *** wdcrearmzero STILL OWES A RUNG-3/4 WITNESS *** -- which is the one actionable item this panel leaves, and it is why the row is HELD rather than closed.  *** PROGRESS: 15 of 23 READ.  EIGHT REMAIN (panel_20260827_134019 x5 -> wdcaltctrlbit [closed]; panel_20260907_221353 x3 -> lcashiftub [closed/low]). ***  *** THREE MORE UNREAD ANSWERS READ 2026-09-18 (panel_20260907_221353), AND THEY CONVERGED ON ONE SETTLING FACT THAT NOBODY EVER LOOKED UP -- ONE GREP, ELEVEN DAYS UNREAD. ***  glm, kimi and minimax independently named THE SAME single missing fact as the only thing standing between the round and a clean pass: THE DECLARED TYPE OF `tag' in DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf).  kimi put it plainest: 'What settles Q1 (the only open technical question): one line -- the declaration of `tag'.'  *** SETTLED 2026-09-18 BY READING IT: `int tag, type1, bus, dev, func, reg;' -- a plain int. ***  AND THE CONSEQUENCE, derived rather than asserted: in the fixed expression `tag & (0x800U << dev)' the UNSIGNED operand forces `tag' to be converted to unsigned int by the usual arithmetic conversions, so the AND is evaluated in unsigned and its TRUTH VALUE is identical to the pre-fix expression's.  The fix removes the signed-overflow UB (`0x800 << 20' on a plain int is 2^31, which does not fit) WITHOUT changing behaviour on any real target.  **THE ROUND'S UNIVERSAL NO-CHANGE CLAIM HOLDS**, and it is now settled by a reading rather than resting on an unverified premise -- which is what all three seats asked for.  OTHER POINTS THEY RAISED, none of them live defects: glm flagged P3 as 'the round's weakest settled premise -- asserted, uninlined, and precisely the shape seven seats ratified last time' (the premise-audit class, correctly identified); kimi noted a DUPLICATE CROSS-REFERENCE (the trailing /* #511 */ on the fixed line plus the citation inside the block -- keep one) and that the control's 3/4 invariant score should be quoted in the `ubsanshiftlane' row as evidence; minimax noted `0x800U << dev' is well-defined only if unsigned int is at least 32 bits, true on every host this project targets.  *** PROGRESS: 18 of 23 READ.  FIVE REMAIN (panel_20260827_134019, -> wdcaltctrlbit [closed]). ***  *** THE LAST FIVE UNREAD ANSWERS READ 2026-09-18 (panel_20260827_134019).  23 OF 23 NOW READ -- the section-G backlog is CLEARED. ***  This was a pass-1 DESIGN panel on a now-CLOSED row, so it was read for the question `seatprescriptiondiff' exists to ask: DID THE PRESCRIPTIONS SURVIVE INTO THE SHIPPED WORK?  *** AND THE ANSWER IS YES -- A NEGATIVE RESULT THAT BOUNDS THE ROW I FILED THIS MORNING. ***  agy prescribed three items.  (1) the predicate fix -- SHIPPED, dev_wdc.c now triggers on WDCTL_RST (0x04) and not WDCTL_4BIT (0x08), with the rising-edge `prev_ctl' machinery and a recorded brace hazard beside it.  (2) the MACHINE_LANDISK alt-status mapping -- NOT in dev_wdc.c, and NOT a silent drop: it was SPLIT INTO ITS OWN ROW `landiskaux', which is open, and OUTSTANDING_BUGS carries the coupling in full.  (3) acceptance rows -- folded, per the kimi/deepseek rulings in the same panel.  *** SO `seatprescriptiondiff' HAS A POPULATION OF ONE (the #531 case), NOT A PATTERN.  A class filed from a single instance is a hypothesis, and this is the first test of it -- it did not generalise.  Recorded as such rather than left looking systemic. ***  AND THE COUPLING WAS HANDLED IN THE SAFE ORDER, which is worth keeping because the unsafe one was live: mapping the landisk register WHILE the predicate still triggered on 0x08 would have latched COMMAND_RESET on SIX routine Device Control writes per probe (a seat measured twelve writes, six of them 0x08, currently all landing on unmapped memory).  The round fixed the PREDICATE first, so `wdcaltctrlbit' is CLOSED as overtaken and `landiskaux' is now OPEN AND UNBLOCKED.  *** THAT MAKES `landiskaux' A ONE-LINE FIX THAT IS NOW SAFE TO TAKE -- a strong critical-and-easily-resolvable candidate for the next round. ***  The other seats' content was design judgement, no live defects: glm listed SEVEN uninlined premises and ranked them by load-bearingness (the premise-audit discipline working as intended); minimax named an option-set hole (C4/B5, 'the brief's C-options jump'); deepseek ruled that a channel reset must clear in-flight transfer, FIFO, phase and interrupt state but NOT per-device-life diagnostics like `warned_*' -- and dev_wdc.c carries 43 `warned_' references, so that distinction is load-bearing there.  *** CLOSED 2026-09-18: ALL 23 READ.  Two were already-fixed or outright false when checked against HEAD, which is why the method was read-THEN-check; one settled an open question three seats had named (the `tag' type); one was a ratification recorded explicitly rather than left blank. ***

THE PRODUCER, read from source rather than taken from any seat:
  * `store_buf()`, `src/core/memory.c:837-857`, calls `cpu->memory_rw(..., psize, MEM_WRITE, ...)` with `psize` walking **1024, 256, 64, 16, 4, 1** (`:839`, `psize >>= 2` at `:852`) whenever the destination is aligned to `psize` and at least `psize` bytes remain.

*** AND THE ANSWER WAS IN A FILE I WAS CITING. ***  `regress/lca_isalane_probe.py:138-146` carries an L4 CORRECTION dated 2026-09-17 -- a day BEFORE my brief -- reading *THAT WIDTH SET IS A WRONG RECORD. I argued that the truncation at `memory_rw.c:495`/`:523` yields `len >= 1`.  It does not: it fires only when `paddr + len > length`, so it can only CLIP `len` DOWN, and an entry `len` of 0 never trips it. WHY IT NEEDS A NON-INSTRUCTION PATH (the probe's own words, `:148-151`): the probe is instruction-driven and the widest Alpha store, STQ, is 8 bytes -- *no instruction-driven row can ever express len > 8.*  **And the product code is CORRECT and must NOT be touched** (`:159-162`): at len 16, `(relative_addr & 3) % 16` reduces to `relative_addr & 3`, in [0,3], safe.  What is owed is a ROW, not a fix.

THE PATH, each link read from source:
  * `machine_alpha.c:189` stores the word `0x3fffffe` at `PROM_ENTRY_PADDR` -- i.e. the PROM entry IS `CALL_PAL 0x3fffffe`, and `cpu_alpha_palcode.c:519-520` dispatches that code to `alpha_prom_call`.
  * `PROM_R_GETENV = 0x22`, `PROM_E_BOOTED_OSFLAGS = 0x8` (`thirdparty/alpha_prom.h:69,85`).
  * GETENV `:141-144`: `len = a3`, capped to `strlen(s)+1`, then `store_buf(cpu, a2, s, len)`, where `s` for OSFLAGS is `boot_string_argument`, set by `-o` (`main.c:434-435`).
  * `store_buf`, `memory.c:837-857`: walks `psize` 1024 -> 256 -> 64 -> 16 and issues ONE `memory_rw(addr, psize)` wherever `addr` is `psize`-aligned and `len >= psize`.

THE CELL, enumerated:
    target  : 0x2ff, the ns16550 SCR -- the probe's own `:127` names it `whose read returns d->reg[] with no side effect`
    SP(0x2ff) = 0x1c0000000 + (0x2ff << 5) = 0x1c0005fe0
    alignment of 0x5fe0:  1024 no,  256 no,  64 no,  16 YES   -> exactly ONE 16-byte memory_rw
    in lca_isa: port = 0x2ff,  ofs = (0x2ff & 3) % 16 = 3,  forwards s[3]

THE ROW: boot `-o ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP` (strlen 16, so `len = min(16, 17) = 16`); guest STBs a SENTINEL to SP(0x2ff) first, then `a0=0x22 a1=0x8 a2=0x1c0005fe0 a3=16`, executes the word `0x03fffffe`, then LDBUs SP(0x2ff).  **FIX: 0x44 (`'D'`, s[3]).  M2: the sentinel, unchanged** -- a 16-byte store fails `len <= 8`, falls into the READ arm, and the SCR is never written.

**TWO THINGS ONLY A RUN SETTLES, named so nobody mistakes this design for a measurement:** whether execution resumes at the next instruction after an inline `CALL_PAL 0x3fffffe` (the real PROM entry is reached by `jsr` and returns by `ret`); and whether `store_buf`'s `memory_rw` translates `a2` the same way the probe's own `SP()` loads do.  **Owed after the owner-driven session's gate run: build it, show it RED under M2 and GREEN on base with ONE frozen script, and cite `lcawidefold` rather than re-filing the one-byte forward it will also observe.**

rows.title: dev_footbridge.c: the CPU interrupt line can STICK HIGH while IRQ_STATUS reads 0.  footbridge_interrupt_deassert() lowers d->irq only when d->irq_asserted is set, and the IRQEnableSet / IRQEnableClear write arms call INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->irq) without setting it.  Sequence (Opus seat, #545 repair pass 2, measured in its in-process differential -- regress/artifacts/fbd5/q2_20260923/p2r_20260923/opus_q2r/dom_witness.txt 'model check'): a device line (cats ISA, line 10) asserts while its enable bit is clear, the guest sets the enable (W188 0x400 -> ASSERT, irq_asserted still 0), the line deasserts -> no DEASSERT; the CPU line stays 1 with nothing pending.  Pre-existing (the enable arms' bodies are upstream).  Fix: the enable arms maintain irq_asserted exactly as the assert/deassert callbacks do.  Witness owed: rung 3 on -E cats needs a real device line; the offline differential can row it now (it counts the calls).  AND THE PRODUCER PAIR'S OWN BIT LOGIC IS FILED HERE BY OWNER RULING (2026-09-23), a DIFFERENT defect from the stuck line (grok, #545 3c's pass), so the round taking this row owes both: #545's detector calls footbridge_interrupt_assert() only to raise one line from an empty status and never calls _deassert(), so `|=` -> `=` in the assert (PR01), the enable test weakened (PR03) and the `~` deleted from _deassert's `irq_status &= ~interrupt->line` (PR04) pass all 864 rows -- disclosed in its contract.  Ready rows: the Opus seat's q2e scratch Y8-Y12 (regress/artifacts/fbd5/q2_20260923/q2e_opus/).

A real ARM narrow load or store hands the device a 1-, 2- or 4-byte buffer (cpu_arm_instr_loadstore.c).  Unobserved on the 864 rows: (1) a FETCH past len whose value no channel uses -- every declined write, and the Opus seat's FW03 (an 8-byte fetch at len 4, measured green, equivalent for the guest) -- UNOBSERVABLE here by construction (the harness's memory helpers record no length); (2) a STORE past len inside a legal write -- `data[len] = 0` in the Clear write (codex, 3e's pass; measured green, qwb QDLEN); (3) the common tail's write-back past len at the legal reads outside X9/X10's five registers, among them VENDOR_ID (+0x00), the timer value (+0x304; +0x324/+0x344/+0x364 fold onto it), FIQEnable (+0x288) and the FIQEnableClear read (+0x28c) -- which X7 reads, and X3 three of them, unchecked -- and the timer LOAD and CLEAR reads, whose 4-byte harness buffer an 8-byte write-back overflows SILENTLY: an 8-byte write-back keyed on any of the seven passes every row (measured, regress/artifacts/fbd5/q2_20260923/qwb_20260923/, three runs, predictions first -- ORDER_NOTE.txt names the file proving each run's order).  Above #545's floor (the tail and the fetch are not predicates dominating the edited arms): disclosed in the contract by repair 3f and filed; the flagship seat's final adjudication upheld the filing.  Fix shape: pad_kept after every read in X3, X7 and the timer rows and after each narrow write in X12/X13 (a new channel on rows that exist, so it owes a table), and a length-recording memory helper for the fetch.

rows.title: gate_hygiene.sh's readiness census is a SPELLING census.  The census round (#546, pass 2 -> F6e) rebuilt its POSITIVE classifications on Python tokens (regress/census_tokens.py: a comment, a string or a docstring is not code; statement boundaries kept; per-occurrence counts), which closed the comment / string / docstring and most spacing evasions pass 2 and F2 measured.  STILL OPEN, each measured passing all 12 readiness rows on the shipped F6e (regress/artifacts/hygienecensus_20260923/controls_c6e/TABLE.txt, the F2 suite): e9, RANKED FIRST -- the TEXTUAL counts are LINE-based and key on `endswith(`, so a space before the paren (`buf.endswith (">")`, the #37 bare defect behind one space) or a backslash continuation (t_bsl) removes a call from all of them; another receiver name (e_e1, n3h); `strip()` or `rstrip("\r\n")` for `rstrip()` (e_e5, n3f); a slice compare (e_e4; n10, `buf.rstrip()[-1:] == ">"`, the bare defect again); a parenthesised receiver (n3b, n3c); a regex readiness test (n3i); readiness moved into a helper module (n3k, n3k2 -- no count sees WHICH probe a helper serves); a probe forking with `forkpty` (n4a -- outside the pty census entirely); `~` on the call (t_tilde, the lexical limit); e10 -- the comment filter drops every PHYSICAL line beginning with `#`, so code after a closing triple quote or in an f-string field, or a whole file saved with CR-only line endings, escapes (the census F4 pass, the Opus seat).  And the deriver's writers are not ATOMIC: a write that fails part-way (a full disk) leaves the gate truncated -- reported since F6e as DERIVE_FAIL rc 6 (controls_c6e t_dfwrite, t_dfgrand); a temporary beside the gate and a rename would keep the old one.  Ranked below live defects: the census guards spellings, not readiness.

(7) A census/parser disagreement -- a `match` class pattern -- has no tool exit; the probe must be edited (kimi-k3:cloud, the F6 pass; t_k14release).  (8) The gate's `whole_full=$(printf ... $whole_files | awk ...)` expands `$whole_files` unquoted (grok, the F6 pass; no real token holds a glob character, and NTFS forbids `*` and `?`). rows.title: cpu_arm: an SPSR restore (LDM {..pc}^, DPI S-to-PC) that sets T keeps decoding ARM words until the dyntrans run loop is next entered -- the Thumb interpreter is chosen only at loop entry, arm_pop never breaks out and word-aligns the PC
rows.state_note: filed 2026-10-07 by owner ruling, from #562's §F2 pass (codex disposition 6: 'Mode filtering alone does not make applying T safe or coherent').  CORRECTED 2026-10-08 by reading the source before the round's records were written: the first filing said a restored T=1 'is not honoured' -- it IS, but late.  cpu_dyntrans.c picks arm_cpu_interpret_thumb_SLOW only at the run function's ENTRY (`if (cpu->cd.arm.cpsr & ARM_FLAG_T)`); the DPI restore breaks out (abortdyntrans_call) only for an ODD destination PC; arm_pop never breaks out and loads the PC as r[ARM_PC] & 0xfffffffc, dropping bit 1 of a Thumb address.  So after a restore that sets T the CPU can keep decoding ARM words until the loop is next entered.  Out of #562's scope (#562 declines only M[4:0]; its probe's `tbit' row pins the T BIT's provenance, not the decoder).  Not witnessed; the round owes a rung-3 attempt first.

rows.title: build trees: a HEADER change leaves stale objects -- the build tracks no header dependencies, propagate_all_trees.sh removes only ${F%.c}.o, and the two-part clearance ([ binary -nt source ]) cannot see an object compiled against the old header

rows.state_note: FOUND 2026-10-09 by #562's gate 14.  #562 inserted `uint32_t mode_warned` into struct arm_cpu (src/include/cpu_arm.h) BEFORE i80321_inten/isrc, tmr0, tmr0_irq/tmr1_irq and tisr; dev_i80321.c is the only object outside src/cpus that touches them.  Every build that rebuilt only src/cpus/*.o (the carrier's recipe, my propagate562.sh and every kill-table clone) linked a dev_i80321.o compiled against the OLD layout, so the device set isrc at the old offset and the guest read 0 -- gate 14's xscale anchor red on the fix and green on HEAD, deterministically.  The two-part clearance PASSED on all three trees: the binary was newer than every source.  propagate_all_trees.sh can relink and report clearance success while header-dependent objects stay stale: `rm -f ${F%.c}.o` deletes nothing for a .h and the link recipe relinks unconditionally (GPT-6 Astra's confirmation; this note first said the tool would report the header stale -- false).  SCOPE MEASURED: only dev_i80321.c reads a field after the insertion point; cd is the last member of struct cpu, so no subsequent struct cpu member shifted, and every other non-CPU ARM access precedes the insertion; the msrmode probe drives -E testarm, which attaches no i80321, so #562's kill-table results are unaffected.  OWED: when a propagated path is a header, delete every object (or every object that includes it) and rebuild; and a third clearance part -- no object older than any edited header -- in the tool and the checkpoint step.

rows.title: cpu_arm.c arm_exception(): Thumb-state aborts save the wrong return address -- data abort LR_abt = instruction + 7, prefetch abort target + 3 (DDI 0100I: + 8 and + 4 in both states)
rows.state_note: filed 2026-10-09: retaddr = cpu->pc (+ 4 for a data abort) + (T ? 2 : 4), and in Thumb state cpu->pc carries bit 0.  MEASURED by Fable 5.1 on the armmmuvehicle pass-1 sessions S10 (Thumb LDR to an unmapped VA: LR_abt = 0x00008107 for an instruction at 0x8100) and S11 (Thumb BX to 0x100001: LR_abt = 0x00100003); read the same day by grok's adversarial job.  DDI 0100I A2.6.6 / A2.6.5 (ddi0100i.txt:2236, :2196) give + 8 and + 4 in both states; IRQ/FIQ are also + 4 in both (:2386, :2440), so the T ? 2 : 4 term is right only for SWI/UND.  A sibling of armthumbabortkill; reachable only with the MMU on, so after armmmuvehicle.

rows.title: dev_vme.c: sub-word VME2 accesses -- 40 width/address combinations at 30 offsets inside cased words reach default: (a host kill today), and a cased base accessed at len != 4 is served with word semantics, lane-wrong on big-endian
rows.state_note: filed 2026-10-09 from Fable 5.1's 7n-4 ruling (regress/artifacts/fablequeue7n_20261009/fable5_rule7n_4.md, populations 3 and 4) with GPT-6 Astra's corrections (regress/artifacts/fablequeue7n_20261009/astra_7n4/codex_astra.txt): 40 width/address combinations at 30 distinct offsets (30 byte accesses + 10 aligned halfword accesses; 16 at the four storing words, 24 at the six other cased words).  'Serve the containing word' is REFUTED: big-endian byte lanes +1/+2 come back wrong (+3 and halfword +2 happen to agree), sub-word writes replace the whole backing word, and a T1COUNT read adds 100 and returns the pre-increment value.  Population 4 (Fable's ELSE #1): an access AT a cased base with len != 4 -- st.b at 0x88 rewrites the whole VBR word, ld.b there returns the low byte; Astra: a doubleword reaching the callback as ONE length-8 access is not established by the files read.  The in-tree OpenBSD 2.2 guest makes no sub-word VME2 access (every vme2reg field is u_long), so LOW.  The width row takes both populations; the FAULT round for population 1 discloses it and pins the interim behaviour with one channel row (the crimectllane precedent).  Reading only; nothing measured.

rows.state_note: filed 2026-10-09 from pcc2c040assertrow's review stage: raised by the deepseek and kimi (kimi-k3:cloud) seats of _scratchpad/panel_20261009_191953, MEASURED 18/18 by the main loop (regress/artifacts/pcc2c040kill/assertrow_review_20261009/probe_eq.raw; base 18/18 in probe_base.raw). rows.title: src/promemul/of.c of_emul(): the OpenFirmware emulation entry calls fatal() + exit(1) when machine->md.of_data is NULL, which is true on every machine except macppc with PROM emulation on (machine_macppc.c returns before of_emul_init when it is off) -- and the ARM and PowerPC decoders route their OpenFirmware magic instruction to it with no machine or privilege check
rows.state_note: filed 2026-10-16 from the adjudication of the agy pack's second readings (packet D, H1): all three seats FILE, HIGH, own row (regress/artifacts/adj_20261016/astra/D_secondreadings/codex_adjD.txt, grok/D_secondreadings/grok_adjD.txt, fable5/fable5_adj_D_secondreadings_v2_FABLE.md).  Source: prescreen_audits5.md of_two/F9.  READ at HEAD by all three: of.c:1096-1101 (the NULL check and the exit), :1078 (the only writer, of_emul_init, called only from machine_macppc.c:99); ARM decode cpu_arm_instr.c:5034-5036 -> X(openfirmware) :988-991; PowerPC decode cpu_ppc_instr.c:4400-4402 -> X(openfirmware) :3956-3958.  A guest instruction therefore ends the emulator process on machines that never set up OpenFirmware.  Not covered by ofopenexit or ofpeerexit (other sites in the same file); Fable 5.1: may share one round with them.  A rung-3 ATTEMPT exists, made by claude-opus-4-8 in the Fable seat's fallback run (so it is not a Fable ruling and owes review before it counts as the witness): regress/artifacts/adj_20261016/fable5/meas_D/witness_hostexit.py and .out, at HEAD e483d931 on the unmodified ARM test machine (the emulator prints `of_emul(): no of_data struct?' and the process exits 1), each with a benign-instruction liveness control that stays alive. ||  [2026-10-21] ARGON SCOPING (packet-fed, a reading not a measurement; regress/artifacts/ofemulnodata/argon_scope_20261021/gemini_web.out, dispositions DISPOSITIONS.md): THREE rounds, not one -- of.c:1100 (this row), :394 (ofpeerexit) and :448 (ofopenexit) differ in semantic class, fix design and detector (the round-scope rule); of.c:549, :577, :1120 and :1201 are UNREACHABLE (machine-setup helpers; arch-switch defaults only ARM and PowerPC reach).  DESIGN for this row: gate the magic word at the DECODERS (cpu_arm_instr.c's SWI case, cpu_ppc_instr.c's sc case) on `cpu->machine->md.of_data != NULL`, so a machine without OpenFirmware executes the word as the architectural SWI / system call it encodes (FAULT) -- NOT an early return inside of_emul, whose callers' tails then jump to the link register as if the call had returned.  Detector: the SWI-exception row on an ARM machine, the sc-exception rows on a non-macppc PowerPC machine and on macppc without PROM emulation, and macppc-with-PROM-emulation accept rows (an OF service still answers).  The title was corrected the same day: macppc without PROM emulation also has of_data NULL (read at machine_macppc.c's `if (!machine->prom_emulation) return;` before of_emul_init).

rows.title: cpu_arm_instr.c: the decoder routes the instruction word 0xef8c64eb (an AL-condition SWI) to X(reboot) -- `cpu->running = 0`, the emulation stops -- on EVERY ARM machine and at ANY privilege level.  machine_cats.c plants that word at 0x41000008 as the cats PROM's reboot entry; on any other ARM machine, or from user mode on cats, one instruction stops the emulated CPU instead of taking the SWI exception the word encodes
rows.note: FILED 2026-10-21 by the main loop (087a90) from Argon's scoping of the of.c exit family (regress/artifacts/ofemulnodata/argon_scope_20261021/gemini_web.out: 'a DIFFERENT ROW ... an unconditional ARM decoder backdoor allowing any ARM guest (including unprivileged user mode) to halt cpu->running'), and READ here at 7f48ea10: cpu_arm_instr.c's SWI decode case sets `ic->f = cond_instr(swi)` and then, for `iword == 0xef8c64eb`, `ic->f = instr(reboot)` with no machine or privilege test; X(reboot) is `cpu->running = 0; cpu->n_translated_instrs --; cpu->cd.arm.next_ic = &nothing_call;`; machine_cats.c stores 0xef8c64ebUL at 0x41000008 (the only writer of the word in src/).  Not the of.c family: no exit(1), no of_emul.  MED by kinship with m88kpsrmxm (a guest action stops the emulated CPU).  No witness yet: a rung-3 probe is one `put w` of the word plus `step` on an unmodified ARM machine, with an ordinary SWI as the control (it must take the SWI vector).  The disposition question for its pass 1: gate the word to cats with PROM emulation (and, if real hardware's reboot needs privilege, to privileged mode), letting everything else take the architectural SWI.

rows.title: cpu_ppc_instr.c X(slw)/X(srw)/X(sraw): the shift amount is masked `& 31`, so shift amounts 32..63 -- which Book I says give 0 (slw, srw) or 64 sign bits with CA = the sign (sraw) -- wrap instead; and in the 64-bit build slw and srw shift the whole register, so bits leak into RA's high word (and srw drags RS's high word into the result).  The 32..63 range is the multi-word shift idiom compilers emit for `long long` on 32-bit PowerPC.  Rung-3 witness on HEAD: 12 of 15 rows FAIL
rows.witness: probe:regress/artifacts/ppcshiftwide/witness_20261020/shift_witness.py -- rung 3, unmodified -E bareppc (PPC970, 64-bit) and -C PPC603 (32-bit), HEAD 1a59a47e (build/gxemul, both clearance parts checked): 3/15 (regress/artifacts/ppcshiftwide/witness_20261020/witness_HEAD.out)
rows.note: FILED 2026-10-20 by the main loop (087a90), found while drafting ppcrlwhighhalf's brief (an Opus 5.5 sub-agent noticed `& 31`) and WITNESSED the same hour.  Book I v2.01 (_scratchpad/ppc_uisa_book1_v201.txt): slw :4404-4414 'The 32-bit result is placed into RA32:63. RA0:31 are set to zero. Shift amounts from 32 to 63 give a zero result.'; srw :4455; sraw :4540-4551 'Shift amounts from 32 to 63 give a result of 64 sign bits, and cause CA to receive the sign bit of (RS)32:63.'  MEASURED (witness_HEAD.out): PPC970 slw sh32 -> 0x12345678, sh33 -> 0x2468acf0, srw sh32 -> 0x12345678, sraw sh32 -> 0xffffffff80000001 with CA 0, the slw control at sh4 -> 0x123456780 (high-word leak), srw with RS high word 0xaaaaaaaa at sh4 -> 0xaaaaaaaa0000001; PPC603 the same 32..63 failures, its sh4 control correct (0x23456780 -- the encodings are right).  Argon (Gemini web, packet-fed, _scratchpad/gweb/jobs_20261020_argonpack21/ppcshift/gemini_web.out) CONFIRMED all 12 failing rows against Book I and found srawi and sld correct; its fix sketch: slw `(uint32_t)((uint64_t)(uint32_t)RS << (RB & 63))`, srw `(uint64_t)(uint32_t)RS >> (RB & 63)`, sraw `sh = RB & 63` (the existing loop then yields all sign bits and CA = sign); six detector rows.  Severity HIGH by kinship with ppcrlwhighhalf (guest-visible wrong results), and the 32..63 range is ordinary compiled code, not a corner.  Needs a round: pass 1, the fix in both builds (MODE32 and 64-bit), a gated probe (gate 13), a kill table. rows.state_note: FIXED by #580 on 2026-11-04 (landing commit 68c0d60b; the records commit after it names it): X(to_be_translated)'s primary switch now raises Reserved Instruction or Coprocessor Unusable for 0x1d, 0x1e off the R5900, LWC2/LDC2/SWC2/SDC2 and LWC3/SWC3 per CPU level, as the ruling of record ordered (R1-R11; the R5900's 0x1e untouched, R3).  Witness 16/80 -> 80/80; the 122-row detector in gate 16 (HEAD 29/122, fix 122/122, dead legs 16/122); test-variant tables 29 of 34 red, the five undetected disclosed (D01, D11, D30 the ISA II cells; D22a/D22b the PC sync).  Pass 2 four seats, text only; the adjudication and its D31 follow-up applied; regress review REGRESS-WITH-FINDINGS (26 checks, 0 floor breaches, 2 record findings, both applied).

entries.note: #580 PASS 1 (bug review) -- agy CLI (gemini-3.8-flash-high, file-reading), outside the 11-03 roster: VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES -- exactly six labels reach default; MDMX RI off the R5900; SWC3 RI only on MIPS32/64, CpU CE=3 below; LDC2/SDC2 CpU CE=2 at every level; default -> RI; "coproc[3] is NULL". Six labels and MDMX adopted (R1-R2); ISA I LDC2/SDC2 refuted by R5, ISA III CP3 forms by D1; default kept; pmax allocates coproc[3] (D2).

#580 PASS 1 (bug review) -- codex GPT-6 Astra (file-reading; _r3 re-fire after an empty first answer): VERDICT: NO-GO -- walked all 64 primaries (six caseless); pmax builds coproc[3] (machine_pmax.c:81/:170); JALX came with the original MIPS16, not only MIPS16e; ISA I LDC2/SDC2 and the MIPS III CP3 slot left open, so only a JALX hunk offered. coproc[3] became D2 (wording fixed, pmax filed); MIPS16 wording adopted (P3); open cells ruled R5 and D1, NO-GO moot (r2 S7).

#580 PASS 1 (bug review) -- grok 4.7 xhigh (file-reading, plan mode): VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES -- the CpU precedent is HI6_COP2, not #236/#309; pmax's live coproc[3] defeats a NULL test, so it proposed an X(cp3_mem) helper with a runtime CU3 check; SWC3 CpU through ISA IV, RI only from MIPS32; no x64 on LDC2/SDC2. #236 fix (P2) and x64 (24KEc rows) adopted; helper not adopted (CpU hard-coded, D2 filed); ISA III-IV SWC3/LWC3 refuted by D1/R11.

#580 PASS 1 (bug review) -- deepseek-v4-pro (packet-fed), outside the 11-03 roster: VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES -- LWC3 and 0x1e reach bad through their own arms, not default; JALX gated on a MIPS16E cpu flag; CpU for every COP2/COP3 load and store at every level; six caseless labels unconfirmed. Arms point stands; no MIPS16E flag exists (m16 = 0), so the arm is plain RI; R5 (ISA I LDC2/SDC2) and D1/R11 (ISA III+ CP3) refute the blanket CpU; grok enumerated the six.

#580 PASS 1 (bug review) -- GLM 5.3 (packet-fed, in the roster): VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES -- the brief's '0x1e is R5900-only' is false; R5900 SQ (0x1f) also stops; SWC3 RI from ISA IV; the R3000 Cause has no CE field; the #309 rt list is self-contradictory (0xd as TNEI). MDMX RI adopted (R2), LQ/SQ filed (F1), SWC3 RI moved to ISA III (D1); R3000 rows measure CE=2/3; TNEI is 0x0e (opcodes_mips.h:244), so the #309 list (unimplemented rt values) holds.

#580 PASS 1 (bug review) -- kimi-k3:cloud (packet-fed substitute), outside the 11-03 roster: VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES -- first to give the shipped split: LWC3/SWC3 CpU CE=3 to ISA II, RI from ISA III; LDC2/SDC2 RI on ISA I; but it called the arm-local fatal() a host kill and asked if COP2/COP3 (0x12/0x13) have cases. Split adopted (D1, R5-R8); fatal() only prints (HEAD stops the CPU and still answers `reg`), and HI6_COP2/COP3 arms exist.

#580 PASS 1 (bug review) -- minimax-m3 (packet-fed), outside the 11-03 roster: VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES -- wants valid JALX, MDMX, LQ and SQ implemented, a MIPS16 decoder kept clear of the RI, owned CPU-STOP rows for whatever stays unimplemented, and CpU at every level for all COP2/COP3 forms. No MIPS16 decoder exists (m16 = 0); MDMX took RI (R2), R5900 LQ/SQ filed (F1) and disclosed, not owned; R5, D1 and R11 refute the blanket CpU.

rows.state_note: Filed 2026-10-25 by #574 (GLM, F2b; Astra: the datasheet paragraph at _scratchpad/i8259/8259A.txt:649 qualifies polling).  No documented guest observes it: NetBSD re-selects 0x0c before every poll and its last selection is the IRR; Linux/malta never writes 0x0c and its spurious path restores 0x0a itself.  A remembered byte (last_rr) is a product addition the addition licence refuses on 'cannot hurt'.  F2d (D8): the IRR-selected-prior case is pinned by `poll once2`; the ISR-selected-prior case (OCW3 0x0b, a poll, a bare read: the model answers IRR, a remembered-selection implementation ISR) is the row owed with any implementation, in the probe's port-I/O shape.

rows.state_note: Filed 2026-10-25 by #574 (Astra and GLM, F2b D5; D_retire_anypic / D_retire_anyline escaped every instrument revision as disclosed, 123/123 on v2g).  RE-GRADED by F2d (pass2_20261025/f2d_20261025/F2D_RULINGS.md D1, D2): the disclosure's warrant -- 'observable only with a pending count >= 2, which only host time produces' -- is WITHDRAWN.  Astra and GLM B derived, and dev_8253.c:118-129 confirms (DEVICE_TICK asserts line 0 on every tick while the count is positive; the only retire is pic8259_acknowledge's), a deterministic construction after ONE host-timer event, in the pit session's own shape: one 8253 event in, line 0 masked by OCW1, a foreign acknowledge (another master line by the poll for D_retire_anyline; the slave's line 0 -- or any slave line, the (pic2, line != 0) cell -- through the GT cascade for D_retire_anypic), then the LEGACY specific EOI of line 0 (not in service: HEAD's consume, no retire), then the next tick: the fix re-asserts line 0 (IRR bit 0 = 1), the mutant does not (0).  Grok's defence of '>= 2' assumes the next line-0 event is an acknowledge.  THE ROWS ARE OWED, NOT DISCLOSED AWAY: the main loop's attempt to write them on 2026-10-25 15:5x was classifier-stopped and, per the standing rule, not retried; #574 landed on v2g with this debt named.  Also owed here: D_nonspec_high (the non-specific arm's highest-bit shape, by construction only) and the non-specific arm's IRR-half reinstatement (HEAD's irr &= ~isr, live under the fix, built by no mutant); and the probe docstring's '>= 2' sentence (regress/i8259_eoi_probe.py:124-126) is a wrong record to correct with the repair.  The earlier band-row idea (two host-timer fires, count deliveries over a window) is superseded by the one-event construction.

state_semantics._WHY: The ledger's schema had NO WRITTEN SEMANTICS. That single absence is the cause behind six mis-counts in one session, two file-reading seats reading OPPOSITE conventions into one closure string, and five seats agreeing on only 4 of 11 rows they were asked to state-check. A field every round ranks and closes from was never defined.
state_semantics._THE_QUESTION_state_ANSWERS: Is anything still owed on this row, and who acts next?
state_semantics._TENSE: *** `state` IS PRESENT-TENSE; `closure.note` IS PAST-TENSE. *** The note is an EVENT LOG of what happened to a STAGE ('CLOSE (assess)' closes the assess stage). `state` asserts what the ROW still owes. **They are independent BY DESIGN** -- 23 rows share the string `CLOSE (assess)` across three states, and that is the ledger working correctly, not a defect: rows that experienced the same stage event legitimately differ in what else they owe. NEITHER can be derived from the other, and both attempts to do so have been measured wrong.
state_semantics.closed: Nothing outstanding; the claim was discharged BY WORK. Mechanical companions, era-scoped: commits, closure.by, and witness if closed on/after 2026-08-19.
state_semantics.dropped: Nothing outstanding; the claim was retired WITHOUT work, with the reason. Confusing this with `closed` is the es438 class -- both mean 'nothing owed', and misstating WHY is what misleads a future reader.
state_semantics.held: Something outstanding, waiting on a NAMED party or event, and carrying the QUESTION it is held for (standing rule). `open`/`held` WITH commits is normal here.
state_semantics._NOT_DERIVABLE_FROM: closure.note, entries, or stage coverage. Establishing a row's state requires a SUBSTANCE READ -- commits, gates, holds, filed questions -- which is what `asicbadaddr` was closed from and is the template.
state_semantics.open: Something outstanding, UNCLAIMED -- the complement of `in work`'s 'actively claimed'. No named party is required (that is `held`) and no work is under way. *** THIS DEFINITION WAS MISSING FROM THE BLOCK UNTIL 2026-08-25, AND `open` IS THE SECOND-LARGEST STATE IN THE LEDGER (46 of 216 rows). *** It appeared only inside `held`'s prose. Found by the fable5 adjudicator when asked to ratify the block -- it was told plainly that ratification was not wanted and to check the premises, and the gap is what that instruction bought. A checker built on the block as written would have misclassified a fifth of the ledger while reporting full coverage, which is this project's own 'a detector built from the wrong census reports full coverage' class wearing schema clothes.
state_semantics._RETROACTIVE_OR_FORWARD_ONLY: *** THE FIRST DRAFT SAID FORWARD-ONLY FLAT, AND THAT WAS HALF RIGHT IN THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. *** The split is by LAYER, and the block's own _TENSE ruling decides it: **the MEANING binds retroactively; only MECHANICAL CHECKS are forward-only by date.** `state` is PRESENT-TENSE, and a present-tense field has no era -- a false state is false NOW. 'Pre-adoption rows are read charitably' would preserve the exact defect this block exists to end (the es438 reader reads 'not done' off shipped, witnessed work TODAY) and would keep the ledger permanently bilingual. Forward-only enforcement follows the boilerplate-check precedent: a rule that retro-fails the archive gets disabled, and a disabled rule protects nothing. *** THE DISHONESTY WORRY DISSOLVES ONCE THE LAYERS ARE SEPARATED: `state` is a LIVE FIELD, NOT HISTORY. *** Correcting it rewrites no history -- `entries`, notes and `commits` are untouched. The migration is the warranted in-place repair already used twice on 2026-08-25: correct the state cell and attach a warrant note naming the row's OWN evidence. NO BULK REWRITE -- the round's central finding stands (state is NOT derivable; five seats agreed on only 4 of 11 rows), so every remaining row gets a substance read.
